Let every preacher praise his holy name forever and ever. Rambler has even stopped hanging around the rowdy dogs in the neighborhood. They come around to try to get him to tear up people's gardens, but Rambler won't go He watches them gloomily from the window. It's almost as if he wishes he could share the good news with them, she says. Maybe he will in his own way. This is story number one. Story number two, not as long. Story number two. Loud Cry Ministries out of White Pine, Tennessee, offers healing of the body with the use of what they call essential oils. Essential oils are to replace, replace much of modern medicine options today. The group believes the ability for the body to be healed with essential oils spans thousands of years back. Quote, it is not a new practice of healing or medicine, but a time-tested means of healing the body that has been lost over time, but is being rediscovered by this current generation. says a spokeswoman. Essential oils supposedly can heal aches, pains, allergies, colds, flus, and even internal diseases. The company believes in sharing, spreading, if you will, the good news of Jesus and selling oil for healing. These, they believe, go hand in hand. Well, which one is true? Story number one or story number two? Who says story number one? The rest of you story number two. Well, it is story number two that is the real story. Story number one comes from a humorous website called LARK News. Story number two, the Ministry of Oils, was brought to our attention by friends that visited with us last week. Evidently, it is another fad that has taken hold in some churches in the South. I bring oil ministry to our attention today because fads Fads among Christians ought not be. I say ought not, not because fads are immoral, but to make the point that fads among Christians are unnecessary. Fads are unnecessary because the gospel is enough. The good news of Jesus Having died and thus paid the penalty for our sins, and of course the glorious news of his resurrection, he is risen, raised from the dead, having overcome sin and death, is most certainly. Enough. No prayer of Debez or slogan bracelet or oil treatment is going to match or even come in second place to the gospel. Let us look here at 1 John chapter 5 and make some observations. The first of which is that there is no fad mentioned by John. In verse 1 of chapter 5, we have a single sentence where we find both the doctrinal test we've been talking about and the social test of a genuine Christian faith. It is a beautiful way of John putting the test of love with a new thought. Everyone who loves the Father loves whoever has been born of him. This is a principle of the Father's own love, so it is not surprising that it should become a principle of our love as well. It also explains the wonderful promise God has made regarding our children, Christian homes, children. I will be a God to you and to your children after you, the Lord had promised. Whoever loves the father or mother will love the father's children also. God loves our children because he loves us. In verse three We find, once again, the moral test, and John expressly ties together the love for God and obedience to his commandments, as he does so well in his gospel. Remember John quoting Jesus, saying, If you love me, you will keep my commandments. Love and commandments, the two, love and obedience. Are not different things, but the same thing. And the point being made here is perhaps perhaps the greatest miscalculation The greatest miscalculation that any Christian can make, or one who calls himself a Christian. You can be a Roman Catholic. And believe that your place in the Roman Church is sufficient for you to get to heaven while ignoring how your everyday living does not match your confession. And you can be a Baptist and believe your place in heaven is secured because you said the sinner's prayer sometime in your life. While also ignoring that your everyday living does not match your confession. In both cases, in other cases, like those two traditions These are the greatest miscalculations a person can make, because it ends in eternal despair. The sense of connection between the last phrase of verse 3 and verse 4, the first sense of verse 4, these are connected by the word for or because. Verse 4 begins, as it begins, is that one of the reasons why God's commandments are not a burden to us is because we have new natures. Natures that thrive on obedience to God, natures that have now the ability to obey. And this has always been true for God's faithful. He does this for us, Old Testament, New Testament. He enables us to obey. Remember Moses telling the Israelites in Deuteronomy 30, verse 11, quote, Now what I am commanding you today is not too difficult for you or beyond your reach. You can do it. I've enabled you to do it. Now from verse 6, we get a variety of interpretations because of the blood and water. Of course, blood and water flowed from Jesus' side when a spear was stuck in him. But then we have the mention of water baptism by Jesus. And the need to be born both of water and the Spirit, said by Jesus. Now, because of the order of these words here, water and blood, you'll notice the order are switched. The reference of Jesus having a spear stuck in his side, blood and water, as opposed to water and blood And that leads me to prefer interpreting John to be speaking of baptism by Jesus, that is Jesus baptism by water. And then referring this to a metaphorical baptism, if you will, that Jesus is born by water in baptism, and by blood born through suffering. Now, John next in verses 7 and 8, he takes out what I would say are the big guns when it comes to argumentation. He brings out the Trinity. And he notes these are the primary witnesses of the work of Jesus and the nature of Jesus in the flesh. And then he brings up the testimony of creation. He says the spirit, the water, and the blood, these are witnesses also to what Jesus did and who he was. For John and therefore for us, there are no other witnesses needed. No other witnesses are greater, as verse 9 tells us. I want to skip down here all the way to verse 13 and you'll see why. We are told, in summary, the entire theme of John's letter. And I want to read that verse out loud again. Verse 13, the entire theme of John's letter. These things I have written to you who believe in the name of the Son of God, that you may know that you have eternal life. And that you may continue to believe in the name of the Son of God. Know you have eternal life and to continue believing in Jesus' name. This theme, combined with verse 5 of this chapter and all the verses leading to verse 13, We are given the main answer to the most important questions that we have to ask ourselves. Am I saved? Am I a child of God? Am I a true follower of Jesus Christ? And is heaven thus really my hope The answer to all of those questions is found in the social test, the necessity of us loving one another. It is found in the moral test, the necessity of us obeying God's commandments. And it is in the doctrinal test And that doctrinal test is found in verse 5, verse 10, verse 11, verse 12, and verse 13. It is, succinctly, believing on the Lord Jesus Christ as Savior. I have much of what I could talk about to you every Sunday. I can expound on many different things that I have opinions about, or thoughts about, or things that I have read from this pulpit. I can expound on how our culture needs a higher standard of morality. We need to better understand philosophy. We need to have better ethics, better logic. None of that truly matters. All are opinions of men. They may be wise, some, and others not so wise. But the most important thing I could preach to you, nothing else even coming close, is the gospel. The gospel. It is to believe on the Lord Jesus Christ as your Savior. Nothing is as important as that. Perhaps because the message of Christian ministers are to preach is so straightforward. I can't believe this, but perhaps it gets boring to some people. Perhaps they get bored by it. God forbid. Perhaps that is why fads rise up. Consider what competes in the pulpit today. Liberal churches have replaced the gospel with social justice sermons. Of course it is true that social justice issues like police shootings and now negligences, these are tragic on both sides. And of course it is true that there are people in law enforcement that abuse their power. Yes, there are. Yet no marching, no protesting, no slogans, certainly no riots. And no pulpit pounding for greater accountability is going to heal like the gospel can heal. It is only the gospel that can bring about real forgiveness, real healing, and true love by and for our fellow man. Liberal churches have also replaced the gospel with calls to save the planet. These earth-first people are arrogant, arrogant enough to think that mankind can cause climate change While ignoring and even turning their back on the one who created it all. The truth regarding the planet Is that God must be identified as the creator and then as the sustainer of it all, and it is only the gospel. The gospel that will move the hearts of mankind to be better stewards of the earth in relation to their love for God. Anything else is idol worship. Liberal churches have also replaced the gospel with calls for acceptance and equality. Words like acceptance and equality are easy words to throw around because, well, they sound loving initially But when they are applied to accepting accepting sinful behavior, insisting on equality for people, Who want their identity to be wrapped up in their sexual orientation, there is nothing that is loving about such a word Such people become entrapped by their sin, and it is only the gospel that can free them from guilt and shame. And it is only the gospel that can give them an identity that is beyond their sexual desires. For it is the gospel of Jesus Christ that allows them to be called, like you and I are called, children of God. Perhaps because the gospel message demands that we who would follow Jesus Must die to ourselves, picking up our own cross. Perhaps that is why there are modern churches and modern pastors that prefer self-help sermons instead of the gospel. Self-help sermons have pastors preaching about how to have a better marriage, how to have more friends. How to raise kids that don't take drugs. How to become a success at work. How to handle money. And these sermons, I believe, are like Pinterest, for those of you who are on that online pad. Learning about that from my wife. They are like Pinterest because they share a lot of ideas and you can pick and choose which one fits you the best. But such sermons are also very useless unless the gospel is preached. It is possible, I say it again, it is possible to have a better marriage, to have more friends, to raise kids not on drugs To be a success at work, to better handle your money, it is possible to do all of that and lose your soul It is only the gospel that gives eternal purpose to our marriages. It is the gospel that won't just keep our kids off drugs, but give them eternal hope. And the devil has had his hand in moving Christians away from the gospel. Christians have argued over music styles for quite some time now, and while such discussions can be interesting. The most important evaluation when it comes to music in corporate worship is whether or not the message of the gospel is being proclaimed in the words we sing. I thank God for what we sing here. While it is true that music styles can move the spirit of a congregation toward God, Even repel him away from God or something in between. The most important evaluation is whether or not the message of the music is connected to the gospel. The devil has also had his hand in moving Christians away from the gospel by focusing on power struggles within the church. When we focus on who we would like to be in charge and who we don't like that is in charge, The devil has focused our attention off of the gospel and most certainly off of the love we are to have for one another. Power struggles are breaking of the Tenth Commandment. And as John has taught us, to love the gospel is to love God's commandments. In the spirit of St. John's focus on the gospel, on believing in Jesus as the Savior. I ask you to join me in recommitting ourselves to the gospel. The good news of Jesus the Christ is the greatest privilege to believe and proclaim. It is what Jesus told the church to hold on to and never let go. This just in story number three from Spring Hill, Florida. After taking time off recently due to ministry burnout, Pastor's wife, Julie Torrey, returned to her church with a new passion, interpretive dance. Though her husband and someone in the congregation have yet to fully embrace her new ministry, she is committed to, quote, communicating the gospel in the beautiful language of dance and movement. My dance interpretations are as important as the sermon itself, Julie says. They speak to people in a unique way. But husband and pastor Ed Torrey appears to have only grudgingly accepted his wife's new calling. He allows her to take the platform after his sermons to give an interpretive dance about what he just preached about. Her quasi-ballet movements, sachets, and twirls have become a regular, if not especially beloved, feature of each service. People note that the pastor Ed often flips through his sermon notes or bulletin while his wife weaves around the stage. You can tell he's not a big fan of dance, says one church member. But Julie won't hear anything but good things. I quit college so he could follow his ministry calling, she says. Now it's my turn. Some now believe Ed's preaching is increasingly more difficult on topics to try to throw Julie off. He just finished a long series on the Trinity, a mini-series on tithing, and is starting a new one he calls a complex theological study of eschatology. Says one member, it's like he's throwing down the gauntlet and says, interpret that. Interpretive dance during worship, the newest Christian book about a shack, slogan bracelets, oil therapy, incense therapy, or whatever is next. Is not sufficient by themselves, nor are they sufficient combined. The word fad means to busy oneself with trifles. It comes from the phrase fiddle-faddle, which traditionally is used to express what is nonsense. Beloved, the gospel is enough. It is more than sufficient. It is what gives us hope, saves our souls, enables us to forgive, and allows us to truly love and to be loved. Of all the privileges I have at being a pastor, the greatest one is proclaiming the gospel. And so I say, as John would, believe on the Lord Jesus. Let us pray

sermons.title: Pray for the Sinner
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: You have to make your love, you are not. In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. I encourage you to turn to first John chapter five, looking at verses fourteen through sixteen. We will not be going through word by word or verse by verse, but focusing on the general message of this section of Scripture. Consider that prayer. Prayer is the most faithful thing we can do as Christians. Prayer, especially when done in private, is the most faithful act we can perform. It is the most faithful act because there is nothing before our senses. We see nothing that we kneel before. We hear nothing that we talk to. We feel nothing but the pain on our knees, and yet we kneel We bow our heads and we speak in our minds or with our lips. We speak to God. Anyone looking upon us without our knowledge, and if such a person is not a believer, is going to think that we are either foolish or delusional. There is nothing there, they claim. We are talking to air, they insist. And yet, and yet and yet we pray. We pray because we believe. It will be 14 years ago this summer that my family and I attended Bruton Parish in Williamsburg on a summer Sunday. We heard a sermon that I am quite positive didn't last more than 10 minutes, likely barely over five. And the message could be summarized with this statement: it is good to pray. It was a memorable service and sermon for several reasons. The first being that we attended the service in a rain downpour. We had camped out the night before, and this was before computer phones So we didn't know what time the service was scheduled. They had several services on Sunday morning, so we pulled up near the church, and to those of you who have been to Williamsburg, it's a bit aways from the church that you can pull up your car Well we pulled up before the church, and I took it upon myself to run in the pouring rain to see when the next service was scheduled. I am from the Seattle area. We don't have umbrellas in Seattle. But it doesn't rain in Seattle like it does here. Although I was wet when I arrived, I found the schedule, and I started to make my way back to our van And as I was running in to the van in this downpouring rain, the van started to pull away. My van I yelled and I waved my hands to no avail. So I was stranded in the pouring rain. While my wife was driving the family van in a circle. And I see it crossing the road, full of blocks ahead of me. I found out later that she was concerned about the people behind her getting upset that she was taking up so much time and so much space. She felt like she had to take the man back and come back around. And she never saw me running or waving. And when I got back to the van, it was as if I had taken a shower in my Sunday clothes. When we finally attended the service, we had to sit in the balcony because Well, there's not enough room in that parish for a family of eight to sit in the lower pews. So we had to go up to the balcony. And sitting in the balcony means that you're the last one to receive communion. And it just so happened that I was the last one down the stairs, and thus the last one to receive communion, and as I approached, they said Not enough room at the altar. So I had to stand there and wait. And then they ran out of elements. So they had to reconsecrate the elements as I'm standing there soaking wet. And finally when I received the communion elements, I started to walk back. And if you've been in that sanctuary, everything is wood and everything is loud and so every creak, every noise included the squishing of my shoes as I stepped every step, breaking the silence and the prayers of the people as I climbed back up to my balcony seat. And all of this was for the message that it was good to pray. I am aware that because of the mainline Episcopalian Church has a Abandoned the historic Christian faith and thus abandoned Holy Scripture, that that sermon could have been a lot worse than it is good to pray. At least the preacher had it right. It is good to pray. St. John tells us with great confidence that it is good to pray. And he wants his readers to have that same confidence that it is good to pray. We have confidence because of the Son of God, because of Jesus That is what he says in verses 12 and 13, as Jesus is the one who we are to believe in. He is the one we are to trust in. And because of the one whom we are to believe in, we can have confidence when we pray. God wants to hear us. He wants to hear us speak to him, but we must do so in the name of Jesus For it is Jesus who makes us righteous so that we can speak to the Heavenly Father, who again wants to hear us. The confidence that John has is first in Jesus, and then next, next in what we pray, the content of our words. John gives us a very helpful qualifier, and the New King James I think says it better, when he says that if we ask anything, quote, according to his will, God's will, that is the will of the Father. He will hear us. Now, if we had stopped at just Asking anything. If you ask anything, then the Father will hear you. We might think that God would be as a Sears catalog for those who are over 50, a Sears catalog. For those who are younger, a shopping website where you simply need to place your order and whatever your heart desires, you will get it. In James' epistle, you will recall, we have a similar qualifier, as James tells us That we have not, we have not what we want because we ask not. We don't ask of the Lord. And then he says, and then when you do actually ask, you ask out of selfishness That's not, of course, what God wants. Instead, the prayers that the Father readily answers are according to His will. And Jesus left us the perfect example when he prayed, not my will, but thy will be done. Finally, regarding prayer, John wants us to know that God hears us. And we could say God hears us because we pray in Jesus' name, and that is absolutely correct. But we can also say that God hears us again because he wants to hear us. The Heavenly Father wants to be our God. He wants us to call upon Him. He wants us to relate to Him. After all, that is why he gave his son, is it not? He wants us to know him. It is the subject of prayer that then leads John to address two very important topics. The first of which is when a brother or sister in Christ is living in sin The second subject is in regards to the sin that leads to death. We're going to have to hold off on that. Connecting the need for Christians to pray with the unfortunate reality that Christian siblings will find themselves caught up in sin, personal sin. shows the very loving heart of Saint John. Again, all of these apostles are wonderful pastors. When we were children, I want you to consider this. Consider this when you were a child. He found it strangely gratifying. When a peer got into trouble, especially when a sibling was disciplined. If you had siblings growing up, remember that you found some type of satisfaction when your brother or sister got into trouble. Now I noticed this in my children. They quickly, quickly testified against their sibling who was guilty of the wrongdoing. And I often considered how much my children could have gotten away with if they had decided to work together and not turn one another in. It could have been an easy coup d'état. But there seems to be something something about an immature person that wants to see his his or her peers get into trouble. I remember that about myself having four other siblings. I remember being lined up. With my four other siblings and my father investigating who left the iron on. Now growing up we had one of those big irons where you would sit down and it was a rolling type thing and you hit a switch and it would come down and it would roll and and and and and you put your clothes through it as it as it brought it through. And if you left that pad on the iron part, well you'd ruin something very expensive and so someone had done that And he lined us all up. And my sister stepped forward and she said, I cannot tell a lie. She pointed to me and said, He did it. And the problem was, I didn't do it. But within immature minds, it is gratifying when anyone else gets into trouble but ourselves. And unfortunately, and this is a lamenting thing, unfortunately some people don't mature. And still, as adults, enjoy watching their peers get into trouble. And I must speak about the moment, for a moment, excuse me, to the crimes and unrest that has occurred in the city of Baltimore this week. I am politically conservative. No surprise to anybody here But what I have been troubled by is when I hear other conservatives on the radio, television, or on the internet who seem to find some satisfaction in the rioting Because it gives them an opportunity to say, see, I told you so. These people become opportunists regarding those criminals who were also opportunists. They become opportunists by condemning liberal policies in the city, claiming that such policies are the cause of the rioting. Whether the argument has any merit or not is irrelevant because there is nothing to be satisfied about when crime and chaos reign. The mature, those who are sensitive to the Holy Spirit, they mourn with those who mourn. Amen. In the Christian faith, in the Christian church, the mature who have been baptized in the Holy Spirit do not take satisfaction when a Christian sins. Those who would say, see, I I I told you so, when a fellow Christian chooses sin over obedience to God That person is not loving as John has been teaching us to love. And right here, at this moment, I need to Share a personal burden that I have felt since I became an ordained minister, something that I have been sensitive about as I have viewed it in my past ministry. The first church I was called to pastor, the only other church I have pastored, but St. Stephen's. Had an attendance when I arrived at about 20 people on an average Sunday. I was assigned to try to rebuild what had fallen apart. It was a in a parish college, excuse me, it was in a college town, a parish in a college town. It had a nice sanctuary. It had an unattached fellowship hall. It had plenty of office and Sunday school classroom space. It was actually set on a hill, like a church should be The entire city could be viewed from this position. And during its most fruitful days, the parish had just over a hundred people in attendance on Sunday mornings. But the church lost a number of families, and the reason it had lost a number of families was how the core people, the main people, Responded to one another when their children became teenagers. You see, when Christian children become Christian teenagers And Christian young adults, yeah, they make some bad decisions And that was what was happening at this church. Some young people experiment with alcohol. They do, with tobacco, with drugs. premarital sex, and other sins of youth. And that is what happened in this church I am describing. That is what many families endured. And when some of the church youth began these sin experiments, The reaction of the other parents in the church was not to come alongside and support the family with a wayward child. No, no, instead they talked amongst themselves. They gossiped about the family who had a children, a child who had children, a child who was in sin. And soon the family that was struggling with to reign in their child felt alone, unloved, and hopeless. And so they left the church. And not soon after, the parents who were gossiping had to deal with their own wayward child. And that led to another family being gossiped about, and thus another family leaving the church. Well loved this sin The sin of man does indeed occur among us. Sin has and is going to happen among us. Our children, our children, our children are going to choose sin and not obey God. And when they do, when they do. When they do, what is the Christian response to be? And it is not teenagers and young adults only that choose sin. There have been, and there are going to be marriages that are going to become troubled among us. There are going to be fathers among us who act like fools. There are going to be mothers among us who do or say what they should not have said or done. And what is the Christian response to be when these things happen? It is most certainly not to gossip. It most certainly isn't to smirk and say, I told you so. I saw it coming. Instead, the church should be the place where parents can go for help, encouragement, support, and what John is teaching us here, which is prayer. The Christian response toward other Christians who are guilty of choosing sin instead of obedience to God is prayer. Because prayer is good. And the prayer need is simple. It's simple. We are to pray that this person in need, this person in sin, would come to repentance and then would be restored to the church in good fellowship. A Christian practicing the love of God wants those who claim to be Christian to find forgiveness and to find peace with God. Within this encouragement for us to pray for fellow Christians, John then mentions, here it is, the sin that leads to death. The sin that leads to death. And although there is great interest as to what this sin actually is that leads to death, I submit to you that it is quite simple. The sin that leads to death is the same sin that Jesus said is the sin against the Holy Spirit The sin against the Holy Spirit and the sin that leads to death is the denial of the truth of the gospel. Plain and simple. And when I say denies the gospel, I am not referring to someone who says they're a Christian and then goes out and sins. That's a person who's a disobedient Christian They're still believing in God, but they want to go their own way. That is not the sin that leads to death. Let me share this extra biblical story that some of you who took the class on Erasmus will remember. When the Apostle John returned from exile, this is the John who wrote this letter, again, extra biblical story. When he returned from exile, he ministered to a young man in whom he saw great promise. And John left the child with a churchman who had the youth baptized and raised him to know Jesus as his Savior. But when this child was older, he became corrupt with other youth of his age. And then he lived a life of petty theft, running with a gang of bandits and practicing violent deeds. When John returned to check on the boy, the churchman pronounced that he was dead. The boy, the churchman said, was dead to God. When John heard this, he tore his clothes as a symbol of mourning. He heard where the youth was hiding, he quickly got on a horse and rode out to the hot hideout And when John approached the young man, the young man immediately recognized John and he felt shame But John ran after him and he said this, Child, don't fear me. If necessary, I will gladly suffer death and give you my life for yours as the Lord suffered death for us. Stop. Believe Christ has sent me. The young man stopped. He threw down his weapons and he wept bitterly. He then flung his arms around John and he begged for forgiveness. And the story finishes by saying John did not leave the man until through prayer, fasting, and instruction, he was restored to the church. Such a story exemplifies that those who choose sin can be forgiven. They are where our prayers are to be focused. Those who commit the sin that leads to death, they don't need our prayers. And it may sound harsh to say this, but John says that. They do not need our prayers. The sin that leads to death is practiced by people who at one time claimed to believe Jesus as Lord and Savior, and then at another time denied Jesus as the Son of God. And note again, it is not that they start living in sin. No, what they do is specifically and willfully deny who Jesus is and what he did. That's the sin that leads to death. Some of you might have heard of a preacher by the name of Rob Bell. He's been popular in uh certain evangelical circles. He was a pastor of a megachurch, 10,000 members at one time. He uh wrote a few books, a couple of books well known, Velvet Elvis The Sex God. These books were quite popular until he came out in 2011 with a book called Love Wins. And in that book, Bell claimed that he no longer believed in a real hell. Well, his denial of this orthodox doctrine, this caused a great stir, and so in response, he decided to resign as pastor. He then became the spiritual advisor of Oprah Winfrey. Those of you who have heard me teach and speak will know how I feel about Oprah Winfrey. Bell said in an interview from this past February that Oprah has now become his spiritual advisor. Among his new beliefs, Bell now only believes in a Jesus who loves, and get this, not a Jesus that atoned for the sins of mankind. The very heart of the gospel. Bell also said publicly that the Bible is irrelevant to modern-day reality. And I choose to be bold to say that Mr. Bell is an example of sin that leads to death. Such a sin can also be traced to the confessions of Jennifer Story, the current pseudo-bishop presiding of the mainline Episcopal Church. Now it is a temptation to stay on this subject of the sin that leads to death because we can think about all the people that it might apply to, but that's not John's point. The point of John is that Christians, out of love for one another, ought to pray, and more specifically, they are to pray for fellow Christians who are caught up in sin. The love we are to practice towards one another wants to see victory in the lives of one another. We want addictions to be overcome. We want marriages to become stronger. We want children to walk with the Lord and that continually. We want friendships to remain. We want to witness forgiveness and practice it toward one another. We want to see the fruit of the Holy Spirit displayed in one another We want to see Satan under the feet of one another. What do we do when we see a brother or sister in Christ sin? What do we do? We pray. Dear Jesus, deliver my brother, deliver my sister from the bondage of sin Give them victory over their flesh and the devil. Dear Jesus, deliver them. Amen. And all of God's people said. Amen.

sermons.title: Stay away...follow Jesus
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: We now come to the end of our study of Saint John's first epistle. After reading the last verses of St. John's first letter, a letter we have been studying for three and a half months I found myself thinking, going back, back again to the last verse, little children, keep yourselves from idols. It is likely that the verse seemed to be written in bold to me and acted as if it was glaring at me, because while reading through the prophets of the Old Testament for the reading the Bible through a 90 days project, it was repeated over and over again as the primary sin of Israel and the primary sin of Judah. Idol worship. We moderns are tempted to gloss over the sin of idol worship because idols don't exist in the Western world. We don't see anyone, non-Christians included, physically bowing down to images of false gods. Thus it would seem that John's words don't apply to us. That is a lie, and we can know it is a lie because these Christians that John was writing to also were not bowing down to physical images. As we consider the context of this letter and the historical situation that surrounded the audience of St. John We can know that the idols that would tempt them could have been im could not have been images made of wood, stone, or precious metals. Instead, they would have been the same type of idols that tempt the modern world today. And with those, we must include false conceptions of God and false conceptions of Jesus. A few Wednesdays ago, I asked those attending Bible study to brainstorm a list of modern idols that we Christians must guard ourselves against. Money was a general answer, and most certainly is tempting to us. We can too easily put our trust in money and not in God. who is our only true provider. We can falsely think that having money would solve most of our worries. In truth, as so many people who win or earn a great deal of money will testify, new money brings a whole new set of worries and a new set, and that new set includes the selling of your soul. Another idol can be worldly success, very much connected to money Worldly success includes greater positions of power, greater positions of influence, and places of prestige. A person can pursue an advanced degree, for example, to be better able to use the gifts God has given to the greatest extent. Or he or she can pursue the same advanced degree for the praise of men. And the motives can also be mixed. The way to test as to whether worldly success is your idol is to see if your definition for success matches that of God's. Jesus said, we are to seek first the kingdom of God. Jesus said that the last shall be first, and the first shall be last. Jesus said, we are not to parade ourselves before men. Jesus said, Blessed are the poor and the meek. Put those goals in front of you, and worldly success will be an idol smashed. Another idol that is a great temptation for us is the idol of family. There is a reason. Consider that there is a reason, Jesus says, that we are to hate. He used that word, it's the way we translate it in the English. We have to hate our mother, brother, sister, and father if we are going to follow him. To hate, in the context of the words of Jesus regarding the family, is to love less. And the standard we are to love less than, well, that's Jesus. Jesus is to be the height of our love, and all other things in our lives must be loved. less. This might be an awkward topic to bring up on Mother's Day of all Sundays, for we are accepting it as very a very good thing that we honor our mothers. But the mothers worthy of the greatest honor are those who love Jesus. For they show their children and their children's children what is most important. A mother who makes her children the center of her life has made an idol. And John says, keep yourselves from idols. The last idol I will mention, with no attempt to pretend to be exhaustive in listing modern idols, the last idol I identify this morning is a false conception of God and of Jesus. I believe this to be a type of idol, John would have us consider, because He was addressing people who believed God the Father would never send his Son Jesus to exist in the world as in the flesh. Recall when we were just beginning our study of this letter of John's that he needed to address the false teaching that Jesus was never a real man, but only appeared as a real man. To these false teachers, Jesus could not have been made a real human flesh of real human flesh, because they already believed that real human flesh was corrupted. And therefore Jesus, the Son of God, would not join himself to what was corrupted. This type of thinking is what logicians identify as circular reasoning. We accept a premise and then reject a counter-premise based off of the first premise we already believe is true without further examination. Here's the argument. Premise. Human flesh is corrupt. Conclusion. Jesus did not take on a human flesh form. Reason? Human flesh is corrupt. Such reasoning cannot, cannot stand on its own. And while you and I do not have trouble with believing Jesus and putting on human flesh. We too might be guilty of making an idol of a god that does not exist. As an example, consider what happens to the psyche of a Christian who accepts the premise that bad things do not happen to God's people. Now, if bad things do not happen to God's people, and my son gets cancer, or my daughter gets molested. Or my wife is falsely accused of a crime, or I myself get beat up on the street, then I am at a crossroad. I am at a crossroad because cancer, molestation, false accusations, and getting beat up. Those are bad things. I am forced to conclude that either God didn't keep his promises to me, or I am not a child of God. Either conclusion leaves my soul empty, hopeless, angry, and eventually bitter, very bitter. Of course, the whole problem is that my first premise, that nothing bad happens to God's people, well, that was false. God never promised such a thing. And such a promise does not come close to how Jesus warned his followers when he said that he himself would suffer, and that afterward his disciples would suffer. The premise that bad things do not happen to God's people does not match with what happened to the disciples and what happened to the to the many martyrs of the Christian faith after them, and continues to happen to martyrs today in the Middle East There is a reason, beloved. A reason that God will wipe away our tears. There is a reason for our crying. There's a reason why God will wipe away our tears when heaven is realized. Tears will be wiped away because, because there will be no more children lost and mothers lost during childbirth. There will be no more cancer. There will be no more birth defects. There will be no more rape. There will be no more murder. There will be no more abuse of any kind. There will be no more rioting. There will be no more injustices by judges or juries. There will be no more fear of sin, and certainly in the end, no fear of death. It has been a number of years that I have shared the following story from this pulpit, so I think it is time to share it again Sharing it in the context of making for ourselves a false image of God. When I was in my early twenties and serving as a youth minister in Kennewick, Washington, at a mid-sized Nazarene parish. I also found myself ministering to newly married couples and young families, even though I was their peer. And no, please, understand, please, that at that time I had no formal theological training, for I I had yet to attend seminary. In fact, it was the following encounter that was that played a part in motivating me to get formal training. Bobby Lynn and I were at the home of a young couple for a meal and fellowship. The young couple was married as long as we had been, about two years. They had a young child, as we did. After swapping fun stories, the conversation got serious as they've opened up to us that they were not doing well intimately. Now again, I was green about such matters myself, so my head was spinning a bit when the conversation started to go the direction it was going. The gist of their concern was that the young wife did not want to be intimate with her husband because she was and always had associated intimacy with violence. And she knew why she associated intimacy with violence. It was because she was raped when she was 15 years old. She told a heartbreaking story about how she had given her life to Jesus when she was around 12 years old, and she took her faith very seriously. She would have never found herself in a situation where she could have been raped, but her older sister was to take care of her while her parents were out of town one weekend. This older sister took her to a party where there was drinking and drugs. This put the young girl in a terrible situation that was taken advantage of by A boy three years, her elder, a rapist. She shed tears while telling us this story, and then asked me a direct question. Where was Jesus when I was being raped? I trust You would understand why I emphasized that I had had no formal training in theology or counseling to reference to reference how I should answer such a question But the Holy Spirit was enough. I said, or the Holy Spirit said to the young woman, Jesus was being raped with you. I remember my answer so vividly because, number one, I knew it was not for me. And number two, it was so very profoundly true. You see, the false image of Jesus is that nothing bad happens to those who believe in him and follow him. The true image of Jesus is that he suffers with us when we suffer. He does not leave us alone, but suffers with us, cries with us, and prays for us. And that truth, as I just stated, good people, that truth, that truth heals. It heals. It breaks down false idols and heals. If you have suffered and all the while wondered where Jesus was, The footprints in the sand poem, it's very good. But it is healing to know that Jesus was with you and therefore suffered with you, and thus he knows you. He truly knows you. At the heart of the young woman's mistrust and confusion was the lack of confidence that Jesus that Jesus actually loved her. Cared for her, and wanted the best for her. Her confidence in her relationship with God was greatly damaged by her expectations upon God that were not met. But the God that she worried about and had lost confidence in was not the true God who made heaven and earth It was not Jesus the Christ, Son of the Living God. It was instead an idol. It was a God she had imagined, and not the God who reveals himself. As I have repeated in these sermons from 1 John, the main goal is for Christians to be confident. confident in their God, confident in Jesus, confident in their salvation. That confidence is to be gained by going through a series of tests we've been examining. To be sure we have the Holy Spirit that it's dwelling within us, which means it's empowering us to overcome sin and to know the voice of God. to know the voice of God. In fact, the word know is a very important word for John. He wants us to know, as he says in chapter 5, verse 13. To know we have eternal life. The two primary verbs meaning to know in the Greek occur almost 40 times in this letter. Also occurring many times in the Gospel of John. John wants Christians to know, to know they have eternal life, to have confidence in our relationship with God. To know that heaven is our eternal home. Even that word confidence is used in this chapter, verse 14. John wants us to be certain of things, the most important of things. And the tests, if you will, are summarized here at the end of John's letter. The first one, we are to love one another. And that was last described in the manner of praying for a brother and sister andor sister in Christ who is in sin. We described this last week The second test to know we are born again is when we keep ourselves from sinning. Verse 18 here in chapter 5. As we discussed earlier, John does not mean that Christians do not continue to sin, but that a Christian is no longer defined by sin. Because Christians are born of God, there has been in them a decisive and clear, evident break with the nature of sin. The new birth changes all parts of the life of a Christian, and that includes morally. The sin that leads to death does not trouble a believer. You don't need to pray for that, we learned from John. And this is also why the wicked one, the devil, cannot touch us. For our new nature is born of Jesus, and Jesus has placed the devil under his feet, and therefore under our feet. In contrast, of the new nature of Christians is the sway and influence the devil has upon the world. And here is the great ironies that only Christians can see and thus know. While the ungodly would see us as delusional, even psychologically broken. The truth is quite different. Sigmund Freud made the argument that Christians show symptoms of obsessive-compulsive disorder, because many practice rituals. But it is the unbeliever who is delusional. People honestly believe that they are captains of their own fate. They honestly believe that. When in fact They are servants of the devil. They are in his grip and under his control. The Bible reminds us that for a time this is his world, the devil's world. At least it is his world from the standpoint of those who continue to belong to him and are thus subject to him. Notice, please, that St. John says the world lies. It's its posture. It lies in the power of the evil one. The ungodly world has a posture of surrender and even relaxation. It is lying down. It is not struggling to break free. It is content to serve the devil. I cannot help but remember when I read this passage how arrogant atheist can be in their condemnation of the religious. How confident they are that it is the Christian who is the fool because we deny what is empirically evident to them They speak as though they see clearly when in truth there is a spiritual world of deception that continues to call them to not look behind the curtain, to not see the that the wizard is a fraud. The third and final test was doctrinal. We who are Christian, we who are Christian are to believe that Jesus came in the flesh, that he was born of water, born of blood, both necessitating flesh. That is the truth that John speaks about in verse 20. We are to know him who is true. And what is true about Jesus was that he was fully God and fully man. He was and is fully divine and fully flesh. And so here we we come back around to the last verse. Little children, keep yourselves from idols. Through these tests, through the messages of these tests, we are to conclude that anything else, anything else is idol worship. And when we know that, can we not better see how those who insist that they can marry their own gender and still follow Jesus are under the spell of the devil and are presently worshiping the idol of immorality. And can we now better understand that those who can espouse hate of their fellow man, while claiming themselves followers of Jesus, are blinded by the devil as they worship an idol of disingenuous love. And we now better recognize that those who want to redefine who Jesus is so that he fits who they want him to be are fooled by the devil over and over again and are worshiping an idol that they wish. was God. Indeed. We can see better, understand better, recognize better. Because God in Jesus for us makes all things new John ends with a warning against idols because anything can be an idol to us. And because anything can be an idol to us, we can only stay away from idols By following Jesus. And so I end with a commission to you Tell someone who does not know Jesus that's truth this week. Everything else is an idol. And the only way to stay away from idols is to follow Jesus. Tell them They need to follow Jesus. Amen

sermons.title: Share the Faith
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: May the words of my mouth and the meditation of our hearts be acceptable in thy sight, O Lord, our strength and our redeemer. In the name of the Father, Son, and the Holy Ghost. Amen. Be seated. They've just finished St. John's first epistle, so we're in a bit of a transition period. Which brought me up to this Sunday during confirmation class, I try to cover as much material as I Possibly can regarding the fundamentals of the Christian faith. And this year I I find that I'm running out of Sunday. So I will not be able to get to the lesson I give in confirmation about sharing your faith. About Teaching one another what Jesus has done for mankind, the gospel, sharing the gospel, sharing the good news of Jesus Christ. But my inability to get to that lesson is a benefit for us because it puts me in this position this morning, trusting in God's providence, to preach about sharing our faith today. I also believe it is a great benefit to the health of God's people When preachers cover the basics of the Christian faith every so often, so that we keep those basics ever before us, always practicing them The basics would be our individual prayer lives, personal Bible reading Family devotions, the giving of our tithes and our offerings, serving according to our gifts, and sharing our faith. With people that God has placed in our lives. Forgive me for a brief testimony about my experiences. When the Lord got a hold of me in the middle of my senior year in high school, my friends would say something to this effect. There is definitely something different about you, but I am not going to ask what it is because I don't want to be preached at. I don't know how many people become Christian because someone preaches at them. Probably not that many. I tried a few times to get my friends to come to Christ using the second-hand method There was a Billy Graham crusade that took place in the Tacoma Dome in the spring of 1983. I invited a number of people, but only two would go with me They did not respond to the call to come down to the floor and receive Jesus. Later I took my best friend Jay to a Silver Wings concert. Anybody remember the group Silver Wings? Nobody remembers Silver. They were a very evangelical group and after a series of numbers, songs, they asked If there was anybody in the audience that wanted to know Jesus to stand up, well I had already uh Come to the Lord, or if the Lord came to me, so uh I wanted though my friend Jay to stand up so badly that I thought, well, I'll go ahead and stand up and that will make him feel more comfortable Well he never stood up and so I sat back down. I invited friends to church worship services with the hope that they would hear the gospel there and become Christian I even missionary dated. For those of you who are not in the know, missionary dating is when a Christian dates a non-Christian with the hope of that relationship leading the person To a relationship with Christ, becoming a Christian. I don't recommend missionary dating. The girl I dated went to worship services with me, but She never gave her life to Jesus. She then broke up with me in the middle of my freshman year in college. And I was a sad sack, if there ever has been one. My first semester in college resulted in my girlfriend breaking up with me, contracting mono, and getting poor grades. I had not walked with Jesus but a whole year, and I found myself a very poor Christian witness. And regarding my sharing of the gospel, you will notice that I did not do much one-on-one sharing. I didn't really do any. I stayed with the second-hand approach, bringing people in my life to these events with the hope that someone else would share the gospel and I could come along and support them. Please understand that I don't think that there is anything inherently wrong with secondhand sharing. There's nothing wrong with inviting people in our lives to church to hear the gospel. Just like we want to invite people to our homes to meet our families because we love our families, so too we can feel that way about our church, and we invite people to church because we want them to experience what we love. perfectly understandable and reasonable and helpful. But all of us should be able to, if the opportunity provides itself, to be able to share one-on-one the gospel. My first parish-sponsored ministry was to college students. And I remember a young coed asking me a fairly direct question that went something like this. Why do I need to believe in Jesus anyway? Why do I need to believe? Now that might sound like a softball question, but what she was getting at was that she didn't understand the concept of original sin. Nor did she understand personal sin, that she had personal sin that needed to be dealt with. Because her thinking didn't include sin and the need for Jesus, then didn't make sense to her. And so Such a topic as sharing your Christian faith, sharing the gospel with another human being, begs the question, where do you begin? The best tool I have ever been given to share my faith, and thus I pass it along to all who are who are part of our confirmation class and new members class Is the tool called the Roman robe. Following the basics in the Book of Romans to share how to come to Christ. The Roman road is a series of verses to memorize, or just you just have to memorize the numbers, to memorize so that anyone who can communicate will be able to communicate the gospel to inquiring souls. It is a referencing of choice verses from St. Paul's letter to the Church at Rome that quickly and simply communicates the fundamentals, the fundamentals of the gospel. So look with me, if you would, at these verses. The first one, the first stop on the Roman road is Romans 1, verse 20. Romans chapter one, verse twenty. First stop on the Roman road. I'm reading this from the NIV. For since the creation of the world, God's invisible qualities, his eternal power, and divine nature have been clearly seen. being understood from what has been made, so that people are without excuse. So that people are without excuse. The verse confirms first that the world was created I don't know if there are those of you who keep up scientifically with what's going on and what's being proposed recently, but modern scientific theory has decided in a new belief regarding the origins of the universe and thus the the earth, and that it is, this is their conclusion, it has always been there. Always eternally been there. No Big Bang, just always been there. Even though the universe is expanding, which clearly indicates that it had a beginning point. Scientists have not liked where the belief in the earth having a beginning point leads to. They don't like that it leads to some saying that the cause was God. So they are willing now to say that it has always been there. And they say their conclusions are based on science. The verse next confirms that evidence of God creating the world is seen, is seen in nature. Such evidence has been called natural law. You can look at the world as creation, you can look at what it communicates, and you can come to some conclusions. The evidence could be the awe that nature gives us when we stare at its grandeur. The evidence could be the position of the earth within the solar system. It is perfectly placed. perfectly tilted, perfectly rotating with perfect gravitational pull, providing the ability for there to be life and life abundant. The evidence could also be the wisdom and causality, as we recognize that that which exists Must exist by some other cause or by the necessity of its own nature. And the earth cannot exist by its own nature. So it must have had an outside agent that brought it into being. Any of these evidences leads us to conclude that God created all that we See all that we hear, all that we taste, all that we touch, all that we smell, everything that we experience. Finally, the verse confirms That the created order evidence around each human being leaves them no excuse to disbelieve or ignore God. We are forced by nature to acknowledge him and then realize we will stand before him, whether we acknowledged him or not. Alright, that's our first stop. Let's go to our second stop. Walking down the road, we come to Romans 3. 23. 3. 23, read this morning, the second stop, second verse on the Roman road, Romans 3. 23. For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God. All sin and all fall short. Now, this passage presents the main problem with humanity. What is our problem? All members of mankind are sinners. The word sin in the Koine Greek means to fall short or to miss the mark. The next question, what have we fallen short of? What have we missed as a mark? Well, that's perfection. We are short of perfection. We fall short of perfectly obeying God's law. Now, this one is not too difficult to explain because people with any type of self-awareness at all must admit that they fall short. They must admit that they sin even if they don't believe in God and thus don't believe in God's law. They have to admit that they fall short because they have not lived up to even their own expect expectations of themselves. Even what we expect of ourselves we don't live up to. Thus we fall short. It is very rare, rare indeed. That you will find a human being who is not carrying around a sense of guilt. Whether it be for breaking God's law, man's law, or what we expect of ourselves, we walk around with guilt. Sigmund Freud recognized that guilt was a major flaw in the human psyche, and this caused him to come up with several theories that would rid humanity of guilt. But it is more, we know, than a mental problem. It is a plague on the entirety of the human condition that cannot be taken away by man. Now before I go on from this, I want to briefly mention original sin and personal sin and their differences. Original sin is what we inherit from Adam. Adam sinned, and because he was the original man, sin started with him. And so he passed it down to every one of his descendants. But he does not pass it down via genetics. There is no sin gene that can be surgically removed or scientifically corrected We are under the covenant God made with man at creation. Adam is our covenant head, and therefore we inherit the covenant of death that comes from Adam. For those who are tempted to say that such an arrangement seems a bit unfair Please remember that as sinful humanity, we are in no position to state what is fair or what is just Next to original sin is personal sin, and I've mentioned it briefly. Personal sins are actions and thoughts that go against God's moral law. God has a standard he requires of all human beings to live by, and anything less than those standards is falling short, and thus we call it sin. And we need not take much time to examine ourselves to come to the conclusion that each of us is guilty of personal sin. With original sin, we have a problem, and with personal sins, we have many other problems. And so we've got to keep going on the road. So our next verse, our next stop on the Roman road is Romans chapter 6, verse 23. Romans 6, 23. For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus, our Lord. I ask rhetorically if there really can be so much packed into a short verse such as this. We have just examined the fact of our guilt, but we had yet to mention the punishment of our guilt for both original sin and personal sin. We recall from Genesis, do we not, the story of what God promised Adam, what would happen if he ate of the forbidden fruit. Well, death. Adam and the punishment was death for every man, woman, and child. And that death is twofold, at least, twofold. We are first dead in spirit. Because of the original sin of Adam and our place under his covenant, we are dead spiritually. We are dead to God. Our ears don't know his voice. Our eyes do not see his evidence. Our wanderings are in a crypt. Even though we think we are alive, we are among the dead. Recall that Jesus spoke to the Pharisees in this same manner. They thought that because they were children of Abraham, because they were keepers of the traditions, that they of all people could conclude that they were alive. But because they could not trust nor believe in Jesus, even after they saw his miracles, well they showed very clearly that they were dead. The second way we are under the curse is in the body. The curse of death included the necessity of us physically dying. To dust we shall return. And not only are each of us cursed to physically die, we are also limited to the years that we can live. With no access to the tree of life, our years are cut short, our bodies grow weak, tired, and frail. Some of us know that better than others. Well, thankfully, the verse does not leave us dead in spirit or in body, for it gives us the good news. Here it is, the gospel. It tells us that God has given mankind a gift. And that gift is eternal life as opposed to death. And eternal life is found in Christ Jesus. And this part of the verse is related to that other verse in the Bible that is packed with so much truth. John 3. 16. There we are told that God loved and therefore he gave, he gave us Jesus Jesus is the sufficient gift for eternal life because he paid the penalty for our sin, both original sin and every one of our personal sins. Every one Because Adam was our covenant head under death, Jesus becomes our covenant head to life. Jesus is then called the new Adam or the second Adam. All that believe in him now come under his covenant, the covenant of Jesus. No longer under the covenant of Adam, but under the covenant of eternal life. That is good news. I remember well The day my now wife, Bobby Lynn, said she would marry me, that was good news. I remember when I was told that I was going to have a child, and then another, and then another. And then another. And then another. It was all good news. And then to be told it's a boy? Five times? It's good news. And then, the precious little girl, good news. And then asked to be a pastor in Maryland, good news. But none of it compares, none of it compares to the good news that God gave Jesus as a gift for my sins. That I could be forgiven and heaven could be my hope. Nothing comes close to that. And I could not say that with greater sincerity than I'm saying it now. Nothing comes close. Everything else that was good news in my life only makes sense because Jesus is my Lord and my Savior. Well we cannot stop here on the Roman road. We've got to keep going. We've heard the good news of Jesus, but we haven't done anything yet to apply that good news to our lives. And so we must continue. Our next stop is Romans 10, verse 9. Romans chapter 10, verse 9. Verse nine. Here it says, What you can do if you declare with your mouth Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead You will be saved. Upon hearing this verse, I think the most appropriate response should be, What? That's all I need to do? You mean to tell me that all is that is needed of me is to confess that Jesus is Lord and believe in my heart, the very core of who I am, that God raised him from the dead, and I will be saved from death and hell? Such questions and wonder are appropriate responses because it is. It truly is remarkable. That is all that is required of any person that wants to have their sins forgiven and who wants heaven to be their home. Now once you have brought a person to the end of this road, Romans 10, 9, you will likely get questions. And this is where most people get nervous. This is where most people, they're looking for that exit sign to get off the Roman road. This is where you wish you were at church or in the office of your pastor so that he can answer the questions that you are afraid of On the one hand, such a concern is reasonable, it's understandable. However, you need not feel fear, for the Holy Spirit is within you And he does not give you a spirit of timidity. You can be brave, for even if you are asked a question that is difficult, There is great effect in admitting that you don't know the answer, but you will help the person find the answer. Such a response shows that you are honest, that you are humble, two qualities the world so desperately needs to see. But the questions most people get after sharing the Roman road have to deal with whether or not God can truly forgive all sins. Some people see themselves as bad, bad sinners who are way past the ability to be redeemed. Some people are so down on themselves because their sins have hurt so many people that they truly don't forgive themselves and have found a bit of catharsis in beating up themselves emotionally When such a person might not be ready for forgiveness, that that can happen But it is within us to answer those questions those who question us in this manner, can God truly forgive all sins We can answer that with confidence. Yes, God can forgive all sins and any number of sins. God not only can, he has, and he does, and he wants to forgive the greatest of sinners among mankind. Believe that. Now you might be thinking to yourself, right now, thinking to yourself, this sounds pretty easy. The Roman road sounds maybe too easy to use to share the gospel. I respond by saying it is easy. Just as easy as it is to come to Jesus and have your sins forgiven, so too it is easy to share the gospel using the Roman road. Now, of course, you don't have to use the Roman road. You can use whatever method you want to. As long as it confirms that there is a God. And that mankind has broken his law and suffered spiritual death. And because we are spiritually dead, we need a Savior to make us alive. And it is Jesus, and only Jesus who is that Savior. And to receive forgiveness from the hope of heaven, they simply must confess and believe. As long as you have all of that down, you're good to go. And before I close this morning I also recognize that some of you might wonder, what about repentance and baptism? After all, that is what St. Peter said when he was asked, what shall we do to be saved? Repent and be baptized. Well, confessing and believing, as Paul says in Romans 10, 9, that is repenting. For it is saying that I was wrong, and now I know. And baptism, well, a person who confesses that Jesus is Lord and believes that God has raised him from the dead, that person is ready for baptism. So next, bring such a person to the church, and we will baptize him or her or them. Tell them, and tell them, now you know what to say. Now you know or are reminded on how to share your faith. So what's the next thing to do? Go share it. Let us pray.

sermons.title: Let us start with wisdom
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Be seated. Today we began a study on the book of Proverbs. I have hesitated to preach from the book of Proverbs because I have previously thought that it did not contain the gospel, and therefore I need not preach from it. Three years ago I took the challenge of studying the book of Proverbs in a Sunday school class. And lo and behold, it became one of the more profound studies I had done. And within it, we found the gospel. And thus we found Jesus. All such discovery encouraged me that I could preach a series of sermons from the book of Proverbs. As a whole, I will say, for preparation for us That you and I are going to hear great wisdom. And by great wisdom I mean not an unearthly profound wisdom, but a wisdom that is so obvious and helpful for everyday living. Part of a minister's responsibility, calling, is to become aware of the secret sins of his people. is also to know and recognize the public sins as well. And what I have concluded over the years is that many Christians get into trouble in their lives because of those secret sins and because of those public sins, but even aside from sins, because of foolish decisions that they make in their lives. Even though we talk of all things becoming new for a person who received Jesus as his or her Lord and Savior, such a newness does not mean that that person All of a sudden becomes wise. For Christians who have walked many years with our Lord and Savior, And you know that each time that they confess their sins before the Lord, that all things become new for them, yet even for them. They make foolish decisions. They are not always wise. It is true. The people go along in life receiving one, seemingly, one bad break after another, with no apparent reason for those bad breaks. A person gets lung cancer and she's never smoked a day in her life. A person gets into an auto accident when doing absolutely nothing wrong on the road. A person can get a broken heart because of a lost love when he or she was always faithful and always loving. And these things happen, and we don't know why, and reasons for such tragedies as tribulations, trials, those reasons will remain a mystery until we get to the other side of eternity. And then there are events. Difficult, painful, and trying events that happen in the lives of people that are caused. Caused by their own foolishness, plain and simple. One of my favorite examples Is the city of New Orleans and Hurricane Katrina, now ten years ago While it was indeed a terrible catastrophe, with many people losing their lives and many more people losing their property. It remains baffling, truly baffling, that people would build a city below sea level And build it in a gulf that is perfect for funneling hurricanes. I imagine that when people Question, why would God allow such a tragedy to happen? I kind of imagine God sitting up there saying, why would you build a city below sea level? But that is foolishness on a big scale. What we need to address is foolishness on a smaller day-to-day scale. Proverbs addresses subjects like a good work ethic versus a bad or poor work ethic, respecting other people's property. Avoiding lust of the flesh. Avoiding unnecessary confrontations. Raising your children to fear the Lord Controlling your temper, telling the truth, being aware of flatterers, being wise with your money, and much, much more. And we need this day-to-day type of wisdom if our lives are going to reflect the Savior. And if we are going to be a people that are happy and free from the worries that bog so many down who do not know the Lord What Proverbs will also teach us in general is that little-used virtue of personal responsibility. Personal responsibility. It will show us how we need to own our own sins. Own our own failures. It will show us how one foolish decision or action leads to another one and then leads to another one and we can trace back where it all went wrong from the beginning and take full responsibility. Now, before we look at specific verses from Proverbs, I need to give you a few caveats. Caveat number one. Proverbs are not promises. Say it again. Proverbs are not promises. Too often people will read a verse such as from Proverbs 22. 6. You're familiar with this one. It says, Train up a child and the way he should go, and when he is old, he will not depart from it. And when they hear that verse, they hear a promise. But there is no promise made Most of the proverbs we will read are maxims or general truths and therefore are not definite, not definite, but instead are true most of the time. Underlying most of the time. The second caveat: some proverbs appear to contradict each other. What we can be sure of is that the contradictions are intentional. It's not as if they weren't aware that they were contradicting each other. When, for example, we are told in Proverbs 26, verse 4, it reads, Do not answer a fool according to his folly, or you yourself will be just like him. And then the verse following, Proverbs 26, verse 5, answer a fool according to his folly, or he will be wise in his own eyes. Notice the proximity of these contradicting verses. That is purposeful. Those who have lived life long enough in this world know that sometimes you need to expose the foolishness of a fool, and so you answer him. And then other times the fool is going on and on so much that if you say anything, you're just joining in with his foolishness, and so you remain quiet. The writers of these Proverbs recognize life's different contexts. Proverbs Proverbs is not situational ethics. Proverbs is situational application. And so we have, in such a situation, as answering a fool. There's also another example that I recall when I was raising my children, we had a rule, no screaming in the house. Because with five under five, screaming could occur a lot. And it disturbed the peace of the home. And so no screaming. But of course In the case of a house fire, screaming is allowed. And the wise recognize different contexts. In the final caveat, I hope you notice that I said writers, as if there is more than one author of these proverbs. And so there is. But the majority of this wisdom was recorded by King Solomon, son of King David. He was the great king of Israel who asked the Lord for wisdom, and God was so pleased by his servant that he gave him wisdom and much, much more. And these verses then are primarily proverbs given to the children of the king, so that they might live life abundantly. And so, and so the King of Kings has them here for us, so that we too might live life abundantly. We will start off this morning going through the first part of chapter one, but understand that this this overview Excuse me, this series is going to be actually studying themes and not particular blocks of passages. But today we start in chapter 1, verses 1 through 6. The verses are an introduction to the book by praising wisdom. It is necessary to remember that as we sit on this side of the resurrection, on this side of the ascension, on this side of the coming of the Holy Spirit, Pentecost Sunday today Our Lord Jesus Christ, wisdom is to be revered and practiced as we are living out our salvation. This is in no way to be understood as gaining our salvation. We are not wise to be saved. We are wise in our salvation. So there is no moralizing going on in Proverbs. We should consider that wisdom, as it is described in this book, is similar to the character of the Holy Spirit. And appropriate to say on Pentecost Sunday, for the Holy Spirit guides us into all truth, and wisdom guides us into truth. The Holy Spirit teaches us to love justice, to love mercy, to walk humbly before God, as does Proverbs. Wisdom in human life is the skill of bringing the mental idea of godliness and righteousness to our life in a beautiful manner so that our thought and our speech and our behavior resembles our Savior. Consider, please, some of the most obvious benefits of living wisely. Number one, if you live wisely, you can avoid unnecessary trials Let's say that a young man is wise and he decides that he's going to get a job and in that job he's going to get up early and be on time every day and he's going to do exactly what his supervisor tells him to do And so he lives that way for years, and he finds himself stable in a good job providing for his family. Just being wise in getting up, being on time, and submitting. Number two, being wise has the benefit of being a good witness to the world. The world sees us, it watches us, and then sees us speak at the right times and be quiet at the right times. It sees us work hard at the right times. We are joyful in the right ways. We are true to our commitments and we are consistent in our convictions. And when unbelievers see that, well, they want what we have, and of course what we have is Jesus Number three, using godly wisdom aids to the salvation of our children. AIDS to the salvation of our children. You know, there is a reason why St. Paul warned parents not to exacerbate their children. He warns in such a manner because parents can be too hard on their children. And parents can also hover too much over their children. And this could lead, this being too hard or hovering, could lead to a child resenting their parents and thus resenting God. Proverbs also provides wisdom on how to guide our children away from the common sins of mankind. One of the chief goals, and I'm sure you parrots have the same, is to keep our children away from the scars of life And sometimes those scars are absolutely necessary. The Holy Spirit has to give them in order for our children to mature But then there are unnecessary scars, unnecessary trials that we want to help our children avoid. And Proverbs helps us do that. Number four, wisdom gives us opportunities to simply help our fellow man. Christian brothers and sisters, as well as secular friends, need the wisdom of God. Many of these proverbs apply to God-fearing and non-God-fearing alike. We have wisdom to offer the world. Number five, and this is my last one on the list. The benefits of wisdom, happiness, and fruitfulness in our lives. Happiness and fruitfulness. I can honestly look back after having studied this wonderful book of Proverbs and conclude that if I had applied some of its wisdom in specific circumstances I would not have had so much trouble in particular relationships. If I would have applied some prints some of these simple principles, I could have better battled personal temptations And here's something to remember. Much of happiness in this life is achieved by simply staying out of trouble. And Proverbs helps us do that. In chapter 1, verse 7, we find why this book is set apart from the rest of worldly wisdom. While the pagan world can offer sage advice, only the Holy Scripture instructs us to fear the Lord. In the Bible, to fear the Lord means unconditional reverence for and surrender to the Lord. It is a basic attitude of willing submission in the heart based on the nature of the living God. And the covenant he has made with us, the salvation he promises us by his grace. Truly, fearing the Lord is what separates sinners and saints. And we can understand what fearing the Lord means by stating what it is not. It is not acting cowardly before God. It is not believing that God wants to squish us like a bug when we sin. No, it is being in awe of him It is being in awe that he would even consider us, that he would love us, that he would save us, that he would want the best for us. What is man, O Lord, that thou art mindful of him? Because Proverbs works upon us from within, the heeding of such wisdom in fearing God forms a character that pleases God. And in verse 8, we are taught that fearing the Lord is directly connected to having reverence for our parents. And so much of society's ills today are because of the breakdown of the family. And a major factor in the breakdown of the family is a lack of reverence children have for their parents.
