We acknowledged how difficult it can be to see others who are downcast, and yet the wisdom of God says That it is better to make people who are downcast your company than to be around prideful people It is better to be downcast yourself, regardless of how painful such lowly emotions can be, than to be caught up in pride. The sin of pride is that dangerous. From Proverbs 29, verse 23. A man's pride will bring him low But the humble in spirit will retain honor. Contemplate how you and I are drawn to root for the underdog. In a competition when the expected winner displays pride. A man's pride will bring him low Because he will be found to be wanting in some area of his life, and all who dislike him will be disgusted by his display of pride, and they will rejoice in his embarrassment. And the second part of the proverb speaks about retaining honor. Honor is hard to gain and very, very easy to lose It takes only one act of foolishness to destroy a person's reputation, regardless of how many good deeds precede that one foolish act. When a person has a humble spirit, people are much more willing to forgive, wanting to forget. People tend to root for the humble and therefore want the humble to retain their honor. We want honorable people, just not arrogant ones. But what does a humble spirit look like? What does a humble-spirited person look like? What does he or she do that reflects a humble spirit? Well, a humble-spirited person does not seek his or her own. The concern of a humble-spirited person is the honor of others A humble-spirited person defers to others. Others go first. Others get the credit. Others' needs are first. A humble-spirited person is always checking his or her motivation. Motivation matters to those who walk in the footsteps of the Lord Jesus. A humble-spirited person is described in the parable Jesus told of the wedding feast. You remember, he says, when you go to this wedding feast, do not take the position of authority or privilege. But sit way back, as if you're of no importance, and allow the person who is giving the wedding to call you forward. That is the humble life. To assume the low position. And if you are ever elevated, allow it to be, but always assume the lower position. It is an act of the will to place oneself in a low position We next consider a more well-known proverb on pride. This is from Proverbs 16, verse 18. Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall. Now this verse is often misquoted, truncated to pride goes before a fall. And that version of it is still true. But the sequence of the entire proverb is important. One thing goes before another, because the first thing is the cause of what follows. If a spirit of humility does what we just described, then a haughty spirit does the opposite. A haughty spirit seeks selfish honor. A haughty spirit considers self first. A haughty spirit has a motivation of being rewarded by men. They want to be rewarded by men. A haughty spirit is so very vile to our God The Jesus directly confronted the Pharisees about their personal pride numerous times In fact, it could be argued that Jesus was not put to death because he claimed himself to be divine, which was the excuse the Pharisees gave. No, it could be argued that Jesus was put to death because of the pride of the Pharisees. Jesus humbled the Pharisees in public. And instead of acknowledging the sin of pride, they increased it all the more, resulting in being overcome by jealousy, envy, and bitterness. Now this next proverb overtly states how detestable pride is in the eyes of God. We read it as our first reading From Proverbs 6. These things the Lord hates. Yes, seven are an abomination to him. A proud look, a lying tongue, hands that shed innocent blood, a heart that devises wicked plans, feet that are swift to running to evil, a false witness who speaks lies speaks lies. And one who sows discord among the brethren. And I argue that the linchpin connecting all of these sins is that first one on the list, pride. Pride. Personal selfish pride. But what is a proud look? We might think we know what a proud look is. A well-dressed woman who sticks her nose back, looking down upon people, we say that's the look of pride A man tilts his head, no expression on his face, acts like he doesn't have a care in the world. Looks like a the sin of pride on his face. But the expression proud look is more of a temper of the mind. Which then can be expressed in face and posture. The lofty look is the indication of swelling pride that has filled the heart It is then the heart that a person has within them a supreme disdain for everything and everybody Consider that the pride listed in this list here first, because it is at the bottom of all the disobedience and rebellion against God's law from the beginning. And as humility is the basis of virtue for the Christian, so pride is the basis of the devil's nature We read elsewhere in Scripture that the face of the Lord is against selfish pride. He resists the proud. He knows them afar off. Instead, God has respect for the lowly. He brings down high looks. He judges those that are high in their own minds. It is against a proud spirit that Job prays to God, quote, to behold everyone that is proud and abase him, and to look upon everyone that is proud and bring him low. Job 40. Well, next in Proverbs we learn how to combat selfish pride. This is from Proverbs 15. The fear of the Lord is the instruction of wisdom, and before honor is humility. And from this we must ask, why must humility necessarily come before honor? Consider that true honor can only come from God. And before God lifts us up, he requires us. To have humility. The proverb also mentions fearing the Lord. And modern Christians are not so much comfortable as talking about fearing the Lord, not as Christians of our past. But the Christian life, as we have noted many times, is a life of tension. And we have tension between fearing God, a God who can throw our bodies and souls into hell. And loving him as a friend. When you treat the proverb as a parallelism, you can see that fear is humility and honor is wisdom. The principle of pride versus humility is also stated slightly different in Proverbs 18, verse 12. Before destruction, the heart of a man is haughty, and before honor is humility. And the emphasis is the same as the proverbs already mentioned, but in contrast to the alternative There is a domino effect regarding the path we choose to take. To go the route of haughtiness is to go the route of destruction. To go the route of humility is to go the route of honor. And whether the results occur in this life or the next does not change what we believe this to be true. From Proverbs 22, verse 4. By humility and fear of the Lord are riches and honor and life. Here again we have humility and the fear of God going hand in hand. Humility, fear of God. The following Happy consequences of humility are riches and honor and life, spiritual riches, riches and grace and glory, honor with God and men, now and in life everlasting Our greatest examples of living a life that fears God are those who we know to be the most humble Moses, you know this, was said to be the most humble man there ever was. And we would think the opposite He Moses had personal time with God Almighty. Moses dined with God. Moses stood on holy ground The face of Moses glowed because he was in an intimate relationship with the triune God. And having such an audience with God, we might think that he would be a proud man. But he did the opposite. Being in the presence of God did the opposite Perhaps we can conclude that the more humble a person is, the more time he or she has spent in the very presence of God And after looking to Moses, we looked to Jesus. Jesus, the Son of God, the second person of the Trinity, the creator of the universe, of all that exists, was humble. Jesus, although he was God, made himself a small reputation and became man. Jesus, who healed the sick and raised the dead, also knelt down and washed the feet of his disciples like a slave. Jesus, who has the authority to cast both bodies and souls into hell and hanging upon the cross, looking down on his executioners, prayed for them Father, forgive them, they do not know what they are doing. Such is the kind of humility we are to practice. Wow. Quite a high calling. This pride versus humility is weighty stuff Perhaps I've been a little bit too serious with you this morning. In honor of the passing of actor and comedian Andy Griffith this past week I recall episodes from the Andy Griffith Show, hands down, the best television comedy sitcom ever. I recall funny episodes revealing the danger of pride in Don Knott's character that laughable, lovable Barney Fife. Like one of the episodes when Barney gave Gomer Pyle a ticket, a small vehicle violation. And this caused Gomer to get upset and declare citizens arrest upon Deputy Fife for doing a U-turn in the public square. The crowd that gathered required Deputy Fife to write himself his own ticket. Because of his pride, he refused and later decided he would rather resign from the force than admit he was wrong. Another episode had Sheriff Andy Taylor needing to go out of town, and that put Deputy Barney Fife in charge as sheriff. Barney quickly let his power go to his head and started arresting citizens for all small infractions. Even Aunt B was arrested. And when Annie returned, he had to dismiss all charges and send everyone home that was incarcerated. Barney later found out that the incident had made him a laughing stock in the town. He quits the force again. And each time Sheriff Taylor has to come up with a scheme to restore Barney's pride. Such stories show a little, a little of how pride brings a person low. But our acts, our feelings of pride, are not worth saving We don't want and don't need a Sheriff Taylor to restore pride to us. No, we need a Savior to forgive us of our pride. and to replace it with his holy humility. Let us hear from the New Testament. The Epistle of St. James chapter 4 verse 10 Humble yourself in the sight of the Lord. This is done when men before the Lord and from their hearts and in sincerity of their souls acknowledge their meanness. their unworthiness, their vileness, their sinfulness, their wretchedness, and implore the grace and mercy of God in Christ. Just as did the patriarchs before us, Abraham, Jacob, Job, Isaiah, Paul, And the publican. And when this is done, men then come close to humility. And the rest of the verse states And he, God, shall lift you up. And this is God's usual way to lift up. He lifts up the meek. He exalts those that humble themselves. He lifts them from their lowest state to set them among princes. He gives them a place and a name in his house. He adorns them with his grace. He clothes them with righteousness, the righteousness of his one and only Son. He grants them nearness to himself, and at last will introduce them into his kingdom of glory forever and forever. Amen. And so this pride versus humility thing, not much of a contest which way we should go. But the battle must be fought. Fought by each and every one of us. Humble yourself in the sight of the Lord, and He will lift you up. Amen. Let us pray

sermons.title: Speaking and Listening
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. You're still in Proverbs, and our topic from Proverbs this morning is about speaking and listening. Count to yourself how many times when you are fellowshipping with brothers and sisters in Christ. For any significant amount of time, count when the conversation turned where it should not have. And things were said that should not have been said, and all that were present were culpable of sin. Go ahead. Count the times that has happened. I'll wait. No, I know none of us could possibly come up with an accurate count and we would not have the time. When my family gets together with extended family, there is a great deal of talking going on. And I'm speculating that 95% of it is good natured, but there is always that 5% that needs to be repented of After we depart from family, I usually ask Bobby Lynn, did I overstate my point in that conversation Or was I talking about such and such a person in too negative of a manner? Or was I unkind when I spoke up during that topic of conversation? And the answers are usually yes, yes, and oh yes, Because we are to understand our Christian life, to include every aspect of our life, then it includes our tongue. It includes our listening. In order for us to lead a good life, a useful life, a godly life, then our speech must be submitted to the Holy Spirit. And that means it is to be governed by the law and will of God. And our listening is to be governed by the same. As Christians, our speaking and listening is to be distinctly Christian. But that is asking a lot. Let us make no mistake about it. It is asking a lot. We know St. James's words to be so very accurate when he says No human can tame the tongue. It is a fire, a world of unrighteousness. The tongue is set among our members, staining the whole body, setting on fire the entire course of our life, and set on fire by hell. We know these words to be true by way of experience. All of us do And we can add to this the modern means of communication, known as digital communication. As great as our modern electronic advances are, they are also More means by which we humans can practice sin. James could easily have said that no human can tame the send button. Our texts, our posts, our emails can easily start a blaze of unrighteousness And for many, it is easier to set a fire with an email, because you don't have to look the person in the eye when you push sin. Let us back up and consider the nature of speaking and listening. The nature of speaking and listening. Speaking and listening by themselves Are quite neutral and really have a great deal of promise for the good. Consider that speaking and listening are the foundation in every human relationship that we have. Our most lasting memories are from words spoken and written in relationships. Speaking itself should be understood as one of the greatest powers that you and I have as human beings. After all, we are made in the image of God. And God spoke the universe into being. Jesus spoke people to be healed He raised people from the dead with words. He depossessed people with his words Our words, being in his image, have intrinsic power for the good if we want. From Proverbs eighteen, verse twenty-one, death and life are in the power of the tongue. And those who love it will eat its fruits. The first part of the verse reminds us that the tongue could go either way. Death and life are polar opposites, and yet the tongue can affect either way. As one commentator noted, the sense of that last part of the verse seems to be that one will Eat the consequences of his words, according to whether his words are good or bad. Those who who love life will speak one way, and his or her words will bring life. And those who love death will speak accordingly and reap accordingly Well, let us now scare ourselves a bit, scare ourselves purposefully, by looking at verses that warn against the dangers of our poor speech choices. Dangers. From Proverbs 18, verse 6. A fool, a fool's lips, walk into a fight, and his mouth invites a beating. I have not been in a fish bite as an adult, but I can imagine how one would start. A fight is likely started by what someone says, and the one who is spoken to ends the discussion with a punch. Now this is from Proverbs 18, 7. A fool's mouth is his ruin, and his lips are a snare to his soul. Well, this proverb warns against something much great of danger than a punch to the mouth. For a soul. To be snared by a person's own lips is likely caused by a person going down the path of falsehood. It is living lies. From Proverbs 29 verse 12. If a ruler listens to falsehoods, all his officials will be wicked. Recall that lying lips are on that list of the six things that God hates. And lying lips spread like a disease. As lies corrupt others who believe them and then repeat them. Lying is not a sin that has a negative effect only on the person that tells the lies. Instead, it is a sin that is contagious. And then there are these contrasting verses, like this one from Proverbs 12, verse 22. Lying lips are an abomination to the Lord, but those who deal truthfully are his delight. Now the word abomination says enough. To delight God is to merely speak the truth. And such is not difficult, not difficult if we believe that the only audience that matters is that of God. From Proverbs 13, verse 3. Whoever guards his mouth preserves his life. He who opens wide his lips comes to ruin. Now, this contrast has a positive stated first, and that is because we must first be quick to listen. To listen, you must keep your mouth closed. To guard our mouths is that we must filter what comes out. And that is done by internal discipline that says no to self many, many times. There's a story of a father who caught his daughter both lying and gossiping. He told her that her punishment was first to take a handful of feathers and place one feather on the doorstep of the home or of a home of a person that she gossiped about. She did so and hurried back to her father. And when she came back, he told her then to go and collect all of those feathers that she had placed on the doorsteps of those she had gossiped. About. Much later, the daughter returned to her father, very forlorn. She confessed her inability to retrieve any of the feathers she had placed on the doorsteps. That is the lesson, said the father. The intention of proverbs like these is to trick the consciences of those who love God, to get them to commit to being honest in their speech so as not to hurt the God that they love. Venting is a selfish act, and a wise person knows that to be true. And hear these proverbs from chapter 13, verse 3. Whoever guards his mouth preserves his life. And from chapter 10, verse 19, when words are many, transgression is not lacking. But whoever restrains his lips is prudent. That should be obvious to us why Proverbs teaches us these things, saying them in so many different ways. It is because sinning with our speech is so easily done and thus so prevalent. It is because the sins of talking too quickly and talking too much that we say what is not for us to say. We say what is unkind. We say what is unnecessary. What we say becomes careless, groundless, selfish, and thus altogether foolish. The teachings from Proverbs regarding listening as opposed to speaking go so far as to prefer Prefer to be a fool and be silent than to speak. This is from Proverbs 17, verse 27 and 28. Whoever restrains his words has knowledge. And he who has a cool spirit is a man of understanding. Even a fool who keeps silent is considered wise. When he closes his lips, he is deemed intelligent. And let us think practically for a moment what it looks like to speak less. You will remember the faithful Christian minister Diedrich Bonhoeffer, who was killed by the Nazis because his Christian faith called him to resist the Nazi regime. Bonhopper secretly trained men for Christian ministry, and he did so with this rule. He did not allow Christian brothers to speak about one another in any way if the other man being spoken about was not present. In a parish such as this, I submit the rule should be That if speech is critical in nature about anyone in the parish, it should not be spoken unless who is being spoken about is present. Can we live by that? That's the standard of Scripture. Such a rule will save us from a great deal of discord and thus a great deal of sin Now the third and final point that Proverbs teaches us about godly and wise speech is that it is kind. Godly speech is kind speech. Kind speech about and toward others is part of our great calling in life. For that great calling is to love God. And our neighbor as ourself. Hear these following proverbs in succession. Anxiety in a man's heart weighs him down, but a good word makes him glad. A gentle tongue is a tree of life. The mouth of the righteous is a fountain of life, but the mouth of the wicked conceals violence. The lips of the righteous feed many. Gracious words are like honeycomb, sweetness to the soul, and health to the body. Whoever covers an offense seeks love, but he who repeats a matter separates close friends. These lessons also teach us that we need not live under a vow of silence. It may have sounded like that this morning. We can speak and our speech can have power But it must be guarded. Christian, regarding our speech, we must live by principles and not by circumstances. When Jesus spoke, he spoke words of eternal life. His church is to speak words of eternal life. He believed it was one of the highest virtues. Aristotle defines friendship in three distinct ways. The first way is friendship of utility. Such friends occur when people exchange goods and services with one another. We see these friends in business transactions. We get to know them, get familiar with them, and appreciate them because we exchange goods with one another. It is a you scratch my back, I will scratch yours relationship. When utility friends are no longer needed. That is, we're no longer needing to exchange goods, well, the friendship ends. The second definition of friendship is of pleasure. But the friendships even in there in those circumstances, those friendships end when the passion ends, when the game's over The final definition of friendship for Aristotle is friendship of virtue Friendship of virtue. Friendship of virtue occurs when two people hold the same moral values and are hoping to bring out the best in one another's character. Regardless of the utility in the relationship or the pleasure in the relationship, they just care about the virtue of the relationship. Regarding friendship of virtue, Aristotle calls it, quote, a complete sort of friendship between people who are good and alike in virtue. sermons.title: Proverbs on Decision Making
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father and of the Son of the Holy Ghost. Amen. You apologize about the mixture and the gospel reading. We will then be uh entering into a study on uh the Gospel according to John. I realized uh in my research that I have never preached to John, and so we're going to take advantage of that opportunity. But today we're in Proverbs. I was recently made aware of a 76-year-old woman who serves her church as the secretary. That she has been writing checks to herself to the total sum of $28,000 this calendar year. The woman is a widow with no money problems that the pastor was aware of at the time of this criminal discovery. I share this with you because our topic from Proverbs today is related to the topic presented last week. This woman who chose, chose to steal from the Lord, did not make her decision to do so with eternity in mind. What she revealed about herself at least, she has a very poor ability to make decisions regarding her personal actions. Many people have hidden sins. We can choose to lust in our minds and no one knows about it. We can choose to envy, and no one is the wiser. We can hold on to bitterness against another person and keep that bitterness to ourselves. But choosing a sin to hide that immediately harms others and is a direct affront to the Lord Jesus, that's a different type of sin altogether, a different level of evil. How a person could choose to sin in such a manner and believe on the Lord Jesus Christ at all? Well, that's a great mystery. Our theme or topic today from the book of Proverbs is the importance of making good decisions. And that sounds like a benign topic compared to the others that we have addressed from Proverbs thus far. But when you put it in light of this woman choosing to steal church funds Well, that's a very important topic indeed. It is important because of how many decisions, important decisions we Christians make in our lives Consider how many important decisions you make. The most important? Following the Lord Jesus Christ as your Savior and Lord. And once that's established, consider all the other ones, how important they are. Who you marry, your occupation. The church you choose to worship. Where you live, the house you buy, the cars you buy, the schooling you choose, the schooling for your children. How to care about your parents when they're old. These are all important decisions. The lesser decisions might be how to prepare for retirement, whether or not to take this job or that job. How to overcome disappointment. Whether you should confront and try to mend a broken relationship. And yet these seemingly lesser important decisions actually might become important depending on the consequences. It is important to recognize that with many decisions that we make, often there is no right or wrong. There is no breaking of God's law involved or even his will involved. But there are degrees of happiness and success And unhappiness and failure according to the decisions that we make. We then are asking, how Proverbs helps us make decisions? Well, first We say that we make good decisions by being wise in our decision making, exercising wisdom or sound judgment. Wisdom for a Christian is using biblical truths that we know and are to apply to our lives and evaluate our circumstances and possible choices that we can make. And then to do the wise and godly thing. Consider the missionary strategy of decision-making by St. Paul in the book of Acts. As we read his decision to go to Cornet and to stay at Corneth for a year and a half, we find he did so because he found there was great success. But then it tells us that he chose to go to Ephesus for three years, twice the amount at Corinth. And not because he had a vision from God, but because he says, a great door of effective work has opened to me, and there are many who oppose me. So, evidently it was wise to stay in Ephesus because the gospel was bringing forth a lot of fruit But he stayed there longer, even longer than Corinth, because he had to establish the church in order to prepare it for the opposition, for the persecution that they would face. That was simply Paul using sound wisdom, practicing sound judgment in his work. It was a wise decision for the reasons that we described, but it was simply a decision that Paul thought there was nothing else he could do. He had to do it. Consider that in other cases Paul moved on in his ministry because there was no great door of effective work open to him. There was no hint that he received any vision or some heavenly direction In fact, if you read through the book of Acts, searching on how the apostles made decisions, most of the time they were made primarily by wisdom. Not special revelation, not a vision while they were sleeping, but by wisdom Now the times that the apostles did make decisions according to a vision we find to be very dramatic. You remember Philip. who was having great success in Samaria. We are told that many of the population was coming to to Jesus Christ as he was preaching the gospel, finding great success, and yet all of a sudden he makes his way through the desert. By special revelation. And he finds himself coming upon an Ethiopian eunuch, and at that time shares the gospel with the man, so that the gospel can be taken back to Africa. Special revelation, dramatic moment, so the gospel can spread. That was not great wisdom, but great moving of the Spirit. And you remember Jesus teaching us about wisdom and how a prudent man, when he sets about to do something, counts the cost of the project. Proverbs in the same way recommends wisdom to us when we are making decisions. Sensible judgment is to be applied to make good judgment. Hear these proverbs from chapter 14, verse 15. A simple man believes anything, but a prudent man gives thoughts to his steps. From chapter 22, verse 3. A prudent man sees danger and takes refuge, but the simple keep going and suffer for it. Or consider chapter 21, verse 5. The plans of the diligent lead surely to abundance, but everyone who is hasty comes only to poverty. According to these verses, what is involved in being prudent is thinking things out. Planning. It is recognizing signs. It is making plans and then carrying them through Consider, and you probably know this better than I, consider the mess that we are in as a nation financially. And know that our governing officials did not give thoughts to their steps. They did not see the dangers, but kept going. and continue to make hasty decisions based on electability, as opposed to what is wise and what is best for our nation. The greatest sin of our nation is abortion. There is no debating that. The second greatest sin, I believe, is the debt we are leaving our children. And both sins are abundantly self-serving and arrogant. Lord have mercy upon us. Christ have mercy upon us. Lord have mercy upon us. From Proverbs 24 verse 27. Prepare your work outside. Get everything ready for yourself in the field. After that, build your house. This proverb may be paraphrased, don't undertake a project in a hasty manner without making preparation. Don't do anything hasty without making preparation. It means much again the same thing as our Lord said, count the cost before beginning an undertaking. Christians are not to be fools in anything in life. The second lesson from Proverbs regarding good decision making is that it requires godly advice and counsel. Now Proverbs probably says more about this than any other way in which we make decisions. Godly advice. Consider these Proverbs from 1114. Where there is no guidance, a people fall. But in an abundance of counselors there is safety. From chapter 15, 22 Without counsel, plans fail, but with many advisors, they succeed. From chapter 20, verse 18, plans are established by counsel and by wise guidance. Wage war. From chapter 24, verse 6. By wise guidance you can wage your war, and in an abundance of counselors there is victory. Now there is of course an underlying assumption here that the counselors that you choose in your life are wise people. Natural counselors are our parents and our grandparents. Teachers and coaches and bosses can be good counselors. And pastors, yes, even pastors, anointed by the Holy Spirit to be a counselor, to bring the Word of God into the people's lives. Too many Christians make decisions unaware of the moral realities that are involved in those decisions. I knew of a couple that was making fertility decisions without including their pastor, and they were placing themselves in a position to abort fertilized eggs. I know of a couple who decided that they no longer wanted to be married while never considering that their divorce, how it would affect their standing before God and before the church I know of families who made decisions regarding youth in Asia that essentially had them choosing death without acknowledging God, who is the only authority when it comes to life and death. We need to know that God has placed counselors in our lives to help us make decisions so as not to offend him. And notice how the Proverbs read refer to multiple counselors. No wise person simply goes on the word of one other person. No wise counselor should ever expect to be the only voice. that is heard. The third lesson from Proverbs is that wise decisions require prayer. That should be obvious to us, shouldn't it? This is from Psalm 25, verse 4 and 5. And here we read how David practiced this. It's very insightful to realize what he's really praying for. He says, show me your ways, O Lord, teach me your paths, guide me in your truth, and teach me, for you are God, my Savior, and my hope is in you all day long. Reading this psalm in part, we can think that David was asking for signs in his life for which way to go. But actually, David was not interested in signs at all. Instead, David wanted the Lord to write God's word on his heart. He wanted his heart purified. He wanted the Lord to grant him fear of God. A confidence in God's law. And we know this is what God wants for each of us who believe in Him. He wants to write His word on our hearts that we might live lives that are honoring to Him. In the same way, hear this from James chapter 1, verse 5. If any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask God, who gives generously to all without reproach, and it will be given him. Ministers like myself will teach that James is instructing us that when we have a dilemma To decide, we ought to ask God, and then God is going to tell us what to do. Considerate, submissive, full of mercy, and good fruit, impartial and sincere. Peacemakers who sow in peace reap a harvest of righteousness. Okay, so let me put these two things together for us. We're to pray for wisdom, but what is the wisdom we are to pray for? Well, from these passages, the wisdom we are to pray for is purity, peace, gentleness, mercy, sincerity, righteousness. If any of you lack wisdom, is the same thing as saying, if any of you lack a godly character Ask of the Lord, and he will give it to you. When it comes to decision making, James is not talking about signs or impressions on the heart to direct us if there's a fork in our road of life. He's talking about godly character. He's talking about a heart that has the Word of God written upon it. Remember, Paul says the same thing to the Thessalonians. This is God's will for you. You want to know God's will? This is it. Your sanctification, your holiness. Proverbs puts it this way. The plans of the heart belong to man, but the answer of the tongue is from the Lord. All the ways of a man are pure in his own eyes, but the Lord weighs the Spirit. Commit your work to the Lord and your plans will be established. Can we paraphrase that? Live a holy life, and God will take care of the rest. And here is another example of how scriptures are so very consistent. You are to offer our lives to God in sincere faith and obedience and ask Him to bless us then with His grace and Spirit. And that is how guidance comes to us, to God's people. They come to us through blessings of the Lord, through our faith, through obedience, through the working of his Holy Spirit in our lives, making us godly, making us righteous, making us holy. That is why Proverbs is so emphatic about humility There are great limitations imposed upon us because we do not know our future. But we do know what the Lord wants of us in our hearts. Hear these proverbs. Many are the plans in the mind of a man, but it is the purpose of the Lord that will stand. The heart of a man plans his way, but the Lord establishes his steps. Do not boast about tomorrow, for you do not know what a day may bring. Our ignorance of the future cannot be overcome. We do not know the future. Even the wisest decisions can lead into troubles of various kinds. And that's no proof that we made the wrong decision. Recall that Paul knew by prophecy that if he went to Jerusalem, that he was going to be arrested. But he believed it was best for him to go because it was a duty. He had promised them that he would come back to them, and so he was going to fulfill his promise. He was to take those Gentiles and show them the church at Jerusalem. He made that promise as well. And so even though he knew he would be arrested, even though he knew it could be his end, he did it anyways. And so we make decisions in life, recognizing that it might not go so well for us. But we recognize also that the Lord's promises are real. He will never leave us nor forsake us. Regardless of the outcome of our decision-making, he will always be with us. That is to be our confidence. And we are to pray like that is our confidence You know, the disciples asked Jesus how they should pray. And you remember what he said, the Lord's Prayer. Our Father who art in heaven. Hallowed be thy name, thy kingdom come, thy will be done. And so when we pray to the Lord to understand his will, make our decisions, where is the priority? In Jesus' prayer, the priority is God's kingdom. And then there in that prayer is an acceptance of our dependency upon God, our daily bread. There is a recognition that without us forgiving and being forgiven, there is nothing else to consider. And the prayer for us to be delivered from evil is a prayer to be holy. And that is God's will. That is what He wants for you and for me to be holy. Fourth and finally, wise decisions will be the responsibility of us exercising our liberty. A liberty that God has given us. God has made us, created us in his image to choose things. He gave us a will, and he wants us to exercise our will There is no particular verse for this point from Proverbs. But we may look back at the verses mentioned and see how such liberty is implied. It's up to us. Make the decision. We're responsible. And such liberty is what makes us human and truly unique of all of God's creatures on the earth. Such liberty is also what enables us to have a personal relationship with God through Jesus, our Savior. I wonder if we can end this discussion of decision making from Proverbs with the simple point that in the end We must choose Jesus. Regardless of how such sounds like a Christian bookstore card, it is true we must choose Jesus. When you make a decision in your life, the most important one that leads everything is to believe and follow Jesus. That makes every other decision very easy. When Jesus said to men, follow me. He is saying what the book of Proverbs is saying. Follow wisdom, follow life, follow holiness. Such is the best decision any person can make. Can I get an amen? Let us pray.

sermons.text: In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. Before we get started, I do want to share with you a quick thought. But I always think, boy, that parents gotta take care of that kid. Um and then when I hear it and I know it's my grandson, makes me smile. We'll start off with a fable from Asa Two Travelers and the Bear. Two boys were taking a shortcut on a narrow path through a dark, tangled woods. They walked silently through the deep shadows, and they pretended not to hear the rustling in the thickets, for neither wanted to admit that he was frightened. Then the air rumbled with a low, menacing growl. Don't look, I'm sure it's nothing, said the first boy quickly. Well, it's a very large nothing, shouted the second boy. There, lumbering toward them, was a monstrous, hairy bear. Two friends began to run. Before they had taken three steps, however, the first boy stumbled and sprawled upon the ground. Help me, he cried out, trying to get up. But his friend ran on. He clambered up a towering pine and sat astride a bough, clutching the tree trunk and quaking. The horrible bear loomed over the first boy, mouth wide, teeth glinting, the bear lunged. Now, luckily for this boy, he had learned his lessons well. And he remembered that bears usually do not bother anything that is not moving. So he threw himself face down in the dirt. When he felt the bear's hot breath on his ankle, the boy stayed very, very still. When a heavy paw lightly touched his back, he closed his eyes and he willed himself not to move. The bear sniffed and snuffled, pawed and prodded and pushed at the boy until finally the beast's muzzle was next to the boy's face. The creature whiffed and snorted, and he nuzzled at the boy's ear. Although the boy was in agony of fright, still he lay unmoving. After a time, the bear became bored with this limp, lump boy. With a final swipe of his huge paw, he turned away and shuffled back into the woods. At that the first boy the first boy's friend came running back. That was amazing, said the second boy. The bear put his nose right on your ear. Why, it looked as though he even whispered a secret to you. What did he say? The first boy glared at his companion. The bear told me I need to find a more dependable friend. Now the moral of that story is what true friendship isn't But is also what underlines many of Aesop's fables and what underlines much of the book of Proverbs. That underlying moral or lesson is cause and effect. It is the truth that for every action there is a reaction. For every decision, there is a consequence. The two boys in Aesop's story chose to take a shortcut in the woods, and that put them in danger of what lived in the woods, cause and effect. The boys chose to continue on in their own path, even when they heard rustling in the thickets, and that was effect of greater fear. When the bear revealed itself, the boys chose to run. And the effect, the result, one boy falling and putting his life in danger, and the other boy only saving himself. When the first boy was about to be eaten by the bear, his quick wisdom to remain still ended up, the effect, saving him. The second boy's choice to abandon his friend ended up costing him his friendship with the first boy and likely his reputation, cause and effect. Cause and effect, action and reaction, decisions and consequences. This is how God has made the world. Hear this proverb. He who is devoid of wisdom despises his neighbor, but a man of understanding holds his peace. Now, hear the same verse in terms of cause and effect. A person who does not act wisely will hate his fellow man. Who can be down the road an asset to him, his neighbor? A man of wisdom will be self-controlled, and it will be to his benefit for the rest of his life. Hear this proverb. As righteousness leads to life, so he who pursues evil pursues it to his own death. And now hear it in terms of action and reaction. A person who lives righteously will inherit life everlasting. A person who lives pursuing evil will end up assuring his eternal death. Hear this proverb. The righteous should choose his friends carefully, for the way of the wicked leads them astray. Now hear it in terms of decisions and consequences. A God-fearing person is to choose his friends carefully because if he or she does not, they will encounter friends who will lead them into sin. Note that none of these examples from Proverbs have the subject matter in common, but what they have is the principle in common of cause and effect. I chose the topic of cause and effect to end our study of Proverbs because it is a topic that our present culture does not understand. And the reality of that lack of understanding needs to be recognized and corrected within the church. The failure to recognize the principle of cause and effect. The principle that God has embedded cause and effect into creation. It has wreaked havoc on our American culture. And I want to address this morning two examples of this havoc. I only address two because they are the most obvious and have caused the greatest of harms. The first example of our failure to recognize and then stay away from the cause and effect is sexual immorality. The recent Supreme Court ruling that allowed our nation to sanction same-sex marriage was a difficult blow to this nation's moral standing before God. There is no means by which we can expect God to bless us as a nation while we ceremonially bless the act of sodomy. But the recent Supreme Court's blessing of sodomy was an effect, not a cause. An effect, not a cause. It may indeed become a cause of other immoral sanctions by our political leaders in years to come, but for now we need to understand it as an effect. As an effect, we can logically acknowledge that there was a cause or causes to this effect. So a rational question is: what were the causes that led our leaders to believe it is perfectly acceptable to sanction Sodom? Well, the first cause that I want to point to is the idol, the idol of individual or personal happiness. That sounds strange, doesn't it? An idol of personal happiness. And my use of happiness is not in the classical sense or in the biblical sense, for in the classical sense. Happiness means being whole. Happiness is living a life that is fulfilling as persons achieve what they are capable of achieving. In comparison, the modern definition of happiness is pleasure of the flesh. It is carnal sanctification. And because the modern culture defines happiness as pleasure of the flesh, well our cultural leaders don't want any person To not be able to pursue the pleasures of the flesh, because to do so, to not deny them that that pursuit, well that goes against natural law. That tells us to deny a person of happiness is fundamentally evil. And so we have become a society that is obsessed with the pleasures of the flesh. And so the effect is the sanctioning of sodomy. But we can't look outside our windows, and we cannot say that is their problem out there. The modern church has allowed the idol of happiness, in the way I'm defining it, to be worshipped within its walls. Too often, parents who say that they are God-fearing look the other way when their children, young adults, are committing fornication. Christian parents are looking the other way, ignoring blatant sin in their homes when they know their children are having sexual intercourse with their girlfriend or boyfriend. And if they won't stand for it in regards to the girlfriend or boyfriend, they accept it, accept such sinful behavior when their child becomes engaged, as if that makes fornication more holy. The truth is fornication is adultery. And adultery is breaking the seventh commandment. It is literally that straightforward. It is time for parents to stop looking the other way and to address the sin directly It is necessary for parents and in particular fathers to assure your children's virginity. Frank and direct accountability about sexual behavior of our children is the responsibility of every parent and especially the fathers. For God has specifically directed, given commandment, that fathers are to assure their daughter's virginity I have had frank and direct conversations with my sons about sexual behavior, not because of my personality, as some might think. But because I truly have thought about having to answer God for not holding my children accountable for such sins. And I fear him more than I fear being uncomfortable in a conversation with my children. All parents need to fear God in such a manner. And what I'm trying to point out to you Is that how Christians view and act regarding sexual immorality as Christians is going to have an effect upon our culture? If we look the other way when it comes to sexual immorality among us, then we will be sowing a seed for our culture. To go even farther in their sexual immorality, just as they have Another cause of the effect of our leaders sanctioning sodomy is how marriage is treated in our culture. I am sorry to admit this. that a man that I truly regard as one of the greatest presidents that this nation's in this nation's history, a man I can say probably that I voted for Was also a fool in regards to the covenant of marriage. Ronald Reagan was the first governor to sign a bill allowing for no fault divorce. The first governor. Such allowances were the cause of many marriages failing without any effort And the more marriage has been treated as a used car transaction, the more its value has been undermined, leading it to be redefined as it is today. And once again, we need not look out the window and place blame on the secular world. Christians above all people should uphold the holiness of the marriage vows and the marriage bed. The effect of not doing so is Adam marrying Steve or Adam marrying Steve and then Stacy and then Mary and then Mark and any number of combinations that really aren't marriages at all The second example of our culture failing to understand the damage that is done by cause and effect. Is the vile act of abortion. Allow me to get out of the way any notion that a woman who has had an abortion is automatically condemned. Our culture has so confused women in regards to their bodies and what an unborn child is that many women choose abortion without considering the basic morality of such an act. The act of abortion can be forgiven by the blood of Jesus, just as any other heinous sin can be forgiven. There is hope, there is peace, there is forgiveness for those who have had abortions or who have supported abortion in the past. Thanks be to God. With that said, let us turn to the subject in light of cause and effect. The shooting in South Carolina That killed God-fearing people at a Bible study. And the killing of reporters live on television just a week ago. are examples of our culture that is not gun happy, but a culture that has lost a sense of value of human life According to a recent study done by Harvard University, mass shootings in America have tripled since 2011. Tripled. And it is not just the statistics that we should be concerned about. It should be the heinousness that are part of these mass shootings. The killers are cold. They're heartless and seemingly soulless And while every culture produces soulless people, let there be no mistake that our culture has mass-produced such people. And the initial cause, hear this now, the initial cause has to be abortion. Beloved, a society cannot allow for children, babies. Hear it again, babies. To be removed from the safest, safest place on this earth, a mother's womb, and casually have their heads cut off, and then remain a sane society A society cannot casually dismember and sell the body parts of babies who were just a few minutes ago prior quietly growing in their mother's womb And think that we can ever care about human life. Let us not for a moment fail to see that there is a connection between how we treat life in a mother's womb. And how we treat life in general as a society. And if a person was to counter my point Of connecting abortion to mass killings, and say that I have no science to back up my point of cause and effect. Allow me to respond by pointing out that we are not in a world that is only governed by what is observable. We are in a world that is governed by the unseen. The sin, the plague of abortion has brought a spirit of death to us as a nation, to our cities, to our suburbs. And the devil is happy about that. I made the point some Sundays ago that the devil has two goals for each of us in this world. He first wants each and every one of us to deny Jesus and thus be punished with him for eternity in hell, or he wants to kill us. And I will state it more personally. He wants you to deny Jesus or he wants you dead. And thus the killing of babies is just right by him. Now if you are not convinced at what I am saying, consider God's modus operandi. St. Paul explained it to the Romans when he describes that when men started to lust after other men, and women started to lust after other women and were persistent about it Paul says God gave them over to such a lust. Gave them over The phrase gave them over refers to letting them be governed by their desires. When God gives a people over to something, anything but him, it is never a good thing. And God did the same with Israel. Time and time again, Israel wanted to be like other nations And so God gave them over to be like other nations. And it always, always turned out to be hell on earth. And such is how we are being judged as a nation, as a society today. You want your freedom to choose? You want the right to kill the most innocent among you? You want death? Here it is. God has given us over. God has given us over to death. It is hard to hear, I know. But death is all around us. Now all that has been said, I realize, is quite heavy. I feel it also. But all that has been said is to be a wake-up call to us. And after we wake up, we need to do things. We need to be calling our congressmen and senators and voice our disapproval of immoral laws. We need to stand shoulder to shoulder, doing whatever we can to protect the unborn. We need to work at being more upstanding before God and men about our own personal morality. And we need to hold on to the good news. The good news was and forever will be that regardless of how the spirit of lust and death dwell among us, Jesus is on the throne of heaven. Jesus has overcome the sin of lust and the effect of death. Don't ever forget that. And because this is true about Jesus, all of this bad news does not and cannot overwhelm us. All is not lost. It never will be. But we need to have the blood of Jesus applied to our homes. And our church, and our community. And however far we can spread the good news that sin can be overcome and death has been overcome. Beloved, we live in tough and confusing times. But these times God has chosen us to live in. Us. You and I. So let us be up to the task. Of being counted as followers of Jesus, believers in God's holy word, defenders of the weak, and lovers of sinners. Amen and Amen.

sermons.title: Born of God
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father and of the Son. Son of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Turn in your Bibles to the Gospel according to Saint John. We're still in the first chapter, first thirteen verses, actually verse six through thirteen we are looking at. I want to start off by having you imagine Imagine a man who was given everything and thus did nothing to earn what he was given. He was given wealth and a job to sustain his wealth so that he never checked his bank account. For he always had enough money to buy whatever he considered buying. He was given family. So that he never had to venture to ask a woman out on a date and risk that she would say no. The woman he was given was perfect for him. She loved him, and he loved her unconditionally. The children he was given were beautiful and obedient. They loved their parents and they did what they were told. He was given friends as well. The people he was closest to always spoke well of him, and he spoke well of them. He never had arguments or jealousies with the people he knew. He was always at peace with all men. And finally, our imaginary man was given good health. He didn't have a personal physician because he was never sick. No cough, no cold, no stomach issues. He was always healthy. Now, I said that our imaginary man was given Given all of this, if such a man existed, would we think that his life circumstances were fair? And I'm using fair as injust Remember, our imaginary man did nothing to earn this wonderful life. It was all given to him. Would he be the type of man living the type of life that all of us would be tempted to covet? Would he be the type of man that we would say to God that his life is too easy for him compared to our lives? Would we think that life isn't fair, that God isn't fair, because such a life is easily lived compared to our own? Although none of our lives are like our imaginary man, can we identify in our lives how much has been given to us? Consider how much of what we have that has indeed been given to us, not earned by us I know that I did not deserve my wife. I know that even those things that I have accomplished in my life, I was able to accomplish because I was given the talents to do so, and I was given the fortitude to pursue. my goals. In fact, when I really think about it, when I really examine my life and take inventory for what I am responsible for It does seem that all of the bad that was and is in my life is caused by me And all that was good and is good was given to me. I don't think that that's much of an exaggeration. And I want you to keep all of this in mind as we examine here John's Gospel. We pick up in John's Gospel at verse 6 of chapter 1, and there we find John the author mentioning John the Baptist. Many scholars read into John's words here, concluding that John the Apostle was once a disciple of John the Baptist. And thus knew why people would think that John the Baptist was the Messiah during his public ministry. Maybe for a time John, our author, thought John the Baptist was the Messiah. It seems that at the mention of light coming into the world That John the author wants the reader to know that John the Baptist was not the light. He wants us to know immediately what the relationship of John the Baptist is or was to Jesus. John the Baptist himself stood for the old order. He was a prophet and a priest in the form of Elijah. And just as the prophets and priests of old were given the task of pointing people to God Well, so John the Baptist was given the task of pointing people to God, but he was now pointing to God in human form. In verse 9, it is made clear that the light, the true light, was to be understood as separate from John the Baptist. Separate from all the prophets, separate from all the priests that came before him. Isaiah, the prophet proclaimed, Arise, shine. For the light has come, and the glory of the Lord is risen upon you. Speaking of Jesus Jesus the Christ is that light. He was the true light. Now the usage of the word true here needs to be clarified It may seem to suggest that all the other prophecies and works of the priests before were false lights. But that is not what John means. Rather, he is saying that Jesus is the real, the genuine. the perfect light, compared to all those that came before that were flickers and shadows and reflection types of what was to come. And the latter part of verse 9 cannot be missed, for it is to be enlightening and convicting that Jesus is the true light who came for all mankind. He did not come for the suburbanites like us only. He did not come for the middle and upper class only. He did not come for only those on the Western hemisphere of the globe. He came for all persons of all economic status and every skin tone. And that means we must acknowledge that means that he came for those who choose to be our enemies. As they worship Allah and chant our demise, guest Jesus came for them as well. And to state that Jesus was in the world in verse 10 is against those who believed that if Jesus was among men, that he was an apparition. Some thought he wasn't truly physical, therefore he didn't really dwell physically on earth. But no. No, John is saying he was physical on this earth. The rest of the verse shows the great irony of Jesus being a creator of a world that does not know him. Does not know him as the creator. And consider how odd that is. It is rather odd that the world does not know its own creator. But it is not odd when you consider how quickly we humans move away from truth. One of the realities we can trace or follow regarding the human condition and how quickly we move away from the truth is seen in our culture today. Up to nineteen up to nineteen seventy-three. Nineteen seventy-three, abortion was illegal in America. It wasn't until 1967 that state legislatures began debating the legality of abortion because too many women were putting their lives in danger having illegal abortions. Just six years later, six years, the Supreme Court decides it is morally acceptable to kill unborn babies. Consider next how quickly we have gone from a nation that considered sodomy a perversion and homosexual marriage to be, well, ridiculous, to now having both sanctioned as the law of the land. And most of us have had our heads spinning, still asking, how did that happen? These are examples and so many others show how quickly the human heart goes away from God. It does not know him. The next, perhaps the most searing part of this section of scripture Know the world, did not know Jesus as creator or any other thing worth noting, and neither did the people whom Jesus chose to be his most intimate people He came to his own, John says. John says he came to his own, meaning the Jewish people. He was a Jewish man. And his own, his people, the people he called out-of-polytheism, the people he rescued from Egypt. The people he made a covenant with, an everlasting covenant. The people he rescued from Babylon. The people that he became as They did not receive him. A literal translation could be, he came to his own things, and they did not accept him. Is there any greater tragedy that the Jewish people not receiving the Messiah they claimed long to see? I don't think there is anything more tragic. You remember Jesus saying, Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you kill the prophets and stone those sent to you. How oft I have longed to gather your children together as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, and you were not willing. It was a willful choice not to receive him. John, thankfully, does not end with such sad news. He turns it around. But, but everyone, all who received Jesus as the Messiah, that's what receiving Jesus is, receiving him as the Messiah Such persons are given the right, the ownership of being children of God. All who receive Jesus are the new chosen people. Do you hear that, church? All who receive Jesus have then the rights and privileges of being sons and daughters of God. As God's children, they become inheritors of God's kingdom. As children of God, they have the privilege of now calling him Father, our Father. The phrase, believe in his name. This is an underscore It is an emphasis on everything that is included in the name of Jesus. Believe on his name. What does that include? The name of Jesus is Messiah. It means creator. It means light and life. It means God. And after saying this, after saying this, it next appears that John, after sharing this glorious good news about receiving Jesus as inheritors of the kingdom of God, and we become God's children. John may be now concerned that the reader would think that receiving the truth About Jesus, well that that we might think it was done by us, by our own wisdom, by us figuring it out. John may be concerned that the reader could conclude that believing in Jesus is a matter of having more wisdom or maybe more goodness in us than those who reject Jesus. And so he clarifies. And what a glorious clarification this is We are to conclude from verse 13 that the only way to become a child of God, to be begotten out of God, is to be born of God. No illustrious and religious human ancestry is sufficient to give any person membership into God's family. To be born of, to not be born of blood, as it says here, to not be born of blood is to not be born into wealth or fame or power. It is amazing to me that there are still people today that consider their birth a gift to the world. As they view their lineage within a family of money, family of fame, a family of power, to be akin to their individual superiority to the rest of human society. I thought those people were part of Jane Austen novels Not Fit for the 21st Century. But alas, there are still those who think of themselves as aristocrats. But hear this: there are no aristocrats in the kingdom of God To not be born of blood is also to be born Jewish and think that such birth gives a person an automatic entry into the kingdom of God. But we remember what John just said. They did not receive him. No such automatic fulfillment is there. And then he says not to be born of the flesh. To not be born of the will of the flesh is to understand the inability. Of an individual to control his or her own birth, or to earn his or her own birth The flesh of men is dying or dead. The will of the flesh is lust and dissatisfied. The flesh wars against the spirit. No. Flesh needs to be renewed. Birth in the spirit must take place. Next, not born of the will of men. To not be born of the will of men is to recognize that the free will of man, which is carnal and corrupt, makes him an enemy of God, making him impotent to everything that is spiritually good. Consider the wills of the best men such as Abraham and David and others Such men, though ever so willing and desirous that their children, their relations, their friends, and their servants should be born again, be partakers of the grace of God, and live in God's sight. Yet, willing all this, their wills failed, as all wills of men fail. No, man must be born another way, the only way, to be born of God. To be born of God is to be given true light and true life, as the versus prior state. It is to be born again. Oh, the sweet emotion of being born again. The sweet objective reality of having old things pass away and all things becoming new. Under this idea, this beautiful, this beautiful reality of being born again, I want to leave you with two points, two points to close with, two points that I I want to say with you from these words of birth. By God. The first is connected to a phone call I received recently. My son Isaac called to ask for some help explaining his upbringing. As most of you know, he's currently working in Tampa as a history teacher at a private Christian school. The administration had encouraged the teachers to share their testimonies about being born again. And for these folks, most of them, their conversion experience is timed and dated They were raised to know that they needed to have a time and a date of their conversion and a story to tell everyone how it happened, a testimony. And that is, for most of them, the only Christian culture that they've ever known. And Isaac said to me Dad, I don't remember a time when Jesus was not my Savior, when I was not a believer. I have believed in Jesus all of my life. What a glorious sound that is. He said, I believed in Jesus all of my life. I said, son, we raised you to say exactly that. Next, he said, but how do I explain it to these people? Well, that is a tougher question, I admit it. For those of us who are not raised in the Christian faith, we likely have a born-again moment. I do. But that moment of choosing to follow Jesus, to believe in him as the Savior and God, was one of many moments in my life. When I have experienced the gracious power of God, that He gave me a deeper faith, a closer walk. And what I am saying, and what I know those of you who have walked with Jesus for many years will agree, is that the Christian life is a series of born-again moments. A series of not seeing so clearly and then seeing very clearly, of being in shadows and then seeing light. And we have those to share, to testify regarding the birth and rebirth that God gives us. Second and last point. John explains That we who follow Jesus have been born of God for the purpose of not misunderstanding the fact that it is God who saves us, as we've already explained. But also to establish an understanding that we are totally and utterly dependent upon God for our birth in his family. Not only are we not to take credit for our new birth, but we are to increase our devotion to our God every moment we are given opportunity. For he is worthy of such devotion, of such praise, of such adulation, with all the energy we have to give. In episode thirty-five of the Great Sitcom of the Nineteen Sixties Gilligan's Island. You didn't anticipate a transition like that, did you? In episode 35 of Gilligan's Island Gilligan saves Mr. Howell, saves his life, by moving him out of harm's way when a boulder is about to fall on him. A boulder Gilligan had accidentally dislodged himself. Mr. Howell is so indebted emotionally to Gilligan that he offers to adopt Gilligan and leave all of his fortune to him. The way I see it. If sitcom writers understand that when you owe your life to someone, you give them all that you have. Then we who follow Jesus can understand what we owe our Savior. We owe him all that we have and all that we are And the crazy, wonderful thing about this glorious gospel is that when you give him all that you have, he gives it back to you. He gives back to you your life. Only this time it really is a life. Let us then be reminded of our imaginary man, who was given everything. He is us. He is us. Therefore, because of what he has been given to us Let our devotion for Jesus increase all the more. Amen and Amen. Let us pray.

sermons.title: What it means to follow Jesus
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
