sermons.text: In the name of the Father, of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. We are continuing in The Gospel according to St. John chapter 13. For those of you who are history buffs, you recognize the name Vitkun Chrisling, Vitkun Chrisling considered himself a patriot of Norway His father served as a Christian chaplain in Norway's military. Chrisling began his political career as a diplomat, representing Norway. Living in Russia. He then returned to Norway to serve as their Minister of Defense. When his party was voted out of office, he was not heard for over a year publicly. On the 9th of April 1940, when the German invasion of Norway was in progress Chrisling attempted to seize power in the world's first radio broadcast coup d'état by claiming himself the new Prime Minister of Norway. But the Germans, as you can imagine, had different plans. From 1942 to 1945, Chrisling served as minister-president Heading the Norwegian State Administration jointly with a German civilian administrator named Joseph Terboven. In truth, Quisling's leadership was nothing more than a pro-Nazi puppet government known as the Quisling regime. After the war, Quisling was put on trial by his fellow countrymen and found guilty of charges that included embezzlement, murder, and high treason. He was executed by a firing squad at Oslo on the 24th of October, 1945. The word quistling has since become a synonym for a collaborationist or a traitor. He is to Norway and their history what Benedict Arnold is to the United States. And so we ask, what prompts a one-time patriot to turn on his own country? Was it for power? Was it for the hate hate of the Jewish race? Or maybe it was just an evil seed always within him We cannot know. But we can ask the same about someone like Absalom that we read this morning. What was in Absalom to betray his very own father? And being a traitor must be very hard to live with. A person likely needs to believe he or she is not a traitor. but is fighting for a a different cause than everyone else, a greater cause, a more just cause. I would think that that is the only way that such a person could sleep at night. Some speculate that Judas, the betrayer, had what he thought was a greater cause in mind. Some speculate that he was trying to get Jesus to reveal himself for who he truly was. And he thought that he could help Jesus along by having him arrested. And then after being arrested, Jesus would show his power over mankind. greatly displaying his strength, followed by establishing his rule over Israel and then his rule over Rome. This type of speculation comes from the fact that Judas, you recall, returned those 30 coins. That he confessed that he had betrayed innocent blood and then with such great remorse went out and hung himself. Did this all because Jesus refused to enact any vengeance. He refused to show any strength, but yet still chose to die on the cross. Such speculation about Judas, from the fact stated, I think is very kind. It's a glass half-full perspective about the character of Judas. It ignores that John exposed Judas earlier as a thief who had been skimming off the top of their treasury. And it ignores that Jesus referred to Judas as responsible for his own betrayal. And it fails to remember John's commentary stating that the devil entered Judas when he took that bread. from Jesus' hand. But such a description by John does not allow us to come to a complete conclusion about the ways of the devil. But his account about the devil entering Judas at that point gives us a hint that when Certain people turn themselves over to their sin and no longer try to resist, no longer have any hesitation. Well then the devil has the transition sealed. He has their soul. It is incomplete and fully under the control of the devil And consider people's lives that you have witnessed, who gave themselves over to a specific sin, ending up ruining them. And such behavior is no different than worshiping an idol and allowing the devil to inhabit the soul. On a side note, on a side note, have you noticed at this time how intense this Gospel of John is? He goes from one hard teaching of Jesus to another with no levity, no soft stories in between. And three weeks prior, we were challenged regarding what it really meant to see Jesus. And next to understand why people don't believe. To next, the most profound moment of humility ever witnessed, Jesus washing his disciples' feet. To this point, where a friend betrayed God in the flesh. I guarantee you will not hear any positive mental attitude preacher on television preach these types of sermons to his people. These are for the chosen people of God who want to walk on the narrow road. There is a great deal of agreement. Among biblical commentators, that the story of Judas and his betrayal is to be a warning, a warning story for you and I. It is a warning that we do not allow greed to take hold of us. It is a warning that we do not allow the riches of the world becoming an idol in our lives. One of the alternating prayers that we pray for morning prayer during the week says, put far from our families we beseech thee Every root of bitterness, the desire for vainglory and the pride of life. Such sins as desire for vainglory and pride of life are practiced while pursuing earthly success. And the things that people identify as earthly success. We are to do all things for the glory of God. We are to do all things for the glory of God because we do not Whatever other reason, we are not doing so for ourselves because when we do it for ourselves, it becomes an idol in our lives. And we slowly give our souls over to the devil. Yes, indeed, Judas can be a warning to us. Another aspect to Judas being a warning to us is the danger of hiding sin in secret. Sins which would not exist if revealed to the light. Remember, Judas was skimming off the top, money that was provided to Jesus and his disciples so that they could minister without the weight of worrying about their dignity. Bread. Judas did it thinking that no one would find out. But God is not a keeper of such secrets. As Scripture says, some people's sins go before them, and some people's sins follow after. And that means that some people's sins are more obvious. We can see them, we watch them. But some people's sins are in secret, and they will be revealed for all to see on the day of judgment. Secret sins are still sins. They require the wages of sin. They require death. Yes, indeed, Judas can be a warning to us. Another warning that comes to us from the life of Judas is the danger of listening to the lies the devil tells you and the lies that you tell yourself. Although we don't know exactly why Judas did what he did, we can at least conclude that he was listening to lies. We can rightly guess that he believed lies, and the belief of those lies led him to betray the only innocent man that ever lived I have come to realize in my own life that I win every argument in my own head. I realized this fourteen years ago while I was riding a lawn tractor. There was a family that used to attend this parish, they no longer do. And I was in serious disagreement with this family I thought they had misled me, and when I said as much, even more was said that should not have been said. Well while mowing I was playing and replaying this argument in my head and I was coming up with point by point by point that showed that I was right in this conflict And then it hit me. No one was rebutting my points. Of course I was in the right in my own head, because no one was there to tell me I was in the wrong. When you reason to yourself and reason to yourself alone, you can justify just about everything that you plan on doing. And the devil will help you. He will bolster your lies, the lies you want to believe. Yes, indeed, Judas can be a warning to us. But along with Jesus Judas being a warning to us, I want us to recognize that Judas as a warning breaks down. It is difficult to make Judas a full example of a warning to us because Judas was ordained by God to do what he did. We must acknowledge that Judas was born to do what he did. Dare I say that Judas was predestined to betray the Lord Jesus? I realize that saying such might sound salacious to some ears who are not used to hearing that God would choose a particular person for the purpose of destruction. But we cannot ignore the facts. First, there are those words that we read this morning from Psalm 41. They are words of prophecy. Even my own familiar friend, whom I trusted, who ate my bread, has lifted up his heel against me To lift up one's heel is to turn and go the other way, away from a friend who is in need. Second, in Psalm 55, David's words speak to the same type of betrayal that is another prophecy. Quote, if any enemy were insulting me, I could endure it. If a foe were rising against me, I could hide. But it is you, a man like myself, my companion, my close friend, with whom I once enjoyed sweet fellowship in the house of God. As we walked among the worshippers. Third, there was the prophecy of Zechariah. That spoke of a person asking for thirty pill pieces of silver, which was the asking price for Jesus. Zechariah also said that the money would be thrown into the house of Jehovah, and that's exactly what Judas did. Then there are the words of Jesus himself. Jesus predicted to his disciples that Judas would betray him And in his high priestly prayer, John 17, Jesus prays to the Father about his disciples. And he says this While I was with them, I was keeping them in your name, which you have given me, and I guarded them, and not one of them perished, but the son of perdition, that the scripture would be fulfilled. Perdition is another word for hell, and thus Jesus is describing Judas as a product of hell and a person who is destined for the same. The betrayal of Judas was meant for evil. The betrayal by Judas was a work of the devil. And yet the betrayal by Judas was the will of God. Well, after having shown that we cannot come to any other conclusion but to say that Judas was predestined by God to betray Jesus, all sorts of questions follow. Again, as we asked a few weeks ago, where does the will of man fit in with the sovereign will of God? We even may dare to ask, how can Judas be blamed and then punished for something he was predestined to do? If we're going to ask such a question and truly want the answer, we need to sit up straight. And we need to take the answer God gives us like mature Christians, if we're going to ask it. And what is the answer that God gives? Well, recall that something similar is discussed in Romans chapter 9. Now remember, and you can turn in your Bibles to Romans 7, but remember Romans chapter 9, preceding Romans chapter 9, excuse me. St. Paul is taught that if a person wanted to be redeemed by keeping the law of God, then such a person would find himself failing and falling woefully short of God's standards. And thus he would have no hope. In chapter seven, Paul describes living a life in which we want to do right We want to do the right thing, and yet we do not do it. We know what is wrong to do, and yet we find ourselves doing just that. He ends up crying out to Jesus at the end of the chapter. And in chapter 8, things turn around because Paul shows how the Christian life can be lived by the power of the Holy Spirit. There does not need to be a concern of how the law condemns, because the Christian is not bound by the law, but made free by the Spirit. And then in chapter 9. In chapter 9, Paul begins to teach the difference between those who are truly the chosen people of God and those who are not. Those who are chosen of God live by the power of the Holy Spirit, whereas the impostors are people who think they are in God's favor and are not, because they live by their flesh and not by the Spirit. By living in the flesh, they're trying to earn God's favor. But as Paul has already shown, that is not possible. Only living in the Spirit, living by the power of the Holy Spirit, can the people of God find peace. And from this discussion, Paul naturally follows the logical conclusion that there are some people who live by the flesh, and always by the flesh, and there are some by the spirit. and only overcome by the Spirit, and the two groups are exclusive from one another. And to explain this exclusiveness of people of the flesh and people of the Spirit, Paul uses an example of Holy Scripture. He points to the sons of Rebecca, and he comments that before those children were born, Neither one having done good or evil, but instead for the purpose of God to be fulfilled, it was God's choice that the younger, that the older, excuse me, serve the younger. Paul then quotes the unexpected words from the prophet Malachi, Jacob I have loved, Esau I have hated. Again, this was God's decision before the twins were born. He chose to love Jacob and he chose to hate Esau. Anticipating what everyone who read his letter would question, Paul next says, is there unrighteousness with God? That's a rhetorical question. But he answers it to be certain that no one would ever consider such a thing. Certainly not, he said. And to explain this further, Paul then quotes from Exodus, where God spoke to Moses, so that Moses would know him better. And he says this. I will have mercy on whomever I will have mercy. I will have compassion on whomever I will have compassion. And this makes sense, of course, because if God is that by which nothing greater can be conceived, then he has every authority to do as he sees fit. Paul then piles on this argument about the superiority of God's will by recalling his words to Pharaoh that explained that King Pharaoh was raised to a stature Raised to a stature because God wanted to use him to reveal God's true glory to his people. And with that point made, Paul anticipates the question we had asked before. How can Judas be blamed and punished for something he was predestined to do? The answer is what Paul gave to the Romans when he said this. But indeed, O man, who are you to reply against God? Who are you to ask such a question? For you who have ears to hear, you recognize that this is a similar answer to the one God gave Job. When Job questioned the wisdom of God allowing Job to suffer, God started by asking Job, Where were you when I created the heavens and the earth? And God continues with such questioning upon Job to make it clear to Job that he is not at the vantage point of being able to ask God such questions. And neither are we. Job couldn't understand the will of God regarding his suffering. Moses couldn't understand it regarding the hardening of Pharaoh's heart. And we can't understand it regarding the predestined betrayal by Judas against Jesus. There are, as Paul underscores, vessels, which are people made for honor, and vessels, people made for dishonor. That is the way of it. And we, you and I, are in no position to question the morality of it. The fact that we are in no position to question the morality or wisdom of Judas being predestined to betray Jesus and thus be a son of hell This connects us to the example of Jesus washing the feet of his disciples. Because when Jesus told us to do likewise, he told us to be humble. We are to take on the humility of Jesus, exemplified by Jesus washing his disciples' feet, and the quickest way, the quickest way we are to be humbled is to understand that Judas And not John betrayed Jesus. That it was Judas and not Matthew who betrayed Jesus. It was Judas and not James who betrayed Jesus, and it was Judas and not me and not you who betrayed Jesus. Only by God's will did anyone but Judas betray Jesus. And you and I are to be humbled by that. We are not Quisling or Benedict Arnold or Absalom or Judas because God chose to be merciful to us. That is humbling. And beloved, while the million-dollar athlete says that he isn't humbled by losing because humility is for losers. And while the million-dollar politician doesn't confess his sins because confessing sins is being humble, and being humble is for losers And entertainers who think that their gift to sing, gift to dance, gift to act are all three, is all because those gifts were given to them by them. We know differently. Humble yourself in the sight of the Lord, the scripture says. And don't worry. Don't worry about being in such a humble state. For the scripture says also that if you do that, if you humble yourself in the sight of the Lord, He will lift you up. He will lift you up. And so we say, Lift us up, Lord Jesus. But first we humble ourselves before you. Let us pray

sermons.title: The Love Standard
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Seed it. Please open your Bibles and turn to John chapter 13. Beginning at the 31st verse, you'll be well served as usual to do so as we go through the Gospel of John We are approaching the text this morning a little differently as I will be commenting On some details going from verse to verse, and then we will hear a summary message of what God has for us. So let's look at John thirteen, starting at verse thirty-one. The person described here As having gone out is of course Judas, the betrayer, and thus Jesus is left with the unsure eleven. Where Jesus says the Son of Man is glorified, he uses the errorist tense, which communicates to us that his glorification has been set. It's been settled. Later in John 17, 10, he says that he has been glorified, and again that means completed in the lives of his disciples. That God is glorified in Jesus is later described by St. Paul to the Colossians as Jesus is described as having been hidden inside God. In such descriptions we have the truth that these are two separate persons, but indeed one God. Verse 32. The first part speaks of mutual glorification, which we can easily understand. The words glorify him immediately are referring to the Father glorifying the Son straight away. The death, resurrection, and ascension of Jesus is near enough that Jesus can touch it, and he is making thus a triumphant statement. Verse 33. This is a very special point in the gospel, as Jesus chooses for the first and only time Such gentle words as little children. He uses this to refer to his disciples, and he seems to be expressing what has been welling up in his heart about them He cares more deeply for his disciples than any man has ever cared for other men. And he may be concerned, calling them little children, that soon they will feel like orphans But only for a time. He needs to remind them of the warning he had given them before Where he is going is the cross. It is the grave. It is his descent into hell. These places they cannot come with him. However, they will walk their own paths. Verse 34. The phrase prior to this verse sets them up for what they are going to be doing and continually doing while Jesus goes where they cannot go. Now I say to you, a new commandment I give you that you love one another. Regarding the base of such a commandment, there is nothing new here. God commanded the Israelites to love one another as if they would love themselves. Love your neighbor as yourself, he told them in Leviticus nineteen. God's standard for his people has always been to love one another. But it is what is said next that makes this commandment Jesus gives, oh, so very new. Jesus said, As I have loved you, that you also love one another. The standard has been raised. We are not to love one another as we would want to be loved anymore. But instead, Jesus told us we are to love in a greater manner. His His manner. Verse 35. There is nothing grammatical to point out in this verse. It is a straightforward truth. And it is, I believe, in the age in which we now live. The best means of evangelism we can offer this world is to love one another. Verse 36. In this verse we are to notice that Peter has passed over what Jesus has just said. Peter ignored it completely and refers back to where Jesus is going. Peter was not listening, and he was not believing the words of Jesus, but instead trusted in his own courage, which we know now that it was no courage at all. Verse 37. Jesus had told his disciples that they were to lay down their lives for him and his kingdom earlier. Peter believed he was ready at a moment's notice. Verse 38. By answering Peter in the form of a question, Jesus is not doubting the sincerity of Peter. He is trying to show Peter that he lacks self-awareness and he lacks fortitude. The meaning of the cock crowing is a little confusing in the New King James, I think. It's simply saying that within the time that the cock crows, within those times, Peter will deny him three times. It is a prophecy, and it most certainly will be fulfilled Juxtaposition is a fancy word coming from the Latin and the Greek. It refers to the close placement of two things. And in literature, it refers to two stories that are close together for a purpose, for a particular meaning. In our reading from John, we are to notice the juxtaposition of Jesus telling his disciples to love one another as he has loved them, and then the story of Peter's hubris. And Jesus prophesying that Peter would deny him three times. And Peter doing so, he was not loving Jesus Along with the examining of the meaning of those two stories, we can examine the closeness of the story of Judas betraying Jesus and Jesus telling his disciples to love one another. Well let us take the latter mention juxtaposition first. Judas, we are told, had just left the remaining eleven disciples with Jesus. And it was not until Judas was gone that Jesus gave this new commandment The reason for waiting must have been that Judas could not have been included in this command, for Judas had already turned his heart over to greed, to power, and to self-love. The devil had entered Judas, and thus Judas had not the capability to love in the manner Jesus commanded. The type of love Christians are to practice to one another is the most unique type of love For it is to be done with the love of Jesus toward one another, our brothers and our sisters in God's family. When when renowned atheist Christopher Hitchens, now deceased, when he debated Christians, he would challenge his opponents and audiences to come up with an act of charity that a Christian could perform that an atheist could not He thought he was being rather whimsical, making a good point that atheists can feed the hungry, care for the sick, and provide for the homeless with altruistic motives just like Christians do, and thus making Christianity unnecessary. But the rebuttal to that argument is quite an easy one The rebuttal was and is that Christians can care for the hungry, the sick, and the homeless with the love of Jesus. And thus bring glory to God while an atheist cannot. And the reason or motive as to why a person performs an act of kindness Or love does matter. Motive matters. It matters in the kingdom of God. So an atheist does an act of kindness because he or she wants to feel better about his or herself, or maybe they just simply care about their fellow human being. And all that is fine But when love is expressed in the name of Jesus, the heavens rejoice, and God is honored, and that is more than just fine. And now we can add to that point and say that not only can Christians do acts of love in a greater manner than an atheist because our acts give glory to God We can also say that we Christians can share a love for one another that the world cannot, for two Christians cannot Loving one another and performing acts of love for one another, bring twice the love of Jesus and twice the amount of honor to God. And that is not bragging. That's just saying what's true Well the next section of juxtaposition is to recognize that Jesus gives the command to his disciples to love one another by a standard of his love for them just after he tells them that he will be going away And where he is going, they cannot go. He tells them to love one another so that they do not split apart from one another due to his absence. And dear Christians, are we not in the same position today? The church has been in this situation since Jesus ascended into heaven. We are to be practicing the love of God toward one another, to encourage one another not to lose heart, but to wait until Jesus returns. And because a day is as a thousand years and a thousand years as a day from God's perspective, Jesus may return today, or he may return a thousand years from today. And so while we wait for him, we are to be loving one another. And the effect of loving one another is so that we do not lose heart and we do not give up waiting. Another effect is that the world will witness our love for one another, and that's an opportunity for them to love the Savior we love. I ask you, why is the church so weak today And if you do not think it is weak, consider that the Christian Church, with all of its denominations, with all of its mega churches and traditions of men Does not have a clear, distinct voice for the culture in which we live. No one is asking, what do the Christians think? No politician today is having a strategy meeting for policy making or campaign planning and asking, what does the Christian Church say today? There is no direct liaison for the Christian faith to the President of the United States to tell him what Christians believe about the moral issues of the day. The only body close to getting there is the Roman Catholic Church. And we haven't had a president ever that I'm aware of that has made policy because of the council of the Pope So why is the church so weak today? We are weak because we are inconsistent theologically, morally, and we are too fractured And why are we too fraction? Because we don't practice loving one another as Jesus command. Let us rehearse what love is when practiced. Remember, it is long suffering. We are to be long suffering with one another. We are to to put up with one another We are to stay in relationships with one another, even when what we say or do to another is not lovable, it's not likable, and it might just be plain annoying. And while the secular world makes jokes and writes skits about loud talkers or soft talkers, or those who always have stories of one upmanship, or those who have body odor, or those who are shy, or those who are obnoxious. Those are the people Christians accept and befriend because love is long suffering. Love is also kind. And being kind is included with long-suffering, but is also going out of our way to care about someone who has had a really bad, horrible day. And it's not fun to listen to someone who's had a really bad, horrible day, but it is kind. And such kindness shows that you care. And I can testify that when you struggle liking someone, you need to start simply being kind to them. Find ways to be kind to them and you will start to like them and guess what? You'll start to care. Love does not envy. Loving another person includes wanting and hoping the best for that other person, even if what they are blessed with is what we've always wanted, and maybe it's more than we've ever wanted. We may try to coach ourselves up not to envy someone because I just don't know what bad part of their life they have going on, and so they might have it equaled out like I do. But that's only to make ourselves feel better. Love does not envy because God has blessed a person, and that means it is God's will that that person is blessed, and therefore we are happy for that person because God's will is being done. Love rejoices when others rejoice. Love does not parade itself. It is not puffed up. The love we have, and the love we are to give to others understands by faith that all things come from God, and thus what I have is God's. If I can publicly speak well, that is from God. If I can run fast, that is from God. If I get a high-paying job, that is from God. If I am pretty, if I am musical, if I have more faith, all of it is from God I'm reminded of an exchange that was took place between Dallas Maverick owner Mark Cuban and one-time NBA great Shaquille O'Neal Shaq, as he is called, questioned the business acumen of Cuban by stating that he simply got lucky in the dot-com era. Well Cuban shot back something like yeah and Shaq worked really hard to be seven feet tall. By such a remark, Cuban does well to reveal the absurdity of one person thinking he is better than another based on what he has been given. And love knows that intuitively. Love does not behave rudely. Practicing love is never being rude, because those who are rude are only thinking about themselves. Love thinks about others first, and that means that love does not seek its own. In a conversation, love does not pretend to listen only to say what they want to say. Love does not enter a business relationship or a friendship because of what can be gained, but instead what can be given. Love does not say, oh, I know what I said hurt people, but I feel better about myself by saying. If something if someone is doing, saying or acting for self, it is not love. Love is not provoked as it thinks no evil. It thinks no evil Love says that I know you did not say that to hurt me, so I am not going to be hurt and I'm not going to be upset at you. Love does not look to be offended, but instead expects to be encouraged. Love does not expect to be ignored, but instead expects to be honored. And if the Christian is ignored by another Christian, well that Christian that was ignored is quite certain that that other Christian must be going through a difficult time, must be taken up with urgent matters, and meant no malice. It takes great effort to expect positive motivation of others, but love makes the effort. Love rejoices in the truth. The truth may be hard to hear. It may be that a person has been harmed by what you said or did, and therefore a person of love is glad to know that he has a chance to apologize and be reconciled. The truth may be that the sin, the problem, the failure is your own, but the love of God re compels you to repent, compels you to make peace and be in good standing with all men. Love bears all things, especially the shortcomings of others, because love overlooks a multitude of sins. Love believes all things, all things including the best from one another, and God's promises Love hopes for all things. All things is hoping the best for one another and for God's promises. Love endures all things. When others don't think well of you, love endures. When others do have malice toward you, love endures. When others don't bear all things, believe all things, or hope for all things, the love of Christ in you will. The final juxtaposition of these stories in John thirteen Is the command of Jesus to love one another just before Jesus tells Peter that Peter's love will fail and that he will deny Jesus. And the closeness of these words exchanged teach us that love practice towards one another is loving a sinner. Notice that there is no shunning, there's no belittling of Peter, although Jesus knew of his weaknesses, and thus he knew sin was inevitable. Love does not avoid sinners or ignore sin, but acknowledges the value of the sinner and the reality of the sin. Only the love of God can care for a sinner as Jesus cares for Peter. And we are to have that love for one another. We are to love one another knowing we are loving a sinner. And we are to love one another knowing that that person will sin against us. And I will sin against them. We will hurt each other, disappoint each other, even leave some scars on one another, and still we're to love one another This call, this command, this standard to love one another as Jesus loved us. is another example of the silliness offered by non-believers who argue that Christianity is a made-up religion so that we might be comforted By a make-believe father figure. That was Freud's argument. But who would make up such a command, a standard as this? If it were made up by one of us, surely we would make it an easier standard. If I was to make up the words Jesus had said, I would have said, I command you a repeat commandment, just don't kill each other. And it would still be difficult, but not as difficult as loving one another as Jesus has loved us. No, this is not made up. The standard is real and it is high. Jesus said to his disciples, and he says to us Love one another as I have loved you, so you are to love one another. And we are to say, thy will be done. Amen? Amen. Let us pray.

sermons.title: Protecting Our Women
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: Imagine that you can actually do the internet basically. May the words of my mouth and the meditation of our hearts be acceptable in thy sight, O Lord, our strength and our redeemer. In the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost. Amen. May be seated. This being Mother's Day, we are veering off from studying the gospel according to Saint John. And as we do, I want you to keep in mind both Deuteronomy passage, Deuteronomy 6, our reading this morning, which is a warning. And then from 2 Timothy 3, which is a depiction of the culture in which we live today. I'd like to address this morning our culture's shortcoming when it comes to how we treat women. Along this line of of thinking, I did some research on how we treat women today as compared to what was expected of Both women and men back as far as the eighteen hundreds. Did you know That in the 1800s it was thought to be unladylike for a woman to yell in any social context? It was socially expected that a woman of a certain body type and temperament would marry a man who would complement her and Her hymn. For example, women with red hair and a flushed complexion were thought to be excitable and hot-tempered So they should marry someone with jet black hair and of a mild temperament A woman with the features of a man should marry a man with features that are more similar to a woman, and so on. Also, it was not ladylike to initiate a visit with a gentleman unless he was an invalid. Now moving to a century later, in Vogue magazine, 1948, the public was given these golden nuggets of advice. Quote A man should always offer a woman a cigarette when he takes one himself, but if she has refused by saying only, not just now, thank you He must repeat the offer every time he decides to have another cigarette for himself. And then this Deference toward older women is a point of good behavior. Women rise when an older woman enters the room unless there are more than ten or twelve present. And then this, I love this one. Regarding dance parties. Quote, it is not difficult for an older woman to accept the fact that she is not the universal ideal of the of a dancing partner. But it is not at all easy for young girls. When the situation seems completely out of hand, when there are no friends sitting in groups and no boys anywhere in sight, And everyone else is dancing gaily, the best thing to do is go home. And next, these are from a 1955 guide on being a good housewife, 1955. When the husband arrives home, quote, let him talk first. Remember, his topics of conversation are more important than yours. And this one. Don't complain if he's home for dinner late or even if he stays out all night. Count this as a minor compared to what he may have gone through throughout the day. And this one tops it off. Quote, don't ask him questions about his actions or question his judgment or integrity. Remember he's the master of the house, and as such will always exercise his will with fairness and truthfulness, you have no right to question him. Now, if such was preached in the church today, the preacher only needs to add Ephesians 5:22: Wives submit to your husbands as to the Lord, and the result would be every woman leaving the service. Serveth with service with their mouth agape and the husband with a smile. This past fall, I spent time reading blogs that were arguing about a certain type of marital relationship that was more biblical and thus more glorifying to God than other views of how a couple should be. should entertain one another in marriage. Complementarianism is very popular in conservative Christian circles. It argues that men and women are equal in value, but have very different roles in marriage, and that these roles complement one another, and they are not to be confused. Nor to be crossed over. Complementarianism tries to avoid the negative connotations of words like hierarchy and patriarchy. And yet some argue they are all the same. The base of complementarianism is the acceptance of the biblical role of the husband doing the leading and the wife doing the submitting. And everything else comes under those primary rules. And some take complementarianism so far as to believe that such roles should also be played out in the social world as well. You shouldn't have any woman as a CEO and certainly not a president. The reaction to this type of teaching is Christian egalitarianism, where men and women are seen as equal in value and equal in responsibility. Some even teach matriarchalism, where the biblical language of men leading and women submitting is completely rejected, and women are seen in this case as spiritually superior. I don't venture into such public discussions about such subjects because, first, I do not think that they are fruitful for the church. We have lost the cultural battles over abortion and homosexual unions. We are losing the battle over bathroom etiquette and women in combat. And all the while, prominent bloggers are arguing over whether women should be the boss over a man in a local corner grocery store, and the extreme position of whether women need men in the church at all. The second reason I don't get involved is that I do not think it is that complicated As I was lamenting to Mr. Mark Hammett last fall about my readings, he said to me in a dry tone, Men love their wives as Christ loved the church. Women submit to their husbands as under the Lord. That sounds like enough. And I echo that and say it is enough indeed. I had a chance to speak to the FCA Fellowship of Christian Athletes at Stevenson University and McDonough School both last week. And I took the opportunity to argue with these young minds that there are absolute moral values, the existence of absolute moral values. In the troubled waters of our culture, there are no strong rocks, no moral absolutes that people can cling to when they are confused. And so I've taught that there are moral absolutes that every culture agrees upon. And they are the same absolutes. We only differ, hear this, we only differ on application. And so we may have differences between cultures on how to apply the moral value of something such as modesty. But every culture has an understanding of the moral value of modesty. It's just how they apply it And it is the same way of thinking with Christians and the biblical values of distinct manhood and distinct womanhood. All Christians have such concepts of what a man should be and do and what a woman should be and do. What we argue about is the application, not the values themselves. Now when I'm speaking about Christians arguing, I'm not talking or including those who are very liberal and are already apostate, not believing the gospel at all, although they may still call themselves Christians. Their lamp has gone out, and it is a waste to knock on their door. They are not part of our discussion I briefly mentioned two, two so-called political issues of today. Gender-neutral bathrooms and women in the military. I mention them because I want to use them to illustrate this morning what God has placed upon my heart on this Mother's Day. I also want you to understand that this pulpit is not silent about contemporary issues I very much want to speak to contemporary issues, but I find that they happen so often and so fast. That if I use this pulpit every Sunday to address what is going on out of our walls, I would neglect the Holy Scriptures. And I cannot neglect the Holy Scriptures. But this Sunday, we're making an exception in terms of addressing what is going on outside our walls. This is the Lord's Day. And it is also Mother's Day. And I want to honor the Lord on His day by honoring the women he has placed in our lives who show us A special side of God's love. Nobody loves like a God-fearing mother. Can I get an Amen? Consider what is at the heart of the political and moral issue of gender-neutral bathrooms or bathrooms Where establishments allow for people who are of one gender but identify with another gender, use the same bathroom facility, the gender that they identify with Instead of the bathroom that is anatomically designed for them. What makes such a dilemma a moral-political issue In the positive, in the positive, I believe it is the virtue of mercy that is involved. The virtue of mercy. The political liberal will label it tolerance. But when tolerance is practiced, not to make a political statement, which is mostly why tolerance is brought up, to make a political statement But when it is only to be kind, when it's only to be kind, tolerance then becomes a subcategory under mercy. It is carrying about the least, the most disenfranchised among us. Or so it seems that way. And this is where the devil has been very clever. He disguises being understanding and then kind to people who are struggling with gender identity. And force a confused culture to accommodate the even more confused. But according to Holy Scripture, such accommodation is not wise. A confused person is a double-minded person, and a double-minded person is unstable in all of his or her ways. The conservatives say that by opening up bathrooms as a choice, you allow for the perverts to take advantage of women and children. Transgender people, gender-confused, and their defenders say that transgender people and gender-confused people are not necessarily perverts any more than a heterosexual is a pervert. They are simply different. And wisdom says that the point isn't the point isn't that transgender people and gender-confused people are perverts. It is that the policy of allowing anyone to use any designated bathroom or to have no designation at all is to give opportunity for perverts to be perverted. Whether they be transgender, gender-confused, homosexual, pedophile, ethobophiles, hepophiles, didn't know there was such a thing, or more common, simply a male teenager who wants to get his thrills. Or a perverted 50-year-old who wants to get his thrills. They all can be perverts who want to expose women and children. To give opportunity for such is simply not wise, and it most certainly does not protect women and children. Now what I uphold to you today is God's standard for protecting women. Hear this from 1 Peter 3. Likewise, husbands, live with your wives in an understanding way. Showing honor to the woman as a weaker vessel, since they are heirs with you of the grace of life, so that your prayers may not be hindered. I am too constrained with time to dissect all that is said here by Peter, other than to underline that the phrase weaker vessel includes physical strength. God has given men the capacity for greater physical strength, greater than women, and as Christians we do not need a new chapter and a new verse in the Bible to conclude. That we are to use said strength to protect women. Especially the women God has placed in our lives. Hear this from St. Paul. But if anyone does not provide for his relatives and especially for the members of his household, he has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever. And without question, what is included in the provision men are to attain for their families is protection, physical protection. Physical protection from anyone who would try to do them harm in any context To the Ephesians, where St. Paul made that supposedly so difficult command, wives submit to your husbands, he then says this. In the same way, husbands should love their wives as their own bodies. He who loves his wife loves himself. So just as we men protect our own bodies, so are we to protect the bodies and the dignity and the reputation and the privacy of our wives. Well, protecting even more. We are to protect even more because we are to love our wives as Jesus loves his church. And Jesus loves his church by laying down his life and fighting the enemy of his church and by playing the watchman. Playing the watchman to see that no one dishonors her Where our culture has failed our women by making them vulnerable in a restroom, we must counter by finding ways to make them feel safe and be safe. What those countermeasures are is a different application according to each home and each man's ability. There will be different applications in each different household. And I would even encourage, if we have a chance to boycott, to boycott. But the principle I point to us to this morning, the truth that I point us to this morning, is to protect our women. It is the responsibility of godly men to sacrificially protect their women. Now regarding women in combat, as many of you have heard Our military leaders have been discussing the likelihood of allowing women to participate in combat side by side with men. And that has now led to the discussion and the likelihood of requiring our young women to register for the draft when they turn 18 years of age. These moves are purposeful to blur the sexes, treating our society as it were androgynous. Let us first acknowledge that God used women such as Jael, as recorded in the Holy Scriptures, to drive a tent peg through the skull of a wicked army commander. He used Deborah to be a leader of his people when no man would step forward and take the responsibility. But these are exceptions and never written in Scripture to be understood as the norm or what would be the norm someday Such women are to be honored, and such men who were cowardly enough not to take responsibility should be shamed. We have already rehearsed the passages from Scripture that teach the duties of men to include physically protecting women. In the Old Testament, there were laws and plays to protect young daughters from being taken advantage of. For example, a daughter who made a pledge that was later proved to be to her disadvantage was given the right to get out of the pledge by the authority of her father. And this, a father was instructed specifically not to give his daughters over to serve the ungodly. And the sexual purity of a daughter was the lawful duty of her father. And these responsibilities of guarding our young women only strengthen what the New Testament commands regarding protecting our women. And treating them as young men and sending them to fight the battles of men is not protecting them. When visiting excuse me when visiting Israel, we had the experience of witnessing young girls carrying around automatic weapons. In Israel, every young person, male or female, ages 18 to 21, are to serve in the military in some capacity. If you witnessed the slideshow that we shared in our visit, you heard Bobby Lynn and I joke of the oddity of witnessing these young women carrying around guns that we had a hard time imagining they could handle. But such is the norm in Israel. It is the norm because every nation around them would like to see them overrun by Islamic jihad And every citizen, Jew and Christian in Israel, they want dead or enslaved. We can all understand that drastic measures require drastic action. When you are outnumbered and you believe in your survival, you train everyone to fight in order to protect what you have. When the enemy is closing in, men protect their women. And when the men are gone, women protect their children. That comes natural to all cultures. But the culture of the United States is not in such a situation, not even close. To treat our daughters as we do our sons is foolish, unwarranted, and most of all cowardly. As Greg Gibson and Owen Scratchon stated in an article titled, We Will Never Let Our Daughters Die For Us. Quote, any man who would ask his wife or daughter to endure the horrors of war to protect him has missed the very core of biblical manhood and Christ's own example as the savior of his bride. Lieutenant Josh Devers, our own Josh, sent me that article. And he is a man, as you know, that has three daughters to protect, a man who has seen the enemy and what the enemy would do to his daughters if they captured them. It is a passion of his to protect them as it should be. In another article written by a man by the name of Matt Walsh, also a father of daughters. This position is taken. Quote My daughter will not sign up for the draft, no matter what the government says. If it becomes law, I will break the law and do so proudly. I will not allow my daughter to be a part of this national disgrace. And if that means we must leave the United States altogether, good riddance. I honestly do not want to live in a country that uses its women as human shields. You have to love the passion and the courage of such a statement. It is a godly passion. While it is true, and I hate this, but while it is true that men can disguise themselves inside a church That upholds the biblical standard of men leading and women submitting, he can hide in the church so that he can abuse his wife. Why, that is a reality That does not discredit what the scripture clearly states. Men are to lead. And that includes protecting women And I add that any man who abuses his wife, or any woman for that matter, is a cowardly sinner who should be publicly shamed. And this should be the conclusion of all God-fearing men who know that their first responsibility is to protect their women. Moses Lewis, in his quite prophetic book, The Abolition of Man. Stated that the final stage of eugenics, which is modern science by the way of prenatal conditioning and by education and by propaganda, based on perfectly applied psychology, having obtained full control over himself, can then win the battle over human nature. He then can make the species whatever he wants it to be. Lewis says, the battle will indeed be won, but who precisely will have won it? What is the victory? For the power of man to make himself what he pleases means that, as we have seen, the power of some men to make other men, and that includes women, what they please them to be. Our culture with its pseudoscience is trying to make our women to be men While there are many things that our culture does that appall us Christians, and yet we do not interfere, I say this is not one of those things. They will not do as they please with the daughters of our Heavenly Father. Men of God are called to protect, first protect our women. So let us, Christian Church, as the Christian church and as Christian men within the church, let us say, Happy Mother's Day. As a pledge that we will protect our women as Jesus called us to do. We will not allow men to make our women what they please. But instead what God has intended. And I ask of all of our men to say, Amen. Let us pray.

sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: The Holy Ghost. Amen. Be seated. Heaven is a wonderful place filled with glory and grace. I want to see my safe. your space. Heaven is a wonderful place. I want to be there. You know, if I was preaching that in South Carolina, you would have joined in with me. You can try it again. Do you know the words? You really do. Heaven is a wonderful place filled with glory and grace. I wanna see. Be my Saviour's face. Heaven is a wonderful place. I wanna be dead. That's a brown circle. The rising interest regarding socialism among college-age students today is surprising. On one hand, because it has not been so long that we cannot Point to the corruption and to the downfall of the Soviet Union as an example of what a society ought not to do. And the cultures of North Korea under A socialist oppressive regime, and the Cuban government, with their socialist poverty, provide for us immediate examples of why socialism does not work. Convinced that socialism is the devil's scheme to convince cultures that heaven can be created by humanity on earth It is to believe that mankind can create a utopia in which all persons have all earthly cares provided for while living within peace with one another. But we know, as Christians who believe in the Holy Scriptures, that the sinful nature of mankind cannot create a utopia. We have, we will, and we do. Turn upon one another. In 1534, a group, 1534, 17 years removed from the beginning of the Reformation. A group of Anabaptists took over the city of Munster in Germany, proclaiming it to be a haven for Baptists who rejected Roman Catholic rule and who were bound to together by the belief in adult adult baptism only, in order to be saved. And they believed that all valuable goods and foods should be shared equally among the inhabitants of the city. The city was named the New Jerusalem. It was named that by its inhabitants. And well over 1,000 new residents flocked. To this walled city. Flock to what they understood to be a heaven on earth The city was soon besieged, however, by a Roman Catholic bishop who wanted to take his city back for the church. Meanwhile, an internal rebel. Rebellion took place within the city walls, resulting in a self-proclaimed Gideon having his head cut off and placed on a spike on the city wall, giving warning to anyone inside and out of this new Jerusalem that it will not be torn down. Next, a self-proclaimed David was given full authority within the city wall. And with that full authority, he proclaimed that he had received a new vision from God that allowed men to take on multiple wives. He then proceeded to marry in 1680. young ones of his own. Within a year the siege took its toll, and with the people starving, the gates had to be opened, and the leaders of the city were captured And imprisoned. So much for a heaven on earth Communities that try to resemble heaven are not possible because heaven by definition is the place that Jesus prepares people that is full of comfort and prosperity and peace and final freedom from sin and death Humanity has no possible means of providing such a setting for itself. And each time a group of people try such a community, a leader goes mad with power. Each community is like those who tried to build the Tower of Babel that they thought would protect them from all of their enemies, including natural disasters. But to come down. And he brings them down himself In John 14, which I encourage you to turn to now, in John fourteen, verse one, Jesus describes heaven proper. Heaven described by Jesus truly is a wonderful place. Jesus does this description of heaven, gives this description of heaven on the healing. Of Peter being overconfident that he would die for the Lord, and then Jesus responding by prophesying that Peter would instead fail Jesus and fail then himself. And I want you to note. that it is on the heels of that because whenever you and I hear John 1, we usually hear it in the context of a funeral sermon. Let's read a passage that gives us hope for heaven. But we have to notice that Jesus gave that hope in the context of Peter denying. Let not your heart be troubled, Jesus says. What a wonderful hope to be given to a man who would fail and fail miserably. Let not your heart be troubled. In the midst of your failure, let not your heart be troubled. In the midst of your sin that seems to count you out, let not your heart be troubled. In the wake of your Denial of Jesus, let not your hearts be troubled. Those words are for all of us. All who have sinned. All who have had their guilt removed are told these same words. Let not your heart be troubled. He goes then to prepare heaven for us because Heaven, he says, is a real place. Today, as you already have known, because of the colors around you and our song sung, we celebrate the Godhead, sending the Holy Spirit to dwell amidst the church and to dwell with And so, in honor of that celebration and in light of Jesus' teaching here in John 14, this says that the Spirit of truth will come and be in the midst of God's people. I start this sermon by saying that because of the Holy Spirit, because of the Holy Spirit, you and I, we can keep our eyes on the heavenly prize. Because Jesus gives the promise of heaven in the context of prophesying Peter's denial of Jesus, we can underline the importance of keeping heaven before us as our ultimate prize. To be sure, there are earthly rewards that are joyful to receive. A prize from school, a promotion at work, a plaque from the lodge, a trophy for the league. championship. All of these are to be praised in this life. But nothing that is rewarded in this life can compare to our heavenly reward. As one Christian pop singer stated, if Jesus went to prepare a place for us, and he is still preparing a place for us, then this must be a garbage dump compared to what he is waiting for. for for us in heaven. Whenever I am feeling defeated in this life, I can always look to the promised heavenly reward and be encouraged Whenever I am dissatisfied in this life, I can always know that heaven will indeed satisfy. Whenever I am discontented in what this life offers, my countenance can be lifted up, knowing that all All I need and more, more than I can ask for or imagine, is awaiting us in heaven. And it is the Holy Spirit who can take me to that state of hope, and this allows me to not get bogged down in the mire in which this fallen world would have me wallow. The Holy Spirit helps me rise above the mire of this world when my eyes see heaven as my reward. And next we see that because of the Holy Spirit, the Father and the Son are always with us. The statement that Jesus makes in verse 6 should be memorized by every Christian, for it truly is what separates the Christian faith from all other religions, and it is what every Christian ought to know. Jesus is not just one way to the Heavenly Father and thus one way to heaven. He is the only way. That cannot be said enough, for it flies directly in the face of compromising churches, and it flies in the face of all other religions. Because of this statement by Jesus, Christians cannot accept the sentiment that all religions are the same or that all religions lead to the same God. They are not the same and they do not lead to the same. But the devil would be happy if you came to such a conclusion. Now Philip in our gospel reading evidently didn't pick up on the significance of what Jesus said, that he's the only way. Philip focused on wanting to see the Father in heaven. And Jesus is disappointed that Philip did not recognize that to see Jesus was to see the Father, thus the Father was in Jesus. And here is another reason why we Christians embrace the doctrine of trin the Trinity, that the three are one and the one are three. When Jesus is with us, the Father is with us, and the Holy Spirit is with us, for the The Holy Spirit, the third person of the Godhead, is the presence of the Father and the presence of the Son, and in and of itself its presence among us. Last summer, I had a good laugh from my son Isaac when the extended family was gathered for a wedding down in North Carolina. And as we tend to do as a family sitting around talking theology, and one member of the family, who I shall not name, claimed that she did not like how Christians talk about Jesus being in their heart and using such language as asking Jesus into your heart She pointed out that Jesus is not in your heart, he is in heaven, seated at the right hand of the Father. What Isaac said that made me laugh was, but that's a technicality. Saying Jesus is not in your heart but in heaven at the right. right hand of the Father is a technicality. For the two and the Holy Spirit are one in substance. Theologically, because if you have seen the Son, you have seen the Father, the same can be said that if you have the Holy Spirit in your heart, you also have the Son, and you have the Father. And to be sure this is a great mystery, because they are separate in person. But it is also true that you cannot have one without having both the others. The Holy Spirit enables us to have the Son. It enables us to have the Father Well next because of the Holy Spirit. Our prayers are heard by the Son and the Father. Our prayers are heard. Having just celebrated Ascension Day, we should have within our consciences the knowledge that Jesus needed to ascend to the Heavenly Father's right hand so that he could be our intercessor. He needs to be the one that pleads on our behalf because he is the one worthy to receive glory and honor and to receive honor from the Father. As it has been said, we pray by the power of the Holy Spirit to the Heavenly Father in the name of Jesus. the Son. All persons are involved in our prayers as we pray to God. When Jesus speaks about prayer in verse 12 through 15, he emphasizes what he will do. Greater works will the church do because of what Jesus will do. Which is to go to the Heavenly Father. We have access to the heavens where God the Father resides because and by way of Jesus. Whatever we ask in his name, he will do. He will do. And then he says, I will pray to the Father, and he will give you another helper, the Holy Spirit. It is his prayer, the prayer of Jesus. That is needed for us to receive the third person of the Trinity. And then Jesus says, I will not leave you orphans, I will come to you. And then he says, I will love him who keeps my commandments. I will manifest myself to him In verses twelve through twenty-one, Jesus says, I will some nine times by my count. Nine times. What he will do. Thus we are utterly dependent on what Jesus will do. Dependency is not a negative, it's not a weakness, it shouldn't be an insecurity, but the opposite of all of those things. We are dependent upon the one who is the most worthy of our trust. We are dependent upon the sinless Savior who loves us to death and beyond death. And who wants us to overcome death just as he did. And with all the confidence we need to be assured, Jesus wants the best for us. And notice how this type of love is affectionate love. It is not begrudging. It is not loving because I have to love. It is loving because I want to. And we hear the affection in Jesus calling us friends. We are his close friends. So close that he lays his life down for us and expects us to do the same for one another. Ask yourself this question. Please ask this question. Why does Jesus repeatedly teach about the need for his followers to love one another? Why does he keep bringing this up? Why is it so important that Jesus would spend so much time teaching love and explaining how we are to love one another? Could it be? Could it be that how Christians love one another is a determining factor on the effectiveness of the preaching of the gospel in the world? Is it possible that for the church to be the salt of the earth and thus prevent a culture from moral decay that Christians need to love one another? Could it be that the manner Christians love one another will actually play a role in the expedient return of Jesus? Think of that. Could it be that Christians have repeatedly underestimated the power of loving one another, the power that that has as a witness to the world that the gospel of Jesus Christ is true? That the only thing that is preventing a revival in this generation is how we are not loving one another. And I shudder considering how I have contributed to the ineffectiveness of the preaching of the gospel in this generation because I have not been good at loving one another. Loving you. Forgive me for making these points with a series of rhetorical questions, but I fail to know how better to say what needs to be said. Is a Christian loving another Christian when he or she gossips or complains about the other? Is a Christian loving another Christian when he or she withholds forgiveness and chooses instead to hold a grudge? Is a Christian loving another Christian when he or she dislikes a trait in that other Christian and therefore decides to make that other Christian feel inadequate and exclude them Is a Christian loving another Christian by choosing to disfellowship with said Christian? Is a Christian loving another Christian when he or she rejects the ecclesiastical leadership God has placed over them? Are we doing this? Is this happening now? Yes, we are, and yes it is. Beloved, do not leave the friendship of a fellow Christian without being in good fellowship with him or her. Do not leave a group of Christian friends without them knowing that you still care for them and that you are still friends with them. Do not separate yourself from a body of believers unless there is sin that they won't repent of or because God is calling you to some geographical distance. Do not speak about other Christians disparagingly. Do not think of yourself better, a better Christian than others. Be humble, be humble. Consider Why Jesus repeats again the commandment for Christians to love one another after he teaches that he chooses his followers. He chose us. We have earned nothing. We have been wise about nothing. We have nothing within ourselves that would allow us to see ourselves better than another believer. And so we should love instead. Well, it is not about to get real here, for we got real. We don't ask whether this is happening now, for we know it just happened. Jesus had made the standard clear. Jesus has taught in such a manner that we cannot hold back any part of our lives from him and we cannot in any shape or form justify not loving one another Abiding in Him, keeping His commands, pleasing the Heavenly Father, and most importantly, loving one another, that is the Christian life. These are the things Christians do, or they need to stop calling themselves Christians. As was stated, there is no going through the motions this morning. But the application, the application is up to each of us individually. And so we close by saying, Lord have mercy upon us. Christ have mercy upon us. Lord have mercy upon us. Let us pray.

sermons.title: To Make Us Ready to be Hated
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.source_file: To Make Us Ready to be Hated.txt
sermons.text: In the name of the Father and of the Son. Of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Seated. Please turn in your Bibles to the Gospel according to St. John chapter 15 from our gospel reading this morning. The disciples were the first To hear the words of Jesus as read from John 15. They were the target audience regarding the suffering Jesus warned about. The hate that Jesus warned about, the martyrdom that Jesus warned about. And here is their fate. James, the brother of John, was beheaded alongside his accuser, who recanted his testimony against James and who became a Christian. Just before they were martyred together. Philip, the first to be called disciple, was scourged, thrown into prison, and later crucified in A. D. fifty-four. Matthew, the former tax collector and gospel writer, suffered martyrdom by axe and sword in A. D. 60. James the Less, brother to our Lord, was beaten and stoned, and finally had his brains dashed with a club. Matthias, the replacement of Judas, was stoned and then beheaded. Andrew, brother of Peter, was hung on a tree and next stoned to death. Peter, after being encouraged by his followers to flee the wrath of Nero, was visited by the Lord as he was walking out of the city and Jesus was walking in. Peter asked where he was going, and Jesus replied, I am come to be crucified again. Peter understood and returned to his fa to face his fate while insisting that he be crucified upside down. as he was not a worthy martyr to die in the same fashion as his Savior. Jude, also called Thaddeus, was crucified at Edessa, which is now modern Turkey In A. D. 72, Bartholomew, after spreading the gospel in India, was beaten and crucified by idolaters. Thomas, the one-time doubter, after enraging pagan priests in Parthia and in India, was martyred by the thrust of a spear. Simon, after preaching in Africa and Europe, was crucified in A. D. 74. John, the beloved writer of this gospel although cast into a cauldron of boiling oil, had his life miraculously preserved and died at an old age Knowledge of suffered persecution and martyrdom of most of the first hearers of Jesus saying, If the world hates you, You know that it hated me before it hated you. Hopefully hearing that gives us a better perspective regarding how serious Jesus was in his warning. And what it was like to be warned in such a manner. I want to touch logistically with you Briefly, you remember that the verses and the chapters of our Bibles were not there originally. In fact it was 1551 that they were placed in our Bibles. Therefore, I think it is best that we ignore chapter 15 and chapter 16 demarcations because we need to understand Jesus is continuing a teaching that he started quite a bit ago. Remembered that Jesus was talking about abiding in him? And then he explained that to abide in him was to obey the commandments of the heavenly father and then he said that the greatest commandment to obey is for us to love one another And notice how that sermon two weeks ago matched so well with the bishop's sermon last week. God is saying something to us and quite loudly, I believe. From talking of abiding and obeying and loving, Jesus next explains that when you do such things, the world will hate you. The word world is cosmos, and it can mean the physical world, or as in this context, the way a culture operates. Later in John's Gospel, Jesus will tell his followers that they are not of this world. And there he means that Christians do not operate the way the culture operates. And that input is added to this passage in that the world hates Christians because they do not operate in the same manner that the culture does. Or at least they shouldn't. Where the culture is unjust, the Christian is to be just. Where the culture is unloving, the Christian is to be loving. Where the culture is calling evil good and good evil. The Christian is to be calling evil evil and good good. And you have heard me say this before, but I'm going to nag you by saying it again. Christians should not be fad followers. Although some fads may be morally benign, Christians should be careful as to what they follow, for you cannot know where it will lead you. especially leads you into placing your trust into something that is not Christ. It is when we are following Christ And not following the cultural fads of the day that the world, the people of our culture, hate us. They hate us because our morality or stance against their immorality makes them feel guilty. And because they feel guilty, they want to shut us up. Even when we have said nothing but merely lived our lives differently than them. The difference bothers them, and so they want to create laws that force us to live as they do. The tragedy in Orlando last week is clear evidence as to why the world hates Christians. For as Christians, we can condemn the mass killing of people by the action of a lone gunman or a group of terrorists. And we can also condemn sodomy, even while our culture tells us that to do so is to side with the terrorists. But our culture is folding in on itself. It's folding in on itself when it tries to embrace Islam as a peaceful religion. And embrace the homosexual lifestyle as normal. For the reality is that the former has already condemned the latter, and that will not change. And Christians, the Christian faith stands back from it all and says that all need to repent and come to the cross to find forgiveness. The culture hates that because it wants all sexual behavior to be normalized and it wants all religions except Christianity to get along And when these things do not happen, the devil convinces the culture that the Christian faith, and thus the Christian church, is at fault. Such was the case when the Roman culture crumbled, and such is the case as the American culture crumbles. When a preacher applies the words of Jesus from John 15, 19 to examples of modern life, he is bound to make someone angry. But that is part of what a preacher must do to shake the sinner from his or her confused state of being. If you claim to follow Jesus and also find yourself popular amongst your unbelieving friends, your unbelieving neighbors, your unbelieving co-workers, and even your unbelieving family, then you are more like the world than you are a follower of Christ. Yes, I said that. And I said that because I don't know how to apply the words of Jesus When he says, if you were of the world, the world would love its own Jesus is not telling us, of course, to be jerks so that the world, our present culture, will hate us, but only to live out our Christian life, and that will be enough. Now, if you say in response to what I have said that you are merely a kind and considerate person to people in your life, and that is what you thought you were supposed to be, I would profoundly agree with you. I am challenging you, however, to consider why the disciples were hated. They were not jerks, they were not unkind. Realize what caused the apostles to be martyred. They spoke up. They challenged the falsehood of the gods of their culture. They claimed there was only one God. And they claim that Jesus was that God, and that mankind could not find forgiveness for their sins outside of Jesus. That is why the world hated the apostles. It was because they spoke up. And by speaking up, they rejected the manner their culture operated. Now, I have heard some of your stories, and I am well aware that some of you know what I'm talking about. As soon as you spoke up in a conversation at work against the sin of sodomy or against the sin of abortion, you felt that hate. As soon as you confessed Jesus as God to an unbelieving family, you felt that palatable social tension. And you knew that if those conversations continued and people heard what you truly believe on such issues, well, those who heard you would likely never speak to you again. It is to be understood, most especially by Christians, that speaking the truth in love and the love of Christ is necessary for people to be saved from sin and death. God spoke the world into existence. Jesus is said to be the Word. Thus God has chosen that the means by which mankind is to be saved is by the truth of the gospel being spoken. We say in our culture that the two subjects that always bring about disputes are religion and politics. And that is because words have power God made it so. Sooner or later the Christian must speak, and those words you speak will cause the world to love you or hate you. Jesus goes on to explain the necessary divide that occurs when people are faced with the choice to believe or to reject him as their savior and as God. Because people of the world do not know the Heavenly Father, they are not going to know, and the word know meaning understand or relate to They are not going to understand or relate to Jesus. And because they do not know or understand Jesus, they are not going to understand or relate to those who follow Jesus. That is the way of it. It can be no different. Because the word hate is used so frequently by Jesus, we should examine it more closely. The Greek word for hate, in its most basic meaning, means to detest. To detest is to want nothing to do with what is hated Therefore, the world, the culture, wants nothing to do with God the Father, and therefore it wants nothing to do with Jesus the Son, and therefore it wants nothing to do with those who follow Jesus. And it is of no use for the Christian to cry foul or to claim such hatred as unjust, for Jesus reminds us in verse 25 that the world hated him without a cause. Which means that they hated him unjustly, and it did not matter. Next, the mention of the Holy Spirit coming and bearing witness and the witness of the apostles as to what they had seen Jesus do. This is the counter to what the world says about Jesus, and we know the world lies about Jesus. The culture would say that Jesus was a false teacher, a pretend miracle worker, and a rebel against the state. But the Holy Spirit and the apostles as eyewitnesses were to be a continuation of the presence of Jesus in the world to save humble sinners Now as I stated earlier, we're to not see chapter 16. We're to understand this is a flowing teaching. And verse 1 of 16 is a continuation of Jesus providing his apostles this teaching that we are privy to here, a teaching that they needed in the immediacy. It was the apostles who would face immediate danger and the choice between martyrdom or to deny faith in Jesus. It was the apostles who needed to apply these words in the immediate future It was the apostles that Jesus was concerned would stumble in their faith because of how difficult the days ahead were going to be It was the apostles who were to be put out of the synagogues. It was the apostles who were killed by those who thought that they were doing God's work. It was the apostles who needed to hear that such things would come to pass and for them to accept it as the will of God. Jesus knew. Jesus knew that the devil would tempt the apostles into thinking that such persecution and such suffering and even death Could not be the will of God. And thus they must be doing something wrong if their preaching and teaching leads to such pain. And so Jesus thwarts such thinking before it can take root, telling them that, yes, indeed, this is my will for you. And sorrow. Sorrow would indeed fill the hearts of the apostles as they watched their Savior die and as they faced their own cowardice in that moment. Sorrow would indeed fill their hearts as they waited those three days. But all of it was for the good All of it was for the eternal good. And even Jesus going away after his resurrection would be for the eternal good. The Holy Spirit needed to come down. The Holy Spirit needed to empower the church in order for God's plan to redeem the world to come to pass. While all of this part of the teaching of Jesus is actually a repeat of what we have studied in John before. There is a point in these passages I want to underline for all of us. Very important. When Jesus says in verse 13 that the Holy Spirit will guide you into all truth, The word you in the Greek is plural. We don't have that in modern English We use you for singular and we use you for plural. In the King's English they use the that meant singular, you, and thou meant you plural. In the South, we know they use you all or y'all. The point of this is to identify that Jesus isn't telling his apostles that the Holy Spirit will lead them individually to the truth. But instead lead all of them together as the church to the truth. And all of them together represented the church. Thus Jesus was telling that the Holy Spirit would lead the church, his chosen people, to all truth. The application for us is that we too are guided by the Holy Spirit to all truth when we are within the church. And I am not talking about the local church, although I am. And I am not talking about the Reformed Episcopal Church, although I am And I am not talking about the Anglican Church in North America, although I am. Instead, I am talking about the church with the big C, the universal church. As long as we stay within the universal church, we are guided into all truth, no matter what happens to the culture around us. And a lot is happening in the culture around us. Although the teaching of John in chapter 15 and 16 had immediate and specific application to the apostles, the same principles apply to Christians of all cultures of all eras.
