He said, and you shall remember the whole way that the Lord your God has led you these 40 years in the wilderness, that he might humble you. Testing you to know what is in your heart, whether you would keep his commandments or not. We can say from this that God tests us to show us our own character, to show us our own hearts. He knows our character, he knows our hearts. God tests us so that we can see ourselves and hopefully be humbled by what we see, and hopefully see our need for a Savior to forgive us and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness. The fact that God tests us is clear in the New Testament. In his epistle, James says this. Count it all joy, my brothers, when you meet various, when you meet trials of various kinds. For you know that the testing of your faith produces steadfastness. In 1 Peter the apostle says Beloved, do not be surprised at the fiery trial when it comes upon you to test you As though something strange were happening to you. But rejoice insofar as you share in the sufferings of Christ. That you may also rejoice and be glad when his glory is revealed. Now there's a passage for you that there's no way we can unpack this morning the idea that we are sharing in the sufferings of Christ, but I assure you it's quite profound. Now each of these verses verifies that when God tests his people He is looking to do something greater within them and greater amongst them. And this is true individually, it is true corporately. God tests to show who we are inside and thus to make us more holy inside and then outside. And we must not shirk a test, for God uses them to form us into his image. We must not shrink at a test, for God uses them to build up in us the character that we lack. When it comes to facing the trials and tests of our lives, corporately, as a family, or as an individual, we are to see that these are opportunities to be sanctified. To be made holy. And such a perspective is similar to what I have counseled parents about misbehaving children, what I have embraced about raising my own children. When a child is wrong And a parent is tempted to be mortified, because it seems to reflect them, mortified at a child's behavior, or They go into denial that their child could ever do whatever that child did. A better choice is to seize the moment as an opportunity to train the child. Misbehavior opportunity. An act of misbehavior can be seen as a gift from God to reveal what is in the child's heart that needs to be trained out. So that the love of God can go in. And it is the same for when we are tested. We get to see what is within us and what needs to be replaced by God's love. Next, when being tested, the people complain All of you adults will relate to what I'm about to describe. As a pastor of a church, of a parish. You are already scrutinized before you say a word. And you are complained about, both deserved and undeserved, because you are in a leadership position. And people sometimes complain about spiritual leadership when it isn't the pastor that is their true target, but the complaint really instead has the target of God. But the pastor is the easiest target, and so he gets it. That comes with the calling, and every pastor learns it very early on in the ministry. And so pastors can identify with the scenario of the people complaining to Moses about not having water and then not having food and then not having water again When actually, actually they are upset at God. Consider the gall, the gall that is recorded in chapter 16, verse 3. For the people to say it would have been better to die as slaves in Egypt than to be hungry in the desert, that is absurd. That anyone can say such absurd things when faith is weak and flesh is strong. Every adult here is in some way in a type of leadership position. Whether it's leadership over your children at home or leadership in work or leadership in a community And you get complaints, and many of those complaints are unfair. And sometimes you get complaints where you are not actually the target, the person that the complainer is upset about. So we can know how Moses felt as he heard Complaints. Complaints he himself could not answer. And because we can identify with Moses. We are to impart more grace to others that we are tempted to complain about. And here is the great irony of all this complaining. If I complain about people who are complaining about me, I am behaving in the same manner, and thus I am no true leader. Did you ever wonder why Israel was not allowed to speak anything out loud while they were walking around the city of Jericho seven times? It wasn't because they were planning a surprise attack that they were stealth. No, the people of Jericho could stand on the top of their walls and see them marching around their city, around and around, seven times. It was not for a surprise attack. It is because God knew that we are fallen people and he knew what we would do if we spoke up. If the Israelites were allowed to talk that day, there would have been complaining and complaining and more complaining. What are we doing this for? Someone would have shouted, This'll never work! And inevitably a little child is going to say, I'm tired. And about the third time around, you're going to hear, not this again. And those types of complaints would build. You know how that goes, complaining snowballs. One person says they don't like Wednesday prayer, study, move to Tuesday. Or they don't like Sunday school snacks before Sunday school. Another agrees, and they find another that agrees. And soon they get a posse. And they gather around the rector's home with pitchforks and burning torches, yelling for the rector to come out and meet his demise. There is a necessary reason why Saint Paul instructed the Philippians, commanded the Philippians do everything. Do everything without grumbling Or complaining. The next stage in our identified pattern is Moses crying out to God. Moses crying out to God, this is what all leaders need to do if you are going to lead in a godly manner. Leaders need to pray. Pray to God, asking God to meet the need. Every loving parent knows the heartache of watching a child go through a try a trial and not being able to help the child A parent can only nurse an illness, can't take it away. A parent can only be encouraging to a child when the child fails, rather than win for the child. A parent can only be a friend to a child when that child is emotionally hurt by peers. And so God God-fearing parents pray, and God-fearing leaders pray when they cannot meet the needs of the people who complain. But Moses is more than just a leader of people. He is also a type. He is also a shadow of the leader to come. Moses was a type of Christ. And so when we read of Moses praying, we are to think about Jesus praying. And to think about Jesus praying is to have faith that Jesus is our intercessor. Consider that Jesus went through all that he did on this earth so that he could go be where he is now. The right hand of the Father. He did all of it to be an intercessor who pleads our cause to the Heavenly Father. And this is why we pray in the name of Jesus. It is the only way for God to hear our prayers is through Jesus. And our prayer life reflects our faith and understanding the importance of Jesus as our intercessor. No other way. This is a small example, I know. But there's a reason why I give this small example. Last week my computer was working very slowly. So as I've done in the past, I turn it off and turn it back on again. Only it didn't turn on again. And it buffeted and then it stopped. I repeated the process, nothing I repeated the process, nothing. And the real concern was that my most recent sermon had not yet been saved, and it was almost finished. I had not backed up my computer in over a month. And so I began to sweat. You know how that happened to me to sweat. I turn it off and turn it on over a dozen times at nothing. And then I pray. In earnest, I prayed. God helped me retrieve that sermon. That's all I can give. That's all I want. It was Thursday after all. I unplugged it, I took it home, I plugged it in, I prayed again, turned it on, and it worked. Thanks be to God. Let your request be made known to God, the scriptures instruct. Let your request be made known to God. Don't believe the devil that God doesn't care about the small things. He cares about the small things. He cares about computers turning on and off. He does care and Jesus wants to intercede for us. Now the next part of the pattern we are noting is that God hears the complaints. And this is the marvelous part of the pattern for me. For me, it is more marvelous than God eventually meeting the need. God tests, we as people complain, our intercessor prays, and God hears. This is marvelous to me because he does not have to hear. It would be perfectly just for God to say that he is not going to listen to any complaining at all. It would be just for God to judge that his people are ingrates, ungrateful, and thus not worthy to be heard, which is true. And this is where Calvinism has a doctrinal theology that gets it right. Calvinism emphasizes the unworthiness of humanity to be saved by God. Calvinists are right to say that what is justice for all humanity is our eternal damnation, and therefore we, individually or corporately Have no right cause to complain that God only saves some, for in truth he does not have to save any at all. All of that is true. But God wants to save, and thus God wants to hear his people cry out. He wants to respond to our cries. For as much as God is just, he is love. In fact, the love he is, that is what will remain. These three things, faith, hope, and love, and the greatest is love. The next and final part of our noted pattern is that God meets the need. God meets the needs of his people. I trust you did not let it go unnoticed that when Moses cries out to God at the bitter water called Mara, which was likely called that after they realized it was bitter, that God used symbolism to meet the needs of the people. Now the NIV, I don't like that translation that was read this morning. King James calls it a tree, not a piece of wood. God instructed Moses to take a near tree and to cast it into the water So that the water would be made sweet to drink. And so Moses took the tree that was pointed out to him, cut it down, and had it cast into the water of Marah, and the water became healthy to drink. But it is not by accident that God had Moses use a tree to sweeten the water. It was a tree, you remember, that was in the Garden of Eden that gave life. It would be a tree that would hang a cursed man on the hill of Calvary that would be the source of living water, a water from which if anyone drank, they would never thirst again. And it is a tree that is described as being at the center of the New Jerusalem, heaven, that comes down and presides as an eternal resting place for the people of God. The tree was not just by accident. And the symbolism continues in this story for what comes down from heaven? Mana. Or heavenly bread, and that a man named Jesus would call himself the bread of life, which, if eaten, a person will never hunger again. And it is not happenstance that the main symbol of Christians gathering together for worship is to remind them of that eternal bread? And thus we hear when we worship, take, eat. This is my body given for you. Do this in remembrance of me. Yes, in every pattern that we examine here in Exodus, God meets the needs of his people, even though they complain. Even though he has shown them time and time again and again that he can be trusted to meet their every need. God is patient. slow to anger, abounding in love, desiring to impart grace to his people. I think this pattern we are noting in this section of scripture is very easy to receive from regarding the message for us, whether it be our corporate life, our family lives, or individual lives. To verify how we are to use the pattern shown to us, we need to be reminded of St. Paul's letter to the Corinthians, chapter 10. And I referred to this back when we talked about the baptism of the people in the Red Sea. Paul points That even though the Israelites were baptized and ate the manna, which all pointed to Christ Jesus, still near all of them did not make it to the Promised Land. Paul then says this, hear it, hear it, hear it. Now these things become our examples to the intent that we should not trust after evil things as they also lusted. That they are these same Israelites who complained and God heard them and answered them and met their need and yet they still did not make it to God's promised land And this pattern is then for us to learn from. It is for us to use as an example of what not to do. First, we are to be aware that God places us in various trials to test us, to see what is inside of us, to mold us, and make us more complete. As Peter said, we should not be surprised at such testing. We should gear up for it. We should acknowledge it when it occurs. And we should face it and we should pass it. And next we should not complain. And if you wonder how such is fair, considering that Israel complained and God still hurt them. Well, recall that God said that he, in times past, overlooked a multitude of sins of his people. But now, coming into the new covenant, we are told to do everything without grumbling or complaining. And next we are to cry out to our intercessor, who is Jesus, who wants to hear our prayers and bring them before the Father, who wants to hear his Son, and to do His will. And next we are to have faith that God does indeed hear our prayers and will meet our need in whatever manner he chooses, whether it be dropping down from heaven or whether it be in the form of a tree. The alternative of not using Israel in the desert as an example for us, as Paul says, is to chase after lusts. And lust does not only refer to the sexual kind. It can apply to lust for prestige amongst our peers. It can refer to earthly treasure. It can refer to positions of authority. Let us be true and say that the fallen human species can lust at practically everything. And chasing after lust is to chase after false gods, and to chase after false gods results in our lives, like the Israelites, scattered throughout the desert, never entering the promised land, which for us is heaven. So there is a dire warning in this story. And Saint Paul wants us to hear it. St. Paul's application of these stories 15, 16, and 17, is not only to hear a dire warning, but to see a gracious God. Who wants to hear us? Who wants to provide for us? He's only asking for loyalty in return. So let us be loyal, for he is worthy. Let us pray.

sermons.title: Every Thought into Captivity
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Although we are a liturgical church, it is nice when things surprise you. I have never done a responsorial reading where one was reading from the NIV and the rest were reading from the New King James. But it made it interesting. As you can tell from our readings this morning, the sermon is not coming from the book of Exodus. I hope that this sermon will help you in the days to come, especially in light of the election. We're not going to be speaking specifically about the election, but I trust you will see how this ties in. A big thank you to the vestry for helping me to attend a conference two weeks ago that spurred me on and allowed me to formulate some clearer thinking. From my personal study and from the lectures of others. Clearer thinking has burdened me to share with you What I believe all of us need to understand considering the day in which we live. The basis of this sermon is from the readings that you heard. Romans chapter 12, 1 and 2, and 2 Corinthians chapter 10 verses 4 through 6 We are told there to be transformed by the renewing of our minds, and for us to critique the thoughts that we are exposed to. And to examine them in light of the Word of God, which is how we bring every thought into captivity. How shall we then live is a series of lectures given by the now deceased Francis Schaefer back in the 1970s. It is a video series that you can now find on the internet, and it is quite dated in terms of the pictures shown, but not dated in terms of its message. The series is based on a simple premise that history flows in the direction of how we think. And how we think determines how we act. Unfortunately, many, many people Do not critique how their culture thinks or how they think themselves. Many people fail to understand themselves in terms of their actions. For they don't recognize what they have believed, what they have thought, what worldview they have accepted, and how such beliefs, thoughts, and views determine their present behavior. Let us first consider the Roman Empire. Governmentally, the Roman Empire was based on an elitist Roman Republic. But it could not sustain itself because its gods were lifeless, and the message, and the masses became envious of the elite. This led to the rise of dictatorships that would hold the empire together by force. But more was needed, and so the famous poet Virgil presented then Emperor Augustus Caesar as a God himself, and thus worthy to be honored and obeyed. We know from our Bibles that the Christian era began during the reign of Augustus Caesar, and within a short time after the death, resurrection, and ascension of Jesus, persecution of Christians began. First by the Jews and then the Romans. And Christians were persecuted by the Romans not because they worshipped Jesus. But because they rejected the Roman culture with its false idols and the worship of the state Thus, what the first century Christians recognized was how the Romans thought The Romans thought that the state itself was to be preserved and preserved at all costs This is how the Romans accepted dictatorships. It was why they made their emperors gods It was why they persecuted the Christians. Because Christians, having rejected the Roman culture, were a threat to the stability of the Roman state. But the Roman Empire could not sustain itself based upon false gods and immoral leaders who looked nothing like the type of God to be obeyed Without an absolute morality, the empire declined into decadence until it no longer cared about the family unit, no longer cared for having and raising children. And no longer cared to defend its borders. There is an obvious pattern in the history of man That has societies attempting to build themselves up in order to sustain themselves. They created infrastructures that allowed the citizens to feed and clothe themselves while defending themselves from enemies for and domestic, and then when they became successful, after a while they then turned into themselves And this is after all what Martin Luther called sin, turning into oneself. And when they turned into themselves, the result was the pursuing of pleasure for the sake of pleasure only. And when this happens to a society as a whole, the basis for the society existing is no longer at the foundation, and the society starts to crack. But this pattern repeats itself when there are no absolutes upon which a society built itself. On the other hand, the proclamation of there being one God and believing upon that one God for truth and for hope allows for a society to exist For reasons that go beyond the citizens and go beyond the society. Such a foundation is sustainable Because each generation points to what is greater than the individual and greater than the society, which can help prevent a people turning in to themselves. And so where are we? Is our American society built upon the belief in the one true God? Or have we turned into ourselves becoming obsessed with pleasure for pleasure's sake? If you conclude with me that we have become obsessed with pleasure for the sake of pleasure. You wonder, like me, how we got here and how we got here so fast. Yes, we could point to the likes of Madeline Murray O'Hare. and her successful campaign to remove prayer from public schools. But it can be logically argued that Miss O'Hare and her campaign against public prayer was a symptom of our eroding society and not the root of the problem. After listening to a lecture by historian Dr. Alan Carlson last week He talked about the involvement of the Roman Catholic Church and Evangelical Protestantism scholars. questioning the Christian faith as the sole arbiter of religious truth all the way back to the nineteen forties. One can see how the enemies of faith have been more successful within the church than without. We can also see that the church has been not just passive, not just on the sidelines, while the Christian faith becomes less and less influential in America. But the church has had a voice in voting for its own demise. It is a demise that has been led by false teachers with their multiple degrees and seminary chairmanships. Who were given leadership of the church, given leadership of the church by the very men ordained to the task of leading God's people. And they went back, these ordained men, back and cowered in their studies, bishop and pastors acquiescing leadership to seminary professors. That is a generalization, but an accurate one as I see it. And so with the church not being salt and light and the world as it was commissioned to be, We've allowed secularists, the pagans, the socialists, the evolutionists The celebrities, the pseudo media outlets. We've allowed them to take the place as our priests They are our priests as they tell us who to worship, how to worship, and like the false gods of the Old Testament, they first want us to offer up our children. If you, like many of us, have felt as though our culture has been taken over by false priests rather quickly. Consider that social media and pseudo-media have played a major role. News gets out quickly, and if it is not news in favor of the ruling party, then news that distracts follows. And what is presented as news is more opinion, is more slant, is more hypocrisy than what was supposed to be news. Our culture has been placed on a toboggan slide to the abyss because all unjust, immoral, and hypocritical behavior is justified or excused. Within the subject of philosophical ethics, there is a theory That is very much embraced by certain candidates and politicians, and it needs to be identified by us and then reviewed The theory is called act utilitarianism or act consequentialism Act-utilitarianism is a theory that originated within the 18th century by a philosopher named Jeremy Bentham. He put forth the thesis that true happiness is when good has been achieved to affect the most people. Thus, utilitarianism as a theory is the search for the greater good, which is good for the most people. Bentham used his theory for uplifting the poor, but modern politicians have used it to their greater good. Act utilitarianism is more than being concerned about the greater good. It is a theory that adds the prefix act. To argue that the actions of a leader in terms of morality does not matter, but only that what the leader does is for the sake of the greater good And so for an old Soviet Union leader, it would mean that the government is morally right to take a farmer's land with no compensation In order to build an airstrip, not caring how long the land has been owned by the farmer's family, but only caring that all is being done for the greater good Politicians today who embrace act utilitarianism get to justify themselves and their supporters around them justify them. And that it doesn't matter if you lie under oath. It doesn't matter if you destroy evidence. It doesn't matter if you lie to the public. It doesn't matter because you are doing it for The greater good. You see, you and I sit in awe as we watch or read a candidate or public office holder lie. And obfuscate the truth and then lie about the lying. And we say to ourselves and to one another, how can that person do that? What has happened to that person's conscience? And the answer is act utilitarianism. They can do it because they have convinced themselves that what they stand for, what they fight for, what they say are their policies, those are the greater good. And because they are fighting for what they believe is the greater good, it doesn't matter how they get there, as long as they get there, and ethics be damned And they actually believe, because all candidates, all candidates have such large egos, they believe that they themselves are the embodiment of the greater good. So whatever he or she decides is ex officio the greater good. The main critique of an act utilitarian position is that it is impossible to know what will eventually turn out to be for the greater good. No one can predict the future. The politicians don't want us to know that or come to that conclusion. A Christian critique is that God's moral law is not trivial A breaking of his law by lying and stealing is a breaking of his covenant, and such a breaking demands appeasement. And the only sufficient appeasement is Christ Jesus, because only the only greater good we can be sure about is Jesus. Another way of thinking that has brought our culture to the point we are in our history is Gnosticism. The first lecturer at the conference I attended two weeks ago was Dr. Robert George, who is a lecturer and McCormick professor of Jewish Prudence At Princeton University. Dr. George's thesis argued that the roots of the heresy of Gnosticism go so very deep into our culture. That the result is the sexual and gender perversions we are now experiencing and having forced before our eyes. I have preached against Gnosticism before from this pulpit, but I have done so in terms of the Christian church. As I have explained that Gnosticism rejects the physical world as unimportant and instead embraces the physical world as important, I mean excuse me, the spiritual world as important. And it believes that when it comes to humanity, what man does in the physical world is not important. It's only the spiritual. And Christianity rejects such a teaching because Jesus was made flesh, God called his creation good And Jesus is still flesh, and when he returns, he will make us whole again, both flesh and spirit. And so humanity is not spirit over flesh, but only hold when we are both flesh and spirit. But this neo-Gnosticism of today approaches the understanding of the body and spirit a little differently. What the Neonostics believe is that a person's identity, a person's true self, is his or her spirit. And a person's spirit is expressed by his or her emotions. The body, they say, is only a tool or a a conduit by which human beings can express their true self, their emotions, their feelings This then allows a person to use his or her body in any manner desired or in any manner that a person who owns that body feels like doing. As Dr. George explained, the body being only a tool or a conduit for how a person feels in the moment can have the plumbing moved around and used for different purposes than what was biologically intended, they can do this because the spirit, the emotions, the feelings of the persons want it that way. And again, the true person is believed to be the emotions. Thus, those who have bought into neo-Gnostic ways of thinking, well, they can't understand Why we become repulsed when a man wants to lie with another man or a woman with another woman or with several partners. They don't perceive where we are coming from when we see it as perverse and mentally unhealthy that a man would want to have surgery so that he can look like a woman, or a woman would want to have surgery to look like a man. And we most certainly get confused when a man wants to be given the anatomy of a woman only so that he can lie with women? And they can't imagine why we would make a big deal about people being able to choose what public bathroom they use according to how they feel on a particular day. Because for them, it is how they feel that is important rather than the current state of their plumbing As you can see, the neo-Gnostic thought allows for any type of morality, especially sexual immorality, to be practiced. Because all is based on how a person feels, because how a person feels is who he or she is. And who are you? Who am I to tell another person how they should feel or tell them who they are? And thus Dr. George labels the age in which we live the age of feeling, because feelings are the authority. When you combine the two philosophies together, the age of feeling, combining it with act utilitarianism And the result is a culture that excuses every immoral, unethical behavior based on the pursuit of the greater good, and the greater good being defined as whatever feels good to each and every individual. Therefore, any dissenting opinion that teaches, preaches, professes an absolute standard for morality. And a need to fear God before the day of judgment, those persons are labeled and categorized as enemies of the greater good and enemies of people's happiness. Now the answer to all of this wrong thinking by some within Christendom has just been plain heresy. And they have had their torches put out, and we cannot reach them. The answer by others is to bend their standards Because they don't want to appear to be an enemy of the greater good or to appear to be an enemy of people's happiness. But those responses are not the response of Holy Scripture As St. Paul instructs, we are to bring every thought into captivity, which means that every manner of thinking is to be evaluated by the standard of Holy Scripture and is to be controlled in a manner that the thinking does not dictate our behavior. And so act utilitarianism is evaluated and seen to fall short of the objective truths of Holy Scripture, which are contained and confessed in our creeds. We can dismiss act utilitarianism because it does not recognize the greater good to be the gospel of the Lord Jesus Christ and the greater good being the kingdom of God. The next thought we must bring into captivity is the spirit of personal happiness that is based on personal feelings. In the age of feelings, Christians must stand firm on the objective truths of the gospel, who Jesus is, what Jesus did, and what he is now doing. Our faith, our belief cannot be based on how we feel in the moment. What is historically and theologically true in the person of Jesus Christ Those who base their belief system on feelings, they will eventually turn inward, and as they do, only hopelessness or the pursuit of pleasure for the sake of pleasure or both will take place. My prophecy is that Christians will eventually be looked to as people to listen to. People to heed, people that have an answer to the confusion that continues to spiral our culture down to the abyss. Christians will be the light of the world and salt of the world as they are commanded to be by the Lord Jesus. That is the hope. That is the hope, but only if we take every thought into captivity, and only if our minds are renewed and transformed by the truth, and not by the prevailing spirits of the secular, godless culture. And the article that I sent to the congregation email list a few weeks ago, it was titled, What Today's Christians can learn from Antiquity about Living in a Pagan World. The author makes the point that when the Roman Empire was cracking and men were pursuing pleasures, over caring for their families And as a result, women were being abused, children were neglected, and the family unit was facing extinction. It was the Christian church that came to the rescue. The Christian Church was looked to as a safe haven for women and as a people of faith that encouraged childbirth and the raising of children. The Christian church also offered the populace something to die for, which means they gave them something to live for. Something greater than themselves. And this can happen again May not happen in my lifetime, but it can happen again. And for it to happen, Christians need to hold on. Christians must not compromise. Christians must be Christ to the world, because we are not believers only for ourselves. We are believers for the kingdom of God to come. Amen? Amen. So when you wake up, Wednesday, November 9th. Hold on. Jesus is still coming. Let us pray.

sermons.title: Stay in the Fight!
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Ghost Amen. Please be seated. We are in Exodus chapter seventeen. As a kid, I only got into fist fights with my brother. There were times when I had stare-downs with my peers, and I was threatened by other kids from a distance, said they were going to beat me up, never came over and did it So I have never known whether I would have been a good fighter. The only thing I knew about myself was that I would not back down to anyone because of my ego. It wouldn't allow me to do it. I was once cornered by two guys near my eighth grade locker who said I should either get down on my knees and Kiss the ground or they were going to beat me up. It didn't take long for a crowd to gather around to see what I was going to do. And again, I assume it was the size of my ego that made me determined to refuse to bend down and kiss the ground, though I knew those guys could smash my face in Thankfully a teacher broke up the gathering and later after my older brother found out what had happened I happened to receive a nice apology from one of the guys telling me it was all a joke. When I knew it wasn't. Another point of fear faced in my life was that as a freshman in high school football camp. The football team would go away to a local community college for the week to concentrate on football only. And one of the first drills we did after receiving full pads was a tackling drill that was designed to see who was tough and who was not. Now, I already knew that I wasn't tough, but I had to show them that I could overcome fear. The drill was simple, and that they had us get into two lines that faced each other, well not facing each other shoulder to shoulder, but in a straight line. And the team was about 60 players total, so the line was about 30 deep on each side. The head coach stood in the middle at the front of the lines And the other coaches stood off to the side, yelling for the players to get pumped up. And the head coach would have the two players at the front of the line get in the ready position and then tossed the ball to one of the players. You didn't know which one was going to get it. And when the player received the ball, he was to run at the defender, and the defender was to run at the ball carrier. with the basic goal of plowing into each other, again, to see who was tough. Well for a freshman This was frightening, and not just because of the collision that you would have to endure, but because you didn't want to face an upperclassman So all of us freshmen are peering around the players in front of us and counting how many people on that side are would match up to where you're at in the line to see who you would face Well, thankfully I faced a fellow freshman who was my height and my build. And when it was our turn, I could see that my opponent was as wide-eyed as I was And when the ball was tossed to him, we ran straight at each other. Both lowering our heads, our helmets hit crown to crown, and we both went backwards on our elms. And from the whooping and hollering of the coaches, it was a success. And because it was over and I was still alive, I thought I succeeded as well. Of course, such silly stories are nothing like what real men face who have to go to combat When their own lives are on the line, and the lives of their buddies are on the line, and the fate of their country is on the line. When we read of Israel at war with other nations, we must rehearse in our minds what we know about the region. It was a desert land with hills and valleys. We need to rehearse what we know about the weaponry. It was stones, spears, and swords. And we need to remind ourselves of their humanity. They were flesh and blood. They feared for their lives and the lives of their loved ones just as any rational person would. But it was necessary for the fighting men to overcome fear back then, just as it is required of military men to overcome fear today. And what the Bible shows us is that fear is best overcome when you know you are in the right fight. And the right fight is the fight that God has called you to engage. For Israel, the first right fight, the first time they fought as a nation, was against the Amalekites. The Amalekites were the right fight because they attacked Israel. The Amalekites are thought to be descendants of Esau. The brother of Jacob, who sold his birthright, and then Jacob stole it also. The Amalekites And Israel would be enemies because of their history if such history were kept alive by the descendants of Esau. We could say that the Amalekites attacked Israel with no provocation, but consider that Israel was using the land of the Amalekites. And the tribal attitude was, any threat to a tribe's way of life was a reason to go to war. Mose instructions introduce us for the first time to Joshua, who was given the responsibility to lead a fit army against the Amalekites. Well, Moses promises to be a prominent leader by symbolizing to the fighting men how the battle would be won. Moses would stand on a hill with the rod of God's authority in his hand being lifted up so that Israel would be not afraid. But would instead know the presence of God, know it was on their side. And so the leaders of Israel, chosen by God, go up the hill to be seen. Moses and Aaron were over 80 years of age, and we are introduced to a man named Her, who is thought to be the husband of Miriam, sister to Moses. As the battle raged, it had ebbs and flows, and it was noticed by the leaders that these ebbs and flows were related to Moses lifting up his hands. When his hands were lifted up, Israel was succeeding. When his hands, the hands of Moses were lowered, that meant the rod of authority was lowered, and Israel's success lessened. And commentators are in agreement that the main lesson, the main lesson of lifting up hands like Moses, is finding success in battle by Intercessory prayer. The hands lifted up are to represent the act of praying, the act of seeking God's favor. When the hands are lowered, we are being dependent upon ourselves, and thus we find ourselves losing the battle. And there is, of course, much to be commended regarding intercessory prayer. We need to pray for one another We need to pray for our nation. We need to pray for our leaders as Ruth did today. The Bible instructs us to do so. And we need to pray for people who are in battles of their own, battles for their own souls, battles for their children, battles for their loved ones. But I am wondering if there is more to the act of Moses lifting up his hands on a hill. Is not Moses to be a type of Christ to us? Was not Jesus a type of prophet as Moses? And so when Moses goes up on a hill, and when Moses lifts up his hands, is he not a type or a shadow? Of the Son of God who will ascend on a hill and have his hands lifted up on a cross. And did not Jesus say that when he is lifted up, that everyone that believes in him will receive eternal life? So just as Israel looked up to Moses, who raised his hands, and they found victory. So too do all people find victory over sin and over death when they look up to Jesus, who spread out his hands for all of mankind. I believe that meaning has to be in this story. And then there's this need of Aaron and her. To hold up the hands of Moses as Moses tired. And this is a lesson for all leaders. For all leaders need the help of others. No man can or should lead alone. And that is so very true, and any good leader knows it is true. And so we need each other and we need to look for ways to help each other. But again, I wonder if there is something more to notice as these two men helped Moses hold up his hands. There were three of them on that hill, after all. And when we think of our salvation, how the Godhead saves us, we are to notice all three. There is the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost that play a part in our salvation. And Jesus is the Savior, yes. Of course. And the Bible says that the Father, God the Father, was in Christ, reconciling the world to himself. And Jesus said that the Holy Spirit would be among us and within us, and that that would be his presence within us. And so we should not fail to see a shadow on that hill of the Godhead, the Trinity, Aaron and her holding up the hands of Moses. And so the Israelites defeated the Amalekites. Again, this is the first battle, the first victory of Israel as a nation. And then they write it down. Historical record. And this is the first recording that we have of something being written down in a book. And the wording of the text implies that that book already existed. So it is likely that it is the same book, the book of Genesis, that the Holy Spirit was having Moses write. And now he is to add to this book of Abraham, book of Jacob, Book of Israel, being saved from the Amalekites. Well because Israel won the day, and because Moses knew why Israel won the day, Moses then worships as a response. God had given the people, his people, the victory. And Moses knows that after such an event, it is natural for our human condition to need to worship. If they did not worship the true God, they would worship something else, because humanity in our fallen state, we worship anything, just as the golden calf will soon teach us. And so Moses leads the people in worship. Now the point of this story for us is intercessory prayer and its importance. Yes, of course. It is to see Jesus on a hill lifted up? Yes. It is leaders needing help? Yes. It is the Trinity saving God's people. Yes. But another point that is needed for us is how we need to fight. There is a reason why Saint Paul used the metaphor of armor needed to live the Christian life. Usually we hear the metaphor from the epistle to the Ephesians, but Paul repeats that metaphor of armor being worn in his letter to the Thessalonians. Which is a letter that could have very well been the second letter Paul ever wrote to the Christian church. And if it is the second letter Paul ever wrote, such would emphasize how important it is. To those early Christians to understand that their walk with Jesus is not a stroll in the park, but a march on a battlefield. Remember, I have said this. The devil has two goals for you. Two. The first is to achieve your death. And the second is to lead you to deny to deny your faith in Jesus Christ. And since the first goal cannot be achieved unless the Heavenly Father allows it, The second goal is where he places most of his efforts. And the devil's modus operandi has not changed. He first works to get you to doubt what God has said to be true, and then replace what God has said to be true with any lie that you would like to believe. This is what he did with Eve. He worked her so that she first didn't remember precisely what God had said. God said, don't touch, don't eat. And then she was led to no longer believe that what God had told her that she would die if she ate that forbidden fruit. The devil is usually subtle, always subtle. And for adults, for adults, it might be that we read a new scientific study coming out that puts into doubt the origin of the universe or who controls the universe. It may be a study that claims a new morality. And if we are not engaged in warfare, If we do not have the helmet of salvation on, we might start to think that such a study might be true And therefore what the Bible says about God as creator, or God being sovereign, or God's moral law being the authority, or maybe of Jesus historically actually living, dying. Rising, that may be fictitious. This type of battle, most adults face. And by the way, a lecture I heard several weeks ago, I mentioned it last week, took scientific study claims to the task by arguing that most scientific studies that make headlines are not scientific at all, but pure speculation for the sake of headline reading. It was a quite provoc provocative presentation. Now as for the battles we face, there is a different type of battle our children face, especially if they attend public school. But this even happens in private schools It is peer pressure. It is the pool that everyone else is doing it or everyone else is not doing it, and therefore our children are tempted very strongly to join the crowd. And this too was part of the devil's temptation technique with Adam and Eve. He convinced them that they could be like God and be like him. knowing personally what is good and what is evil. He tempted them by calling them to join the crowd. It didn't matter that God knew good and evil being greater than evil, and that the devil knew good and evil by practicing evil. That was a technicality the devil didn't share. God would have shown Adam and Eve what good and evil was if they would have overcome the temptation to do evil, just as Jesus did. But Adam and Eve wanted to experience evil, and so they sinned. For our children, the temptations to be like the crowd are numerous. and seemingly more than my generation experienced or the generation before me experienced Children are tempted, we know, to join the crowd by taking drugs, drinking alcohol, having sex, but not just having sex with the opposite sex only Children are tempted to join the crowd by rebelling against parents, stealing from parents, shaming classmates, participating with or in pornography. destroying property, escaping into virtual realities, taking pride in laziness, cheating in school, betraying trust through social media And whatever else the crowd can think of doing that would look cool and be embarrassing to the parents. And kids are tempted to follow their peers in what they do not do, especially go to church If our children are asking their classmates or their neighbors how many of them attend church on Sunday, the number would be terribly low. And our children would feel even more isolated, even more alone. And feeling isolated and feeling alone is fertile ground. Fertile ground for a child to give into the temptation to join their peers. There is a battle raging right now for the souls of our children. And we, every one of us, in some way need to engage in that fight. So there are personal battles we are engaged in, and there are battles for our children we must fight, and there are others still. There is a battle for our marriages. Every person here that is married is under attack, as the devil would love to destroy Christian families by separating husbands and wives. Husbands and wives need to engage that battle and fight for their marriage because God hates divorce And because the fallout of divorce in the Christian marriage could lead to children no longer trusting what their parents taught them about God and no longer being able to know what unconditional love looks like or feels like. And then there are the battles that go on in the church There is the battle for churches to remain faithful to the gospel, to not give in to false spirits that speak of relativism. And be a follower of the culture instead of salt and life in a city on a hill. And there are personal battles that the devil stirs up within the local churches. Tempt us to fight with one another over trivial issues. And for some, they're not trivial at all. They mean everything. A result of my teaching a class on New Testament survey has caused me to notice How Paul ends his epistles to the churches, these local churches, with some sort of encouragement for them to get along and for them to forgive one another. The warnings are so that the local church does not let the devil get a foothold. And you know He has a foothold when you are walking around holding a grudge against a fellow Christian in your church. If you hold that grudge, you are obeying the devil. You are fighting on his side. When it comes to finding success in our battles As the saying goes, eighty percent of success is just showing up For the Christian success in the battle is found in us fighting the good fight and having the faith that because Jesus was lifted up, because Jesus' arms were raised, our battles are won. But you have to stay in the battle to see the fruition of the victories that God has for His people. You have to stay in the battle. You have to continue to stay and fight against your besetting sins. You have to stay and fight for the souls of your children. You have to stay and fight for your marriage. You have to stay and fight for your universal and local church. You have to stay and fight. And I know it gets worrisome, believe me, I know. I know it seems easier to put down the sword. I know. I know you want to see the end is near. It's got to be near. I know. But stay in the fight. We need to stay in it together. And those who stay in the fight are promised those words. Well done, thou good and faithful servant, enter into your rest. But we will only hear those words. If we stay in the fight, let us pray.

sermons.title: Ecclesiastical Authority
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: Amen. Maybe seated. We are continuing our study from Exodus. We will do well to turn to Exodus 18 and focus on passages that were read from the lect from the lectern this morning. You notice that most of us have who like sports have our teams. We speak about them as if they are us. A few years ago, when the Ravens won the Super Bowl, Ravens fans said, we won! We beat the 49ers. The true fans, those who by definition are fanatics, live or die emotionally on each play. And thus on a Sunday afternoon, we are up and down with each snap of the ball. During those summer weekdays, we are up and down emotionally with every pitch. Interestingly, psychologists have come up with theories as to why people get so crazy about their teens. Reason number one The need for belonging. Just like humans need food and shelter, there is a natural need to be in community. And our teams provide community. Number two, establishing identity. One of the extremely important parts of being a human being is to have personal identity And projecting that identity to others. The Ravens or Steelers or whatever team provides identity. Reaping the benefits. Number three. Right after your favorite team wins, your self-esteem goes higher and males actually get males get a boost in testosterone. Number four, fighting loneliness. People who have a sense of belonging to a community usually feel less lonely than others And so the Orioles help us feel less lonely. Number five, unexpected rewards and addictions. When a reward is unexpected, people get more hooked to whatever they are doing, making the playoffs as an unexpected reward. And then number six, tribal wars. Long ago, the psychologists say, tribes used to fight each other, and the winning tribe reaped all the benefits. As humans, we become more civilized, and thus our ancient desires have shifted a bit into a different form. Thus we no longer hate the Philistines, we hate the Steelers, right? I don't really care, Larry, by the way. Number seven, distraction. Life is full of problems and tough times. People who cheer for sports teams get so immersed into their experience that they manage to forget about their problems for a little while. Well if we take this list of observations and apply it to our particular religious denomination We can see some of the same. We can become like fans that defend the honor of their team. By defending the particular way that we practice our faith, believing that we do it better than others. We defend how we interpret the scripture as if we are holding up the number one sign so that others will know that we are the number one denomination. For example, I've had a discussion, or many discussions, with the likes of Presbyterians who, when defending their two-office system of Presbyter, Elder, and Deacon I have been told that, well, our way is biblical. And that was supposed to end the discussion, one of those drop the mic moments. They were number one. Their team, their denomination is biblical, and mine is not. The natural question to ask is what do the scriptures say about church government? Or what does it mean to say that a church government is biblical? We are recognizing all Saints Day, Sunday, today, and thus I thought it would be good for us to discover how the saints of old have understood how God structured his church. and to see the benefits of a particular structured government based on a biblical interpretation The Episcopal tradition argues that the office of bishop goes back to the Exodus of Israel and is derived directly from Exodus chapter 18. Which is where we find ourselves in our study in the book of Exodus. In Exodus 18, we meet up again with Jethro, the father-in-law to Moses. We are told in Exodus chapter 3, verse 1, that Jethro was a priest of Midian. This means that his priesthood did not come from Aaron, and it could not have, because that was just being established. If Jethro was a pagan priest, as some have insisted, we must question what a pagan priest is doing in advising the leader of God's people, Moses. And further, we should ask, why does Moses record a pagan priest offering a sacrifice to the one true God? And to further the problem, why do the elders of Israel, including Aaron, the head of the priests, eat the meat offered to God by a pagan priest? The only way, the only way to make any sense of it is to conclude that Jethro was not a pagan priest, but instead a priest in the line of Melchizedek. As such, he would be in the line of Christ, who we are told in the book of Hebrews, that Jesus is a priest in the order of Melchizedek. Thus, the actions of Jethro and his advice to Moses are significant in teaching us today how God structures the leadership of his people. And remember this. We are a people of both the Old and New Testaments. Both of them inform our faith. The first thing Jethro does, as mentioned, is lead the nation of Israel in a worship service, which ends in a sacramental meal. Then he restructures the leadership of God's people. Now turn there if you would in your Bibles 2, chapter 18. Starting at verse 13. And I want to summarize that whole section, verse 13 through 27, to notice what Jethro does. He wisely structures the leadership of God's people to rulers of groups, rulers of groups of thousands. Of groups of hundreds, of groups of fifty, and even groups of ten. And this system is both representative and hierarchical Each ruler represents the ruler above him to the people he is to care for. As we will see, the early Christian church. Took this model as the definitive model for church government to cover both the Old and New Testaments. This was the model that the apostles followed when they made their decisions concerning hierarchy. We can say this definitively because of what Clement of Rome wrote as a second-generation church leader. With the words similar to those of Jethro and Exodus 18, Calamenth wrote the following about church government. All are not generals, nor commanders of a thousand, nor of a hundred, nor of fifty, but each in his own rank. Clement went on to explain how the apostles arrived at establishing a threefold office of government. He said, quote, the apostles received the gospel for us from the Lord Jesus Christ. Jesus the Christ was sent from God. Thus Christ is from God and the apostles from Christ. In both instances, the order of procedure depends on God's will. And so the apostles, after having received their orders and being fully convinced by the resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ, And assured by God's word, went out in the confidence of the Holy Spirit to preach the good news. They preached in country and city and appointed their first converts. After testifying to them by the Spirit to be the bishops and deacons of future believers And is it any wonder that those Christians whom God had entrusted with such a duty should have appointed the officers mentioned For blessed Moses too, who was a faithful servant in all God's house, recorded in the sacred books All the orders given to him and the rest of the prophets followed in his train of testifying of his legislation. End quote I hope you caught the significance of Clement's testimony, for he described the apostles as they established the ministry of the church. That ministry established, they were conscientious of the structure Moses instituted at the advice of Jethro. It was a representative and hierarchical government that he instituted and the church instituted. And this is how it developed in the early church, as it naturally would. Just like Moses when the church was newly formed. And located in Jerusalem, the apostles oversaw everything just like Moses oversaw everything. But when the church grew numerically and geographically It became impossible for the apostles to be able to lead all aspects of the church. We then see a natural change in Acts chapter 6. Where it was necessary to choose men to oversee the ministry inside the church, ministry toward the weaker. So that, remember, in Acts 6, so that the Apostles could focus on the work of the ministry of the Word of God We believe that this was the newly formed office of the Dioconate, which our patron St. Stephen's was prominent. The Apostle Paul continued the practice of ordaining men for the ministry by laying on of hands, as recorded in Acts 14. There the Apostle Paul needed to move on to other regions to preach the gospel. And thus he left behind him men ordained, elders, presbyters, to take over the teaching and the preaching and to distribute the sacraments that he had already established. From the very beginning, Saint Paul personally laid his hands on men whom he ordained to be presbyters as described in 1 Timothy 4. Consider what the laying on of hands was. It was the symbol of transferring the apostolic authority and blessing upon men deemed suitable to lead the church. And when church growth was at a strong pace, Paul, and this is important, Paul then gives Timothy and Titus the authority to ordain. So that the increase of leadership would match the increase of disciples. Our own Bishop Cheney, one of the first bishops of the Reformed Episcopal Church, pointed out that Timothy and Titus were given authority that no other presbyters were given. Even giving Timothy the authority to forbid certain the preaching of certain doctrines, which most certainly is Or at least was the first authority owned by the apostles. And next Cheney points out Paul instructs Timothy on what is required of an elder and a deacon. And he makes the point that Timothy would only need such instruction if Timothy himself was involved in choosing presbyters and deacons. Next is a quote from Cheney. It seems almost impossible to avoid the conclusion that these two early ministers of Christ, Timothy and Titus. were entrusted by apostolic hands with precisely the duties and responsibilities that are now pertained to the office of bishop. The conclusion then is that certain men were given authority to have oversight of the church, which focused on admitting men to the ministry and protecting right doctrine. However, and this is important also, the giving of authority to men who would follow the apostles was not a blank check. There was a limit in that the apostles were the final authority on what is to be considered, accepted, and believed to be the Word of God. After the apostles passed from this life to the next, there were no new letters or new revelations regarding what the church would see to be the Word of God. John Scott, well-respected Anglican and evangelical theologian, said the following. The apostles of Jesus Christ were unique. Unique in their experience of the Jesus of history. Unique In their sight of the risen Lord, unique in their commission by Christ's authority, and unique in their inspiration by Christ's Spirit. We may not exalt our opinions over theirs or claim our authority is as great as theirs. For their opinions and authority are Christ's. If we would bow to his authority, we therefore must bow to theirs. End quote And such a thought has been the historic understanding of the Church in the West, in the East, among Catholics, Orthodox, and Protestants. At least it was until the liberals have started influencing the mainline churches, and literally all hell has broken loose. After the apostles went to be with the Lord, there became a natural division of responsibility within the church. To the diakonate was delegated the ministry of humble service as described in Acts 6 and as demonstrated by the life of Christ. The responsibility of presbyters became the proclamation of apostolic truth, the gospel of Jesus Christ, through the ministry of Word and Sacrament. And to the episcopate was delegated the preservation of apostolic doctrine by ordination and pastor oversight. Our own Bishop Cummins, founding bishop of the REC, explained it as follows, quote, For a time the apostles were the sole office bearers in the church. The necessities of the church gave rise to the establishment of the diaconate. The diaconate was an office established by the apostles. Those elected to fill this office were set apart to their work by laying on of hands of the apostles The Presbyterate, or office of Presbyter, is of undisputed apostolic origin, and arose also out of the necessities of the church The apostles were compelled to provide church communities with officers to instruct, to guide, to rule, and to watch over them. And Cummins continued in order to explain the relationship a bishop is to have with the presbyters of the church. Quote, the episcopate is found in the New Testament as an office exercised by one who was himself a fellow presbyter. Commissioned or set apart for the exercise of such powers as were rendered necessary by the exigencies of the Church, and for the promotion of general oversight and superintendence. The office of bishop is best summarized to be first among equals. The account of Moses being advised by his father-in-law Jethro regarding how to structure his government oversight for the sake of ministering best To the people God could have viewed as mere historical. God could have just made it something to do then, as opposed to now, and nothing more. But then again, why would Moses record it? We can assume many events occurred in the days of Israel being led by Moses that were not recorded in the book of Exodus. They weren't to be considered by us. They didn't matter. They were not as important as the manner in which leadership was structured. And so when we say that our episcopal form of government is biblical, we do not mean that our witness to the fact is only from the New Testament. But also from the Old Testament and from the practice of the first and second century church as they understood the Old Testament principle to be applied in the New Testament context. Why I believe this is most relevant for us today is because of how crucial it is for Christians to come together. And to be trusting of the ordained leadership God has chosen. And by trusting, I do not mean being led blindly, or giving ourselves over to leadership that is hypocritical or abusive. I simply mean that just as God chooses leaders over nations, So too does he choose leaders over Christians, his church. And we are to trust that such leaders are for our good. Until they prove unworthy of their office. And beloved, these are evil days. Mark it as so We are living in a dry and thirsty land. We are living in days of upheaval, days of confusion. Days where evil is indeed called good, and good is indeed called evil The church therefore needs to be one. It needs to be united so that we can hold one another up as the secular world tries to beat us into submission. And an important way for us to be one, to be united, is to be able to aid one another in the trust that the leadership God has chosen for us is what is best for us. It is what we need. And I anticipate what some of you are thinking. You may think, boy, is that a self-promoting sermon or what? And I can only say no. We came upon Exodus 18, honestly. It is a historical account from which I am giving a modern application. And it is a necessary application as we are living in a culture that takes ungodly pride in throwing off leadership. In disrespecting those who have been placed by God in positions of authority, there is a reason why independent churches have multiplied in the United States We don't like when we don't like, when we don't like our religious leaders, well, we promote another one and start another church. Or promote ourselves and start another church. But that would not have worked in the days of Moses. And let us be honest, it doesn't work very well today. Oh, there are churches that are independent, having thrown off previous leadership, and some other churches that are growing and large, but I would say ineffectual. Certainly ineffectual in changing the culture in which we live. The smallness of our own denomination teaches us how difficult it is to make a difference when nobody knows your name. But the days are here, beloved, that require the people of God to come together for the sake of maintaining our own faith, for the sake of preserving the gospel. For the sake of the kingdom of God being established on earth as it is in heaven. The days are evil, beloved. So let us follow those God has chosen to lead us. Just this past council, Thursday. The presiding bishop of the Reformed Episcopal Church, Bishop Groth, gave a charge to all churches in the Reformed Episcopal Church. He pointed us to the general council that will be held in Dallas, Texas on June 14th through the 16th. And he asked us to do these four things. He said, for each parish, to number one, pray for God to work in the hearts of pastors to be good shepherds. Number two, to pray for the Lord to remove spiritual impediments in our individual lives and in the life of the church. Number three, to pray to God that each parish might help lead at least one new convert to Christ. Number four, to pray that all of God's people would have openness of hearts and minds to facilitate the transformation to holiness. Of course, these are good things to pray always. But our church leader told us to pray this way until the meeting in Dallas. This particular way. And so that's what we will do. Let us pray. Our gracious and heavenly Father. We pray, dear Lord, that you would work in the hearts of the pastors who lead your children, your people. Father, may their hearts be turned to you And may they in turn love your people. We pray, O Lord, for the removal of spiritual impediments. Sins in our individual lives and sins in the life of the church, each local parish, each denomination. May we confront it, repent of it, and be done away with it. We pray, dear Lord, that our parish might see one, two, three converts to Christ from now until June. That your kingdom might grow and your children might come home. And we pray that all of God's people would be open, their hearts and minds open. To facilitate a transformation in their individual lives and in the lives of your church to holiness, to be like Jesus. These things we pray in Jesus' name and all of God's people said. Amen.

sermons.title: All Together Different
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Be seated. In our study of Exodus, we are at Exodus chapter 19. And this morning we're going to walk through it a bit like a Bible study. So I encourage you to pick up a Bible. Open it up and turn to Exodus 19 Verse one. In the third month, after the children of Israel had gone out of the land of Egypt, on the same day they came to the wilderness of Sidon. The month mentioned here is part of our May and part of our June. The day of the month is not given. Verse 2. For they had departed from Rapidim. And come to the wilderness of Sinai and camped in the wilderness. So Israel encamped there before the mount. The location of Sinai eludes us even today. Some commentators speculate that because the word Sinai is of uncertain origin that the text of Exodus itself provides the meaning. The exact location thus is not important. But what is important to understand is that whatever place God is making a covenant with Israel by way of his commandments, which he is about to give, that place is Sinai. The Sinai is synonymous with the law. Verse 3 And Moses went up to God, and the Lord called to him from the mountain, saying, Thus you shall stay to the house of Jacob and tell the children of Israel. And here is a standing principle in our relationship with God. God calls. God is the one who starts the relationship. God calls and his people are to respond. Verse four You have seen what I did to the Egyptians and how I bore you on eagle's wings and brought you to myself. So what God is about to tell Moses and the people is to be based on what he has accomplished to save them from Egypt. It is also stated poetically in terms of eagle's wings. Eagles, as we know, are the most majestic birds on earth. They allow us a beautiful personal metaphor for how God saves his people and how he protects them with his metaphorical wings. Verse 5. Now therefore, if you will indeed obey my voice and keep my covenant, then you shall be a special treasure to me above all people, for all the earth is mine. Here we learn that God's covenant is conditional. Certain things must be done on the side of the people for the covenant to be realized. For God's people, what is to be done is obedience. Obedience to God's covenant law, which he will give next. After he establishes his place and after he establishes the people's place, his place is to set the parameters of the covenant And the place of the people is to accept the parameters of the covenant or die. And I say it that way because there is no bargaining The covenant God makes with his people is not a collaborative effort. It is his way or death. We are always to keep that in mind. Verse 6. And you shall be to me a kingdom, a priest, and a holy nation. These are the words which you shall speak to the children of Israel. What God wants his people to be is first to be contrasted with what they were, which isn't in a state of servitude. They were in bondage. We know now because we know Jesus that what God wants of his people is to be little Christs, or will we say, Christians. Who are called such because they have been purified, made clean by the Son of God. Verse 7 So Moses came and called for the elders of the people and laid before them all these words which the Lord commanded him. This is the leadership that we spoke about last week from Exodus 18. Moses tells his elders, and they tell the people. Verse 8. Then all the people answered together and said, All that the Lord has spoken, we will do. So Moses brought back the words of the people to the Lord. The ascent of the people should be commended because they had not yet been given the stipulations for this covenant. The law had not yet been heard, yet they willed in that moment to obey. But of course they would be foolish not to trust God Who had shown time and time again that he was a God who was trustworthy. Verse nine And the Lord said to Moses, Behold, I come to you in the thick cloud, that the people may hear when I speak with you and believe you forever. So Moses told the words of the people To the Lord. Here is God in a great cloud, it says, not a pillar cloud as before, but a great cloud. And such a cloud Jesus will be riding upon on his second coming. Here is a cloud of authority and a cloud of mystery. Verses 10 and 11. Then the Lord said to Moses, Go to the people and consecrate them today and tomorrow and let them wash their clothes. And let them be ready for the third day, for on the third day the Lord will come down upon the Mount Sinai in the sight of all the people. The people needed to be sanctified, which is to be made holy, because they were going to meet with God. who is holy. The required washing was not because they could get all of the dirt out of their clothes. But was a lesson for the people that God is holy, and thus he should be approached, approached as he directs. Verse 12 and 13. You shall set bounds for the people all around, saying, Take heed to yourselves that you do not go up to the mountains or touch its base. Whoever touches the mountain shall surely be put to death. Not a hand shall touch him, but he shall surely be stoned or shocked with an arrow, whether man or beast, he shall not live When the trumpet sounds long, they shall come near the mountain. Fear. Fear is what God is after with his instruction here. Not fear as in scared senseless or frightened so that the people turn and run But fear in terms of awe, of wonder, and warning that God is not to be trivialized, and that experiencing Him is not common to the fallen man. People can only approach God's presence as he stipulates and in no other manner. Verse 14 and 15. So Moses went down from the mountain to the people and sanctified the people, and they washed their clothes. And he said to the people, Be ready. For the third day, do not come near your wives. Moses instructs as God commanded. The restriction against conjugal opportunities communicates the soul-mindedness of the people that they are to have that soul-mindedness when they encounter Dha. Verse 16. Then it came to pass on the third day in the morning that there were thunderings and lightnings and a thick cloud on the mountain, and the sound of the trumpet was very loud. so that all the people who were in the camp trembled. Indicated in this description is that God wants his people to fear. He wants to put a fear in the people to scare sin out of them. God wants his people to understand how serious it is to be before God. To be in the hands of God. Verse 17 and 18. And Moses brought the people out of the camp to meet with God, and they stood at the foot of the mountain. Now Mount Sinai was completely in smoke because the Lord descended upon it in fire. Its smoke ascended like the smoke of a furnace, and the whole mountain quaked greatly We have to wonder what were they thinking? What were they thinking in that moment What crossed their mind? What did they say, if anything? What did they want to say, but didn't? This was a moment like no other moment in the whole of the history of mankind. A moment that was no doubt awe-inspiring and also very humbling. Verse 19 and 20. And when the blast of the trumpet sounded long and became louder and louder, Moses spoke, and God answered him by voice. Then the Lord came down upon Mount Sinai on the top of the mountain, and the Lord called Moses to the top of the mountain, and Moses went up. Thus in the great dramatic moment of God meeting his people and sounds and quakes going around the people, there came a voice. It is a voice that is distinctly God's voice. It is a voice of mercy and kindness. Kindness in that God would speak, in that God would lower himself to come down to the people. When God calls Moses up, it is to communicate to him a calling up of the people. And Moses as his as their representative. Verse 20 and 20 21 and 22. And the Lord said to Moses, Go down and warn the people lest they break through to gaze at the Lord, and many of them perish. Also let the priests who come near the Lord consecrate themselves, lest the Lord break out against them. So here is a give and take. There may have been some who were more curious than fearful, and thus wanted to peek at the presence of God. God has grace for them. There are some who needed to stand before God, the priests, to receive his instruction, and God wanted to be merciful to them. Verse 23-25. But Moses said to the Lord, The people cannot come up to Mount Sinai, for you warned us, saying, Set bounds around the mountain and consecrate it. Then the Lord said to him, Away, get down and then come up, you and Aaron with you. But do not let the priests and the people break through and come up to the Lord. Lest he break out against them. So Moses went down to the people and spoke to them. So apparently Moses was a bit confused. God had said the people should come up, and then he said the people would perish if they came up upon the mountain upon which God was resting himself. God helps Moses understand that as his prophet and as Aaron his priest, when they come up, the people come up. And all of this Moses did as God commanded. And all of this was to prepare the people to receive God's mandate, his commandments for the covenant And comparing the one true God to the gods that were worshipped at this Sinai Peninsula at the time of the arrival of Israel into the Promised Land. There is one primary difference we need to identify. And I say one, because although we can identify some of the names of the many gods that were worshipped in this region We do not have sufficient evidence to know how these false gods were worshipped, how they were served. Archaeologists conclude that the religious practices of this region were recorded on papyrus, and papyrus in that region could not survive long, and thus they leave not much evidence behind. So we must surmise is that God, the God of Israel, was different than these gods because he could not be satisfied. He could not be appeased by the people. We know this at least that the worship of the false gods of the region consisted of appeasing the gods So that the gods would not punish the people. And this, those of you who know your history, know it is very similar to the Greek and the Romans as they worship their false gods. The gods of the region were temperamental, and the people thought they could satisfy those temperaments by their offerings, by their sacrifices. But the God of Israel, the God who says he is the only God, was showing Israel at the foot of Mount Sinai that he could not be appeased. And that he was altogether something different than the people had ever known. He was holy. He was great. He was mighty He was too wonderful to be looked upon by fallen human eyes. And as the one true God was showing Israel who he was, he was also showing them who they were. They were not worthy to see and to know God unless God made them worthy. They were not able to appease him, but were required instead to obey him. Unlike the many gods of the region, the God of Israel, the only God, spoke, and what he spoke was to be heeded. What he spoke wasn't out of an unpredictable temperament. It was instead eternal truth. What the one true God spoke was objective. It was grounded in reality, and what God spoke was to be done. At the age of twenty-four, a girl by the name of Kanika from India became a Christian in secret. Her conversion was a secret to her parents who were devout Hindus Hindus are polytheistic. They worship animals and plants and trees and even rivers. Idols of many sorts And the gods they worship are gods that need to be, require to be, appeased. And one morning, Kanika's family woke up at dawn. To join a long line of practicing Hindus waiting to worship Manasa Devi, the goddess of snakes. Which this goddess is thought to cure chickenpox and other diseases. When worshipping Manasa Devi, Hindus avoid apparently avoid heat. The day before the ceremony, they didn't cook their food or use hot water. They also left food in the road as an offering to this goddess.
