Most are aware that Christians in India face persecution in the form of violence, shunning, and yes, even death. Kanika knew she would face such persecution, even by the hands of her own family. But she chose to follow Jesus because she recognized him as one and not many And it was revealed to her that this one true God is not like many gods, because the one true God appeases himself by dying for all of mankind. God revealed himself to Israel in the manner that we read in Exodus 19, so as to separate himself from all the false gods that Israel had been exposed to and would be exposed to. Israel needed to understand God as holy and fearful. And it is that holy and fearful God that revealed himself later as the Son of Man. The Son of God. And we are to contrast the God of Sinai with the Son of God, the one who walked among men. Whereas the God of Sinai called Moses to come up and relay his words to the people, Jesus the Son of God, calls people to himself to hear his words, to hear the word of God. Jesus spoke the word to us, and he is the word of God to us. Whereas God instructed Israel to obey him in order to be a part of the covenant that he was making with Israel. Jesus went and did the obedience for us. That was in his temptation accomplished in the desert. It is what his faithfulness on the cross accomplished. He became our obedience, so that, as Paul said to the Galatians, so that we could put on Jesus. We put on righteousness. Adam and Eve had to put on animal skin to cover their nakedness. We get to put on Jesus. And thus we get to put on righteousness, and thus we are clothed for heaven And whereas God wanted the people of Israel to be holy, a holy nation, Jesus makes us a holy nation. As our propitiation, he becomes our righteousness, so that we are able to offer up our lives. as sacrifices to God, which Paul said is our reasonable service. We are to enter the Holy of Holies, which is the presence of Jesus, having our sins forgiven, having our petitions heard. Whereas the people had to respond in unison in agreement to what God had said, followers, believers in Jesus get to speak both as a people And yet also as individuals, because we have free access to the Holy of Holies. We have free access to Jesus as our high priest. Whereas the people had to be consecrated by washing their own clothes so as to resemble in some way a type of holiness. We who know Jesus have had our clothing, our sins, washed in the blood of the Lamb. And thus being given robes of white, we have been given clothes suitable for the wedding feast. Whereas the people of God were called to come forward, but not get too close, to not touch, to not see. We who know Jesus get to come and taste and see that the Lord is good. We get to look behind the curtain. We get to taste the bread and the wine. And we have the promise that we shall see God face to face. Jesus and only Jesus makes all of this possible. He makes the God of Exodus 19 approachable. But there is a problem. The devil has succeeded amongst our own to present God. As either the God of Exodus nineteen, who is fearful and unapproachable, or Or a God that is so very amiable and comfortable that he is Jesus in genes. The God that is holy, fearful, and unapproachable is a God that many perceive they can't speak to, for their sins are too many and too often repeated. I might think that he is a God who will reject me because of my unfaithfulness, my unkindness, my lack of stewardship, my lustfulness, my hypocrisy. He is a God who will reject me immediately, for he sees right through me. And so with that perspective, many walk away from God. And the Jesus in Jeans, well, he is approachable, very likable. He likes the music I like. He understands my troubles. He listens really well. He doesn't judge me and I don't feel guilty being around him. But since that Jesus doesn't seem to require anything of me, well I stay in my sinful ways. You hear the problem, I trust. Either extreme views of God by themselves may corrupt the gospel. Comparing the Jesus of the Gospels to the God of Sinai, they can seem many, many miles apart. There is a better picture for us. And that picture is from the book of Revelation Remember when John is taken up into heaven, he sees, as recorded in chapter four, a throne. And one who sits on the throne. He's not given a name. He is said to look like Jasper and Sardis. And there was a rainbow around the throne and those 24 elders around the one. The one on the throne. And from that throne came lightning and thunder. Sounds like Exodus 19. And there were creatures flying all around the one on the throne, saying, Holy, holy, holy. And the creatures and elders repeatedly fall down before the one. And then from the throne comes a scroll to be opened But amongst the many creatures around the throne, no one is worthy to open that scroll until a lamb is spotted. Spotted between the elders and the one. He is the worthy one And so the same God who is on the throne is the same lamb who is worthy to be slain. And such is a healthy view, the Christian understanding of who God is. He is the God of Sinai and Jesus of Nazareth. He is the one on the throne and the one lamb who was slain. God wants us to know him, to know him as the God of Sinai and the Lamb. Fear, awe, love, and approachable. That is the one true God To know him any differently is to not know him. To know him as Sinai and the Lamb, that is to be saved. Amen. Let us pray

sermons.title: Making Us All Together Different
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: It plays our places, what we want to do, and you can In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. We remain in Exodus this morning, but just a little bit differently. Having preached through Exodus chapter 19, we come to chapter 20 The very chapter where we hear for the first time the Ten Commandments. I preached a few years ago a series of sermons examining each of the Ten Commandments listed And so we are not going to rewind here. What I think is necessary for us is to acknowledge that The other commandments given after the Ten Commandments, or the Ten Words as the Jewish people refer to them. It is argued, and I think argued well, that the commandments that come after the Ten Commandments are more specific applications of the more general commandments, the general Ten Commandments. And while the Ten Commandments are understandable by most in terms of why they are needed and what they mean. The other commandments that are more specific in their application are not so easily understood by many in terms of why they are necessary. Some laws seem obscure and others seem outdated. The law against working on the Sabbath and the punishment being death if it's broken. is an example. The law is understandable, but the punishment of death seems extreme. Then there are laws against the eating of shellfish. Another against cooking a kid goat in its mother's milk. Another against weaving two different types of bread together. Another against planting two different types of crops in the same field. Another against cutting the edges of one's beard. And even more that have been labeled by unbelievers to be well weird The critics of these laws have been many of late, as it is one of the strategies of modern atheists to argue that the laws found in the Old Testament are so weird That they discredit the whole Bible entirely. We would respond that such a conclusion is knee-jerk. And as both cultural and chronological snobbery on their part, as they consider their perspective in such matters more sophisticated today, And that the laws of old were formed and followed out of ignorance. Their accused ignorance is matched by the level of their arrogance. A 12th century rabbi by the name of Moses ben Maimon counted 613 distinct laws in the Old Testament. 613. That's a lot of do's and don'ts. To begin to understand what Christians are to do with these many laws, we have to be reminded of the overall purpose of the law. What was God's main purpose in giving all of these laws? Some have said that the laws are given out of practical purposes, or for practical purposes. We Don't have laws that govern us because and yet because we are fallen creatures and we have the ability to destroy ourselves, the law is given that it might help us not do that, not destroy ourselves There were, to be sure, practical reasons with certain laws given. St. Paul tells us that the real purpose of the law Was and still is to lead a person to Jesus. Paul said to the Galatians that the law is as a tutoring That leads us to Christ so that we might be justified by faith. And it works like the following We hear a commandment, and two things seem to happen within us. First, we want to break the commandment. As St. Paul described in Romans, it is as if something evil is woken up inside of us when we are told specifically what not to do. I can say something as ridiculous as no one in the sanctuary during the service can look at his or her shoes. That's the commandment. You can't look at your shoes. And what do we want to do as soon as we hear such a commandment? What does everybody want to do? Look at their shoes. And so evil within us is revealed when we are given a commandment. And the second thing that happens when a law is given is we are feeling guilty. Because we could not keep the law. Some of you have looked at your shoes. We can't keep the law. And St. Paul described it for us all. When he said that he does the very thing he does not want to do, and what he does want to do, that very thing he does not do. And so we are all guilty for things we have done and things we have left undone. What wretched creatures we all are. Who shall save us from this? And to understand the various laws given, we also need to rehearse where Israel was when they were given these laws. Israel was in the Sinai Peninsula, about to enter the Promised Land. They were amongst polytheistic people They were the only tribe that worshipped one God. And the manner these other tribes worshiped their false gods was vast immoral. And at worst, abominable. Abominable against God and against humanity. Thus what these cultures practice in their everyday behavior and in their false worship is directly connected to the type of laws given to the people to govern them and thus keep them away from falling into the habits of the tribes around them Let's take the law that prohibits cooking a young goat, a kid, in its mother's milk. Although there is much debate about the origin of this law, it can be justifiably concluded that such was actually being done in the region of the Sinai Peninsula By pagan tribes as some type of fertility ritual. From the law that forbids it, we can conclude that there is a natural care that is in exchange by a mother of an animal providing milk for her kid. And thus to kill the kid, the young goat, and that which is to nourish him, is a perversion that Israel was to have nothing to do with Now consider next the common principles that are that is found the common principle that is found in some of the laws that are labeled weird In Leviticus 19 and in Deuteronomy 22, there are laws that prohibit the mixed breeding and cross-breeding of cattle. There are also laws that prohibit using two kinds of steed in a field, as mentioned. Laws that prohibit the mixing of fibers And even prohibit the ploughing of a field with a donkey on one side of a yoke and an oxen on the other. Well, what do these laws have in common? What principle is in each of these laws? Well, I hope it is obvious that God is symbolically teaching Israel that they are to be separate from the people around them. They are not to mix with pagan people. And this has nothing to do with race, but had everything to do with the false gods these other nations worshipped. Bad company corrupts. It indeed does. And bad company that would tempt you to worship false gods is the worst kind of bad company. And what I hope is being made more obvious when we consider these examples is that the Christian life The Christian life and the good news of God are embedded in the laws that he gave to Israel. And to see this even more clearly, we must consider the laws that forbid certain meats, dietary laws. How Christians are to treat others, especially those who are weaker among us, can be seen in the dietary laws. Listen to this quote by Mary Douglas, a scholar and author. She says this, the forbidden animal species exemplify the predators, on the one hand, That is those who eat blood, and on the other, the sufferers of injustice. Consider the list, especially the swarming insects, the chameleon with its lumpy face the high-humped tortoise and beetle, and the ants lumbering under their huge loads. Think of the the blindness of worms and bats The vulnerability of fish without scales. Think of their human parallels. The laborers, the beggars, the orphans, and defenseless widows. Not themselves, but the behavior that reduces them to this state is an abomination No wonder the Lord made the crawling things and found them good. It is not in the grand style of the law to take time off from cosmic themes to teach that these pathetic creatures. are to be shunned because their bodies are disgusting, vile, bad, any more than it is consistent with its theme of justice to teach that the poor are to be shunned. Shunning is not the issue. Predation is wrong. Eating is a form of predation, and the poor are not prey. I love that last point. The poor are not praying. And we are to understand that by what we eat or do not eat. It is wise to find a Christian witness in our diet. God spoke to Israel through his law and addressed all aspects of living as his people. Thus we can say that it is not what is eaten or not eaten that matters to the Christian today, for all food has been declared clean in the book of Acts. The issue is that we are taught what we are taught in the dietary laws, which is also taught in the New Testament, we are to care for the poor. The disenfranchised, the needy, the weak, the widowed. Israel was to avoid eating what symbolized preying on the vulnerable in society And we as Christians are to avoid forgetting about the vulnerable. Such is profound, I think. Another importance of the various laws in the Old Testament is the need for justice. Our God, the one true God, is a God of justice. The law of Moses acknowledges that individual persons have been given rights by God. The right to life is one as the sixth commandment states. The right to personal property is another as the eighth commandment states. Thus, when a life is either harmed or taken by another person, the person taking the life must be held accountable. And when property is stolen or devalued, the property or value must be restored by the guilty party. And as a just God, there is within the law a recognition that not every time a life is taken or a life is maimed is someone directly responsible. There is then recognized a difference between premeditated murder and a death by accident And there is a recognition for the need of restitution, which is obviously missing in our culture today If a young man was to steal my car and take it for a joyride and crash it, And total the vehicle and was caught and had to go to jail for his crime I would begin to contribute to his incarceration by my tax money going to pay for his bed, food, and clothes. And since I only have liability insurance on my vehicle, I am without a car. And still footing the food and housing bill for the criminal who made off with my vehicle. Where is the justice in such a scenario? In God's law, restitution and more is required. For instance, in Exodus 22, it is commanded that if one man steals another man's livestock, kills it and slaughters it, And he is found guilty, he is to pay the victim five oxen for one oxen stolen, and four sheep for one sheep stolen. That is restitution. That is justice. For a proper understanding of the many laws found in the Old Testament It is vital that we understand as his people what God was doing with all of these 613 laws. What we can know about many Old Testament laws is from the words of Jesus Himself. Remember, when addressing the issue of divorce, Jesus said the following, because of the hardness of heart Because of the hardness of heart, Moses allowed you to divorce your wives, but from the beginning it was not so What was not so from the beginning? Well it was that God, what he intended all along, which was that men do not divorce their wives. But God knew how weak men were, and so he permitted divorce for a time. He knew where the Israelites had come from and what tribes what they were practicing around them He knew how they would be influenced, and so he gave them certain laws for a time We also see this idea of laws for a time when Jesus says in several places regarding the law, you have heard it said, da-da-da, but I say da-da-da And whenever Jesus said such a thing, he always was raising the standard of holiness, he was never lowering it. And we are to conclude then that the law of Moses was never thought of as a finished product or a final standard. It was instead a standard to be used for a time, and during that time the people of God were to be carefully pulled away from the cultural influences around them. pulled away in order that they might be a different people, a strange people, a peculiar people. They were to be different, strange and peculiar, and that they were a holy people, as their lives conformed to the image of God and not the fallen humanity around them. When raising our children, we taught them to embrace being different. Not for the sake of being different, mind you. But to get them used to being different, so that when their faith made them stand out, when they took a moral stand and No one else took it. Or when they spoke a truth and no one else wanted to hear it, and they found themselves ostracized because of it. They would know that feeling of being different already, and it would not scare them A grand lie that many, many churches, many, many churches believed, started I think around the early 1980s. And it is still believed today. It is the lie that the church or each local church needs to assimilate into its surroundings And part of assimilating is to look like the culture. And so local churches started playing music and corporate worship that had the a similar sound to what is playing on the radio And buildings started to look like buildings that allowed for multiple activities because that's what was being done in the culture. And pastor started dressing casual, and furnishing started to be put in theater style And pulpits were removed, and cordless microphones were used, and churches would advertise themselves saying to this unbelieving world, you won't even know you're in church. Thankfully, thankfully, God has revealed the lie to some. The Holy Spirit has reminded some Christian leaders that the word church It's ecclesia, which means the called out once. The church is a call is called out to be distinct from the culture that surrounds it. The Holy Spirit has reminded leaders of the teachings of Jesus that his church is to be like a city on a hill, which means it is to be a beacon that guides the lost. The church is not to follow anyone, but the Savior. And look how much our culture needs to follow truth. This last election shows how divided we are as a culture. And the church should have never assimilated into a political party and should never assimilate into a culture of division. We as Christians, as a people of God, are to be different. We are to to provide for a lost and dying world. What it does not have and what it cannot get anywhere else. Tell me Tell me, where are the people of our culture going to hear? Remember, O man, from dust you came, and to dust you shall return. Who is going to say such words if the church does not? Where else is the culture going to hear that the wages of sin is death? But the free gift of eternal life is in Christ Jesus. Where else is that going to be heard if it's not said by the church? And who else is going to say, this is my body and offer you bread, and this is my blood and offer you wine? No one but the people of God will say it. And so we are to embrace being different. And that is why it is good for me to wear a white robe when we worship. We are to be different. That is why we have a pulpit and have a lectern and have a communion table. These are set aside for specific uses in corporate worship because what we use them for is different. You don't bring your lunch in here, pull up a chair at the communion table, and eat a tuna sandwich, crack open a coke and a bag of chips You don't do that because the table is different and you're different. This truth has been building up in me for some time. I want us to embrace being different. That we actually are a city on a hill I want every soul that is seeking God in our area to know us and to find us and to experience what is different when they do find us. I want every soul that is seeking God to say when they come here, here is different, and here is what I need. I close with a portion of a letter that I hope highlights what is needed today. Our Academy has reached out to local churches to see if they would advertise the ministry of our school to the families in their parish. One particular female who calls herself pastor wrote the following email reply. She said, I commend you for reaching out to our congregation. It is good when we share our blessings from God with one another. However, after reading both your church's website as well as your academy's website, I am unable to support this ministry After much prayer, I am sad that we have differences that keep us apart. As you might have known, I am a woman, Pastor, which would be impossible in your faith tradition. I also have grave concerns about your church's stand on human sexuality. My faith tradition believes that the Bible is inspi the inspired Word of God. I struggle with picking and choosing Bible passages. If all sins were held in the same degree, I don't understand why your pastor has cut his hair. I wonder if anyone in your congregation has eaten crabs or other shellfish. I think this time in our church's history, we are called to come together in grace and mercy and love for all people. Did you notice the poor reference to the Old Testament law? The logic is that if obscure laws in the Old Testament are subject to change, Then laws that are of a moral nature are subject to change as well. Such a response Reveals an assimilation to a culture in which instead of calling people out of sin and out of the culture It makes them feel comfortable in both their sin and in the culture. That is not what the law was for It is not what Jesus told his church to be and to do. The law called the people out. And Jesus instructed us to be different in order to help save people. And that's what we're going to do. Amen. Let us pray.

sermons.title: What we are capable of
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. May be seated. We are looking at Exodus 32, as usual, encourage you to turn in your few Bibles there to Exodus 32, but I begin with a few stories At the end of November 2011, five years ago, a high school student in Sacramento, California, or high school student, in Sacramento, California, experienced a loud explosion that was heard throughout the entire building The source? Two student boys ages 16 and 15 lit an M80 firework and threw it into a toilet bowl. And shattered the light fixture, blowing the entire toilet to pieces On a history test question, a high school student was asked, what ended in 1896? Knowing only one answer, the student wrote 1895. On a math question, a student was given a right triangle And told to find the X. The only answer the student knew was to circle the X and write, here it is A mother confessed to receiving a note from her daughter's kindergarten teacher informing her that her daughter had brought her baby brother's dried-up umbilical cord That had just fallen off to show and tell and passed it around. Another parent confessed that he received a phone call from his son's teacher who informed him that his son had brought dog poop to school to show for show and tell, explaining that he thought it was cool because it had carrots in it. I share these true stories with you because they are proof that a parent is a fool Who says something like, my child would never do that? Our children are capable of most any action that would embarrass us. But what do you think you are capable of doing? What are we, as grown-ups, capable of doing Too many Christians hear or read for themselves the story of Israel worshipping the Golden Bull and conclude that they would never do such a thing. They would never turn away from God so quickly after witnessing the ten plagues, the parted sea, the fallen mamma, the water from rocks, and the giving of the Ten Commandments. But how do we know we would not worship that golden bull? The truth is we don't know, and we cannot know until we are faced with such a temptation. The theme for this sermon is St. Paul's words to the Corinthians, who after describing the very sin that we read about in Exodus 32, Paul gave this following admonishment. After describing the sin of Israel in the desert Worshiping a false idol. Paul says, whoever thinks he stands, take heed lest he fall. In the context, it is saying that whoever thinks he or she would not have committed the same sin of idolatry as Israel did, as recorded in Exodus 32, such a person is to receive a warning that too much confidence in self may be the cause of your ultimate downfall I've chosen to preach from Exodus 32, which means we're jumping 10 chapters here. Because last week we discussed the placement of the minor laws, which are commentaries on the general Ten Commandments. Now we're not going to go through all of those minor laws, but I am cherry-picking passages that I believe will be the most useful for us from Exodus. And so we are here in Exodus 32. Moses had been gone, by the time this is written, almost forty days. From what the people could see, the top of the mountain was alive with lightning and thunder With the power of God on display and the weakness of man realized, the people could easily have concluded that Moses was dead. If Moses was dead, the people had no leader, no visible leader, no visible representation of God. And it is difficult to read what Aaron did next. Some suggest that Aaron was stalling. Because Moses had to plead later for Aaron's life, we can say that God certainly held him culpable. And we should note that what is sometimes translated calf, you've heard me say a young bull, which means the idol would have been a full-grown animal. Now, one defense of Aaron is that some pagan worshipers would use golden bulls, statues, as a seat. for the God they worship to sit upon. Thus Aaron perhaps was trying to compromise by believing that he was only making a throne for the one true God. The text suggests that the idol was first rough cast in solid gold and then finished with some sort of tool. When Aaron presents the finished idol, he says, these are your gods. And this causes us to question, why would he use the plural form? The New King James Version translates it as God, singular, but the original Hebrew is plural. And it matches what the people requested. They requested of Aaron, make us gods. But the idol was one. Some commentators say that it is worded in the plural because the first of the Ten Commandments is worded in the plural. No other gods before me. Aaron could very well be referring to that commandment when he says, Here are your gods. Adding more to not fully condemning Aaron, we hear him say that the worship at the feet of the idol was to be a feast to the Lord. He uses the word Yahweh. in that text. The behavior described while the people are worshiping is truly what condemns them. It reveals what was truly in their hearts. They wanted to express themselves in the manner that they did. They behaved like the tribes around them as they mixed their understanding of God with their desires of the flesh. But we we would never give in to the desires of the flesh, right? We would never do that When God reveals to Moses what the people are doing, we hear a bit of sarcasm as he calls the people Moses people. God does not want to take ownership of them while they are reveling. God then calls the people stiff-necked. Which is a farmer's metaphor for an ox or a horse that won't respond to the rope being tugged. It means stubborn and willful But we we would never be stubborn or willful, right? When Moses pleads for the people, he reveals his heart. And his reasoning, notice his reasoning that he states back to the Lord, why not to kill all of these people? His reasoning is not to save the people foremost, but to save the reputation of God. And Moses makes no excuse for the behavior of the people. He is so very different than leaders of today who find every reason under the sun to explain away their own evil behavior or the evil behavior of others. In verse 14, where the New King James uses the word relented, it is actually literally repented. The Lord repented. That God repented is not as if he was surprised by what was happening or that he literally changed his mind. Bad theologians make a great deal out of such a passage. The description of God repenting is an anthropomorphic description It is the action of God being described in human terms so that you and I can understand. It means here that God was going in a different direction than he originally said he would go. And we must remember that God's covenant with his people is conditional. When the people sin, well plans change. Moses next makes his way down the mountain, and we read for the first and last time that the law was written on both sides of the tablets. The emphasis on the divine origin of the writing is important as to what's going to happen next. As Moses comes down the mountain, he meets up with Joshua, who had been waiting all those forty days at a distance from Moses and up on the mountain away from the unfaithful people below. When Moses comes an eyewitness to the sin of the people that they were committing, it seems that it overwhelmed him. We should consider that he was with the Lord all those days. He was coming from the very essence of holiness. Coming from the essence of holiness to next being a witness to actions so vile and offensive that Moses had to act emotionally. Moses showed righteous indignation as he broke the tablets. Moses does what we would have done, right? He is offended by sins of the flesh just as we would be, and we are, right? Of course, the breaking of the tablets was not simply an act of unbridled anger. It was also a symbolic act representing the fact that Moses was a witness to Israel breaking her covenant with God. Breaking it by breaking most of the Ten Commandments in one day. After Moses broke the tablets, he next destroyed the idol itself. As he had the gold ground into powder, poured it out over water, and forced the Israelites to drink it. The irony in that is in the fact that they could drink, they could consume the idol that they were worshiping. It was to impress upon them the powerlessness that such idols have. And this is what we would do, right? We would do that Grind that idol down. We would be wise to show sinful people the error of their ways. Right? Our sadness regarding Aaron's actions is doubled when he gives a lame description of how this idle bull was cast. He sounds very much like an adolescent making up a lie when he says the gold was thrown into the fire and a golden bull popped out. We would never do that, right? We would never make an excuse for what we did Or tell a story about how things actually didn't happen as if they actually happened, right? We would never do that. In fact, we would never sin to begin with. So we wouldn't have to lie about it. Right? St. Paul's warning to the Corinthians is to humble every believer that has ears to hear. Whoever thinks he stands, take heed lest he fall The fall is in the same manner, the same way Israel fell. It is doing something we think we would never do. It is to think too highly of our constitutions and our own wills, as if we ourselves can ward off sin by our own wisdom and our own strength. From the writings of Polycarp, a second-century Christian bishop, we hear of a man named Quintus. He is a mere footnote in the history of Christianity, but he is an important footnote. As he is noted as one of the first apostates. His story is told in brief. Quintus was a new convert to Christianity in the midst of great persecution by the Romans upon the Christians. Quintus made a big show of himself originally as he volunteered himself and a few others to be put on trial for his faith. But when the Roman Procouncil showed the wild beasts he would be thrown to, well, Quintus turned. He renounced his faith and made an offering to the Roman gods. But that is not what we would have done. We would not have cowered at the sight of beasts. We would have been faithful, even as the beasts were devouring us. Right? There's not a quintess among us, right? In the fourth century, a young boy named Julian was grandson to Constantine. Who, as we know, was the first Roman emperor to claim a faith in Jesus as his Savior and who made the expression of Christian worship lawful within the Roman Empire, the great Constantine. Julian had a chance to build upon the faith of his grandfather, but because of the infighting of his family for the throne of the Roman Empire. After the death of Constantine, Julian wanted nothing more to do with Christianity, for he never saw the faith lived out by his parents. So instead of helping Christianity spread, Julian became its greatest enemy. He even tried to restore the pagan practices of early Rome. He thus became known as Julian the Apostate. But we we would have understood what Julian was doing. You and I would never go apostate. We would have seen the gospel of Jesus Christ from the scriptures, not having to worry about whether our family was living out the faith. Right? Thomas Krabner in 1533, chosen to be Archbishop of Canterbury. Once his appointment was approved by the Pope, Cramner declared King Henry's marriage to Catherine Boyd. Four months later, he married him to Anne Boleyn. With Thomas Cromwell, he supported the translation of the Bible into English. In 1545, he wrote a litany that is still used in the church. Under the reign of Edward VI, Cramner was allowed to make the doctrinal changes that he thought necessary for the church. In 1549, he helped complete the Book of Common Prayer. During the reign of Edward VI, son of Henry VIII, Cramber returned to the Church of England, and truly established it as Protestant. And after Edward's death, Cramner supported Lady Jane Grade as successor. Her nine-day reign was followed by the Roman Catholic Mary. Who tried him for treason. After a long trial and imprisonment, Cramner became weak in the faith, weak in his resolve to stand for the gospel truth. In his weakened state, he signed a declaration that rescinded his previous beliefs, thinking that if he did so, it would save him from the death penalty. But that was not the manner of Queen Mary, who ordered Cramner to be burned at a stake. Having realized his foolish weaknesses, Cramner rescinded his rescinding and dramatically stuck his right hand that signed that declaration, stuck that in the fire first. That it would burn first, claiming again the gospel. We can now see that Cramler was a weak man. We would not have weakened in prison. We would have stared the death sentence down, stood up to bloody Mary. All of us would have. Right? Frankie Schaefer is the son of Francis Schaefer, the well-known evangelist and Christian apologist from the 1970s and 80s. Francis Schaefer was as influential in the Christian church during those two decades as Billy Graham was. Frankie Schaefer grew up in a home that held the gospel of Jesus Christ as central to all of life. But Frankie became a bitter man after his parents died. He didn't appreciate how he was raised as he came to think it was some sort of brainwashing. He has, in his adult life, renounced most of what his parents have taught him, and now he calls himself an atheist who believes in God, but not Jesus as God. And we say, what a waste. He threw away a Christian heritage we would have loved to have had. We would have appreciated everything about our parents and our faith heritage. Right? George Perdiccas was an original member of the News Boys. The News Boys is a band that has produced Christian pop rock since the 1980s. Perdiccas, although he left the band a number of years ago, came out publicly as an atheist last year. While proclaiming his atheism, he also tried to expose the Christian pop music industry as being full of hypocrites who only care about making money. Perdiccas claims that one in ten persons in Christian pop music industry is actually a Christian. I am glad none of us has been hypocritical in living out our faith. We would never claim Jesus and not be a true believer. And we would never make false claims about the sins of others, right? Whoever thinks he stands, take heed, lest he fall. Israel turning so quickly to false idols is a sad story, but it is a story of the human condition. It is a story of how far from glory we all are, and how much our souls need to be made holy and made secure in the love of God. Remember, a repeated message in the book of Revelation is for all Christians to hold on. To hold on. And whenever someone tells you to hold on, something's come. Hold on. We are told to hold on to the truths of the gospel. We are told to hold on to the faith we have been given and to grow in that faith, holding on. We have to live our lives with the confession that we too could fall away, turn away, no longer believe, or be fooled. to believe what is false. And that knowledge is to make us humble. And when we are humble, God lifts us up. When St. Paul uses the story of Israel worshipping a golden calf as a warning to Christians, it is not to make them insecure. But only to humble them. This is the perfect lesson for the first Sunday in Advent Where we take the time to consider our preparation for the coming of Jesus. Because Jesus is coming, we need to take heed Thus we fall. Right? Let us pray.

sermons.title: Anticipation
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit. Amen. May be seated. Anticipation. We can never know about the days ahead, but we think about them anyway. Anticipation. Anticipation. It's making me wait. It's keeping me waiting. Remember that song? All you do is date yourselves with me. Surely you can remember that upside-down Heinz ketchup bottle, right? And the long-waited expectation for that red bliss to drop on that fresh hot dog. It's just, right? But what is it about waiting that stirs the soul? The expectation or wait for something can be exhilarating, exhausting. Nerve-wracking and sometimes downright scary. For those of you who have parented children, think about your firstborn. All the thoughts and all the questions that you have What will it be like to be a parent? Will I be a good one? What will my child be like? The anticipation of bringing a child into this world and then caring for that child until adulthood is awesome in every way. Now we won't mention those whole teenage years and those lessons. By lessons I mean yours, not theirs. Well imagine being pregnant with a baby that was well conceived in a miraculous way. Imagine, if you will, being Mary and having the Holy One of Israel in your belly. I heard it said by a wise bishop not long ago that we are better with our Bibles open than with them closed. So if you have a mind to open your Bibles, please open to our gospel reading, which is Luke chapter 1, beginning in verse. 26. Very familiar story. One a passage that is actually placed in the Book of Common Prayer for the reading at Easter. The Annunciation for the Blessed Mary, which obviously is fitting and rightly so, but it is also certainly appropriate as a passage as we anticipate The celebration of the coming of our Lord. So as we move into this Advent season What is your anticipation? What is on your heart and mind as you consider the coming season? Let's be honest, for many of us Many people today, the biggest concern is how I'm going to pay for it. And possibly the biggest anticipation is waiting to see how much your Christmas bonus is going to be if you even get one anymore. and how much of your Christmas list you have to charge. Now I realize that many people here and elsewhere don't get caught up into the whole competing with Santa Claus thing, and I applaud you. Maybe you teach your child at three or four years old the real meaning, the real story. But even for you, there's a big anticipation about the coming of this coming Christmas Why is it that we are so filled with anticipation for the coming of Christmas? Well, I think Christmas is a time for hope for most of us. And for even those who differ in what their hope is in, there's a real sense of anticipation that comes over you the closer you get to Christmas Day. Maybe this year will be the season when a lost relationship is rekindled or healed. Maybe this season will be a season that my family will draw closer to the real meaning of Christmas. Have you ever hoped like that? If only this year I'll put the hustle bustle behind me and slow down my life enough So that we can feel the joy and anticipation for the coming of the King of Kings. So let's look this morning at Mary's anticipation. Imagine, first of all, her original perplexity when the angel Gabriel came to her announcing her good fortune. That she was going to be the blessed one of all women and conceived from the Holy Spirit, the Son of the Most High. Imagine the fear and uncertainty she must have had for the things to come that first Advent season. Although Gabriel does give her an immediate comfort by saying, do not be afraid, Mary, for you have found favor with God. Yet she was still uncertain about her circumstances. So God gives her further encouragement Gabriel informs her that Elizabeth is also carrying a miracle child. Verse 36. Behold, even your relative Elizabeth has also conceived a son in her old age. That she who was called barren is now in her sixth month. For nothing is impossible with God. Now, one of the ways that God encourages us when we are troubled Confused or hurting is to put someone in our lives who is going through a similar situation Or has been in that situation before. Has that ever happened to you? No matter your trial or difficulty, amazingly God puts you in circumstance after circumstance. Where you're either encouraging someone else with what you are going through or you are being encouraged by what they have gone through. It's in these moments that God wants to show us What a faithful and gracious God He is. God lets us know that there's a bigger story in our trial or situation than maybe we see or feel at that time. Sometimes he wants to show us something about ourselves. Sometimes he's teaching us about other people. But always he's showing himself to us. He wants us to look with hope and anticipation toward the season ahead, no matter what the issue or event might be, and no matter who might be in that greater story. In this case, it was a close relative, and Mary's response is immediate. She hurried to Elizabeth as fast as she could. We see that in verse 39. Now I, like most of you, have read or heard this passage year after year over and over again, and sometimes I ponder, why did God choose Mary? Why did God choose this young teenage girl from nowhere? I think the answer, I believe, is Found in the verses from 46 on, for Mary's response to Elizabeth's early words. Mary says, My soul exalts the Lord, and my spirit has rejoiced in God my Savior. For he has had regard for the humble state of his bondservant. For behold, from this time on, all generations will count me blessed, for the mighty one has done great things for me. And holy is his name. Here we see servanthood, not as one who acts as a submissive slave who has no choice. But rather as one who reflects the deep and powerful act of hope, Mary stood in hope and faith of God's gracious intentions that were about to be acted out within her. She acted out in service and obedience to the mighty one who had done great things for her. Has he done great things for you? Now servanthood runs counterclock uh counter-culture to the thinking of most of our society today, does it not? We equate servanthood with weakness. Servants are those who are unable to achieve enough success to become masters. Servants are those who don't know the language well, who aren't well educated, who come from Humble meanings, they don't come from families of prominence and success. Servants are not the ones who receive our admiration today. They are the high achievers, the wealthy, the famous. They can buy anything they want, go anywhere they want, and seemingly they can do anything they want They're on the cover of a magazine or in the spotlight somewhere. And even though we read about their personal drama and dysfunction, We still seem to be in awe of them and seem to want a life that's closer to theirs than the one that God offers us. Not so with Mary. God spoke and Mary obeyed. In a true biblical sense, obedience is hearing God Trusting God and doing what he asks. Mary teaches us that the most powerful people are those who are strong enough to become servants. Mary saw something greater in this song of hers. She gives us insight toward the end into her hope. In verse 51, she says He has scattered those who are proud in the thoughts of their heart. He has brought down rulers from their thrones, and has exalted those who are humble. He has filled the hungry with good things and sent away the rich empty-handed. Mary moves us from a quiet lullaby of praise. To a harsh reality. For those of us who think That all that we have has been blessed because of our great faithfulness, the new automobiles, the fancy homes. The full pantries, video cinemas in our family rooms. And somehow that's all a reward for our extraordinary faithfulness. We need to wake up. Mary knew better, and probably we do as well. While God does allow his people to prosper, thankfully, at times He still more often works in the humble. They are often more able to see clearly The lowly and the humble, the needy. The wealthy and the prosperous aren't off the hook. They just probably need to look or listen a little harder. You don't have to be a Mother Teresa or a Mary for that matter. God has something special for each of us to share in our own place in life. It doesn't have to be a week of service in Haiti or the Philippines cleaning up after a tragedy. It can be the smallest answer of obedience Visiting someone in a nursing home, someone who is homebound, providing food For a family in need. Helping the homeless or working with disadvantaged or abused children. The Advent season is a time to reflect on the love and gift that lay in the manger. What more humble setting could the King of Kings have come in? He didn't come to be served. He came to serve. I love the collar for this morning. We we we read two colleagues through the season. We read the first colic of the Advent season again every week and in the middle of that colic is a reminder of Christ's humility In the epistle to the Philippians, Paul talks about how Jesus emptied himself by taking on the form of a servant. Philippians 2, beginning in verse 6, who although he existed in the form of God, did not regard equality with God as things to be grasped. He emptied himself, taking on the form of a bond servant, and being made in the likeness of men, being found in appearance as a man, he humbled himself by becoming obedient to the point of death. Even death on a cross. In his incarnation, Jesus did not empty himself of any part of his essence as God. But rather he gave up or laid aside his privileges as God and took on to himself humanity. While retaining the essence of God, he became completely human. This is the concept difficult for most of us to put our arms around. But in basic terms, Jesus added to his divine essence a servant's essence. Paul does not say that Christ exchange the form of God for a the form of a servant, involving any loss of deity or any attributes of deity. Rather the incarnate Christ continued in his very nature. But added to himself the nature of a servant. Now, a servant is the lowest status on the social ladder. The exact opposite of the term Lord, a title in which Paul later in this passage tells us that we will all one day confess. Is it not amazing to think that a God who created the whole universe, who rules over all creation Would choose to add to himself the nature of a servant. As I do some introspection of myself from time to time, I find that this is an attribute that I need to improve on in my walk, to be a better servant for Christ. Now saying that Christ took on the likeness of a man also does not mean that Christ only appeared to be a man, as some heresies would have it. Rather, lightness emphasizes identity. He possessed all aspects of being human, except unlike all humanity, he was sinless. Although he never sinned and did not deserve to die, our suffering servants chose to die so that the sins of the world could be put on him. And Christ did not just die for us. He endured a suffering death, even the death on a cross. So why was Paul taking the Philippians and us down this long road of Christ's humility? Obviously, to make a great point. If Jesus Christ humbled himself so deeply, we should be willing to humble ourselves in our own small way. Surely if he became obedient to the extent of death, even the death on a cross, we should be more increasingly obedient to divine direction. And to living a life in the spirit of oneness, loneliness, and helpfulness, which is pleasing to God. These are attributes and characteristics of a servant. This is the babe that we celebrate this Advent season. This is the babe that lay in a manger. So back to Mary and her anticipation. Perhaps Mary can help us to understand that servanthood is not the condition that is left to those who cannot manage anything else. But rather it is a way that a person of faith finds the path that God has asked them to travel Mary's anticipation was no doubt mixed with anxiousness at times, worry of what her life to come would be, worry about what her son's life would become. But she followed that pathway of trust, obedience, and servanthood right to the foot of the cross. How about you? Your path may be long, it may be narrow, it may be very rocky, but it can lead to a humble setting, a stable, a manger. And eventually a cross. May he give us marriage strength and servanthood so that we might rightly bear our own. Amen.

sermons.text: In the name of the Father, of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. While in seminary back in nineteen ninety-four In Kansas City, Missouri, as they like to say. After putting the kids down, Bobby Lynn and I turned on the television. And lo and behold, the Christmas special was playing. A Christmas special hosted by Kathy Lee Gifford. It was the sappiest Christmas special we had ever seen, but it was like a car wreck in that you find yourself not being able to turn away The next three years, and I say this honestly, we happened upon that Christmas special by Kathy Lee Gifford. Every year it was stumbling on, happened to, turn it on, and there it is, and you can't turn away. Every year it was a car wreck. In one of those years, we heard the song for the first time, Mary Did You Know? It was sung by an opera singer and I must say, quite well done. Bobby, Lynn, and I were moved by the performance, by the words of the song. And soon after, Kenny Rogers recorded a duet with Winona Judd of that same song, and it was well done, and again we enjoyed the message. But in the next year, another Kathy Lee Gifford Christmas special, Kathy Lee sang the same song with Kenny Rogers And I lost all enjoyment. Nothing personal against Kathy Lee. She seems like a fine person. But the singing was subpar. The song has since been recorded by a number of artists, including the Pentatonics, and I have regained an appreciation for it. What I want us to realize about the song Mary, did you know, is that we who are liturgical in our worship should be able to answer that repeated question in the song because we sing things like the Magnificant The Magnificant was a song of praise sung by Mary as she was inspired by the Holy Spirit after the angel announced she would be with child and after she visited with Elizabeth confirming the words of the angel The repeated question is, Mary, did you know? And the simple answer is yes. Yes. Mary knew because the angel told her. Now let us examine the questions as they are sung in the song Mary Did You Know. First, Mary, did you know that your baby boy would one day walk on water? The answer, well, yes, she did. She was told by the angel that the son she would give birth to would have a kingdom that would have no end. And we learned from lessons and sermons on the gospel according to St. John last year that Jesus walking on water. was in part symbolic of him having power over all nations, as restless waters in Holy Scripture represent nations in rebellion. And by Jesus walking on water, he symbolized that he had authority over all nations. So yes, she knew Jesus would walk on water. The next question, Larry, did you know that your baby boy would save our sons and daughters? Well, in Mary's song Back to the Lord the Magnificant, Mary sings these words. His mercy is on them that fear him throughout all generations. And He, remembering his mercy, hath opened his servant Israel, as he promised to our forefathers Abraham and his seed forever. Thus, Mary understood, at least within these words, that we are saved by God's mercy. It is by his mercy that Jesus died in our place, and we are saved by being made Abraham's seed. For we are his offspring by faith, as we have the same faith as Abraham. So yes, Mary knew that Jesus would save us as sons and daughters. The next question. Mary, did you know that your baby boy has come to make you new? This child that you delivered will soon deliver you. The answer? Well, like the previous explanations, making people new and delivering people from sin and death is saving them. So yes, Mary knew. Now, the Roman Catholic and Eastern Orthodox traditions have Mary as sinless and therefore having no need to be saved like the rest of us who have such a need. But since we are Protestant, we won't worry too much about that. The next question, Mary, did you know that your baby boy will give sight to a blind man? The answer? Well, being blind can be both physical and spiritual, and when it is physical, it is symbolic of being spiritually blind. So being given sight is like being saved and delivered. So stated, as stated previous, yes, Mary knew. But even she knew in the physical realm, Mary knew for the handicapped are the meek Of this world. And Mary saying, He hath put down the mighty from their seat and hath exalted the humble and the meek. Exalting the meek includes healing the blind. So, yes, Mary knew. The next question. Mary, did you know that your baby boy will calm the storm with his hand? The answer? Well, walking on water and calming the storm occurred at the same time, and we said that the storm represents raging nations And we already pointed out that Jesus would be the king of a kingdom that would have no end. So yes, Jesus knew he would calm the storm. Or Mary knew, excuse me. And he calms the storms of hearts, does he not? And the lives of sinners. And Mary also saying, he hath showed strength with his arm. So yes, Mary knew he would calm the storm with his hand. Many, many storms, unlimited storms he would calm. The next question. Mary, did you know that your baby boy has walked where angels trod? When you kiss your little baby, you kiss the face of God. The answer She was told by the angel Gabriel that the son she would give birth to was the son of the highest. And that he would be great, and that he would reign forever. And since the divine only has sons that are divine And only God can reign forever. Mary did in fact know that when she kissed the face of her baby, she kissed the face of God. The song then asks in rapid fire, the blind will see, the deaf will hear, the dead will live again. The lame will leap, the dumb will speak, the praises of the Lamb. Mary, did you know? As in, did you know Jesus could do and would do all such miracles? The answers. Well, just as we can say that Mary understood her son giving sight to the blind, so we can conclude that he would give sound to the deaf. Life to the dead, strength to the lame, and voice to the silent. So Mary knew a whole lot more than she has been given credit for. And then there is that one verse in Luke 2 verse 19. But Mary treasured up all these things and pondered them in her heart. She helped us realize that what she was giving birth to was quite profound. even more profound than her words could express. And yet they reveal a great deal to us. And so we have answered the many questions of that song. Mary, did you know? Questions from what the angel told Mary and what Mary praised in, again called the Magnificat. The magnificat is a collage of holy scripture taken from the Old Testament. The words in such praises reveal a woman who was steeped in Holy Scripture. It reveals a woman who had profound understanding to what God's plan of salvation was and how he would go about implementing that plan. Mary's song is called the Magnificat after the first word of the hymn in the Latin translation of the Bible. The song begins with a message of grace, extraordinary grace as it was, that God had shown to her. And she realized and rejoiced that it was a grace to many more than just herself. Her gift was theirs. Her happiness would be theirs. Her salvation would be for the world's salvation. And she seems genuine in her happiness for the blessings of others as well as those of her own. Mary perhaps was the first to understand Christmas. She loved God And loved the people of God. And therefore loved what God was giving to his people She felt deeply about the oppressed circumstances in her own times, and she longed for that day of deliverance. She was, like Simeon later, the old man she would meet in eight days, waiting. She was waiting also for the consolation of Israel. And she could never be really happy if her own circumstances were favorable and those of the Church of God, the people of God, were not. What God was doing, she realized, was helping his servant Israel, his people. That's what made all of this so immensely wonderful and important. And this is a great example for us. I pray you remember this from this day. True humility and godliness is interested in greater things than our own salvation. Than our own salvation. A godly person who has the Holy Spirit is concerned for the kingdom of God in this world. What we have from Mary then is a deep understanding of how revolutionary It was for God to send his one and only Son into the world in the manner that He chose. What Mary knew was that by sending the Savior through the womb of a lowly handmaiden, the world's thinking was being turned upside down. Consider that the world thinks that what the rich have is security and pleasure, and it's what everybody else wants That is why their money is so important to them, and that is why many envy them. They don't have to worry seemingly about their jobs. They don't have to worry about their bills They don't have to worry about whether they can afford medical treatment for themselves or their children. They are even seemingly more beautiful, or they can buy the most expensive clothes and afford plastic surgery. But these secure, pleasurable, and beautiful people, God has sent them empty away. And instead exalted the lowly. Mary, in her poverty and hunger, revels in the greatness of God. And only those who understand what God has done on the day we celebrate, this day, by giving his only son by way of a virgin born and a lowly stable, only those who Know the greatness of God. And that is what we are to focus upon, what we know about the greatness of God because of Christmas Day Please, please, do not hear in this sermon a criticism of the song Mary Did You Know. Mark Lowry, the writer of the song, communicates quite well how profound God becoming man is, and challenges all of us to think upon the great mystery. And wondered of Jesus being God and yet being cradled in his mother's arms. We have heard how Mary knew quite a bit, but not all of it. No one actually can. No one actually can because it is so profound But what Mary knew is what we know, what you and I know. We know that Jesus is the great I am. And thus it is for us to do what Mary did next, to treasure up all of these things and ponder them in our hearts. Let us pray.

sermons.title: New Beginnings
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Have you seated? Because of the secular culture that dominates us, it is good to be reminded that this still is the Christmas season. This is the eighth day of Christmas. as we look forward to Epiphany on January sixth. Julius Caesar And Pope Gregory the Thirteenth are responsible. They are responsible for rose parades. drunken escapades and football all day for each contributed to January 1st being the beginning of a new year Our culture includes January 1st in its holiday greetings, happy holidays, we say, or rather more precisely, happy holy days. But there is nothing holy about this day. There is nothing that is Christian about this day But there is something about marking the beginning of a new year that has Christian faith principles naturally embedded in it. The principle, I'm sure you can guess, is an opportunity for new beginnings The Christian faith is the only faith in the history of mankind. I don't overstate it. In the history of mankind to offer new beginnings every day and every moment of a day. Each time we confess sin, seek forgiveness, we have a new beginning. And each time we commit ourselves to new disciplines, to new ministry, to new study, to new behavior, to new attitudes, we have new beginnings. Regardless of the rightness of the reformers who challenged the Roman Catholic Church in the 16th century Each branch of the Christian church, the Christian Church has flaws when it comes to the doctrine of sanctification. Or, more simply, understanding what it means to live a holy life. Protestants have maligned the Roman Catholics for purposefully sinning Monday through Saturday, only to receive absolution on Sunday, and then begin sinning all over again when Mass is done But Protestant branches in all their various colors have particular sins that they overlook. The Church of the Nazarene, of which I was a part for several years, insisted on its members avoiding sins of the flesh, and thus required the avoidance of movies in general. to avoid lust. No dancing, even between spouses, to avoid lust. No drinking of alcohol or smoking of any kind to avoid being unseemly. But sins such as gluttony and obesity, which are also sins of the flesh, were often ignored. Non-denominational Baptistic churches can also try to avoid those sins of the flesh, just like the Nazarenes try to do. But are then guilty of gossip and slander, even gossip and slander of other Christians, with no apparent awareness of the seriousness of such sins. Reformed Presbyterians can be assured that their doctrine of justification and sanctification are systematic. But the pride that they have because they can win an argument with an Armenian is just as serious as the pride of Adam and his original sin. And those of us who are of the Anglican tradition can be as prideful as the Presbyterians because we believe our reverence of worshiping God liturgically Should be looked to as an example for the rest of the church. And we can be even accused of pursuing our liturgy before pursuing holy lives. The point I'm trying to make is that every Christian from every branch of the Christian church has a need for new beginnings because we have sins to confess. And to turn away from, and we have new commitments for holy living to make and to live up to We want to avoid what Dietrich Bonhoeffer famously described as cheap grace. Which is a grace that doesn't cost us anything. It is a grace that doesn't pursue a holy life. Such is not the grace of Holy Scripture. Instead, as J. I. Packer tartly put it The Bible's prescription for a faithful Christian life is not to let go and let God, but trust God and get going. Therefore, our effort, even our struggle for holy living from new beginnings, is essential to faithful Christian living as the Bible describes it. The author of the Hebrews, as was read this morning, says that we are called to resist the sins that so easily beset us. That we are to be admonished and exhorted simply to try harder to overcome these sins. These have been called besetting sins, which are sins we are personally prone to commit. Thomas the Tempest in his classic and important devotional titled The Imitation of Christ. Talks about the struggle that so many Christians have with habits that are simple Of course, we're not talking about heinous sins such as living the life as a thief or an adulterer or any of the other top ten. What Thomas Ecampus means is that the struggle for sanctification is often so difficult, and the victories that we achieve over besetting sins seem to be so few and far between. That even in the lives of the greatest saints, there were few who were able to overcome habitual sinful patterns. Each of us, each of us have life experiences that will tell us the same But Christians are called to stay in the fight. And that means to stay in the pursuit of holy living. And that means to experience new beginnings. So, what will you consecrate on in the days and months of this new year? What new beginnings? Do you need this month, this year? Well, a most obvious place to start for new beginnings May be for a greater and more disciplined commitment to reading the Bible, to reading God's Word. From Psalm 119, verse 9, how can a young man keep his ways pure by living according to your word? Is the answer. But how will a young man or an old man, a young girl or an old woman, keep pure if he or she does not know the word of God? If the Word of God is not a living voice in his or her heart, how will they hear God and know his way? The Word of God, which is, after all, the voice of God, is a wonderful power in the Christian life if it gets a chance to do its work. It is not the Word of God lying unremembered on the pages of your Bible. But the Word of God living in your heart that changes your life, that awakens your conscience, and keeps it awake. That enlivens your holy desires, that makes you wise in the choices you make. And keeps the Lord front and center in all that you think and in all that you do. To begin anew in relation to the Bible, a person needs to repent. Repent for not having read and faithfully digested the Word of God After confession is made and forgiveness received, disciplines need to be established in everyday living. There should be a regular time in an average day when the word of God is attentively read and listened to. The advances in technology should be to the advantage of the Christian who pursues a holy life. The Bible can be accessed in many different mediums at all times during the day. And we should be accessing it when possible. I will add to the importance of the Word of God a personal testimony of how much knowing God's Word has shaped my life. And I realized, I realized that I preach for a living, and thus the importance of the Word of God might sound obvious coming from me. But a layman has just as many usages of the Bible as any preacher does. And the more you know God's Word. The more you know God's Word, the easier it is to make wise decisions, to think healthier about the world. To be able to discern the spirits of the age, to see God and the moving of the Holy Spirit in everyday life. There is truly nothing that can replace knowing the Bible. Consider this. The power of the Word of God with just three words. In the summer of 1940, more than 350,000 soldiers, most of them British, were trapped at Dunkirk. The German forces were on their way, and they had the capacity to wipe out the British expeditionary force. When it seemed certain that the Allied forces at Dunkirk would be massacred, a British naval officer cabled back three words to London. But if not. The three words were a reference to the faith of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. In the book of Daniel. In Daniel, the young men were given the choice. They could bow to the pagan idol or be thrown into the fiery furnace. They courageously chose to face the furnace rather than disobey the commandments of God. And this was their testimony, you recall, in Daniel. They said, Our God, whom we serve, is able to deliver us from the fiery furnace, and he will deliver us out of thy hand, O King. But if not, let it be known unto thee, O King, that we will not serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image that thou hast set up. Knowing God's word makes just three words come alive to the power of helping men face seemingly certain death. Knowing God's word gives eternal life Another area of new beginnings that we will all likely need greater, more disciplined commitment to is to pray. You pray, you pray, to be sure you do. You pray before meals, you pray in church, you pray now and then But prayer, earnest and familiar talking with God as defined, as defining prayer. Is not the lifeblood of your daily life, as you know it well ought to be. Ought to be for any serious Christian, for any man or woman who intends to live by faith. And the first step to improve your prayer life is to confess to God how short you have fallen in praying as you ought. All of us need to confess when we have fallen short of praying as we should And husbands and fathers especially should repent for not leading your wife and children in prayer on a regular basis. Pray without ceasing, Paul exhorts us. But for many of us, those words are more of a rebuke than they are an encouragement. Alexander White was only speaking the truth when he said that there is nothing we are so bad at all of our days as prayer. The Lord Jesus, you know, was a man of prayer. And he had no need to pray for the things that usually take up our prayers. He also taught us to pray and urged us to pray. And surely he knows what is best for us. Whatever effort faithful prayer requires of us, it must be worth it, altogether worth it To help your prayer life, you can read some good books of prayer this year. Alexander White's Lord, Teach Us to Pray. C. S. Lewis's Letters to Malcolm These are all reasonable books to read and to encourage you to pray each day, to pray. Pray for the things you know you ought to pray for. Pray for the things you know you need to say to God. We have been wonderfully gifted with a prayer book that gives us words to pray when we lack the words or when we are just too shy to pray. You can pray the prayers of the morning prayer or from the family prayer section. And then such prayers can lead you to pray extemporaneously, so that your heart is free to tell the Lord what you need and how you feel. The point is to pray. And because we have been given the gift of historical and reverent worship in the Book of Common Prayer We may be entrapped to conclude that prayer must be formal and must be of a certain posture, etc. But if we are to do as St. Paul instructs and pray without ceasing, we must understand and practice prayer as regularly and continuous in conversation with God. I lost my wallet last weekend. That's not new for me to do. But I searched high and low and I retraced my steps going from place to place asking managers if they had recovered a lost wallet. Embarrassingly, I admit that I never asked Jesus. That's right, the preacher never asked Jesus. When I realized I was depending on my own strength, I confessed my sin to the Lord. My wife will attest to this. I confessed my sin, received his mercy, and I asked him to help me Within an hour, my wallet was found. I had a new beginning. God made me a new man. Through prayer, through confession. God gave me a new beginning and He gave me back my wallets. New beginnings regarding the study of the Bible And a regular prayer life are always possible and something most everyone needs But we must address more particular needs for new beginnings if this sermon is going to have any lasting meaning or make any lasting difference. There is likely among us the need for new beginnings when it comes to sins of the flesh. Especially sins of the flesh as lust. And the first lust that we think about is sexual lust. Some men, mostly young men, struggle to avoid lusting after women. Confessing a weakness for wanting sexual pleasure over wanting to please God is required. New beginnings are always available when such confession is made. Jesus forgives sins of the flesh. But added to such new beginnings should be a determination to be more disciplined when it comes to avoiding opportunities to lust. The book of Proverbs warns young men not to venture down the path that leads to the doorstep of a harlot. A modern application is not venturing down a website or a television series that exists for the sole purpose of exalting sexual lust. Overcoming besetting sins has to include wisdom that helps us be led away from temptation. And since we are on the subject of lust, we are not to ignore the besetting sin of the lust for food. We hear often that gluttony is a problem in the United States, but is it not also a problem among Christians who eat too much or too much of the wrong foods? and thus use food as a coping mechanism as opposed to being empowered by the Holy Spirit New beginnings are needed and are available to any of us who say no to the desire to overeat or eat what is wrong for us. Another need for new beginnings is likely in the category of relationships. The standard of God's love is put before us so very high that we can always confess that we fall short. Remember that definition of love that is given to us by St. Paul. Love is patient, love is kind It doesn't envy, it doesn't boast, it's not proud, it does not dishonor others, it is not self-seeking, it is not easily angered, it keeps no record of wrong. Love does not delight in evil, but rejoices in the truth, always protects, always trusts, always hopes, always perseveres. Now take away all those fringe relationships you have and focus on the people that you love the most that you're closest to and measure your life against that definition. How are you loving them? Have you been patient with them? Have you always been kind? Have you been too proud and put yourself first before them? Have you kept record of wrong? Have you always protected, always trusted, always persevered for them? But the answer is no, in part or in the whole, there is a need for new beginnings. You are in need to confess your sins and in need to receive the forgiveness Jesus offers and commit yourself to love as He has prescribed and described. And then you take away all those people who are closest to you and look at the fringe people in your life. Do you love them as well? As you ought. Another opportunity for new beginnings. As a pastor for over 20 years now, I have experienced the greatest need in the Christian life In relationships with one another is the need to forgive. I say it is a need for Christians because We know that when we withhold forgiveness, we're doing damage psychologically to ourselves, emotionally, to ourselves. But for Christians, the standard is even higher. For we will be judged as we judge others. We will be forgiven in the same manner that we forgive others. Such a warning should be shot across our bow. No sin done to us is bad enough that we should prevent our own forgiveness. I hope you heard that. What are the other needs among us that cry out for an opportunity for new beginnings? I have mentioned common besetting sins, but I may not have touched on yours. There is the love of money, the love of fame. The sin of general pride, all these need confessing, repentance, and new beginnings. There is the sin of envy and then sloth. And greed and overall hate. They need to be confessed, for they are displeasing to God. They are in need of the blood of Jesus to cleanse. The point is that new beginnings are available to the Christian no matter the sin, no matter how long a person has known Christ Jesus. I close with this example of a hero of mine of sorts, John Wesley. John Wesley grew up in the home of an Anglican priest and was trained to be a priest himself even as a young child. He studied theology at Oxford. He went to the newly discovered Americas as a missionary. He also lived a disciplined life that by any standard of any age would be considered holy. And in spite of these realities, he was always in need of new beginnings. Wesley himself tells of a new beginning in the narrative insert regarding his experience at Aldersgate in May of 1738. He describes the turmoil and breakthrough that he underwent that month. In the days immediately prior to May 24th, he says his spirit was marked by, quote, strange indifference. Dullness, a coldness toward God, an unusual frequent relapses into sin, his confession And following this Frank confession, Wesley quickly contrasts that state of existence to what happened to him on May 24, 1738. He says this In the evening I went very unwillingly to a society in Aldersgate Street, where one was reading Luther's preface to the Epistle to the Romans. About a quarter before nine, while he was describing the change which God works in the heart through faith in Christ, I felt my heart strangely warmed. I felt I did trust in Christ, Christ alone for salvation, and an assurance was given to me that He has taken away my sins. Even mine, and save me from the law of sin and death. Leslie's life prior to this experience, if it were yours or my life, we would consider ourselves in good standing with God. But the prompting of the Holy Spirit and the accepting of the Christian call for new beginnings, Wesley heard He became obedient and received the forgiveness he needed that day. Today, as every day does on this calendar Provides new beginnings. Let us then have them. Amen and Amen. Let us pray.

sermons.title: Sojourners of the Dispersion
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Leave me seated. As our second reading indicated Today we start a series of sermons from 1 Peter. If you wonder why we are hearing from 1 Peter. The honest answer is that we finished our study of Exodus, and I wanted to study a book of the New Testament. I've never preached to you from 1 Peter, so here we go. First I remind you of the personality of Peter.
