God is calling men to preach as he does in every generation. The question for us is, who is listening? Who thinks the call is worthy to be pursued? Can a man who thinks he is to be a businessman, to be a coach, to be a doctor? Can he be interrupted? Can a call to wear a collar be worth more than a piece of paper? The field is still ripe for harvest, and the laborers are still few. And if men don't start heeding the call, then we've got to leave it up to George. He's not going to do a very good job. Let us pray.

sermons.title: The Virtue of Humility
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. I apologize, it sounds like Carol Channing is preaching to you this morning. But I have been truly blessed and I want to give the Lord praise. I literally lost my voice Earlier this week could not speak much at all. And God has by his grace brought it back. I was concerned. Molly had suggested it to us That perhaps we had a Zechariah and Elizabeth thing going on, that would mean I have an announcement for you that Bobby Lynn is pregnant. She's not I'm very grateful for healing. I said for healing. Grateful for healing. We are in 1 Peter chapter 5. We are ending our study of 1 Peter here on Palm Sunday. St. Peter closes his instruction on leadership in the church with the instruction to young people in general, upholding the virtue of humility. Saint Augustine said, Do you wish to rise? Begin by descending You plan a tower that will pierce the clouds, lay first the foundation of humility. Humility is essential to godliness. Humility is a foundation of righteousness. Humility is essential to godliness and righteousness because both come from faith in Jesus. As humility is required to confess sins and to accept the forgiveness that Jesus offers. Sins cannot be forgiven. Mistakes cannot be learned from without humility. Chuck Daly, a former NBA coach, now deceased said the following about a form of humility. It's discouraging to make a mistake, but it's humiliating when you find out you're so unimportant that nobody notices it. And some of us need to be humiliated from time to time. Humility allows us to see ourselves as we truly are. Comedian Phyllis Diller said of humility, you know what keeps me humble? Mirrors What would be the most humbling of revelations is for there to be held up before us a mirror that would reflect our hearts. The mixed motives within our hearts for practically everything we do would bring a great deal of humility to our consciences. Of course, the opposite of humility is pride. Thus we need, we need Warnings against pride. We can presume that St. Peter's instruction for the people of God to uphold the virtue of humility is important. Because the sin of pride is so very, very harmful. The great Baptist preacher Charles Spurgeon said Quote, there is nothing into which the heart of man so easily falls as pride. And yet there is no vice which is more frequently, more emphatically, and more eloquently condemned in Scripture. The scourge of human pride has been condemned by the law, by the prophets, by the apostles. Evangelists, through strident preaching, condemning personal pride, have filled altar calls with people whose consciences have been seared. We might say that God Himself spoke most excellently through the prophets when he condemned the sin of the pride of humanity. An example of this is found in the words of the prophet Isaiah, chapter 14, where the Lord's holy words Seem to have risen up as if he is turning over the tables of the money changers, as his anger is waxed hot against the pride of man. When he would utterly and affectionately condemn the most prideful of men. He says concerning the great mighty king of Babylon, quote, Hell from beneath is excited about you to meet you at your coming. It stirs up from the dead. All the chief ones of the earth, it is raised up from their thrones, all the kings of the nations, they all speak and say to you, Have you also become as weak as we? Have you become like us? Your pomp is brought down to Shaol. And the sound of your stringed instruments, the maggot is spread under you, and worms cover you. How you are fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, Son of the Morning! How you are cut down to the ground, you are weakened, you who weaken the nations. For you have said in your heart, I will ascend into heaven. I will exalt my throne above the stars of God. I will also sit on the mount of the congregation On the farthest sides of the north. I will ascend above the heights of the clouds. I will be like the Most High. Yet you shall be brought down to Sha'ol, to the deepest depths of the pit. Those who see you will gaze at you and consider you saying, is this the man who made the earth tremble, who shook kingdoms, who made the world as a wilderness, and destroyed its cities? Who did open the house of all prisoners from such a poetic proclamation of justice? We can see The pride of man from God's vantage point. A very foolish aspect of pride. is mankind's inability to see himself in his pride. For if he could, he might be less apt to think of himself in any manner that would bring Praise to self. God so eloquently speaks against the sin of pride Especially the pride of kings who make themselves to be like God, because of how audacious And truly silly it is for any human being to place himself on a level that would be remotely equal to God Before the destruction, the heart of man is haughty. So says Proverbs Consider where the seat of pride is, where it resides. It is in the heart of man. And what is the consequence of pride? Destruction and nothing less. Pride is the firstborn son of hell. It is like a parent of all that is unclean and vile. And the great irony is that pride is a groundless thing. It places a man's footing on seeking sand, on shifting bars, on bubbles that burst. And again, what sense is there for personal pride? Our frailty should be sufficient to bring us loath and to keep us loath. For we are but dust, we are but vapor, and thus we shall be gone tomorrow Jesus tells us that no person can add even a single hour to his or her life. And yet we try, various fads, to do that very thing he tells us we cannot do. And consider what we owe. What each man and woman owes to God. We are debtors because we are trespassers. We are sinners. And we have nothing of our own for which we can pay our debt. We are beggars, we are paupers before God and before our fellow man. And here is another great irony with pride. The more you have it The more you are in debt to God. Again, pride is a brainless thing As well as a groundless thing, for it brings no profit with it. You gain nothing. There is no wisdom in self-exaltation. Consider that other vices have some excuse, for men seem to gain something in the immediate by them, such as lust and pleasures enjoyed in the moment. But the man who is proud sells his soul cheaply. And it is the soul, the very essence of a person that is cheapened by pride. Human pride is at the heart of the devil's deception. It is at the heart of the devil's nature. And therefore, whoever bows to pride is a disciple of the evil one. But what of humility? Humility is a grace that has many promises of reward given to it in Scripture. We are aware that there are but three virtues that remain faith, hope, and love. But humility is no less than that trio, for it is required in order for us to receive the three that remain. We need humility to have faith, to trust in that which we cannot see. We need humility to hold on to hope, for hope is admitting that we cannot control the future. And we need humility for receiving love. For we are most unlovable in and of ourselves. And yet humility allows us to love because God first loved us. Every grace seems to be like a nail on which precious blessings hang. And humility hath many a mercy suspended from it. Hear these proclamations from Holy Scripture. He that exalts himself shall be humbled, and he that humbles himself shall be exalted. Blessed are the poor in spirit. God hates the proud, but gives grace to the humble. God brings down the mighty from their seats and exalts the humble and the meek. Consider the men most praised in the Bible, praised by God Himself, are men who were the most humble. Moses and Jesus were both praised by God to be the most humble Moses was said by God to be the most humble man on earth. And Jesus was even greater than Moses in all ways, including his humility. From the lives of Moses and Jesus, we see that men who are closest to the Heavenly Father were and are men who were and are the most humble. A person then who truly knows God knows humility. As we look more closely at St. Peter's description of humility, we can receive practical examples of what humility within the Christian life looks like. Look with me at verse five. In the New King James it begins by including submissiveness. We are to be submissive to those God has called to be our presbyters, our priests, our bishops Such submission is not so difficult when we respect and like our pastor or bishop. It is much much harder when we do not. And yet a humble person is able to submit to his or her elders not because of the person in the office. But because of the office itself and the truth that the person in the office was chosen by God Humility identifies the order of God's authority with the appreciation. That all leaders have been chosen by God, and each leader we submit to, submit to by faith. For we trust that God will care for us even under a foolish leader. Saint Peter did this very thing, suffering under the leadership of the Roman Emperor Nero, suffering even to the point of his martyrdom But submitting under the leadership of the church is arguably more difficult than submitting to political authority. For if you do not submit to political authority, you can be punished. Punished in ways that could harm you even unto death. And thus you have immediate motivation to submit. On the other hand, if you do not submit to church authorities, well what recourse do they have, really have in your life? The church authorities could refuse Holy Communion. We call it excommunication. The church can treat you like an unbeliever that needs to repent and to publicly confess your sins and a true faith. But what is that to a parishioner who can drive one or two blocks down the road, enter into a church that call themselves Christians And be given holy communion, full membership, and a listening ear when you tell them how terrible the people are down Liberty Road. During the culmination service, that which is read during Ash Wednesday, we hear these words. In the primitive church, there was a godly discipline that at the beginning of Lent, such persons as stood convicted of notorious sin were put to open penance. and punished in this world, that their souls might be saved in the last day, and that others admonished by their example might be the more afraid to offend. Instead, whereof until the said discipline may be restored again, which is to be wished, and it goes on. And that last part used to catch me. I wondered why excommunication, such as practiced in local churches, why doesn't that count? Why are they still wishing for this? And then it struck me, what they're really wishing for is that an excommunication would be honored by all the churches. And honored by all that confessed Jesus, so that a sinner could not go down the road into another church. So that people would in fact fear God And take warning and take heed and turn from their sin. For the people of God to submit, as Saint Peter instructs, there needs to be a receiving of the instructions the Holy Spirit impressed upon the second generation Christians who lived after the apostles to submit to their church officers. From Saint Ignatius to the Ephesian Church, he wrote this, second generation It is proper, therefore, in every way to glorify Jesus Christ, who has glorified you, so that you, joined together in a united obedience and subject to the bishop and presbytery, may be sanctified in every respect. Again, from Saint Ignatius, he says, the one who honors the bishop has been honored by God. And the one who does anything without the bishop's knowledge serves the devil. And what would cause someone to work without the knowledge of the bishop? But pride, submission to church leadership is humility before God. And then next, St. Peter includes his instruction to submit to one another. Humility is to submit to one another. Now St. Paul says the same, even before he says, wives submit to your husbands, first he says, submit one to another. Submission then is foundational in our relationships with one another. It is living the instruction. Treat others as more important than yourself. Submitting to one another is assuring that your brother or sister in Jesus Christ are before you in that line at the buffet and are after you in that line for volunteering for work. Submitting to one another is bearing up the burdens of your fellow Christians, so that they do not carry such a load and cares and trials so much That they are overwhelmed and cannot move forward. Submitting to one another says to a fellow Christian, I got this. Let me help you with that. Submitting to one another says to a fellow Christians, your needs first, your wants first. Your feelings first. Submitting to one another is faith lived out For it is saying as a testimony that when the needs of others are placed before your own, you may get the short stick. But that is acceptable in this life. Because God will exalt you in due time. Consider that your fellow man who has no faith in God gets quite upset rather quickly when his needs are not met. And he gets especially upset when his needs are not met and someone else's are being met He gets upset because he has no concept of there being a reality beyond what is immediate. He gets upset because he has no hope for a reward that is ahead of him that is eternal But the Christian does. The Christian has the motivation to remain humble and thus He gives deference, the Christian does, to his fellow Christian, because well God is against the proud He resists them after all. And because by God's grace, he will reward those who are humble in heaven, clothing them with righteousness when they clothe themselves with humility. Beloved, what more do we need in order to be convinced to choose humility over pride? We have heard great warnings against human pride. We have heard great promises for living humble lives. There is no more that we need other than maybe a story. There once was a parish. A parish that had a submission problem. Their problem was that they submitted to one another too much. When sharing a pot muck dinner, no one would get up to eat because each was waiting for the other to go first. When participating in a work day on church property. No one hardly worked because so many people showed up. The work took little time to complete When giving tithes and offerings, the vestry became flustered because the monies received doubled each year, and they were running out of ways to spend it. When it came to bearing one another's burdens, there were ladies who didn't get a call to make meals for those in need because the list was so long for volunteers, and meals were made and delivered before anybody asked. In fact, this parish was so submissive, so submissive, that the prayer requests made were actually prayed for instead of reasons for gossip. Now that's submission. And how did this happen? How did this parish become an example of submission? Here's the answer. They heard and read that Saint Peter instructed for Christians to submit to one another, being clothed with humility. And they did it. Let us pray. Our Father, we thank you for a message that is so important on a day like this, to understand your zeal. For the downing of pride and the raising up of humility, for that is what you did. And Father, we are grateful for the challenge in our lives May we heed the words of St. Peter and be excited about what you will do lifting us up. In Jesus' name we pray. Amen.

sermons.title: A Day for Laughter
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. Wonderful to hear that trumpet played, amen. This is an Isaac day. This is a day for Isaac. It is an Isaac day because Isaac means laughter. For Christians, Resurrection Day is a day of laughter When we named our thirdborn Isaac, we did not know how appropriate a name it would be for him. He has told us that he has learned that his name communicates one of three things to people When people find out his name is Isaac, they are first surprised that he is not African American and he is not a bartender on the love boat. That's a reference. We're a different generation. Next they assume he is either Jewish or homeschooled Or apparently there is no other category for a white person named Isaac than to be Jewish or homeschooled. But we are glad we named our third son Isaac because of his laugh His laugh is hearty and it is contagious. When he laughs, you need to laugh with him because his laugh overtakes his body and the volume overtakes the rooms. And so he is living up to his name. But laughter is not always contagious, for it can be quite awkward when we do not know whether to laugh during an uncomfortable social moment. or how to interpret certain types of laughter. In the classic American film Goodfellas There is a scene that depicts how socially awkward laughing can be. You didn't know you'd come to Easter Sunday service and hear good fellas. But here we are. The characters are at a bar. They have women hanging on them. They are buzzed with alcohol And Tommy DeVito, the loose cannon played by Joe Pesci, makes a joke. And Henry Hill, played by Ray Leota, says to Tommy, you're a pistol. You're really funny. You're really funny. And Tommy stops laughing and says, what do you mean, I'm funny? And Harry says, it's funny. You know, it's a good story. It's funny. You're a funny guy. And he laughs. Tommy, what do you mean? You mean the way I talk? What? Henry says, it's just, you know, you're just funny. It's funny. You know, the way that you tell the story and everything. Tommy, it's quiet now in the bar. Funny how? What's funny about Anthony, another character, tries to break the tension. Tommy, you you got it all wrong. Tommy says, oh, oh, Anthony? But he's a big boy. He knows what he said. What did you say? Funny out. Henry, well just what? Just, you know, you're funny. You mean let me understand this because yeah, you know, maybe it's me. It's a little messed up. I'm a little messed up, maybe But it I'm funny how? I mean funny like I'm a clown? I amuse you I make you laugh I'm here to amuse you what do you mean funny funny how how am I funny And Henry, well just you know how you tell a story. What? And Tommy, no, no, I don't know. You said it. How do I know? You said I'm funny How the am I funny? What is so funny about me? Tell me what's funny. Henry, after a long pause. Get out of here, Tommy. And the tension finally breaks, and everyone laughs, even Tommy What was funny in the beginning all of a sudden wasn't funny. And when everyone laughed again, it was for a much different reason than before. Now let us go back to that name, Isaac. When God chose the name for Abraham and Sarah's first offspring, he also changed the name of Abraham and Sarah. who were previously, as you know, named Abram and Sarai. By changing their names, God was putting himself into his chosen covenant family. He was putting his name, Yah. He was putting his name Yah in their names. And so it was Sarya and Abra-Yah. And Abraham's name came to mean father of many nations, and Sarah's name came to mean princess, which was fitting for the son she was to give birth to. In Genesis 17, God informs Abraham that his prayers had been heard and they would be answered as God would give he and Sarah a son. And when Abraham heard the news, he laughed. He fell on his face and he laughed. But Abraham did not laugh to express disbelief. He did not laugh to mock. He laughed instead out of joy and out of trust. He laughed with amazement that God would make an irony out of his life by bringing forth a covenant son to be born to a man who was 99 and his wife 90 years of age. Abraham's laugh was out of wonder and awe that God would choose at the time of the life he was in to give him a son. that would be used to bring forth a nation, a nation so large that it could not be numbered. And God knew the heart of Abraham. He knew that Abraham's laugh was a laugh of faith. And so he responded to Abraham laughing by confirming to Abraham that Sarah would indeed bear him a son. And next God instructs Abraham to call their son Laughter. Isaac, as a symbol that God had brought wonder and joy to Abraham and to Sarah. There is, however, another side of that story. The name given to the firstborn, Sarah, did not hear the news. She was not there with Abraham when he first heard that they would bring forth a son. And so Sarah heard later. In fact, the account of God's promise being fulfilled came to Sarah by one of the three men who came to speak to Abraham about Sodom and Gomorrah. Sarah overheard. And when she overheard them talking, confirming the promise of the Son coming to be born to Abraham and Sarah, Sarah laughed. We read in Genesis 18. Now Sarah was listening at the entrance to the tent, which was behind him, behind Abraham. Abraham and Sarah were already very old. Sarah was past the age of childbearing. So Sarah laughed to herself, as she thought, After I am worn out, and my lord is old, will I now have this pleasure? Then the Lord said to Abraham, Why did Sarah laugh and say, Will I really have a child now that I am old? And then the Lord said, Is anything too hard for the Lord? I will return to you at the appointed time next year, and Sarah will have a son. Sarah was afraid, so she lied and said, I did not laugh. But the messenger said, Yes, you did laugh. That's an awkward moment. That's an awkward scene described. To me, the visitor might have well said, Am I a clown? Do I amuse you? The narrative ends abruptly because awkward moments end with uncomfortable silence. The moment was awkward and clumsy because Sarah's was a not a laughter of wonder, not a laughter of joy, but a laughter of faithless scoffing. It is most obvious how different her laughter was from that of Abraham because of the response of the Lord as he asked the rhetorical question through one of the three men. The question we heard, is there anything too hard for the Lord? And then when Sarah was confronted by the visitor about her laughter, she gives it away. That she was laughing in the form of scoffing when she denied that she had laughed. She denied it because she knew where her heart was in her laughter. Today, Christians make a dramatic claim. Claim that it's much more miraculous than a woman of 90 years giving birth to a firstborn son. And the claim Christians make, particularly on this day, garners the laughter of wonder and joy or the laughter of faithless scoffing. Laughter as faithless scoffing likely began when Mary tried to explain to others how she became pregnant without ever knowing a man. We are not privy to those conversations, but the one we are privy to are the Pharisees laughing at Jesus. Laughing when he said, for the temple to be torn down and that he would rebuild it in three days. Their mocking laughter was from the absurdity that Jesus spoke That he have some way have the power to tear down such a great temple. But that absurdity was a metaphor. For what was directly in front of them. It was Jesus who was the temple that would be destroyed and raised in three days, and that would not be funny to them And we know that Jesus was laughed at when people shamed him and spit on him, blindfolded him, hit him, telling him to prophesy regarding who hit him. And then they hung him on a tree and laughingly told him to come down. Even the chief priest laughed at him with a scoff, saying that he saved others and he can't even save himself. And of course, the sign placed above his head, reading King of the Jews, that was both a mocking laugh at Jesus and the entire Jewish people. Who laughed until they didn't like being laughed at. When St. Paul explains to the Christians at Koroth the uniqueness of the gospel, He prepares them for the disdain that they will receive from Jews and Gentiles alike, saying that Jesus as the Savior, being crucified dead and buried, and being raised from the dead would be a stumbling block to the Jews and foolishness to the Greeks. The word foolishness, the word foolishness means that people would find the gospel story something to laugh at. It would be something seen as folly. Something to laugh at because of it being preposterous. On such a line of thinking, I would guess, would have passed away with the first century, and that I suspected that arguments against the gospel, against the resurrection of Jesus Would have become more sophisticated and thoughtful, more than merely labeling it preposterous, laughing at it in scorn, and then moving along. But I ran across an article titled Argument Against the Resurrection of Jesus. And it was written in 2011. The main premise in the argument for Jesus not being raised from the dead, if he did indeed physically die, is that it is physically impossible to be raised from the dead after three days. In summary, Jesus is not alive because it's impossible In other words, it is preposterous. To say he is alive is foolishness and does something to laugh at, just as it was in the first century. From my studies in philosophy, I conclude that the modern primary source of doubt regarding the resurrection of Jesus And of any miracles occurring at any time, and in particular regarding miracles described in the Bible, the primary source of doubt is David Hume Hume became a dominant source in the field of philosophy because of his denial of the ability to prove causality. It's bore some of you, but let me get through this. Hume argued that one event that seemingly seemingly caused another event That the cause itself cannot be proven because cause cannot be experienced. Cause cannot be experienced. What you experience is the result of an action, but not the cause itself. And so because you did not experience the cause itself with your senses, You cannot for certain say that one thing caused another thing to happen. And this challenge to the theory of causality made Hume a hero with atheists They wanted to reject the claims of Holy Scripture, and Hume gave them an argument. A claim. A claim to reject all miracles. Now listen to Hume himself. He said, quote, Upon the whole, we may conclude that the Christian religion not only was at first attended with miracles, but But even at this day cannot be believed by any reasonable person without one. Mere reason is insufficient to convince us of its ferocity And whoever is moved by faith to assent to it is conscious of his continued miracle in his own person. which subverts all the principles of his understanding and gives him determination to believe what is most contrary to custom and experience Catch that? Allow me to summarize. Christianity cannot be believed because it is based on miracles. Miracles cannot be believed because they cannot be proven by reason, nor can they be understood by custom or experience. So if miracles are not true, neither is Christianity. In summary of the summary, the resurrection of Jesus did not occur because it is impossible. It is preposterous. It is foolishness, and thus it is something to laugh at. David Hume's argument has withstood the test of time, as it is still accepted as the standard regarding the reason why philosophers reject Christianity. And yet it may surprise some when they hear that Christians, for the most part, do not have a problem with Hume's logic. It is true that causes cannot be experienced, but they are rationally presumed. Miracles such as the resurrection of Jesus from the dead, having been in the grave three days, is indeed impossible. But it is the meaning of the word impossible and the meaning of the word miracle that Christians understand differently than those who do not believe. When the word impossible is used, it must always refer to humanity and never refer to God. For as the messenger to Sarah stated, nothing is too hard for God. And next is the definition of miracle. From the Greek language, the word miracle refers to a supernatural work of wonder. A supernatural work of wonder. What is supernatural is that which goes beyond nature. Thus it goes beyond our senses. What is a wonder is that which extends beyond our experiences Thus we must say that a miracle, by definition, is an event that for mankind is impossible. And we can re reverse the logic to say that it would not be a miracle unless it was impossible for man. It is a miracle because it is impossible. And such is the Christian answer to the objections of the Greeks, to Hume, and any unbeliever, past or present, that denies the resurrection of Jesus. It is indeed impossible that a man can die and lie in the grave for three days and rise alive and live forever. That's impossible. And because it is impossible, and because it did happen, we believe We believe Jesus to be the Son of God. Because what he did is impossible. And Hume has become a hero of skepticism, as skeptics love to doubt everything, disbelieving anything they themselves have not experienced. And we should feel sorry for such people, for they have no wonder in their lives. They do not know what laughter out of wonder and joy feels like. But that doesn't mean hope is lost for the skeptic. After all, it was not lost for Sarah. Laughter and wonder and joy was heard on Sarah's lips when she gave birth to Isaac, and she said the following. God has made me to laugh. Everyone that hears shall laugh with me, for I have borne Abraham a son in his old age. God thus turned Sarah's laughter of mocking and scorn to laughter of wonder and joy, and he can do the same for anyone who calls upon him. And what better day to call upon him than the day we celebrate Jesus being risen, risen indeed. And so, why do you laugh today? What is at the heart of your laughter? The Lord says to each of us, why did you laugh? And we might say to that question, I laughed because Jesus was dead and now he is alive, alive forevermore. I laugh because my heart is filled with both wonder and joy. Wonder because my senses and my heart have been opened to a reality that overcomes sin and death And joy. Joy because my sin is forgiven and my soul is set free. I laugh and it is wonderful. Let us pray.

sermons.title: Bondservants love
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. You be seated. It will be much to your benefit to have your Bible open and follow along with me from 2 Peter chapter 1. Finishing first Peter now going on into second Peter. Saint Peter opens his second letter by referring to himself as a bond servant. I would like you to ask yourself if you can refer to yourself as a bondservant of Jesus Christ. A bondservant is a slave. A slave does the bidding of his master. Do you do the bidding of Jesus Christ? And I don't want you to quickly answer that question by saying to yourself that you believe in Jesus. That's too easy of an answer. Yes, I believe in Jesus. Well, good for you. But are you a bondservant of Jesus? You do his bidding whenever and whatever he bids you to do. In order to answer such a question, each of us has to be introspective. We have to be able to examine ourselves. And in order to be introspective, we have to have some sort of self-awareness. And self-awareness is not easy to come by. Not many have it. Oh, we may have it in certain places in our lives, but not in others. And it is where we don't have self-awareness that others become distracted by what we are not aware of. All of us have been in the presence of a person who has food on his face. Such a person carries on a conversation that may or may not be interesting. No one would know because of that crumb of food on his face. And it distracts anything else he's trying to say. But he is unaware of that crumb, and so he keeps talking as if there's nothing at all distracting from what he is saying And the same is true when there is a character flaw that everyone else is aware of except the person doing the talking. The flaw distracts. The philosopher Aristotle, in his work on rhetoric, made the point from natural law that a person For him to be an effective speaker, he needs to have an ethos, which is a character that is consistent with what he is speaking about. For example, if I was to speak about the dangers of gossip, and I myself was a serial gossiper, the flaw in my character would distract. from what I was speaking about and would require for me to wipe off that crumb of gossip I have on my face before anyone else would bother to know what I have to say on the topic. Well, the same can be said proclaiming you are a bondservant of Jesus Christ. If you are not loving your wife as Jesus loves the church, if you are not submitting to your husband as Sarah did, calling him Lord. If you are not obeying the Sabbath by regularly attending church, if you are not training your children in the Lord, if you are not loving to your neighbor, if you are not caring for the poor and widowed, you have something on your face. Bondservants of Jesus do such things and much, much more. And when we don't and claim ourselves to be bondservants, we have something on our face. Peter could say he was a bondservant as his life was completely dedicated to serving Jesus, as the end of his days showed. You remember being crucified upside down, he would not deny Jesus again, and he did not feel he was worthy to be even martyred the way Jesus died So the bondservant of Jesus, Peter, writes to Christians a final time, describing them as having obtained a precious faith. That's what he tells us. We've obtained a precious faith by means of the righteousness of God who was revealed in Jesus the Messiah. He then tells them that God has given them everything that is needed to live a life of godliness, which is a life like Jesus. A life that God has called all who believe in him to follow, because we're all to be bondservants. By God's glory and his virtue, his holiness, which was displayed in the person and accomplishments of Jesus of Nazareth, we are called to be God's people and live as God's people. And as God's people we have been given precious promises, which include being partakers of the divine nature. Did you catch that phrase? We are partakers of the divine nature of God Himself. We, having that nature, have escaped the corruption of the world. The corruption through the lust of the world. Corruption in the world through lust includes any vice that rules over us instead of being ruled by us. It includes any desire that is served by us as opposed to serving us. The latter is what the world perceives, and it is under the curse of the devil. The world says that every desire that we have is who we are. And that it is perfectly acceptable, even desirable, that we obey our every lust. This is why some people identify themselves by the lust they fulfill And this is a great deception of the evil one. Mark it as such that people identify themselves according to their sexual desires. I hope you consider how ridiculous that is. We don't do that with any other desire. People don't introduce themselves saying, hi, my name's Eric. I am a liker of Snickers bars. Or hi, my name is Eric, I desire pepperoni pizza. How ridiculous it would be to try to get people to know you by what you desire! And yet it is expected that a lesbian, a gay, a bisexual person lead with such a title as if that is who they are, and not simply what they prefer or desire. All lusts are possible identities if only we allow them to be Those without the Holy Spirit dwelling in them feel as though they cannot control themselves, as if their lusts are their masters, and therefore they cannot be condemned for obeying their masters. But Christians are not of this world. We are partakers of the divine nature, which is the same as saying the Holy Spirit dwells in us. God dwells in us, and thus we have the authority to say no to our ungodly lusts. And let us look at the other side for a moment, not being confused by the devil, when he makes us feel guilty for our lusts. For example, men and women desire sexual expression. And God said that such is good He merely puts protection of standards before us that a lust does not become an idol that we serve. God gives us desires to eat and drink and tells us to enjoy, each. God gives us lust for laughter and merriment, each for its appropriate time and place. And God gives us lust for the sacred. I presume you have never thought of desiring the sacred in terms of lust, but lust is merely desiring something of the flesh. And the flesh, God said, when he made it, was good. At least it was good at creation. And after the fall of mankind, it looks to be redeemed. But once the flesh begins to be redeemed, once a person has been Christianized, the flesh is used to serve, not to be served. So enjoy your desires, enjoy your lust as God has intended for you to do. Let them serve you and not you serve them. Having then left the corruption of the world and its lust, Peter instructs us Christians to add. Thus we are replacing what we've left behind. He says we are to add virtue, which is godly character, and then to add from virtue knowledge, which is knowing God. And then to add to knowledge self-control, which is God governing the body. And to add to self-control perseverance, which is staying the course, never giving up the faith. And to add to perseverance, godliness, which is obedience to God. And to add to perseverance, brotherly kindness, which is loving our brothers and sisters in Christ carefully. And to add to brotherly kindness, love, which is agape God's unconditional love. And here we are again at love. We cannot escape the command to love each other as God loves us. Jesus says such love would be our greatest testimony to the world that we are his people. Paul said that love is what remains and is the greatest of all characters. John said that we cannot say we know God if we do not love one another. And Peter underlined the same in his first letter. And here he builds everything else in the Christian life up to this crescendo of Christian living. Identifying it the crescendo as loving one another. When you are in a conversation with someone And that person keeps repeating one word or one thought, one phrase, you get the feeling that that one word, one phrase is important to them. We leave for a few days and we keep repeating to our children, take care of the dog. Take care of the dog. The repetition instructs, communicates that that is important to us. Well, consider how often Christians are instructed to love one another. It is repeated and repeated in various forms and in various teachers, so it must be very, very, very important. And as effectual as Christian loving one another can be, so too is it dangerous for the church when it does not occur. When Christians fail to love one another, it damages the testimony of the church to the world, as well as harming the souls of the individuals who are not loving. It damages the soul because in not loving we're abiding in sin. We're making a choice to harbor hate in the heart or to choose bitterness over joy. And let us be certain that not loving is by choice. We are to notice that these things were to add to our lives. To replace ungodly lusts of this world are to be done by our own volition. We are making choices when we add or do not add. When we adding faith, virtue, knowledge, self-control, perseverance, brotherly kindness, and love, we do it by choice, and we do it each moment of every day. When I promised to follow Jesus right before my eighteenth birthday. I knew I was making a conscious choice, enabled by the Holy Spirit. And I found that each moment that I faced a temptation I was making a choice to either go back to the previous life I had lived without knowledge of God. Or I was to go forward. And it was all my choice. I had to make a choice and another choice and another choice and another choice, and that's the Christian life. That is what it is to be a bondservant of Jesus. We make choices to obey or not to obey each moment of every day. The responsibility to choose to add faith in everything else that leads up to love, that choice is our own. And the reality of us being responsible for our choices as to whether we add the characters listed by Saint Paul, that's given to us in verse 8 as a conditional. A conditional. An if and then statement is a conditional, and the condition is determined by our choices. If we add the godly characteristics St. Peter lists to our lives, he says we will have new life, which is the opposite of being barren. And we will have fruitful lives, which is having even more godly characteristics to add to the godly characters we just added. To not add, to not add what is needed in terms of godliness to our lives. He says his first short-sighted, which is our inability to see beyond self And that inability leads to blindness. And being blind leads us back to committing our old sins, going back to Egypt, just as a dog returns to its own vomit. In verse ten, we get a therefore. The word therefore indicates a conclude a conclusion. Thus far, then, we have been given an argument as to what we are to be and what we are to be doing. We are to be bondservants. And as bondservants, we have been given everything we need to live holy lives. With everything necessary given to us, we are to make choices as to whether or not we will add godly characteristics to our personalities. And that will lead to more abundant life, or to not add them, will lead ourselves back to our former sins By adding the godly characteristic St. Peter lists to our lives, he says, we are assuring our call and our election. So this section of scripture is getting very interesting theologically because he brings the truth of being called and elected. I've heard many a Christian say that they either don't believe in the concept of election, God choosing who will be saved, or they don't like the teaching about election. But to either believe or not believe To like or dislike a truth about election is to come away from Scripture, editing it for yourself. It is to edit the Bible, God's revealed will to us, to edit it according to how we want it to read, as opposed to it being God's redemptive story. Such editing is arrogant and blasphemous. We must see it that way. The Bible clearly teaches that God calls people to Himself. Many are called, few are chosen. The Bible clearly teaches that God has indeed elected those who are to be His people As St. Paul said, God has mercy on whom he wills, and whom he wills he hardens. Just as God elected Jacob over Esau, so he elects all who believe in him. That is what the Holy Scripture teaches, regardless of what we want to believe or not believe, or what we like or do not like To assure our call and election is to be confident that we are indeed God's children. We are inheritors of eternal life. To not know if we are God's children is to invite great angst to our lives. Great angst brings insecurity, and insecurity brings a great fear to body and soul. Thus adding the characteristics listed by St. Peter does the opposite. It gives us security. It gives us peace. It gives us security and peace that we are in good relationship with our Creator, and it gives us confidence that heaven is indeed our home. The argument by St. Peter flows. As believers in the Lord Jesus Christ, we are given everything we need to live righteous lives, lives that reflect what Jesus has done for us. It is then our responsibility to make choices, to add to what God has given, to add virtue, knowledge, self-control, perseverance, brotherly kindness, and love. And when we do so, we secure our place as inheritors of God's kingdom. And in summary, if I may. Our love for the brethren, our love for fellow Christians, is an assurance to us that we are indeed followers of the Lord Jesus, children of God, inheritors of the kingdom, our love for one another. I would confess to you this day how the people of this parish Have sanctified me in the manner that you love one another. Although I can preach about the need for us to love one another, and I can teach about it, and I can admonish you again and again to love more, it is you who have shown me how to love one another. The love of God is so very evident in many of you. Take, for example, Austin and Karen Foreman, who consider each of their friends people they need to help when help is needed. They drive people to doctor's appointments, sit with people in waiting rooms and by bedsides. They take people to get their medicines or to the store for food or to simply sit with them and be company. And the Moors, Bill and Betty, taken countless people to appointments and to worship on Sunday or into their home simply to chat. Others of you sit with the sick, provide meals for the needy, get on your knees to bear the burdens of one another, and keep your word. When you say you are available when someone is in need. We preachers can too easily come in and out of people's lives. We can preach and serve for a time, and when the loving gets tough, we can pack up and leave for another parish to repeat our actions and our sermons and then move on again when they are all spent. How can we say we love people, love as God loves, as we are commanded to love, and at the same time walk out of people's lives? To walk out of people's lives is not to love. And the people in this parish have taught me that. I remember being impressed, so very impressed, when I saw and heard of the notes and the phone calls of encouragement that were and are shared in this parish And I have no doubt it started with the spirit of love exemplified by the Reverend Godman and his lovely wife, Suzette. But because the love of God is boundless, there is always ways for us to improve on loving one another. And as we do, as we do, the more secure in Christ we will be I started this sermon asking if you are a bondservant of Jesus Christ. Again, each of us has to answer that personally with self-awareness. Self-awareness and full knowledge of where we are in Christ. But I wish to say as a whole St. Stephen's parish is a bondservant of Christ. And I say for you and with you, may that always be until the Lord returns. Amen. Let us pray.

sermons.title: Reminding You
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, of the Son, of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. Turn your Bibles to 2 Peter. Second Peter chapter one beginning at twelfth verse. St. Peter has taught us Thus far in this his second letter, the Christians have been given enough by God to enable them to live holy lives. A holy life is a life pleasing to God. And our Savior Jesus Christ is the model of the holy life we are to live. In verse 12 of chapter 1, where we pick up for this sermon, Peter acknowledges that every Christian who will read this letter That his readers are already established in the truth that he is teaching. Which is to say, they already know what he is saying. But he admits that he must repeat it, for that is his duty. Remember that it was Jesus who asked Peter if Peter loved him Peter said, Yes, and Jesus said, feed my sheep. The exchange occurred three times. And even though Peter became discouraged by Jesus repeating the question, the three times were poignant, for they were symbolic of the fact that Jesus had been forgiven. I'm sorry, I'm sorry, that Jesus had forgiven Peter for denying him those three times. And it was also to underline how important it was for the apostles to feed the sheep of Jesus. To feed the sheep was and is to teach God's people. And if that was not done, Peter would have been negligent. Recall that in the book of Acts, the apostles devoted themselves to preaching and teaching about Jesus. That focus is to continue today. Pastors are called to preach and teach about Jesus. Unfortunately, that does not happen as it should in many churches for a number of different reasons. Some pastors simply don't believe in Jesus, resulting in the pulpit becoming a place where they share their political opinions or their shrink-think. Other pastors want to be entertaining, and so they spend most of their time behind the pulpit telling stories and sharing anecdotes. Others want to draw a large crowd, and so they treat the pulpit and Christian worship as self-help gatherings. where people can practice thinking positively about self and learn how to be a better businessman or woman, better husband or wife, better father or mother, better friend, better coworker, have a better marriage, etcetera. Etc. , etc. Preaching Jesus apparently does not draw large crowds. It has gotten so bad in churches in the United States that one conservative preacher put out a satire that said, how to be a better preacher than 99% of pastors His answer? Simply preach that Jesus died for you. Simply preaching that Jesus died for you, you have preached better than 99% of what is said in pulpits today. And I fear that sarcasm is not much of an exaggeration. St. Peter didn't preach or teach to gather large crowds. In fact, he said that he knew he was reminding the Christians of what they already knew. Now, how boring is that? How boring it would be to come to church to be reminded of what you already know. It would be boring because we don't forget, do we? It would be boring because what we hear we already fully understand. We already have applied the truths in all of our ways of our lives. And we would be bored because, well, you can only hear that Jesus died for you so many times, right? Can I get an amen? No, don't say amen. We need to hear the truth again and again of Jesus dying for us. Because we need it to increase our love for him. And then increase our love for one another. And then increase our devotion to him. And then increase our dedication to him. And then increase our resistance to sin. And then increase our boldness to stand up for him. And then increase our words to evangelize for him. And then increase our praise for him. And then gather together to hear again that Jesus died for you. Now can I get an amen? Now St. Peter next doubles down on this emphasis of reminding Christians of what he knows they know. And explains his motivation, which is his inevitable death. We are to understand his use of a tent metaphor as a way to explain how the body is a vehicle. that houses the spirit of the individual, that has been made alive by the Holy Spirit, and that that said spirit in each of us is eternal. Peter, however, does not want us to mistake the understanding of our bodies as tents in terms of the spirit needing to escape the body or the tent. Remember that God made our bodies and he said they are good. The problem is we are subject to mortality because of the curse mankind is under. Our spirits need new bodies in order to be free and to live eternally as whole human beings, just as Jesus is. From the last line in verse 14, we can accept that the Holy Spirit has pressed upon Peter, that his life in this world will shortly end. And it did. As verse 15 explains, by Saint Peter writing these reminders down This is to ensure that Christians will always have the reminders, the necessary reminders in front of them. Reminders of who Jesus is and what God had done in Jesus for our salvation. In writing it down, it remains with them always to be referred back to after Peter's death. And this means that we need to be reminded of our need to be reminded. Remember when Saint Paul wrote to the Galatians, and he was expressing his aghast that they had so quickly been led astray into false doctrine. False doctrine is thinking falsely about God. And so what is true for the Galatians could be true for any of us if we are not reminded. And beloved, this is the way of the devil. He leads people away from believing in Jesus by corrupting their way of thinking about Jesus. He leads them away by tempting them to think in terms of life circumstances instead of terms of eternal truth. And so when life circumstances change, the way we think changes. And the way we think that changes includes doctrine. And doctrine is what we think about God. The most common example, how easily absolutes can change when the behavior of our loved ones change. And so if I believe the doctrine that homosexual behavior is sinful, and my brother reveals himself to be a homosexual, I am tempted to change my view on the morality of homosexual behavior because I want to think well of my brother. And when I change such a view, it allows me to question other teachings of the Bible, which could lead me to reject or redact all the doctrine the Bible teaches And so my relationship with my brother becomes an idol. I wish to serve rather than the doctrines that are taught me in Holy Scripture. And you have witnessed this type of changing of doctrine just as I have. We believe Divorce is sinful until our own child gets a divorce, or maybe I myself get a divorce, and suddenly it's not so sinful anymore. We believe sex outside of marriage is sinful until a sibling starts to live with her boyfriend. We believe Jesus is the only way to heaven until Aunt Beatrice becomes a universalist And by golly, we all like Aunt Beatrice, and we don't want to think about her going to hell, and so we change our doctrine, making Jesus a way to heaven and not the way to heaven. Such occurrences we all know all too well. Therefore, we need to be reminded of true doctrine. St. Peter next lets us know where his sound doctrine was derived. He was a witness himself. The origin is himself as a witness. The Apostle John used the same source of authority, his own experience. As eyewitnesses, the apostles could confirm what Jesus taught, what miracles he performed, and what was done to him. And it is the testimony of the apostles that the church today depends upon, and we do so unapologetically. Those of you who have studied philosophy a little bit, even, know the subject of epistemology, which is the study of knowledge or the study of how we know things. Most people don't search into what it means to know something or how knowledge is obtained. We just say that we know certain things and we don't know much about certain things. But epistemology asks what it means to say that you know something. For example, I can say that I know that 2 plus 2 equals 4, but what does that mean? Do I know how two plus two equals four? Do I have a knowledge of numbers and their eternal quality before I can say I know that two plus two equals four? It's simply stating a fact, memorizing a fact. Is that actual knowledge An empiricist would say that a person cannot say he or she knows anything unless it is experienced by the senses. Thus, according to an empiricist, only the apostles could say that they know Jesus because they experienced him with their senses. You and I, however, cannot say that we know Jesus because we know him by the testimony of others and not by our own senses. A believer who's more in touch with their feelings might argue that he or she has experienced Jesus with their senses and that they felt the presence of Jesus or heard his voice speak to them personally. And the empiricist would argue that such experience is not measurable and therefore cannot be counted as experience and thus no real knowledge. So how is the empiricist to be countered in terms of being convinced that Jesus can be known through eyewitness testimony of the apostles? Well the answer is actually simple. Consider that we cannot make good decisions in life unless we base those decisions on the knowledge and a great deal of knowledge that we use from somebody else Not by our own experience, but rather by the experience of others. If we only knew truth by our own experience, history would be meaningless, and as would moral lessons. In truth, we depend a great deal on the knowledge gained by the experience of others. For instance, I say that Mount Everest is over 29,000 feet high because I trust in the measurements made by others who have calculated its height. I am also aware that falling from such a height means certain death, because others have experienced it, and that's good enough for me to gain some knowledge. I know falling over 29,000 feet kills a human being. Testimony of someone else. And so we trust in the testimony of the apostles without reservation to trust them because we found that the words they heard from Jesus that they repeated to us, those words have life. Words like no other man has spoken. We believe their testimony that Jesus is alive, having been raised from the dead, because it makes sense. It makes sense in terms of what was prophesied. It makes sense of the consistency of the accounts of the apostles. It makes sense as to how those Roman guards were thwarted. But we also believe. We also believe because we experienced the weight of sin brought upon our own consciences. And we experience that sin lifted and gone from us, and we don't care if an empiricist can measure such a thing. We know it to be true. It is as real to us as anything we have seen with our eyes, touched with our fingers, heard with our ears, smelled with our nose, tasted with our tongue. Jesus is alive, my sins are forgiven, heaven's gates are opened wide. That's what a Christian believes. That is what Saint Peter reminds us of. The testimony of the apostles as a source of eternal truth known is in contrast to the cunning-devised fables. Now because St. Peter does not identify what these specific fables are, this allows us to say, in general, that false made-up stories are dangerous, some of them. A fable, you know, is a made-up story. Some fables are very effective at teaching moral lessons, as we know Esau fables. The fables that are told and written that attempt to evoke religious devotion, those are of a different nature altogether. Such can be told to detract from truth. We know the Greeks telling stories of the gods, who sound a lot more like human beings. Among the Norsemen there was the story told of Odin, their chief god, who gained great wisdom by going through various trials in order to achieve knowledge of the realm of the dead He sacrificed himself. It was after his sacrifice that he returned from the dead stronger than ever. The only problem with that story is that it was told of their God after Christianity had reached the Norsemen. These unbelievers wanted their God to be greater than Jesus, and so they made it up. Other religions such as Hinduism have resurrection-like stories, but none of them are witnessed by men who tell their eyewitness accounts. Christians, Christians are to be a people of truth, for Jesus is the truth. And this means that fables that engender faith or promote religious faith or teaches religious doctrine, these cannot be acceptable in the church. Maybe some of you have received emails that tell stories of young Christians standing up to their college professors and going toe-to-toe with them by way of cunning argumentation. Where in the end the supposed student makes the professor look foolish and all the while proves to everyone that God exists. In one story, a college girl proves that her professor doesn't have a brain by using his own argumentation that God doesn't exist. How clever. In another, the student who proves that God exists is identified as Albert Einstein. But no true story of anything remotely like these stories told have ever been documented as true. But they are passed around on the internet for the purpose of encouraging Christians that we have truth on our side. The problem with that is that we should not be encouraged that we have truth on our side by way of telling-coming fables. We don't need fables. Instead, we need to put our confidence in the same place Peter did. Who was an eyewitness and a person of faith as he trusted the Holy Scriptures. He trusted in the prophets who confirmed the Old Testament narrative as it spoke of the Jesus who was to come. The apostles compared the person of Jesus that they knew personally to the words of the prophets and found that Jesus fulfilled all that they knew and more. And notice how Peter accepts the knowledge passed on to him by the prophets as they were witnesses to God's word, writing it down from their hearts. His confidence of faith in the authority of Holy Scripture and specifically the words of the prophets is to be our confidence as well. As St. Peter confirms, the words of the prophets came from God. And Jesus came from God. And Jesus said that he speaks only what the Father tells him to speak. And Jesus died for your sins. And that is enough. While attending seminary, In the mid-1990s, the same time there was a gathering of so-called biblical scholars taking place at the Westar Institute. The gathering was called the Jesus Seminar. The seminar was made up of 150 critical scholars, I put scholars in quotes, who came together in agreement already that the gospel accounts of Jesus were more mythical than factual. Their presuppositions came to be because of their seminary training. That consisted of liberal scholarship that included that the Bible was an archaic book That did not stand up to the scrutiny brought upon it today by the Enlightenment. And thus the Christian church needed to develop a new way of interpreting the Bible. The conclusion of the Jesus seminar was that Jesus was nothing more than an itinerant, Hellenistic, Jewish sage and a faith healer. who preached a gospel of liberation from injustices. That same Jesus is what is preached and prayed to in mainline churches across the globe today. And that preaching of that Jesus has led to the ordination of women, the consecration of a homosexual bishop, the blessing of same-sex unions, the denial of Jesus being God. The denial of the historic resurrection of Jesus, and thus the corruption of the gospel. And if that is the real Jesus If that is the real Jesus, then you and I are condemned, or you and I are still in our sins. But Jesus died for your sins. And there I did it again. I preached better than 99% of the preachers preaching today. What Saint Peter knew was the Jesus who died for our sins. What St. Peter knew were the holy scriptures that confirm Jesus died for our sins. That was enough. And that is enough to know. It is enough to believe Personally, I have always thought it remarkable that any scholar, again in quotes, could spend his energy studying a new Jesus. When it takes eternity to know the depth of the revealed Jesus in Holy Scripture. Saint Peter reminded us May we keep being reminded. Let us pray. Our gracious Lord, how grateful we are, how you use men like Peter To maintain the faith, to teach the doctrines that are true, and to remind us of them over and over again. Father, may we never tire of hearing the truth, of believing the truth, of knowing that Jesus died for our sins. It is in his name that we pray. Amen.

sermons.title: The Presence of False Teachers
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: May the words of my mouth and the meditation of our hearts be accessible in thy sight, O Lord, our strength and our redeemer. In the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please turn to 2 Peter 2 Where we pick up our study on first and second Peter. I trust that those of you who are sports fans have noticed that sportscasters and athletes can and do say some of the dumbest things. Here are some dumb things sports announcers and athletes have said. From Trent Dilfer Former Baltimore Ravens Super Bowl champion quarterback and current analyst, he said You cannot lose games in the NFL and still win. At least the logic is sound. From former basketball coach and announcer Doug Collins, anytime Detroit scores more than a hundred points and holds the other team below a hundred points, they almost always win. Can't argue the numbers. When Shaquille O'Neal, former basketball player and current anal analyst Played in Greece with Team USA, he was asked by a reporter if he had visited the Parthenon. He responded, I can't really remember the names of all the clubs that we went to. At least he's honest. Former Major League Baseball star and current announcer Alex Rodriguez. Once said, therapy can be good. It can be therapeutic. 1970s baseball player Tito Fuentes, wonder how many remember him, told the reporter that teams should not throw at him purposefully to hit him Because I'm a father of five or six kids. And we wonder which one is the correct number Jason Kidd, a former basketball and great uh basketball grade and current NBA coach said, we're going to turn this team 360 degrees around. And that probably didn't take long. And a former NFL quarterback and current announcer, you know him well, Joe Fiseman, said, nobody in football should be called a genius. A genius is a guy like Norman Einstein. Apparently, Albert had a brother. Now we can laugh at such statements because we know that when the persons are making these statements, they're simply not paying attention to what they are saying. Rather than speaking purposefully as a fool. Speaking purposefully. These speakers are harmless They are in contrast to the teachers addressed in 2 Peter 2. Those teachers described are secretly bringing destruction. purposefully, secretly bringing destruction. They are teaching falsely on purpose. They are teaching falsely on purpose because they are covetous. And what did they covet? They coveted what any false teacher then, today, and any other time in history of the Christian church They coveted power, influence, and money. Power, influence, and money. I addressed last Sunday the problem of poor preaching in Christian pulpits today. And then I ran across this study. Done by Lingenir Ministry, a ministry led by conservative theologian R. C. Sprohl The survey was taken three years ago questioning Bible-believing Christians who attend corporate worship regularly, questioning them about their beliefs. The good news of the study was that 96% of those pulled believe in the resurrection of Jesus. Thanks be to God. 92% believe that salvation is through Jesus alone. And 88% believe that the Bible is indeed the Word of God. The bad news is That 22% believe God the Father is more divine than Jesus the Son. More than half, 51%, believe the Holy Spirit is a force rather than a person. And 68% believe that the people actually initiate a relationship with God instead of God initiating the relationship. What is interesting about these latter beliefs is that each of them line up with beliefs that the church has rejected. and labeled heresies. Not just recently. So the false doctrines are not new. Believing God the Father is more divine than Jesus is a form of Arianism, and the teaching of Arius led to the first council of the church. You know it as the Council of Nicaea in 325 A. D. And eventually that meeting led to the Nicene Creed. At the same council of Nicaea, the church addressed the heresy by a group called the Spirit Fighters. These spirit fighters taught that the spirit was not a person, but a mere source of power. That is one reason why the Nicene Creed goes to greater length, more detailed length of what the Holy Spirit is, as opposed to the Apostles' Creed. And finally, the belief that humans individually choose to seek out God rather than God seeking out them is a form of Pelagiism. Which taught that every human was born into a state of innocency with the ability to choose to follow God or not to follow God. The church denounced such teachings at the Council of Carthage in 418 A. D. The church stated that the Bible clearly teaches that mankind is born under a curse of Adam and need God to give life so that people can follow him. Now the question that needs to be answered is what is the cause of these heretical beliefs among Christians today? Are preachers responsible for this false teaching? Is it Sunday school teachers and Bible study leaders that are falsely teaching God's people? Is it televangelists that are leading people to a false understanding and thus a false faith in God? Are there radio preachers and teachers that are not careful with their instruction? And if it is Psalm or all of the above Are they doing it purposefully? Are they purposefully leading people astray? I did some searching for heresies this week being propagated by televangelists today. And what I found, first of all, was easy to find. And second, the same type of heresies already mentioned are being taught today over the airwaves. Here is what one televangelist said when explaining that Jesus spoke to him personally. He told the people listening to him that Jesus said to him Don't be disturbed when people put you down and speak harshly and roughly of you. They spoke that way of me. Should they not speak that way of you? They crucified me for claiming that I was God. But I didn't claim I was God. I claimed I walked with him and he was in me. Hallelujah. Beloved Arius the heretic of the fourth century would have said amen to such false teaching. And he was condemned 1,692 years ago. And then there are popular radio preachers who are Baptistic in their theology and preach a decision-oriented gospel. that tells non-believers that Jesus paid it all for them, but yet their salvation is determined determined by them making a decision to follow Jesus. And that type of teaching is so common, it might just sound acceptable to some of you, but again, Pelagian the Heretic was condemned 1,599 years ago For such preaching. Beloved, we are coming upon the 500th anniversary of the Reformation this coming October. And thus it is fitting for us to underline what is good about it today. And oh, please hear me. I do not say that everything about the Reformation was good for the Church. The Reformation has rightly been compared to the division of Israel in the Old Testament. being divided into two distinct nations, the northern tribes and the southern tribes. And after the division it was inevitable that Israel would be led to worship false gods. and be overthrown by foreign powers. And the same can be said for the Christian Church First being divided in 1054 east and west, and next when it was divided in the west into Protestant and Roman Catholic. And then among the Protestants there were groups such as the Anabaptists who did the proverbial throwing the baby out with the back water or the baptismal water. See what I did there? Deciding that everyone but them had this Reformation thing all wrong, and it was up to them to return the church to its first century days. But of course the Anabaptists couldn't agree on everything, and so they split again and again. Presbyterians couldn't agree on everything, so they split and continue to split. Lutherans have split and split again. Anglican Episcopalians have split and are still splitting Even groups who split have split. And there are the independents who don't have any source of authority behind them but their own testimony. And now the Christian Church. The Christian Church is so divided, it is easily conquered by liberals and fearful fundamentalists. And the result is a Christian church that has but a high-pitched, squeaky voice in society that no one listens to with any seriousness. And frankly, a voice that's rather annoying even to us in the church. But, however, on the other hand What was good about the Reformation was that it re-established what the Bible clearly teaches about the human nature, the result of the fall of Adam and Eve. It teaches that the nature of every person is dead to God. The dead state of the soul then affirms the necessity of the Holy Spirit reviving a human soul so that a person Then can make a decision to follow Jesus. Thus, salvation is by grace alone, grace of God alone By faith alone, faith that is a gift from God. It is then not based on people making good decisions for themselves. It is God who gives the faith that enables the decision for too long Christians and the church has played at preaching the gospel using advertising techniques that Make Jesus look no more important than or necessary than a fad diet or a new style of clothing. Fads fade and styles go out. But the Word of God, the gospel of the Lord Jesus Christ, you know it is forever. Now the last obvious heresy that is preached openly today is a bit surprising because of how blatant it is. Now you know I don't agree with health and wealth gospel preaching, preached by many televangelists I believe they misrepresent passages of Scripture that give hope for our eternal home where moth and rust do not corrupt, instead of caring about wealth in this life. But what is really troubling is not that the preachers tell you that God wants you to be successful. That's really not the problem But when they sell you something, such as a blessing or a healing, teaching that such can be obtained by money. And it doesn't matter how the preacher so-called couches such an offering. To sell blessings of the Holy Spirit is simonizing, plain and simple. Simonizing is named, you remember, after the heretical act of Simon Magus, who is recorded in the book of Acts as having thought that he could buy the Holy Spirit from the apostles and do miracles himself. Such a thought and such an attempt was heretical and has always been heretical in the church. Blessings of the Holy Spirit cannot be purchased by the gold of men. And anyone who preaches or pretends that it can be should be defrocked of his ordination orders if he has any. And even taken to the mat. I know that we are to follow Jesus in suffering instead of causing others to suffer, but it does appear on this side of heaven and being under the sun, that a good old fist pounding might put some of these false teachers in the corner that they might not come out of. Besides, the ones I see on T V could do a few push ups Beloved, false teaching leads to false Jesus. And a false Jesus leads to hell. It is that simple. It is why St. Peter addresses the subject of false teachers. It is too earnest to ignore. And the second point made by St. Peter in this section of his letter is connected to the first, and that he wants his audience to fear. To fear accepting or being led or being one of the false teachers. He wants them to fear That God will indeed bring judgment upon such teachers and upon those who follow such teachers. And he wants his audience to be confident in God's righteous judgment. Even though it appears that God's judgment at the moment is quiet. As God says through the psalmist Quote, these things you have done, and I kept silence. You thought I was just like you. Be not fooled, we learn from that passage, by got by God's silence. Be not fooled by God's silence. You see, the fool sleeps with his neighbor's wife. He goes home, and his wife suspects nothing. No lightning strikes him from above. And so he thinks that such silence means he has gotten away with adultery. Be not fooled by God's silence. A man spends a lifetime lying. He cheats on his schoolwork and he receives a diploma. He takes credit for other people's work and he gets a promotion. He falsely fills out his tax forms, and the government gives him a rebate. Be not fooled by God's silence. A preacher tells his congregation that God is more concerned about unity than he is about sexual morality. He proclaims to the congregation that unity is a greater moral standard than fornication or sodomy. He teaches his congregation that acceptance of alternative lifestyles is a higher doctrine than even the Trinity. He preaches on Easter morning that the resurrection of Jesus is not to be understood as a historical event, but a metaphor to be used to show how all of us can rise above moral prejudices. He teaches, proclaims, and preaches this way, and nothing happens to him. He has his health, he has wealth, he has influence, he has titles. Be not fooled by God's silence. The evidence is too numerous to conclude that God will remain silent. As he said through the psalmist, he is not like men. Men like to forget about it. Just forget about it. Move on. Nothing to see here. Men like to forget their wrongs that were never atoned for. The foolish man asks, why can't God just forget about sins of the past and move on? Men move on themselves, they do wrong and move away. They speak out of turn, cause trouble, create angst, and they leave, thinking that what they leave is forgotten Be not fooled by God's silence. Here is Peter's argument that God will not remain silent. If God did not let the angels in heaven who rebelled against him go unpunished, why would he let false teachers in the church go unpunished? If he would not let men on earth whose hearts were bent toward evil go unpunished, drowning them in the flood, the great flood, why would he let false prophets go unpunished? If he would not let those who inhabited Sodom and Gomorrah go unpunished, having perverted themselves in ways not to be spoken about. How would he not punish those who bring into the church destructive heresies? Such questions, as you know, are rhetorical. The answer to each is obvious and the same. God will not let the guilty go unpunished, be not fooled by God's silence. It is astounding that false teachers appear to have no fear of God. This week I heard a false teacher tell his audience that God spoke to him personally about an issue of ministry in which God Asked this man for personal advice. And the false teacher gave the advice to God, telling God That he shouldn't do what God was planning but should go somewhere else and God agreed with him And as far as I could tell, no one left the sanctuary. No one protested. That's such a ridiculous testimony. And people to this day still give to this false teacher. He gets airtime and he gets money. He and his listeners are being fooled by God's silence. This next one really gets me. Two false teachers are sitting at a small table across from one another and talking about the power that every Christian has. And the statement is made that Jesus is not the only Son of God. The other host nods in full agreement, adding that Jesus was merely the first fruits of many sons of God. And that means that all followers are sons like Jesus is a son. Beloved, a false teacher cannot be more contradictory to Holy Scripture with such a teaching. We know the word. John 3. 16 plainly says that God so loved the world that he gave his only begotten Son. And these two false teachers continue to teach and people continue to send them money while all parties are fooled by God's silence. Allow me one more point about false teachers and false teachings. Much of what is blatant false teaching today Started with teaching that didn't seem so dangerous. It started with Bible interpretation methods that were experimental. It started with looking at St. Paul's teaching on certain subjects with contemporary glasses and finding him to be a bit chauvinistic. Even homophobic. And once those accusations were in place, St. Paul's teaching on women being leaders in the church was doubted. When that was doubted, St. Paul's teaching on other moral issues was doubted.
