And finding stories about outside the Bible about faith being applied. To trying and tempting times is easy because Christians have been collecting those stories for generations. We have the Fox's book of martyrs that inform us that each of the apostles died in their faith in Jesus. In faith, James the Great, brother to John, died by beheading. In faith, Philip was scourged, imprisoned, and afterwards crucified. In faith, Matthew was speared to death. In faith, James, the brother to our Lord, was stoned and clubbed to death In faith, Matthias, the one chosen to replace Judas, was stoned and beheaded. In faith, Andrew was crucified on an X-shaped cross. In faith, Peter was crucified upside down. In faith, Paul was beheaded by a sword. In faith, Jude was also crucified. In faith, Bartholomew was cruelly beaten and then crucified. By faith, Thomas, like Matthew, was on the wrong end of a spear. By faith, Simon the Zealot joined those who had been crucified. And many, many more died with their faith in Jesus intact. And while I put before us many faithful examples of Christians maintaining their faith until their last breath, It is a failing of this preacher to only put great stories of faith before us. We must not underestimate. The examples of every day, day in and day out, faith that is practiced by so many among us and who have gone before us. No book of martyrs Is written for the mother who by faith changes the diapers of her children and keeps the kitchen floor clean. No record is kept of the father who gets up before the Son and puts in eight or more hours of work every day but Sunday so that his family has food and clothing and many more things. No award is given in this life at least that recognizes a woman who stays in a marriage in which she is not happy. No well done is spoken to the life of a teenager in this life who resists the temptations in which his peers wallow. And yet every day, everyday faith is essential because everyday faith is saving faith. Everyday faith says that Jesus is Lord and Savior, regardless of what is on the news. Everyday faith says that circumstances in this life do not dictate who is God, and that there is one God who is revealed to us as Father, Son, and Holy Ghost. Everyday faith sees eternal value in the mundane things of life And so faith is a foundation stone in the Christian life. Our perfection, our holiness, our eternal reward is built upon the faith that we have. In Jesus as our Savior and our God. And faith is a gift from God. Both saving faith and spiritual gift of faith are gifts from God. And we can ask for more if we need it. And God will grant it. Such is the nature of the foundation of faith. May it be firmly established in us all. Let us pray. Our Father I confess there is much more to be said about faith. But we pray here that what is foundational about it would be established in all of our lives. And we say together, I believe, help my unbelief. In Jesus' name we pray. Amen.

sermons.title: Unity Baptism
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. We are continuing our summer series on the foundation stones as listed in the book of Hebrews, chapter six. I start with the following as a repeat analogy, identifying points of division amongst the followers of Jesus as described in the New Testament. There were two groups that had much in common. Most importantly, they were eyewitnesses to a miracle of Jesus healing a blind man. In John chapter 9, we are told the story of a man who was blind from birth, being brought to Jesus. The disciples were curious as to why the man was blind, thinking that such a curse was caused by either his sins or the sins of his parents. Jesus exclaimed, explained, excuse me, that neither was the cause, but only that Jesus might be revealed as the light of the world. Jesus then spit on the ground, made some mud from the ground, and his saliva, with his saliva, and placed the mud on the blind man's eyes. He then instructed the blind man to wash his face in the sacred pool of Siloam. The result was that the man was healed of blindness. Next, in Mark chapter 8, Jesus comes to the town of Bethshaizda, where some people brought a blind man to him, asking for him to be healed. Jesus took the man out of the village, spit on the man's eyes directly, and then put his hands on him At first, the man could see only outlines of the world until Jesus put his hands on him again, and the result was that his sight was fully restored. When the two stories of these blind men being healed were told separately, those who told the story of the first man Insisted that if a blind man is to be healed, he must have mud placed on his eyes. In contrast, those who told the story of the second man being healed insisted that hands must be laid upon a man who is blind in order to be healed. When the two groups heard the story of the other, they dug in, insisting that what must be done for a blind man to be healed is mud. No. Hands laid upon. Soon the side that insisted on mud being applied for a man to be healed of blindness, well they became known as the Mudites And the group that insisted only on the laying on of hands, they became known as the anti-Muddites. Such is the story of the first two Christian denominations. You don't believe that story, I trust. But all too soon the glory that was to be given to God for a miracle of healing the blind was ignored, and each focusing on mud or anti-mud I know that such a story is unfortunately easily believed among Christians because we have an embarrassing history of dividing from each other over ignorant and ridiculous reasons. But the story of the Mudites and the Anti-Muddites, even though it is not true, highlights the absurdity of Christian division among us. Now speaking about Christian division is most appropriate as we come to this third foundation stone as found in Hebrews 6, verse 2. For there we find the foundation stone of the doctrine of baptisms. Not surprisingly, there is a controversy, not only about the rite of baptisms, but about the passage itself. For scholars believe that the word doctrine is the focus of the verse and not the word baptisms. Well to cut short that discussion, you need only to know that I side with the traditional interpretation, which is to focus on the foundation stone of baptisms. And the first baptism we are looking at is by water. The second baptism of the baptism's plural is the baptism of the Holy Ghost. Consider and lament regarding the great irony that baptism and baptisms Are supposed to be the truths that unite the people of God, and yet they are what Christians use to separate from one another And overarching the separations Christians make with each other is the priestly prayer that Jesus prayed, that his followers would be united with each other as Jesus was united with the Father. The manner that Christians divide with one another is in direct defiance of that prayer. Let us not sugarcoat that truth. Christian baptisms. Allow us to see that every Christian is united in Jesus Christ. Because there is only one God to whom we are baptized, and we are baptized into only one family. And as his family, we are co-inheritors to his kingdom. All who have fulfilled the requirement to repent and be baptized are co-inheritors of God. Regardless of whether we like each other or whether we fully agree with one another. Let's get a brief history of baptism. The brief history of baptism in the Old Testament is that there were requirements from the law for ceremonial washings in order for a person to be clean, cleansed, and considered ceremonially clean The priests were required to go through a full washing before they could minister before the Lord as a priest. And this was done by the pouring of water, such as was done over Aaron and his sons. Others, that is the Levites, were sprinkled. It was commanded that all the Levites be sprinkled if they were to serve in the holy place or not. Other required washings were for men who had semenal emissions, women who had blood emissions Also, any person who came in physical contact with a dead animal or a human body were required to go through a ceremony of cleansing. And during the intertestament times, the Jewish people added to the ceremonial washings required of the Old Testament. Using bathing rites to symbolize all moments in which they were setting themselves aside for God. And our trip to Israel, we saw the unearthing of Israelite homes from the first century. And there they had bathing structures as part of the interior of their home. Not to take a bath as you and I would, but for the ritual of being cleansed before God. They were called mikbols. And thus, when John the Baptist and Jesus came along preaching repentance and using the symbol of baptism Well, that symbol was very familiar to the Jewish people in that era. And the accounts of specific baptisms described in the New Testament do not allow, and this is important Do not allow for any Christian group to insist that the mode of baptism be done in one particular manner. And that statement is important for Christian unity. When Jesus is baptized in the Jordan River, It was assumed by our Baptist friends that he must have been fully immersed. Nowhere in the Bible Does it say that Jesus was fully immersed? But the Baptist type churches and their teachers conclude that he was because of the word baptism in the Greek. Using it to refer to the dying of a cloth to change its color. And since the dyeing of a cloth needed to be immersed in order for it to be effective, they take that word and assume that all baptisms must be fully immersed. In fact, some Baptist groups are so adamant about this need that if a person is dumped in the water and one body part flies out, well that has to be done all over again. just in case one body part might be left out at the resurrection. And such groups also insist That anyone who has to be immersed and who has not been immersed is not truly baptized and thus not a Christian, and thus hellbound. And it does not matter to them that to believe such is to say that children born into Christian homes are hellbound until they are baptized. And then these groups are inconsistent when they teach their children to pray before they're baptized For such an inconsistency in their theology would actually say that that child's a sinner and shouldn't pray the Lord's Prayer or any other prayer until they are baptized The account of the jailer and his family being baptized as recorded in the book of Acts. Allows us to conclude that immersion is not necessary for a person to be baptized. Remember the story in Acts chapter 16. Paul and Silas are rotting in jail. Guilty of the crime of preaching the gospel of Jesus. And they sang and prayed to the glory of God. And when they sang and prayed, their chains fell off. They were loosened and the doors of the jail came open. And the jailer who was responsible for the prisoners saw what happened and concluded that he would be tried and hung for allowing these prisoners to escape. But instead he walks in, and there are Paul and Silas still sitting in their cell. And when Paul and Silas shared the good news of Jesus to this jailer, offering forgiveness of sins and eternal life, The jailer believed, Luke says. And then Luke writes this. The jailer took them, that is Paul and Silas, and washed their wounds. And without delay, he and all his household were baptized. Baptized in the jail cell Where's the Jordan River in that story? Where's the possibility of being immersed in that story? There was only water basins used for washing and drinking. And yet the whole household of the jailer was baptized. And such a scenario fits well with how priests were baptized or ceremonially washed before entering the temple. They were not immersed, but poured upon, sprinkled upon, as the law required. And so we, as part of the royal priesthood, are to be received. as being baptized whether water is poured upon us, sprinkled upon us, or covering us. And such a perspective is charity. Charity from one Christian to another. It is the same charity that Jesus affords us every day. But enough about the mode of baptism. The devil loves for Christians to debate about the mode of baptism: sprinkling, pouring, covering. And so we talk positively about baptism, what it is for every Christian. Notice from our reading in Colossians chapter 2. Baptism is the mark of the covenant that God places upon each of his people, proclaiming them to be his own. And we know that God commanded circumcision of all males born in the covenant of Abraham And it was commanded of the males because they were to be the covenant heads of their families. And the women who came under those covenant heads were also inheritors to the covenant of Abraham. And we learn later in the Old Testament that the act of male circumcision was a sign of something greater that God wanted to do for his people. What he wanted to do greater is circumcise the heart. And the circumcision of heart Is for every person necessary because every individual is born in sin and thus an enemy of God Enemies of God have hearts that are hardened by sin and hardened by the sin nature. The sin nature needs to be removed in order for an individual to love God. For that is what is required to love God with all of our heart. And so in Colossians we read Paul teaching Christians, that baptism in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Ghost is the new circumcision, the sign of the covenant that God has with his people in Christ. Baptism replaces circumcision as a sign and a seal that God's people are marked by Him and they have new hearts to beat for Him. And such a sign is not just for males, but for females as well. And because it is related to circumcision. Christianity of the early church understood it as a right to include children born into a covenant home. If a child was circumcised according to the law of Moses in order to be a part of the covenant that God made with Abraham. And as baptism replaces circumcision as a sign and seal of the covenant God made in Jesus. So then children born in the homes of people who believe in Jesus ought to be baptized. In fact John Calvin, that studious reformer, argued that children born into covenant homes are owed, owed Christian baptism. It is their right as covenant children. The argument for infant baptism does not need to be more complicated than that explained. And as a side note, if I may, I encourage you not to be shy about using the sign of the cross. That is placed upon every person baptized in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Ghost. And too often Protestants think, well, that's what Roman Catholics do. No, we ought not let the Roman Catholics steal everything that's good. To use the sign of the cross is to be reminded that we have been marked by God in baptism, we are his. And if you're going to do it properly, you need to do the three fingers to remind you of the Father, the Son, and of the Holy Ghost It is good to remind yourself with the sign of the cross that you have been marked by God and you are His. Now the next baptism that must be included in this doctrine of baptisms plural is the baptism of the Holy Spirit. And such a baptism was promised by Jesus, who taught his followers that a comforter would come and lead them into all truth. And he described it as power coming to them from on high It is the Holy Spirit who has promised to come upon and baptize every person who confesses Jesus as Lord and Savior and who have been baptized in water. And the Holy Spirit is to be the person of God who also brings unity to the people of God For he is one Spirit, and thus he dwells in the hearts and minds of Christians. He is the same Spirit dwelling in each of us. He is how God can be in all places at all times. Unfortunately, again, that which is to unite us as God's presence being shared by each of us has been another means That the devil has used to divide us. In the book of Acts, there was division Because people had been baptized in water, but had not yet received the external gifts of the Holy Spirit. Others had received spiritual gifts from the Holy Spirit and had not yet been baptized in water. And this gave Christians grounds to argue with one another and insist that their experience was the correct experience, just like the Mudites and the Anti-Muddites. And these opportunities for Christians to divide, well, these opportunities necessitated St. Paul. St. Peter, St. James, St. John, to write in their letters the importance of unity with brothers and sisters in Christ. It was a problem then and it's a problem now. Bobby Lynn and I Experience firsthand how Christians use the baptism of the Holy Spirit to divide Christians In our college days, we were part of an independent church that was making much of their Christian doctrine up as they went along. And part of what they insisted upon was that every person display a proof of being baptized in the Holy Spirit. And that act of proof was speaking in an unknown tongue. If that could not be done The church leadership concluded that such a person who couldn't speak in tongues was not baptized in the Holy Spirit. And this conclusion then allowed the leadership to describe themselves as spirit-filled Christians and all others as marginal Christians. And looking back on that experience makes us sad to this day. The simple truth is that a person who believes in Jesus can know he or she has the Holy Spirit, been baptized in the Holy Spirit, not by a special gift. But by simply the ability to confess Jesus as Lord and Savior. Hear this from St. Paul. No one can say that Jesus is Lord except by the Holy Spirit. And from St. John, by this you know the Spirit of God. Every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is of God. No other test is necessary. Confession, sincere confession of Jesus as Savior and Lord is sufficient proof that the Holy Spirit dwells within you. Has baptized you, marked you. Hallelujah. Thanks be to God. Now there is much, much more to be said about the doctrine of baptisms. But what we have heard here this morning are the fundamentals, the foundation stone. And what stands out to me is how the fundamentals are to unite us, not divide us. Unity and peace amongst Christians has fallen on very hard times in this generation. Primarily Because of the liberals confessing to be Christian and yet having placed the priority of unity over correct doctrine And this we shall not do. For if we do, we no longer are Christian. If there is to be division among us, it is to be a division based on whether we believe Jesus to be the only Messiah or not. It is to be based on there being but one God, revealed as Father, Son, and Holy Ghost. If a teacher or church leader insists that Jesus was just a prophet or not God or that God, the God of Christianity is one of many revelations about God. Well, then we should separate ourselves from such blasphemy. But may it never be that we divide over the doctrine of baptisms. For baptism in water is where we all come together, identifying with what Jesus did. Baptism of the Holy Spirit, allowing us to confess Jesus as God is to unite us. Because we are all filled by the same Spirit, the very presence of God within each of us. I close with an important distinction regarding baptisms. A parishioner recently said to me, having come from a different background than Anglican, that he realized for the first time That baptism is not something he is to do for God, but something that God does and has done for him. For him, that was a profound realization. And it should be for all of us. God does the work in baptism. He does the work in the water, in the name of the Trinity, and in the faith of those who participate. And God does the work with the Spirit as He fills and enables his people to have faith and to confess the truth, a truth we could never confess on our own. The doctrine of baptism is to be laid in our hearts, in our lives, and we are to build upon it just as we do. As we build on faith towards God, as we leave dead works behind. Let us pray.

sermons.title: Laying on of hands
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Maybe seated. Well first thank Nathan for his good words, and we will fled as a church to pray for him, his family, his ministry. We continue our series this morning on the six foundation stones as listed in Hebrews chapter six, verses one through three. According to the Urban Dictionary, cooties are highly contagious as they breed inside young boys and young girls. They can be released by a boy touching a girl or a girl touching a boy. As the one who gets cooties gets it. By being touched by the opposite sex. When I was a child in elementary school, we would yell that a certain girl had cooties And then we would run away, but in truth we were hoping that she would chase us and touch us if possible. It is interesting that the Urban Dictionary continues its definition by the following statement about Kudis. Cooties are diseases that the opposite sex has that gives you a reason not to be around them When you get older, cooties become known as SDDs. That was news to me And the innocency of childhood is quickly swept away. Now the subject of Tutis seems applicable as we come to our fourth foundation stone. We have heard about repentance from dead works, faith toward God, doctrine of baptisms, and now we come to the laying on of hands. While the first three initially make sense as foundational beliefs to be established in every Christian life This fourth foundation, the laying on of hands, does not seem to have an obvious purpose. After all, the laying out of hands is how you get cooties. And some people have such a strong belief in the danger of cooties, they won't shake other people's hands, they won't use public utilities, and they won't even handle doorknob handles handled by others. We say such people are suffering by obsessive compulsive disorder, having the fear of the germs of others, where we just simply know they don't want to get cooties. Now the laying on of hands can also be associated with superstition, as pagan worship seems to have practiced the laying on of hands in their rituals, at least according to Hollywood. The truth is that the laying on of hands is quite unique to Holy Scripture. And most depictions of pagan groups laying hands upon a person is actually taken from Holy Scripture And the first thing we need to know about the laying on of hands is its relation to the third foundation stone, which you recall is the doctrine of baptisms preached about last week. I mentioned a few weeks ago about the presence of parallelisms found in these foundation stones. Whereas repentance from dead works communicates something similar to faith toward God, and thus is a parallelism. So does the doctrine of baptisms communicate something about the laying on of hands as a parallelism? And we see this more clearly in the book of Acts, where people are baptized in water and then have hands laid upon them so as to be baptized in the Holy Spirit. As rituals in the church became more structured, the rite of baptism became associated with the laying on of hands. At first by the sign of the cross being placed on the forehead for a person recently baptized, and next the laying on of hands over the head of a person With the prayer that the Holy Spirit might dwell in the heart of the newly baptized. And later still, when the church instituted the ritual of confirmation. which was the affirming of a person's earlier baptism, hands were laid upon those being confirmed in order to seal Their baptismal vows. Thus the early Christians knew the relationship of baptism and the laying on of hands. They went together. And so the laying on of hands is a foundation stone related to the doctrine of baptism, or baptisms. But it's even more than that. Throughout the Holy Scripture, both the Old and New Testament Tell of the laying on of hands as a weighty symbol. A weighty symbol that passed along blessings Passed along miracles, wholly separated persons to service, and imparted gifts of the Holy Spirit. In regards to blessings, we recall Jacob, the patriarch, laying hands upon Joseph's children, blessing them, and prophesying over them. It was the high priest who was instructed by God to raise his hands over the people and bless them. And Jesus, of course, as we read, took children in his arms, and it says, put his hands on them and bless them. And then, interestingly to me, Jesus takes on this position as a high priest. At the end of the Gospel of Luke, before he ascends, the scripture says that he laid his hands upon those who followed him and blessed them. We are also aware of the many times that Jesus placed his hands upon those in need of a miracle. He laid his hands upon the deaf, the blind, and those with various diseases, and he healed them all. Thus far, then, the laying out of hands is used in Holy Scripture to impart something good from one person to another. And it it is a physical act. As a physical act, it is acknowledging that the physical world that God created is just as important As the spiritual world. Because the laying out of hands involves one human being touching another human being. For something good to occur, a blessing from God or a healing, God is using that physical touch, transferring his grace, a means of grace. And we are to conclude that the physical world is a means by which God communicates his gospel. You might anticipate from my sermons past where I'm going to go with my next point Once again, we have the opportunity to understand the physical world as important and necessary. As God has chosen it to be used to save sinners and to redeem his creation. It is then necessary for me to bring up the subject of the heresy of Gnosticism. Recall that Gnosticism is the belief that the spiritual world is the most important, and that that means the physical world is less important, or maybe even not important at all. Historic and modern-day Gnostics either deny the pleasures of the flesh or indulge in pleasures of the flesh, for to them the flesh is meaningless. According to them, the flesh, the physical world doesn't matter. Only the spirit of a person and the spiritual world has eternal value, according to the Gnostics. Now I remind you that Gnosticism is a heresy because it denies what God said about his creation at the time of creation when he looked upon it and said It is good. Gnosticism also blasphemes the Savior, Jesus, who took on human flesh, making himself a man. And remaining a man, a physical man, even to this day. Gnosticism Also does not understand the future salvation promised by God, who said that there will be a new heaven and a new earth, a new physical earth that is fully redeemed Just as the souls of the chosen of mankind will be fully redeemed. God wants to redeem the physical world. But Gnosticism is a sneaky heresy. It is a sneaky heresy because it is not so obvious. Consider. Consider a couple makes a seemingly innocent decision to get married in the open, such as in a park or at the beach. Why get married outside of the church building? Is it because the church building doesn't matter? Is it because God is spirit and he can be anywhere and thus he doesn't need to be represented by a church building? If the answer is yes, then please understand that such thinking is a form of Gnosticism. Think differently by understanding a church building as a covering, as a physical covering that represents God's people and the protection provided by God's people. Which is the church. The church has been referred to as an ark for Christians. An ark like Noah's Ark. And that is why the central part of the church building that you're sitting in now is known as the nave, coming from the Latin word navis, which literally means ship. God's people are to consider themselves in a ship that is sailing to the heavenly shore while the world drowns in sin around them. To be saved, a Christian must be within the ship, within the nave. I realized by using This example, I may be alienating some of you who were married outdoors. I am not questioning the validity of your marriage or your marital vows I'm simply pointing out that we can think like a Gnostic without realizing it. Now consider another example. What do you do with Bibles that are torn, worn, and have bindings that no longer hold the pages together? Are such Bibles to be simply tossed in the nearest garbage can? Perhaps for some reasons our consciences cannot explain we are uncomfortable tossing a Bible into a garbage can. And what is it that stops our conscience? Perhaps it is the Holy Spirit telling us that what was specifically set aside by God to be used by God, a Bible, is not something that you physically mistreat. Such would be a conviction against Gnosticism. On a side note, um For our conscious sake, Christians have either burned old Bibles in a ceremony or buried them as symbolic seed. Well, consider this next example. You are in charge of the sacristry on a particular Sunday The service is over, and you come upon the Holy Communion plate, and there is bread left over, and there is wine left over in the cup. Is it natural and without any prick of your conscience to throw the bread into the garbage and to dump the wine down the sink? For a person of faith, such would not be natural, because you had just witnessed The minister of the gospel pray, prayers of consecration over that same bread and wine. You saw people receiving that bread and that wine with faith in their hearts and eating with Jesus until he comes again waiting for him. The people eat and drink with faith, that the bread and the wine are a means of grace to them. How they are a means of grace is unknown. We don't say. We don't try to explain the value of the bread that is broken in the name of Jesus, or the effectiveness of the wine that is poured out in the name of Jesus. For we see them as holy mysteries and rest in such mysteries. What we do know is that it is not a mystery if that bread is thrown out and treated like a mere snack, and the wine poured down like any other beverage. Our understanding of the dangers of Gnosticism may not be keen, but we know that leftover consecrated bread and wine should be treated differently. That is why the extra is consumed or ceremonially poured out to the birds of the air and to the ground from which man came. What I am arguing is that the people of God, the people in which the Holy Spirit dwells, when they stop and consider, inherently know the dangers of Gnosticism. Such examples lead us to the next purpose in Holy Scripture about the imposition of hands. The next purpose is for the setting aside or separating something for a holy purpose. The blessing of the bread and the wine at Holy Communion are the first obvious example. The first furnishings used in the tabernacle of Moses, such as the offering table and the utensils. The Ark of the Covenant, the lampstand and its utensils, the altar for incense and the altar for burnt offerings. We're all to be consecrated, set aside, hands laid upon them for a holy use And so the church does the same today as it sets aside holy places in this sanctuary. Sanctuary, literally meaning holy place. And we set aside all the utensils in the sanctuary. Hands have been laid upon our lectionary for it to be used to read God's Word. Hands have been laid upon this pulpit, so it is used to preach God's word. Hands have been laid upon the communion table, so that it is set aside to be used as a holy furnishing to bless the bread. and the why. Thus we don't use the lectionary to read a false script. We don't use the pulpit to proclaim a lie or fables. And we don't use the Lord's table to open a bag to lunch and to rest our soda. For people who have faith in Jesus, Jesus who became flesh. Who took on the form of this world, we know instinctively that such places and such furnishings are for holy use. It is unnatural to our consciences to desecrate them and to desecrate them Is to take them as simply something in which we don't abide or revere just like any other furnishing to be used for our personal use But setting aside things for God's holy use goes beyond buildings and furnishings by the laying on of hands. In the Old Testament, hands were imposed on sacrificial animals in order to set them apart for special use. Also the Levites had hands laid upon them during a ceremony of consecrating them for service in the Holy Temple. Even Moses laid hands upon Joshua during a ritual that designated Joshua as the successor of Moses. And such actions set the precedent for Christian leaders to lay hands upon church leaders so that they might be consecrated, set aside for God's holy use. Remember in the book of Acts, we read first of the six deacons that had hands laid upon them, consecrating them for their office as church leaders. Saul and Barnabas had hands laid upon them to separate them for the task of groundbreaking missionary work. And we can safely read into St. Paul's instruction, read this morning, for Timothy not to lay hands on any man suddenly. That the laying on of hands was a practice done by church leaders to separate and specifically anoint men to church ministry. St. Timothy was warned to not to anoint a man to serve in the church who had not been carefully examined in order to assure that the leadership that is passed on to such men that their character would not shame the gospel. Now I need to stay on this point, of using the laying on of hands for the purpose of ordaining ministers. For I lament that the right of ordination is not taken seriously enough in the church today. It is not taken seriously enough by laity and by clergy. Of course, I'm speaking in generalities, I don't have individuals in mind. I believe it is important that every man who pursues to formally serve the church in the office of deacon or of presbyter To do his best to be part of apostolic succession. For those who are not familiar with the term apostolic succession, please know. That it is a belief that the authority and responsibility of the formal church offices are in line with the same offices commissioned by the apostles. If I see myself in apostolic succession, the hope is that the bishop who ordained me was ordained himself by someone, who was ordained himself by someone, who was ordained himself by someone that is part of the chain, the succession that goes all the way back to the apostles. This is the hold that the laying on of hands is a continuation of the laying on of hands that started with the apostles. Now, admittedly, such seems rather difficult because there have been so many divisions within the church, and it would thus seem hard to document such succession. But the Roman Catholic Church has documentation they believe leads back to the laying on of hands of the apostles. And the Church of England has records that although break off from the Roman Church, they actually can chart The continuation of bishops through Cranmer and others who were consecrated in the Church of Rome. And so the Reformed Episcopal Church can do the same As we have charts that show a continuation of the American Episcopal Church, which was a continuation of the Church of England, which was a continuation of the Church of Rome in England Which was a continuation of the first century church where the gospel was first brought to the British Islands by none other than Joseph of Arimathea. Beloved, if the laying on of hands is a foundation stone for Christians, and if the laying on of hands was the practice of the apostles to ordain men to the ministry, It then should matter to clergy and laity that we do our due diligence to be a part of a succession of the laying out of hands. That is a chain of hands that leads to the apostles, that leads to those who are anointed by the Savior Himself. Now as I say this, I am making no determination on the legitimacy or illegitimacy of the ordination of men who cannot trace themselves back to the apostles. There are many men within many other branches of Christ's church that display gifts that I could only pray to ever have. I only state that it is within the responsibility of every man who pursues holy orders to get in line with the laying on of hands. If the laying on of hands is a foundation stone, it seems, from this minister's vantage point, that such is the least a man can do who wishes to be anointed to preach the gospel. It is the least to be done. But all of us, all of us need the laying on of hands. All of us need the cooties of the Lord. offered by way of laying on of hands, whether it be at baptism, at confirmation. Healings, blessings, ordinations. All of us need hands God's hands laid upon us. Laid upon us until he comes again. Let us pray.

sermons.title: Resurrection of the Body
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In name of the Father and of the Son. And of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. Remind you as we begin that we're continuing our series, our summer series on the foundation stones of our faith as listed in Hebrews chapter six, verses one through three I believe the word obsession doesn't seem to be a word that expresses well enough how important our bodies are to us. According to Market Data Enterprises, Americans spend over $60 billion a year on gym memberships and weight loss programs. Billion. Sixty billion with a B. A survey out in April of this year revealed that the average American woman spends three hundred hundred thousand dollars on cosmetic products in her lifetime And we can add to those numbers $60 billion in 206-16 spent on cosmetic plastic surgery. And we can add to those numbers the amount of people who pursue the pleasures of the flesh through pornography, and those who overindulge the flesh in food. And we have the evidence for more than an obsession that people have about their bodies But the body is good, isn't it? That was the conclusion we were to draw from our anti-gnostic point made last week. God said our bodies are good at creation. Jesus became like us, which is to say, he took on the flesh like ours, and he remains in the flesh. The body of each human is good, insofar as they are what God created out of the dust of the earth. Our bodies are good because God chooses the Holy Spirit to dwell in us, which is to dwell in our bodies. But obsessions regarding the bodies are not just unwise, they are sinful. Obsessions with the body are sinful because they become an idol to us. Our weight gain and figure shape can be so important to us that such becomes an idol that we bow down to and serve, and thus it is sin to us. Just being preoccupied with how other people look upon your physique can be sin to us when it becomes too important to us. Our flesh can be so important to us in other ways, such as wanting to feed its appetites So that we bow down to sex or alcohol or drugs or food, and thus such becomes sin to us. Thou shalt have no other gods before me. We confess that today. And that includes obsessions or sins of the flesh. And yet, and yet God plans to redeem the flesh, our flesh. In fact The fifth foundation stone in Hebrews chapter six, the resurrection of the body. Whereas the laying out of hands was not so readily understandable to us as a foundation stone for our Christian faith, the resurrection of the body should be more evident to us as to why it's important. It is important to the Christian faith because it started with Jesus being raised from the dead If Jesus was not raised from the dead, St. Paul tells us that the rest of our faith, well, it's in vain. The Christian faith would have no substance to it if Jesus be not raised from the dead. If Jesus is not raised from the dead, our sins are still in the grave along with his body. And you and I are wasting our time right here and right now. Believing in the resurrection of Jesus and the proclamation of the resurrection of Jesus is what it is to be a Christian. That's why it's a foundation stone. After all, it's part of our creeds We confess that we believe in the resurrection of the body, the first body being that of Jesus, and afterward all bodies Will be resurrected. Some having new bodies that will live for eternity, and others who will receive bodies that will suffer for eternity. So, let us examine some of the basics of what it means to say I believe in the resurrect or the resurrection of the body. Yes, because of the resurrection of the body, we will have physical bodies raised. In whatever condition they are, they will be raised. Our souls will be reunited with our transformed physical bodies, brought back to life from the dead. And Scripture teaches this in many different ways. So first, simply to speak of a resurrection of the dead as Matthew 22, Luke 14, 1 Corinthians 15 as read today. This is implying physicality. That is what the resurrection is. And this again speaks against that sneaky heresy Gnosticism. The Bible does not have a category for a concept of a resurrected body remaining physically in the grave. And there is clear evidence that what God intended for mankind in the Garden of Eden is going to be fulfilled in the new heaven and the new earth. That's where redeemed bodies will live. Paradise. Second, Philippians chapter 3 teaches us that the resurrected body of Jesus Is the pattern for our resurrected bodies. St. Paul wrote this: for our citizenship is in heaven from which also we eagerly wait for a Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ, who will transform the body of our humble state into the conformity of the body of His glory. But what type of body did Jesus have? Well we know that Christ was raised in a physical body because the disciples ate with him after the resurrection Also, Jesus outright declared that his resurrected body was physical and it was touchable. Remember, he said, see my hands and my feet, that is myself, touch me and see. For a spirit does not have flesh and bones, as you see that I have, Jesus said to his disciples. And since Christ's resurrection is the pattern for our resurrection, we will therefore be raised with physical bodies. Third, Romans chapter eight speaks of waiting for the redemption of our bodies. Our bodies are not going to be thrown away. They are going to be renewed, revitalized, restored. And you may think that what you have is not worth saving, but God, who made Adam from the dust, can take what is dusty about you and your body and make it last for eternity. That is what we believe when we say, I believe in the resurrection of the body, my body. Fourth, Jesus speaks of the resurrection as involving the coming forth of individuals out of their tombs. Which is clearly indicating a physical resurrection. Jesus said, do not marvel at this For an hour is coming in which all who are in the tombs will hear his voice and will come forth those who did the good deeds to the resurrection of life, and those who committed evil deeds to the resurrection of judgment. Fifth, even the Old Testament speaks of the resurrection as being physical. In Daniel we hear, and many of those who sleep in the dust of the ground will awake, these to everlasting life, but others to disgrace and everlasting contempt. Likewise we read in the book of Job, I know that my Redeemer lives, and at the last he will take his stand on the earth. Even after my skin is destroyed, yet from my flesh shall I see God, whom I myself shall behold, and whom my eyes shall see, and not another. My heart faiths within me. And so our resurrection is physical But let us discuss the considerations Christians should think upon because of the resurrection of the body. Because of the resurrection of the body, we should think well about our physical bodies. Not as we recently heard, where the physical body is an idol. People today are working for preservation of their bodies, not the resurrection of their bodies. Instead, we need to think well of God as he said what was good, and that is thinking well of our bodies. We have all heard the story of the great marathoner who went out for his daily run only to return, have a heart attack, and die. Now we remind ourselves of such stories to help us realize that an obsession with exercise can't prevent our bodies from getting old and from dying. But such stories should not convince us not to exercise. We should strive to be healthy as long as possible. And it is true that our bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit. God chooses to abide in our bodies. And it should not matter how saggy and old our bodies get. We should still honor the presence of the Holy Spirit and the humility of God taking upon himself to dwell in us. We should care for our physical bodies all of our days. Another consideration and one that is I know controversial Is how we treat our human bodies after we die. I have been asked on numerous occasions whether it is right or wrong for a Christian to be cremated. And when I am asked such questions, it is usually followed by some sort of statement that gives examples of People who have had their bodies blown up or burned alive or buried at sea. And it seems that there's no chance that that body could come back together at the resurrection Those examples are seemingly used to say that it is then acceptable for Christians to be cremated. Well, what I want us to contemplate first on this issue, when we consider the subject of the morality of cremation. Is that such topics do not have to be put in moral categories, which is to say that we don't have to think about such topics in terms of right or wrong, good or bad. The scriptures have a whole section of wisdom literature that is to help God's people make decisions and understand complex topics in terms of wise. and unwise, not right or wrong. If you want to argue with God that cremation is perfectly acceptable because of the violent death of others, well That's what you will do. Unfortunately, many people decide to be cremated or to cremate a loved one based on convenience and cost and nothing more. For them, the wisdom is that money for a grave in a casket is a waste. But Christians are to be about more than what is cheapest and what is practical. Christians are to consider all aspects of their faith, even the witness that they have to the world after they die. If a person who wishes to be cremated desires to witness to the world that he is originally from dust and to dust he shall return, and in this case rather quickly, then that is what is going to be his last testimony But there is another testimony that says that the body God has given me, he has said he will raise from the dead. And so I will have my body lowered into the ground as a testimony that God will one day raise it up and make it brand new. Having presided over a fair share of funerals and memorials, I have noticed that there is a great witness missing. When the casket is not there to lower into the ground. And even when there is a casket, the actual burial is usually hidden from the family. They all say their goodbyes to their loved one in the casket, and that will be lowered after everyone leaves, lowered by the cemetery workers. And I believe there is something missing, a great power of emotion that could stay with us and be meaningful for us. If we were to witness the casket being lowered into the ground and covered with dirt. Because when we see such an event, we are faced with what could be life-changing emotions. We are faced with life-changing images. We are faced first with our own mortality. And that mortality is no more real than when it is a loved one who is in that gasket being lowered into the ground. And when the dirt is dumped on the same coffin, we are faced with the proclamation that one day that body will be raised from the dead either to eternal life or eternal death. And I ask you rhetorically, what other times in our lives are we faced with such important realities? What other times? That in no way does the Bible state that God's love for us and his forgiveness offered to us through Jesus is determined by whether we are cremated or buried. That's ridiculous. That being said, there is a witness in how the Christian treats his or her body. In response to the foundation stone of the resurrection of the body. And there is also a testimony that needs to be stated of the historic church. To consider when we decide whether or not to cremate a Christian body. The rise of Christianity in the Roman world. saw an end to the practice of cremation of the dead. While earlier, most pagan religions not only practiced cremation, but prescribed it as an important ritual. For Christians, both in the East and the West, Christian burial was a continuation of Jewish practices that believed that the body would be resurrected. And therefore, the integrity of the body was to be respected. The church, both in the east and the west, placed The burning of the body in the same category as abortion, drug use, and any form of body desecration Cremation is still outlawed according to church law of Eastern Orthodoxy. And it was outlawed in Europe because of Christian tradition until the end of the 19th century. And it was not until 1963, under Vatican II, that the Roman Catholic Church lifted a ban on creation. I mean on cremation. In summary, the Christian Church Universal has recognized the importance of honoring the body. Now I close this sermon on the foundation stone of the resurrection of the body by addressing a childlike question that all of us have asked, all of us. What are our resurrected bodies going to be like? We naturally want to know if we will be recognizable and will we be able to recognize others We want to know that what age we will be at the resurrection, or if age will be a concept at all We might want to know what our new bodies will be capable of doing, or what limitations they might have, if any. Well, from Holy Scripture, we can answer parts of these curiosities. We can affirm from the resurrected body of Jesus that again we will have physical bodies. We learn from St. Paul in his letter to the Corinthians, read this morning, that our bodies will be incorruptible, which means they will not age and they will not die. We know from the story of Moses and Elijah appearing in transfigured form, as this is Transfiguration Sunday. Moses and Elijah appearing in transfigured form before Jesus and the apostles, that there will be some type of recognition You ever wonder how they knew it was Elijah and Moses? I don't know. But some sort of recognition will be available to us. Remember that the men on the road to Emmaus, they didn't recognize Jesus was right there with them, with them until they partook of eating with him. But they did eventually recognize him. And we can expect our bodies to have an extra-dimensional quality. That was exemplified by Moses and Elijah being transfigured. And exemplified by Jesus walking into a room with doors and windows shut. And by Jesus being taken up by way of the clouds. And really, the only other thing that we can know about our bodies Is that they will not suffer pain, will not suffer illness, no tears will be shed, and sin will reign no more. Aside from what has been just described, the Holy Scriptures don't provide details. But what the Bible provides is enough for us to rejoice in the hope. That we have of a new resurrected body. And as a side note, just to solve a pet peeve of mine Let us once again put to bed the idea that we are going to be angels. We are not going to be angels. And no saint of God who has gone before us, who has been received by Jesus, is an angel. We shouldn't want to be angels. We should want to be children of God, created in his image, inheritors of his kingdom. As God's adopted children, our promised reward is the resurrection of our bodies, and for our bodies to dwell in paradise. The angels actually want to be like us. And so let us hear the confession again. I believe in the resurrection of the body. Let us pray.

sermons.title: Eternal Judgment
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: And of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. Before I get into the topic this morning, I hope to get a couple of amens from you. Considering the events that occurred in Charlottesville yesterday It should be heard from this pulpit and believed by everyone who confesses Jesus as Savior and Lord. That racism is abhorrent to the gospel. Amen. Let it also be said But the only hope for the hearts of men not to be racist, not to think of themselves as better than another made in God's image. The only answer is the gospel. Amen. Last week, excuse me, we looked at the fifth foundation stone for our summer series. From Hebrews chapter 6. And I'm recognizing a parallelism for today from that which was discussed last week We talked about the fifth foundation stone being the resurrection of our bodies. And now we come upon the sixth and final foundation stone. Which is what our bodies are resurrected to do, which is at first to go through eternal judgment. Eternal judgment is the sixth foundation stone. Eternal judgment is the decision time for all of mankind, all of man who ever lived. It is a time in which Jesus gathers all human beings together and then separates them He will separate humanity as the Bible describes, which is like separating the sheep from the goats or the wheat from the tares. The sheep or wheat will be rewarded with heaven, and the goats or tares will be condemned to eternal punishment. Excuse me. This is going to be a rough one. The uh Farside comic strip was one of my favorites, and I am sorry that its creator, Gary Larson, stopped writing them. But I remembered two of them while preparing this sermon. The two were about hell The first depicts a large man with devil horns, all dressed in a red robe, holding a pitchfork to the back of a man, average height, average weight. When the man is standing facing two doors, the devil creature says to the man, come on, come on, it's either one or the other. And the door on the left reads, Damned if you do, and the door on the right reads, Damned if you don't The second comic is a depiction of a number of people waiting in line to be checked into hell. The caption reads, Nerds in Hell. And a character in a comic is a nerdy-looking guy turning around to the guy behind him and asking, is it hot enough for ya? Well, I didn't expect much of a laugh on that. These descriptions are obviously meant to be physically viewed. But the second one always makes me chuckle because I know guys like that. And I know guys who will say nerdy things in awkward moments. But the point of these examples is that for an unbelieving world, hell is not a real place. Instead, it is a concept to make fun of, or to laugh at, or to treat in a glib manner, as an extension of how all Christian beliefs are treated by the unbelieving world. And Christians can get sucked into treating such a place in a glib manner Now I'm not suggesting that we shouldn't laugh at jokes and comic strips and poke fun that poke fun of hell when the subject is objectively funny God gives Christians freedom, and part of that freedom is to laugh, to laugh at those things that are genuinely comical But hell as a place in the end is a very serious reality. But even as a reality, respectable people don't like the subject of hell at all. As they struggle to connect their knowledge of God's love and the idea that there is a place made. So that the devil and his angels and all sinners can be tortured there forever The great Christian writer and thinker C. S. Lewis said the following about hell from his book, The Problem of Pain. Quote, there is no doctrine which I would more willingly remove from Christianity than this, if it lay in my power But it has the full support of Scripture, and especially of the Lord's own words. It has always been held by Christendom, and it has the support of reason. End quote Lewis, like most of us, would prefer that sinners be annihilated and thus no longer have an existence instead of eternal torture. But such is simply not possible. Consider how could a human being made in God's image no longer have an existence? The spirit of every human being has an everlasting quality that cannot be extinguished And we know this because we have memories of one another, and those memories are where our spirits meet with other people's spirits, even those no longer with us. And besides, as Lewis points out, Scripture is very clear about the existence of hell. In Scripture, Jesus speaks extensively about the place of hell. In Matthew chapter 10, verse 28, Jesus spoke of the body and soul being destroyed in hell. In Matthew thirteen, Jesus describes the end judgment of angels, gathering up all who practice lawlessness and throwing them into the fire, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth. In Mark 9, Jesus uses the following phrase to describe hell. He uses the phrase three times. He says, it is a place where their worm does not die, and the fire is not quenched. And then in Matthew 25, where Jesus is describing that separation of the sheep and the goats, he plainly states that the goats will go the way of eternal punishment. And then, of course, the book of Revelation also clearly defines hell as a place of eternal punishment. In Revelation chapter 20, we read that Satan, the Antichrist, false prophets, and all people who followed them will be cast into the lake of fire. Where they will be tormented night, day and night, forever and ever. Hell, beloved, is real And it is indeed serious. But what gets people to hell? C. S. Lewis said, quote, there are only two kinds of people in the end. Those who say to God, Thy will be done. And those to whom God says, Thy will be done. It is a clever way to understand the judgment of God, but it is not accurate. It communicates that people in hell have a choice. Remember the story of Jesus told of Lazarus. Lazarus and the rich ruler. The rich man was in hell, but he didn't want to be in hell. But his life on earth determined that hell would be his eternal home. So people who go to hell don't truly get what they want. After all, they have believed lies all of their lives They have been led astray by those lies. Those lies have tricked them into thinking that they didn't have to answer to anyone in the end. And only in the end will the truth have to be accepted. And what is so interesting now about the parable of the sheep and the goats is how Jesus describes the identity of the sheep and the goats. That it is determined by what they did and did not do in this life. It would seem that such a determining factor would be the opposite Of what the gospel means. The gospel, after all, is what Jesus died for our sins We're just to say that he died for what we failed to do in obeying his law. And what we did do in breaking his law. The gospel says we are forgiven and saved from hell by the works of Jesus, not by our own. But the parable of the sheep and the goats compares the sheep caring for the least of humanity in this life, while the goats cared not at all for the least of humanity. And the difference between the sheep and the goats then is what they did in this life and didn't do in this life. So how does this parable match up with the gospel? Well it matches up cleanly when the context of the parable of the sheep and the goats is taken within the concept of the gospel in its entirety. God's people, the sheep, having been forgiven and made God's children. Behave as God's children by caring for the least of humanity, just as Jesus did. The actions of the sheep reveal that they are sheep, and the actions of the ghosts reveal that they are goats. Within the parable, we learn that good works are not what saves anyone, but the sheep did not even know that they were doing good works that pleased God. They did not know because they didn't do it to earn God's favor. It was what was natural to them. Good works of caring for the least of humanity is not something God's people tout about, but what they naturally do. Now another type of person that is destined for hell are perhaps the scariest for the Christian. For they are people who confess some type of faith in Jesus, but in truth, it's no saving faith at all. Be reminded these words from Jesus. Not everyone who says to me, Lord, Lord, will enter the kingdom of heaven. But the one who does the will of my Father who is in heaven. On that day many will say, Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in your name, cast out demons in your name, and do many mighty works in your name? And then I will declare to them, I never knew you. Depart from me, you workers of lawlessness. And notice again how the works of a person matches his or her faith or non-faith. And people who use the name of Jesus as a prop for personal gain are prime examples of people whom Jesus will say, I never knew you. Now I started with the topic of hell in reference to eternal judgment because I wanted to finish with the good stuff. But note, please, a bad habit that we can have when we mention eternal judgment. We only think of condemnation in hell. Eternal judgment, hell. Perhaps it is actually a good sign that we do so, because we readily know our personal guilt. But the mention of eternal judgment for the Christian is to conjure up A fear of hell and a hope of heaven. Heaven promised. When I was searching For a call in my life, just out of college, I started working for the church that we were attending as an outreach minister to college students. I think I wanted to be an ordained minister, but I was not yet confident that I should be. The pastor thought I had necessary gifts, so he hired me to work with college students. Well, after a particular service where the minister gave a stirring sermon that demanded an altar call, those of you who have baptistic backgrounds know what that is. People are asked to come forward and be prayed for to receive Jesus as their Savior or to confess sin. Well, a particular female college student that I had not yet met walked down the aisle and knelt for prayer. I followed her and I knelt next to her and I asked her what she would like prayer for. She said that she didn't know And so I thought I'd take advantage of this exchange, and I asked her, Do you want to go to heaven? And her response, her faithful facial expression, I can clearly see in my mind. She pinched her eyebrows together and she said, why would I want to go to heaven? I had never had anybody ask that question to me before. And I thought the answer was self-explanatory, but in truth the only answer I had was better than going to hell. Having read the Bible through a few times since then, I can now answer the question better. Heaven will be a glorious feast for our senses, as we will witness the glory of God in the eyes of the resurrected Jesus. And there will be streets of gold, and our dwelling place will be a city built with costly stones and crystal clear jasper. Our dwelling homes will be places fit for sons and daughters of the Most High God. And in heaven we will know it also for what it does not have. As there will be no tears, and no reason for tears, for there will be no pain, no sorrow. All will be done away with. They will be done away with because sin and death will be thrown into that lake of fire, along with the devil and his angels. Now for that young woman, I suppose the latter part of my description of her needing there to be no more guilt. Would have been a good answer for young people struggle with a great deal of sin. To know that in heaven sin is vanquished And that all pain that sin causes is thrown out, that certainly is a great appeal to a guilty conscience. Yes, heaven will be a wonderful place for the reasons already stated and certainly more. But heaven is a problem in our culture in the same manner that hell is a problem. Heaven is treated in our culture as glibly as hell is treated. There are too many jokes and comics about heaven, Saint Peter at the gate asking different questions and different doors with different rooms with different groups in heaven And well, it's all there to distract us from treating heaven as a real place that will fulfill all the promises of Holy Scripture. And then there is the depiction of heaven in the book of Revelation. Remember at the beginning of that book, it depicts heaven in a manner that does not appeal to modern man. It describes angels chanting holy, holy, holy over and over again It describes elders of the faith surrounding the throne of Jesus, bowing down, throwing down their crowns, bowing down, throwing down their crowns. And in fact, for some it all sounds quite boring Some Christians fear that heaven is going to be like a church service over and over again. And most people barely make it through a church service and are quite glad that you only have to come here once a week. And even though some don't attend but once a week, they get excited to go on vacation because they think they can take a vacation from attending church. And even when they attend church services, they get so bored of the singing and of the praying they don't sing much anymore and their mind wanders when we pray. With such an attitude towards church services, they multiply it a hundred times and conclude that that's what heaven's going to be like. And if so, well, maybe hell will have better parties. After all, hell is where most rock and roll musicians are going, thus they'll probably have better parties And if you're offended about rock and roll, I'll really care. Um And if you think I'm exaggerating about this type of thinking, consider why many evangelical churches have chosen to present to the congregation a rock concert In substitute for corporate singing. Such churches fear boring people Some even have light shows along with their rock concert and pastors in jeans so that the congregation or audience won't be bored. Where such church leaders fail when they work to not bore their audience is to understand that boredom is a product of sin. Where there is sin, there is death. And death is the only enemy, is only an enemy when time is a factor. And the Bible teaches us that when heaven is populated with God's people, death will be vanquished. Time is no more necessary. And thus no possibility for boredom. To capitulate to boredom, then is to capitulate to sin. And thus another great quality of liturgical worship is that it calls the believer to resist the temptations of the flesh that lead to boredom. As it calls God's people to serve in a manner with which God is pleased, rather than the audience being pleased. But I digress just a little. Just like we ask how people get to hell, we must also ask how people get to heaven. And you know the answer, but it is always worth repeating. By the grace of God, through Jesus the Savior, is how people get to heaven. But what about the good works of the sheep? Again, those good works are what the sheep do automatically do because their sins have been forgiven and Jesus has set them free On the day of judgment, when all of mankind have reformed bodies and are placed before God. Every knee is going to bow in acknowledgement and honor of Jesus being the Savior and King of the world. Some knees will bow willingly and humbly, while the rest will be forced. Many are called, but few are chosen. Many will be forced to bow, while few will bow automatically. On the day of judgment, justice, eternal justice, will be heard and served. Should that scare you? Well, only if you don't know Jesus as Savior and Lord. And yes, the Holy Spirit uses fright to get us right. To get us right, to meet our Maker. But it need not scare us if Jesus is our Savior and our lives are lived according to him as our Savior. And so there you have it. The sixth foundation stone is laid. What did the writer of Hebrews say? Let us lay these six foundation stones that we might go on to perfection. Let us pray. Gracious and merciful Lord, we thank you for judgment day. For the hope that it gives us as Christians, as believers in your Son. Father, may we always check our lives to be sure we line up with the sheep Line up with the wheat. And Father, may that day come, and may you be glorified forever and ever. Amen.

sermons.title: Fathers of our Heritage
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Having finished our study of the six foundation stones of the Christian faith As listed in Hebrews chapter 6. I now turn us to burdens that God has laid upon my heart I know that such burdens are subjective, but I hope to convince you that they are what God would have us hear. The general burden God laid upon my heart is the importance of fatherhood. This burden is in regards to fatherhood in families, yes, but also the fatherhood of our heritage and the fatherhood of our God. The burn has grown in me of late because of how I see our culture being challenged about the fathers of our past, the fathers of this nation. And their legacies, marked by monuments. When I first started writing this sermon On Monday, the public discussion was about one monument. What has transpired since has been in the blink of an eye. It has escalated quickly. Besides monuments, the burden regarding fathers has been growing in me because in my readings of late I have become convinced That every problem we have in this life, whether it is besetting sins, psychological weaknesses, or relational problems, all of them have an origin in our need. For our Heavenly Father. Finally, the burden has grown in me because I wonder if men, as fathers of children today appreciate the powerful influence they have upon the family as a whole, and appreciate the power so much that they are careful when to use it and when not to use it to the glory of God and to the salvation of their family, which are not mutually exclusive. And I begin with what I am burdened about by looking at the topic of taking down and even destroying monuments that are in honor of men, our patriotic fathers. who contributed to the founding of this nation or who participated in important historical events of our nation, but who also have sinful flaws that are publicly known. Allow me to rehearse the facts as I understand them. The clashes that occurred in Charlottesville, Virginia last week started because of a plan For the city government to remove a statue memorializing Robert E. Lee, the most prominent leader of the Confederate States from the Civil War Discussions for the removal of the statue started in two thousand twelve with the basic premise that Honoring a Confederate soldier who fought for the South during the Civil War makes citizens, certain citizens, uncomfortable as they find it offensive. They find it offensive because their historical understanding is that the Civil War was a war about slavery and only slavery. And those who fought for the South were in favor of slavery. And those who fought for the North were against slavery. A true educated person would recognize that such a summary of the Civil War is woefully inaccurate and more propaganda than history. But such is the product of modern public education Consider with me, if we were to follow this approach to monuments, memorials, and remembrances that honor our founding fathers Where it would end up if we were to consistently apply it. A consistent application of such an approach To do away with any monument, memorial, or remembrance of our founding fathers, of whom had character flaws. Would change the identity of the United States so that it would be unrecognizable to my generation or any generation that came before my own. Most of you know that I was born in Washington State. Washington State is named after, of course, George Washington, the great general of the war for independence. And of course, the first president under our nation's constitution. Did you know? In the entire United States, 31 counties are named after George Washington. So also are 241 townships. along with several cities, city streets and universities. And then there is the Washington Monument at the center of the National Mall the face of our dollar bills, the face of one of the four honored on Mount Rushmore, and the namesake that is our nation's capital. But did you also know George Washington was a slave owner? Of course, you knew that. George was an active slave holder for 56 years and owned as many as 317 slaves on his property at one time. And interestingly, most of the slaves owned by Robert E. Lee were inherited to him through his wife, who was related to George Washington. The point is that if any remembrance, memorial, or monument of Lee is offensive, any such thing that identifies George Washington should be equally offensive. When I started this sermon, writing this sermon, such was not the case, but it is now But what is wrong here? Why have remembrances, memorials, and monuments of certain men become sources of discomfort and offense? I believe the answer lies in our culture's rejection of the gospel If you are tempted to conclude that only a preacher could find such a connection, I ask that you hear me out. The connection between rejecting images of our forefathers and rejecting the gospel can be seen in the content of the gospel. For the gospel story begins with the fall of humanity. Adam, our covenant head, sinning in the garden. It was then passed on through the family of Noah who liked to get drunk and embarrass their father. It was then passed on to Abraham, who himself owned slaves and had more than one wife, and who lied about Sarah being his wife in order to protect himself. It then passed on through Isaac who sinned as his father did. And then to Jacob, who was a liar and a horrible father himself. And the next father was Judah, who slept with his own daughter-in-law when she fooled him into thinking she was a prostitute. Now we could stop there without adding to the lineage from which God brought forth Jesus, a lineage that includes an actual prostitute. And a king who committed adultery and tried to cover it up with murder while having multiple wives and some very godless children. That is the legacy of our fathers of the faith. And yet, and yet We accept the outcome. The outcome who is Jesus. Because of Jesus. Not because of the sins of the fathers. And this type of legacy mapping we should apply to the church as we accept weaknesses of the disciples and sins of the church leaders, both within the church and within politics. Not because of their weaknesses, but because of what God, what Jesus did with them and through them As an Anglican, I can actually find enjoyment talking about the beginnings of the Church of England Starting with a sex-craved king, Henry VIII, who declared himself the head of the Anglican Church After divorcing his wife and having her live in exile so that he could marry a better-looking woman named Anne. But poor Anne couldn't give birth to a boy, so Henry had her head chopped off. Henry had six wives total in his life, and there is a quick poem about their fate. Quote King Henry VIII, to six wives he was wedded. One died, one survived, two divorced, two beheaded. End quote. Well, after recounting the men God chose to bring forth his son into the world, isn't it just like our God to choose such a man, King Henry, to be the father of the Church of England? But our culture doesn't know the gospel in the manner I just described. Where God uses imperfect men to bring forth his plan of salvation. Our culture doesn't know the gospel at all. And so it can cannot take the good and the bad of our patriotic fathers. When people of our days see bad, they only see bad, they cannot see past it. They cannot see around it. They believe that they can purify today by ridding the culture of anything that reminds us of our sins of yesterday, the sins of our fathers. And doing so could not be the more opposite of what God would have his people do. Have you ever considered that Israel is the only nation in the world That keeps the stories of its failings as part of its sacred writings? Have you ever considered Why the New Testament contains stories of Christians failing to live up to the standards Jesus set? It is because by keeping such records we are forever reminded of our fallen human condition, and thus our need for God to save us To deliver us. To understand what is going on around you, around us regarding the erasing of our culture's past You must understand what I have just explained, for it is going to continue. We don't know what to do with the sins of our fathers. And so we pretend they did not exist. And it is the church that is to respond By showing how flaws of the past can be redeeming if we look to the only redeemer. To be embarrassed, hurt, and offended by remembrances, memorials, and monuments of our founding fathers is to be embarrassed, hurt, and offended by who we are. For what they did and what they stood for as part of who we are as a culture and as individuals. And the devil, of course is very happy about all of this, if happiness is what it should be called. He is happy because embarrassment and disagreement and hatred bring about chaos. And the devil loves chaos. He loves disorder. And the easiest and oldest way to bring about disorder is to divide and conquer The oldest strategy in war is to divide and conquer. Armies are easier to defeat when they are smaller. Armies are easier to defeat when they cannot communicate battalion to battalion. The devil knows this. He was the first to use it. Notice in the book of Genesis the story of Eve being deceived, and then Adam. The devil, by way of the body of a serpent, attacked Eve when she was alone. When alone he could confuse her by twisting God's words. When alone he could play on her constitution and understanding instead of as she would have been if she were one with her husband. Also considered that when Cain and Abel came to blows, that Cain and Abel were separated from their parents. There was no one to cause Cain to question his unchained emotions when alone he killed Abel. Divide and conquer. Now I I don't have permission to use a particular child's name, so I won't. But a father of a toddler that I know quite well recently told me that his son has started to use the tactic of crying to his mother when his daddy says no or crying to his daddy when mommy says no. And I conclude from such an anecdotal example that divide and conquer is an inherent strategy within our fallen and sinful natures. Referring back to the events in Charlottesville last week, I read an article that explained that White supremacy, white nationalism, or neo-Nazis are lined up by the secular media to be part of conservative parties of America. In truth, they are alt-right, which is short for alternative right. And these groups have nothing in common with conservatives politically. Or principally. Such groups are fascists, first and last. And as authoritarian nationalists, they work to suppress groups that are not like them. Across from them in Charlottesville were people from Black Lives Matter groups, as well as a group called Antifa. I had never heard of Antifa. Their claim is to be a group that gathers to protest fascists like the white white supremacist. However, this group also aligns itself with socialism and communism, which ironically has its own form of fascism.
