Of the sun standing still, of Samson destroying pillars, of Gideon gathering a small army Of David cutting the head off of a giant. Of Solomon and his wisdom. Of Elijah mocking false prophets. Of Elisha floating an axe head. Of a virgin giving birth, of a man turning water into wine, walking on water. Healing a child, giving sight to the blind, and raising himself from the dead In the book of Revelation, Christians are told to hold on. Hold on to those stories. And holding on takes effort. It takes great effort because the devil and his demons tempt us to relax. Take it easy. Don't worry about knowing the stories or telling the stories. Watch this movie or or or this television show instead. You can watch eight episodes in a row and not realize you've been sitting in front of your television for six hours Or read social media instead. Pay attention to what your neighbor had to eat for dinner last night. He's posted two pictures from different angles. Or pay attention instead to an argument between political opponents who are not listening to each other. Before you know it, an hour has gone by or two. That is much easier than telling stories. And it takes great effort to hold on, because the unbelieving world hates the stories. It mocks them and questions our history and our intelligence. It takes great effort because faith without works is dead. The question was asked two weeks ago as to how we got here. I describe the condition of the church as to how it has accepted the sins of the world without discipline, and how it has accepted the practices of the world without questioning. That is how we got here. And those things are caused by lethargy as well. It takes great effort to discipline sinners in our midst. It is easy, so very easy, to look the other way when a man in the church is unfaithful to his wife. It is easy, so easy to ignore a teenager who is in rebellion against his parents. It is easy, so very easy, to allow a brother in Christ to turn to vices, to cope with life's stresses, and not say anything It is easy, so very easy, to refuse to forgive when a wrong has been done to you and expect the worst of those you do not like. And to gossip about a person you do not understand. On the opposite end It takes great effort to confront the sinner, to confront the teenager in rebellion or a friend who's been turning the vices. It takes great effort to love, as the scripture defines love, for that means you must forgive sins when done to you. You must think the best. And not speak evil of another. What we choose to do regarding such matters, these actions define our name. Hear this from Proverbs chapter 22, verse 1. A good name is more desirable than great riches. The godly understand that. The world sees it differently, of course, and in case of riches, it understands it with a twist. According to the wisdom of the world, great riches is what gives you a good name. Athletes. Believe riches give them a good name when they pump their bodies full of banned substances cheating the process Businessmen believe the riches give you a good name when they take advantage of the least in society, in the media. The media believes the riches give you a good name as they uphold the most salacious among us, and they uphold them because it increases their ratings, and that increases advertisers, which gives them great riches. For the Christian, for the godly, for the righteous, it is not so. A good name is indeed more desirable. A major part of Christianity, the Christian covenant we are under, is what we pass down to the generations that follow us Recall that when St. Peter preached his first sermon on the day of Pentecost, he stated that the promises found in the good news of Jesus were for them and for their children. The promises are expected to be inherited. And in order for them to be inherited, they must be kept and cared for and then purposefully given away. And we don't hear enough about the responsibility of Christians to pass on an inheritance. God, who is our Father, tells us that we who believe are his inheritors And as inheritors, he expects us to leave behind an inheritance like our Heavenly Father does for us. Practically, such a responsibility to leave behind an inheritance includes earthly goods. An unrighteous man stores up goods for himself, earthly goods, that he will not have use of when he is no more. Hear this from Proverbs 13, verse 22. A good man leaves an inheritance to his children's children. This means practically That the national debt we are leaving to our children's children is a sin before God. Believe that A generation must rise up and say, we will sacrifice for the sake of those who follow us, if that national debt will ever be paid. And the verse also means that goods in this life should be passed down, even if they are of minimal value, if just to say to those who follow us that we want God's blessings for you. Of course, the most important inheritance we leave behind will be faith in Jesus. And the most important last name we honor will be Christian. You never truly know the perception that people have about you. You all of us have a perception about ourselves and a perception that we want others to have about us, but you never really know how people are thinking about you So I don't know what all of your perceptions are about my beloved Bobby Lynn. I can say that when it came to raising young children She could be a bulldog. As mentioned, I emphasize to all of my children that being a Jorgensen Was being a Christian witness and slaying dragons. But the most important reputation I wanted them to be concerned about was the name Christian. I repeated to them that their most important identity was to be a follower of Jesus Christ. And it was Bobby Lynn who reminded them of that identity in bulldog-like fashion. For instance, she would remind our children that they were Christian first and last when they were in public and not behaving like Christians. This occurred multiple times in sporting competitions. If she witnessed any of our children get mad at a referee or at an opponent or ignore a coach or be a poor sport. She would stare them down until they got eye contact with her. And she would scrunch up her pretty little face And point her forehead rapidly, touching her forehead. And the children knew what it meant. It meant that at their baptism, they were marked with the sign of the cross. And she was reminding them of that sign and how they were to live up to that sign. I fell in love with her again and again when she would do that. And I believe our marriage is so very strong in part because of how important it was to both of us. To pass on our faith in Jesus to our children. So, what does your name mean? What reputation does your name have amongst outsiders? Does your name resonate with the most holy of names, Jesus the Christ? Are you being careful that your name is written so that you can enter the heavenly promised land? And you know, it's just a list of names It is a list of names that probably when you're reading through the Bible in 90 days or maybe through the year, when you come to that list in Ezra, you probably don't read all of them, right? But it is an important list of names, for it reminds us that there is another list of names that the Bible calls the book of life. And it is important that your own name is on it. But the most important Name to us, passed down from generation to generation, one that you should never bring shame It is Jesus' name. May his name be all of our last name. Let us pray. Our gracious God, we are thankful here for the principle of passing down from generation to generation who we are under your covenant. That we all carry the name of Christ, that we all are Christian. Father, help each parent, grandparent. Help their children and their grandchildren embrace that identity, for we do want our names written in your book of life. Grant it, dear Lord, we pray in Jesus' name. Amen

sermons.title: Priority of Corporate Worship
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. May be seated. I may boast a little bit about that baptism. I still got it. Although I must say, bouncing up and down, I actually ran out of breath. Golly day, getting old. We are in Ezra chapter 3. The reading was from the whole chapter, so we will be covering the whole chapter. Let's begin by imagining. Imagine with me a once great nation. A nation that most of its citizens considered to be a Christian nation. Imagine it being rich in Christian tradition. With its laws and national celebrations respecting and following the Christian calendar. And this went on for generations. Then imagine those in charge of that nation suddenly turning against the Christian religion, making the Christian church an enemy of the state. That is what happened in Russia within less than a year after the Tsar of Russia abdicated his throne in 1917. Next, when a band of militant atheists seized power in Russia, citizens and government officials began looting churches. mocking the Christian religion and Christian believers unmercifully, and even murdering the church's clergy. How events can turn so opposite of what they had been can be traced back to what was done and not done within the Orthodox Church of Russia. The church was unprepared to speak to the political shifts that were taking place. There were philosophical challenges of the day that the clergy were not prepared to address. It was as if Marxism was something only politicians needed to worry about. And the church only recognized its mistake. when it was stripped of any influence. But the church as a whole in Russia had started to break down long before 1917, starting with the local churches. By the end of the 19th century, nihilists and radical populists had started to influence the people of the countryside. The influence was partly due to the average village priest, who was usually a peasant himself, being poorly educated and sometimes morally corrupt. The local people did not revere their pastor, but merely saw him as an equal, if not their inferior. Weekly services were poorly done in the Slavic language, which most people could barely understand, and the sermons. The sermons had no intellectual satisfaction Initially, when Marxism started to take root in Russia, many Christians, many Christians welcomed it, thinking that it was compatible to their faith. In truth. In truth, leaders such as Lenin understood Christianity to be the primary enemy of the state. The state that he wished to establish. So the Orthodox Church became a target for destruction. As of today, although the current Russian leader is trying to ban evangelism in Russia, The Russian church is making somewhat of an impressive comeback. It has started to bring its cathedrals back to their original beauty. And there has been a resurgence of Russian Orthodox Christians returning to their faith, but not necessarily to the church. The Russian Orthodox Church is the most modern example I could come up with that resembles what we read about in Ezra chapter 3. Let us look at what brought about these events in Ezra chapter 3 in outline form. Remember that Israel egregiously sinned before God, causing God, forcing his hand. to have to fulfill his warning that they would be overrun by a foreign nation and be taken into captivity. That warning and promise was all the way back in Deuteronomy Babylon was used to fulfill that warning, and then Babylon was overthrown by the Persians. It was under Persian rule when King Cyrus the Great was moved by the Holy Spirit to allow former citizens of Israel to return to their nation's capital and to restore their holy temple. God wanted to be corporately worshipped by his people once again. And God brought them forth so that they could worship him as a people. And it must be noted that the reason God gives for Israel being freed from slavery under Egypt was so that the people of Israel could corporately worship him And the reason for Israel being released from exile is so that Israel could corporately worship him. After accounting for the number of people to return and to what patriarch families they all were connected under with Abraham's covenant. They then leave Israel, I mean leave for Israel, and arrive at the city of Jerusalem, as recorded in Ezra chapter 3. Now we learned from Ezra that this was the seventh month. And that month in the Hebrew calendar is Tishri, which is, interestingly, for us, right now. It is the overlap of September and October. And so we can say that they gathered right now 2,552 years ago. The statement that they gathered together as one is a commentary on what God had done to bring about unity with his people. Their unity was undeniable. The first thing that people do at their arrival in Jerusalem was to worship corporately And to worship corporately, they were to perform acts of worship according to the law of Moses. And the first law of Moses to be obeyed was for the people to fall under proper leadership. Jeshua is mentioned. He's identified elsewhere as the high priest, so that is according to the law of Moses. And certainly what was offered and how it was offered to God was according to the law of Moses. In verse 3, we get both commentary and play-by-play. We are told that the people were scared because of the nations that surrounded them, as those nations did not want Israel to return to their land. But their desire to corporately worship God, that desire was more important than their fears, we should say greater than their fears. So they did as the law required, worshipped instead of feared. What is described regarding the altar? is likely a new altar being built on the foundation of the old one. Sacrificial offerings offered morning and night, again according to the law of Moses. Then in verses 4 through 6, we are told how the people followed the Jewish calendar by worshiping rightly before God during the days that God had set aside. And the people made sacrificial offerings on those days as prescribed. They did this even before the physical foundation of the temple was restored. Hence corporate worship was their priority. Verse 7 informs us that the rebuilding got started. All contributed financially The tradesmen with skill were commissioned, and it was all done according to the permission granted by King Cyrus the Great. Verse 8 marks the time that actual work started, which was one and a half years after they arrived. All of the time in between, they continued to offer sacrifices to God, obeying their festival days again as prescribed by Moses. And Ezra wants us to know, Ezra being the author, that the work was done with formality. According to verse 10, as the foundation of the temple was being rebuilt, the priests stood within the temple, wearing their priestly garments, blowing trumpets, clanging their cymbals. Presenting a joyful noise to God. The reference here to the ordinance of King David is likely a recalling of 1 Chronicles 15. where David instructs the Levites to appoint skillful musicians to play before God. And there David is acting very much like the Messiah who would be both king and priest. The praise and shouting and giving thanks to God in unison of heart and unison of words is then described in verse 11. And this is caused, this this joyfulness is caused by the progress that they're making in building this temple, which is why they came there in the first place. But there is another reaction described in verses 12 and 13. And that reaction reveals deep and mixed emotions. Emotions were mixed because of all that had been lost, which is what Israel had been missing when they could not worship God as He prescribed them to worship. The weeping was a lament for all that the people of God had not been able to do while they were in exile, and the temple lie in ruins. Perhaps a metaphor of marriage will get us close to feeling what the people of Israel were feeling when they shouted with joy and were also weeping A couple separates from one another because of foolish emotions, unnecessary words, and the harboring of bitterness. All the while they still share an abiding love for one another. Apart, they feel the pains of loneliness and regret. They are sobered up by their loneliness and regret, allowing them to see that they were wrong. Wrong in their emotions, wrong in their words, wrong in withholding forgiveness. When they finally come together again, they rejoice with passionate love. But their sorrow is mixed in there as well. For they realized how much they missed one another and how much time was wasted being apart, all the while they could have felt love from one another. God has used the metaphor marriage to describe his relationship with his people. It is a natural metaphor for how his people can know his love. It is how you and I can know his love. From Ezra chapter 3, we learn that Israel, the Israelites understood that their corporate worship with God and for God was to be their priority. And again I use a marriage analogy. As discussed in Sunday school last week, a strong marriage begins with a husband and wife centering the family life around their marriage. That's the center of the family. It should not be centered around the children. If it is, children get a false sense of their importance And they'll be psychologically insecure, not having the assurance of their parents' love for one another. And that is true when it comes to worshiping God first and foremost. Without placing the worship of God first in our family homes, we create an insecurity in each family member. As each family member is not sure that God is their God and that they are his people. Making corporate worship a priority communicates to each family member what should be in regards to priorities of the family and priorities of each family member. Next, we can learn the priority of corporate worship as opposed to individual worship. Consider when Abraham and then Isaac and then Jacob, when they worshiped God, it was as individuals and as a family. And as such, there were no laws given by God on how worship was to be constructed. Now they knew of the stories of Cain and Abel making offerings, and so that's what they did, but the details are scarce. When Moses was called to God to lead Israel out of Egypt for the purpose of worshiping God as a people, it was the first time Israel would worship corporately. It was then that God gave instructions about corporate worship, how it was to be done. Instructions are given and commandments are established for corporate worship because God is with his people as they worship in ways like no other time where two or more are gathered he is in their midst And if you were to ask me how, he is present differently or in a more unique manner than other times, I will simply answer to you, I don't know. I do know that Jesus promised that the Holy Spirit would dwell in the hearts of every believer. I know that to be true. And I also know that he said that where two or more are gathered, he would be there in the midst, which is different than the Holy Spirit in our heart. It is a special promise, separate and different from other promises of his presence. And also, and this is this is such a very important point. The unique and special presence of God is in the bread and wine that we consume at Holy Communion. No, I'm not talking about a superstitious belief of what the bread becomes and what the wine becomes. I'm referring to the truth. That St. Paul described, you remember when he warned those Christians in Corinth that if people ate of that bread and drank of that cup unworthily, that they would become sick, and even some would be judged to death. From what we can reason, if God's judgment is present when consuming the bread and wine, well so then is his grace. When those eat it by faith. How, you ask? I don't know I do know because they are holy mysteries. And holy mysteries is sufficient Also, in Ezra chapter 3, we are reminded that there are right and wrong ways to worship God. That truth has been difficult for Western Christians to accept. The spirit of individualism is strong in our culture And with the denial of the existence of objective beauty and absolute truth, it is a free-for-all in Christian communities to worship God how a person wants to worship God. And our understanding of God is selective, as many cannot imagine him having a personality that rejects the attempt of anyone worshiping him. After all, we are a culture that thinks that effort matters most. Right? As long as you try, well, you're going to get the praise because you tried. That is why when Johnny is on his first baseball team, And the coach sticks him out in right field because that's the least possible place a ball will be hit. And Johnny has his mitt on his head, all the while blowing bubbles with his bubblegum And a ball is hit to him, and he doesn't have a clue that the ball is sitting right next to him And yet when he hears all this screaming and yelling, the batter is running around the bases, everybody on both sides is screaming. Johnny finally figures out that the ball is next to him and picks it up and doesn't quite know who to throw it to, but somebody's yelling at him, so he throws it to that guy All the while the batter gets to third, and we hear from the stands, good effort, Johnny, good effort. Well, we all know that that was not a good effort by Johnny. And in fact, even if Johnny was to have hustled some time in there. If he did not know where he was assigned to throw it to, to hit the cutoff man, it still wouldn't be a good effort What is good is what is right. And what is right when it comes to worshiping God is to obey Him. Cain. Cain did not obey God, and his worship of God was rejected. The sons of Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu, offered up fire to God, not according to the law, and God put them to death. King Saul's sacrificial worship was rejected because of his disobedience and dishonesty. But he made the effort, some would say. Effort without obedience is no virtue. God later rejected all of Israel's worship, even that which was being done according to the law of Moses. He still rejected it because Israel was also worshiping and serving. Other gods. Causing God to say to obey is better than sacrifice. Right ritual means nothing to God if sin is harbored. Unfortunately, when God says to Israel that he does not delight in their sacrifices or that he rejects their rituals, Some modern interpreters have concluded that God doesn't want any more rituals. And because God doesn't want any ritual at all, they conclude that they are free to worship God in whatever manner they prefer. And the result of that, the result of that is rock concerts on Sunday mornings. The result of that is a pastor riding his motorcycle into a sanctuary. That really did happen. The result is miming, clowning, special effects, coffee breaks, communion happy meals, positive mental attitude sermons, and whatever else that looks Like the world with a Christian stamped on it. The truth is that God is the one who prescribed the ritual. Because he prescribed it, it is perfect. What is not perfect is believing that ritual can cover up sin. Once again, we are answering the question asked a few weeks ago, how did we get here? The here is the immorality accepted by churches that call themselves Christian. The here we have come to is the watered-down truth or the avoiding of truth preached and taught behind pulpits. The cause of how we got here is taking for granted the privilege we have of corporately worshiping God. The cause of how we got here is not insisting that our corporate worship be reverent and that it be true And such is the responsibility of laity and clergy alike. The scripture tells us to weep with those who weep. And so we weep with those who lament as to what has been lost by the Christian church when it compromised its corporate worship. just as those who wept in Ezra chapter 3. But we rejoice. Also we rejoice as Scripture instructs. We rejoice with those who rejoice Because we get to hear God's word, and we get to gather together around His table, and we get to baptize the covenant child. In the Exodus, corporate worship was the priority. When Israel returns from exile, it is the priority again. It then sounds like it should be for us. Let us pray. Father, we are thankful for the privilege it is to gather here today and to gather every Sunday as a people To call upon you that every confidence we are heard. We thank you for your presence. Father, may we never Evermore take it for granted. In Jesus' name we pray. Amen.

sermons.title: Never Give In
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Be seated. I'd like you to take your Bibles and turn to Ezra chapter 4. Ezra chapter 4. We will be working through these verses specifically. I begin with commentary on each of the passages read from Ezra IV. Verse 1. To call the tribes adversaries is to make an important distinction when they make their request to help build this building. Verse 2. The request may seem kind, it may seem noble to help, but it is based on a lie. The people were from the Samaritan region. Yes, they acknowledged the God of the Hebrews, but only that he was one of many gods. And they did not worship as the Jews did, for the Jews worshiped according to the law of Moses Instead, they worshiped by their own customs, which were more pagan in their origin than they did come from the law of Moses. Verse 3 The refusal of the offer to help is based on what is stated in verse 1. The leaders of Israel knew that the people offering were liars. They knew they were actual enemies, and thus they were not for the same cause or of the same faith. As it had been, so it would ever be that the nations that surrounded Israel were pagan idol worshipers. Always trying and unfortunately succeeding at dragging Israel into their false worship. To refuse this help was according to the law of Moses and paying attention to the warnings that God gave through his prophets when Israel would enter the promised land. Verse four. The reaction of the Samaritans to the refusal Is proof that they had no true intention of aiding the Israelites. Their task was always to divide Being turned away gave them more reason to stop the work, to divide. Verse 5 Who these enemies of Israel hired were counselors in the court of King Cyrus. And this bribing and influence lasted eight more years. Bribing in such Oriental courts was quite common. And it is easy to imagine that the king would not think much about this small tribe of Israel, whatever they were doing. He would likely be more concerned about the commanders that he put in place in this Samaritan region. Verse 6. The point of this verse is to note that a new letter was written when a new king was put in place. The letter is to keep this building program at a standstill perpetually. Verse 7. The name Artaterxes stands out to us because it is the same name we find in the book of Nehemiah that we're studying on Tuesdays and Wednesdays, Wednesdays And it's also found in the book of Esther. The problem with concluding that this is the same king identified in Esther Is that Persian kings took on many names, and so we have many Dariuses and many Xerxes. Also, the timing of this being Esther's king, it's a little bit hard to fit into her narrative. So we can only say that it might be the same king. Verse 8. Here is the identification of the leaders assigned to the Samaritan region. These are the antagonists to the story, Rehum and Shimshai. I had uh Phil, our reader, skip verses 9 and 10. I didn't want us to pretend like he was pronouncing the names correctly. God knows them. Verse eleven The mention of beyond the river is a reference to the Euphrates River, and the phrase and so forth is a reference back to the writers. Verse 12. The description of the temple as rebellious and the city as evil. Is a persuasive description that reveals the writer's unapologetic prejudice against the Israelites Verse 13. There was no proof to the accusations ascribed to the Israelites. We should call it what it is. It is slander. It was a lie to predict what the Jewish people were going to do. But lies like they do today. are justified because supposedly they serve a greater purpose. Greater purpose, so-called. Verse 14 The play here is to side with the king. Side with him as if they are loyal subjects, who are informing for the sake of the king and for the sake of his kingdom. When in truth they are only concerned about themselves and their vindictive hearts. Verse fifteen. Here is a clever ploy, and it will it will work. Any record of Israel rebelling in the past will be proof to not trusting them in the present. And of course, what the books contain would be previous accusations. with no necessary proof. The accusations from the past, which the Samaritans would know about because they made them They would be sufficient enough to condemn the present Israelites. It is true that Israel rebelled against Babylon. But no such rebellion occurred under Persian rule. Verse 16 Here is another unscrupulous use of language to make unfounded claims against the people of God. The warning was both to appeal to fear and a false presentation of loyalty to the king of Persia. Let us first note from this passage of Scripture, and in particular from the letter itself. How alike it is with the false accusations compared to the false accusations placed on Jesus. Jesus when he stood before the Sanhedrin. Jesus when he stood before Pilate. The Sanhedrin. Accepted false accusations that Jesus was going to destroy the temple and then rebuild it Of course, we know that he was referring to his own body as the temple, and he was referring to rebuilding as in resurrected But here we have in Ezra a dispute about rebuilding the temple. The Sanhedrin also accepted false testimony against Jesus. That accuse him of being in rebellion by wanting to do away with the law of Moses Such was the opposite of what Jesus said, which was that he came to fulfill the law, which he did. The accusation of rebelliousness of Jewish people in Ezra is further forced by prophesying that they would not pay taxes. Pay tributes to the king, as well as not obey the customs of the Persian kingdom And then we remember from this that the Pharisees tried to trap Jesus into not paying taxes to Caesar. Which would have been a clear act of rebellion under Roman law. And the primary accusation that the Pharisees and Sadducees placed upon Jesus Was to testify that Jesus claimed to be King of the Jews. By branding Jesus with such a claim, they were assuring themselves That Jesus would be brought to stand trial before the Romans. And a similar claim is made here. As they accused the Israelites of rebelling against the king of Persia. And next, we recall that in the twisted moment, in Jesus' day. Of the people claiming no allegiance to Jesus, but only to Caesar, they chanted, We have no king but Caesar. And so here in Ezra, we have Samaritans willing to accept Persian authority when it means that they will get in the end what they desire. Common enemies do make for strange bedfellows Well, from these commonalities, we can see that the devil does not change his tactics His approach for tearing down the righteous is to mock and then to falsely accuse and then to place fear in the heart of those in authority. The devil twists words. He twists the word of God. He twists the word of teachers. He twists the word of Christian to Christian. With the goal of causing strife, causing distrust, causing division. His tactics are the same. The devil collects false testimony. The devil knows who is on the take. He knows who loves money more than they love their own honor. And so he buys false testimony. He buys off judges. He buys off politicians in order to influence the highest of political authorities. His tactics are the same. The devil tempts leaders towards paranoia. He takes men of weak moral constitutions and weak hearts, weak hearts that fear, and he tempts them to think that the innocent and the oppressed are out to get them. He got Herod to fear children. He got the Pharisees to fear their Messiah. He got the Romans to fear a small sect of Jesus followers. And he gets Hollywood to fear Christian ethics. His tactics are the same. And I believe it is important To note these same tactics practiced by the devil. For when we see them practiced, then we are to know what we are up against. And this allows me to take a tangent point or tangent road here to make an important point for today. I said that the devil takes advantage of men of weak moral constitutions and weak hearts, that fear And that is what I believe was done to a man who would shoot and kill people in a crowd at a country music concert in Las Vegas to that. Men and women who give themselves over to hate and fear and bitterness and anger. Can be possessed by the devil and used as instruments for destruction. I have said before, and so I say again. The devil has two goals for each of us. The first is to kill you, and the second is to get you to believe, as a believer, to deny faith in Jesus. It is one or the other. It is natural for society to look for a motive as to why a person would commit horrifying acts. We think that if we know the motive, that we can attack the problem socially and prevent it from happening again. But a blind culture, blind to the truth of God, and blind to the spiritual warfare that surrounds them, they cannot conceive of combating the devil. The devil is in such horrifying acts. Do not doubt it. And because the weapons of our warfare are not carnal, not physical, not with guns, we resort to prayer in the name of Jesus. To rebuke the evil one, to warn against his method of taking over the wills of the weak. His tactics are the same. Looking back upon the text read from Ezra IV, I wish for us now to focus our attention upon The will and determine obedience of the Israelites, as they refuse to allow liars and deceivers to play a part in rebuilding the temple. If a preacher can play like a doctor for a moment and point out what is being done wrong in the body of Christ that is causing that same body illness Than injury. This preacher identifies the problem of Christians allowing the secular world to influence our thinking And believing with lies and deceptions. And let us look first about a deception It is a deception for secular education to present itself as objective. Not having an agenda that wants God dead and wants humanity to enthrone itself as king and god And I know this firsthand, because most of my children attended a secular high school, although it was private. Much of our conversations before and after school consisted of having to debunk some of the history, so-called, that they were taught the sexuality that they were taught, the science so-called that they were taught, and the sociology that was forced upon them We believed that our children's souls were at stake, and our children's children's souls were at stake, and thus we could not allow false teachings to go unchallenged. Such a topic allows us to talk next about a lie. It is a lie to conclude that if you are pursuing Christian education for your child, Whether at home or at an academy like our own, that children will not sin and will not be exposed to sin. That is a lie. And it is caused by another lie that assumes that Christians are fully sanctified and thus practicing no vices and have no moral failings. The truth is that Christian institutions and Christian homes house sinful people who practice vices Who struggle with the setting sins and commit moral failings. And the lie that Christians do not have such sins can extend to the church. Where we might assume that the preacher is fully sanctified and the rest of the leadership are mostly sanctified, and that they should be Jesus to us in every way possible. The problem with that lie is that we know we shouldn't think in such a manner. But we want to because we want Jesus to be tangible to us right in front of us But it is a lie, and we need to call it such, or we will repeatedly be disappointed, and then disillusioned, and disillusionment leads to unbelief. Another deception. Another deception is that what entertains us has no ability to harm us. Consider that every story has a spirit of truth or falsehood behind it. Stories are alive, just as beliefs are alive, teachings are alive, doctrines are alive, worldviews are alive. That is why St. Paul instructs Christians to bring every thought into captivity. Thoughts need to be controlled by the Holy Spirit because they will run wild. They will cause havoc. Because the spirit that gives them life is untamed. Examine, if you would, what spirit is behind the television shows that you watch. There are plenty of possibilities. There is the spirit of greed, spirit of lust. The spirit of envy, the spirit of strife, the spirit of condemnation, and the spirit of hate. And certainly there are spirits of peace, of love, of forgiveness, of unity and alike, which does your entertainment give you Apply such questions to the movies you see and the music you hear or the news source that you choose Identifying their agenda is identifying their spirit, and that spirit is to be brought into captivity. Another lie is that bad company doesn't influence us. We like to think that we only influence ourselves. We like to think of ourselves as captain of our own ship. We do it our way along with Frank Sinatra. But bad company does corrupt good character, as St. Paul warns. The Israelites had finally, finally understood the truth when they turned the Samaritans away. Close fellowship with unbelievers is like being on a stepladder. I was told when I was early in my faith. It is much easier to be pulled down than it is to pull anyone up. A husband and father who hangs out with his work buddies or old school buddies after work and socializes with them on a regular basis is going to be encouraged to drink more alcohol. To turn a deaf ear to his wife, to lust after girls seen in the bar, to forget about his marital vows and attending his daughter's recital. A wife and mother who socializes regularly with her old classmates or club friends. She is going to be encouraged not to listen to her husband, to expect her husband to do her duties to gossip and slander friends and neighbors alike, and to party like the guys party. Both of these people need believers in their lives to encourage them toward righteousness and upright living. They need people in their lives that help them fight against their sinful urges, not coaching them to obey them. If an unbeliever's marriage is on the rocks, believe that that person will want to move your marriage to the same place, because misery does indeed love company. People who are struggling with a vice are going to want you to struggle with them. That is the way of it. It cannot be helped. It was said earlier that the devil does not change his tactics. Eve was separated from Adam, you remember. Eve was alone with the serpent. Eve was alone and vulnerable to doubt what God actually said. The devil's tactics are the same. When Peter was stealth in our reading following Jesus after Jesus' arrest, he found himself being warmed by a fire made by people he did not know. It was those people he did not know, and it was those people that when they he then feared, and they asked him if he was a follower of Jesus, he denied it. Consider where what would happen to Peter if he was with the other apostles. Consider if he was in with the right people. Would he have ever denied Jesus? The devil does not change his tactics. They are the same. We have been asking how we got here in this series, how we got to a place where the church is a reproach to our culture. We got here by not doing what Israel finally does. In Ezra chapter 4, they did not compromise. They did not give in to social pressure. There is a rumored story about Sir Winston Churchill. Giving a speech to his old boys' school near the end of his life. It describes him as rising to the podium slowly. Before a much anticipated large crowd, the crowd with much anticipation. Although a long oratory was expected, the crowd only heard the following. Young men, never give up, never give up, never, never, never, never, never, never. And the rumor has it that he then sat down. Well, the truth is that such a speech was not near the end of his life. It was actually during World War II. And it was not just a few lines, but part of a two-page long speech. And he did not say, never give up. Instead, he said, never give in. That phrase fits well with the message from this passage from Ezra. Never compromise your convictions. Never give in Never give in. Never, never, never, never, never, never. Let us pray. Our Father, we are so grateful For a story of your people, not giving in, not compromising, saying no to that which would corrupt them And so we take it now as a message to the church today to not compromise, to build the house by your direction Father, forgive us for what lies in the past and direct us for what lies in the future. In Jesus' name we pray. Amen.

sermons.title: Preached and Received
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, of the Son, of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Be seated. I encourage you to turn in your Bible. to the end of chapter four of Ezra and the beginning of chapter five. Ezra chapter four and into chapter five I have been asked several times how a man can know that he's called to the ministry. There is an ununderstandable hesitation by some who pursue holy orders, and that is as it should be. St. Paul warned that God will judge teachers of his word using a higher standard than everyone else. Gospel preachers are stewards of the greatest story ever told. They are keepers of the pearl of great price. False teachers and poor teachers can do great damage to the body of Christ. Their fate is truly a sinner in the hands of an angry God It is true, as St. Paul said, that a pastor is a high calling, thus it is not to be entered into lightly. And I imagine the hesitation by some men is also caused by making observations of those who are presently serving in the ministry. A man who is truly trying to make a difference for the kingdom of God is going to face opposition. And the local church has no shortage of critics. Every pastor that is accomplishing anything positive for the kingdom of God will tell you that he has questioned his call to the ministry several times. even after his training is over and he is ordained to the task. There are many moments. As you know, that a pastor falls short. It could be that he is not up to the task of helping someone in need. He may find himself failing to get the trust of certain parishioners. He can fail to connect with Christians who need his counsel. And his tongue can be the untamed horse just as any other Christian, resulting in him saying the wrong thing or saying the right thing in the wrong way. There are times when a minister can't get out of his own way, causing him not just to wonder why this certain person doesn't come to church anymore But actually he is surprised that anyone would come to the parish where he is a pastor. It is at those times that he needs a more objective source to confirm his calling. And so he must remember that the church did examine him, and God, via the church, ordained him, and that should be enough. To keep him going, to not give up. But there is a subjective side to this call of a minister as well. I consider it just as important as the objective parts. It is an internal burning, as the prophet Jeremiah described That will only be quenched if he, as a preacher, speaks the truth from the Word of God. The need to speak the truth of God must be a burning desire. If a man has such a desire, he finds that no other calling in life can satisfy. The truth must be preached, and he must preach it. If a man has that, it can sustain him Through lonely times and barren seasons. The call on the man to preach is relevant to our study in Ezra chapter 5. Because God called Haggai and Zachariah to prophesy God's word to the Israelites, having been stalled 15 years From rebuilding the temple. Ezra does not inform us regarding the details of the words prophesied by Haggai and Zechariah But we only need to look at the books of Haggai and Zechariah to find out what God had them speak. Haggai is listed first, and he comes in our Bibles just before Zechariah. The name Haggai. It means to make a pilgrimage. And it is likely that Haggai had to make a pilgrimage to Israel to preach or prophesy to them. But the meaning may also refer to why the Israelites should be rebuilding the temple. It was so that the Israelites could make a pilgrimage to Jerusalem to visit the temple. It would be to visit the temple that again the project had been stalled for 15 years. Nothing else. Nothing else about Haggai but this call to prophesy. Nothing else is known. And such is as it should be. For it is not the man Haggai that is important, but the message he spoke. Haggai was to be an instrument of God to his people, and thus the personality of Haggai is irrelevant. When Jesus instructed his followers to die to themselves, to lose their lives in order to gain eternal life. And when St. Paul said that he no longer lived, but instead it was Christ Jesus that lived in him, in these descriptions we hear a higher standard than has ever been required by God. And yet it is a standard that, if met, would allow people to see Jesus in us instead of just seeing us. Several years ago, I was asked to preach at the installment service of my brother-in-law into the parish that today he continues to serve in North Carolina. I chose a passage from the gospel according to St. John Where there is a group of men who are coming from Betheda, who come to Philip, one of the apostles, and said to them this short request, Sir, we wish to see Jesus. That verse stood out to me because uh when I first preached, the first places I preached That verse was behind the pulpit. That same verse engraved so that only the preacher could see it. Sir, we wish to see Jesus. And so I admonish my brother-in-law that if he is to be an anointed preacher to the people God has given him responsibility for, He is to work so that when he preaches, they see Jesus. Because that is why they come. They wish to see Jesus. But even while I preached that sermon, I couldn't get out of the way of myself. I have my own quirks, I have my own sense of humor, and that can easily get into the way And most certainly gets in the way too much from behind this pulpit. God hearing preacher A God-fearing preacher is to remember that the people who attend service every week come to see Jesus And for that to happen, a preacher, a prophet needs to get out of the way. But it is not easy to get out of the way. It is not easy to die to sell. And yet that is the standard. Now the message that Haggai was to prophesy to the Israelites, all we need to do is read Haggai. was that they had become reluctant builders. And they had become reluctant builders because they had become complacent. And then they became lazy. And then they became faithless. They were reluctant because their progress had been thwarted by their enemies around them. They had received orders not to continue building because the Samaritans kept writing letters to the kings of Persia, and the kings of Persia kept siding with the Samaritans And the more letters that cited with the Samaritans, the more Israel forgot the promises of God They forgot that God had promised that they were to go back to that promised land and rebuild the temple. God told them they were to do that, but they forgot. And when the promises are forgotten, because their cause keeps getting thwarted and derailed, that's when faithlessness creeps in. And faithlessness says Did God really say that that's what he wanted us to do? Is God really on our side when our enemies are so successful around us? So prayers offered then start to become weakly spaded. Offerings are still offered, but with less zeal. Apathy and acceptance set in as present circumstances become more comfortable. And soon the people no longer care whether the temple gets rebuilt. And so it is required that God speak through a man to stir up the people. Hence, the word of God must be spoken. The word of God must be spoken to make the people of God uncomfortable about where they are sitting. The word of God must be spoken to make people so uncomfortable they cannot stay sitting any longer. The word of God must be spoken so that the people of God get out of their position of sloth and get something done for the kingdom of God. And some people like to hear the word that wakes them up and gets them moving. And, well, others do not. And those who do not also don't like the messenger because they don't like his message. They are uncomfortable in they are comfortable, excuse me, in their sloth, and they want to remain in their sloth. And they say, who are you, prophet slash, preacher, to tell me what I am to be doing or what I am doing wrong? But the prophet slash preacher must speak the word of God. It must be spoken. And he must speak while knowing that some will reject what he says. And some will reject him because of what he says. But he no longer lives, but instead Jesus lives in him. And so he can't be concerned for himself, but only for the word. A prophet, slash, preacher, also takes comfort. In knowing that what he says to God's people, no matter how uncomfortable it is to say, are not his words, but the word of God. And I've been using Prophet Slash Preacher title to make that point that it's the Word of God. You see, I know that when we hear the word prophet, we might be prone to think in terms of words of God that are new, or words that describe the future. But the words of Haggai were not words that were new, but words of God that God had already stated. And it was the call of Haggai to bring those words to life in the present circumstances of the people of Israel who were stuck in their sin. And that call of Haggai to bring the Word of God into the context of the people of God so that they would start building again. That is the same call preachers of the gospel have upon them today. Ordained ministers of the gospel are to bring the Word of God to bear in the lives of the people of God, the people that God has given him to care for. And in doing so, the preacher does not say anything new, but only shows that what God has already said applies to every life circumstance of every believer. When I was in my charismatic circles during some of my college years I recall men talking about wanting to hear a new word from God. They would word it that way, requesting a fresh word from God. And I have become wiser over the years to now see such a request as unnecessary and unfortunate. Such a request is unnecessary because what God has said in Jesus is sufficient. And what we have in Holy Scripture is more than enough. To learn the truths that we need to live holy lives. It takes more than many lifetimes to digest and practice all that the Bible now teaches us. So much so that we don't need anything new. Besides, when something is eternal, as the Word of God is eternal, why does it need to be new? It lasts forever. As I said, the word of God must be spoken. And just as importantly in this passage from Ezra, just as importantly the Word of God must be received. The reception of the Word of God is the responsibility of the laity. And frankly, I don't know what is more difficult. To speak the Word of God or to receive the Word of God? As a preacher, I've experienced, of course, both. I know when the word of God that I'm going to speak is going to hit a nerve and it might get some visceral reaction from some. And I know when the Word of God preached has tempted a visceral reaction within me. And both ends are difficult to experience. After all, we are all still in the flesh. We all wrestle for the flesh to be put down and the Spirit of God to reign within us. And thus we are when we are told that we are not living how we should, or we are not thinking how we should, it's not pleasing to God. And it needed to be pointed out to us because we couldn't figure it out ourselves Well that's difficult to hear, no matter how many years you have called yourself Christian Yeah, on the other side, every preacher likes to be liked. No matter what tough exterior we can put on, acting like, oh, it doesn't matter how people perceive me. The truth is We all like to be liked. So when you have to proclaim something that makes it possible for people to not like you, it's not easy So God's word needs to be spoken, and God's word needs to be heard, and neither of those things are easy. Both can be hard. To embolden us to do both, we must consider the alternative. What if it's not preached and not received? Recall where Saint Paul instructed Timothy to preach the word He said to be ready in season and out of season. And then he said the following, for the time will come when people will not put up with sound doctrine. Instead, to suit their own desires, they will gather around them a great number of teachers to say what their itching ears want to hear. To be sure, a description of a time when people have itching ears could apply to all ages. But I wonder if we are in an era when there is more scratching going on than ever before. A man who preaches in one of the largest churches in the United States was asked whether people who don't believe in Jesus will go to heaven. His answer, well, I I'm very careful about saying who would and who wouldn't go to heaven I don't know. Well oh, I don't know if I believe they're wrong. When asked about issues such as abortion and same-sex marriage, he replied, you know, I don't go there. Do I hear some scratching? When asked why they attend the positive message megachurch known as the gospel with a smile, a couple said, because the messages are always uplifting, always positive. Scratching and more scratching. But the megachurches don't have a corner market on satisfying itching ears. Liberal mainline churches have been scratching such ears for decades. In mainline liberal Christian churches, God is both feminine and masculine. And humanity is needed by God to achieve his divine aims. Scratch. Scratch. The Bible, congregations are told, tells stories that are metaphorical, not literal. Even the story of Jesus being raised from the dead. Scratch. Scratch. According to liberal theologians, Jesus held transformative values that were progressive. And thus, Christians today must have an ethics standard that is progressive as well, which is to say that ethics change over time. Scratch. Scratch. Because ethics change with time, abortion, homosexuality, divorce, contraception, adultery, and even prostitution, these are not hot buttons, but instead are private decisions. Scratch, scratch. And from the top of the leadership to the lowest of the laity, universalism is preached and embraced. So that all feel good when anyone dies because everyone is going to heaven. Scratch, scratch, scratch But megachurches and liberal churches don't have the corner market on scratching ears. Churches that claim to believe the Bible to be fully the Word of God and hold to the Orthodox Christian faith, these have itching ears and ways to scratch them. I know of a wealthy donor in a local church that wanted his daughter to marry in the church by the present pastor. Even though she wanted to marry a Mormon. The pastor stood his ground. That would be unequally yoked. So he refused. But the father of this young girl was a great donor and threatened to pull his financial support from the church. Which required an immediate elders meeting called to talk some sense into the preacher. Scratch. Scratch. I know a preacher who discovered that when he preached topical sermons that tried to help people be better businessmen or better friends or better married couples or find peace of mind. Well, those sermons received the greatest praise from the congregation. And so he abandoned expository sermons that looked closely at the Word of God and he replaced them for what the people wanted most. Scratch. Scratch. Beloved, in order for the kingdom of God to come In order for God's will to be done on earth as it is in heaven, the word of God must be spoken. Not the words of a man, but the word of God must be proclaimed. And the word of God spoken for it to have an effect at building the kingdom of God, it must be received. And by received we mean acknowledged as true and then acted upon Look at verse 2 from Ezra 5. I love this verse. Verse 2 of Ezra 5, it simply states that after Haggai and Zechariah spoke the word of God, the leaders and the people rose up, got up off of their slothful posture And began to build. Thus, all that it took to get the people going after 15 years of sloth All that it took was the word of God to be spoken and the word of God to be received. And the verse ends by saying that the prophets then helped the people build. So there it is. The prophets, the preachers of God's word are in the kingdom of God building project with the people. For the kingdom of God to be built, it must be built together with the clergy and the laity being faithful to the Word of God. It sounds so simple. And yet and yet so many do not do their part. Let each of us be sure to do our part. Let us pray.

sermons.title: The Gospel in Ezra
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. In your Bibles, we're going to be covering from Ezra chapter 5. Through Ezra chapter six. So we're dealing with all the content of five and then all the content of chapter six. Historical negationism. Historical negationism is making illegitimate distortions of historical record. It is also called by some historical revisionism, but such a description is not harsh enough. Historical negationism is doing more than revising the past. It is an attempt to change the past. From what it truly was. It is for good forging documents and labeling them as genuine evidence It is the inventing of implausible reasons for distrusting genuine documents. It is manipulating statistics to say something did or did not happen. Notable examples include Holocaust denial. Armenian genocide denial, Japanese war crime denial, and American Southern slavery depictions. The purpose is primarily for the sake of propaganda. For example, if the Nazi Party of Germany wants to make a political comeback To regain political power, it would have to change the number of Jews that were killed in concentration camps. In fact, it would likely have to deny the existence of concentration camps altogether. They would then have to come up with evidence that would put into question historical footage, both in moving pictures and still pictures, of the many people who were discovered by the Allies when they opened up those gates to those camps. The Nazis would then have to destroy or change documents that ordered such camps to exist. And the words of Hitler calling for the extinction of the Jews would have to be stricken or distorted. And finally, the Nazis would have to come up with evidence that shows that the Allies were not less evil than the Nazis when it came to war crimes. That would play on the consciences of the masses. From my research of the subject of Holocaust denial, I discovered that the Germans had in place before the Second World War ended, that if they were to be defeated, they would destroy all German records that spoke of the Holocaust. Tells you what they really knew about the Holocaust. Himmler was one leader who ordered camps to be destroyed, even the breaking down of crematoria to hide evidence of crimes against humanity. And perhaps most of us think in the following manner. The inhumanity And the vast number of deaths caused by the Holocaust give us a sense of disbelief To our consciences, perhaps because we don't want to believe that our fellow human beings are capable of such atrocities. And when we see the evidence in picture form, we do believe it. And such pictures are so horrifying, we are in disbelief that anyone would deny that it happened When considering what we have just witnessed, at a certain level, we are watching historical negationism occur among us today. We have seemingly very uneducated people insisting that we tear down images of men of our nation's history that had beliefs that we deem now unconscionable. Such men had prejudices that some conclude disqualify them from the human race, even if the memory of them includes virtues that are worthy to emulate. And I preached several weeks ago that to destroy monuments to such men is to not understand the gospel. And I use that because here in Ezra V, we have the privy to a letter that shows a people. Who understand the grace of God so much that they have every confidence that God would give them victory over their detractors. And that they could and would fulfill God's call on them to rebuild the temple. They did this all in light of their own sin, knowing their sin Allow me to retell the story that is found in Ezra 5 and 6 so that we don't have to read it all this morning. I hope that once we do, then we can highlight two portions of this narrative that I believe stand out Recall from last week that we learned that Israel had stopped rebuilding the temple because the Samaritan leaders They kept writing letters to the kings of Persia and getting those kings to side with them in regards to forcing the Israelites to stop rebuilding. Every time there was a new king of Persia, he would be told how dangerous these small the small tribe of Israel was, those that had returned to rebuild the temple A return, by the way, that was not only allowed by Cyrus, king of Persia, but Cyrus helped them along the way. But the Samaritans kept lying in their letters, saying that Israel was a bunch of rebels, and so Israel kept running into walls. Soon they got tired of being turned away, and so they chose to be faithless. They no longer believed that God wanted them to build or rebuild the temple. And then because God called his prophets, Haggai and Zechariah, and their words were believed by the people, causing them to get up. off of their faithless rear ends and start building again. But the Samaritan regional governor, appointed by the king of Persia, didn't like the fact that the Israelites had started building the temple again. So he challenged them and he asked them by what authority they were doing this work. Now it should be noted that the governor went to great lengths to be just. He needs to be given credit for that. He did great went to great lengths to be just. In the matter, because he allowed the people of Israel to present their side of the events and to testify of their perspective in the letter sent to the king. A letter, as I mentioned, was then sent to Darius, the then king of Persia, and it included Israel's side. How they saw the issue. After the king received the information, he had his scholars search the archives to see if the testimony of Israel was true. And of course it was true. And this caused King Darius to issue a decree that verified all of the testimony of the Israelites, and he even re-upped the commitment of Cyrus. Allowing and aiding the Jews to rebuild the temple. Tatania is his name, the governor. And all who were under him had no choice but to abide by the king's directive. And so we read at the end of chapter 6. That Israel finished the work that they had started, and they next offered to the Lord offerings of worship according to the law of Moses. And they did so, dedicating the rebuilt temple. And it says, with all joy. Chapter 5 and chapter 6 of Ezra. And what we have in these chapters is a story about how God sifted the hearts of the kings of Persia through his hands, moving them as he willed. The obstacles that were set before the Israelites were of no consequence when the people worked by faith and not by science. In these chapters, we have a story about how God used his own people. Used his own people to work towards his sovereign will. For that to be fulfilled, and he also used people that are not his people to work with his people to accomplish his sovereign will And we can conclude that no matter how chaotic the world seems, we can conclude that God does the same today. He uses his people. And he uses people who are not his people to work toward fulfilling his sovereign will. And all of us can say thanks be to God. What stands out in the events described in these two chapters, I believe, is twofold. The first standout is the honest confession made by the Israelites in their letter to the king, King Darius. They could have, in their reaccount of the events, left their past sins out. They could have briefly mentioned why they lost their land, not stating any detail. Instead, they confessed that their forefathers, in blood and in faith, had provoked the one true God in order to reveal his wrath. Their punishment was to become enslaved and taken from the land God had given them and place them in the land of what was Babylonia and now Persia It was their sin. They owned it. And they repeated it in writing so all could know it. I started off the sermon by talking about historical negationism because Israel is so very unique in doing the opposite. For they have the ability as a people to freely record the sins of their forefathers and confess those sins as their own. What these people of God seem to have understood is that the sins of their forefathers is part of who they are. It's part of their identity. That God has both punished them as a people and forgiven them as a people in relation to the sins of their forefathers is who they are I have mentioned before that I don't know of any people in the history of the world that records in detail the sins of their forefathers in the same manner that Israel has done. Historical negationism for Israel would be to try to erase the grace of God upon them, and they could not do that. It appears to be important to the redemption of God's people to acknowledge the sins of our past. And the mercies of God regarding those sins. In order to see ourselves for who we truly are Then this should occur as a nation, should occur as a church, and should occur within individual families. Consider the history of this parish. God has done gracious things among us, even while we have broken relationships with many people who no longer attend this parish. And I've said and done things in my relationship with people that have fallen short of the glory of God. Some have been confessed and offensive mended, and some have not. And all of these those instances are part of my history, and part of the history of this church, and my identity as a pastor of this church. But we don't record those breakups. If I'm going to write a summary of each year, I don't record those breakups Those lost relationships. Because they're not pleasant. But they are us. They are me Consider that when we read our New Testaments, we see similar stories. Mark left the mission field out of fear. Paul no longer trusted Mark. Barnabas left Paul because he disagreed with the way Mark was treated. Later, Paul confronted Peter on having on behaving like a hypocrite and told others about it. Other people left Paul's ministry because the temptations of the world was too strong for them. People lied to the church leaders and they were judged on the spot, and that's part of the church's identity There was incest in the church. Detractors sent false letters in Paul's name to cause fear. That's part of their identity. There were several false teachers and people who stirred up dissension and people who were filled with fear and all of it had to be overcome by confession and forgiveness and reconciliation. All of that and more happened in the first century church. That is the church. That is us. When we confess it as us, it allows us to be free of it. For we can be confident it is washed under the blood of Jesus. And what we have done wrong and what has been forgiven us make up who we are before God Now, I know how that might have sounded to some, and so I need to make a side note And I'm not saying that each of us needs to go around confessing our past sins to one another. That would be uh unnecessary But when past sins are true and they have relevant information about present circumstances, we should find freedom to share about those sins. Because the blood of Christ is applied to those sins, and that gives glory to God as a testimony to his mercies in Jesus. And when we have a chance to do that, that we ought to do. The second thing worth noting From chapters five and six is found in one particular phrase, in one particular verse. Look at chapter five, verse five. The phrase is, but the eye of their God was upon the elders. The eye of God was upon them. God was watching over their situation. And God was caring for them so that the outcome would be to his will and to their favor. Hear this truth from Psalm 34, 15. The eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous. Now that may concern you because you think that you are not righteous. And this is true in and of yourselves. But you are not in and of yourselves, you are not alone. Jesus has forgiven you, the Holy Spirit dwells in you, and it is the forgiveness of God in Christ that makes you righteous So the eyes of the Lord are upon you. And from Job 36, 7 we hear how God cares for his people. Quote, He withdraweth not his eyes from them. He doesn't stop looking out for you and watching out for you When I say to my wife, which I do from time to time, I admired you from afar today, what am I communicating? Am I not communicating that I looked upon her with love and I looked upon her full of care, admiration, and affection? What I can't tell my wife is that my eyes were upon her in order to protect her from danger. I cannot mean that because I do not have the ability to be omnipresent. Thus it is only God who can say that he looks upon his people, and that means that he loves, cares for, admires, has affection for, and protects his people. Consider the whole time Samaritan enemies were writing Persian kings trying to negate history, God had his eyes upon his people. The whole time the people stopped working and thus stopped believing God's promises, God had his eye upon his people so that their faith would return. The time that Israel made itself vulnerable by telling King Darius about their sinful past, God had his eyes of mercy upon them, having forgiven their sin and turning the heart of the King Darius Toward their favor. When Ezra describes these events in chapters 5 and 6, we are to know that Ezra was not present. Ezra was not yet in Jerusalem when these events happened. They were told to him. And in recounting of the events, as he writes them down, he places that phrase, but the eye of God was upon the elders. That's his phrase. Ezra is then commenting by the influence of the Holy Spirit to describe the events in such a manner. It is Ezra who had faith that God was involved in every aspect of these events, even though the people Only saw letters going back and forth and angst among their enemies who kept trying to stop them from working Thus we can say that God enjoys being behind the scenes. God's way is to partake in the salvation of his people without being seen. And that is interesting to note when we add that knowledge of God to the fact that God wants his people to worship him. You see, secular critics accuse God of having some type of ego because he requires his people to worship him. The truth is we have to worship him. That is not just a law, it is our nature. The created has to worship the creator. But not for the ego of the creator, but for the natural urge of the created. Thus God works behind the scenes And it is the nature of the Godhead, the three in one, to give glory to one another. And so the Father praises the Son and the Spirit And the son praises the father and the spirit. And the spirit praises the father and the son. And all of them love God's people. Realize, beloved, that to say that the eye of God is upon his people is to say that God loves his people. And in an age of itching ears and scratching clergy, it is frustrating to highlight God's love for his people. Because it is so often said that it fails to be in the right context and carry the full weight that it should. But it must be said, and it must be believed. God loves his people. He shows his love by watching over them, by having his eye upon them. He loves each of you. He watches over each of you. He has his eye upon each of you. And that is not scratching ears, but preaching the truth. And just because you don't see him, just because you don't know where he is, you are to be assured that he is with you, watching you, and watching over you. That is his promise, and he fulfills his promises. He is a God of covenant. Now God's providence was evident this week. We sing one hymn for morning prayer throughout the week. And this week's hymn was Jesus Loves Me. And I considered the third line of that. It fit quite well. It reads, Jesus loves me, loves me still, though I'm very weak and ill. Now the author, Anna Warner, originally penned it as a poem for a novel. It was a poem to be read to a dying child. Now it continues. From his shining throne on high comes to watch me where I lie. It is because of the fact that Jesus watches us that we sing the next, which is, yes, Jesus loves me. Thus the two standout points from chapters 5 and 6 of Ezra are that the people honestly confess their sin and that God loves them. That is the gospel. That is the message of Jesus. The good news is that while we were still in our sin, God loved us. And therefore gave us his son. You say, you got that out of Ezra? You got the gospel? Yes, we did. Let us pray. Our Father, we are thankful, so thankful that here in The historic book, in the events that transpired, we find the basics of what saves us and continues to save us. The fact that we are sinners, yes. Sinners fallen, yes. Sinners with guilty pasts, yes. And also your people loved by you. And for this all, for this all, that is who we are, and we thank you for making us who we are. In Jesus' name. Amen.

sermons.title: Overcoming Stupidity and Ignorance
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. In honor of the 500th year anniversary. Of Dr. Martin Luther hanging his 95 feces on the door of Wittenberg Castle Church in order to challenge the Roman Catholic Church to address its abuses I give you this quote from Luther's larger catechism, where he is honest about how difficult the role of parenting is. He said, quote, As a rule, the parents too are themselves stupid and ignorant One fool teaches another, and as they lived, so lived their children after them. End quote. We don't hear such frank speaking today, and that is a shame. Such direct speaking cuts to the heart of the human condition, even the condition of those who know Jesus as their Lord and Savior. Being on this side of heaven means that we are stupid and ignorant And what we pass on to our children is stupid and ignorant, and we need not feel depressed about that. When we compare all the glorious truths of the heavens and the earth to what we understand as individuals We should conclude that we are stupid and ignorant. When we consider the great mysteries of God, which include his triune nature, along with his oneness. We are stupid and ignorant. When we try to contemplate how everything exists by the means of God, And that God had no beginning himself, but exists by the necessity of his own nature. We again can conclude about ourselves that we are stupid and ignorant. Although such line of thinking, along such line of thinking we should remember Job, who thought that he had a right to question God about his own suffering. The very idea of questioning God revealed that Job is stupid and ignorant. As God asks questions that Job cannot possibly answer with proof that he is not stupid and ignorant. Where were you, Job, when I laid the foundation of the earth? Tell me if you have understanding. Job cannot answer. He cannot answer because he knows that he has been uncovered, revealed. The truth is before him about himself. He is stupid and ignorant. Every parent must understand that they are stupid and ignorant. If mom and dad are going to pass on anything of value to their children, Of the many things we want our children to know, there is a reality that parents will fall vastly short at teaching their children. And therefore, there is a necessity that God, by the person of the Holy Spirit, fill in the many, many gaps that parents leave in the lives of their children. Adding to the many gaps parents leave when educating their children in the truths of God's world There is also the reality of parents harming their children either carelessly or intentionally. There are parents who abuse their children emotionally and physically. And such abuse gives deep scars to children that makes it seemingly impossible to overcome. Because the people that were supposed to love them most didn't love them at all. Am I depressing you? You've just heard from the pulpit this Sunday morning. That you are stupid and ignorant, and that you're going to pass down that stupidity and ignorance to your children. You heard as well that the reality that some children are abused by their own parents That would make any happy person depressed when considering such confessions. But we need to consider the realities of the human condition Even when we read of the heritage of Ezra as he himself lists that heritage Although he comes from the line of Aaron, and that may impress us all, Aaron the high priest, the brother to Moses. He also comes from a line that is guilty of leading the people of God into worshiping a golden calf, an idol. And a line that is Aaron's that contained Aaron's sons who offered strange fire in the tabernacle and who were struck dead by God because of it. Where we might have read Ezra's lineage and been impressed, we should reconsider by remembering the great offenses made by Aaron and his lineage. They were stupid and ignorant. The lineage listed is incomplete. It only lists 16 generations instead of the needed 27. But the number of men listed is for brevity's sake. And for mentioning those God used to lead his people. Sariah is mentioned. He was the high priest that was slain by Nebuchadnezzar, as recorded in Jeremiah chapter 52. That Ezra was of the line of the first high priest, Aaron, and of the high priest who last served in Israel before Babylonian exile. Sariah. These truths make him suitable, Ezra, a suitable man for the time God called him. And most importantly, it shows that God fulfills his covenant promises. Even when his people don't fulfill their promises, God fulfills his. A large and repeated oversight amongst Christians is to not understand God in terms of covenant. The Jesus and Only Me crowd teaches that Jesus should be related to in terms of being a personal savior only. But Jesus is the Savior of a people as a whole, as much as he is of individual persons.
