At his ascension, he went to prepare a place for his bride, the church. And he is returning to retrieve his bride, the church. The church is made up of individuals, and he knows each of his individuals by name. But he retrieves them together as one. A really bad theology has swept through Western Christianity, specifically through Protestant and Evangelical Christianity. It is to believe that God's covenant is actually a series of different covenants, different what they call dispensations. It is the teaching that God dealt with Adam and Eve differently than he dealt with Abraham. And that was different than how he would deal with Moses. And the Israelites. And that was different than what he promised King David. And that is different than what he established under Jesus. Some of these ignorant teachers even go so far as to say that none of the Old Testament is needed because under the covenant of Jesus the law is not necessary. Accept the law of tithing. That seems to be the only law these teachers think is applicable to today. Wonder why Proper teaching of all of Scripture is that the covenant of God made under Adam continued in his covenant with Abraham, and that continued in his covenant with Moses, and that continued in his promises with David, and all of them, all of them were fulfilled in the person of Jesus of Nazareth. They were and are the same covenant with new revelations along the way. And this teaching of Holy Scripture has been the teaching of the Christian faith, both east and west. Since the time of the apostles, and when the church started keeping records and holding councils. It is the teaching of the church because it is the teaching of Holy Scripture. When Paul teaches that Abraham was made righteous by faith, He is teaching that the God of the covenant of Abraham is the God of the covenant we are under in Jesus. When Jesus says that Abraham saw his day and was glad And the Psalms of David and the prophets spoke about him. He is saying that in all is one, one covenant revealed and fulfilled in Jesus. And when Ezra, when Ezra lists the line of his family and mentions the last priest who served in Israel To the first high priest named Aaron. He is showing how God is the same God that delivered Israel out of Egypt. As he is the God who is now leading Israel back from exile The purpose of Ezra listing his own lineage is also to help the reader understand what is happening next. Ezra was being appointed by God to lead Israel in the task of beautifying the temple. But that was not all. Ezra was also given the task by God to beautify the people of Israel. To prove he was called to the task, three things needed to be in place. First, Ezra needed to be of the correct lineage according to the law of Moses, and he's proven that that is so. Second, he needed to receive permission and freedom from the king of Persia to implement his plans to beautify the temple. And that occurred by a letter prepared by King Artaterxes, which both empowered Ezra to return to Jerusalem and to carry out his calling. As well as to prove that God had moved upon the king's heart, just as he did when Zerubbabel was allowed to return. And the final thing, the final thing needed for Ezra to return and lead Israel is found in verse 10. I didn't like the NIB how it read. Saul, read the New King James here. Verse 10, chapter 7 Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of the Lord and to do it and to teach statutes and ordinances in Israel. This is where we will focus our attention. We focus our attention here because this is where we become less stupid and less ignorant. And this is where a generation needs to rise up and fill the church with men who have prepared their hearts to seek the law of the Lord and to teach the truths of Holy Scripture according to the revelation of Jesus Christ. It is most appropriate that we hear the Sunday after Reformation Sunday of the importance of preparing our hearts to seek the word of the Lord. The hand of God was upon many of the original reformers back in 1517 and following. And I say that not as a matter of rejoicing. I do not believe the Reformation as a whole is something that we should celebrate. It should not be celebrated because it split the church. It should not be celebrated because the church remains split and splintered. But the Reformation is something to commemorate because from it the gospel was preserved. And by that I mean the message of the gospel was no longer obscured by extra-biblical doctrines such as purgatory. And no longer obscured by false teachings that said we were able to pay for God's forgiveness. It's actually blasphemous. The Bible teaches that people are saved, forgiven of their sins, and receivers of the hope of heaven by means of the grace of God and the gift of faith in his atoning work. That is it. That is all that is needed, and we say thanks be to God. And that truth alone is enough evidence to say that the hand of God was upon the reformers. The other evidence of God's providential hand was the timing of the inventing, of course, of the printing press. Most of you know, around the year 1440, a German goldsmith named Johannes Gutenberg invented the printing press. And that by the 1500s allowed multiple volumes of books to be printed in a relatively short period of time. And this resulted in Luther not only translating the Bible into German for the people of Germany to hear God's word in their own tongue, but also to read it. To read it. As it was available to be printed and reprinted on a large scale. Such is evidence of God's hand God wants his holy word to be accessible to his people so that they may read it and know it and believe it. because of God's hand upon the Reformation, including all the technological advances we have today It is possible for every one of us, hear this now, it is possible for every one of us to prepare our hearts to seek the word of the Lord and to do so just as Ezra did. All of us have access to Bibles that are translated by good, sound scholarship Yes, there are some bad translations out there, so I don't make a general statement about all that's available in English. But good ones are readily available in print and digital form There is the King James Version, the New King James Version, the New American Standard, the English Standard Version, and yes, I'll even take the NIV Those of you who sit in my Bible study would appreciate that. All of them give us access to know the Word of God. And to know the Word of God is to overcome stupidity and ignorance. Because each of us is able to do as Ezra did, we can know the Word of God. And the New King James says next, and do it. That is, obey it. We can live out the Word of God. Consider that strife and anger can be overcome in your life if you practice what the Epistle of James teaches, which is where we are instructed to be quick to listen. Slow to speak, slow to anger, and to humble ourselves Consider that strife in relationships can be overcome and true healing can take place when we live by the definition of love. Which is not to keep record of wrong, to actually think the best first about someone else. To forgive one another, truly forgive Consider that fear can be dominated by love when we choose to trust God as our defender. All such is doing the Word of God. Because each of us is able to do as Ezra did, we can know the Word of God and do it and hear this now for everyone. We can teach it. We can teach it. All of us, every one of us, is a teacher. Husbands and wives who have healthy biblical relationships, relationships that are submitting to one another, as St. Paul instructs to the Ephesians. Such husbands and wives are regularly teaching one another. When I learn something new while studying it for a sermon, I tell my wife about it. When she is reading a book on Christian living and she shares some insights that she is struck by, I receive education. And when she simply lets me know what a woman's mind is thinking in a situation, that's a teaching moment. And then the teaching is passed on to the children. Mothers and fathers should be regularly telling their children what they have been learning. And children should be telling their friends what they have been learning. Ironing, iron, sharpening, iron. That is the Christian life for all believers. Teaching and learning is discipleship, and that is what Jesus wants us to be. Disciples. A disciple is one who is ready to learn So it is good news that each of us can be as Ezra, and thus each of us can know the Word of God, each of us can do the Word of God, and each of us can teach it. And yet there is something unique about Ezra that needs to be acknowledged. Let's not overlook that Ezra was a priest. He was a man called to minister in God's house. And under the covenant of Christ Jesus, there continues a call to minister in God's house. The concern is that there are not enough men who heed the call and do as Ezra did. Which is to set his heart to know the Word of God and to do it and to teach it within the house of God. And so I stand here again with the admonishment for young men to consider, consider the call to be a deacon, to be a presbyter, to be a bishop. But the church doesn't need more bodies for the sake of having more bodies to fill pulpits. No, the church needs men who will prepare their hearts to know God's word and to do it and to teach it. In our own diocese, there are at least three parishes that I know of that are in need of rectors, pastors. There are 13 seminarians enrolled in our seminary, but not all of them, I think not most of them, are Reformed Episcopal. Then there is a need to plant new churches, which is as we as a parish are hoping to do in the region of North Carroll County. When Jesus said that the fields are ripe for harvest, but the laborers are few I have often wondered if he was simply talking about his day or for only certain days down through the ages. How do you know Numbers show that Christian faithfulness is shrinking in the United States at an alarming rate. And has almost died out in Europe, as you know. Thus it can be asked, are there fields ripe for harvest today? My wisdom is that we don't know until we send laborers out into the field. And so there is something formal about Ezra coming to Jerusalem as he is has prepared himself to know God's word and to do it and to be able to teach as a priest. But there is something very practical as well. We live in a time where each of us can be ready. To know God's word and to do it and to teach it. There are always a need for Sunday school teachers Catechism teachers, Bible study leaders. You know, we have in this parish no restriction on how many Bible studies go on throughout the week. No restrictions So what say ye? So what say ye? I hope it is here I am. Let us pray

Before we address that message, I want you to enter a world with me that is unknown to most of you. It is the world of sermon preparation. I didn't say it was an exciting world. Sermon preparation can go one of many ways, of course. One of the easiest ways for a sermon to be prepared is to tell the story of a biblical hero. And then uphold that hero's virtue as an example to all of us. It is treating the Bible stories like Aesop fables And it is trying to find some moral to the story. Another easy approach to sermon preparation is examining a particular promise made in Scripture and explain how it can be applied to individual and corporate lives today Here are examples of each of those. Let us say that we are examining St. Peter's sermon on the day of Pentecost as recorded in Acts chapter 2. As we do, we note that he used a miracle of which many people witnessed. That miracle was many uneducated people speaking in unknown tongues And Peter screenboarded off of that miracle to tell of Jesus. He next used prophecies from the Old Testament. and explains how they are being fulfilled before the eyes of the audience. He pointed to Jesus, of whom the crowd knew of, saw themselves. And announced him to be the fulfillment of David's promised Messiah. He then revealed that certain promises God made about the Messiah We're actually prophecies regarding Jesus being raised from the dead Now this model of preaching, the preacher, could then apply to the Christians today as to how you and I can present the gospel to a lost and dying world. The problems, however, are numerous. First, you and I are not Peter. That is a big problem in and of itself. Second, the prophecy being fulfilled before the eyes of over 3,000 people Has not happened to any of us. Third, a person or a crowd we would speak to is not going to know Jesus having experienced him in bodily form personally Fourth, and finally, most of us, if not all of us, will not be in a position to speak to a crowd of people who are inquiring about a miracle that just happened. And when I say that, I don't mean to say that such a scenario cannot happen, but only to say that it rarely happens. And you can say, as a counter, that it doesn't happen because I don't have faith enough. If I just had more faith, and I would say in retort that I believe in such occurrences with faith at least the size of a mustard seed And still, such has not happened to me. Now, to be fair, there are principles that we can learn from St. Peter's sermon in regards to how you and I can share our faith, but that would not be an apple to apple comparison The other example is from the likes of passages such as 2 Chronicles 7 verse 14. And you've heard this many times. It reads If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, pray and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways, then I will hear from heaven and will heal their land. With such verses, preachers have been guilty of applying a historical situation With the nation of Israel, a nation God chose to occupy a particular land of promise, a land from which the Messiah of the world would come And use that scenario as applicable to countries like the United States of America. Now, as I have said before, I am a proud American. I am a patriot. I would fight for the freedoms we have been blessed to enjoy. But the promise of 2 Chronicles 7 is not directed at the United States of America. The only reasonable contemporary application of that verse would be to the church. And the land to be healed would have to be the body of Christ on this side of heaven. Again, these are examples of easy preaching. Take a story or verse of promise, apply it to the situation of contemporary, everyday life, and the preacher has finished his work for the week. And considering the narrative from Ezra, read for us a letter from King Artaterxes on behalf of Ezra, the new high priest of Israel. I found myself in preparation this week leaning toward the easy way. Which is to talk to you about the letter of the King of Kings and Lord of Lords that he has the letter he has written for you And I am confessing this easy way to you because I took it. I took it because it actually does apply to us today. And it is my job to convince you of that. So here goes. Now last week I said that Ezra needed three things in order to accomplish the goal of beautifying the temple and beautifying the people of God. First he needed the lineage proof that he was of the line of the high priest that was satisfied. We looked at the third requirement last week, which was that Ezra needed to have studied the Word of God and prepared to live it and prepared to teach it. That was also done. The second requirement is what we look at today, which was that Ezra needed official permission from the king of Persia. To be able to travel and proceed with the tasks necessary to beautify the temple and God's people Today, we read that letter of permission. What we could focus on is verse 27 of this chapter. Which is a commentary in the form of praise by Ezra. In verse 27, he describes how God had moved the heart of the king to write this letter and allow all that was necessary for Ezra to fulfill his call. But we have already spent a good deal of time confirming that God sifts the hearts of kings through his hands, and thus he directs the futures of the nations. And so I see it as unnecessary for us to focus on such here. Instead, we will look at the general content of the letter and prove And prove to our hearts and to our minds and to our souls that God has given such a letter to all who believe in Jesus as Savior. Look at verse 12. From verse 12 of chapter 7, we read that the king of Persia acknowledged Ezra's God as the God of heaven. which is the God of all gods. The same is what God has written upon the heart of believers, Who confess no other God but the God of creation, who is the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost. From verse 13, there is a commission for Ezra to go, which reminds us, reminds us that Christians have a commission. Called the Great Commission, which is to go into all the world and to preach the gospel. That's part of our letter. From verse 14, we read that the king provided guards for Ezra to protect him on his journey. So too, do Christians have the Holy Spirit who abides within the souls of God's people As do Christians have God's angels who aid Christians in terms of service and protection, according to Scripture. From verses 15 and 16. We are reminded that our God owns the cattle on a thousand hills. And as such, no money is an object for him. Not difficult. He can provide it If we need it to further his kingdom, it will be provided. Somehow and some way it will be provided From verse 17, we are reminded what is our priority, and that is the priority of worship. And not to worship how we desire, but how God Himself desires to be worshipped. I've heard a preacher say recently that there is one congregant in a worship service. One congregant, and that is God. From verses 18 through 19, we are reminded of the freedom that each believer has in Christ Jesus. We are told here that for Ezra and Israel, after beautifying the temple, they were free to use silver and gold that was left over in any manner they desired. Such is the freedom given to believers in Jesus, who are free to live not according to the law, but by faith. And in that faith there is great freedom. And in that faith is great freedom in living alive before God as long as God is given what is God's. From verse 20, we hear of a unique authority given to Ezra. He is able to take from the treasury of every local ruler what he needs to finish the work for the temple. This is right in accordance with his high priestly office. This is similar to what the New Testament teaches in regards to providing in the house of God for those who teach well. From verses twenty-one and twenty-two, we read of a broad instruction given by the king. saying that all in the region are to provide what is necessary for Ezra and to do so with the understanding that Ezra is among them as a teacher of the law of God. And reading that, I could not help but remember of Jesus sending out the 70 disciples. You remember that story? And telling them not to take extra supplies, but to expect each town to provide for them. Why Because they were bringing the good news. And as recipients of the good news, they should provide for those who were bringing the news. The towns that did not provide would be blessed, I'm excuse, that did provide would be blessed, and the towns that did not provide, they would be cursed. From verse 23, we hear an acknowledgement again that the God of Ezra is the God of heaven. And because that is so, whatever he requires by way of Ezra is to be done. What is acknowledged by the king is what Jesus said to the 70 that he sent out. A curse is possible if the people refuse the good news. So why refuse and bring such a curse upon yourself? Such is a rhetorical question. No man in his right mind would do such a thing. From verses 24 through 26, it is prescribed the extent of the authority to Ezra, given to Ezra by the king. And the parameters placed upon the local rulers who were to fully cooperate with Ezra regarding all the things that he requests. And there is strict judgment as a part of the extension of Ezra's authority given to him by the king. As believers in Jesus, we should draw parallels in this giving of authority. To the authority Jesus gave his church. When he spoke to the apostles in the gospel according to St. John, he said, Whatever you bind on earth shall be bound. And whatever you loose shall be loosened. And remember when he sent out those same 70 we've been referring to. And they returned to him. They were rejoicing because they had cast out demons in the name of Jesus. And it worked. Jesus, in hearing this, described seeing Satan and his power falling from the sky. Christians are told, as Paul told Timothy, that we are not given a spirit of timidity. But one of power and authority. We the believers in Jesus Christ have authority over the principalities and powers of this and every age. Amen and Amen. A letter given by an earthly king that allows for a chosen servant of God to go forward And to build the kingdom of God. Is that not evidence that God goes before his people? to prepare a way for them to be successful successful in fulfilling his will. What I believe the Holy Spirit wants us to be convinced of is that God has written a letter for his church. to go forward into the world so as to have dominion over principalities and rulers of this world in order to preach and teach the gospel of Jesus Christ so that men and women can be free. Then it is one thing to say that we have such a letter of authority, a letter of freedom to preach and to teach the gospel. And quite another. Quite another thing to live and thus act out that same authority and freedom. But what would it take to convince us that God has given us a letter to go forward? The following is a story told by a college student named Bella House. Bella fondly remembers a night at the movies when her father told her about how God went before him. She starts, we were standing in line waiting to watch The Incredibles, one of my favorite movies. I'm eight, he says, and my brother and sister are with me, hands in their pockets, looking suspicious. Stop squirming, I say. I'm the oldest, and I know what's at stake. My dad leans in to talk to us. We're almost in. You're doing great. But we stop This is dangerous territory. We haven't made it into the dark interior of the theater. Instead, we've turned off and are standing in line. I smell of the popcorn wafing toward us Get the big one, mom says. Her favorite thing about going to the movies is the popcorn. Everything else is just extra. We're going to be compromised, I glance around. Once, twice, no one is looking this way. Let's get some water cups too, mom says. I groan, but soon we're walking away When the whole family was settled into the theater before any commercials or premieres, my dad starts with his story. He says, it was as if we were part of a James Bond film, except that we were missionaries. Smuggling Bibles into the mainland of China with the very real possibility of getting discovered. We did it a number of times. We would go at four or five in the morning. It was still dark. All of us cold and able to see our breath, shaking with nervous, exciting energy. We showed up at an apartment, three or four at a time. Gathered in the main room, the people we had come to see would start to tell us our directions for the day. Every time we went in, it would be different. A new place to leave from, on a different train. And there were slides to teach us. The slides were exact. Pictures of every train station, every train, every street turn that we would have to take. We would have to memorize everything. There was never any written instructions. The customs station was right after you walked off the train wherever you were going. And if you made it through that, then all you'd have to do was follow the street signs that the slides had indicated earlier Making it to a hotel entrance that you'd already seen on a slide. You would go down from the first floor to the basement. There would be bathrooms next to a series of lockers. Our job would be to take the Bibles that we had smuggled there, place them in a bag, and put them in the lockers. And after, we would need to give the claim ticket to our Chinese contact, a man who had traveled with us and was part of the secret underground church. so that he would take them on from there. My father paused for a moment, looked around, and continued. Every time we did this, when we got there, they would say, okay, now we want you to pray about how you want to bring the Bibles in. It's completely up to you. You can put them in your bag. You can hide them. You can do anything you want. So we would pray. Once I rolled them up and put them around my legs and around my stomach and chest and arms. And I put just taped them to myself and then threw on my huge coat. It was an uncomfortable train ride. But when I got to the customs house, I walked right through. I went into the bathroom, and the only difficulty was how loud the tape was as I pulled it off of myself and the Bibles. I stuffed them in an old suitcase and then went and then it went through baggage claim. I received the claim ticket. and put the suitcase where it needed to go and handed my claim ticket on to m over to my Chinese contact, who would then pass it on to the right people. Another time I prayed, and I really felt that I should just put the Bibles into a big suitcase. So I got one, a roller bag, and filled it completely full of Bibles. There was nothing else in there. No clothes, no anything, just Bibles. And I also had my other smaller bag with with my clothes and about ten Bibles. After my train ride, I got to customs and I had uh the x-ray had them x-ray my bags And they x-rayed the first. And this Chinese lady who could have started for the Chinese basketball team as was a head taller than me, was starting to yell at me in Chinese. My 6'2 Grand German father smirked, thinking back at the scene. He said, Bible, Bible, Bible were the only words of her yelling that I could understand. She grabbed my bag and then led me over to a table. She opened my bag, took out the ten Bibles, and she's still yelling in Chinese, You Bible, you Bible! Now I should tell you, I wasn't nervous. We were told that they couldn't do much to us as Westerners because of international relations. The worst they could do to us was to detain us in a room, question us, and yell at us some more. This made us untouchable in a way. And we were told by our friends that lived there to take advantage of it. I think you and I would say that they had a letter from the King of Kings. He continues. They as natives could be thrown in prison, and at one point one of the men, a part of the underground church, was thrown into prison, and that created a lot of distress for his family and the church. In the meantime, no one looks at the other little the other rollerbag that I have. So I'm standing there with my suitcase and the rollerbag, and the rollerbag is just filled, 50 Bibles at least, probably more than that. And she's just yelling at me. And then another guy comes over and he's yelling at me too. And I still can't understand any of it. And finally she says, you go. I say, go. Yeah, go. They stamp my passport, I grab it, my suitcase, and the roller bag, and I just walk in. And I got this huge bag of Bibles through customs. So I don't know if God just made the bag invisible to them, or if maybe they were Christians, but working for the government. So they thought if they made a big scene about the first bag, no one would question that they missed the other one I'm not sure. I don't know what happened. I really can't tell you. I think we do. He had a letter from the King of Kings. What can I tell you though is where the Bibles do go. Our Chinese contact, a part of the Underground Church, gives out the Bibles to all the churches across the mainland China. The Bibles are then cut apart and rebound as individual books. So instead of one person getting a whole Bible, the whole church is given a Bible The 66 portions would be traded back and forth. Oh, you have Luke? Well, I have axe. Let's trade. And they would And so Bibles that we smuggled in wouldn't be wasted. They would be poured over and memorized and passed on so that everyone in the community could read God's word. He paused for a moment, letting that sink into our shining faces. We loved his stories, and we loved hearing about how he helped hundreds of people hear about Jesus. Music started playing over the speaker and the lights began to dim. It's starting, whispered my brother, as the previews began to play. My dad leans over to me. Hey Bella Past those gummy bears. I pull them out of my stuffed pocket and hand them to him. Nice work smuggling them in, he says, before opening the bag. Does God go before his people today? Has he written letters for us to overcome obstacles of the enemy today? He most certainly has, and Bella's father knows. He has written letters for all who believe in his son. And the letters are for each of us to go forward, to increase the kingdom of God. And the only question is, what are you going to do with your letter? Let us pray. Of God and Father, this short narrative of Ezra receiving a letter most certainly reminds us of what you have written for us, and that it is written in the blood of Christ, your Son, our Lord. And so give us all the more confidence to know that as we go forward, that as we go forward in your name, that we do so with your blessing, we do so with you going before us. Father, may we have every confidence that you desire to use us to build your kingdom. In Jesus' name we pray. Amen.

sermons.text: Always tell me the same thing. In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. We are covering Ezra chapter 8 today, and we started reading at verse 15. But I will be mentioning the verses prior to that, so uh that would be good for your reference. I begin, however, with a song. The lyrics go as follows. Life was filled with guns and war, and all of us got trampled on the floor. I wish we'd all been ready. Children died, the days grew cold, a piece of bread could buy a bag of gold. I wish we all had been ready. There's no time to change your mind. The sun has come and you've been left behind. A man and wife asleep in bed. She hears a noise and turns her head. He's gone. I wish we'd all been ready. Two men walking up a hill. One disappears and one's left standing still. I wish we'd all been ready. There's no time to change your mind. The sun has come and you've been left behind. Children died. The days grew cold. A piece of bread could buy a bag of gold. I wish we'd all been ready. There's no time to change your mind. The sun has come, and you've been left behind. The fathers spoke, the demons died. How could you have been so blind? There's no time to change your mind. The sun has come, and you have been left behind. These lyrics just read are from a song written by a Christian rock musician named Larry Norman. Back in nineteen sixty-nine. Can you believe that? Nineteen sixty-nine It is based on the teaching that Jesus is going to return, and to do so at a time when many say that they are Christian, being unaware that they are not ready for his return. The way of teaching about the end time says that Jesus will rapture, take us out, the church, out of the world, the true faithful. And take them into a heavenly hope, while others who were unprepared will have to stay behind and suffer Many tribulations and even go through the great battle known as Armageddon. I have faded in sermons and Bible studies over my 18 years with you That this interpretation of the end times, beginning with a rapture, and then a tribulation, and then Armageddon, is flawed. It is a flawed understanding of the Bible. And the simple fact that it is a new teaching about the end of days should be reason enough For us to highly scrutinize this teaching. But the one thing this view of the end days does Is literally scare the hell out of anyone who wants to be with Jesus But fears that he or she will not be found worthy. And according to that song means not be ready. The lyrics to the song just read are scary. Guns and wars seem to dominate, and gold can't buy bread, and children are dead. And those who weren't ready for the return of Jesus will witness it all and suffer through it all. That is scary stuff indeed. And being scared can be motivating as a factor to either fight or fight. And since the principalities and powers that which we are to fight are spiritual, Well, those who are left behind only have one option, that is to flight. But where is there to go to be safe from all of this devastation? There is no place. And it is scary indeed. Now I got to thinking about being left behind when reading of Ezra taking inventory of the people who had come with him on his journey to Jerusalem. Chapter 8 is a look back at chapter 7. Chapter 8 provides the details as to who came along with Ezra having received all that he needed to return to Jerusalem. And I admit I am concerned for those of you who have not been with us every Sunday as we walked through Ezra You may not have caught up on the internet listening to the sermons. And so I get concerned that if you hear only bits and pieces of the narrative, it starts to become irrelevant. For your understanding. I therefore wish to rehearse very quickly where we are. The remaining two tribes of Israel were taken into captivity by the Babylonians at the beginning of the 6th century BC, a long time ago. The Babylonians were eventually overthrown by the Persians, and under Persian rule, some Jews who were in captivity were allowed to return to their capital city of Jerusalem near seventy years later Only to find that the temple and the walls around the city were in great disrepair. The first wave of the Jews came back to the city of Jerusalem under the leadership of Zerubbabel, who was a political leader. They first set about the task of rebuilding the temple. Ezra, a high priest, was then allowed to return to Jerusalem to beautify the temple. and return the valuables to its treasury that had been taken by Nebuchadnezzar, and returned those valuables to the place of the holy, or the holy place, and then to the holy of holies. To go back to the holy city of Jerusalem, you remember that Ezra needed to procure proof of his high priesthood. Proof of his skill as a teacher of the law, and then proof of the permission given to him by the king of Persia. He had satisfied all that was necessary for his return, but there were still problems. According to chapter 8, where we are in the narrative, Ezra learned that the Levites, the tribe of men commissioned by God to serve in the temple, had not returned with him. Such an omission was a big deal. Consider that a call had gone out to any and all Jews who wanted to return to the Holy City And upon hearing the call, none, none of those who were Levites, the priests of God, none of them heeded the call. None. Consider even further that the very existence of the tribe of Levi was so that their descendants could worship within the temple of God. It then can only be concluded that upon hearing the call to return to Jerusalem, the holy city of God, the Levites rejected the call with the attitude Of preferring being in captivity under Persian rule. It is difficult. To imagine how they could not see such a choice as being greatly offensive to God. It is to be accepted that there are men who are called of God to the task of leading God's people who do so by finding the easiest route. We can well assume that in the captivity in the lands of Persia, synagogues had been set up. where these priests had prayed and preached God's law while keeping the Sabbath and having God's people gather each week on that Saturday. But when the temple was open to them and the true service they were ordained to practice was available to them. They chose to remain in the synagogues where it was safe for them. There is no right apology for this choosing safety over God's call. There is no explanation for this that puts these Levites in a good light. They were cowards. They were not leaders as they were ordained to be. They are certainly not the role models that God expected them to be To be light, to be safe, to receive a regular paycheck is as much as some men desire. They gain what it is for them, the whole world. And as Jesus said, lose their soul. They lose their soul because they know that God has called them to something greater, something more profound, and it is a call that will cost them their identity, their earthly security. Jerusalem at the time was a very unsafe place in terms of having enemies around the city. They were hostile to the Jews and hostile to their reconstruction of the temple. And they were hostile to any favoritism given to them by the king of Persia. And thus, if any Levite were to go to Jerusalem, he would face enemies and he would be a prime target because he's a leader of the people. And when they heard of this possibility, this unsafe area, they said, no thanks. No thanks said them all. It has been said that this return of the Israelites to the holy city of Jerusalem is to be considered like a second Exodus. Being similar to Israel exiting out of Egypt. And the reluctance of many to return to Jerusalem. You remember it's similar to those who during the Exodus, when they were faced with adversity, they desired to return back to Egypt. We turn back to slavery rather than be free and face their possible demise. Live free or die. That is not in the heart of some. Not during the exodus, not during the return from Persia, and not today. In chapter 8, verse 18, we read that Ezra did indeed procure the necessary Levites to go along with him. Even though they were reluctant, he was able to convince them. And it is at that moment that Ezra needs to publicly acknowledge the hand of God in this return. God had overcome the wills of men. God had to intervene into the hearts of men in order to get them to do as he willed. And as Ezra desires. Thus Ezra says, the good hand of God was upon us. Verse 15. He then says and confesses, when it is evident that there was nothing that they could have done to change the situation, God had to intervene, and God did. The remainder of the narrative in chapter 8 tells how Ezra struggled as to whether or not receive help from the soldiers of the king of Persia. He wanted his faith in God and the faith of the people in God to take care of the people and take care of their possessions. They wanted to be protected by God, not by the horses and soldiers of Persia. And so Ezra prays over their possessions. He prays over the people. And as they travel, they are kept safe from robbers and enemies. And Ezra pronounces, as you see in verse 31, where there he says plainly, God delivered us. The end of the narrative of chapter eight describes how the valuables for the temple were weighed and accounted for. And this was followed by a ceremony of worshiping, where those offered praise to God, offerings to God, who were once children in captivity, under the Babylonians. And then they were ruled by the Persians. And now as adults they had come home to the city of God and were worshiping him freely, freely as their souls desired. Such is the story of Ezra returning to Jerusalem to fulfill his call to beautify the temple and to beautify the people. And this beautifying of the people that will come soon enough, as we shall see in chapter 9. But where I want our focus to be, our attention to be this morning Is the reality of those who were left behind, those who did not come on the journey. Under Zerubbabel, the first wave of the Jews returning to Jerusalem numbered 42,360. Under Ezra, the number of Jews that return was around 5,000. Scholars project that the number of people that return to Jerusalem under Zerubbabel and under Ezra is no more than one-fourth of the total Jewish population that lived in exile in the land of Persia. And that means But the vast majority of God's people chose to stay behind and to live in captivity rather than return to the holy city and to worship God as the law commanded. Only one fourth. Adding these people to the number of Levites who were reluctant to return, and the Levites who never did return. We have different groupings of people that resemble the Christian church today. Different groupings that resemble you and I. The first grouping, the first grouping is made up of those who are in the world and of the world. They think they are Christian, but their way of thinking and living is a product of the world around them. These people have grown accustomed to how the world around them works. And they have modified their lives to adapt and to be a part of the world. These are the people to whom St. Paul says, be not conform to this world These are the ones for whom the law reads from Exodus 23, you shall not follow a multitude to do evil, neither shall you side with many who pervert justice. And hear this warning from St. James to these people of the world. Know you not that friendship with the world means enmity with God. These are the people for whom Saint John describes as having once been with us But have since left us, and because they have left us, we can conclude that they never were truly a part of us. Such is sad. The existence of such people is painful, and it is real. When I first read The Last Battle, which is the last installment of the Narnia book series written by C. S. Lewis. I remember resenting how Susan, the once queen of Narnia, and known as the gentle queen, how she is described. The three other children, Peter, Edmund, and Lucy, all die in a train accident. And that takes them on to their final journey. Their journey to the real Narnia, which is heaven. Susan, on the other hand, is left behind. She is described by other characters in the book as being only interested in nylons, lipstick, and invitations. She is described by Polly Plummer as follows, quote, She wasted all her school time wanting to be the age she is now. And she'll waste all the rest of her life trying to stay that age. Her whole idea is to race on to the silliest time of one's life as quick as she can. And then stop there as long as she can. Thus the reader fears that Susan Who had tasted and experienced the goodness of Narnia and the goodness of Aslan, she would be lost forever. And such is easy to resent because we don't want such to be possible, and we don't want such to be possible for anyone, especially not for ourselves. The second grouping is made up of those who want to believe, who want to be brave, who want to be a part of this return from exile. Only fear has gripped them, and thus they require a testimony of those who have gone before them. These people are weak in their faith, and therefore they need support and love and they need examples in front of them. To these people, Saint Paul said that Christians have not been given a spirit of timidity, but one of authority. For these people, mature Christians, are instructed to first consider the weak in faith among them and to adjust their lives accordingly, so that the weak would not be offended. For these people, Saint Paul said, follow me, for I follow Christ Such people do not want to be left behind, but are waiting for their faith to be built up so that they can walk confidently when they return from exile. Such people are looking for examples in the lives of people who say they are Christian as they want to live the life of faith. But they want those lives to show evidence that faith is real and the promises of God are realized. I imagine the apostles being in this category. For even though they left everything to follow Jesus, still in the end they looked to find safe places. They hid until they heard the news from the women that Jesus was not in the tomb. They hid until Peter and John ran ahead and found the tomb empty. They hid until Jesus appeared to them in a room with no open doors. And even some like Thomas still wouldn't believe until he could know for sure himself and not depend on the testimony of others. Each of them had a level of weakness that needed verification, and each had a requirement of verification that needed to be met. before they would come out of their perceived safe places. Even like the Levites in Ezra's day, some had to be coerced into coming out of hiding. But when they did, when they did come out, they were free. I anticipate That these groupings hit home with each of us. Each of us knows someone who likes to claim a form of Christian faith, and we want them to be Christian But their daily living proves that they are of the world. And that means they have chosen to stay in exile, like the majority of people in Ezra's day. And it is important that we do not turn a blind eye to such people, regardless of how close we are to them. If such people describe our children, a close friend, a mother, a father The devil would want us to believe everything's okay. Not to worry about his or her soul. But that is a lie. Our worry is to turn into prayer and faith that the salvation of the soul of our dear loved one It can be achieved. Our worry is to turn into words of truth and hope for that loved one to repent and to be forgiven. That is the only way, and we must not deny that. The second grouping consists of many people we know, and it may include us. We believe, or we know people who believe in Jesus, but they need our help. We need help. We need help to believe with all of our heart. We need help to step out of our safe place and to get going to the place that is our eternal home. And courageous Christians are needed to help Christians who fear, who are staying in that safe place. The good news is that our God has been patient, not wanting any to perish. And so people in every grouping have the opportunity today to step out and to start toward Jerusalem. The good news is that if you are breathing, if a loved one is breathing, it is not too late. So together at this time let us pray for them. Our gracious and merciful Father, we thank of those left behind. those who have become of the world and claim still the faith in you. And we ask, gracious Lord, that you would intervene, that you would change the wills and hearts of men and women. To see that being of the world is being enmity an enemy of God, of you And so bring them to repentance, give them faith for salvation, and help them on the road to eternal life And from those who fear, for those who believe yet need help in their unbelief. Father, help them to see those who have gone before, those in front of them, those who say, Follow me, for I follow Christ. Help them to step out of their supposed safe place and to start the way towards the heavenly city. These we pray for, and we pray for ourselves in Jesus' name. Amen.

sermons.title: Give Thanks? No thanks
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Be seated. I want to publicly thank Becky for filling in. We do want to be praying for Janice. She is under the weather tonight. And I do encourage you to note that this is a service in which you have an opportunity to give God thanks and praise for whatever He has laid upon your heart And uh wish you'd be thinking about that even now before we come to that time The passage for the homily tonight is First Thessalonians five eighteen First Thessalonians five eighteen. Give thanks in all circumstances. Give thanks in all circumstances. I am going to choose to rebel against God's instruction tonight. I am rebelling against his instruction to give thanks in all circumstances. Hear me out. I choose not to give thanks, not to give thanks for the construction on bridges one and two. On Highway 26, leading east away from Eldersburg or west toward Eldersburg I have lived here 18 plus years, and no such work has been done on one said bridge. until these last two years, and that work is constant. And such constant work has made me late on several occasions And there is no warning that such work will start, nor is there warning as to when it will stop. It starts, and then it stops, and then it starts again. And now both bridges are being worked on at the same time. So that drivers have to stop and wait in line at one bridge, only to travel less than a mile and wait again at the next bridge. I say end Liberty Road Bridge work by doing it right the first time Can I get an amen? Amen. I also choose not to give thanks this day or any day for walnuts. Think about it. It adds up. Ralnuts are way too difficult to deshell. A vice plier instrument is required No worthwhile nut should need its own true tool to deshell. Also The nut is dangerous for people like me, who, if eaten fresh, will have our throats swollen so that we can barely breathe. Also, walnuts have ruined, ruined perfectly good chocolate chip cookies. Great care goes in to getting the right amount of sugar, vanilla extract, to get the dough consistent And even to rightly number the chocolate chips per cookie, only to have the taste hijacked by walnuts. Those who want walnuts on their cookies should make and eat walnut cookies while leaving chocolate chip cookies alone. Can I get an amen? I also choose not to give thanks for commercials that follow every kickoff of a pro football game. The games are long enough, the quality of play today is poor enough, to not have a team score To watch the boring extra point, break for commercial, come back to see a kickoff that usually isn't returned anyways, and then have a new set of commercials The games are not worth the time as they play these days, very poor quality of football, and many players are not worth supporting Stop commercial breaks after kickoffs. Can I get an amen? I also choose not to give thanks for the national news media in these United States. We get it. You hate President Donald Trump. Fine. You hate those who voted for Donald Trump. Fine. But if Christians of the first century can put up with being ruled by Nero, Nero, who use Christians as lion food and tiki torches Then anyone can endure the Donald. If Christians can heed the words of Saint Paul and pray for their political leaders, like Nero. And Domitian and Trajan, all who murdered Christians. It seems that the secular world news maker-uppers can be civil about the Trumpster. Can I get an amen? Finally, at least for tonight, I choose not to give thanks for the majority of information people post on social media. Well, I want to know how my grandchildren, nephews and nieces, and brothers and sisters are doing, and the blessings of my fellow Christians that they are experiencing. I do not want to know what your meal looks like that you enjoyed at Bob Evans. Nor do I want to know what the roadkill looked like when you ran over it this morning. Nor do I want to know what your used socks look like that you're trying to sell to your next door neighbor There used to be such thing as TMI. Too much information. Well, we ought to get back to that. No more TMI on social media Can I get an amen? It must be questioned regarding why St. Paul instructs Christians to give thanks in all circumstances. What is the primary purpose? Why can't we do just as I have done and draw lines in proverbial sand? And say that there are certain things we will not be thankful for, and have reasonable and thus legitimate reasons not to be thankful. Well, I have to answer my own questions, don't I? Yes, I do. It is an important principle to live by that if you're going to ask questions, ask serious questions, then you had better be mature enough and strong enough to hear the answers The context of St. Paul's instruction for Christians to give thanks in all circumstances is the simple directive to pray. He first says pray and then he says give thanks in all circumstances. Thus all Christians are to pray at all times, that is, the Christian life. It is a life that is in constant communication with God. Well, of course it is There is nothing better for the human soul than to be in constant communication and thus a constant relationship with the God who made heaven and earth and who holds all things together. Thus, as a greater detail to the type of prayers Christians are to be engaged in We are to be engaged in prayer of thanksgiving for all things. In everything, Christians are to give thanks in every circumstance, in joy and in sorrow. For everything, for prosperity, and for adversity in every place, in the house of God, and on the bed of sickness. Christians should not only be engaged in constant prayer, but in constant prayer of thanksgiving. Our prayers should partake largely of the nature of thanksgiving. For this, this thankful spirit is the will of God. It is God's desire for each of his children in Christ Jesus, the sphere in which we will Live in God, displayed before Him a heart of gratefulness, a heart of thankfulness. Consider how it makes so much sense. That because Jesus, his life, death, and resurrection, ascension enables our forgiveness and our inheritance that we should be living lives of thankfulness at all times. And there are other passages, like that of Romans chapter 5, beginning at verse 4. There, St. Paul describes Christians giving glory to God in the midst of their tribulations. And from St. James, we are instructed to count it all, all of it, every part of a moment in life, count it all to be joy. Even as he says, when we fall into various trials. Saint Peter states such joyfulness as a fact. As if it is naturally a part of a Christian's disposition to greatly rejoice, even though for a little while our lives may have grieved us. with various trials. What else is there to conclude other than Christians are to be a people that express thankfulness in all circumstances? And such thankfulness consists of giving glory to God, even in the midst of when we are going through difficult times that we call trials. It is choosing a countenance of joyfulness in the midst of said difficult times, even to the point of rejoicing. Because we are to have faith that whatever it is we are currently experiencing, there is a greater outcome that will give glory to God. Thus, I must be challenged in regard to any right that I might claim or have claimed. to my own predisposition of being not thankful Choosing to be not thankful in certain circumstances is choosing to not be a follower of Jesus Christ. Choosing to not give glory to God in the midst of tribulations is to not obey God. Choosing to not count it joy, to not be joyful, in the midst of different types of trials, is choosing to not be as Jesus is And there is no righteousness in such a choice or such an attitude. And so I must be thankful for construction on bridges closest to Eldersburg. Because, well, they procure the safety of many people in the future, and the waiting sanctifies my spirit That I might trust in God for the moments I am delayed and for the discipline my life needs that requires me to plan ahead. Instead of traveling without preparation for possible delays, for my rebuke For being unthankful, can I get an amen? I must also choose to be thankful for walnuts Some people, enough people to bother me, like walnuts. And to my horrible surprise, some people like walnuts in their chocolate chip cookies Therefore, I am to be thankful that people have the opportunity to enjoy what they like, and when people put walnuts into chocolate chip cookies, I have the opportunity To think of the desire and wants of other people rather than my own. Walnuts and chocolate chip cookies is another opportunity to die to myself, and that is always a good thing. Can I get an amen? I must also choose to be thankful for commercials during inopportune times, during professional football games. Commercials help these games be shown in my living room. Commercials are sometimes more entertaining than the games. And commercials help me stop thinking about what I want, but accept what I cannot control. For that rebuke, I need an amen. Also I must be thankful for national media and their bias reporting I could be thankful that it sheds light on ingrained hypocrisy of our secular society, but that doesn't please God. What pleases God is to be thankful for revelations and how to pray for the lost, the deceived, the spiteful, the bitter, and souls that choose to be enraged. I, as a Christian, need to pray for their souls and not for better treatment of a standing president or anyone else, for that matter. Reporter and talking heads are people, and they need a Savior. And for that rebuke, I need an Amen. Finally and somewhat surprisingly to me I must be thankful for social media that displays pictures of dinner plates and other unnecessary posts. that provide nothing interesting or informative for society as a whole. And I am to be thankful for another opportunity to die to myself. Does not make social media about me. And I am to be thankful that I can turn it off and not be a part of it at any time that I choose, and I'll assert assume your amen on that point. So we are instructed to be thankful in all circumstances. But we can settle for most, right? That should be enough. No. He says all. But surely we can have certain things we are unthankful for? No. Thankful in all circumstances And we give thanks not just because of the good we can make out of those circumstances. We are to be thankful because we have been told to do so. We have been told to be so because we are a people of faith. We are a people who give thanks in all circumstances because we believe God. And we believe that he works all things to the good for those who love him and are called according to his purpose. That is what God said Amen. Let us pray

sermons.title: Faith Taken Seriously
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. I've told a similar story to this in different venues. We are in Ezra chapter 9, a very difficult section of scripture, and as such, the topic will not be easy to digest. But I begin with this story. My second year of teaching Western philosophy to college students, we were in the section on ethics. And I was hearing papers about an ethical dilemma that I had placed before them. The students were to imagine themselves as part of a hiking trip. made up of religious people, of whom they were one of the party. And one of the beliefs of this group was they confessed that cannibalism was sin. That belief came into play because the hiking trip became a disaster when a snow blizzard overcame the hikers And after several days of being stranded, they ran out of food and found no wild game about them, and some in their party had died. The ethical dilemma was if the remaining hikers should choose to eat Those who had died in order to remain alive as long as there was a possibility of being rescued. Every answer given out of the first five students who presented, every answer justified why they would choose cannibalism over death. Not one of the students' answers considered the religious objection that I placed in a scenario. Upon hearing the fifth response in favor of cannibalism, I once again pointed out that the presenter was ignoring. the religious convictions placed in the dilemma, and I followed up with the challenge as to why this religious conviction was being ignored. The response I received unnerved me even to today. The female student presenting at the time stated that she did not include religious conviction against cannibalism because she had never met anyone who was that serious about their religion. What I ask you is an appropriate response to such a statement. I could only thank ouch on behalf of the church and Lord Jesus have mercy on us all. The narrative from Ezra 9 is the reference that I have been using These past few weeks when I have said that Ezra's responsibility was to come back to Jerusalem And to beautify the temple, and then to beautify the people of Israel The beauty of the temple was provided by hard work and by the returning of furnishings that were stolen by Nebuchadnezzar, and these were made of fine wood and overlaid with gold. To beautify the people of God, prevalent sin amongst the people had to be identified, confessed. repented of, and then proper obedience restored. The problem was that the prevalent sin was not simple And proper restoration and obedience meant great personal pain and heartache. And with these considerations, this is what the appropriate concern was and the question that needed to be asked. Was there anyone in Jerusalem that was that serious about their religion? Asked another way, did anyone in Israel have a true faith in God? Now, we can answer that by saying at least Ezra did. Anyone else remained to be seen. But let us hear again what God had said regarding the issues of this sin that Israel had committed. The first statement comes from Leviticus chapter 18, verse 3, all the way back after the Exodus. God said this. You must not do as they do in Egypt, where you used to live, and you must not do as they do in the land of Canaan, where I am bringing you. Do not follow their practices. And what were these practices? Well, Leviticus 20 has a list as to what the worshipers of false idols were doing and what Israel was not to be doing. To worship false idols, there were requirements. Those requirements were the offering of children for sacrifice. It was the turning to spiritists as mediums. It was the practice of the fiality. It was the practice of incest in all of its various perverted arrangements. It was because of such abominable sins that God abhorred the nations that surrounded Israel and forbid them. Forbid them from making covenants with any nation, or making a covenant from one family to another. Which meant that they could not intermarry with these nations. Such is what God clearly said in more than one place. and in more than one context, and therefore this issue was without equivocation. And yet Israel disobeyed. And it was the nations around them that helped lead them to a state of perpetual disobedience. Disobedience that led them to become a vassal state of Babylon, and then a nation in captivity, and then a nation under slavery, under Persian rule. That's where we find Israel in Ezra. Thus the sin that started the people of God down the road to exile, down the road to slavery, was being repeated. by those who had returned from exile, a people who were supposed to be free again As stated, God had been clear about his prohibition for his people to intermarry with people of the land of Canaan. The explicit general reason for this prohibition was that the people of Canaan had been prostituting themselves to false gods. and have been doing so for generations. And they had had every intention of leading God's people into the same The people of Abraham's race, they wanted to be like them, worshiping false idols. It may be helpful to note that Ezra himself did not personally raise this issue Actually, Ezra was simply teaching the Bible. And the sin of the people became so evident. That the people needed to confess it, from the Levites to the average man. God's law had been exposed and exposed the sin. And anyone who heard it had a conscience that was found guilty and needed to acknowledge their sin. And because of the day and age in which we live, it is necessary to point out, necessary, That God's law of banning Jews from intermarrying with the people who were of the land of Canaan, that law was not racist. Was not. After all, Moses married a Midianite. Boaz of the line of David married Ruth, who was a Moabite. Both Moses' wife and Boaz's wife put their trust in the God of their husbands, and that made them a part of the covenant. It made them a part of God's people. The actual problem was the detestable practices of the people of Canaan, as was listed earlier And the very possible reality that the men intermarrying with such women, with such practices, would draw themselves into such practices. The person of King Solomon had always been the most prominent example to the Jews of a man being led into false worship by foreign wives. Verse two of chapter nine gives us the evidence as to what God sees as most important. when it comes to intermarrying with people who worship false gods. The confession of the people states that they had intermarried and thus mixed Mixed the holy seed with the people of the land. The holy seed. The holy seed was the promised Messiah. Now this mixture was in no way a concern, again, for a mixture of race. As pointed out, Ruth was of a different race, but she ended up being of the lineage of Jesus. As was Rahab, of a different race, and she was of the lineage of Jesus, who was the holy seed. So the dangerous mixture of the holy seed promised to crush that serpent's head in the covenant found in the book of Genesis. The danger was the mixture of false gods, not different races. Next, we have the intercessory prayer offered by Ezra after the people confessed their sin. And this prayer provides a type of Jesus who intercedes for you and I. He intercedes regarding all of the manners that we have mixed ourselves with that which is unholy. There are no excuses made in Ezra's prayer as is Jesus' prayer for us. There are no easy ways out of the situation. These Jews had brought it on themselves, and the response is going to be painful. There most certainly was no option to continue the practice of intermarrying that was begun, and we find a rhetorical question offered in verse 14. God had not delivered justice upon them as their sin deserved, and to continue such a practice would only ask for that judgment. But for Ezra, the sin of the people, and as I said, both clergy and laity alike. The sin is a testimony for him against the entire nation of Israel down through the ages. In verse 7, he rehearses the guilt of the days of their forefathers, who were guilty of delivering the entire nation into the hands of foreign kings. In verse 9, Ezra rehearses the once enslaved state of the people of God in Persia, and how God did not forsake them, but took them out of bondage and extended his mercy, reviving them. And as they returned to Jerusalem to restore what had been broken down, they knew not to give their daughters and sons away to foreign people. Foreign people who worshiped false gods. But no matter how clear the instructions were, the people were guilty. Of every walk, of every status, of every tribe, they were guilty of intermarrying foreign people, and thus bringing the camp of Israel, bringing into their camp foreign gods. Who were not gods at all, but deaf and dumb idols and evil spirits that worship the devil himself. And I ask if we are all alike when we think about what to do next. Are we all alike in terms of where our minds and hearts go when we hear of such sin and then wonder how it should be rectified? Who among us today can agree that such intermarrying is wrong? As wrong as can be, and yet And yet we imagine that the best thing that can be done to help the situation is to forgive the wrongdoers. encouraged their foreign spouses to worship the God of Israel and to continue as they had been doing to enable the families to stay together. After all, we so easily conclude that the keeping together of each family unit is the most important principle of all If that is how you and I are thinking, is it not fair to challenge said principle regarding from where such thinking comes from? Where in the Bible can this justification be found? Family together first, no matter what. Where does God say in any variety of ways that keeping the family unit together is the most important principle to follow? There is no place that God teaches such a principle. Even though when he Makes honoring thy father and thy mother one of the top ten priorities Yet that commandment cannot stand alone. That commandment makes sense only if the first commandment is followed, which is that there is but one true God and no other gods before him. Only then, only then can we say to honor thy father and mother, because we know the one true God. Remember these words of Jesus. You can get that all way. Remember these words of Jesus. If anyone comes to me and does not hate Father and mother, wife and children, brothers and sisters, yes, even his own life, such a person cannot be my disciple Do not these words apply to the sin of Israel in the days of Ezra? If you say that they do not, then you need to tell me what they mean. If you're convinced they do not, then we need to have you write a dissertation and explain it so that it can be shared with all Christians. So that we don't have to feel bad about broken families that are broken because of the sin of intermarrying, intermarrying with unbelievers. And Christians loving family members first before loving Jesus. We all need to hear that dissertation. But no such dissertation has been written because the sin of the people of Ezra's day is obvious. And the meaning of Jesus' words regarding loving him first, that meaning is plain. The real problem, the actual issue, the ultimate dilemma is caused by our emotions. For it is what the breaking up of a family does to our emotions that causes us to look for another alternative instead of the obvious Of breaking God's law and the plain spoken words of Jesus. It can only be imagined how many souls have been compromised into the hands of the devil. By the emotions of a mother who insisted that it was perfectly acceptable for her daughter baptized into the covenant of Christ, having professed a faith in Jesus, it's okay for her to be married to an unbeliever for the simple reason that she fell in love. And the father not wanting to have an argument with his wife allows the mother to give her final blessing And the years pass on, and the grandchildren are a result, and none is baptized. None are raised to hear their father pray to God. None are raised to confess Jesus as Lord and Savior. Secular school is followed by more secular school, and the grandchildren are in and of the world, and the idol of the flesh is the God obeyed first and most often. In the end, that family, that faith in Jesus Christ dies with grandma and grandpa, all because the daughter fell in love with an unbeliever, and no one would deny her of said love. How many souls have been lost, families made dysfunctional, and extended families in a continuous state of bereavement because parents have blessed sinful marriages? And church authorities have looked the other way, not wanting to cause problems that would hurt their bottom line. Because we cannot answer such questions with actual numbers does not mean we cannot guess that the number is grotesque. And to the shame of many Christian families and many local churches. Behind such circumstances is the evil spirit That calls Christians and non-Christians alike to worship the false idol of earthly happiness. Of course, the idol is no happiness at all. It is a moment happiness. It is a fleeting happiness. It is mere pleasure of the flesh masquerading as happiness. And all the while, true happiness, happiness that consists of peace with God and peace with our fellow man, is nowhere among those bowing to earthly happiness. Happiness that even the ancient philosophers knew to be otherworldly is not pursued or considered because the lie has been believed. Which is that personal and immediate pleasure is the best that this world can give. That is a lie. Next week we will learn what to do when caught in a lie. It is enough for us today to ponder and deepen the truth that such happiness in this world is a lie. Religious faith amongst the people of Israel in Ezra's day was a faith of indifference. Faith of indifference doesn't believe that having faith in God really matters. And the evidence today, well that seems pretty obvious. After all, Christians today get shot by crazy people, just like Muslims do and people of no faith do. But I am called to show you why such is also a lie. The Jewish people were to have the same faith as their father Abraham. And Christians are to have the same faith as Father Abraham as well. And that faith that Abraham saw beyond his day And beyond immediate happiness, and his faith saw to the day of Jesus. Abraham saw his day and was glad. We are to see the days of Jesus ahead also, and be glad. We are to see the days of Jesus as a people serious about their Christian faith, not pursuing happiness for the sake of immediate gratification in this life. A six-pack of beer can do that. What Christians are to pursue is eternal happiness. Which is peace with God, and that is doing his will and being as he wills. I hope you heard our call-up for today. Our call-ak, our prayer for today, this Sunday before Advent, asks God to stir us up. Stir us up. And that means to wake us up. Which means to give us a living faith, which is a faith that we are serious about. By God's grace, may more college students be able to testify that there are Christians who are serious about their faith. Let us pray

sermons.title: Put It Away
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, of the Son, of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. It helped you to turn in your Bibles to Ezra chapter 10. Ezra chapter 10. And I would say that it was obviously providential that I learned this week about an upcoming movie to be released by Paramount Pictures That is based on Ezra chapter ten. It is called the Family That Stood Alone. It is a story based off of the narrative of Ezra chapter 10 and specifically verse 15 where we ended. A man by the name of Jehosiah stands against the leaders of Israel, and specifically against Ezra, the high priest. As he decides that he will not go along with the apparent forced divorce from his wife Halafa. He chooses instead to live in exile amidst pagan tribes in order to devote himself to the woman he decides is his only true love. The story depicts the hard decision made by Jehaziah to leave his family's faith, withstand persecution from his own Jewish people. And have the decision to live for the love of his life, even to embrace her gods. The story is summarized as love conquering divisiveness and love conquering dead traditions. Can we imagine watching such a movie and getting sucked into this love story of Jehosiah and Hallah as they are determined to overcome the stubbornness of their traditional leader Ezra, overcome their family that's stuck in their prejudicial ways The love of Jehosiah and Halal on the movie screen can be believed to be more pure than any religious conviction and certainly more important than any religious law. I will not be watching the movie The Family That Stood Alone. And well, no one else will be watching the movie The Family That Stood Alone because I made it up But it sounded believable, didn't it? I hope it sounded believable. At least based it off of generic love stories that Hollywood displays that have the underlying message that human romantic love conquers all circumstances, even religious circumstances. Well, just as Ezra 9, chapter 9 was a difficult passage of Scripture to address and to embrace, so too is Ezra chapter 10. For it is the outcome of the sin that was revealed in Ezra chapter 9. The sin revealed, you remember, was Jewish men who having returned from exile and settled back into the city of God, Jerusalem, they began to marry pagan wives. As shown last week, such behavior is clearly forbidden by God And it should be acknowledged that there was no possible way for any of these Jewish men not to know that to do so was against Jewish law unless they had been sleeping throughout all of their synagogue and temple worship services. And Ezra chapter ten The narrative takes us to the moment of decision regarding what is to be done about the sin of God's people intermarrying with people who worship false gods. From chapter 10, verse 1, the truth of the sins committed is verified by the weeping of the people. They are either guilty of committing such sin themselves, or they are living amidst friends and family who have committed that sin. Verse 2 is the confession, and it is a confession not just of a few guilty families, but of the entire people. For it is acknowledged that where one family or one person of a family sinned, and nothing was done against such a sin, That all of God's people are then complicit in the sin, which means guilty. The restoration stated in verse 3 is the obvious necessary response to a guilty plea. The men who took foreign wives must put away their wives, which means divorce their wives. In order to take away the godless influence that was in the midst of God's people For Ezra, the matter was not easy. It was not easy because of the re Lational and thus emotional pain of what it meant to put away these women Ezra the high priest is not a callous man, and that he is only concerned about the law of God being upheld. With no care or concern about obeying God's law and how that's affecting the people, emotionally, relationally But he cares most about not putting away godless influences that will affect the people's relationship with God. That's most important. And so Ezra displays a mourning for the sin of the people. He displays a bereavement for a loss of relationship. the brokenness that was between the people and their God. The loss of relationship will be, yes, between husbands and wives. But more importantly, the loss of relationship between God and his people. And Ezra displays the heart of God, Who does not want any to perish, and that includes the people who worship pagan gods. Instead, as he says, he desires that all people come to repentance. Not continue in their sin, but repent. So in Ezra we see a type of Jesus, how Jesus is for us. He is the intercessor between God and the sinners. He is the one who mourns for our sins. It is not his sins for which he mourns, but the sins of God's people. Jesus mourns for us when we sin. He mourns and goes through bereavement when we choose to break God's commandments He laments our decisions that choose pleasure in this life as opposed to obedience that leads to pleasures forevermore. Jesus is like a husband at the wake for his own wife For he mourns for us when we choose to be indifferent about what influences we allow to direct our lives. And so the only possible way to rectify the scenario is to put away the sin. It is to stop sinning, and to stop sinning, the guilty must separate themselves from their pagan wives. As we consider the emotional pain of such separation, I wonder if it can be softened a little bit. Maybe a little bit. Consider first how easily Mosaic law allowed for men to divorce a wife. It was not required of a husband to find anything morally wrong in his wife to justify a certificate of divorce. Now Jesus will make moral failing the requirement of his followers for divorce, but Jesus explained that God allowed for easier divorce under the law of Moses. because he knew the hardness of the hearts of the people. Thus God allowed for a lower standard to be applied until the time of Jesus He now is the eternal standard. And so divorces were not uncommon in the days of Ezra, and certainly not difficult to acquire. Many of those pagan wives could have expected to be handed a certificate of divorce for any reason at all and be sent back to their pagan tribe. Does that help?
