By his righteous obedience and sonship. Jesus is set above all the heavenly hosts in verses 8 and 9. Jesus is the creator of the heavenly hosts. That means he is eternal. The eternity of angels and the eternity of humanity depends on Jesus. Verses 10 through 12. Jesus is the victor, the spoiler and inheritor of the Father, verse 13. Jesus is unlike the angels who are, as we have noted in verse 14, ministering spirits. They serve him. Mind you, we do not need to look down upon angels for being ministering spirits. That is not the preacher's intention. It simply must be noted that to fall back on entrusting oneself to angels and looking for their place in your salvation That is bankrupt. It is empty. A simple comparison of angels to Jesus, God's Son. Should pull us away from placing our hope in creatures that are among us to serve, certainly not to save Now the most fundamental point in comparing Jesus to angels, and then he will to Moses and then to Melchizedek and anything else. Is that he must be Jesus the central focus and central hope of our lives? Like the first commandment, we cannot have any other God before him. Not in front, not next to, and not even behind. He is all in terms of our salvation. It is not Jesus and the angels that save. It is not Jesus and the Virgin Mother that saves. It is Jesus alone. That is why it is so important for the church to clarify her statements about what she believes about Jesus. More fundamental than anything else that is within our our duty to control. If Jesus is not rightly understood, then it is not Jesus we are worshiping. It is not Jesus in whom we are placing our faith, and as such, we still are in our sin. And as a more general point, I am noticing more and more how much our personal doctrines about God, what we think about God, affects our worship and our daily devotion to Him. Consider that if we think upon God as casual, God's a casual guy, then we are casual. If we think upon God as angry, then we turn into frightened disciples If we think upon our salvation as procured by our own choice, because we're smart enough to follow Him, to believe, that living out our faith is based on what we like, what we don't like, our preferred choices. In the fourth century, near the beginning of the church's ecumenical councils, Which clarified the church's teachings on the person of Jesus. When asked what kept him alive and of sound mind during his time of torture Theodorus described a young man standing by him in white, who with a soft and comfortable handkerchief wiped off the sweat from his body and spoke encouraging words. When the torment was done, the man in white, what Theodorus believed to be an angel, was gone. Such an angel might seem worthy of our praise and gratefulness as he graciously ministered to the frailties of humanity. But we are to remember that such are ministering spirits who serve at the behest of the Savior. These ministering angels are merely doing what they are told and nothing more. It is the one who orders the angel's care. Who assigns the gentle touch or helpful hand of a fellow human being? It is he that is worthy of our praise and of our thanksgiving. And he alone. And the helping hand of a stranger who appears out of nowhere is the character of the Savior. And the calming word of a gentle voice in the midst of chaos is the love of God. The protective care and spiritual battles of the heavenly host fought on our behalf. Reflect the glory of our Lord Jesus Christ. It is He alone that is to be glorified. That thing could be a ministering spirit that is there only to be directed by God to serve. It could be an earthly servant who, when he passes away or fails to live up to the ideals of Scripture, causes his followers to become prey of the devil. It could be emotions that give us earthly highs but never last long enough and become harder to achieve as time moves on. It could be traditions that we think are means of grace in and of themselves without the presence of Jesus necessary. These can eventually find us trusting in tradition rather than Christ The message of Jesus being superior to angels is the same as it will be when we are told he is superior to Moses and to Melchizedek or any other false mediator. Persevering in the faith means that we trust in Jesus for our salvation. First and last. And we never stopped. Amen. Let us pray
