The woman's seed will crush the serpent's head. The Apostle Paul to the Galatians points out that that word seed is singular. Not seeds, seed. The seed is a son to be born to a woman, to a virgin. He will crush the serpent's head. He will spill his blood upon a hill called the skull. But this promise was not immediately realized after the fall, as we know. In the meantime, God provided a covering for sin The covering was a precursor, a type, a shadow of the sacrifice of God's son. God has Adam and Eve throw away their silly coverings and provides for them coats of skin to clothe them. In doing so, God's work has to take place of God's rest. His work breaks his time of rest. God works to restore blessedness. And notice that he acts as priest, offering himself the sacrifice. He sheds the blood of the animal for men to be covered for death is required for sin. He does this to care for the immediate needs of his most important creation, man. And he does so as a foreshadow of the works of his son, who will also be a priest who offers a sacrifice himself. God did not have to do this. He did not have to do this. It would have been just, it would have been fair for him to destroy mankind at that moment. He would have been right in requiring Adam's blood. Instead, he promises a second Adam. What are we to say to this? There is no place for questioning God's ways when this is told as part of the story. All skepticism, second guessing, and doubting are silenced when we know the whole story. We are all Adam. We all have sinned, having our wills inflamed with emotion and having passions overriding our understanding. We are all Adam trying to foolishly cover up our sin with fig leaves while trying to hide from God. And then there is God. Taking on the form of a man, the second Adam, and providing death so that we can be forgiven. What can we say to this? But praise the Lord, O my soul, and all that is within me, praise his holy name. It is because of the second Adam that we can rejoice that God is a God of covenant For just as we were under the covenant of Adam in our sin, we are to understand that believing in Jesus Christ as the Christ means we are under the covenant of the second Adam And under that covenant we are forgiven. We are made sons and daughters of God. This moves us to say again. Praise the Lord, O my soul, and all that is within me, praise his holy name. Let us pray. Gracious and merciful God here in the garden. And here at the fall of our parents, we see ourselves But most importantly, we see you. Jesus, we see you. And so may we rise up and say, praise the Lord, all my soul, and all that is within me. We are truly blessed to be under the second Adam. It is in his name that we pray. Amen.

sermons.title: Flesh vs Spirit
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost, Amen. You'd be seated The reading from Genesis was the correct one this week. We are continuing our series on the book of Genesis. When a new patient Settled comfortably into the couch of his psychiatrist, the doctor said, I am not familiar with your problem. Please start from the beginning. The patient paused and then responded, Well, in the beginning I made heaven and earth. That was a joke. My wife tells me I shouldn't make jokes from the pulpit. The professional fields of psychology and psychiatry have become a part of mainstream America, and that is both good and bad. It is good because these fields recognize the importance of the psyche, of the soul of man. It is bad because too often these Professionals don't look beyond the soul of man to the one who created the soul and is himself fully spirit. They do not look to God as the answer to man's troubles. An appropriate criticism of psychology is from a Roman Catholic priest who said, on plain simple matters of fact. Any twelve men or women, and especially any twelve, are more likely to see straight and talk straight than any twelve professors of psychology for whom the world The word intelligence has ceased to have any definite meaning. Psychologists, on the whole Have taken the exercise of self-examination and made it a lifelong journey where there is no point that is ever reached. Another joke. Have to say that beforehand before I tell it. Asks the difference between a psychi- psychiatrist and a psychologist The answer is when a person says, I hate my mother, the psychiatrist responds, and how does that make you feel? Or the psychologist says, thanks for sharing In either case, nothing is resolved. No forgiveness is called for. No reconciliation occurs. I realize that I have been hard on psychologists and psychiatrists, and I do not want to pass such criticism on to Christian psychologists or psychiatrists because they do appoint their patients to God They are not with whom I'm to whom I am referring. Many people have been helped by professionals in these fields, and I therefore do not this moment discredit their usefulness in the usefulness of such a profession For Christians, however, I fear that we spend too much time trying to discover what made us the person we are, i. e. , examining our upbringing and so forth Rather than dealing with what is, with what we are now. At the heart of who we are, of who every person is, is the same. Although we manifest our sins and righteousness differently, each of us is the same. And I intend to prove it as we examine Cain and Abel. As the text says, Adam and Eve conceived, they had two children just after they were removed from the garden. They conceive more later, but the first two are what's most important in the story of God redeeming humanity. We can see by Eve's response to these children that she had in her mind the promise of God that she would bring forth the seed, an offering. That would be to God as an offspring that would defeat the serpent Satan and restore them to paradise. That was likely in her mind. With each son, she had hope that he was the one. Every Israelite mother carried the same hope that her son would be the one. As we examine these first offspring of humanity, we notice that they represent ourselves. Their personal selves is us. Cain and Abel represent all of humanity, and that what comes from Adam is both carnal, that is of the flesh, Cain, and spiritual, Abel. From Adam comes a son of the flesh, a son who acts out of his flesh, Cain, and a man who acts out of his spirit, Abel. From every man there are fruits of the carnal and of the spiritual. And not surprisingly, those two are at odds. As the Apostle Paul said, the flesh lusts against the spirit and the spirit against the flesh, and these are contrary to one another. We might say that within each man there is a form of schizophrenia or multiple personality disorder. The battle that rages is similar to the battle waged by Cain and Abel. It's within all of us. When explaining the resurrection of Jesus and then of those who follow him, the Apostle Paul said, the spiritual is not first, but the natural, and afterward the spiritual. And so it is with the birth of Cain, who was born first, and then Abel. It is the carnal mind that comes out of man first, as he is now born under Adam and thus born into sin. The carnal mind has enmity against God. This is Cain. But there is a second birth, another life-born, which comes by grace and is of the Spirit. As it says in John's Gospel, the children of God are born not of blood, not of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God. This is Abel. Thus begins the flesh and the spirit striving together between them and in us. The manner that both the flesh and spirit work is exemplified in the lives of Cain and Abel, the carnal mind, that Cain within us Ignores sin and is busy trying to improve fallen creation. The earth is cursed, and so the carnal mind does not Does what comes naturally? What comes naturally is to overcome the curse, to work. Cain is sincere in his effort, like many religious people are. Yet those who work to overcome the curse make a grievous mistake. They understand that by their work they are pleasing God. Their righteousness is not of God, but of self. It is self-righteousness. In contrast, Abel acknowledges sin. He sees sin and its result, and so when he comes to worship God, he does so in the form of an atonement. Atonement through death. Cain instead offers to God fruit from the ground as a type of triumph for overcoming the curse. And yet the fruit is not the best fruit. It is not the first fruit. It is merely a portion of what Cain was successful in growing. Abel, again, in contrast, offers the firstling of his flock. He offers the first of what he had, and he offers all of it. Having the mind of the Spirit, being born of the Spirit, Abel knew what honor God. The flesh by itself cannot honor God. Those who are in the flesh, Paul said, cannot please God. The works of the flesh are evident, he told the Galatians, but not to those who have carnal minds like Cain. The carnal mind, like Cain, does not respond to God's rejection with sorrow or repentance. I should have done better, God, no. Instead, he seethes with jealousy and anger. Its only answer is to kill what it envies The flesh rises against the spirit to quench it, to snuff it out. Cain killed Abel. The first offspring killed the second offspring out of jealousy and hate. As a result of this sin, Cain is sent out from the presence of the Lord He will receive no inheritance. He can claim no land as his own. As an act of grace, he is marked for protection as being of God And given a promise that anyone attempting to have retribution toward Cain will be punished. And this tells us that God still acknowledges Cain, a man of the flesh. He still acknowledges him as his creation in his image. Yet, as a man of the flesh, he cannot walk with God. Like all men of the flesh, God will use him He uses Cain and his offspring to craft metals, to build tents, and to make and play instruments. All of these will become useful in God's kingdom, but the flesh that is corrupted will remain having enmity with God. And not only can we identify Cain and Abel as symbols of our interpersonal struggles We can also see them as foreshadows of the conflict between religious leaders of Israel and our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. The Pharisees and the Sadducees. They were like Cain. They were governed by their flesh. The Pharisees trusted in their man-made laws and considered their personal disciplines as most pleasing to God. The Sadducees trusted in their birthright as priests. They used their birthright and man-made laws to overcome the curse. But the ministry of Jesus and its fruits allowed them to see that what Jesus was offering to the Father was being accepted while their works were not. They became jealous. They became jealous of that offered life of Christ, that it was being accepted by God while their offerings were being rejected. They, like Cain, like all flesh, rose up to kill the spirit. And what we learn from the death of Abel and the death of Christ is that the spirit of the righteous does not stay in that cursed ground. The righteous rise. Abel is resurrected in the person of Seth, not like the pagans understand reincarnation. It is a resurrection of a man of the Spirit. Here is another man of the Spirit. Seth is born to replace Abel, as Eve herself states. It is from Seth line that men of the Spirit are born. The flesh gives birth to flesh, the spirit gives birth to spirit. Seth is the chosen one, not the chosen one, but the one chosen from whom the line of the Savior would begin. The line is recorded by Saint Luke in the third chapter of his gospel. The line begins with Adam, and then Seth, and then Enosh, down to Noah, down to Abraham, down to David, and ultimately to Jesus, son of Joseph. And please notice the difference between the line of Cain and the line of Seth. If you look in your Bibles, chapters 4 and 5 of Genesis, Each of their line is highlighted by the name Lamech. Lamech is in both of their lines. The similarity shared in these lines reminds us that in this life there is a resemblance between the flesh and the spirit. The flesh and the spirit are together for the long run, at least until judgment. The flesh is in the state of corruption, and the spirit is alive, having been born anew in Christ, but they dwell together. until the flesh corrupt gives way to a new body that will last for eternity. In the meantime The speech of Lamech in the line of Seth is to be contrasted with the speech of Lamech in the line of Cain. The words of Lamech in the line of Seth are recorded in chapter 5, verse 29. And there he acknowledges the curse of the ground and speaks of hope for better things. The words of Lamech in the line of Cain consist of boasting They are recorded in chapter 4, verse 23, where he brags of killing a man and receiving no punishment for his deed. He's above everything. Where one man is confessing sin, the other is boasting of his work. And essentially saying, Where is God's judgment? I challenge it. I trust that by now you have noticed the struggle of every man is depicted in the lives of Cain and Abel. That struggle goes on within each of us, each day. It is that struggle that the Apostle Paul describes in his epistle to the Romans, chapter 7 and 8, and his epistle to the Galatians in chapter 5. It is not a struggle that is without hope, for we have already seen how God resurrects zones of the Spirit We are with hope, for as Seth replaced Abel, Jesus rose from the dead and promises that those who believe in him will raise, be raised in the same manner. And we look to the resurrection, the flesh, as it continues to war against the spirit and the spirit against the flesh, we look for the resurrection. Now before we cease contrasting Cain and Abel, we must also see something else in the story, something that I found once I discovered this as extremely profound and even life-changing. In the genealogy of Cain, again, Genesis chapter 4, verses 16 through 24, we are to notice that not once Is there a record of a death? In Cain's line, there's no record of a death. No death is recorded in any of Cain's offspring. In contrast, the genealogy of Seth in chapter 5, verse 1 through 30, death is recorded of every one of them Except the one that was not because God took him. It tells us Adam lived so many years and died Seth lived so many years and died. Enosh lived so many years and died. And so it is recorded of Seth's line. But what does that mean for us? No death, death. It means first that the people of the flesh, those in Cain's line, do not die because they're already dead Man is born into sin, born into death. Men of the flesh are dead in their trespasses and sins. If they die again, it is eternal damnation. Secondly, it means that the men of the Spirit are men who embrace, and hear it now, are men who embrace death. Men of the Spirit embrace death. And by this I mean that they recognize the need to die to themselves in this life and to die in Christ at the end of their days that they may live forever. Be reminded of the words of our Lord referring to the need to die. That's what he meant when he said, Pick up your cross and follow me. He said, Take no thought of your life. And he that finds his life shall lose it. And he who loses his life for my sake shall find it. And he that seeks to save his life shall lose it. And he that loses his life shall preserve it in the end. In the same line of thought, the Apostle Paul said, consider others as more important than yourselves. What else can be concluded from these words other than to follow Christ is to die? To be of the Spirit is to die. Much of our psychological struggles can be attributed to not having yet died to ourselves. As professing followers of Jesus Christ, we are making a claim that He alone is our God and we are His servants. And yet much of what we pursue, what we devote ourselves to in this life, has nothing to do with following Jesus. It is important for us to acknowledge that God has a right to govern every aspect of our lives. Because he has that right. If there are areas in our individual lives that we continue to self-govern, he can, if and when he wants to, insist that we turn over that area in our lives to him. In many instances, he causes us to die to an aspect of our lives that we thought we controlled. It can be something as seemingly innocent as a young girl having always dreamed of her wedding day, that it would be a certain way, and God insisting that she die to such a dream. It can be and has been a young man who puts his identity in sports and God takes it away, causing him to die to such superficial self-images. It can be and has been another man who puts his security in his fiancee. And God insists that he be first in that young man's life. It can be a woman who has begun to pursue her career first before pursuing the kingdom of God. And God stops her in her tracks, causing her to die to herself. God even causes fathers and mothers to die to their obsession over their children. When God says he is to be first priority, That there are to be no other gods before him, and a parent puts a child in God's place, God will in some way cause that parent to die to such idolatry At the other end, God causes children to put their faith and security in Him instead of leaning on their parents for all their worldly needs. And from these examples, I hope you get the idea that to follow Christ, to be of the Spirit, is to embrace death. We are to die to ourselves, so that Christ may live in us. Just as those of the Spirit who were in the lineage of Christ needed to die, so that Christ might come forth. Being born of a virgin, so too do those of us who are in Christ need to die to ourselves that Christ might come through us. Each of us There is no other way but death. Abel understood this. Cain did not. Friends of God, be not dismayed, that there is no other way but death. Jesus is the first fruits of the resurrection. If we die to ourselves, we are promised that we too will be raised to eternal life. So let us be in the lineage of those of the Spirit Of those who die. Let us pray. A gracious and merciful God Through these two brothers, we certainly see ourselves, inwardly see ourselves, and we also see the call that is upon all of us who say we believe in your Son Jesus. To die. To die. Father, wherever we need to, reveal it to us that we may live. In Jesus' name we pray.

sermons.title: Flooded Baptism
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. We are actually covering the narrative of Genesis 6 through 8. So if you want to follow along In case you haven't noticed, I have been preaching through Genesis using an interpretative technique titled typology. Bible interpreters can be placed into four camps, or at least I place them in four camps. The first camp interprets the Bible, failing to connect the stories and the themes. And thus the Bible is like a set of fables to them. The second camp connects the Old Testament stories together, and so as far as they can be understood, they're just by themselves Failing to connect the Old Testament to the New Testament, treating them as truly two separate books and thus two separate covenants. The third can't connects the biblical stories of the Old and the New Testament together to make a chain The chain links allow us to see the connection between the promised seed in Genesis to the child born of a virgin in Bethlehem. The chain links convince us that the covenant of Abraham is the covenant of Christ, and that they are both by faith. Such an understanding of the whole of Scripture is glorious to behold, and well blessed is a people to receive such teaching. I used to be in the third camp until now. Now I am part of a fourth camp. The fourth camp does more than connect the stories of Scripture as in one chain. Holy Scripture, as far as I can understand it, is more like a male shirt. We normally think of the word mail in terms of what we receive in our mailboxes. The word mail, however, originally meant chain. It was used to refer to delivering letters because the letter was a sort of chain that connected people. A mail or chain shirt comes from medieval armor that was worn by knights and others to protect them from harm of a swiped sword I believe the Word of God is more like a male shirt because it is a series of chain links. connecting in more than one direction to form a protection, a protection against falsehood. Typology, like a male shirt, connects many different biblical stories, themes, and theological truths so that the fullness of Scripture can be understood and applied without contradiction. Now, a criticism of typology is that it appears to ignore or discredit the historical truths. of particular biblical characters, places, and events. For some, the perspective treats the biblical stories again as mere fables But this is refuted by pointing out that typology not only does not ignore historical truths, but actually expounds upon them. Cain and Abel are perfect examples. Cain and Abel were real men. They were the first two sons born to Adam and Eve. Cain truly, actually, and with malice killed Abel. All information told as facts in Scripture regarding the two brothers, we can accept as truth. And yet there is more to the story. We learned that Cain was a man of the flesh, Abel a man of the spirit. From Adam comes flesh and spirit, and the two are opposed to one another, just as the New Testament says. Where the typology of Cain and Abel has its appeal is that we know the same is true with each of us, within us. The flesh and the spirit are at odds. Where the Spirit is willing, the flesh is weak. Although we know what is right to do, we fail to do it. We find both the fruit of the flesh and the fruit of the spirit coming out of us. The battle raged between the brothers helps us understand what is going on inside us. The birth of Seth and the line of the Spirit continues to give us hope that in the end the Spirit will win out. The New Testament uses typology as an example, is the typology of Noah, and the flood being as our baptism. But before we get there, I wish to show you the many typologies in the story of Noah. First, we examine the increase of sin that brings about the flood. The multiplying of men automatically results in the multiplying of sin. Church leaders don't often consider the reality that the more members you have in your church, the more sin is multiplied in your midst. That should not dissuade the church from evangelism, but only make the point that with more people come more problems And this increase in sin includes the multiplying of those in the line of Cain and those in the line of Seth, flesh and spirit. Daughters of men are described here in Genesis to represent the affections of men. Our affections are not our emotions, although our emotions add to our affections. Affections are those things we long for to provide us deep satisfaction. These affections, these daughters of men, well, they are attractive So attractive that they get the attention of the sons of God. There is great debate as to who the sons of God are, and I am not going to spend my time debating it. I will simply side with those who understand them to be angels or heavenly creatures Thus, we have affections seducing spirits, and the results in the narrative are giants. These giants are both large physical beings, and they are earth-borne thoughts which are full of crime and violence. They are colossus sinners who epitomize how depraved and destructive the flesh can be when it is enlarged. The confusion as to the identity of the sons of God and their interaction with the daughters of men reflects the confusion brought about by the mixture of the flesh and the spirit. Such a mixture is warned against in the law of Moses as the Israelites were commanded not to intermarry with pagan nations. It is also warned about in the New Testament when the Apostle Paul tells those Corinthian Christians not to be unequally yoked. To be unequally yoked is to be married to someone who is pulling in life in a different direction than faith in God would take him. To not intermix with unbelievers is also warned against as Christians are told that friendship with the world, you know it, hostility toward God. The result of faith's intermarrying and friendships with the worldly ideas and philosophies is Colossus sin, both in mind and action. It is colossus because it mixes together truth with lies. It allows foxes to sleep with hens and wolves to sleep with lambs. When such syncretism occurs, there is never an instance where those of the Spirit raise up toward godliness, those of the flesh. It's always the other way around Like King Solomon marrying women who worship idols, men born of the Spirit are brought down, brought low when they intermix with people of the flesh. And because these people had tasted the heavenly gift and then departed from it, as the writer to the Hebrews tells us, it would have been better that they had never known the truth. God has no choice but to destroy humanity. The sin is too large. And yet, thankfully, there is another type in this story. A man named Noah finds grace in the eyes of the Lord. With Noah, God would start the generations of man over again. Noah is a man of the spirit. He is in the line of Seth. Noah is one man, the only man among all other men that is considered righteous. His loneliness among men is a precursor and shadow of another man to come, who will also be alone among men in his righteousness. And yet by him all who would be saved are saved. Noah is also like the man to come in that he is to work with wood. He is a carpenter of swords, as God instructs him to build a boat. The wood that he is to cut down and reform will be fashioned into a work of faith. that is a vehicle of safety for those who cling to it as a symbol of judgment to those who mock it. As the ark was made up of many beams, so is the cross made of beams, and it too delivers Christians from the world. Another way that Noah is a new Adam is the way that he recovers man's power over the beasts. It is not for mere practicality that God brings in each species of beast two by two so that their kind can be saved. It is also to demonstrate that the salvation of mankind includes restoration. God is saving man and restoring him to the Garden of Eden, where beasts and men dwell in peace. God's chosen means by which he would save mankind consisted of both destruction and preservation. We also know it as death and resurrection. God chose to flood the earth, killing all of mankind except the household of Noah The rest of the earth that is living, the vegetation, the animals, are also killed, except those who are led into the ark. So just as the sin of Adam affected all of creation, so does the colossus sin of mankind in Noah's day. The result of sin is still death. Now for some, it is tempting to question why God would choose a flood. Again, I remind you that it is not for us to ask why, but for us to accept what is or what was. From a typological view, the purpose of the flood is first to judge the sin of mankind And then to point to the salvation men will find by being baptized in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost. It is the Apostle Peter who draws a direct relationship from the salvation Christians have in the sacrament of baptism to the flood in Noah's day. Eight souls were saved through the water. Those eight souls were souls of Noah's family. Peter uses that historical fact to refer to Christian baptism. Christian baptism saves because it symbolizes man being dead in his sin. Christian baptism saves because it is a profession in the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead. Christian baptism saves because it is done in the name of the Trinity, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost. We established a distinction between the land and water when we discussed creation in chapter one. Remember that the water represents the pagan nations, and the land represents the people of God, his chosen people. It is appropriate then for the water to overrun mankind, for all men but Noah became men of the flesh. To be saved in this life, Noah is not taken out like Enoch, but is assigned by God to endure the flood. And yet he does more than endure. We are to notice that the Lord shuts in the occupants of the ark. That means that their souls are secure. Those within could not get out, and that was a good thing. Thus being shut in, they are prisoners, but listen, prisoners of hope. Their salvation is secured, and so it is with all of those who are in the covenant with the living God. Their salvation cannot be taken from them. He has locked his people down so that they cannot be lost, even when they foolishly want to stray. And second, we notice that the Ark is a home. It is a house for Noah, his family, and the animals chosen by God. As such, it is like the church. For it is within the church that God's people are saved from a world that is drowning. And if you paid any attention to the hearings these past weeks, you know the world is drowning. The word for church you remember is eklesia, meaning the called out ones Moses and his family were called out from among all other men. Christians are called out from among all other men as well, and the church building is where they gather To be saved, it was necessary that they stayed in the ark. They most assuredly became tired of one another. No doubt they were tempted to be fearful, frustrated, anxious. That is what occurs when people go through a trial together. Surely the odor within the ark was difficult to bear on the certain days with animals present? Sometimes the church is like the ark. It's not a very pleasant place to be. But the church, like the ark, is God's chosen vessel to save his people. As I described during my sermons on Christian worship, you will remember that the pews have traditionally been aligned like those in this sanctuary, not because it is the most practical way to hear a sermon or to sing together, but to replicate a galley in a ship. Early Christian architects wanted the building and its furnishings to communicate a theological truth And so the pews were placed in a position that would remind us that we are servants on the same ship. And to get where we all want to go, that beautiful heavenly shore, we must row together. And the third thing we notice is that the ark is said to have gone through the flood. This is such an important point. The New King James Version says that the ark moved about the face of the waters. It went through the rolling waves. It was tossed and tilted. Water crashed upon its sides, and still it remained on top of the waters. The point to be made here is that God's people are not saved from trials, tribulations, death, and judgment, but through them. And I will say it again, we are saved through them. There is no place for name it, claim it theology in the midst of a flood. There is no prosperity doctrine that is going to save a man from a time of trial. All who have been baptized into the Christian faith must understand that part of that sacrament includes being baptized into Christ's death. Noah and his family were baptized through the flood. Within the flood was death, and within them was fear of death. That's what it is to go through. Every one of the three thousand that were baptized on the day of Pentecost after Peter preached and told them to repent and be baptized to be saved. Every one of them was soon to discover that once you are marked by Christ, you will go through trials and tribulations. It's inevitable. As a Christian, the world hates you. The devil will unceasingly tempt you. And God, yes, will test you. And with all of that going on, we struggle within ourselves not to walk into our own temptation. In one sense, I thought this week, it is odd that we celebrate a baptism. For when an adult or a child is baptized, it assures a life of trials and tribulations. Temptations and testing will assuredly follow It is not an easy road we set for our children that we set for new believers. Yet all of us who have been baptized are on that same road. And it's narrow. And few travel on it. We are on the same road because we believe. We have faith that in getting through the trial, death, and judgment, there is a reward too wonderful to describe. For Noah, his family, and the cargo within the Ark, the reward was dry land. The land is first felt rather than seen as the ark runs aground, but land is not detected by sight. It is like the apostles who saw an empty grave and they weren't sure what it meant. They felt something. There was evidence of hope, but their eyes had not yet detected a rising. For Noah and family, it was in the tenth month, on the first day of the month, that land was seen. Just as in the days of creation, when land rose up from the water, so it did again. It is a resurrection. or a precursor to a more glorious one when the Son of God will rise from the land Thus, the appearance of land reminds us that we are not only baptized into Jesus' death, but also into his resurrection. That is why we believers choose the narrow road. That is why we remain on that road through trials, tribulations, death, and judgment, at the other end is our resurrection, our eternal life. When land was spotted by Noah, chapter 8, verse 6, records that he opened the window of the ark. What a great metaphor for what God has done for all who have been baptized in his name. He lets us see land when he opens a window. He gives us glimpses into heaven when he opens a window. He lets us see the byproduct of resurrection even before we experience it ourselves. Consider. Have you ever had hearty fellowship with family or Christian friends when the stories are full of life and the room is filled with laughter? That is an open window. If you have ever felt the love of another human being to where you swear it is unconditional and honest. That is a window opened. When you stop and look at God's created work around you, and a sense of awe and wonder floods your soul, that is an open window. When you are at peace with all people that you know, and your conscience is clear, and you lay your head down at night in peace, that is a window opened. The flood was the greatest judgment God placed upon the earth, upon humanity. It took away life from man and beasts. And yet in the midst of such great judgment is an open window that gives promises of a better day, a day of resurrection. This narrative in Genesis is not complete until we add what is seen on the throne room of the exalted Jesus as it is described in the book of Revelation. There you remember Jesus sits with a sea of glass before him and a rainbow that is a full circle. The sea that raged and destroyed is now calm and serves as a reflector in heaven. It reflects heaven. The promises of God are so true and thus fulfilled that the rainbow itself is complete. That is the end of the story of Noah and the flood, and we anxiously await that end. Until then, we need to keep some windows open. Let us pray. Our gracious and heavenly Father, we thank you for the truth that is set herein in this narrative. Noah, his family, the flood, judgment, and here, yes, resurrection. Bless our minds, dear Lord, that we might believe even more to see how you planned it all along. You have always planned our salvation. May we embrace it. In Jesus' name we pray. Amen.

sermons.title: Living out our baptism
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: And so he died on To take place from great In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. If you haven't been able to make it to Sunday school this year, I encourage you to start. We had a good presentation by the Reverend Lamboy. In regards to where works and faith come together in the Christian life, and it fits so well with our sermon that's coming to us from Genesis chapters 8 and 9. It is difficult to contain one's excitement about such a series as this. Well, at least my excitement about this series We have discovered more in the first eight chapters of Genesis than most have seen in the entire book, and I hope that as a result Faith in all of us has increased and will continue to increase. Our faith has been given the opportunity to increase because We were able to make connections from the very beginning of man to the life and sacrifice of Jesus to our contemporary lives. Without these connections, a reader of Holy Scripture could conclude that the story of God's people is made up actually of a series of failures and corrections. It would look something like this. God created the world and mankind. Mankind sinned, so God had to kick them out of paradise and come up with a new plan to bring them back. In the meantime, man continued to sin, causing God to judge the whole world with the flood to start over, because he did it wrong the first time. After the flood, the sin of mankind continued, causing God to confuse our languages. It didn't work again Soon after, God chose one man through whom he would teach what it meant to worship the only true God. This one man was Abraham, who was like Noah before him, who was like Adam before him. Whereas each man was to be the first to begin a race of people who were true worshipers of God. He keeps trying to reinvent. He keeps trying to correct Because we too often think that God is like us and that he makes mistakes, erases his mistakes, and starts over again. It can appear to us that God just can't seem to get it right. And by seeing what we have seen So far here in Genesis, we are now aware that Adam is like Christ and that he is the first of many to come Cain and Abel are like the flesh and spirit that struggle within each man. The giants that roam the earth coming down from the daughters of men are like Colossus sin. That mankind can produce when he is left to himself. The flood is like the baptism that each man of sin must go through as he is buried with Christ. The rising Lamb that comes up after the flood is like the resurrection of every man who has been baptized, resulting in the hope of everlasting life. These stories from Genesis and their New Testament counterparts reveal that the way of salvation has always been the same. There's never been a new plan. What is drawn out in Genesis is compacted and revealed through the Son of God, Jesus Christ, our Lord. If the story of Noah and his family and the animals two by two are a type of baptism Which they clearly are, then what might we learn about the life of Noah and his family after their baptism? Well, just as a person must begin to live out his or her baptism, no longer walking by the flesh, but by the spirit. So Noah and his family learn what it means to live out their baptism in the world. And that leads us to learn what it means to walk In good works as we live out our faith. Noah's family, like all who come out of the world, have been born anew after those baptismal waters. And they must make then a transition. What they find is opportunities for true liberty, true joy, and true peace. These are opportunities because through Noah's family, they've been given new life and a fresh world. And yet still the old world remains. And that means they have to learn how to live in that old world with new life within them. Noah and his family are the salt and light of the earth, just as Christians are. And thus we have responsibilities and we have blessings. What were they to do next? Well, first the text says they went forth. The New King James says they went out out of the ark. And that's That phrase went forth is the ideal of liberty. We described the inhabitants of the ark as it went through the flood, that they were prisoners of hope They were secure for their own good, but they were still prisoners. Now they are free to roam, free to establish, free to plant, to harvest, to build, to multiply. There are no restrictions, no rules, no prohibitions for them. Those who have been baptized in Christ are also liberated. Christians are not bound by the law, as the law is no longer a burden, for it has been fulfilled in Christ, so that we who follow him are made free by the grace of God. All things are now permissible. Dietary laws are done away with. Sacrificial laws have been satisfied. Those who are in Christ are free, and we say free indeed. And yet, and yet, all things are permissible, but not all things are profitable. Freedom in Christ is only limited by the flesh of man. So the second act of Noah after having been baptized is to worship. Noah built an altar to the Lord and offered burnt offerings. In his freedom, note this, in his freedom, the first thing Noah does is worship God. This worship is not done because he has to do it. Noah understands after having been through the flood waters that it was a privilege to worship the one true living God, to know his name I fear too many in the Christian community view worship of God and their attendance to church services as a have-to. Guilt is what brings them, and if there was no guilt, they would not come. Others compare a worship service to the many activities they would rather be doing And when we in such a manner, well, the worship of God loses out. With such a comparison, worship in this life will always lose out. Guilt can only last for a short while before it loses its effectiveness. The only lasting reason for someone to worship the one true living God is to comprehend the privilege that we have to do so. For Noah, that privilege was evident by the fact that all other men besides his family were drowned in the flood waters. that he himself was left, that he himself knows the truth, made it a privilege to call upon God. The third act of Noah and his family in living out their baptism is to be fruitful and multiply. Just as God said to Adam and Eve, so he says to Noah, his wife, Noah's sons, and their wives. All of them be fruitful and multiply. The command is for practical reasons, of course The earth needed to be repopulated. The promised seed from Genesis 3 that had to come forth to crush the serpent's head. Noah's family must multiply Some Christians today, and I wish there were more, admittedly, take the command literally Today, believing that it is their godly attribute to have a large number of children, to be fruitful, to multiply. Blessed is the man whose quiver is full, says the psalmist. As the command was given to Adam and then to Noah, so today parents believe it was given to them. Amen. There is nothing inherently godly, however, by simply procreating. What Christians need to understand is that the command to be fruitful also refers to godliness. Godly virtues are referred to in Scripture as fruits of the Holy Spirit indwelling in a man and a woman. Thus, when we seek to obey the command to be fruitful and multiply, it is important and even necessary that we understand it to include both having children First step, and raising them to walk with the living God. After all, populating hell is not difficult to do. I am sure we agree that there are enough backsliding lukewarm Christians in the world And that group does not need to be added to by those who believe there is virtue in simply having a lot of children, while not taking the pains to raise them in the fear and admonition of the Lord. Yes, Christians in living out their baptism are to be fruitful and multiply. And that means to us that we are to multiply and be fruitful in a godly sense. Populating heaven is a Christian parent's primary goal. The fourth act in living out baptism Is for mankind's power over beasts to be restored. Typologically, and we talked about this last week, typologically speaking The mention of beasts refers to the faculties of man. Our emotions are like beasts. Our desires are like untamed lions. Our anger can be like a fierce bear. After the baptism of a man, the Lord gives a power over such faculties that they did not have previously. The fear of you and the dread of you shall be on every beast of the earth, says the Lord to Noah and his family. This authority over beastly desires is understood when the Apostle Paul calls Christians to bring every thought into captivity, to control it. Said authority is expected by St. James, who tells the Christian to be angry, but sin not. Control it. There is an expectation in such passages that Christians have the capability, even the power within them to overcome evil. I know very well that this is opposed to modern thinking where scientists conclude that we are nothing more than our genetic makeup. You are what you are, you desire what you desire. Behaviors such as gluttony and alcoholism, drug addiction, and other vices are simply a result of how a person is genetically disposed, so it is believed. While there is much to be respected regarding one person's genetic disposition as opposed to another, Christians cannot accept that any disposition Any disposition relieves a person of their being culpable before a God for their behavior. Christians cannot do this because Scripture does not. It makes sense that because each person is genetically different, one man could be more susceptible to drug addiction as an example to another Yet Scripture does not allow susceptibility to be an excuse for sin. The post-baptized individual has been given authority over their faculties. Greater is he that is in you than he that is in the world. No temptation will come upon a man that he cannot overcome by the power of the Spirit of God. Each person baptized in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Ghost has the authority and power of the Trinity at their disposal. The beasts are given into your hand, says the Lord. As author Andrew Jukes stated, If the animal in us is not subject to the mind, it is because the mind or man is not subject to the Lord. And when we are, the reverse happens. The fifth style, lifestyle change, embraced by a person baptized and now walking with the Lord, interestingly, is the eating of meat. Before the flood, man's food was vegetation. In Genesis 1, the Lord told man that every herb bearing seed and every tree in which there is fruit is for man to eat. Now, after the flood, the Lord says to Noah, Every moving thing that lives shall be meat to you. Again, before the flood, the bodies of beasts had been consumed only by the Lord in fire. They had been his meat. Their death satisfied him. After the flood, upon the resurrection of the ground, Noah and his family walked on, the meat of animals would satisfy them. The command to eat of meat is clearly again a type. A type to what the New Testament calls meat. Recall that when the disciples were concerned about Jesus, he wasn't eating, and they were worried about him. They came to him and told them he needed to have something to eat. He responded by saying that he did have meat. That he did have meat, and that meat was to do the will of the Father. And later he says that unless a man eat of his flesh and drink of his blood, he cannot be his disciple. He followed that strange statement by saying that his own flesh was meat Recalled the writer to the Hebrews uses the idea of meat to explain the difference between simple doctrine of God and those that are of greater sustenance, deeper, more profound. He called those doctrines meat. From Hebrews 5, verse 14, we read, but solid food, meat, belongs to those who are of full age. Those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil. So eating meat for the Christian is more than enjoying a good steak. Added to it is to know the deeper truths of God. That is meat to us. The sixth expected change of Noah and his family after having been baptized through the flood is requiring the life of a man for taking the life of another man. The standard thus has been raised, whereas before the blood of Cain was not required for the blood of Abel. Lamech, remember, in the line of Cain would brag about killing a man, and yet nothing was required of him. Such amnesty ends with Noah. Noah's line is the spiritual line, and those of the Spirit are required proper judgment upon those who are guilty of shedding another man's blood. The justification is stated in verse 6 of chapter 9. Man is created in the image of God. And to the modern mind, the killing of one man because he killed another simply means that there are two men dead. But God reveals the value of his image. By insisting that the only thing of equal value is his image. All murder, therefore, is to be judged. Under the covenant of Christ, this is taken to a higher standard still. You remember from the Sermon on the Mount Not only can men not murder one another without having to pay the penalty with their own life, but it is now forbidden to even hate another man, for that is murder within the heart. Not only can we not murder, but we are not to verbally abuse another man, for that too is damaging a man created in God's image. Well, the seventh and final change that man is to make in his life after being baptized is really not a change in lifestyle or actions or behavior. It is simply to know what God will do. Change in life, to know what God will do God says to Noah that he will establish his covenant with him and his family after him. The token of the covenant will be a bow in the clouds. The focus of the covenant made is what God will do. I will establish He says, I will look upon the bow, he says. I will remember, he says Here is a distinct difference between thou shall not, or thou shalt, and I will. With Adam, the focus was upon what man could and could not do. It was a sort of covenant of works. Here, the focus is upon what God will do. Thus God's covenant with Noah is grace. It is one of promise, and one that is dependent upon God to perform and fulfill. The type should be obvious to us who follow Christ, for we too are under that covenant of grace and not works. Our salvation is dependent upon what God has done, what he has promised he will perform. The covenant sign for us is not the rainbow as Noah received. For in Christ, you remember, that's a full circle, literally. Under Noah's covenant, it was halved. It is incomplete In Christ it is full as it is noted in John's vision where Christ is sitting on that throne, shining like Jasper, and around the throne, around it is the rainbow. Completed. With these seven noticeable changes in the life of Noah and his family after coming through the baptismal type waters of the flood. Is a type of the joys of living out the Christian life. Noah and his sons were regenerated to things which fallen Adam never heard of. Freedom and worship and increase and power over beasts outside and within. These are freely given by God. In Noah's world sin is judged. And in Noah's world salvation is not by works, but by grace. Like Noah. Like Noah, we have much to do to live out our baptism And unlike Noah, we practice our faith, we live out our baptism in full revelation that God is the Father and the Son and the Holy Ghost. What we should see is that living out our Christian lives includes overcoming and reclaiming. We are to spend all of our days overcoming beasts that are vices to us. We are to reclaim freedoms such as Loving your spouse and loving her well. Raising your children to know the Lord all their days, without exception. These are not easy tasks. No, they are not. But there is a reason why Jesus will say to us, will say to us, Well done, good and faithful servants. Such a welcome into heaven only makes sense if we spend all of our days working out our salvation, living out our baptism. Noah and his family did, and we are to do the same. Let us pray. Our gracious and merciful God, for this high calling we are grateful To know that our salvation is not baptism and done, confess our sins and done, but that we are to live out a life of faith that is both pleasing to you and rewarding to us. May this picture of Noah and his family going forth be for us how we should go forth and do the same. May it be so, we pray in Jesus' name. Amen.

sermons.title: Three Anti-Types
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Be seated. In your Bibles you will note that we are covering Genesis chapter nine and into ten and into eleven even though our reading only came from Genesis nine. As a prelude, I mention That in formal and informal debate, it is important to define terms Oftentimes, proofs for arguments are written and followed, with either side using different definitions, and the result is arguing past one another. For example, we might argue whether batgamon is a sport. To determine whether it is or not, we must first agree on our definitions of batgamon and sport. And if you are a politician, you will need to define what the word is means. That's a nineteen nineties reference for those of you who are young. Some defined a term by a synonym. A synonym, you remember, is a different word with the same meaning. Synonyms, however, are limited because many words do not have exact synonyms. A more formal means of defining a term is lexical. A lexical definition provides an established meaning of a term, and you know those are found in dictionaries. And for those of you younger, those are books, and they have words in them. However, the most popular way to define a term is neither by synonym nor from a dictionary. It is in casual conversation defining a term by example. For instance, if I am trying to define the term sport by example, I would say that a sport is like the game of baseball. In baseball, there is physical exertion. Skill is required. Strategy to defeat an opponent is necessary to be successful. And a score is kept to determine a winner. I would never say when asked to define the word sport that it's like Batgamon. In fact, I would use another common means to define a term, which is to state what a term is not. If I was asked what a sport is, I could answer, well, it's not backgammon. A typology is similar to defining by example And a part of typology or typological interpretation is recognizing anti-type. Anti-type. Meaning that we can discover Who our Savior is by examining the person of Noah, and we can know who Jesus is not by examining the failures of Noah and his sons and those who come after. For as much as we have discovered the gospel within the story of Noah, we must also recognize that there is failure, great failure. And with that great failure is a recognition that there needs to be a person who comes along later who is greater than Noah. As righteous as Noah was and is, his life is a type of a man who has been baptized. Who is under the covenant of grace, and yet he is still a fallen man. He is not the son of God, and the record of the latter part of his life reveals this. Again, today we examine three forms of failure that are recorded in Genesis 9, 10, and 11. In each of these failures, we will likely see ourselves and the fallen men that we live amongst. And these failures will also allow us to highlight a man who did not fail, and in fact, faced even greater temptations and yet chose, yes, chose not to sin. The first two failures described in general are the misapplying of good things In Noah we have external blessings misused by his volition, and the result is to his own shame. In Nimrod, we have personal gifts that are perverted to injure others. In Babel, we have an outright apostasy So there was a systematic goal of highlighting man's glory over God. Noah and his fall comes first. His failure is great even though he is one of the elect. He is a believer. Believers do fail and fall, and some fall very hard Their salvation is not lost, but their reputation is, and their relationship to others may be lost as well. The fall described here with Noah is hard because he was the only man who was righteous. And yet he chose to abuse God's good gifts. Before regeneration, before the baptismal waters of the flood, Noah cut down trees. Laying the axe to them to build the ark. His cutting down was similar to how God would cut down all of the rest of mankind in the flood. After the flood, Noah became a planter. Now consider that. Consider that he became a planter. It is appropriate for a man who has been saved because he is a sower of seeds. As a sower of seeds, he gets a harvest of ten, twenty, a hundredfold. The kingdom of God is like a seed, Jesus said. The Son of God is like a sower in the field, Jesus taught. The seed is the truth of the gospel, and the ground represents the hearts of men. Thus, it is natural for Noah as a type of Jesus to plant a vineyard. A vineyard is also appropriate for regenerate man, for that is the work of the church. The vine is to be trained, which means it's to be pruned and cultivated. The church being the continuation of the incarnation of Jesus is to train its members. Sin is to be pruned off. Righteousness is to be cultivated. The result is precious juice, fruit of the vine. It is the fruit of the vine that makes the heart of men glad. Drink thy wine with a merry heart, says the writer of Ecclesiastes. For laughter and wine maketh merry. As part of the seven-day sacrifice that Aaron and his sons were commanded to perform. The use of wine is mentioned, and it's the same type of wine that Noah is making here and drinking here. Wine is a gift of God. But like any gift, it can be mistreated and even abused. Noah abused the wine. He becomes drunk with his own fruit. And the scripture warns us of this elsewhere. You have heard these before. Wine is a mocker. Strong drink is a brawler. Those who linger long at the wine find that it bites like a serpent. As a result, Noah is bitten and then he is mocked. Christians should be reminded of the words of Scripture: all things are permissible, but not all things are profitable. Noah is never forbidden to drink of the vine, but his abuse of his freedom leads to his shame. In Christ there is much freedom. We are neither bound by the law nor ruled by the flesh And yet to disobey the law or allow the flesh to reign will only end in our personal shame. Shall we go on sinning that grace may abound? May it never be, Paul says. In Noah's case, his nakedness is exposed. Having lost his reason in his drunkard state, he sheds his clothes, and people are able to see him as he truly is. Freedom abused exposes inner struggles. Freedom abused exposes to others who we really are. A man can only hide sin for so long. He can be fooled for a time, thinking that because no one has seen him sin, his sin is not known. He is fooled by the silence of God. Nothing happens to him, at least at first. As we see in the life of Noah, freedom taken too far exposes a man. It may be in his youth he is exposed, or it may be in his older days, or it may be when he stands before God at the day of judgment. Whatever the scenario, every man's sin will be exposed. Unfortunately, but not uncommonly Sin of the father brings out sin of the son. Ham sees his father's nakedness. And if that would have ended there, that would have been enough. But Ham tells of the shame. Tells of the shame of his father to others. Noah's fall was a misuse, even an abuse of blessings. Ham's exposure of his father, that's a lack of love. There are some whose hearts are so selfish, so filled with spite, that they look for opportunities to expose the sin of others. Meanwhile, they continue to hide their bitterness and conceit within. Beloved, the more I serve as a pastor, the more I'm convinced That bitterness is an ever-present sin waiting to devour its next victim. Be warned. Be warned away from it. Rebuke unforgiving thoughts. Thankfully, there are those like Shem and Jepheth who are charitable, understanding that to condemn their father is to condemn themselves. And so they act with charity by walking backward. Walking backward to cover their father Here is an example to us, to all of us. Coming upon the sin of a member of Christ's church should not mean that we begin a series of phone calls or emails to inform others. It should mean that we take the opportunity to show charity. Love covers a multitude of sin. Covers. This does not mean that we ignore the sin revealed. It does not mean that we don't bother with the person and leave them to their own sin. It means that we go to the brother alone and call him to repentance so that we might win him back. It means that we can acknowledge the sin and then walk backwards. Beloved, we need more walking backwards. If you have ever shared the sins of others for no redemptive purpose, you need to turn around and walk backwards. If you have ever condemned in your heart a brother or sister in Christ because of a revealed moral weakness, you need to start walking backwards. If you have ever withheld forgiveness from a Christian and house bitterness toward another child of God, it is time to walk backwards. And to do so quickly, for the devil is squeezing you. Beloved, walk backwards. The church needs more people to walk backwards. Our next anti-type compared to Jesus is Nimrod. In whom we see a worse form of evil than in Noah. Noah misused blessings and exposed himself. Nimrod exalts himself to the Lord over his brethren. Little is told of this form of apostasy, but what is told is enough. Nimrod, his name literally means rebel. His rebellion was in his leadership As he moved, hear this now, he moved God's people away from the family, from a patriarchal government which was instituted by God And he changed society into a kingdom ruled by violence. First, Nimrod began to be a mighty one. It says he was a mighty hunter before the Lord. And being before the Lord meant that he did it in the sight of God and he bragged about it. And then he became revered by the people that they looked to him, Nimrod, for strength and protection before they looked to God. You will remember Israel repeating this sin as they look to other nations to help them instead of looking to God. The sin repeats itself, especially when Assyria comes knocking and they go of all places to Egypt to look for help. Once again, choosing the strength of man and of the armies of men instead of the one true living God. The gifts of God to Nimrod are strength, bravery, leadership Instead of using these gifts, he uses them to elevate himself and to enslave a people. Nimrod evokes a spirit of domination, seeking to enslave and impose a yoke and place chains upon bodies and minds of his brethren of all people. We can conclude these things about Nimrod from chapter 10, verse 10, where it reads, And the beginning of his kingdom was Babel. This is the first kingdom of man. It is Nimrod's kingdom. Babel, which means confusion. That confusion plays both ways. And then it refers to the confusion of a people who lived in the kingdom of Nimrod while still knowing the God of their ancestor Noah. And that that word confusion refers to a confusion that will come to their languages and that will separate them From Nimrod we have other nations rising up and imitating what he started. Other cities of other nations rise up with different systems or polities that no longer resemble the family. These cities of nations with their national systems and false religions are seen later by the Apostle John in his revelatory vision. Like Babylon the Great, their judgment is assured. It will be in the pit of fire. The third failure, and thus the anti-type to Jesus amongst Noah's descendants, the third one is the building of Babel. As stated previous, this failure is different in that it is not a misuse of a gift, as Noah's was. It is not misapplying of gifts and hurting many people as Nimrod did. This failure is an evil worse than Nimrod's. Because it is a systematic departure from the truth. It is done with the purpose of self-exaltation instead of God's glory. In short, it is apostasy. The story begins in chapter 11, look at it, with a people traveling to find land. They soon find a plane, and doubtless it was a plane much like that that was chosen by Lot. It was a plane that was attractive to the eyes. When their pilgrimage ended, their thoughts turned to their own glory. And we note here that for the people of God the pilgrimage never ends Our pilgrimage does not end until we cross over to the other side unto God's glory. But those who live for themselves, their journey ends when they say it ends. When it ends, they turn inward and attempt to build up themselves. What they want to build is a monument to themselves. They say to one another, let us make. God once said that, let us make, when He created man. Thus the Babylonians took it upon themselves to speak like God They, of course, cannot create, but in their minds they are, they are like God, and because they think they are like God, they believe they have a place in heaven. And so they build a building to ascend to heaven. The people of Babel Have left the worship of the one true God and exchanged it for a worship of themselves. In response, God confuses their language. This is necessary so that man cannot communicate easily, making unity more difficult, for in his unity Without God, man becomes delusional, believing that he is God. And if you examine history with the knowledge of the Babylonians, You can see how this attempt to raise up nations so that they can be like God has been tried and retried in different parts of the world throughout history. With these failures, starting with Noah and then Nimrod and then Babel We might become dismayed because of man's depravity and the depth of that depravity. As I stated at the beginning of this sermon, there are types and there are anti-types. And these failures are anti-types And as such, they allow us to see how Jesus Christ is superior to all of these failures An easy comparison is our reading, our gospel reading today, Jesus in the desert being tempted by Satan. Whereas Noah misused a blessing of God and became drunk with the fruit of the vine, Jesus in contrast resist the temptation to turn a stone into bread. And Jesus was perfectly within his right to eat bread. He had the power of the Trinity at his disposal to make bread from stone, and he resisted. In his freedom, he remained disciplined. Whereas Nimrod used his gifts of leadership, strength, and bravery to create his own kingdom and to oppress men. Jesus, in contrast, is offered all authority over the kingdoms of this world, and yet he resists. The authority the devil offered him was one of fear and oppression. To receive that authority, Jesus merely needed to bend his knee to Satan. To do so would obviously break the first commandment. It would also be to believe that the same that same lie that Nimrod believed Which was that true authority resided on earth. True authority is only found, however, in the one true God who reigns in heaven. Finally, whereas the people of Babel worked to prove that they were like God by building a tower up to what they thought was their rightful place. heaven, Jesus in contrast, resists the temptation to prove that he is the Messiah, the Son of God, by jumping off the pinnacle of the temple and surviving. The citizens of Babel put God to a foolish test. The tower never would have reached heaven, but in their foolishness, that is what they continued to believe. Jesus resists foolishness and by doing so opens the eyes of men. Although the failures of Noah, Nimrod, and the citizens of Babel reveal how hopeless mankind is when he relies on his own strength and his own wisdom. The contrast found in Jesus allows us to have faith, our faith, confirmed in Him alone. Where men failed, he succeeded, and that is why we praise him. These three failures were necessary. So that men would look for someone who would never fail. Our failures are necessary. so that we would look to the only true Savior, Jesus the Christ, from the failures of men. Come the glory of God. Amen. Let us pray. Our gracious and merciful Father. For these who came before us who, although chosen by you Although believers in you, for these who have failed, we see ourselves and we see our own failures. We see our need to walk backwards We see our need to relinquish our own strengths and to only serve in our strengths in your kingdom. And we see that the only way to achieve heaven is by Jesus alone. And so with those confessions, we confess our failures, but also our salvation in Jesus. In name whom we pray. Amen.

sermons.title: Get Out!
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. We continue our look at the book of Genesis, covering chapter twelve and and to thirteen a little bit. Fitting for infant baptism to talk about parenting When you are in the middle of a tough parenting moment, it is hard to find anything funny about it You can get caught up in the tough moments, and each moment can feel like it is the most important part of your parenting life. For instance, you tell your toddler not to touch the figurine on the end table. He continues to eye the figurine while moving toward it and you repeat yourself, don't touch. He continues to move. No, you say. He looks back while his hand is reaching toward it, toward what he desires. He looks at you and continues to move forward with his arm stretched out. No, you say, No, no, no. And finally, the deed is done. He has picked up the figurine and is trying to place it in his mouth while he continues to look at you. Once the deed is done, you have to get up from what you are doing and discipline. After all, the book of Proverbs says that a child left to himself is hated by his father The toddler has disobeyed and he needs to be disciplined, and discipline takes time. First there is resistance, then there is crying, then there is consoling, and finally reconciliation. You, the parrot, settle back down in what you were doing while the toddler starts to make his way toward the figurine again, and the whole process of don't touch, no no, starts all over again Subjectively, that is not funny. But objectively, it is pretty funny. Watching a new parent go through such a scenario is funny when Like us, we don't have toddlers anymore. We are able to see what is funny because we are now more objective Using this example, we should try to imagine what it is like for God to say to us, don't touch. And yet we still move closer to the item with our hand stretched out. And like the toddler, we might even look back to God and see how He is responding as we continue to move forward. God says, no, again. Instead we move forward to grab what is forbidden. It all seems to play out like a parent toddler scenario Only he is not a mortal parent, and we are not toddlers, even though we act like toddlers. In Genesis chapter 12, what God says to Abram is to bring him to a true faith is what he says to all of us. And he has said it enough that we should have listened by now and by listening be saved. When God described before the flood, what he described before the flood was true after the flood, and that is that the heart of mankind is bent toward wickedness. But God said he would not destroy creation again by such a means. As Noah's sons begat children, spreading across the globe, they also begat sin. Because the heart of mankind was bent toward evil, and there were more people on the earth, there were more opportunities to sin. A sin common to mankind during the early days of Abram was polytheism, the belief and the worship of many gods. Polytheism had has been embraced by many groups of humanity in history because having gods helps explain the world the way it is. Fire gods, water gods, sex gods are all invented so that the experience of humanity could have some sort of binding commonality. Once the story of Adam and Eve and Noah and family are gone from the memory, something has to replace the truth about the one true God. And so having many gods is attempted. The result is the only God having to reveal himself to mankind in order to make proper worship and true faith occur amongst God's people once again. And so God chose Abram. And the first instruction, even the first words that God spoke to his chosen one, were get out. Get out. The spoken get out is similar to don't touch It needs to be obeyed for our own good and right away. The call to get out expects prompt obedience It is a call to get out of a land of idolatry. It is a call for Abram to remove himself from people from people who do not believe in the one true God or worship in a true holy manner. It is a call for Abram to separate himself from all that would entangle him to the spirit of the age and the ways of the world around him. The word of truth, the word of God, comes to the chosen one, Abram, and demands Abram be sanctified, be set apart from that which is around him. Get thee out, the Lord says. In order to be saved, Abraham must obey. Graciously, God does not place such a demand upon Abram without help. Along with God's command to get out comes the promise, I will. Where God calls, both truth and grace are found. God says, I will. I will show you a land. I will make you a great nation. I will bless you. I will bless those who bless you. I will curse those who curse you. That is what God will do. This is how He saves men from sin and from themselves. He calls them out, meaning out of their sinful state, their sinful lives, and off of the road to perdition. And while he calls them, he gives them what they need to be forgiven, to overcome temptation, and to walk on that narrow road that leads to eternal life. Similar words, to get out, with the same intention, were uttered by Jesus, who said to Peter and Andrew, follow me. Follow me. For in following him, there was a separation from what was around them. And then the promised, I will. I will make you fishers of men. In another place he said, come unto me, which is another call of separation. And then the promise, I will give you rest. These are not words of suggestion, mind you. They do not include qualifiers, as it would be best if you did what I am telling you to do. For Peter and Andrew, to be saved was a must that they follow. For any man to be saved, he must come unto Jesus. Nowhere is necessary separation stated so forthrightly than in St. Paul's second recorded letter to the Corinthian Church, where he said, quote, Do not be unequally yoked with unbelievers, for what fellowship has righteousness with lawlessness, and what communion has light with darkness. The apostle then quotes a prophet. Therefore, come out from among them and be separate, says the Lord. Do not touch what is unclean, and I will receive you. I will be a father to you, and you shall be my sons and daughters, says the Lord Almighty What we have here again is a call to be separate. And then the Lord gives a promise of what he will do. The directive not to touch what is unclean. Well, that fits well with the opening example in the sermon How often does the Lord need to say to us that we must be separate from the world so that we might be saved? Do not think for one moment that he is not aware how difficult it is to separate ourselves from our surroundings For some people they must separate themselves from the only things they have ever known. Yet separate they must And our Savior knows his request is not easy. And that is why he gives us the I will. You separate and I will. The way of the cross is never easy. And did he not say that few travel on that narrow road? We are to conclude that few travel on it because it is the most difficult road to travel. Abraham, or Abram, excuse me, was slow to get out. The call was to get out of his country, his hometown, and to get out of his father's house. Abram got out of his country and away from the people whom he had known all of his life, but not from his father's house. And this is not a criticism for Abram was honoring his father as he should. The family, you'll note, traveled together from Ur to Haran. It was only after the father's death at Haran that Abram was able to get out from his father's house. His temptation, like all of ours, was to try to improve on his father's house. Rather than forsake it. God instructs us to flee, and because of our emotionally attachments, our emotional attachments, we perceive that such A reaction is unnecessary. That's too broad too general. We just need more time. That our family might change, our friends can come around. Our situation will change in our favor. And God will finally accept us all. Meanwhile, God continues to say, get thee out. God continues to say it because Abram's father's house, like his past life, was full of many gods. Abram's father is a type for us, and that he can represent what is old and what is dying. For us to get out completely, the old must die. Abram is able to depart, he is able to get out from both his country and his father's house when his father is dead. Terah died in Haran and he stayed there. And we again are slow to learn this lesson, but it must be learned, even faith, for Abraham, Abraham was a man of faith. Even faith cannot take the old things into the place of promise. The river of Jordan is not passed over until the old is dead. In Christ, old things pass away. In Christ, all things become new. It is only the new that can enter into the heavenly realm. It must be faced with bold acknowledgement that the old cannot be saved, it cannot be improved, and so it cannot be taken with us. It must pass away. The old was buried with Christ in baptism and must not, cannot continue on. And I refrain at this point in the sermon from listing examples of possible old things that you have tried to keep alive in your life. It is for each of us to be honest before God and His ever-present spirit about what the old things are that we have tried to improve upon and take with us rather than letting them die as they must. They are sins that you have wrestled to overcome, maybe even before you were a Christian or before you took your Christian faith seriously. They must have a final death. We notice that when Abram passes over the Jordan and into the Promised Land, he is introduced to trials. Obviously the devil is not finished with the man who has converted and even left behind the old things of the world. No, such a man is still a marked man. The devil still tempts, and the Lord himself still tries a man to test his mettle and make his faith stronger. And first we notice that although the land of Canaan is to be given by God to Abram and his descendants, Abram enters with no specific claim to any part of the land. Abram is a tent dweller. He is a pilgrim within the land of promise. It is healthy, then, for us to remember at the point of this story that although the land of Cana is a type of our heavenly home, it is not our heavenly home The spirit of faith may enjoy life on this earth, it may enjoy outward things to a point, but it recognizes that this is not our final dwelling place. Just as the Son of Man had no place to lay his head, neither does Abram, and neither do we. Even though we lay our head in the same bed, even in the same lot for twenty, forty, even sixty years This is still not our home. We, like Abram, are pilgrims. The pilgrim life is appointed For all who follow Christ, because true life is always on the go, always moving. Andrew Jukes explained the importance of being on a pilgrimage when he said In the course of a pilgrimage Trials befall us, which others never meet with.
