As hearers of God's word, we must be willing to receive what is spoken to us based on the substance of the message rather than the matter or manner in which it is spoken. The apostle did not come to the Corinthians with eloquent words or wisdom. And again, the word wisdom is Sophia. And in the Greek, it refers to the wisdom of the world, which is to follow the rules of logic. The wisdom of the world, as we noted last week, was philosophical and religious. The philosophical world rejects the possibility of miracles and wishes to dabble into theory. Never satisfied with a conclusion. The world of logic deals with the validity and invalidity of an argument rather than truth. And that may sound strange, but it is accurate. Only when formal logic is used to find a sound argument is it at all worried about truth. The problem with both these branches of wisdom, theory and logic, is that the search for truth is not the goal. I had a professor of philosophy in a seminary who told us that he was ridiculed by his colleagues because he was a Christian. Professional philosophers believe that they should always be seeking wisdom, never setting on any wisdom being enough. His defense was that in seeking wisdom, there's nothing wrong with stopping when you find it, and he found it in Jesus. But Paul rejected the approach of a rhetorician, a logician, and philosopher. For he knew that if he was to come to the Corinthians, impressing them with his oratory skills and reasoning ability, The gospel he was preaching would be rejected and accepted for the wrong reason. Instead, he proclaimed the testimony of God That's what he says, the testimony of God. The very essence of the testimony of God is described in the first two As Jesus Christ and Him crucified. That is what we attempted to embrace last week The testimony of God, that is what God spoke, was his son, Jesus. Jesus was the word that God testified. And all that Jesus said and did for our salvation, his birth, his teaching, his miracles, his death, his resurrection, his ascension, the coming of the Holy Spirit are parts of the testimony of God. The apostle trusted in the substance of God's testimony, believing that that alone was sufficient for people to be saved. We must notice and contrast our own era to that of the apostles' approach. He finds no need for slick advertising. He does not need to practice the old bait and switch. Where there is an appeal to the masses of some entertainment ploy, and then we lock them in and force the gospel down their throat He doesn't need a mass marketing plan such as a packaged book deal followed by speaking engagements and autograph sessions. He doesn't need to write a dissertation that examines all the possible exceptions to the gospel and then refuting each of them. Saint Paul believed that the substance of the gospel is sufficient. We next find that the reason for the apostle's optimism is his understanding and faith in the work of the Holy Spirit. He describes in verse 3 that he came to the Corinthians in weakness, fear, and trembling. Now the adjectives of weakness, fear, and trembling can be summed up in one word, humility. He was weak because he knew that his own speaking abilities and wisdom was not going to convince anybody His fear was that he would be rejected, ridiculed, and possibly even beaten for what he was proclaiming. And there was no doubt in his mind that his fear also, and possibly for the most part, was caused by his reverence for God. He did not want to interfere with the message of the gospel by allowing himself to let God down by himself getting in the way. And we can get in the way. It can be very tempting to take personally arguments thrown up against what you are proclaiming. We then become defensive as if we are defending ourselves. We think we are defending God, but we are really defending ourselves. And besides, God doesn't need us to defend him. It is at best If preachers, teachers, and evangelists, even laity who ministered to another in the name of Christ, do their best to get out of the way. We are to do everything we can to stay on message, not being concerned about how we are being received personally We have spent some time this morning talking about how hearers we are to listen to the substance of the message rather than the manner it is given. On the other hand, for those who proclaim the gospel, whether it be from a pulpit or over the fence to our neighbors, we must be careful about the manner in which we speak. We must do so as the apostle is describing and get out of the way so that the message is what is heard first and foremost. To do so, that is to get out of the way, we must believe in the power and ultimate influence of the Holy Spirit The apostle uses the word dynamos to describe the spirit, which, as you likely guessed, is the root word for our English word dynamite. The Spirit is the explosive power of God who demonstrates the truth of the gospel. The apostle does not describe what he means by demonstration of the power of the Spirit, and he could mean the miracles that occurred at the hands of the Apostles by the moving of the Holy Spirit. People see such and are convinced that what they are hearing is true. This use of miracles, however, as as being power. is not so effective when you look how many Jesus performed, and yet at the end of his life There were none who benefited from those miracles who spoke in his defense or on his behalf. Another meaning of the phrase, demonstration of the power of the Spirit, could be how the people responded to the gospel message. And were transformed by faith upon hearing it without Paul using anything but plain speak. It is this demonstration of the power of the Spirit that we should celebrate for it works within us something that we can't work in ourselves. The Spirit grants faith where skepticism reigned. The Spirit works love where bitterness ruled. The Spirit grants hope when only disappointment has been known. This is the demonstration of the power of the Spirit that men can be changed from inside to out. From the apostles' words, we learn a lesson, both as hearers and witnesses of the gospel. As hearers, we are to hear with ears of faith going beyond the manner of speech. In our maturity, we are to care less and less for the manner And be most concerned about the substance of the message, what is being said. As witnesses, we must do our best to get out of the way That our personalities might not interfere, that our preferences might not be known. But the message, most importantly, We must get ourselves out of the way so the message is the focus, not the messenger In both cases, whether as a hearer or a witness to the gospel, we must have faith that the Holy Spirit will transform the hearts of men and women because the gospel is true. As hearers and witnesses, it truly does come down to the issue of faith. Well perhaps you can settle a question or debate for us. The Reverend McCarrell And I have been talking about strategies to use to get this new ministry in Westminster growing. There are resources that tell him he is to market this new parish by doing a demographic study. And from that information gathered, he is to appeal to what the people in the area prefer. From what St. Paul has said in these five verses, what strategy do you think that he would tell us to use To get St. Andrews growing, to get it to be a viable, self-sufficient parish. Well, after what I have preached, you likely have guessed that that is a rhetorical question. We know the least he would say St. Paul would say is to preach Jesus and Jesus crucified and let the Holy Spirit do the rest. Of course, there is nothing wrong with getting word out that you are present in the community and inform the community how they can come and hear what you have to say. But beyond that, the strategy is simple. Beloved, the kingdom of God needs good listeners and plain speakers and cantaloupe stories once in a while. May that be said of us. Let us pray. Our God, we thank you for the simplicity of the gospel message and for the courage and example of St. Paul. May that continue to be our approach here at St. Stephen's, and for the Reverend McCarrell and all who would claim Jesus That we might speak Jesus and Him crucified, and Holy Spirit trusts in your transformation power. This we pray in Jesus' name. Amen.

sermons.title: Dependency on the Spirit
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. Turn your Bibles to 1 Corinthians chapter 2. Starting at verse six and finishing up that chapter. In general, this latter section of 1 Corinthians chapter 2 tells us that the mysteries of God Do not match up with the wisdom of the human mind. Because we as Christians have the Holy Spirit, we can understand the revealed mysteries of God. But this means the world will not understand us, nor will we understand the world. There has been no time in my lifetime where that has been truer than right now. The Bible warns us that good will be called evil and evil will be called good. And that much we have seen before But men being called women, and women being called men, and children being born with no gender claim is beyond a mindlessness any of us would have predicted. For people's identity and thus their self-worth being found And dictated by their sexual desires is so very unwise, even the wisdom of man can see it as foolishness. The wisdom of humanity, for example, was smart enough to be able to identify and able to say That people who identified as transgender were suffering from a mental disorder. The wisdom of humanity read the statistic. That 41% of people who identify as transgender in the United States have it have attempted suicide. That's compared to 4. 6% of the rest of the population. But the warped-minded, whom only care about protecting their sexual desires Say no, and argue that transgender-identifying people only have a high suicide rate attempt because of how they are persecuted by society. And while persecutions may play a role in suicide attempts amongst transgender identifying people, those who counsel the same people Know the mental confusion and turmoil that their patients suffer. Such people need our sympathy, they need our love, they need our help. But no, culturally, too much pressure was coming from the warped-minded sexual desire protectors that just this last May, just this last May The World Health Organization took transgender identity off of the mental disorder list. So now no one suffering from such confusion gets any help. Thus, our culture has gone so mad that those who say they care most for the sexually confused care least And yet see themselves as righteous in doing so. Switching gears One of the reasons I was drawn to the study of logic was my intrinsic acceptance that there is objectivity in the world. The discipline of logic identifies what is objective in the world and gives the objective names, identity. With those names, logic provides tools for discernment. From a Christian perspective, the discipline of logic is an attribute of God that Reflects God's created world. Therefore, logic, that is deductive logic, follows a set of rules that are in place in the world God created. For example, you know this. If A equals B and B equals C, then A equals C. This logical argument follows rules that cannot be broken. If a law is broken in a logical argument, the conclusion is said to be invalid Which is to say that it is not supported by the structure of the argument. An argument may be expressed as follows. Some Christians are not critical thinkers. Some pagans are not critical thinkers. Therefore, some pagans are Christians. Now, most of us would readily identify that there is something wrong with such an argument, but we could not identify what's wrong with it unless we had some training. In basic logic, the student learns how to prove the invalidity of arguments by what we call counterexamples. If I can present an argument using the same form as the previous argument, substituting a conclusion with a statement that is obviously false, I can prove the previous argument to be invalid. For example, some women are not lawyers. That's true. Some men are not Lawyers. That's true. Therefore, some men are women. Now you intrinsically know that such an argument is invalid, but you don't know why. The discipline of logic identifies the why. But such logic doesn't penetrate the culture we now have. Now in our upside-down culture, some men may feel they are women, making this argument valid for them. It doesn't matter that genetically speaking this argument is absurd. But today, how a person feels eliminates all rules of logic What is a Christian to do? What is the church to do to turn the culture toward God? And back to common sense living, let alone righteous living. I don't want to be overly simple when I answer such questions So I will give part of an answer of what we are to do. We are to become more conscientiously dependent on the Holy Spirit. St. Paul is teaching us in chapter 2 that we are fully dependent on the Holy Spirit to understand the things of God. We have read that the apostle did not come preaching with the wisdom of men. In fact He even discredits such wisdom, leaving us with the possible conclusion that Christians aren't to understand or study the wisdom of the world at all. Let it be stated emphatically that that is not what he is saying here. The apostle is using the wisdom of the world in two ways. The first way is to compare or contrast the wisdom of the world with the mysteries of God's wisdom. The second is to reveal how the wisdom of the world in no way is a means to salvation The wisdom of man, such as the discipline of logic, is like the saying that I have heard our senior warden who who professes when he is on the golf course and he hits a good shot Even a blind squirrel finds an acorn every now and again. That is true of Stan's golf game, and it is true regarding the wisdom of the world. We do stumble on to truth every now and again, even though such truth is revealed outside of a person's knowledge of God. For example, the pound per square inch of the pull of gravity is a constant, whether you are a Christian or a non-Christian. Mathematics, biology, physics, and so forth have truths that are constant, discoverable, and understandable, whether one is a believer in Jesus Christ or not. What modern man glories in is the fact that he is wise enough to discover these facts of the world around him. From the humanist perspective, since the days of the Enlightenment, modern man believes in his capabilities, his ability to think. He believes them to be endless. Much like the builders of the Tower of Babel, modern man believes that with enough time, he can find the keys to the universe to unlock all of its mysteries Enabling him to solve world hungry, bring an end to wars, cure sickness and disease of every kind. Be guilt-free while expressing his sexual desires, and yes, even discover how a human can live forever. By way of contrast, we are asked to compare the wisdom of mankind to the wisdom of God. According to verse 6, the wisdom of the gospel of which the apostle preaches is not the wisdom of the contemporary man of his time or of ours. The wisdom of God is mysterious, secret, and hidden. The only way then for any man to receive such wisdom is by revelation, not by personal discovery. And the revelations of God are only revealed to an individual by the Holy Spirit. The revelations of God are so beyond the wisdom of man. And the apostle points this out in verse 8 that even after God's plan was completed through his Son, It was still not understood by the rulers of that day. Rulers were usually perceived by the masses as being the most wise, the most thoughtful, insightful. Yet even these men who are attributed great wisdom did not know to whom they were speaking, mocking, accusing, and murdering. And he stood personally before them. It is proper for us to be reminded of an often quoted passage that gets many Christians out of trouble. It is from Isaiah chapter 55, where the Lord says, my thoughts are not your thoughts. Neither are your ways my ways. As the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts. Now, we tend to use this passage when questions come to us regarding the truths of God's universe, and because we don't know the answer, we say, well, God's ways are above our ways, and so on. This passage is most appropriate to use when describing how our salvation is accomplished. Imagine if you or I were to be the decision makers of how men were to be saved. How would we save mankind? Perhaps we would start a feasibility study, then follow up with a survey. Those always are helpful. We could find a contractor with a good reputation, but on the low end of the cost scale He most certainly wouldn't do as God has done. From the Old Testament, we should realize that our ways are not his ways. When Abraham is instructed by the Lord to leave his land and family and to travel to a new land, obeying a new God, this would have been seen by us to be very unwise. When Joshua is instructed to defeat a fortified city by marching around it for seven days and then, on one day, seven times, and then shouting at it. You and I would have said that our leader has become a bit insane. If we were within the Council of Gideon and heard that only 300 men were to go up against the army of the Midianites We would have speculated that a mutiny was required. Our thoughts are not his thoughts. Our wisdom is not his wisdom. A blind squirrel may find an acorn, but he will never find the pearl of great price, and neither will a human being. What is needed more than the wisdom of man, what is needed is beyond our grasp, but not certainly not beyond availability To understand what we need, we must first be reminded of our humble state. All men are born in sin. Which means the spirit of deadness is within us. We are captivated by it. Without the Holy Spirit, we are dead spiritually. And the cause of that death we know is Adam's sin, and we are covenant members of his family. Thus we receive that death. And this is what it means to say for the wages of sin is death. It is our spiritual death We being dead need to be revived. God needs to come down and reveal to us our dead state, our blind state. We are utterly dependent upon God to reveal to us what we would not imagine, could not conceive, could not understand, could not see for ourselves. We are dependent on the revelatory work of the Spirit of God, each of us. Revelation, the scholars tell us, occurs in both the natural and the spiritual. We remember from Romans chapter 1 how the Apostle Paul refers to natural revelation where he says that God has revealed himself in creation and therefore no one is without excuse for not believing that he exists. Natural revelation tells us that there is order in the universe. It tells us that there are laws that govern God's creation. It tells us that there is never an effect without a cause. It is fair to conclude then that God is the cause and the world is the effect. The question that is asked by many is just how far does natural revelation go? To question it poignantly, can a man find salvation in Christ? Via natural revelation. From the words of the Apostle Paul in our passage, we can conclude that the answer is no. I ran across this quote by G. K. Chesterton, and it confirms to me again that the man was a prophet. He said, quote, today the scientific temper is scientific doubt It isn't scientific doubt of religion. It is scientific doubt of science. The whole thing is working backwards and destroying itself. And so far as one can guess, it will end in that mystical ignorance in which all those myths arose. That was said a hundred years ago and applies more to our day. While the secular cries for science to be heated over God. When science says what is obvious about humanity that men are biologically men and women are biologically women, the whole thing starts working backwards as science then is no longer accepted as an authority. From Chesterton's insights and from what our culture is doing to itself, we can see how dead people eventually turn on themselves. Dead people turn on dead people. Of course they are going to destroy themselves because they are already destroyed. That's all they know. They think they can save themselves. But they will only destroy themselves more than they are already destroyed. After all, what is destroyed only has the ability to destroy itself more This is not a Pentecost Sunday sermon, but a mere sermon from 1 Corinthians chapter 2. And yet is the glorious truth that the only way for humanity to get out of the cycle of destroying itself is to have an intervention by the Holy Spirit. When telling the gospel story, we say that the incarnation of Jesus was necessary. We say that the death of Jesus was necessary. We say that the resurrection was necessary. I remind us every year how important Ascension Day is. And while we on Pentecost Sunday say that the Holy Spirit is important, we must say it and believe it every day, not only for ourselves. but for the dead and the self-destroying world. Without the Spirit, the plan of God could not have been understood, could not have been believed, could not have been embraced. As Jesus said, I will send the Holy Spirit and He will reveal all things to you. He that is the Spirit will lead us to all truth. I believe it to be humorous and somewhat pleasing to see how when Paul is making this point, he he uses human wisdom, he uses logic to explain to us our dependency on the Holy Spirit. In verse 11, he explains that only a man truly knows his own thoughts, just as God only knows his own thoughts. Hence, it takes the Holy Spirit to reveal to us what God has thought of our salvation. Now, along with our realized dependency upon the Holy Spirit, comes the recognition, as he says here, that the Spirit has a particular language. By referring to words taught here, he's not talking about the gift of tongues. He is referring to a vocabulary that can only be understood by Christians, by people who have been awakened by the Holy Spirit. Throughout this sermon, I have used language like pearl of great price, death, and being made alive, being blind, and now seen. Those who have been awakened by the Spirit understand and relate to that language. For it describes what we have experienced by the power of the Holy Spirit. Because we speak a different language, we should not be surprised when men without the Spirit do not understand or relate to what we are saying or how we are living. Our reasoning, our language, and our judgments will be different than the world. And we should not be surprised or offended when the world has conflicts with us as a result. As the Spirit reveals more and more to us, we become people who make judgments about things And that phrase that Paul uses is not to be understood that we judge people, for only God will judge man But regarding things of the world, we we are to be with the Holy Spirit's help making decisions discerning what is righteous and unrighteous, what is holy or unholy, what is beneficial or dangerous, what is of the flesh or what is of God. Perhaps if we start and consistently continue to look at the world, the unbelieving world. As destroyed and continuing to destroy itself, perhaps we would have greater compassion towards people And with our compassion, we will pray more diligently for the Holy Spirit to reveal himself to the unbelievers. To young believers that we know in our lives, like our family members, and strangers that we will meet, people at our work The Holy Spirit has to intervene in their lives. God has to open their eyes to see the truth. And you can reason with them if you will. You can continue to be frustrated by their baffling moral reasoning if you must. But it should be expected. In Dante's Inferno, the fifth level of hell Finds punishment for those given to wrath and sullenness. Dante sees both sins as the sin of anger. If you have seen on the news those who protest for their sexual desires to be fulfilled, you will see people who are given over to anger. The eternal punishment of the of the wrathful, of those given over to anger, is that they repeatedly consume one another. Repeatedly consume one another That is the nature of the demonic that has taken over our culture. Let us do battle with such demons. Calling for the Holy Spirit to guide our family, our friends, strangers we come to meet, that he might reveal the truth to them. That is their only hope. And it is ours as well. Let us pray. Our God, we thank you for the confidence of Saint Paul in the Holy Spirit, penetrating that which the wisdom of man cannot And here we stand amidst a culture that has truly lost its way, is turning on itself for destruction. Father, Holy Spirit, come be among us. Father, penetrate the hearts of those who need it. That truth might be seen and people might be saved. This we pray in Jesus' name. Amen.

sermons.title: Undivided Increase
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. We continue our series in the book of First Corinthians, so I encourage you to turn there. As an introduction, share with you how several years ago it dawned on me When my children were young, oldest in their early teens and the rest younger, that if they were to coordinate themselves They would have gotten away with a great deal of disobedience and mischief. If they had looked out for one another when it came to mom and dad finding out about their bad behavior If they had coordinated their stories so as to make plans so that mom and dad would not be aware, if they would have worked as a team to get what they wanted They could have easily outmaneuvered Bobby Lynn and I. But alas, they usually turned on one another There was always a tattletale in the bunch who wanted a sibling to get into trouble more than he or she wanted to get away with something. And the desire for a sibling to get into trouble was usually out of spite for a past wrong done to them, or simple jealousy not wanting to see a sibling get praise over them. I know this because I grew up in a household that had siblings close together in age. I know this because I too am a sinner. And when sinners live together and are immature in their character, spite and jealousy are commonplace. When spite and jealousy are present between family members, the result is a sin that God the Father has told us he particularly hates. In the book of Proverbs, you remember in chapter 6, we are told that there are six things the Lord hates, seven things that are detestable to him. Being his servants, followers, and being called his children, it seems wise that once we know what these seven things are, we should try to avoid them at all costs. Of course, each should be avoided with the same determination, but the seventh one is going to be our focus this morning. To understand the syntax better, we may condense the passage to say, the Lord detests a man who stirs up dissension among brothers. The words stir up are used in a metaphorical sense, in that the dissension is used as a pot or a meal. That is agreeable when at rest, but when it is stirred, it changes its relation. It's no longer edible. This proverb recognizes the possibility of dissension, even between God's people, that it is always a possibility. If the causes of dissension are left alone, we continue to be united. When another comes along and stirs us up The result is fight, jealousy, and anger. The reasons for someone stirring up dissension within God's family are numerous and varied according to personalities and problems with which an individual is dealing What occurs most often by my observation is that persons do not usually realize they are stirring up dissension. Yet that is exactly what they are doing. What are we doing, if not stirring up dissension, when we speak unkindly of a brother or sister in Christ? What are we doing, if not stirring up dissension, when we pass on an unfavorable story about a brother or sister in Christ? What are we doing if not stirring up dissension when we criticize the ministry of a person or that of a church? What are we doing, if not stirring up dissension, when we declare our spirituality to be superior to another? Our ability, it seems, to stir up dissension knows no bounds. This is why the apostle has spoken so very directly to the Corinthians about unity. We concluded from the first chapter that unity, our unity, is not to be based on our likes or dislikes Our personalities and backgrounds, or our preferences, even preferences in music, our unity is based on our confession. What we confess of Christ and the residing Spirit of God that lives within each of us, those are what unite us. In the passage read this morning, the apostle attacks a specific cause of Christian disunity. And he does so once again in a direct manner. But before I get to that, I need to smash an idol here and now. We must smash an idol of unity at all costs. Such is the priority of liberal churches that worship the idol of unity so devoutly that they will not call people the people of God to holy living. They worship unity over the moral purity of the people, leaving people comfortable in their sin. That idol is not of God and is to become fragments and discarded, which is to say smashed. Amen? In 1 Corinthians 3, St. Paul has gone from a deep description regarding both our dependency and freedom in the Spirit, that's chapter 2. to essentially chastising the Christians worshiping at this Corinthian church. I would even characterize the tone of this passage to be a lecture It is a lecture from a father figure to his children in Christ as he corrects them and directs them away from their immature behavior. No one knows how well the Corinthian Christians accepted these words from the apostle. But I think it is fair to speculate when considering our own personalities that some did not take too kindly to being referred to as babies who still need milk. When the apostle first ministered to them, of course he gave them milk, for they were naturally immature in their faith. The disappointment is caused by the discovery that the church has not matured and that they still need milk rather than meat. And the analogy of an infant growing to an adult can be offensive, but it can also be very effective It provides many truths with one picture. And the most obvious truth includes the need for milk at one stage and the need for solid foods at another stage. Each type of food furthers the maturation. Another truth, this is a good one, another truth is that we are always maturing. Life in the body of Christ does not consist of stunted growth. There is always more to learn, more to be challenged by, more to believe. As E. M. Bounds has stated, quote, all of life is but a preparation for what is to come after. The primer of faith is never closed for the child of God. Its lessons never end. No matter what circumstances may abode, we remain under the bar of instruction forever. Every incident builds upon the last and anticipates the next. Oh, how much more we need to live being aware of such a truth. We're always learning. The Christians at Corinth had to understand that truth, truth that they are always growing. is necessary to build upon the lessons of the past. They are a divided people here and and these divided people are identified by the fact that they still drink milk as a main course. And the evidence of their infantile stage is the jealousy and the quarreling among them. But feelings of jealousy and quarreling are not exclusive to the Christians at Corinth. I dare say that there is not a body of Christ. that comes together, that does not have the temptation to be jealous or quarrel amongst themselves. We can succumb to jealousy due to another's financial state compared to ours We can be jealous of another's education, their spouse, their children, their background, their heritage, their looks. Jealousy, of course, leads to quarrels, and this is what James said in his epistle. James asks, what causes fights and quarrels among you? Don't they come from your desires that battle within you? You want something, but don't get it. You kill and covet, but you cannot have what you want. Seems here from James that the only motivation for quarrels is selfish, is self. One of the main causes of their quarreling and jealousy in Corinth is the spiritual pride certain parties have over others because of whose ministry they were converted under and whom they claim to still be following. Some said that they followed the ministry of Paul, some say Apollos, others say Peter. I can testify to you today that such speech has occurred in every circle of faith that I have been a part of. Growing up Roman Catholic gave me a sense of pride by the fact that I was baptized into the only true church. That's what they told me. That is what the Roman Catholics believe, that they are the only true church. I was taught that all Protestant churches were illegitimate wannabes. They were insufficient and lacked the keys of the kingdom that were only given to Peter and all those who followed after him in his papal office. I am of the true church, I could say. Yet after I had been born again, having a born-again experience, I was led to a non-denominational charismatic church And that group taught me to understand the difference between a common Christian and a spirit-filled Christian. The spirit-filled Christian was one who had been baptized in the Holy Spirit, evidence for speaking in tongues. It became part of our discussion with other Christians to question them, well, are you spirit-filled? If they were not, we would consider them to be inferior in the faith. The third group I joined was the Church of the Nazarene, which is part of the holiness tradition. That tradition believes that the entire sanctification of a person, entire sanctification, is possible in this life. And identifies Christians as either entirely sanctified or not entirely sanctified. And now I have entered a fourth group, which is of the Reformed Episcopal Church, and the Reformed Episcopal Church is a partner of Anglicanism. Anglicans are marked by their adherence to the liturgy found in the Book of Common Prayer. And Anglicans cannot only see their worship as superior to other churches. They can be uppity toward one another depending on what version of the Book of Common Prayer is followed. We, in case you didn't know, follow the 1662 version. So neener, neener, neener to those who don't All kidding aside, there are other respectable versions of the Book of Common Prayer, but but I want you to know my opinion about the 1979 version. That has been adopted by the Episcopal Church and is used today. And it is one of the worst versions ever printed. And the Church of England never recognized it as legitimate, and it should be avoided. The apostle's lecture continues as describing persons who are divided. He calls them, hear this, mere men. As mere men, they are no different than men of the world. Men of the world divide over personality and preferences. Men of the world allow jealousy to justify their intolerance. Men of the world choose another to follow in order to be different than the rest and raise their level of self-worth. Mere men do not recognize that the men they are following, the sides they are choosing, also consist of mere men. What is a minister, after all, but a man? And in accordance with the pecking order of society, a minister is lower, for he is to be a servant. Two men. See verse five. As a servant, a minister merely does what he is assigned to do, and by all accounts of Holy Scripture, it is not an enjoyable job. Even though we only work on Sunday. Look at the life of Moses. His own countrymen exiled him. When he returned, he was thought to be a zealot He was called of God to appear before mighty Pharaoh with a stick in hand and a message from God saying, Pharaoh, you are to obey me. Look at Aaron, a weak man, if there ever was one in Scripture, who had the people telling him what to do on one side and the voice of God on another. He was the one assigned to go into the Holy of Holies to offer an annual sacrifice to God. If he or the sacrifice were not found worthy, it would cost him his life on the spot. How many of you would want such a job? Then there is the likes of Samuel who had to speak the truth to an obstinate people. And Elijah, who had to confront an insane king and his wife, who was also insane, rebuking them for their sin. Then there are the likes of Jeremiah who was a single voice against numerous prophets. Those prophets told the king and the people Everything was perfectly fine. God was loving us. We're doing everything right. At the same time, Jeremiah had the true word of God burning in his heart. Burning in his heart so hot, it was necessary for him to either speak it or be consumed by it. When he spoke it, he was ridiculed, rejected, and even exiled, because it was not the message the people wanted. He told them God was not pleased. There was sin and it needed to be repented of, or they would be destroyed as a nation. The end result was Jeremiah being taken away and exiled to Egypt as a false prophet, and the false prophets being heeded. Men who speak the truth as God has revealed it do not revel in their calling. Such a calling has never been easy and it never will be. A minister, a true minister, does not speak on his own or come up with his own doctrine, but he gets it from God, from his holy word. To choose the side of one minister over another is to focus upon the man, not the message. And ministers also do not have the same responsibilities. And the Corinthians should have known this. Paul came introducing the gospel to the people at Corinth. Apollo followed by providing clarification and teaching as to what Paul introduced. If there were any results in what was if there were any results in both of their work, it was not due to what the person planted or what the person watered. It was due to God. Many of us, many of us will speak highly of ministers who have influenced our lives, and that is perfectly understandable. But we should be thankful to God for them and the reality that God used them, but in reality how effectual they were in our lives was actually God. Many have attributed godliness to the Reverend Billy Graham for his ministry. It is certainly necessary that we give God thanks for such a faithful servant. But as the Nixon tapes revealed, Graham was not a perfect man. The fruit of his ministry was not due to the greatness of Billy Graham, but the grace of God. God gave the increase. While the divided are drinking their milk as an entree and acting like mere men Paul says the united see God. The united are well aware that ministers are only men, and that God gives the increase. The United see that whatever has grown, whatever is fruitful, whatever remains, is because of God. Now I personally have never built anything lasting in my life, although as I s as I wrote that down, I remember as one time I tried to build a doghouse And I did such a terrible job on that doghouse using old lumber that when we went to move, I we couldn't move it out of its place, and the dog never slept in it. So I don't really think that's building anything. But I have hung sheet rocks, I have laid tresses, I have pounded shingles, but I did not build anything. I was just a laborer. And so I am today. So is any man who ministers the gospel. We are just laborers To see a man and to choose to follow or not follow him based on whether we like him or dislike him is to be blinded to God. I could be a definitive imbecile, hardly able to put two sentences together, and if God wanted to use me to bring people to Christ, then they are going to be brought to Christ. Unfortunately, if such a scenario existed, we would still have some people saying, I am a Paul, I am of Apollos, and I am of imbecile. This, of course, is the talk of mere men. The undivided, the united, say, I am of God. The primary doctrine of the Christian faith, as you know, is the doctrine of the Trinity. God in three persons, yet one God. There is difference and there is unity. We confess that the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are separate persons and one substance. That unity we highlight this morning, for it was Jesus, as was read today, in the high priestly prayer, as recorded in John 17. It is there that Jesus prayed that his followers would be one, united, as he and the Father are united. The depth of that prayer cannot be overstated. We are to be united with the same unity, the same oneness of the Trinity. That is a high calling indeed. And until it happens, we continue to fall short of God's perfect will. It is on that convicting note that I wish to end this morning. Until Christ's prayer is answered, we continue to we need to continue to confess that we are in sin. For what is sin is falling short of God's perfect will. And what is God's perfect will, but that his people be not divided but united as the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are united. And so may the Trinity be our example. May we settle for nothing less. When a brother speaks divisively, let us point him to the unity of the Trinity. When a sister acts divisively, let us point her to the unity of the Trinity. We are not followers of mere men, and we are not to be mere men. We are followers of the Trinity. And we are to be one. Let us pray. Father, we thank you for the fervent message of the apostle now bringing twice in these first three chapters the issue the subject of the unity necessary of your people Father, may we heed it, may we be humbled by it, and may it be the goal of each one of us here. We pray this in Jesus' name. Amen.

sermons.title: The Only Foundation
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Ghost, Amen. Please be seated. Turn in your Bibles to First Corinthians chapter three. We're picking up at verse 10. First Corinthians chapter 3, 10 through 23. You've ever noticed nursery rhymes nursery rhymes cause us to abandon reality. Take, for example, the story of the three little pigs. We are asked to buy into the fact that three little pigs can build houses One made of straw, one made of wood, and the last of brick, were to believe this without questioning how they can grasp a hammer or a towel with hoofs and no opposing thumbs. There are too many questions related to the story that go unanswered. For example, where did they learn the skills to construct a home? What does a pig need a home for anyway? How did they purchase the materials that they needed? How did they hoist trusses and lay roofing with no construction equipment? The only character in the three little pigs story that remains true to reality is the wolf. The wolf, after all, wants to eat, and a pig is a pretty good meal for a wolf. Of course, how the wolf ends up being able to blow houses down made of straw and wood is not known, but at least the wolf is acting like a wolf. What I consider a great irony in the story is that a pig that is able to build houses is certainly able to tote a 12-gauge shotgun With one pull of the trigger, with those magical hoofs, the wolf would be dead and the pigs could live in whatever house they wished. Of course, this is getting off the moral of the story, which teaches us that if something is to be built to last, it must be built over time and with quality material. The pig that builds his house with straw is able to finish sooner than his brothers and with less sweat, but he is the first to have to abandon his home. The second finish is a little later than the first, but is quicker than the third, for he builds his house out of wood The wood is sturdier than the straw, and it takes longer for the wolf to blow his house down, but the wolf eventually succeeds. The two brothers then must flee from the woodhouse to the brick house built by the third pig. The house took more time made out of brick and more effort to build, but it was able to withstand the blowing of the wolf and all of them were safe. That is a happy ending, although in the original story The first two pigs actually get eaten by the wolf, and it's only the third that survives. But that's much sadder, so we have to pretend that when the first pig had his house blown down, that he was faster than a wolf. and ran to the to the house made of wood and then they both were faster than the wolf and made it to the brick house. All of it very unbelievable Of course, you may be wondering what this has to do with 1 Corinthians chapter 3. Well, after the Apostle Paul chastised the Corinthians for their disunis unity He describes the importance of building upon the faith of a person, and by using lasting materials, and builders, using builders who are responsible Most scholars believe this passage of scripture is directed to ministers, for they are called to build into the lives of their people. And we will concur that this is the primary audience. But we will also recognize that the laity are to learn something from these instructions as well. This passage is especially important for our day. In the first century, as I noted a few weeks ago, there were not a lot of teachers to choose from. Paul came preaching the gospel. Apollos continued Paul's teaching, bringing the Corinthians to a greater depth in faith. And some teachings had been received by letter and messengers of St. Peter, yet there was no second Church of the Corinthians to attend. There were no books to buy or Christian radio to hear. Today our ability to choose the teachers and preachers of the gospel, or builders, as Paul would call them. is like standing in line at the Golden Corral. There is much to choose, and most of us try a little bit of each. When my children were young and given free reign to fill up their own drinking cup at a restaurant like Golden Corral, they would, you know, a little bit of this, a little bit of this, a little bit of this, a little bit of this But that's what some people do with their theology. A little bit of this, a little bit of this, a little bit of this. They sample a little from several teachers, not realizing that some teachings contradict others as some soda drinks don't mix well together. So the lessons learned in this passage can be heard by laity As you recognize that you are responsible for the choices you make on who you allow to build in your life and what type of materials you're allowing them to use. Well regardless of whom the laity chooses or how ministers build, the one thing necessary is that the foundation must be Jesus Christ. That is in verse 11. The manner that the apostle phrases this passage causes us to question whether he is saying that it is impossible for another to lay a foundation beside Jesus Christ. or that no other foundation can replace Christ who has already been laid as a foundation. The latter interpretation fits the context best. However, the apostle could well be saying both, as it is argued that there is no other foundation to build upon but Jesus Christ. Jesus Christ is the foundation of the church, both personally and doctrinally. He is the personal foundation in that he is real. He existed. He died. He rose again, and he lives forevermore. Christians do not build their lives on legend or myth, but on a person who is both human and divine. Our foundation is as doctrinal as it is personal, for we build upon Jesus Christ, who was revealed to us as God's only begotten Son. He was begotten, we say, not made. This means that he had no beginning, but always was. It was at the incarnation that he was begotten as a man and remained so, sitting at the right hand of the Father. Doctrinally, we say he created all things. He atoned for the sins of man. He is coming again to judge the living and the dead. Doctrinally, we say that he is the only way to the Father, and that if a man desires eternal life, he must believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, having no other gods before him. A minister must believe, teach, and preach that Jesus Christ is the only foundation, or he is not a Christian minister. A minister who rejects this foundation, the chief cornerstone, must himself be rejected by the church as an apostate and disciplined until he repents. It is sad to report that too often in our day the church has done little to ensure God's people have a firm foundation being preached and taught from pulpits It can seem immature to name names and thus appear to be a tattletale, but I believe It is necessary for the church to publicly rebuke, as Scripture commands, those who preach and teach falsely. Some of you may have heard this name, Bishop Spong, S-P-O-N-G, Spong. He's an example for us. He was a bishop of Newark, New Jersey, serving within the Episcopal Church, who has written books explicitly denying the resurrection of Christ. And denying other core Christian doctrines, yet he has never been brought up on charges from his denomination. The catastrophic result of the church's unwillingness to ensure Jesus Christ as foundational is evident in a poll that was conducted among American Protestants. An amazing 78% of Presbyterians nationwide believe that a man's work is what gets him to heaven. 78% The numbers among Lutherans, Methodists, and Episcopalians are slightly higher. Only 33% of Lutherans, 33% of Methodists, and 28% of Episcopalians believe that Jesus was without sin. Paul Himlike, a theologian, Lutheran theologian at Roanoke College, stated that, quote, these figures signal a complete breakdown of catechetical instruction. An absolute collapse, he said, in mainline Protestantism. Episcopal theologian Gerald McDermott, also of our own note. Concurs the same as he states, quote, This happened because in the last thirty years American pastors have lost their nerve to preach a theology that goes against the grain. They are afraid to preach and teach anything that challenges what people already think. The result is a belief in a meek, mild-mannered God who does not want to judge us. As Christians, I believe it is important that you know who has rejected Jesus Christ as foundation. But once the foundation of Jesus Christ has been laid, is it necessary to build? And we must concur that the building materials with which we build does matter. It can be a great danger to understand one's Christian faith as merely a one-time experience. Once that experience with God is over, we may be convinced that that was enough. Nothing more needs to be done. The illustration of our lives being built communicate that the experience of laying a foundation is only the beginning. If someone converts to Christianity by confessing their sin and Christ as their Savior, that is not an end. That is a beginning. That is why when our Lord appeared to Peter after his resurrection, he told Peter, Feed, my sheep. Feeding is another metaphor like building. Each inform us that there is more growth to take place. And besides, as has been noted by many, Jesus didn't commission the church to make converts. He called the church to make disciples, and a disciple is always learning by definition. It is not difficult to understand, and that is why the lesson of the found of that is found in the nursery rhyme of the three little pigs That the type of building materials used determine how long the structure will last. In verse twelve We find the description of the optional building materials. We have gold, silver, costly stone, wood, hay, or straw. Although these materials are listed in succession, there is an obvious division between the materials that are precious and last versus those that are common and destructible. The precious and lasting materials are those that can stand heat of fire, and in case of fire, are actually purified in the process. The other materials cannot last within a fire, but are destroyed. Therefore, the only way to tell whether one has used lasting or destructible material To build his life is to see whether his building survives the fire of the last day. Our present-day culture provides a good example about how buildings can appear to be made of lasting material, but when they are tested are found to be mere facades We can cover our houses with brick facade, with wood facade, and to the eye it can appear that that's good quality, but when tested, they are shown to be lacking. In verse 13, the apostle states that a man's work will be shown for what it is on the day it will be brought to light It will be revealed with fire, and the fire will test the quality of each man's work. The use of the word day appears to refer to either the light of day revealing a man's work or the day of judgment. as in that one particular day when all of humanity will stand before the judgment seat of Christ The latter interpretation is more likely, for when Paul uses the word day, it is usually in reference to the last day, to judgment day. It is on that day that each person will be shown for who he or she truly is, and what quality is his or her building material. What will be revealed is that while many appear to be godly, for they say all the right things and appear to have all things in order, The day, that is judgment day, will reveal it was all just a facade. And the opposite is true. Others appear to be living disordered lives and say confusing things, but on that day, judgment day, it will be revealed that they have a firm foundation. The fire that reveals what material is lasting and what is destructible is a fire that can be used of God in this present life and the life to come. The life to come again refers to eternal judgment. And this life, the fire exists in the form of trials and tribulations. When these are experienced individually and corporately, they reveal what we are made of, what is really within us. The building material used by parents upon their children is revealed as lasting or consumable when a child is out on his own. The material of a marriage is revealed when stress, financial struggle, and in-law strain the relationship. The building material of a parish is revealed when sin knocks at the door, when disagreement occurs, when dissension is stirred from within. These are the times that tell us what we are truly made of. As the apostle describes in verses 14 and 15, The day of judgment and fire from present trials can reveal a building built with destructible materials. And this alone, he says, however, does not exclude a person from the kingdom of God. A person who has the foundation of Jesus Christ, they will be saved, to be sure. However, a life built with perishable materials will be one of pain and one to escape. Too often we see Christians struggling in their marriage, in their church, with their children, in their finances, etc. , etc. , as they appear to move from one tragedy to another They suffer loss and continuous setbacks for the simple reason that their life is built with perishable, destructible material. They are saved But through present-day fire. The encouragement of the Apostle is for all builders to use lasting materials. And for all laity to receive only lasting materials. For the simple reason that all of God's people are temples. Temples. The temple, as it is designed and built in the Old Testament, is made of and adorned with gold and silver and costly stones. If we are the temples of God, that is, we are chosen receptacles of the Holy Spirit, then we should be built with nothing less than that which is precious, lasting, and costly. The problem resides in the disbelief that God's people are actually temples If ministers truly believe such, they would not build into people's lives simple and mostly incomplete truths. There continues a strong wind of influence today from ministers to make their messages relevant. The critique is that the message of man suffering in sin and in need of repentance and a savior is no longer attractive to the modern ear. The result are sermons comparable to the Time and Life series. Well that's dating myself. Time and Life How To book series, you remember published many years ago Every sermon is based on how to, how to be a better husband, how to be successful in your job, how to be at peace with yourself, etc. The gospel has become a self-help motivational series rather than a transformational truth that leads a person out of sin. and into the loving, gracious presence of Almighty God through the meritorious work of Jesus Christ. If a builder uses the wisdom of this world, he is using wood, hay, and straw. And these will be consumed, and the wolf will have its way with the builders. Those who allow such materials to build their lives may be saved, but with sorrow and suffering in this life. The call is for Christians to build and be built with materials that last, and we do so because of whom we are in Christ. This is why the apostle ends this section by telling us that all things are ours. What does he mean by that? All things are ours. By this he is stating that we are owned temples, and as such we should be built up like his temple. Live and be built up to your potential. You are responsible. In the Christian faith, we do not suspend reality with fairy tale. We are not pigs, for we have opposable thumbs. We can be built up with gold, silver, and costly stones. I will continue to do my best To build up in your lives what is precious and what will survive fire. But building takes time It takes money. It takes great effort, patience, and carefulness. If the Lord gives us the time, may we give him our best effort. Amen. Let us pray. Our Father, we thank you for this lasting metaphor. Of how our lives are to be built, of how your church is to be built. Father, may we not compromise in any time that we do, bring us to repentance and give us better minds. And may we pass the foundation stone on to our children and our children's children, that all of us and our families may be built up until that day. In Jesus' name we pray. Amen.

sermons.title: Baptized to life or death
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: It will break me, like now me and only all my glory. Name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. It's good to have in-laws here. Appreciate the McNulty family. And since they're here, I thought I'd begin with a story that I had heard. This story is about a young boy who went to his parents to ask them about the beginning of the human race. He asked his mother, he said, Mom, where did the human race come from? And she told him that God created Adam and Eve and that they had children and they eventually populated the earth. But the boy was still curious, so he went and asked his father He said that humans evolved from primitive creatures to monkeys and eventually humans. Confused, the boy returned to his mother and asked, how come she said that humans came from God and dad said they came from monkeys And the mother without hesitation said, Because I was describing the history of my side of the family. The McNultys are great in-laws and we hope they feel the same about us. And we all take the role of raising children, grandchildren quite seriously because raising children can be difficult Comedian Jerry Seinfeld said that having a two-year-old is like having a blender with no top on it Comedian Jim Gaffigan said that if you want to know what it's like to have a fourth child, imagine yourself drowning and someone hands you a baby. Regarding parenting techniques, comedian Stephen Wright said that his grandfather would have him stand in the closet for five minutes without moving and told him it was elevator practice And comedian Michael McIntyre said that young couples that look forward to being parents that think it's going to be so wonderful He describes a young couple saying goodnight to each other before children. They say, sleep well, darling, and the husband and the wife says, Oh, I will. And McIntyre is so disgusted by their confidence that he says he can't remember the last time he said to his wife, Sleep well, darling. For with two toddlers, what they say to each other before they go to bed is, good luck. So what did you come here to see today? Some of you came this morning not knowing there was a baptism, so you say you simply came to see Jesus. And he is with us in word and in sacrament. But if you knew there was a baptism today and you came anticipating the baptism, I ask again, what did you come to see? From unbelieving eyes, what you see is a baby getting wet and a bunch of adults making a big deal about it. Before the eyes of Christians, however, what we see is something a great deal more than a baby getting wet. The Apostle Peter gives us a type and an anti-type picture of what occurs when a person is baptized. The type is Noah's family, being saved through the waters of the flood. The anti-type is the reality that the rest of humanity, all but Noah's family, is destroyed by the flood. So as where some were saved by the water, and so many were condemned in the water, water that was sanctioned by God. So now so many are saved by the water God sanctions that baptism within his covenant with Christ as its head. In Holy Scripture, the images are constant, for water is used both to save and to condemn. Consider the waters of the Red Sea. St. Paul uses the image of the Israelites escaping bondage in Egypt by passing through the Red Sea on dry ground, and he says it was their baptism. And we remember in that story that the same water was used to drown the Egyptian army. For after the Israelites had crossed over, the walls of water came crashing down on the enemies of God's people. And so it is with water baptism. Baptism can be to many a means of grace, wherein God washes the heart clean of original sin As the Holy Spirit becomes an integral part of a person's life, as he or she is now marked by God and a member of Christ's Church, or Or the water is used as a testimony against him, which is to say that he was given the birthright of a child of God, but sold the birthright for the ways of the world. And so what was just done for Jacob's son will either be water poured upon him that saves him, or condemns him. I know that doesn't sound like good news, but you need to hear me out. This is a celebratory time, to be sure. But it is only celebratory if we take the vows we have heard very seriously. For reasons only God knows, the salvation each of us has is not dependent on anything we can do. But we work out our salvation in a manner that perceives that it is up to us And it's the same for our children's salvation, for they are fully dependent on what we do and yet fully responsible themselves. These two realities are consistent with the tensions we experience while living the Christian life. God is responsible for our salvation, and yet St. Paul tells the Philippians, work out your own salvation. In fear and trembling. So James, the brother of our Lord, says: without your works, your faith is meaningless And yet God says through the prophet Isaiah, your works are as filthy rags. So which is it? Well it's both. It is both. Anglicans define a sacrament as an outward sign of an inward work of grace. Hence we believe that when we are doing something outwardly like pouring water on a child God is doing something inwardly, spiritually, in the heart and soul of the person being baptized. And when God does something like give new spiritual life to a person, whether a child or an adult The spiritual world consists of angelic celebration and demonic gnashing of teeth. From now until Jacobson is in his own grave, a spiritual battle will be going on for his soul. In an addendum to the screw tape letters, C. S. Lewis added a toast given by the demon screw tape. to a group of graduating demons who finished their training on how to tempt humans to sin and and disbelief The toast is given at a banquet, and the main course the devils are feasting upon are human souls. Such is a poignant description of how devils look upon our children, their souls, to tear into and to devour. If we would more readily see the souls of our children in such a light, I venture to say that our motivation to raise them in the Christian faith with a great deal of intention Would always be before us. Examine yourselves, dear parents, on how well you make sure your children are in the right type of car seat How well you monitor their allergies, how well you keep them away from other children who are sick, how well you put nets around their trampoline and railings on their beds Compare all of that care you take for your children's physical well-being and compare it to what you do for their spiritual well-being. It is a terrible irony. God must view when he witnesses how much care we put into preserving the physical lives of our children When maybe if they're blessed, they would reach the age of 90 years and then become dust. Yet their soul will live on forever. What part of us needs more care? That which is here and gone, or that which is forever? It is too obvious a question to answer, and yet how poorly we care for the spirituality of our children, for it shows that we don't answer the question correctly. From the beginning point of God calling Israel out of Egypt to be his own special people, he instructed them to be careful and instructed their children. How children are instructed is the foundation of a strong family and a strong church. Remember from Deuteronomy chapter 6, where God tells the Israelites that they are to keep his law. And then he makes it clear. He expects them by keeping his law, that it be passed down from generation to generation. He said, that you may fear the Lord your God, to keep all his statutes and commandments, which I command you and your son. and your grandson. And then after the people are instructed to love God with all their heart, soul, and strength, God says in his law, quote, and these words which I command you today shall be in your heart. You shall teach them diligently to your children, and shall talk of them when you sit in your house, when you walk by the way, when you lie down, and when you rise up. Parents, do an inventory for me. How much of the conversation in your household pertains to God and how much the things of the world Do a ratio. One to one? Oh, that would be wonderful. What about one to ten? Ten being things of the world and one being the things of God. Your honest ratio will convict you on how much more you need to speak to your children about the things of God The word translated diligently as in diligently teach your children includes meditation, repetition, and memorization. Meditation includes how we are to understand what God means by a particular commandment. Repetition refers to the mechanism of how we are to hear the word over and over so that we do not forget it. Memorization describes us not only knowing it in our heads, but in our hearts. And the postures described, such as sitting, walking, and lying, they communicate that the training in God's word is to be received in all parts of life. A child raised as a Christian is not only to know the Ten Commandments, but know how to apply each to his everyday life circumstance. God commands to have no other gods before him. That's easily applied. We're not to be worshiping something like the Muslim God But an even closer study shows that we must not worship sports, sports teams, recreation God's commandment not to steal. That's easily understood. I'm not to take that which doesn't belong to me. But with a more educated look, we can see that to borrow something from someone and not to care for it, causing it to lose its value, well that too is stealing. God forbidding adultery is clearly obeyed by not sleeping with another person besides your spouse But a more trained mind and heart knows it applies to not walking into a red light district or scrolling through inappropriate websites. Beloved, what I am describing is intentional parenting. It is being sure that you do your part in training your children as God has instructed. The book of Proverbs is a training letter from a father to his son. So when it says that the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom, A child is to understand that to be in awe of God first will make all other knowledge meaningful, eternally meaningful. And the instruction is based on the principle found in Deuteronomy chapter 6, as it is diligently teaching your children. When parents are told in Proverbs that whoever does not use a rod to discipline his child is actually hating his child. And whoever disciplines his child is showing true love. The teaching is based on Deuteronomy chapter 6. It is recognizing that a child left to himself or herself will be deprived of learning self-discipline. A child that has not been trained to be able to practice self-discipline, which includes self-control, is a child abused because he or she is being deprived. Bobby Lynn and I did not enjoy spanking our children, but we did it because we believed God's word over the wisdom and emotions of the world. We did it because we wanted our children to be able to say no to their impulses and desires when they were not appropriate. We did it because we wanted our children, and this is so very, very important, we wanted our children to be able to endure When God was chastening them. For when God chastens our children, and they are not used to enduring the chastening. The devil tempts them to be bitter toward God, and such bitterness leads to unbelief, and the devil enjoys feasting on the souls of the people brought up in Christian homes. They are the tastiest of souls for them. When in Proverbs we are warned against passing by the house of a harlot, it is hearkening back to Deuteronomy chapter 6 When Proverbs tells us to be sure to have trustworthy friends and wise counselors and God-fearing spouses, it is hearkening back to Deuteronomy 6. But let us go to the New Testament if I have not yet convinced you about intentional parenting. When Jesus saw his disciples resisting parents who were bringing their children to Jesus to be blessed, and Jesus said, suffer The little children and forbid them not to come to me, for such is the kingdom of heaven. He was referring back to Deuteronomy chapter 6. When St. Paul instructs the children in Colossians to obey their parents in all things, with the expectation there that parents were obeying Deuteronomy chapter 6, diligently teaching their children. When he tells fathers in the Ephesian church to not provoke children to anger by being too hard or overbearing, but instead for the fathers to bring up their children in the discipline and instruction of the Lord, he is repeating Deuteronomy chapter 6. Intentional parenting is also called covenantal parenting. Covenantal parenting recognizes that God relates to us in a covenant manner. A covenant manner means that our relationship with God is based on agreed promises and behaviors. We are the ones who promise certain behaviors, such as believing on the Lord Jesus Christ, and God is the one who keeps his promises when we do. And so we commit to obeying his commandments and believing in his son, and he promises to never leave us or forsake us, but to ensure our salvation. As I have underlined and highlighted for us, a prominent command he places upon his people is for us to teach his promised commandments to our children. In a resolute manner, they are to be taught, to help them apply God's word in all contexts of life And when we add that principle to the words quoted by St. Peter at Pentecost, that the covenant God makes with his people is for you, he said. and for your children and for those who are afar off, which is generations to come. It can be seen from this that God does not just want us to teach his word to our children. but for our children to teach it to their children and so on and so forth until he comes again. And while we have focused on the positive we are to teach our children, We must also be warned about the negatives, for the devil would love to teach our children. When Jesus said to his disciples that he was sending them into the midst of snakes and vipers, He was using the metaphor to describe false teachers. Remember in the garden, the devil took the form of a serpent and he twisted God's words. He does exactly the same today. And he changes the phrase just slightly, but it's basically the same. He questions, did God really say? And so parents, if you surround yourself with teach your child, with teachers who say Moses didn't really part the Red Sea, or Jesus could not have possibly walked on water Or you don't really believe in the resurrection, do you? All such phrases and questions are seeds of doubt. So that the demons can get the ultimate prize, which is to feed on the souls of our children. And if I'm scaring you, I'm trying to. So what did you see today? Like when Elisha the prophet was surrounded by an enemy who had brought an army to capture him and likely kill him, and his servant quaked with fear. Elisha prayed that his servant would have eyes to see the spiritual world that Elisha could see. And they could then see the army of angels that were protecting them. Well, in a similar manner, I am preaching so that each of us could see a spiritual world that should frighten us enough to be intentional about the souls of our children. And when we are intentional, God will meet our children. God will preserve their souls. Beloved, act as if it is all up to you. And pray and believe it is all up to God. Let us pray. Our Father, for such truths, we bring them before your people, and for all of us Parents, grandparents, great-grandparents to embrace these truths. Help us all to be intentional for the sake of one another's children, let alone our own That we might be a covenant people who raise covenant children to your glory until you come again. In Jesus' name we pray. Amen.

sermons.title: Judged Clergy
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. You would turn in your Bibles to 1 Corinthians chapter 4. We are covering this portion that was read, verses 1 through 5. It was received in the mail. It was a package of olive oil accompanied with a letter. Which read, use this holy Bible anointed oil. James 5, 14 says, to turn God's healing and prosperity on in your life. Are you sick in your body? Use this holy Bible anointed oil. Are you sick financially? Use this holy Bible anointed oil. Open this holy Bible anointed oil. Do not waste a drop. Jesus is represented by this faith oil. Make a cross on your forehead with it. And then by faith go into your room by yourself and take the money out of your wallet and make a cross on each bill so that God will heal your money problems. Take your checkbook, anoint it with this holy Bible anointed oil. Then write the largest check you can and anoint it with this holy Bible anointed oil and send it to me. I need your support This is important to you. When you anoint your money with this holy Bible anointed oil, make a cross on each bill and send it to me, and God will bless you. Don't waste a drop signed a man of God for 50 years. And you probably didn't receive such a letter in the mail. But many Christians have, and many Christians have done exactly what this man of God for 50 years suggests to be done. Stories of ministers abusing their office do not normally come in the mail, but today they do seem to be a part of our regular news cycle. It seemed for a while that we would hear story after story of Roman Catholics' records being uncovered of claims of abuse by Roman Catholic priests. But it just doesn't happen in the Roman Catholic Church. In February of this year, the Houston Chronicle uncovered 20 years of sex. abuse and cover-up within Southern Baptist churches with over seven hundred credible victims. That is a travesty. It is an affront to the bride of Christ. With so-called Protestant ministers taking advantage of gullible Christians financially and sexually And Roman Catholic priests acting out their perversions on children, this hardly seems a time to preach about a proper perspective from God's people towards ministers of the gospel. But on second thought, it may be the perfect time. Within the institutions like the Roman Catholic Church, priests were more likely held in too high esteem than making them seem as if they were incapable of doing harm. On the other hand, some Protestant ministers are not regarded highly enough as their words are treated as if they're just like anyone else's. In the independent traditions, the esteem for a minister is based mostly on his charisma. The people are motivated by the personality of the man rather than the truth of his words or because of the office that he holds. From the words of the Apostle Paul in 1 Corinthians chapter 4 It is there that we receive a redemptive view of a minister. This view moves us away from judging that which we cannot judge and preparing ourselves for the day that we will be judged. And 1 Corinthians chapter 4. St. Paul continues his thesis that disunity caused by Christians choosing one minister over another is nonsensical. It is nonsensical in that a minister is merely a man. This is what we talked about last two weeks ago from chapter 3. And Paul uses that phrase, a mere man. The description of a minister being a mere man is more fully developed here in chapter four. As a mere man Is described as a servant of Christ and a steward of the mysteries of God. A servant, by definition, does the bidding of a master. In this case, a master, a be master, is Christ. The distinction of Christ being a minister's master is vital to the survival of a minister. A minister of the gospel must serve Christ. For if he becomes a servant of another man or of a congregation, he begins to do the bidding of the other man or the congregation. Whether it be a man or a congregation, he is to do the bidding for Christ. I'll take this example Let's say a minister wishes to teach and preach on eternal judgment, believing that God wishes to enkindle within his parish a greater fear of eternal damnation and a greater hope for heaven As this teaching progresses in sermons and Bible studies, a number of parishioners become irritated as the weight of God's word begins to crush their complacency. They in turn complained to one another, complained to the parish council, complained to the vestry, for someone to get the minister to redirect his teaching. If the minister complies, due to the complaints of the people, he is not doing the ministry that Christ has called him to do, as he understands it. And if he does the bidding of Christ, he will be rejected by the will of the people. He must trust then that the bidding of Christ is what is best for the people, whether it be their bidding or not. Well such a scenario is why the polity of a church matters A congregational church where the congregation has the authority to hire and fire a minister at will Is only asking for trouble to be brought upon itself, for the bidding of the people may prevent them from hearing the word that God wants them to hear. Under an episcopal form of government, a minister's position as pastor is determined by bishops, not the laity.
