In our text this morning, these three appeared to lead the apostle to discuss an overriding principle. That principle is summarized in the first sentence of verse 12, which states that all things are lawful, but all things are not helpful. The first part of the statement acknowledges what we call Christian liberty. Christian liberty is the freedom that every Christian has to enjoy life. Under the covenant of Christ, we are not bound by the law which restricts what we can eat or drink. We are not restricted as to which Days we can walk a certain distance. We are not required to offer sacrifice when we fall short of God's glory. Our salvation is not based on what we have to do or what we cannot do. This does not mean the law of God is irrelevant. It simply means that we are bound by a greater law, which says to love our God with all of our heart, soul, mind, and strength in our neighbor as ourselves. It is in such love that grants us freedom in Christ, making all things lawful The second part of the statement balances out just how far Christian liberty goes. Yes, all things are lawful, but not all things are helpful or beneficial. I may have the freedom to do this or that, but doing this or that may not be beneficial to me. The second part of the verse explains this further All things are lawful for the apostle, but he will not be brought under the power of anything Here is a mature Christian response to liberty. It is a realization that while I may be free to do things I once could not do, I find myself bound up by that freedom. Allow me a personal testimony. Many of you know that I spent some time in the denomination The Church of the Nazarene. It is a denomination that has identified itself by what it restricts of its members. The bylaws require that members do not smoke, do not drink alcohol, no dancing of any kind. And no attendance to the movie theater. Bobby Lynn and I were faithful to these restrictions, while our members were not. And not that we agreed with them. In fact, we did not. But we believed that we had given vows to the church, and therefore they were binding to us while we were under those vows. Why we had become part of that denomination, that's for another sermon. Unfortunately, we were one of the few, as I said, in the parish that abided by these restrictions And I'm not ashamed to tell you that when I became a Reformed Episcopalian, I immediately bought a bottle of wine. I went out and bought my first pipe, smoked tobacco, and we went to a movie. Upon doing so, I was reminded of this passage Which warns of such behavior, although permissible, can become addictive. Alcohol has robbed many a man's soul. Tobacco has taken many a man's lungs. It is all too common that the pretense of moral freedom ends in moral bondage. We think we're free as it wraps itself around us. As the poet observes, the waves of the sea are thought to be free But the ocean itself, as it rages and swells, in the bound, in the bond of a boundless obedience dwells. We learn from the apostle this short proverb: Christian liberty must not exceed Christian propriety or wisdom. Verse 12 is a set-up passage. It is an ethical principle that sets us up for the issue of sexual immorality that the apostle wishes to address again. But to see the issue only as sexual immorality is not to properly interpret St. Paul's teaching here. Sexual immorality is an easy example to show how one can think he is free to express his fleshly desires. And while he expresses his freedom, he becomes bound by the same. It could be sexual passion. Drugs, alcohol, the love of money, the pursuit of fame, earthly possessions, etc. , etc. Obviously, sexuality was an important issue to address with the Corinthians, for as I described, you remember a few sermons back. The temple of Aphrodite looms over that ancient city as a constant reminder of those who are pulled by sexual desires. And considering our present culture, it is in a subject still important to address A pulpit that does not address the sins of the day is occupied by a man who is unfaithful to his calling. Sexual immorality is a sin that all of us have fallen into or been affected by. If we are going to do battle with the sins of our day, this is one we must face head-on with our armor strapped tight. But we also must see it as an example of any sin that can make us a slave. In verse 13 The food for the stomach is compared to the body for sexual immorality. And we must do some reading between the lines to understand why these two issues are compared. Later in the epistle, the apostle is going to talk about eating meat offered to idols. And here it makes a brief reference to food. Apparently, some Corinthians have used this. Issue as a logical argument for their participation in sexual immorality. The logic seems to have been that if we are free to eat what we want as Christians then we are free to indulge in sexual pleasures as we want. Isn't it the same? Well excuse the pun, but the apostle finds this argument hard to digest The comparison between the stomach and food versus our bodies for sexual immorality cannot be made. The stomach is solely for digesting food, and food is for being digested in the stomach. Each of these is not only made for one another, but share the same fate of being destroyed in the end. In comparison, our bodies were created for the purpose of sexual morality. Not sexual immorality. Our bodies were created for the Lord Himself. The apostle says elsewhere, I am not my own. And none of us are, who are in Christ. We are not our own, whether it is our soul or our body. As our bodies are the Lord here, so They will be for eternity, as verse 14 promises. Our bodies will be raised in the last day. What they will look like is again something the apostle addresses later. Here he confirms the accuracy of our confession when we say we believe in the resurrection of the body. If the fact that our bodies will be resurrected is not enough to keep us from sexual immorality The greater base of the argument is laid with the explanation that we are united with Christ. To be a member with Christ is to be one with Christ. It is very similar to the language used to talk about when a couple comes and is united or married, the two becoming one flesh. Remember, in the book of Ephesians, the apostle describes our unity with Christ as a great mystery. It cannot fully be understood, but it is most certainly real. The word member, member here literally means a limb or a body part. And Jesus describes his people as the body parts, and he is the head. He elsewhere describes us as branches being grafted into the vine. Thus, we are physically a part of Christ, who is our vine, who is our head, who is our substance for life. The repercussions for not understanding and appreciating our unity with Christ can be blasphemy. The crass analogy of the apostle that the apostle brings in here takes this to another level. To join our bodies with a harlot for the purpose of sexual immorality is to join the body of Christ to participate in the same. Thus, what Christ refused to do on earth, which was to sin, we caused him to do as members of his body when we participate in sexual immorality. And this, my dear friends, is a bucket of cold water. Sin always, always has a greater consequence beyond our person. In the case of sexual immorality, the greater consequence is that we bring in Christ Himself. We involve Him. How this is, we cannot fully know, but the apostle wants us to be appalled at that possibility. It would be understandable after such a statement to question how this how this could be. After all, Christ is a separate person, he was fully man, he is fully man, he has his own body. Our sin certainly does not make him a sinner, does it? Well, verses 16 and 17 should help us understand how the apostle addresses these questions. According to verse 16, when one is joined with another sexually, there is something beyond the physical that is occurring. This is described in the same manner of union between a man and a woman in marriage. The language used by the apostle comes from Genesis Since the time of Adam and Eve, all unions in marriage are described as two becoming one. The union again is described in the Epistle of Ephesians as a mystery. It is spiritual, thus it cannot be seen. It is mysterious, and therefore it cannot be fully understood. Nevertheless, it is real. And this our young adults must understand. There's no delineation such as casual sex in Holy Scripture. As Christians, all sexuality with our bodies is of a spiritual nature. The mystery of the spiritual presence of Christ, along with our spirit joining with another is a powerful truth that cannot be hidden or couched in language such as casual or premarital. Something more is going on besides simply physical contact. Many of you have heard sermons in the past who perhaps remember from your philosophy that that heresy of Gnosticism. And I remind you, it's a belief that It is the spirit that matters and the flesh doesn't really matter as a concern at all. Well the fallout from a belief like that is the separation of the body from the spirit, treating them separately. Some Gnostics believe that one could do imaginable or unimaginable things to the body, and the spirit would not be affected. But as you can see, we have not rejected that belief in our culture For many behave as if the pleasures they pursue with their body does not have a lasting consequence on the soul. As God's creation, our bodies and spirits were to be forever united. God did not create us to separate our spirit from our bodies. But when sin entered the world, it brought forth judgment of death. Death for a man is separation from spirit and body. This is unnatural. And it is why it is promised that in the last day we will be resurrected and behold once again with new bodies. Because of the unity of our bodies have with our spirit, and because as Christians our spirit is united to Christ Whenever we join our bodies to, whatever we join our bodies to is what we bring to in Christ. We include Him. And so we say, the apostle cries, get out of there Once you have understood what is happening when you join your body to another outside of the marriage covenant, flee from that sin There cannot be a milling around, a debating of the many factors involved. Get out of that bed, get out of that relationship, run like Joseph from Potiphar's wife. There is nothing else to do but to run. Now the final three verses of this chapter solidify why we should flee. And brings in the principle of proprietorship. Proprietorship is different than propriety, as propriety refers to what is proper or upstanding behavior. Proprietorship refers to ownership. A proprietor of a building is the owner of a building, and the proprietor of our body, our body, is God. In verse 18, we are told that the sin of sexual immorality is different than other sins in that it is against our own bodies. Other sins, such as the abuse of drugs and gluttony, and so forth, appear to be the same on the surface However, because sexual immorality contains the mysterious element which makes two persons become one and thus brings the Spirit of Christ into it. It is a different sin in a mysterious way. When we sin against our own bodies in this manner, we sin against the owner of our body, who is God. What is not a mystery is how the principle God as proprietor of our bodies does apply to our temptations of the flesh. Towards gluttony, emaciation, drunken stupors, drug-induced altered consciousness One merely needs to read the local news to see how often our neighbors are being killed because of dangerous drugs that enslave a person to take their own life, finding the high. More valuable than their life. Verse 19 explains, how the gospel of Jesus Christ is to change our understanding of what our bodies are to include. And who owns our bodies? Our bodies are temples of the Holy Spirit. The Holy Spirit is within all who are Christian. And here he gives us the image of the temple, giving two insights. First, like Solomon's temple, our bodies are houses of the presence of God. Second, like Solomon's temple, we are owned by God. This is his house. He is the proprietor. How the body is used and what the body is used for is to be dictated by the owner. Of course it should be. Thus we acknowledge that we are not our own. We have been bought with a price. To be bought with a price is to be delivered by purchase. The deliverance of men from the power and condemnation of sin was by ransom. We were justly held in bondage due to our sin. The blood of Christ is our ransom. It meets the demands of justice. Because of this, we are to use our bodies to glorify God. To use them for another purpose is to blaspheme the one who owns us. Glorifying God with our bodies is not complicated. It is using our bodies in the manner that God intended. Sexual intimacy saved in practice only within the marriage covenant that brings glory to God. Now it may seem fair. It may seem fair to ask, is St. Paul obsessed with sexuality? Here we are in chapter 6. It's been addressed three times. Well, instead of examining him, let's examine our culture. From the National Center of Sexual Exploitation, May 2019. Sixty-four percent of young adults ages 13 to 24 actively seek out pornography weekly or more often. Thirty-five percent of all internet downloads are porn related. Thirty-five percent From the Statistica Research Department, January 2018, the average number of sexual partners for United States citizens of a lifetime is just under 11. Eleven. The percent of Americans who have had one night stands is fifty-eight percent. Seventy percent of Americans believe fornication is acceptable moral behavior. St. Paul obsessed with sexual immorality? Hardly. Now if you can stand apart from these statistics, having limited sexual partners, not having a one-night stand, not believing fornication is acceptable behavior. And if there are a good number of people like yourself that can stand apart from these numbers, it means that the average number of sexual partners and one night stands and the accepting of fornication is actually much higher amidst the rest of our fellow Americans. This is the world in which we live Sexual immorality is the accepted moral standard of our day. If Christians are to be victorious over the sexual immorality of today, We must cry out to young and old alike to flee from sexual immorality and we must teach the reason why. For the Christian, Christ is within you. You are not your own. Your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit. Use your body to bring glory to God. And our victory over sins of the body goes beyond our sexuality to anything that would enslave us if it could. Christ Jesus came to set us free. Free from the guilt of original sin. Free from guilt of personal sin. Free from guilty consciences. And free from being enslaved by compulsiveness of desires of the flesh. Again, from St. Paul. All things are lawful, but I will not be brought under the power of any. Our God, we all confess and recognize that as much as this topic is brought up It is so easily convicting for all of us as have been confessed, have committed such sin, or have been affected by such sin. Father, help us to embrace the higher standard. Help us, as the call act has said today, to understand your scriptures are there, all of them, for our learning. May we learn today of these warnings and abide by them. In Jesus' name we pray. Amen.

sermons.title: Surrender, a Marriage Example
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. We are looking at First Corinthians chapter seven. Encourage you to turn there in your Bibles. I wish to begin this sermon with a prelude of sorts. I have come across these one-liners or quips about marriage that I wish to share. Jack Benny said, My wife Mary and I have been married for 47 years, and never once have we gotten into an argument enough, serious enough, to consider divorce. Murder, yes, but divorce never. Henny Youngman, I wonder how many know that name. And the young man said, My wife dresses the kill. She cooks the same way The originator of this next quote is unknown, but it's still true. A good marriage is one where each partner secretly suspects that they got the better deal. This is from philosopher Michel de Montaigne. He said a good marriage would be between a blind wife and a deaf husband. And he wasn't trying to be funny. This uh this one is another again from an author unknown, but it fits the context of our passage quite well It's don't make love by the garden gate. Love is blind, but the neighbors ain't. And finally this one from Rodney Dangerfield, gotta imagine him My wife was afraid of the dark. Then she saw me naked and now she's afraid of the light. Now, these quips are humorous to most of us because they have a little bit of truth mixed in with some exaggeration. We laugh because we really do not agree with the full content of what is said, but sometimes we do feel what it is implying. If these one-liners were actually feelings of a man or a woman toward his or her spouse, then we would not be laughing. There would be deeper problems to address There is not a marriage today that does not have serious problems that have either been worked through or are being worked through. I say this so that none of us who might have had a marital problem or are going through a marital problem don't feel like outcasts. It is always comforting to know when you are not the only one. If I were the only sinner that needed redemption, that would be very lonely and quite embarrassing. But because I am one of many, I recognize my sin is both personal and something bigger than myself. When a couple understands that their difficulties and strife are similar to other couples, they are less embarrassed and more likely to seek help and to do better. It has been my experience, both in counseling couples and in my own marriage, that the issue of physical intimacy within marriage is a major cause of conflict. between a husband and a wife. The top four, you can probably list them as I do. Communication, finances, our kids, and sexual intimacy. I will admit that the issue we are going to discuss this morning is one that would seem more appropriate to highlight in a marriage seminar. You may notice as you look around, this is not a marriage seminar. There are children present. There are adults here who are not married. Even though this is the case, I believe this issue is most appropriate for us for two reasons, primarily. First, I'm preaching through the book of 1 Corinthians, and this is the next passage. You don't avoid the next passage. Second, strong marriages are vital to the health of Christ's church and the health of our children. This church cares about your marriage, and I submit to you that we are the only ones outside of your immediate family that truly does care about your marriage. The world would love to see Christian marriages fail, for it helps them to feel better about their own failures. When we hear statistics that say that the divorce rate amongst Christians is as high as the secular world, that should be a point of embarrassment to us. Something must be done. Something must be done to address the topic, and so it must be preached. And my final point of introduction before we get to the text, for those who are not married, Paul addresses your position in life as well. But the words spoken to those who are married must be listened to, not only to those who are married, but to the young who will be married, and to those who might be able to help others who are having trouble in their marriages. And so this again is appropriate. And finally, finally, this is a good Advent topic It is a good Advent topic because it helps sanctify us. And anything that helps sanctify us prepares us for the coming of Christ. And so let us look at the first part of 1 Corinthians chapter 7. After addressing, you remember the issue of sexual immorality, which we've heard already. And the calling of the Corinthians to glorify God with their bodies, the apostle moves his comments toward a response to a question written to him by members of the church. We summarize from the information of Paul writing a previous letter. Remember this is likely the second letter to the Corinthians. That he's responding to them a letter written back to him that there was a continuous correspondence between the church and the apostles. His flow from discussing sexual immorality to discussing marital fidelity is a natural one. For as we discussed last week, the simple way to glorify God with our bodies is to participate in sexual intimacy only within the context of marital vows. So verse one begins the transition with the apostle referring to a letter he had received that asked a question. or possible questions about relationships between men and women. Paul does not repeat the question, but we get the gist of the inquiry from the answer that he gives. Paul's initial straightforward answer is that it is good for a man not to touch a woman. This is a way of saying that it is good for a man not to have sexual relations with a woman. Interestingly, the translator of the NIV, if you have that version, translates it, it is good for a man not to marry. Which is not what Paul is saying, but he will talk about later on. You see, if Paul is saying it's good for a Christian not to marry, That seems uh at odds at first, as he appears to be restricting something that he actually condones later on. In his first epistle to Timothy, the apostle warned of a great day of apostasy when men and women would be forbidden to be married. In his epistle to the Ephesians, the apostle upholds marriage as a type of relationship with Christ and his church. Also, the apostle is well aware of God saying in Genesis that it is not good for man to be alone. So, with all of this in the background, we can conclude that the apostle is forbidding or even discouraging marriage altogether. He is not It is safest to interpret that the apostle is considering the Corinthian church's peculiar situation. Here is a group of Christians living in a hostile environment, hostile to the morality of biblical moral law. Persecution and even death. Even death became a natural part of living for Christ in Roman-occupied territory What Paul says here and later about the benefits of not being married can be described as wise counsel, considering the dangerous day in which they lived. If a man or a woman did not know how much longer he had to live, it was best to devote oneself to prayer and to witnessing. Rather than starting a family, only to have to abandon that family by death later. This advice is quickly changed. When the apostle considers another circumstance, it is the circumstance of sexuality, immorality that surrounds them, which we've talked about at length We have previously described this, but I need to portray it in a little bit different way. Cities like Corinth were free to express their sexuality in religious ceremonies. Free sexual expression, both heterosexual and homosexual, could be seen in local temples by passers-by. It would not be unusual for young and old to be exposed to public nudity and public intimacy. Now this may be appalling to us, who know no such behavior in our community, right? And yet I remember well our family making trips down to Myrtle Beach 15 years or so ago and seeing some similar immorality shots on several corners. I could not help but wonder why such a vacation spot needed so many peep shows. The only answer could be that there were plenty of peepers to keep those shows in business. Because there is so much immorality surrounding these people of God in Corinth, it is then appropriate, and in some cases necessary. that each man has his own wife and each woman her own husband. But of course it is simply not enough to have a wife or a husband to protect oneself from sexual immorality. The wife and husband must be available to each other, Paul says. And here is where too many Christian couples get into trouble. The apostles' words could not only be straightforward, and yet they are too easily ignored. Both husbands and wives are instructed to fulfill their marital duty And what is that duty? Verse 4 and 5 make it clear. The husband's body is not his own, and the wife's body is not her own. The New King James, which we read from, describes it in the sense of authority. The woman does not have authority over her own body, but the man does, the husband The man does not have authority over his own body, but the woman does, the wife. Because this is so, and it is. The command is given in verse 5 not to deprive one another. It is unfortunately inevitable that when this passage is studied, Especially by a couple who is having some marital strife, the husband is all for what it says, and the wife cannot believe what she is reading. This passage, of course, does not give license for abuse. One is not given license to hold this passage over another for claiming the freedom to mistreat a spouse's body. What this does speak to is the necessary principle in marriage and in Christian life. And that principle is surrender. Surrender. If marriage is a type of how Christ is related to his church, we can learn how to be better husbands and wives by watching what Christ does for his church The church's body is Christ's body. He has authority over us. With that authority, he does what is best for us and for him. His acts of love will naturally preserve his body, naturally. At times he requires of his body, his church, what is difficult, but never impossible. Other times he showers his body with gifts and luxuries. Always, always he is acting for the best interest of his body. The same should be occurring within a marriage relationship Each person should be acting for the best interest of the other. Each person should understand the strengths and weaknesses of the other. I often use the following analogy for younger couples. This analogy was given to me. I think it describes well the difference between men and women in intimacy. A man responds as a microwave, whereas a woman responds like a crockpot. With the microwave, a few buttons are pushed and it's cooking. A crock pot, however, takes its time getting warmed up. One must be patient with the crock pot, and one must appreciate the speed of a microwave. The microwave cannot expect the crockpot to be as fast as he is. To carry the analogy further, it is best for the microwave to be placed on thaw for a time. There is a concession that the apostle makes for when a husband and wife should not be intimate. That concession is when such separation is agreed upon by both parties. The reason for this separation is for a time devoted to prayer. Such prayer disciplines, the spiritual as well as the physical. It is important to note that what is agreed upon is separation, not the coming together. Separation is agreed upon, the coming together should always be. Too often a wife may believe That the coming together must be agreed upon, and sometimes she wishes she could be disagreeable. I used to watch, and I'm sure many of you did, the television show Everybody Loves Raymond. um quite a bit ago now. It was intelligent comedy at times, an exaggerated marital comedy, enjoyable. But what I became perturbed with in that show was how the wife would use her sexuality to punish her husband. If she was not happy with him, she withheld herself from him. This withholding led to his grobling, and that was portrayed as funny. As we read the apostles' words here, her behavior was not funny, it was sinful, and his was just pathetic. Now I recognize that in saying this, that the difference between men and women appears to place all of the pressure upon the woman. The reason for the microwave and crockpot analogy was to take that pressure off. It is the husband who is commanded to love his wife as Christ loved the church. We must interpret chapter 7 of 1 Corinthians, including all other passages that teach about marriage in the Bible. This is not to be interpreted in a vacuum, as they say. It must include Paul's instruction of how a husband is to treat his wife. The husband must be patient, long-suffering, and gracious to the needs of his spouse. Such is biblical love toward her. The wife, for her part, must never refuse the advances of her husband. If each is obedient unto the Lord, If each long-suffering, patient, gracious, never refusing, if each is obedient unto the Lord, neither spouse will be in want. In verse 6, the apostle backs away a bit, not intending to sound as if every man or woman should be married. In fact, he goes back to his original point, which is to say that it would be better not to touch, not to be married. The reason for this position we have briefly discussed, It was their circumstance, the circumstance of the day. It was the danger of death. But it was also something else. You see, Paul believed in the imminent return of Christ And so if Jesus is coming back soon, stop worrying about marital issues and focus on his return. Later in this letter, in fact the same chapter, the apostle will explain all of this further. What he articulates as a fact many Christians do not accept. What he accepts is that many cannot exercise the self-control to remain unmarried. In fact, the apostle even calls it a gift to be able to remain unmarried. He accepts the fact that we are all fallen creatures. We at times burn with desires that we seemingly cannot control. A way to protect ourselves from such burnings without sin is to be married. It is within the marriage covenant that a man or woman can burn with passion without the threat of burning for eternity. We like to believe that as Christians we are able to withstand the temptations such as lust of the flesh. As ideal and righteous as such resistance is, it is not likely. And to this the apostle consents. And not only does he consent that some temptations of the flesh can be difficult, so does our Heavenly Father. You remember the story of King David and his adulterous affair with Bathsheba? That when the Lord confronts David about his sin, he confronts him through the words of the prophet Nathan. Nathan says this, catch what's what's implied here. This is God speaking to David. I gave you your master's house, that is Saul's house, and your master's wives, plural, into your keeping. And if that had not, if that had been too little, I also would have given you much more. Much more of what? Wives. Women. The Lord would have given more because he knows the weakness of men, especially of kings. This is what our Savior says. You remember to the Pharisees when he explains why the law of Moses allows for simple divorce. It was due, he said, to the hardness of the hearts of the people. God made concession because of the hardness of their heart. God knows the passions that burn within. He does not condemn us for these, but requires us to express them within the context of marriage. In doing so, we actually live out the gospel. The gospel, the good news of Christ redeeming us out of our sin. He gives of himself for us. In the context of marriage, our controlled passions can be expressed in a righteous fashion by being selfless and giving of ourselves to our spouse. In doing so, we sanctify our spouse. In doing so, we witness the gospel to a selfish world. And in doing so, we glorify God. Well, this last point of glorifying God, I must emphasize to close. The Christian life is understanding our individual lives to be about things much larger than ourselves Our sexual lives are not about ourselves, but about our spouse and things greater. Our marital relationship is not about the two of us, but about our testimony of Christ and his church. Our testimony of Christ and his church is part of our commission by Jesus to go into all the world and preach the gospel. And our testimony of Christ and His church fulfills our overall purpose for existing, which is to bring glory to God. You see, a limited mind of faith sees Paul's instructions about principles of marital intimacy here in 1 Corinthians 7. And concludes that it's about men getting from their wives intimate passion whenever they want to. Hardly. It is living out the gospel. It is dying to self, both male and female. It is a practical example of the Christian life Being summarized as being as the Apostle Paul said, it is no longer I that live, but Christ that lives in me, and the life I now have. I live for him. Let us pray. Our gracious and heavenly Father For the importance of this topic, we we make notice beyond our own sexual desires and to the fact that we are to die to ourselves, that we are to be witnesses of the gospel in our marriages. And that we are to truly glorify you in all that we do. May each of us take into account our own life and how we can better do so. You pray this in Jesus' name, Amen

sermons.title: An Instrument Used by God
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. Turn in your Bibles to First Corinthians chapter seven. We are working from verse ten to verse twenty-four. And those who have been regular with us last four weeks, you should know I'm not preaching on sex this morning. Now a necessary point to address in these verses is how the apostle differentiates between what the Lord says and what he, Paul, says Let us understand that to differentiate in this manner does not alter the authority of each of the statements. Paul is referring to what Christ has addressed first, such as we find in Matthew chapter 19, and then he, and then what he has not said. When Paul says, I not the Lord, he is not simply submitting his opinion, but is identifying something that has not yet been addressed. Let us be confident that all that is said is to be understood as inspired by the Holy Spirit It is the liberal mind and heart that wishes for Paul to be saying that what he is now writing is not authoritative. And so now we can look at other writings and say, well, they're not authoritative either. Once you do that, you are now picking and choosing what is authoritative. Thus, such a person is creating his own Bible, and that quasi-bible is very much like the mind of the person picking and choosing what is authoritative. A Christian must never do that. So verses ten through eleven These refer to the words, our Lord Christ, who forbids the type of divorce that was allowed by Mosaic law. He raises the standard, no longer allowing a man to submit a certificate simply because he is unhappy. Essentially, divorce is not allowed, but except for violation of the covenant vow. As the prophet has said, God hates divorce. If one goes against such directive, he or she must remain unmarried, for that is the path that he or she has chosen. You know, and I know that there are many examples that people will come up with to say that such a divorce principle, it doesn't apply to their situation. If we go there, we dismiss what Jesus has taught. And again, a Christian must never do that. Verse 12 through 14 give us the indication of why this is an issue amongst these Corinthians. People converting from pagan religions to Christianity went through dramatic change. If one spouse converted and the other did not, A great conflict was possible. We should imagine a husband saying to his newly converted wife, What do you mean you're not no longer coming to the perverted party tonight? All the neighbors are expecting us there. Jesus warned that the gospel would elevate conflict within households. It is understandable that Christians wondered if they should leave these volatile relationships or stay and model Christ. The apostle explains, however, that if the unbelieving spouse is willing to stay in the relationship, then the converted spouse must stay as well. The benefit, he says, of the Christian presence in the home is sanctification. Sanctification means being made holy. A believing spouse can help make holy an unbelieving spouse simply by living amongst the unbelieving spouse. This does not mean, as some can be confused, that by a Christian's mere presence in the home that their spouse will be saved from eternal fire. What it does mean is that the unbelieving spouse becomes an instrument of our Heavenly Father used in his hand for the sake of the believing spouse and for the sake of the children. Vessels, instruments used for worship and sacrifices themselves used in the temple were called holy Holy, not that there was an inward change, but there was a use now set apart for that instrument. Sanctified. Holy. This is how an unbelieving spouse is made holy, separated for God's use. Referring to the children as clean rather than unclean is that similar language that the Jews would use in referring to those of Jewish heritage, they were clean, and those of Gentile heritage. Unclean. A clean child is clean because he or she is a covenant child born into the covenant of Jesus Christ. According to the apostle, it takes one believing parent to make a child clean. This is why the church historic has practiced infant baptism of families with only one believing parent. At verse fifteen, he tells us that when circumstances change, so does permission. To leave has been understood by the church to be a spouse abandoning the relationship for whatever reason If a believer is abandoned by an unbeliever, the believer, he tells us, the spouse that is left behind, is not bound anymore in the relationship, but is free. This also applies to unfortunate cases where two professing Christians are married and one leaves, abandoning the other. The one left behind is free, according to this passage, from fulfilling his or her marital vows if one of the other is acting unfaithfully. And I must also mention that some theologians, including myself, have concluded that certain instances of spousal abuse can be considered abandoning as a man's primary role is to protect his spouse and yet he might become the biggest danger in the home. Such is abandoning a husband's primary role. The word peace is used to describe relationships that are not antagonistic. If one is abandoned, the pain goes deep, but it must not reside in bitterness. Being at peace Even with those who have left us, preserves the testimony of the gospel. And you remember last week that is to be our priority, the testimony of the gospel. Verse 16. If one can stay in a relationship with an unbeliever, there is a greater possibility of him or her, that is the unbeliever, being saved. The word saved this time refers to being saved from eternal fire and saved unto eternal life. Verse 17 deals with retaining one's place, and that does not refer to social standing. This is not a forbidding of climbing the ladder of success. One's place used here is one's circumstance. Verse 18. The reference to circumcision is literal, not figurative. Some were tempted to believe that they needed to be circumcised in order to be Christian. And Paul addressed that quickly, he does so at length, to the church at Galatia. Now if you look at verse 17 and then verse 20 and verse 24 They all say similar things and it's like a Big Mac sandwich. There are three layers and in between those layers are instructions to remain circumcised if you are circumcised and to remain uncircumcised if you are uncircumcised. Even those who were slaves can remain slaves or, he says, free, stay in your same situation or don't. The main point is that a Christian, as a Christian, you are to obey the commands of God and not men. Thus Christians are not to be enslaved by any man, but only in servitude to Christ. Due to the nature of the instructions given by the apostle in this section of Scripture, it is easy to get caught up in the controversies. And miss the principles used to address the controversies. If the apostle were here right now Taking questions. He would spend hours upon hours putting before him different scenarios of marriages separations and divorces, thinking that there has to be exceptions or non-applications of our marriage situation as opposed to what Jesus and Paul have taught. The scenarios Paul deals with here in 1 Corinthians are specific, and yet I present to you That there are underlying principles taught that help us with the many scenarios that we all face. The main principle, the main principle is to be content The contentment I referred to is not merely happiness in stagnation, but a contentment to be used by God in whatever circumstance we find ourselves. In accordance with the sin in which we are born, this type of contentment does not come naturally. We have to work at it. Each Sunday during the penitential season, within the full Holy Communion service, you know that we read the Ten Commandments, and you know what number 10 states And ten there is coveting, and we know that at the heart of discontentment is coveting. I am not content with my own house so I covet my neighbors. I am not content with my wife so I covet my co-worker. I am not content with my car so I covet all the cars that pass me on the highway The fallen nature within us wants to be, hear this now, wants to be like God, which means we want to decide for ourselves what we will enjoy and what we can destroy. If we see that we want what we might insist on having, then we're going to think that in our hearts and soon enough do it in our actions. Because of our fallen state, we want to be like God, we don't naturally appreciate being used by God. We don't see it as a privilege to be used as an instrument for the sake of God's sovereign will. Children's stories, such as The Velveteen Rabbit, teach children what a privilege it is to be used by another. To be ignored or neglected in modern movies such as the Toy Story of, I guess it's number four now, those are all tragedies to be thrown away A simple heart that receives one's place as a privilege, as a privileged place regarding What God wants to use us for, no matter what it is, is understanding God's grace. The example of a spouse called to remain with his or her mate after conversion is a call to be used by God. And I remind you of earlier sermons where we learned that the environment of the newly converted Christian within the Corinthian culture was not an agreeable one. An unbelieving husband could very well be sexually promiscuous, physically threatening, verbally disagreeable. An unbelieving woman could be sexually promiscuous, a gossip, and an idol worshiper. Our Heavenly Father, of course, does not require us to stay in relationships where our lives are in danger. However, he does call us to endure the disagreeable The glory of God being used in this manner is that a believer can help make an unbeliever an instrument to be used for God's glory. Consider that the instruments that were washed and consecrated and then made holy for the use in Moses' tabernacle and Solomon's temple. were used to pour out water for cleaning, burn incense, carry the sacrifice, and so on. These each participated in bringing worship and glory to God. Without their knowledge, unbelieving spouses can be used in like manner as a tool of God to worship him and bring him glory. If the unbelieving spouse stays in the marriage, both can be instruments, the unbelieving and the believing, instruments for God. And this sanctification process most importantly flows to the children, as our Heavenly Father uses both the believing and unbelieving spouse to raise the children for God's glory. The end result to this faithfulness is the possibility, as God would will it, for an unbelieving spouse to become a believer. Again, this happens as the believer allows God to use him or her as a tool for his kingdom. The key component of this occurring is the believer being content to be used. So another environment of challenge in Corinth was for the slaves. Who were instructed by the apostle to remain slaves for the glory of God. Let us remember that slavery in Corinth Was not as was practiced in the United States, we tend to only see such issues through our lens, our own personal lens Slavery in the United States was first caused by man stealing or kidnapping, and such is clearly prohibited in both the Old and New Testaments. Much of slavery in the New Testament was a result of money being owed. People were enslaved until they could pay back the money they owed. So the instruction for slaves to stay, if they so wish, which is to be content, is an interesting instruction considering the epistle of Philemon where we understand Paul to have met a runaway slave named Onesimus, and Paul sends Onesimus back as he's converted to Christianity. And he sends him back to his master Philemon, who's also a Christian, and he tells them that they are to receive each other as brothers in Christ. With such instruction, the apostle is utterly consistent. He calls a man to remain as he is a slave. If such a man can be freed legally, then by all means be free. Regardless of being slave or free in this world, Paul wants Christians, you and I, to understand that he or she is both free in Christ, but also a slave to Christ. Thus one can be a slave to Christ by serving a human master or a slave to Christ in another capacity. Once again, there is an underlining call to be content, to be used. Qualifying is important here, for we must never get an understanding that we are forbidden to climb the social ladder of success. The call to remain in one's place does not mean we're not allowed to work hard and to enter a higher socioeconomic class. Christianity is not a caste system. It is a faith in God who rewards his own according to his will. Work hard, climb economic ladders, but no matter what rung of the ladder you are on, be content. Our call is to be content in God's will. If my place is as a cup that is filled and poured out continually, then that is what I will be. If my place is to be the gold around the priest's neck or the undergarment of his cloak, whichever it is, that is what I will be. If I am privileged to participate in feasting on a sacrifice or simply an observer of the feast, receiving the benefits of the same, then that is what I will be. Understand, dear ones, that it is the nature of sin that calls us to be discontent. Our redeemed hearts must recall the grace bestowed upon us, giving us the privilege to be used at all. It is a privilege to be used of God, and for each of us, he has a will in which we can find contentment. And this whole topic reminded me of a story that I need to close with because I like it so much. It is the story of the three trees, and most appropriate this time of year. Once upon a time, on a mountaintop, three little trees stood and dreamed of what they wanted to become when they grew up. The first little tree looked up at the stars and said, I want to hold treasure. I want to be covered with gold and filled with precious stones. I'll be the most beautiful treasure chest in the world. The second little tree looked out at the small stream trickling by on its way to the ocean. I want to be a traveling mighty waters and carrying powerful kings. I'll be the strongest ship in the world The third little tree looked down into the valley below, where busy men and women worked in a busy town. I don't want to leave the mountaintop at all. I want to grow so tall that when people stop and look at me, they'll raise their eyes to heaven and think of God. I will be the tallest tree in the world. Years passed, the rain came, the sun shone, and the little trees grew tall. One day, three woodcutters climbed the mountain The first woodcutter looked at the first tree and said, This tree is beautiful. It's perfect for me. With a swoop of his axe, the first tree fell. Now I shall be made into a beautiful chest. I shall hold wonderful treasures, the first tree said. The second woodcutter looked at the second tree and said, This tree is strong. It is perfect for me With a swoop of his shiny axe, the second tree fell. Now I shall sail mighty waters, thought the second tree. I shall be a strong ship for mighty kings. The third tree fell, felt her heart sink, when the loud last woodcutter looked her way. She stood straight and tall and pointed bravely to heaven But the woodcutter never even looked up. Any kind of tree will do for me, he muttered. The swoop of his shiny axe, the third tree fell. The first tree rejoiced when the woodcutter brought her to a carpenter's shop, but the carpenter fashioned the tree into a feed box for animals. The once beautiful tree was not covered with gold nor with treasure. She was coated with sawdust and filled with hay for hungry farm animals. The second tree smiled when the woodcutter took her to a shipyard, but no mighty sailing ship was made that day. Instead the once strong tree was hammered and sawed into a simple fishing boat She was too small and too weak to sail in the ocean or even a river. Instead, she was taken to a little lake The third tree was confused when the woodcutter cut her into strong beams and left her in a lumber yard. What happened? The once tall tree wondered. All I ever wanted was to stay on the mountaintop and point to God. Many, many days and nights passed. The three trees nearly forgot their dreams. But one night golden starlight poured over the first tree as a young woman placed her newborn baby in the feed box. I wish I could make a cradle for him, her husband whispered. The woman squeezed his hand and smiled as the starlight shone on the smooth and sturdy wood. This manger is beautiful, she said And suddenly the first tree knew he was holding the greatest treasure in the world. One evening, a tired traveler and his friends crowded into an old fishing boat. The traveler fell asleep as the second tree quietly sailed into the lake. Soon a thundering and thrashing storm arose. The little tree shuddered She knew she did not have the strength to carry so many passengers safely through the wind and rain. The tired man awakened. He stood up, stretched out his hand, and said, Peace. The storm stopped as quickly as it had begun, and suddenly the second tree knew he was carrying the king of heaven and earth. On Friday morning, the third tree was startled when her beams were yanked from the forgotten woodpile. She flinched as she was carried through an angry, jeering crowd. She shuddered when soldiers nailed a man's hands to her. She felt ugly and harsh and cruel. But on Sunday morning, when the sun rose and the earth trembled, With joy beneath her, the third tree knew that God's love had changed everything. It had made the third tree strong. And every time people thought of the third tree, they would think of God. Thus, there are blessings ahead if we allow God to use us as He wills. Let us pray. And Father, we thank you for such a wonderful image this time of year. To be mindful of what a privilege it is to be used, to be content, to To realize how unbelievable it is that you call us your children and that we are now even in your kingdom. May this message go throughout our hearts, and to those we love this season, we pray in Jesus' name. Amen. It is our honor to worship the Lord in the giving of our tithes and our offerings. Most of us know that only the Gospels of Matthew and Luke give the narrative of the birth of Jesus. Mark bypasses it altogether, getting right to the heart of the gospel message, and John paints the picture of Jesus on a scale of creation itself, providing a more poetic tone. Scholars believe that the narrative in Luke's gospel was received from Mary, while Matthew's tells the story from the perspective of Joseph, at least some of the perspective of Joseph. What I will do to start this morning is to place the stories in Luke and Matthew in a chronological order as much as we possibly can. The story begins with the angel Gabriel appearing to Zacharias while he served his time in the temple praying and offering incense to the Lord. Zacharias was told by the angel Gabriel he would have a son, even though he and his wife Elizabeth were older and thus passed the time of bearing children. Like Sarah before him, Zacharias was shocked to hear such words from the angel, and that shock made him question the possibility So, in response, the angel made Zacharias mute until the baby was born. Next, the angel appeared to Mary, who was told she was highly favored And that the Lord, by means of the Holy Spirit, would impregnate her with the Christ child. Mary told Elizabeth about a child, and so she visited Mary is told about Elizabeth having a child, and so she goes and visits Elizabeth because they are relatives Upon her visit, Elizabeth believed the story of Mary and called her highly favored and Being that Mary was or the Christ child was in Mary's womb, such a presence was made evident by the baby in Elizabeth's womb, leaping to celebrate the presence of Christ. Mary believed and so she celebrated by singing a song of belief we know as the Magnificat Next, Elizabeth gave birth to a son and insisted he be called John, just as the angel instructed Quickly the tongue of Zacharias was freed, and he breaks out in song of his belief regarding the call upon his son's life to prepare the way of God's child, and He prays and sings about the fulfillment of God's promise to Abraham. Sometime after Mary was visited by the angel, she tells Joseph, the man she was engaged to, what had happened to her. The details of that encounter are not known to us, but we are told that Joseph was a righteous man, and in being righteous, he did not want to disgrace Mary. So he put it in his plans to divorce her quietly. And we met recognize, you see, that such engagement engagements in Jewish tradition, that was a promise exchanged To go back on a promise meant a type of covenant had been broken, and thus a type of divorce was needed also. Before Joseph could go through with his plan, an angel appeared to him in a dream, confirming Mary's story that the child within her was conceived by God. Joseph believed what he was told, and took Mary as his wife, and did not lie with her before she gave birth to the promised child. In the latter part of Mary's pregnancy, Caesar Augustus puts out a call for all Jewish citizens to return to their family's town. So that a census could be taken, so that once the citizens were counted, Caesar then knows how much he can tax them. So Joseph, required by law, takes himself and his pregnant wife to Bethlehem to report for the census and to pay his taxes. When they arrived in Bethlehem, Mary begins the process of birth, causing Joseph to look for a place where she can have the baby, but there are no available rooms because The house of David had returned to the city of David, Bethlehem, and there were too many people and not enough rooms for lodging. So the next best thing is to sleep with the animals in their shelter, and so Joseph finds such a shelter for his family. Mary gives birth to Jesus, wrapping him in bands of cloth to keep him warm and snug, while next laying him in a trough for livestock, we call it a manger. likely filling it with straw. Historians believe a nursemaid would have been called to help Mary, but that's not told to us in the story. Because it is quite an event for God to become man, angels appear to shepherds in their fields and announce the worthy glory to be given to God for his tremendous act of love. And the angels instruct the shepherds to believe what they are being told and to go see for themselves the child born to save the world from sin and shame. And the shepherds did as they were told, and when they saw the child, they told Joseph and Mary about the angels and what they said. And Mary, we are told, pondered all of this in her heart. She pondered it, which means she reflected upon it, she considered the various meanings of it, and she believed. That ends the narrative of the birth of Jesus, but of course there is more when the Magi follow a star and Herod hears about it, but that is for Epiphany. What I ask of you today, after hearing the story again told in what is most likely the chronological order, what I ask of you today is, do you believe it? Do you believe all of it? Now don't dismiss that question with an immediate answer such as, well, of course I believe it. Examine yourself and see that the answer is not a quick or simple one. I had a professor in seminary who told the story of attending a theological seminar. where he was talking with a fellow professor, and the man was a liberal man, and asked him if he really believed the stories of the Bible like the sun standing still in the book of Joshua so that Israel could win a battle. And my professor responded, Yes, I believe, like I believe that Jonah swallowed the whale. He thought his answer was quite clever. That is why he told us the story. But I knew from taking this professor for several classes. that he did indeed struggle to believe the more fantastic stories of the Bible, even the details of the birth of Jesus. There are likely many reasons why people become doubtful of the miracles described in the Bible. One that I know of is how life experiences can make us cynics about life in general. Oh, we believe in God. That's easy enough. Jesus? Sure. I believe in him and love him as my Savior. But all of that other stuff just seems to distract from the basics of religion, and it seems to be used to divide us. And such is how a cynic thinks. And we get cynical because much of our lives is void of the miraculous. We don't witness children born to virgins. We don't hear of people being healed of diseases like we read of in the Bible. And when we do hear of it, there is no verification of a bona fide miracle, or it happened in a jungle in South America, and so we don't know what to do with that type of testimony. Our lives are so void of the miraculous that we start calling things that are not miracles miracles. I really did have a hard time writing this down, but I need to say sorry But a miracle is not the US hockey team beating the Soviet Union hockey team, even though that was a great moment. And a miracle is not a teenage boy cleaning his room. A miracle is best defined by examples. A miracle is a virgin giving birth to a child. That's a miracle. Consider how some treat the teachings of the Bible. I preached on wives and husbands obeying the teachings of St. Paul. This past Sunday, which talked about allowing our spouse to have authority over our bodies. I don't know how many of you believed what the passage was saying. And how many actually obey it or have obeyed it? If you don't obey it, does it not show that you don't believe all that the Bible teaches? And if you don't believe all that the Bible teaches, then you are picking and choosing what you want to obey and what you don't want to obey. And that makes you the authority over your faith rather than the God you say you love and believe in and the Jesus you say you have faith in. There are other such teachings in the Bible that people don't think are very important to follow, such as wives submitting to their husbands, husbands sacrificially loving their wives all followers of Jesus, putting him as priority before our children, our grandchildren, and our spouses Those are easily dismissed as not important because they are emotionally hard to accept. Other such warnings against gossip and being busy bodies are weaked at because everybody does it and it can't be all bad. And that Sabbath law, that just doesn't come close to applying to the Christian life, and certainly is not going to interfere with my love for the ravens. Or my soccer star child, God wants me to be happy more than anything else, right? Such thinking might sound right to some, but it is not what the Bible teaches. The Bible teaches that how we treat our spouse is directly correlated to how we portray the gospel to the world. The Bible teaches that we are to love Jesus more than anything else. And if anything even comes close to competing with our love for God, it is to be labeled an idol and an idol smash. The Bible teaches that gossip and being a busy body are just as serious as the sins of sexual immorality and taking of the Lord's name in vain. Those who live in such sins will die in such sins, and to live in such sins is evidence that the Holy Spirit does not live in you like you think he does. The Bible never teaches, even remotely, that your happiness is what God wants most. The only happiness that God wants is for you, that you would love Him with all of your heart, soul, mind, and strength, and your neighbor as yourself. And the only way you can do that is by having faith in Jesus. Your earthly happiness does not equate to eternal happiness, as our study of Job this year has verified. Examine how many things you believe without ever questioning the information. You believe something as simple as George Washington being the first president of the United States without any doubt in your mind And yet you have not done a personal study to ensure that that is true You accept that in 1969 Neil Armstrong stepped onto the surface of the moon, and you believe it, even when there are doubters who say it was staged. We believe such information as factual because such information doesn't change us. We don't have to do anything with that information. But when you believe the Bible and all its stories, you have to do something. You have to believe, and then your life is to be lived in accordance with what you believe. So ask yourself again, do you believe the Christmas story as told in the Gospels? Think upon it. Does it change your life at all? Do you believe every detail? I say you can and you should. And the reason why we should believe is the person of Jesus. We can believe every detail of the Christmas story because it is told by those who follow Jesus, who knew him and his family personally. And we believe in Jesus because he had and has the words of eternal life. No one is ever taught like him. No one has known the heart of humanity like him. No one has explained the truth like Jesus explained the truth. No one defined love like Jesus defined it and lived it. No one loves the least among humanity and bravely rebukes the greatest among humanity at the same time. No one makes grand promises and fulfills every one of them. No one but Jesus. And no one has overcome death as Jesus did. That seals it for me, and I trust it does for you. The Christmas story is before us this holy day, with all its miraculous and unbelievable, believable stories. All its believable details. Believe the details, all of them. And teach them to your children and to their children. Every detail. And let it change us, and them, and the next generation, until Jesus comes again. Let us believe the details for the glory of God. Amen.

sermons.title: Christmas Eve 2019
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Ghost, Amen. Please be seated. I want you to recognize that there is a great irony in many so-called Christmas movies. For many of them focus on some type of means or manner that Christmas needs to be saved. My personal memory allows me to conclude that such Christmas needing to be saved type movies began with Rudolph, the red-nosed reindeer. You recall that it was one foggy Christmas Eve that Santa realized he would not be able to fly his sleigh and deliver toys in the great fog that evidently covered the entire globe. He next realized that a reindeer with a glowing red nose would be able to cut through the fog and lead Santa around the world safely. It is a wonder that engineers and manufacturers have not yet discovered how red glowing lights pierce through dense fog. It appears that there is a lot of money to be made if a company wanted to learn from Santa and Rudolph. But as I said, Rudolph was the first. Here are some other titles of movies of Saving Christmas. There is The Dog Who Saved Christmas Vacation. The night they, whoever they are, the night they saved Christmas, the tree that saved Christmas, the three dogateers that saved Christmas Surviving Christmas, which we actually watched and I don't recommend it. The Toys That Saved Christmas And who could forget, Ernest saves Christmas. I could go on, but I won't. There was even a movie produced by Christians five years ago titled What was it titled? Saving Christmas. And the gist of the plot was in the movie was that Christians are overreacting to the secular world in terms of it basically hoarding Christmas for themselves. And so it was a message to say that it's okay as a Christian to decorate trees and to light candles and to have lights and to have candy canes because all of them or each of them symbolize something about the Christmas story. And so We give gifts because God gave us Jesus and remember the candy cane is the shepherd's staff and the white is his purity, the red is his blood, and we can go on and on and talk about Such symbolism. It is a type of film that's supposed to help Christians feel better about the festiveness that we put into our Christian Christmas celebrations. Now, I said that there is a great irony in all of this, and here it is, as far as I can see it. It is the fact that Christmas is about God saving us. Not us or they or Ernest saving Christmas. Christmas is about God saving us. And why does God need to save us? Well, here is the coal in your stocking. You and I are guilty of sin. We deserve coal in our stockings. We are guilty of sin because we are of the human race, which has walked away from God's covenant with us We are guilty of sin because each of us in our individual lives have committed acts of sin such as worshiping false idols. Taking God's name in vain, dishonoring the Sabbath, dishonoring our parents, hating our fellow man, committing sexual immorality in thought and deed. Taking material wealth from others, lying about our lives, and doing so purposefully and coveting, which is simply not appreciating, first of all, all that you've been blessed to have. That is how we have sinned. And we have sinned against our own consciences. How many people do not talk about that type of sin, but we all know it is part of each of our story. We do things we know we shouldn't do, and we do things we know we should we don't do things we know we should do, and we justify it, all of it. To ourselves and conclude that we are at least not as bad as Hitler, and that makes us good in a generic sense. But our conscience is no different. Consider this example. Does your heart ever jump when someone knocks at your door at home? We have become so isolated from one another, and we rarely visit one another, especially out of the blue, with someone coming over. When I was a kid, we went from house to house to our with to our friends' houses in the block every day. So knocking was part of everyday life. But now we jump inwardly and outwardly when someone knocks at our door Who could that be? What do they want? Well that jumping inwardly is what happens when someone confronts you about the things that you have done wrong. We get a similar feeling. The same as when mom and dad would call you to their room to talk to you. Or a teacher wants you to stay after school. Or a pastor calls you to his study and does not tell you what he wants to talk about. Our hearts jump, our throats get a lump, we can't swallow. Because we are guilty. We have guilt that we carry around and fear we have that someone is going to uncover who we really are and what we really have done. My whole point in describing this is to say, such is what God came to save us from. He came to save us from our own personal guilt as well as our guilt of being part of Adam's race and our personal sins that broke God's commandments. Mary knew that Christmas was about God saving his people when she sang these words. And his mercy is on them that fear him from generation to generation. It is God's mercy of how we are saved. Zacharias saying about Christmas being about God saving his people with these words. For God has visited and redeemed his people. He has raised up a horn of salvation for us. Simeon knew that Christmas was about God saving his people with these words of prayer after seeing the Christ child. For my eyes have seen your salvation. Anna, the prophetess's widow, knew that Christmas was about God saving his people when she saw Jesus Jesus and proclaimed the child to be the redemption, the means of salvation for Israel, for God's people. Now I know that some of you did not come here to hear that you are a sinner needing to be saved. I am aware of what sells I have witnessed churches advertising their Christmas services as being nothing but celebration. But about what they are celebrating, I'm not sure. I was made aware of a church in Florida that celebrated Christmas with what they called Christmas Olay. Which consisted of having a circus show to replicate the popular movie The Greatest Showman. They had women in tights dance around the stage, jugglers, magicians, trapeze artists. How such a production presented the story of God saving his people from the guilt of their sin I don't know, and neither did the parishioners, or we can call them the audience who attended said church. And such a description of a church service so-called reminds me of what else is being taught in some of these churches. Some people are hearing that Jesus came to save them from their times of emotional depression, from anxieties, and from periods of stress. No, he did not. Jesus came to be like us to save us from sin. And the result of sin, which is death, both spiritually and physically, and he came to save us from Satan's power. Now I will grant you that a result of Jesus forgiving our sins can be a lighter consciousness, and a lighter consciousness can help us with bouts of depression and anxiety and stress, and all that is good. But that is a byproduct of our sins being forgiven, which again is why Jesus was sent to us. There is another genre of Christmas movies that is not about saving Christmas, but about saving people. It's a wonderful life. It's about saving a good man from great despair. Family man is about saving a man from a life of only pursuing worldly endeavors. Home Alone is about saving a kid from criminals. And A Christmas Story. Well I don't really know what that movie's about. Other than a boy getting a BB gun. I mentioned such movies because those are the usual ones that Bobby Lynn and I watch during this season We like them because of their sentimentality. We like them because they have a sincere message to them. And yet, the Christmas story isn't about saving people from despair, even. Because they are being accused of stealing a bank deposit Uncle Billy carelessly gave to Mr. Potter. And I realize that may sound strange to some of your ears because you think that the Christmas story must be about saving people from despair. Well it can be, if that despair is caused by a person not being in right relationship with God. If the despair is caused by a recognition that I am a sinner in need of a savior, and I am crying out to God to be saved from my sin and the punishment of death. Then yes, the Christmas story is about saving from despair. But the point is the same as I made. When I said God becoming man dwelling among us was not to overcome depression, anxiety, and the like. Overcoming despair over one's sins cannot be solved by family and friends gathering together to donate money so that a person won't go to jail. That is another part of a wonderful life, in case you didn't catch the reference. Money can't save me from eternal death. Money can't pay for my sins. The wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus. I have not seen Ernest Saves Christmas. For those of you who are young, Ernest was a character in the 80s that saved a lot of things. But here's some of the plot of the movie. A man claiming to be Santa Claus arrives in Orlando, Florida, where Ernest P. Laurel is working as a taxicab driver. He picks up Santa. Who tells Ernest that he is on his way to inform a local celebrity named Joe Carruthers that he has been chosen to be the next Santa Claus. Joe hosts a local children's program with emphasis on manners and integrity. While they are driving, a runaway teenage girl who says she is named Harmony, Starr, joins Ernest and Santa in the taxicab. When they get to their destination, Santa possesses no legal currency, only play money. So he his uh so he in his Christmas spirit, Ernest tells him that the ride is free. The decision gets Ernest fired from his job. Ernest later discovers that Santa left his magic sack in the taxicab and Ernest begins to press to find the old man and return it to him. At the Orlando Children's Museum, Santa tries talking to Joe, but Rudy is interrupted and rebuffed by Joe's agent, Marty Brock. Santa begins to worry when he discovers his sack is missing. and becomes even more discouraged because of his increasing forgetfulness result of being sat there for 151 years. Ernest poses as an employee of a governor of harmony as a governor's niece and to help Santa escape from jail by convincing the police chief that Santa must be taken to an insane asylum. Santa explains to Ernest and the Harmony that he has been handed the job in eighteen eighty nine and he's been losing his magic ever since. The only way to restore it is to make someone else the new Santa. Ernest disguises himself as a snake rancher so he can sneak Santa into a movie studio, and I'm going to stop here because it's crazy and silly and stupid Such a story is not about Christmas. Christmas is Christmas is Christmas is Christmas. It is God, it is Mary, it is Joseph, it is a baby named Jesus, it is shepherds, it is a manger, it is peace on earth and goodwill towards men, because God gave his only son.

sermons.title: Staying Where You Are
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. We are continuing our series in the book of First Corinthians. We are covering 1 Corinthians chapter 7, verse 25 through 40, which was our epistle reading. Encourage you to turn there in your Bible. The Apostle Paul was wrong. The Apostle Paul was wrong. Does that unnerve you to hear me say that? It should, because you don't know why I'm saying it. If you ever wondered why churches and denominations go from believing the Bible and all that it teaches To not believing it, especially its most important part, it is usually caused by the seminaries of the particular denomination That should not force you to conclude that seminaries alone as institutions are the cause of Christian liberalism, because they are not. It is the heart of humanity that is the cause. But what happens at many seminaries is reoccurring. Professors are hired who have little to no experience being a pastor, and yet they are to train future pastors. And these professors are given classes to teach and are also expected to do research and to be published in books or scholarly journals in order to raise the prestige of the seminary and thus garner grants and financial gifts from alumni and supporters. In order to be published, professors must find new information in their particular field of study. Because so much has been written about the Bible, to find new information forces professors to speculate about what the Bible does not say and then to defend their speculations. When this happens, the Holy Scriptures are reinterpreted, and the authority of the Scripture in the eyes of the professors and the students, well, it's lessened. And this happens again and again until the scripture has no authority in the eyes of future pastors. Add to these realities the spirit of the age that vagues Christians to fall in line with progressive thinking, and you have a complete abandonment of the Christian faith. But back to my point that the Apostle Paul was wrong. When saying this, I am not doubting the authority of Holy Scripture. The apostle was wrong when he thought that Jesus would return in his lifetime. Now please don't hear me say that he was wrong to think that Jesus would return in his lifetime. All Christians are to live their lives Believing that Jesus is going to return in their lifetime. You and I are to believe that. To think in such a manner is to motivate Christians to be ready for Jesus. Paul was simply wrong in that Jesus did not return in his lifetime. And it is Paul's conclusion. That Jesus is going to return that causes him to address the issue of not being married. I am being open with you when I say that I really don't like to preach this section of Scripture. I am a man who believes that the institution of marriage is so very sacred and so very necessary to practice and embrace. Because it saves generations from so many sins that corrupt our individual lives and corrupt our culture. But these are St. Paul's words, and these words are inspired by God, and so they must be heard and they must be understood. And I am identifying the providence of God in that we are addressing a teaching of St. Paul that is most certainly controversial, a teaching to a Gentile people. As we are on the eve of Epiphany, where we celebrate God revealing salvation to the Gentiles, you and me. The overriding message being, and I I want you to hold on to this, of this passage of scripture, the overriding meaning Is for Christians to redeem the time for the days are evil. Redeem the time for the days in which we live are evil. The apostle gives three reasons why a person should not marry. You remember after struggling, or suggesting, excuse me, the same earlier in the chapter. He went on to explain the proper behavior that is to be had between a husband and wife in a marriage. Each spouse should be available to the other for physical passion to be expressed. Each spouse should also allow himself or herself to be used for the sanctification of the other. And after giving those two instructions, he turns his attention again to those who are in the church yet unmarried. And as a side note, I wish for you to notice that I'm using the term unmarried. This is as opposed to the term single. And it is not as though the word single is a bad word, but it does separate the unmarried into a category of appearing to be ostracized from community, single, by themselves I heard a story several years ago of a minister and his family sitting at a church function. All of the singles were being recognized as available, and prayers were being offered up on their behalf to find someone and the person that was doing the speaking identified the pastor's daughter as being single The pastor's quick retort was, She is not single, she is a daughter. And the point of that retort was to claim her as not being separate from the community of faith. Being single or unmarried is not a disease, such as leprosy, which separates a person from the rest of society. The unmarried can and do play a vital role in the health of the community of faith. Of course they do, and Paul will explain how. The unmarried should not be seen as mere singles, but be seen as daughters and sons and friends and mothers and fathers. And finally, and most importantly, they are members of the body of Christ, like all of us are. So turning back to our text, we again see that Paul submits three reasons why persons within the church of his day should remain unmarried. The first was the increased suffering marriage would bring.
