And we thank you for the love that goes so greatly deep into our hearts and souls that we can freely love others in need. Father, help each of us see ways in which we can be a city set on a hill, a light in the midst of darkness for the people around us. We pray this in Jesus' name. Amen.

sermons.title: Love in these times
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. For those who are joining us, newly joining us, we are walking through First Corinthians And we are now upon 1 Corinthians chapter 13. And as we venture into the chapter on love We must remember context. Context, context, context. St. Paul has been writing a great deal on the problems of the Christians at Corinth. beginning with selfishness and egotistical in the venue of corporate worship. Rich people were gloating over poor people. People with ecstatic gifts were perceiving themselves more favored by God, and those who had visible responsibilities were considering themselves more important than other members of the church. These problems led the Holy Spirit to anoint Paul with these words about what he calls in chapter 12, verse 31, a more excellent way. Besides gloating, besides self-congratulating, and besides self-love, there is a more excellent way. Unfortunately and necessarily, we must first address what love, as described in chapter 13, is not. Little trivia. Besides words like I, you, the, what are referred to as common words What do you guess is the most uncommon word in popular music today, including hip-hop, rap, R<unk>B, and heavy metal? Yes, you guessed it. It is the word love. As most of you know, the Greek language, the language from which we receive most of the New Testament, has several words for our one word of love. Thus it is helpful if we add descriptives to our one word. Descriptive words we could add to the love songs that are sung in popular music are lust, love, warm, fuzzy, love. sentimental love, and so on. Such love is not the love of 1 Corinthians chapter 13. Such love has little or nothing to do with the love of 1 Corinthians chapter 13. If you were one of many young couples who chose 1 Corinthians chapter 13 to read during your wedding you might be disappointed to know that the love described here is also not married love, although it can be in various places applied to a marital relationship. No, the love here is not married love. It is not friend to a friend. It is not sibling to sibling. It is not parent to child. It is not child to parent. Instead, it is a love that is to be practiced from one Christian to another. Remember the context of the chapter. Some of us are aware that the Greek word used here by St. Paul for love is agape. Some have said that agape is God's love. Actually, God's love is many different loves. But Paul was compelled to describe the ideal of the gospel life with the word agape, because no other Greek word The word agape expresses the love of esteem and reverence and sacred tenderness. This word was not classical, for no heathen writer had used it. But the verb agapa o, corresponding with the Latin biligo, These are reserved for this loftier kind of love, the substantive, which together with the substantive agape cis, used in the Latin, we can also find in Jeremiah chapter 31. The word is thus, as Archbishop Trent has said, born in the bosom of revealed religion. The Vulgate chose caritas, where we get our word charity, to express this love of reason, affection, dearness. This love that reigns between human beings and between man and God. But the Greek word use is not as important As how the word is described and then how it is to be practiced. It is fair to say that this chapter on love is the most beautiful of all chapters in the Bible. And it is also the most convicting of chapters, because the standard of love described is most difficult to live up to, but strive to live up to it, we must. And so we look at each verse of the chapter. We note in verse 1 that there is a shift to the first person. Paul is using himself again as an example. And he begins with tongues, because it was the spiritual gift that was most popular amongst the Corinthians. The list of gifts next given were those that the Corinthians were congratulating themselves for possessing. We are also to be aware that the first three verses describe powers and gifts that the apostle himself had. He was a prophet. He worked miracles. He revealed mysteries. He had suffered the loss of all things for Christ's sake. He speaks then with special authority, for no Corinthian had gifts such as the Apostle Paul had been given. But still he will say, without love, it is all worthless. What follows next is Paul's characterization of love in behavior, not in feeling. A worldly mind thinks upon love as a feeling, whereas the Bible invariably thinks of it first as a way of life, a way of behavior, a commitment to others. Love. Love is suffering long. Love puts up with a lot. Love is kind. It gives a lot. Love is content. It is content with itself as it does not envy. And humble before God and man, as it is not puffed up. We know from reading this letter up to this point that there was a considerable amount of envy in the church. rivalries between teachers, the poor looking wistfully at the rich, those with lesser gifts looking at those with more powerful ones. Love overcomes all such temptations. It may be that what love is not, as stated in verse 5, is actually what the Corinthians and everyone and anyone who does not have love actually describing what they are. When people don't practice love, they are rude. As were the Corinthians to one another at the Lord's table. When people don't practice love, they are self-seeking, as the Corinthians are described in chapter 12, and we will see in chapter 14. By not rude, Paul means that love is considerate of other people's feelings and take care not to offend, at least offending unnecessarily. By keeping no record of wrongs, he means that love does not hold a grudge. To bear all things is to endure wrongs and evils and cover them with beautiful restraint. Love covers all sins, the scripture tells us. To believe all things takes the best and kindest views of all persons in all circumstances, as long as it is possible to do so. It is the opposite to the modern spirit. The modern spirit which drags everything into the mud, paints it in the darkest of colors, and makes the worst of it. Thus love is entirely alien from the spirit of the cynic, the pessimist, the ecclesiastical rival, the anonymous slanderer, the secret detractor. That love, hopes in all things, shows that the Christian life is averse to sourness and gloom. As our love for one another is to take the sunny, the cheerful view of man and of the world, because that is what God does. And love endures all things. Whether all things is seventy times seven, the offenses of our brother, or wrongs of a stranger, or even the sufferings of self. With such descriptions of love, the readers and hearers of this love are to realize that we have a picture of the life and character of Christ. The text in verse 8, as you may know, has been a hot button in the debate between those who still believe in the supernatural gifts being practiced by Christians today, such as tongues and healing. There's also a verse that has taken the other side that says that all of these things have ceased But this, however, is not a verse for either side of that issue. That is placing too much weight on this text. Instead, Paul's point is simply that while these spiritual gifts are limited in duration, love, that's the focus, will endure forever. And so he sets forth three of the spiritual gifts that are temporary, that are destined to come to an end. Verse 9 and 10 are crucial for humbling all of us regarding what we can understand about the world and the kingdom of God, this side of heaven. Everything we do in life is in pieces. How many voices have you heard regarding this most recent virus outbreak? that have only a piece of the truth with a lot more that is not understood. That is the way of it. That is the way about everything. We will only understand impart until the world as we know it is no more Verse 10 provides us the hope that the whole will indeed be known, and the whole will be perfect, for it will be as God wills it. That is where we are to place our faith. In verses 11 through 12, Paul elaborates his point about their present knowledge being imperfect and temporary. He expressed it by way of two analogies, the point he made in verses 9 and 10. He is still talking about differences between the present and the future, between the complete and the incomplete, and the imperfect to the perfect. The time is coming when our knowledge, now imperfect, will be perfect. The imperfect will fall away. But love never comes to an end. Love is now, and love is forever The choice of analogy of a mirror probably stems from the fact that Corinth was famous as a producer of the finest bronze mirrors in antiquity. This verse in my ministry has come into use many different times For it is my experience that Christians become frustrated because they cannot see clearly. And they become frustrated with their spiritual leaders because we cannot see clearly. But the fact that none of us can see clearly is to be accepted with great humility, for those are the places where we cannot see clearly that we are to walk by faith not. by sight. In verse 13 is the memorized triad summing up the entire Christian life. We live in faith, trusting in Jesus Christ for our salvation. We live in hope of a future guaranteed to us by Christ's death and resurrection. And we live in love, serving one another as dear brothers and sisters in Christ. Love is the greatest because it alone of the three continues forever After faith is given away to sight and hope is given away to fulfillment, what is left is love. I ask that you oblige me at this point in the sermon, as I wish to present to you a testimony of sorts. This passage of scripture is near and dear to my heart and soul because back in nineteen eighty-two I read it for the first time, and God used it to change my life. I had been given a Bible for Christmas that year from my sister. In front of that Bible, it had a page that gave directions to the reader regarding where certain subjects were addressed. It read something like, If you are discouraged, read such and such chapter and verse. If you need hope, read such and such chapter and verse. And if you want to know about love, read 1 Corinthians chapter 13. I wanted to know about love. So I turned to the chapter and read it. And after I did, I remember feeling two things, at least. First, I felt terribly sad because the love described I had never experienced from anyone, and I had never loved anyone in such a manner. But I knew I wanted and I needed that love. The second way I felt was hopeful, even uplifted by the idea that such a love was possible. If it was possible to be loved in the manner described and to love in the manner described, then I wanted to be a Christian. I wanted to love and I wanted to be loved. That is when the Holy Spirit grabbed me out of my slew of despond and directed me to follow Christ. Another testimony I have. Is that there have been relationships that I have found to be in trouble during my pastoral ministry that were only changed for the better? When I examine my thoughts and behaviors in light of this love described in this chapter. Consider relationships that find you in moments of strife. And do an inventory regarding your love behavior toward the person with whom you are at odds. Are you suffering long? If not, you should be. Are you being kind? Are you struggling with any type of envy? Are you seeing yourself as better than that person? Have you behaved rudely? Have you sought what is best for you only? Have you thought said person was of lesser value than yourself? Have you kept record of wrongs? Have you believed the best, hoped the best, and endured hardships for this person? Any and all failures to these standards is a failure to love, and thus requires repentance and changed behavior. Beloved, the love of God is powerful as it changes individual lives and relationships always for the better. When it is witnessed even by unbelieving hearts, it shakes the soul, for the beauty of it cannot be denied. This love, as St. Paul describes, is fundamental to Christianity. It is a basic. More than other parts of our lives as Christians, it is indispensable. Love is the sum and substance of the obedience that we owe to God. It has been asked. whether non-Christians can love in this manner described by St. Paul. And I believe it is important to acknowledge that non-Christians can think the best about another person. They can be kind, they can reject envy, but instead choose to think the best of others. They cannot keep record of wrongs, and they can hope for the best, and they can endure the worst. All aspects of this love can be known by an unbeliever, in part, at least. When they do love, however, The power to love is not the Holy Spirit. And the end of such love is not to the glory of God, which is why the Christian is to love. To really love another human being requires knowing the grace of God and the salvation through Jesus Christ. Because it requires a change of heart, it requires a new birth, a new creation that frees a person from the bondage of self-love, from the bondage of darkness, from the bondage of foolishness of sin. That is what Saint Teresa meant when she said, quote, Satan could not be Satan any longer if once he could love his neighbor as himself. To do that, you see, you must have a new heart. You must know Jesus Christ and the grace of God. You must have new motives and new longings and new powers within you. And I shared with the Congregation of St. Stephen's how we can love our neighbor as ourselves these days of this viral trial. By cooperating with the quarantine requests. We can also love by checking in on our brothers and sisters in Christ to see if they need anything, anything at all Love practice can also include sharing the truth about Jesus with Christians and non-Christians As all, all need to hear that God so loved the world that he gave his only son. Ears need to hear that God will never leave or forsake those who love Him. Ears need to hear that regardless of circumstance, when we are followers of Jesus Christ, we are never crushed. never driven to despair, never forsaken, never destroyed, but instead are healed, repaired, protected, and restored. Finally, we are to be convinced that love as described here is a choice, a choice we make, and as a choice it becomes our responsibility to live it. It is what we choose to do or not to do. Because it is the only thing that will remain, the choice seems easy enough. Let us pray. Our God, we thank you for this message of love that is not only beautiful, but is awakening of the soul. It helps us, dear Lord, during this time of crisis, during this time of confusion. Love does remain, no matter what happens around us. Your love remains. And so now, Lord, help us all receive the challenge to pick it up and to practice it with one another. We pray this in Jesus' name. Amen.

sermons.title: Need for Prophecy
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Turn with me, if you would, to 1 Corinthians chapter 14. We continue our series on the book of Corinthians, and although we read through verse 9, we will actually be covering through verse 25. Because that's a bit lengthy, we will not go verse by verse this morning, but instead I will give a summation of the points that St. Paul is making. Because love has been proven to be the more excellent way, and because the Corinthian Christians need such love to overcome the many sins of selfishness that they have been practicing Paul points to the gift that best expresses agape love, and that gift is prophecy. The gift of prophecy is up against the popular gift of speaking in an unknown tongue. Evidently the gift of speaking in tongues was quite popular in Corinth for reasons that we cannot fully know. For those of you who are not aware, I have a background in regards to the gift of speaking in tongues I was part of an independent charismatic church during my late teens that insisted that every member speak in tongues as evidence of being baptized in the Holy Spirit. So I'm not speaking only from an exegetical point of view, but also from experience. I am convinced that the speaking in tongues in Scripture is referring to persons Who can speak languages of men that they themselves have not learned? This is clearly seen in Acts chapter 2 and elsewhere in the book of Acts. There is no reason for present-day Bible readers to read into Paul's letters here, for example. That somehow the gift of tongues had changed from the events in the book of Acts to the time of these Corinthian Christians into being anything else but languages of men. If it is interpreted to be anything else, like languages of angels, as some have claimed, well the burden is on them for proof. My experience taught me that the claim to speak a language of angels is an easy way to pretend that you have the gift of speaking in tongues. and then to pretend that you are able to interpret something that no one else can interpret. But I do not say that all who pretend are doing so to be deceitful Some are so very anxious to have the gift of tongues that they have convinced themselves that they have it. We should not judge their hearts. Paul's basic point is that the gift of tongues being made a priority in regards to a gift desired, a gift pursued, is not an expression of the love that he spoke about so beautifully in the previous chapter. A person who speaks in tongues edifies himself because he feels a special connection with God, and that feeling of connection only benefits him or her. An example is found of different musical instruments. If those instruments all sounded the same, being indistinguishable from one another, they would not communicate anything beautiful or useful. So it is when people speak in languages that are not understood for those listening. The next point is how useful language can be in all their distinctions But only when the language or the languages are understood by the listen the listeners. When we have problems With others who are foreign to us, it is usually because we cannot understand one another. Language barriers sustain personal barriers. One simple solution, Paul suggests, is that if anyone speaks in a tongue so that others can hear, there should be an interpretation of what was uttered so that all Christians who are gathered for worship can be edified. To speak only for the edification of the one speaking is not love practiced. The main point being that love is practiced by caring about the edification of others rather than self. An example of how tongues does not edify, and it can actually condemn, is the quote Paul gives from Isaiah 28. The point there being that the foreign language of the Assyrian invaders represented a judgment on God's people For God, as it were, is speaking to them in a foreign language, because they would not hear the truth in their own language. To know the truth in a language understood is far, far better. Words not understood keep an unbeliever in a state of unbelief. Words understood by a believer feeds his belief. Now mixed in with the various lessons on why tongues is a gift for the church I'm sorry, right? Tongues as as a gift for the church had weaknesses for the edification of the church as a whole. In there are also instructions on what is to be preferred, which is prophecy Now before we look at the benefits of prophecy, let it be understood that the gift of prophecy is not just knowing about the future. In fact, in all of Scripture, the practice of prophecy is rarely telling of an unknown future, but is instead the application of God's word in present and in future circumstances. The prophet takes God's word already revealed and applies it so that the people can understand it and then obey it. The best summary I have heard is that prophecy is bringing God's word to bear in the lives of people. An unbeliever can hear it and know it is of God and repent and believe. And a believer can hear it and know it is from God and change his or her life to better honor God. In summary, love is the more excellent way, and the best way to love is to speak forth the Word of God to those who would hear. That summary point then leads me to address primarily two things for us today. The first is that we need to hear the word of God applied to our present circumstance, which is living within this pandemic. Preachers need to prophesy regarding how we are to understand God's word and thus God's will in light of a virus that has scared us so that we remain separated from one another, and tempting others to hoard goods, so that they will not be in want while not caring about the needs of others. There are also questions that go unanswered regarding how we are to understand and then communicate God's will during a time of crisis. Simple questions such as, did God cause this viral outbreak? And is God judging the world with such an outbreak? These are on the minds of unbelievers and believers. So we must. What must the prophet utter? What must the prophet utter in times is these. Regarding questions of God's judgment and a viral outbreak, such as the one we are experiencing There is no direct word given by God to his prophets that says this particular outbreak is a judgment for these particular sins And when these particular sins are confessed and turned away from, that God will bring healing. I do not have a specific word such as that, and I don't know anyone that does. Of course, there are specific sins of our nation. And in the world that have earned God's wrath, such as people celebrating abortions, celebrating sodomy, fornication, adultery There are politicians and corporate leaders who are indeed guilty of feeding systemic hatred, of oppressing the poor. There is severe persecution of Christians in various parts of the world. These sins and others are most certainly worthy of any and all types of judgment that God wants to bring down In this life. But viral outbreaks are not new to the world. For anyone who has learned elementary human history knows of much greater outbreaks that one than the one we are experiencing. What we can clearly conclude from God's word is that suffering a pandemic is a result of living in a cursed world. The Bible tells us that because of the sin of Adam and Eve, the world is cursed. Fires, floods, earthquakes, tornadoes, famines, hurricanes, pestilence. And other types of disasters are caused by living in a world that suffers in death because the wages of sin is death. And don't forget how human beings contribute to fires and floods and other disasters. Careless people start forest fires and destroy acres of good timber, kill habitats for animals, and destroy people's homes. Floods occur because people build cities below sea level. And then blame God when those cities flood. And pestilence occurs because people eat and sell unclean animals that can infect a few and then infect many. What we can know from God's word is that anytime there is a fear for loss of life, anytime something happens that causes people to face their mortality God uses it to bring people to repentance. Remember from Luke chapter 13 where Jesus is questioned about an incident that is not recorded in history but is consistent with the behavior of Pontius Pilate, who likely tortured rebellious Galileans by killing them on the floor of the temple, thus desecrating the temple The people wondered what sins were committed by the victims to deserve such a fate. Such questions are similar to the ones referenced earlier as people want to know how dirty are God's hands when tragedy strikes. Jesus' answer is so insightful because he doubles down with another example. He mentions an accident where a tower in a nearby city to Old Jerusalem fell and killed 18 people. In such instances, we are not to conclude, Jesus taught, that those who suffered were worthy of such an accident. Such was the foolish logic of Job's companions. Instead, we are to understand that no one is more or less a sinner in a sense that some deserve to die by tragedy. But instead, we are all sinners, and whenever we are faced with our mortality, we are to take it as an opportunity to repent of our sins and believe on the Lord Jesus Christ. So that we can avoid the ultimate tragedy, which is hellfire. That is always the message of a prophet Repent and believe on the Lord Jesus Christ and be saved. What else should a prophet be saying in times like these? Besides the call to repentance and believe in Jesus, the prophet must call God's people to fear not. Because Jesus has overcome sin and death, we are not to fear sickness, disaster, even death For the Christian, to die is gain, to live is Christ. Jesus promised that he would never leave his people He is with each of us as we go through this trial, reminding us that his perfect love casts out fear, and that the only one to fear is the Heavenly Father, and the Father loves us so That he takes us under his mighty wing to be our shelter, protecting us from the enemy, even the enemy of pestilence. Besides the call to repentance and then the call to fear not, the prophet must speak of the second greatest law, which is to love thy neighbor as thyself. Clear evidence is before us regarding how far our culture has fallen away from the Christian ethic. that at one time made people in towns and counties in America united in caring about one another. The hoarding that has been occurring is disgraceful, as it is not only rejecting loving thy neighbor, but makes a clear statement In favor of the demise of one's neighbor, for we are leaving some people to fend for themselves with no means to do so. What makes the hoarding even more alarming is how unnecessary it all is. We are the richest nation in the world, the richest the world has ever known. We throw out food each day that is greater than what smaller nations consume in a day. Such selfishness is so very unnecessary. But it is a sign of how people want to be put want to put their security for their future in food or in sanitation rather than God. Thus, it is for the Church to exemplify what it means to love our neighbor. Christians must not hoard and repent if any of us is guilty of doing so. Christians are to call on our neighbors. We are to allow other people to go before us at the market. We are to ration when we can. We are to use only what is necessary and trust God, for He is the one who gives us our daily bread. Of course, there are many other things for a prophet to say during times like these, but the three I have mentioned are sufficient enough to show why prophecy is to be the foremost gift to be pursued, for it is the very practice of love within the church. It is what the church and the unbelieving world needs. This then brings us to the second point I wish to make about the gift of prophecy. And that is the need for prophets. I understand that there are plenty of people who are preaching in America today, and so it may seem like we have enough prophets. But there are few prophets, preachers, who are preaching the Word of God boldly and unapologetically. There are men and women who preach politics, usually liberal politics Who insists that to truly love someone, you must allow them to be comfortable in their lifestyle, no matter if their lifestyle is offensive to God. You have preachers who use the name of Jesus, having no faith in the actual Jesus, and most certainly not believing what the gospel says Jesus. Christian churches, or what used to be Christian churches, are being used to lump the Christian faith with all other religions so that all faiths and all gods are indistinguishable. Just how the devil likes it. And there are preachers who insist that the gospel is all about health and wealth in this life. They too are like Job's companions as they project the Christian life as obtaining earthly wealth and earthly influence. while their followers send them see faith money because God wants these preachers to be on the top of the wealth pyramid. These preachers are nothing more than pyramid scheme salesmen whose product is Jesus but Jesus light. Such preachers have not had much to say during these days, if you've noticed. They can't name and claim healing for a virus to be gone. So they have to wait for a healthier time for people to tune in again. Along these same lines, unfortunately, there are also preachers who tout a new idea Something never revealed about Jesus before, but now only to them. The character of these false prophets is no more holy than that of the health and wealth preachers. And then there are preachers who are scared when prophesying. They don't want to offend. They don't want to lose their job. They want to be liked, and so they prophesy what is safe. But the church doesn't need safe preaching. The unbelieving world doesn't need scared preachers. And neither believers nor unbelievers need unbelieving preachers. Neither believers nor unbelievers need the lie of health and wealth preaching. Neither believers nor unbelievers need a new revelation when they cannot understand the basic revelation of Jesus being God and man. Instead, the believing and unbelieving world need men to prophesy the truth God has gifted humanity in the Holy Scriptures. And it is to be done aggressively and forthrightly, with faith that God's word feeds the believer and converts the unbeliever. Remember that the gift of prophecy, the gift of speaking forth the words of God into the lives of people, is a gift of love in action. Recall how Proverbs teaches that if a parent withholds discipline from a child, He or she or both are actually hating the child. They are withholding self-discipline the child needs. And when a parent disciplines a child, he or she or both are practicing love in the same way. When the word of God is prophesied for the hearing of believers and unbelievers, so that they can be in right relationship with God, they are practicing love. To withhold God's word from people who are made in his image is actually to hate. I know that preachers who fail to fully preach God's word don't feel they are hating and would never accept that description, but if you have a truth you are unwilling to share that will save someone From suffering in sin and eternal death, then hating is an appropriate description So who will speak as Isaiah the prophet did, and say, Here am I, Lord, send me. Jesus said, we heard that in his day the fields were ripe for harvest, but the laborers were lacking. Well, they are lacking today. If what I am preaching is true, may we have an abundance of men take up the call to prophesy, which is to love the world as God does. Amen. Let us pray. Our God, we thank you for this challenge to pursue prophecy. To pursue applying your word to the current circumstances in which we live. No greater time is there. And because we thank you for this, we also want to be a people who receive it. Help us to be people who are doers of your word and not just hearers. Father, help us to live out these prophecies. In Jesus' name we pray. Amen.

sermons.title: Palm Sunday 2020
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Turn with me, if you would, to 1 Corinthians chapter 14. Because that's a bit lengthy, we will not go verse by verse this morning, but instead I will give a summation of the points that St. Paul is making. Because love has been proven to be the more excellent way, and because the Corinthian Christians need such love to overcome the many sins of selfishness that they have been practicing Paul points to the gift that best expresses agape love, and that gift is prophecy. The gift of prophecy is up against the popular gift of speaking in an unknown tongue. Evidently the gift of speaking in tongues was quite popular in Corinth for reasons that we cannot fully know. For those of you who are not aware, I have a background in regards to the gift of speaking in tongues I was part of an independent charismatic church during my late teens that insisted that every member speak in tongues as evidence of being baptized in the Holy Spirit. So I'm not speaking only from an exegetical point of view, but also from experience. I am convinced that the speaking in tongues in Scripture is referring to persons Who can speak languages of men that they themselves have not learned? This is clearly seen in Acts chapter 2 and elsewhere in the book of Acts. There is no reason for present-day Bible readers to read into Paul's letters here, for example. That somehow the gift of tongues had changed from the events in the book of Acts to the time of these Corinthian Christians into being anything else but languages of men. If it is interpreted to be anything else, like languages of angels, as some have claimed, well the burden is on them for proof. My experience taught me that the claim to speak a language of angels is an easy way to pretend that you have the gift of speaking in tongues. and then to pretend that you are able to interpret something that no one else can interpret. But I do not say that all who pretend are doing so to be deceitful Some are so very anxious to have the gift of tongues that they have convinced themselves that they have it. We should not judge their hearts. Paul's basic point is that the gift of tongues being made a priority in regards to a gift desired, a gift pursued, is not an expression of the love that he spoke about so beautifully in the previous chapter. A person who speaks in tongues edifies himself because he feels a special connection with God, and that feeling of connection only benefits him or her. An example is found of different musical instruments. If those instruments all sounded the same, being indistinguishable from one another, they would not communicate anything beautiful or useful. So it is when people speak in languages that are not understood for those listening. The next point is how useful language can be in all their distinctions But only when the language or the languages are understood by the listen the listeners. When we have problems With others who are foreign to us, it is usually because we cannot understand one another. Language barriers sustain personal barriers. One simple solution, Paul suggests, is that if anyone speaks in a tongue so that others can hear, there should be an interpretation of what was uttered so that all Christians who are gathered for worship can be edified. To speak only for the edification of the one speaking is not love practiced. The main point being that love is practiced by caring about the edification of others rather than self. An example of how tongues does not edify, and it can actually condemn, is the quote Paul gives from Isaiah 28. The point there being that the foreign language of the Assyrian invaders represented a judgment on God's people For God, as it were, is speaking to them in a foreign language, because they would not hear the truth in their own language. To know the truth in a language understood is far, far better. Words not understood keep an unbeliever in a state of unbelief. Words understood by a believer feeds his belief. Now mixed in with the various lessons on why tongues is a gift for the church I'm sorry, right? Tongues as as a gift for the church had weaknesses for the edification of the church as a whole. In there are also instructions on what is to be preferred, which is prophecy Now before we look at the benefits of prophecy, let it be understood that the gift of prophecy is not just knowing about the future. In fact, in all of Scripture, the practice of prophecy is rarely telling of an unknown future, but is instead the application of God's word in present and in future circumstances. The prophet takes God's word already revealed and applies it so that the people can understand it and then obey it. The best summary I have heard is that prophecy is bringing God's word to bear in the lives of people. An unbeliever can hear it and know it is of God and repent and believe. And a believer can hear it and know it is from God and change his or her life to better honor God. In summary, love is the more excellent way, and the best way to love is to speak forth the Word of God to those who would hear. That summary point then leads me to address primarily two things for us today. The first is that we need to hear the word of God applied to our present circumstance, which is living within this pandemic. Preachers need to prophesy regarding how we are to understand God's word and thus God's will in light of a virus that has scared us so that we remain separated from one another, and tempting others to hoard goods, so that they will not be in want while not caring about the needs of others. There are also questions that go unanswered regarding how we are to understand and then communicate God's will during a time of crisis. Simple questions such as, did God cause this viral outbreak? And is God judging the world with such an outbreak? These are on the minds of unbelievers and believers. So we must. What must the prophet utter? What must the prophet utter in times is these. Regarding questions of God's judgment and a viral outbreak, such as the one we are experiencing There is no direct word given by God to his prophets that says this particular outbreak is a judgment for these particular sins And when these particular sins are confessed and turned away from, that God will bring healing. I do not have a specific word such as that, and I don't know anyone that does. Of course, there are specific sins of our nation. And in the world that have earned God's wrath, such as people celebrating abortions, celebrating sodomy, fornication, adultery There are politicians and corporate leaders who are indeed guilty of feeding systemic hatred, of oppressing the poor. There is severe persecution of Christians in various parts of the world. These sins and others are most certainly worthy of any and all types of judgment that God wants to bring down In this life. But viral outbreaks are not new to the world. For anyone who has learned elementary human history knows of much greater outbreaks that one than the one we are experiencing. What we can clearly conclude from God's word is that suffering a pandemic is a result of living in a cursed world. The Bible tells us that because of the sin of Adam and Eve, the world is cursed. Fires, floods, earthquakes, tornadoes, famines, hurricanes, pestilence. And other types of disasters are caused by living in a world that suffers in death because the wages of sin is death. And don't forget how human beings contribute to fires and floods and other disasters. Careless people start forest fires and destroy acres of good timber, kill habitats for animals, and destroy people's homes. Floods occur because people build cities below sea level. And then blame God when those cities flood. And pestilence occurs because people eat and sell unclean animals that can infect a few and then infect many. What we can know from God's word is that anytime there is a fear for loss of life, anytime something happens that causes people to face their mortality God uses it to bring people to repentance. Remember from Luke chapter 13 where Jesus is questioned about an incident that is not recorded in history but is consistent with the behavior of Pontius Pilate, who likely tortured rebellious Galileans by killing them on the floor of the temple, thus desecrating the temple The people wondered what sins were committed by the victims to deserve such a fate. Such questions are similar to the ones referenced earlier as people want to know how dirty are God's hands when tragedy strikes. Jesus' answer is so insightful because he doubles down with another example. He mentions an accident where a tower in a nearby city to Old Jerusalem fell and killed 18 people. In such instances, we are not to conclude, Jesus taught, that those who suffered were worthy of such an accident. Such was the foolish logic of Job's companions. Instead, we are to understand that no one is more or less a sinner in a sense that some deserve to die by tragedy. But instead, we are all sinners, and whenever we are faced with our mortality, we are to take it as an opportunity to repent of our sins and believe on the Lord Jesus Christ. So that we can avoid the ultimate tragedy, which is hellfire. That is always the message of a prophet Repent and believe on the Lord Jesus Christ and be saved. What else should a prophet be saying in times like these? Besides the call to repentance and believe in Jesus, the prophet must call God's people to fear not. Because Jesus has overcome sin and death, we are not to fear sickness, disaster, even death For the Christian, to die is gain, to live is Christ. Jesus promised that he would never leave his people He is with each of us as we go through this trial, reminding us that his perfect love casts out fear, and that the only one to fear is the Heavenly Father, and the Father loves us so That he takes us under his mighty wing to be our shelter, protecting us from the enemy, even the enemy of pestilence. Besides the call to repentance and then the call to fear not, the prophet must speak of the second greatest law, which is to love thy neighbor as thyself. Clear evidence is before us regarding how far our culture has fallen away from the Christian ethic. that at one time made people in towns and counties in America united in caring about one another. The hoarding that has been occurring is disgraceful, as it is not only rejecting loving thy neighbor, but makes a clear statement In favor of the demise of one's neighbor, for we are leaving some people to fend for themselves with no means to do so. What makes the hoarding even more alarming is how unnecessary it all is. We are the richest nation in the world, the richest the world has ever known. We throw out food each day that is greater than what smaller nations consume in a day. Such selfishness is so very unnecessary. But it is a sign of how people want to be put want to put their security for their future in food or in sanitation rather than God. Thus, it is for the Church to exemplify what it means to love our neighbor. Christians must not hoard and repent if any of us is guilty of doing so. Christians are to call on our neighbors. We are to allow other people to go before us at the market. We are to ration when we can. We are to use only what is necessary and trust God, for He is the one who gives us our daily bread. Of course, there are many other things for a prophet to say during times like these, but the three I have mentioned are sufficient enough to show why prophecy is to be the foremost gift to be pursued, for it is the very practice of love within the church. It is what the church and the unbelieving world needs. This then brings us to the second point I wish to make about the gift of prophecy. And that is the need for prophets. I understand that there are plenty of people who are preaching in America today, and so it may seem like we have enough prophets. But there are few prophets, preachers, who are preaching the Word of God boldly and unapologetically. There are men and women who preach politics, usually liberal politics Who insists that to truly love someone, you must allow them to be comfortable in their lifestyle, no matter if their lifestyle is offensive to God. You have preachers who use the name of Jesus, having no faith in the actual Jesus, and most certainly not believing what the gospel says Jesus. Christian churches, or what used to be Christian churches, are being used to lump the Christian faith with all other religions so that all faiths and all gods are indistinguishable. Just how the devil likes it. And there are preachers who insist that the gospel is all about health and wealth in this life. They too are like Job's companions as they project the Christian life as obtaining earthly wealth and earthly influence. while their followers send them see faith money because God wants these preachers to be on the top of the wealth pyramid. These preachers are nothing more than pyramid scheme salesmen whose product is Jesus but Jesus light. Such preachers have not had much to say during these days, if you've noticed. And it is to be done aggressively and forthrightly, with faith that God's word feeds the believer and converts the unbeliever. Remember that the gift of prophecy, the gift of speaking forth the words of God into the lives of people, is a gift of love in action. Recall how Proverbs teaches that if a parent withholds discipline from a child, He or she or both are actually hating the child. They are withholding self-discipline the child needs. And when a parent disciplines a child, he or she or both are practicing love in the same way.
