The Greek text can be translated that even if any obey not the word, as though in some cases at least it might be expected that husband and wife would have both then converted together. Using the phrase the word, we have a familiar collective expression of the whole doctrine of the gospel. The word was Jesus, and all that was spoken about him was the gospel. The Greek verb to obey not implies a positive Antagonism rather than a mere absence of belief or obedience. And this means that the husband might not only have not believed, but he didn't like the faith Next is the phrase, may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives Now the Greek word this time for word has no article before it, so it's referring to being without speech, without a word being uttered. It is the silent preaching of conduct is what the apostle relied on as believing it to be the most effective instrument of conversion than, let's say, an argument or a debate. The verb be won literally means to be gained over. And we have the same word used in 1 Corinthians 9 and from the teaching of our Lord. And Peter might have been A little impressed by that reference in Matthew 18 where it talks about a sinner being won over to repentance. Verse 2. Because the unbelieving husband will be jealous and watch to see if his wife does what what his wife does while embracing this religion that he thinks is foolish. It is the hope that he can conclude in the end that Jesus must be the Messiah, for his wife could not have been so chaste if he wasn't. And the adjective chaste is here to be taken in a larger sense. It is the same which enters into the verb translated purify or purity. It is implied that this fear of the husband has been an incentive for a sweet virtue to be revealed in the wife It is like saying that she will so timidly be so timidly pure as to be effective upon his conscience. Verse 3. Two things are to be noted about the advice given in this verse. First, it is not intended directly as a corrective of vanity St. Peter is not warning them to beware of the love of dress, although the three words used here, plating, wearing, or literally mean putting around oneself or putting on And it might be referring a little bit to the elaborate way in which dressing might take a bit too much time But the main thought is, how are the husbands to be attracted to the faith? Well, not, says St. Peter, by external prettiness of adornment, but by inward graces. Second, the apostle is not forbidding the use of gold or other precious ornaments on a woman But that such adorning is not in the place of what should be most attractive to the unbelieving husband. Hence verse 4, the hidden is here equivalent to the inward person, and and Paul uses that in Romans 7. And first or 2 Corinthians 4 and in the in the letter to the Ephesians, this idea of that we have a hidden life in Christ. It's in the heart. It's where God is fashioning us to the likeness of Christ, forming us, the new person, which is renewed in the knowledge and image of Christ. That's what our focus is to be. This is hidden. It does not display itself like those conspicuous ornaments that he mentions in verse 3. To win her husband to Christ, her character is to be of a meek and quiet spirit. And such ornamentation is incorruptible, not like those corruptible things that adorn the outer person. The meek spirit, this meek spirit described, does not flash into anger Does not answer back, but instead takes harsh words gently and humbly The quiet spirit is calm and tranquil, peaceful in itself. It spreads peace around. And then he says, which is in the sight of God a great price. The adjective great price, interestingly, is also used in Mark chapter 14, where Mary anoints Jesus with an ointment, that of great price. Outward adornments are costly in the sight of the world. The meek and quiet spirit is precious in the sight of God. Verse five. It is obvious from the special instance given in the next verse that the apostle has in his mind exclusively the saintly wives and mothers of the Old Testament. He says such women trusted God, and we more accurately could say they hoped in God, the idea of trust. Is of course not far removed from hope. He then says that they were hopeful while being in subjection unto their husbands. And we see a repetition of this verb submit. It's used by Peter twice before this, and perhaps should be noted as a key note of the epistle itself. All of us who follow Christ must live submissively. Verse six Sarah, wife of Abraham, is the given example. You remember that her name was changed from Sarai to Sarah. For God had breathed his Yah name into her, and she was prophesied to be a mother of kings. And even that being true, she obeyed Abraham. And this is spoken in praise of her obedience. Calling Abraham Lord was not merely a compliment from her to him, but was the reality of her heart, thereby acknowledging his authority over her own subjection. Peter next says to all wives, whose daughters you are, not only according to the flesh, but spiritually according to the promise. By imitation of Sarah and her faith and her holiness, Christian wives can be successors as long as you do well by following her good works, which was submission. To not be afraid with any terror is to do your duty with a resolute mind and to keep from that which is contrary to your faith. Or as long as you subject yourself to your husband willingly, cheerfully, without fear of being taken advantage of, or fear of being ridiculed by those who claim that they are free from their husbands. When we hear instructions from Holy Scripture that tell us not to be conformed to this world. And that we are not to love this world, and for us to set our affections on things above rather than things of this world, and that friendship with the world is is being an enemy of God. Perhaps there is no better or more obvious way to sperm this world than for a Christian to live a life of submission. Because everything that happens in our lives is providential, meaning that God is working in our lives for the good, and the good is establishing his kingdom on earth You and I love it when God allows for us to see his providence at work. Well, just before I started studying this passage about submission of women to their husbands Bobby Lynn and I took a long car ride, and during that ride, she read to me from a book that she was enjoying, titled You are not enough, and that is okay. The author is a young woman by the name of Ali Beth Stucky. In an interview about her book, Ali Beth states that her audience is young women, and her concern is for what she has labeled trendy narcissism. She describes trendy narcissism as a belief in self that says to every woman that you are sufficient within yourself, having the ability to have internally Joy and finding that joy internally. The first step then is to love yourself and come to the realization of just how awesome you are Which then allows a young woman to find her own truth. The base premise of this trendy narcissism is that you are the most important person in your life. And this leads to allowing a young woman to become literally her own God. Evidently the message of self-love and self-determinism regarding truth is presently trending on social media. It is a message that is widespread, and we can understand why it is trending For when we are told that thinking of yourself first and last, well, that's a virtue now. Well, we already do that quite easily. If someone is going to tell us that to do so is to be a good person, then our ears are tickled and our consciences are muffled. The book Bobby Lynn is reading intersects for me with a book I recently finished titled Live Not by Lies. It's by Rod Durrer. It is Drewer's premise that there are very similar signposts of warnings that are presently trending in the United States and the West in general that are frightfully similar To pre-communist Russia. And the alarmists that Drewer uses to highlight his concerns are former citizens of the Soviet Union who escaped the Soviet bloc. countries never imagining that they would see the same politics developing in the United States They are scared, and Drewer wants us to be warned and then to do something about it. One of the signpost concern concern identified by Drewer is The ideal of groupthink, and the speed at which groupthink occurs, being aided by the internet and social media. Group think goes along with group identity, which tells us that we are not individuals who are working out our lives to the best that we are able. but that we are to identify with the groups who are genetically like us. And we are to be seen as no different than our group. i. e. , all blacks think alike, all whites think alike, all Latinos think alike, etc. And then once we have been forced into our group, We then need to be reformed to thinking as our governing authorities would have us think, while throwing out all the prejudice that comes with our group. Once we have been brought into a larger group, think that's trendy, we are only one step away from totalitarianism. And as theologians, and you and I are you're a Christian, you are a theologian, it gets interesting, it gets fascinating, I believe, for us. First, there is a group of young women, imagine, who all think alike because they have embraced the worldview of self-love, self-determination, self-truth. Once that group is formed, then they can be guided by a larger group think that starts to believe that class disparities are the root cause of all suffering in the world This conclusion allows them to listen to leaders who believe the government can get rid of class disparities and bring everyone under one large roof of cooperation and prosperity. Now, in truth, as history has shown, there will be no cooperation, but only subjugation, where all citizens submit to the state. As we step back and look at such a scenario, we can see that the devil is up to his old tricks. In fact, he doesn't even vary from what he did to Adam and Eve. He tells us we are oppressed and that we don't get to have the freedoms and rights that we deserve. We don't get to be as God is. That is what he told Eve. And that is what he tells every person who doesn't like their current position in life And once he gets you to go down a road he says will lead to your freedom and your rights realized, he next pulls the old switcheroo. And you find yourself merely having traded one bondage for another. Only the next one is much, much tighter. That is what he does to women who balk at St. Peter's teaching on wives submitting to their husbands. For anyone who has tempted to balk at such teaching, concluding that it is not addressing modern issues and thus is a teaching that time has passed by I implore you to examine St. Peter's main point in bringing up the subject at all. The scenario is a woman Who has become a Christian and her husband has not. And he may even see the Christian faith as an enemy. If a wife finds herself in such a situation, she can have hope that her husband will be converted to the Christian faith. And she has been given a pathway for that to happen, which is her submitting to her husband, so that he does not see the Christian faith as an enemy. And so that he concludes that Jesus, the Jesus that she serves, must be the Messiah because a woman A woman would not be so chaste and caring if Jesus were not the Messiah. Thus, the end goal is the eternal salvation of the husband. And then the salvation of the household, and then to the glory of God. And we can imagine even further that a family Who are all believing on the Lord Jesus Christ and who serve Him faithfully, that they will be a witness to the truth of the gospel, and thus the truth of Jesus as the Messiah And then other families watching them and observing them and seeing that they truly believe that they too would come to a to the faith And thus the belief spreads. And you can see then a whole town that believes on the Lord Jesus Christ. First a wife, then a husband, then a family, then a town, then a nation, then a world? Is that too wild to imagine? Maybe that is the providence of God. I plan to state an argument next about the importance of wives submitting to their own husbands with the point that well you're gonna have to submit to someone. Just like our young girl scenario, who thought they were not submitting to anyone but self until Group fate lured them into submitting to a totalitarian state. And once again we can hear Bob Dylan singing in the background, well, you gotta serve somebody. Might be the devil, it might be the Lord, but you gotta serve somebody But that argument fell flat as I saw the outline. It was rather simplistic. Wives submit to your husbands because, well, that's the best scenario you're going to get in life. There is not a lot of hope in such an argument. A better argument to encourage wives to be submissive toward their own husbands is the freedom We don't often hear that. Freedom and submission. But the freedom we find in submission. Beloved, we are made for submission. Every human being submits to something or someone. The thing might be an ideology or a desire. The someone may be a political leader, a guru, a boss, or something else. As Christians, we first and foremost submit to the Lord Jesus Christ. And we have no better example of living a submissive life than Jesus Himself You remember that it was Jesus that testified that he does not do anything unless the Father wills it. The submission of Jesus took him to the cross where he died and then was buried and then was set free as no other man has been set free. Thus, true freedom is found submitting to Jesus Christ. And finally, submitting the act of humbling oneself to the authority placed over us Well, it's not effectual. It has no value if it is done only for the submission itself. It must be done in faith. In faith, believing that God will use it to build his kingdom. And Sarah is the example, and so it is Sarah to whom we turn. Abraham not only lied by saying Sarah was not his wife, he did it twice. And each time it was done to protect himself, not his bride, himself. Abraham, we remember, was a type of Jesus, but but only a type. He was weak in certain ways, especially when it came to the sin of self-preservation. But Sarah went along with him and did so both times. To do so, she had to have faith that God would make up for the deficiencies of her husband. Every woman has had to watch her husband make a decision that seems foolish or at least a mistake. If any wife wishes to be a daughter of Sarah, she should say her peace, for she is the helpmeet. That's what she was created to be. She's designed to aid her husband, to be by his side, to help him If a husband does not look to his wife for said help, he is indeed the foolish one. But after she shares her peace, she must trust in God that he will guide her husband. She must have faith that God will work all things to the good for those who love him. That is his promise for all of us. To submit. To submit is to have the mind of Christ Jesus. God takes care of the rest. Let us pray. Now God, we thank you for this standard, and we know how difficult it is in this day especially to live up to it. But we see your word, we believe it to be true, and so we entrust ourselves to it. May all wives take the challenge on personally to submit to their husbands. And may all husbands live lives that are worthy of it. We pray this in Jesus' name. Amen

sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: Name of the Father, of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. No, you didn't hear incorrectly. The reader of our first lesson didn't get it wrong. I didn't send out the wrong passage to our secretary, Kimberly. Actually, I did. She had text me and asked me, Are you sure about this verse? And I said, Oh yeah, I'm sure. No, I sent her the wrong verse. It's verse 7 of chapter 3, but it's just one verse. It is correct that this sermon is based on looking at just one verse. But the verse is quite full, and it forces us to look at a larger issue, which is the Christian family. So let us look at 1 Peter chapter 3, verse 7. Technically, technically first. Verse 7. The term, as it begins likewise, refers to the subject of submission. This is in sync with St. Paul. Who said for Christians to submit to one another, and then went on to describe how husbands are to submit to wives and wives to husbands, but to do so differently. Thus, submission is not at all one-sided, though the husband's submission to the wife will be of a different kind than of the wife to the husband. In order to understand this more difficult passage, we must remember what St. Peter's objective is all throughout these instructions of chapter 3. It was to commend Christianity to jealous onlookers. Last week we noted that a wife's behavior toward her unbelieving husband Has the goal of convincing him that Jesus is the Messiah. This verse may be a reference, may be a reference to help men who have unbelieving wives. To see the faith in their husbands and thus they too would want to become a Christian A believing husband and an unbelieving wife was more rare than the reversal, but it did and does happen. And so the first thing is that believing husbands are to, he says, dwell with their wives. Which is to say, not divorce them, nor cease their conjugal cohabitation with them, for such would not be a witness to the love and patience of the Savior. The phrase with understanding is like an adverb, such as scientifically or intelligently. It means that the husband is to study, to enter into the whole information of the case, to take everything into account about his wife. Husband and wife will not continue together happily without pains taken to understand their particular situation. What the husband is to understand is his wife's strengths and weaknesses compared to his. The honor he gives to her is his means. This is the way a man, a husband, submits. And he is to do so, keeping in mind that she is a weaker vessel. This explains the saying, according to knowledge, the thing which the husband is to specially understand and take into account is that he is dealing with a person who has less strength Than himself. The whole of chivalry is in these words. The weakness here ascribed to the female sex is primarily that of the body Though it may perhaps indicate a frailty in other respects as well. And he says, giving honor. And the word forgiving implies rendering someone a portion of what is due them. They are owed it And what is here called honor is not to be understood only for a wife's daily needs, as some have said, nor is the wife only to be honored by giving uh consulted in affair giving opportunity to consult in affairs of everyday life, put in charge of some area of the household Instead, the honor to be accorded to the wife is as a joint heir of the grace of life. It is that chaste respect for which the wife is meant in prayer, in the prayer book at the giving of rings, some of you will remember this part of the service, where the man says, With my body I thee worship. It means that the husband must not dare to take any liberties with his wife. It would not be likely the Christian husband would prove his Christian religion to his unbelieving wife if She found that he took a shallow view of their intimate life. And as being heirs together of the grace of life, the meaning is is quite full for in one case deference is paid to the wife on the grounds of her possessing a joint dignity with the husband. And in another case on the grounds that the husband does not possess his dignity unless he is co-jointly joined to his wife. That dignity which they cojointly inherit, they possess as a gift from God. It's called the grace of life. This is generally interpreted to mean everlasting life Understandably, life is often used in the New Testament to mean eternal life. And then he finishes the point with that your prayers be not hindered. The prayers are the husbands' prayers alone, not necessarily their prayers with their wives as jointly praying. It is easy to imagine A man having trouble praying to the Lord with his conscience being seared, that conscience seared because he has not been giving honor to his wife, and thus his prayers are clogged. Peter, again, is likely concerned that these prayers are for his wife to come to the faith. What I am called to underline and emphasize for us from this verse Is the underlying and clearly implied power that is unleashed when a man is a good husband and a good father But first, let us hear some alarming numbers. In a book titled Mama Bear Apologetics, specifically from Chapter 1. Writers Hilary Ferrer and Julie Luce state, the problem within the Christian evangelical church today is a youth exodus. Hear the following. This is a quote from the book. The youth exodus refers to the percentage of Christian youth who stop attending church. This includes those who go on to declare themselves atheists, agnostics, or more recently, checking off the title none, as in no religious affiliation. This exodus has been widely researched, documented, and discussed, but in many Christian circles it is also widely ignored. And while there are some varying opinions and what can look like contradictory statistics, The bottom line is that it is real and it is bad. And now it's becoming more ramp. among young people prior to entering college, which used to be the exit ramp. Here's another quote. Most studies indicate that 45 to 48 percent of youth leave church after their freshman year in college and never return. Never. The percentages vary based on denomination, but the problem is the same. David Kinneman found that age after age 15, almost 60% of young Christians had disconnected from their church, 60%. More than half, 54% of high school students attend church, but once they hit college, the problem gets worse Frequent attendance drops from 54% in high school to 25% in college. Over half. Non-attendance goes up from 20% in high school to 38% in college. In a 2006 Barna study, 61% of 20-somethings who had attended church as teens were no longer spiritually engaged. 61%. One study showed that 70% of teens who attended youth group stopped attending church within two years of their high school graduation. 70%. But the problem isn't only young people leaving the church, for even those who stay are likely disengaged, not paying attention. Here is another quote. In three independent surveys conducted by Josh McDowell, the Barna Group, and researcher Mike Nappa. It was discovered that among self-proclaimed Christian teens, teens who called themselves Christian, 41% were uncertain whether Jesus was physically resurrected. That's the basis of all of Christianity. Sixty-three percent didn't believe Jesus to be the son of the one true God. Sixty-three percent 44 believed the Bible to be just one of many authority voices about Jesus. What's another authority? 33 believe that Jesus is not the only way to heaven. One-third. Only 5% studied the Bible daily, down from 8% in 1991. A growing majority believe the Holy Spirit is only a symbol of God's presence or power rather than a person of the Trinity. 60% are uncertain, unsettled or confused about whether the Bible can be trusted. 60% Seventy percent express persistent, measurable doubts that the bot about what the Bible says about Jesus. Seventy percent. Most certainly, local and denominational churches are to be criticized for these statistics. But the most important critique is with the parents. And with the one responsible for the teaching in the home, at least responsible in seeing that it gets done, is the Father. If we were to describe each family as a ship, then the captain would be the father. And anytime a ship runs aground, it is the captain who is responsible. Notice, please, that I did not say the Father is always at fault. I said he is responsible, responsible to God. The captain may have put the first mate in charge, and it may have been the poor decision of the first mate that caused the ship to run aground, but the captain is still responsible. Several years ago, I was trying to help a particular father see his responsibility in the troubles of his family. And he pushed back at me, claiming that with my logic, I make God responsible for the sin of mankind. What he failed to see is that God did take full responsibility for the sin of mankind by sending his only begotten Son. We learn then from God that there is power in fathers taking full responsibility and then doing something about it. So, what are we to do about our children walking away from the faith? What are we to do with our children knowing little of the faith to even believing what is heretical? And what are we to do about the ever-rising antagonism against the Christian faith as Christians are publicly maligned as bigoted and ignorant, having fears of every sexual proclivity? Well the first place to do, the first place to start is to do as St. Peter instructs. Husbands need to begin to take responsibility for the spiritual health of their family by giving honor to their wives. Each husband is to examine his wife in terms of what her needs are and provide for those needs. And while providing for those needs, most notably providing for her physical protection The wife as a weaker vessel needs to feel safe, and that safe feeling must be provided by the husband. Yes, I am aware that there are marriages that find the woman being stronger and more physically capable of protecting herself in a braver manner than her husband. But again, exceptions don't break the rule. In most situations, over 99% of situations, of a husband-and-wife relationship, the wife is the weaker vessel deserving of protection by her husband. And this is why spouse abuse is so heinous, for it is contrary to one of the most important roles a husband is to play in the home. And to treat a wife as a weaker vessel needing protection goes against the spirit of this age that tries to ignore the differences between men and women. A recent interviewer on the campus of the University of Washington asked a number of students if they thought there was a difference between men and women. And the answers received are disheartening. The students use phrases like gender fluidity, choosing one's gender, gender identity. One student claimed that the differences between men and women are only in the mind, rather than scientifically or biologically. According to another student, the differences between men and women are actually a social construct as opposed to being based on observable realities or historical realities. Scientifically, it has been measured that boys and girls are relatively the same, both in body structure and in mental stability, until puberty kicks in. When boys receive an increase of testosterone, they tend to grow larger physically compared to their female peers, and especially larger in the upper body. Interestingly, statistics reveal that in altercations that occur in marriages, physical altercations, it is more likely for the wife to attack the husband. Researchers believe this is the case because a woman knows that she will not do much harm to her husband as she is aware that she does not pose a physical threat to him as he does to her. Because the consequences of the wife attacking the husband are limited, she feels freer to act out in an aggressive manner. In terms of mental stability, women after puberty have greater anxiety than men, and researchers believe this is the case because women feel more vulnerable physically and sexually. Physically because of the size and strength deficit, and sexually because the consequences of the sexual act are negatively much greater for the woman than it is for the man. And finally, a woman's anxiety is even more heightened when she has a child. Now she and the child are vulnerable and she has an innate feeling of responsibility to protect the child even with her physical deficit as compared to men It is then for husbands to be aware of these deficits in their wives and make up for them whenever and however possible. And this is where the power of taking responsibility is seen, for when children see their father caring for their mother in a protective manner, there is Great security in knowing that mom and dad are committed to being with one another. And therefore the child can feel safe because the family unit is secure. But also the child gets a glimpse of God as he sees his father take responsibility for the marriage, as he does his best to secure his wife That is what God does through Jesus, as Jesus cares for his bride, the church. If you have received marital counseling from me, you will remember that I tell every couple to treat their relationship as the most important relationship in the home Don't make the children the central focus of the family. If you have done so, repent of it and change. Make the marriage, the relationship between a husband and wife, the most important relationship, and watch the children mature within that secure environment. It is St. Paul who extends teachings about husbands and wives, and we learn from St. Peter himself that he is very much aware of what St. Paul has written. And when we go to St. Paul, we hear him teaching of the mystery that a husband and wife reveal. For they are types, they are shadows of the relationship that Jesus has with his church, his bride. Therefore, there is something mysteriously hidden and thus mysteriously learned when a wife submits to her husband as submitting to Christ. And when the husband loves his wife in the same manner that Christ loves his church, the children are the benefactors of the mysterious truths, for they get a slight peak. into the heavenly realities that will be realized after Jesus returns and all things become new And this leads us to addressing how children fit into the teachings here by St. Peter and by St. Paul. Peter does not address the subject of children because his focus is on how a believing spouse is to minister to an unbelieving spouse so that the household becomes all believing. But Paul addresses relationships from parents to children and children to parents. And first he reminds children to submit to their parents based on the principle of the fifth commandment. Which you remember is honor your father and mother. And Paul rightly points out that it is the first commandment given that includes a promise, and that promise is long and prosperous life. Beloved, the good life begins by honoring those who have the greatest authority over you, for we are to understand that to honor our parents is to honor God. How we learn to honor our parents is going to play a major role on how we learn to honor God as we get older. Now this is followed by Paul with the instruction for fathers not to provoke their children to wrath. This is necessary, for it is a tendency of a father to be too harsh on his child, and harshness That does not include asking for forgiveness and showing humility when wrong can tempt a child toward bitterness. It is one thing to have high standards for a child, nothing wrong with that. It is another to browbeat the child when he or she doesn't live up to those standards. Such is provoking a child to wrath. It's damaging to a child and possibly for the rest of his life. Instead, a father is to train a child with the Word of God as the direct authority, not the father, the Word of God. And such training is intentional. It consists of much more than dropping a child off for Sunday school or for youth group. It must be engaging the child about the faith and about how to apply the faith to everyday life. And most importantly, it is living out the faith yourself, which doesn't mean you are perfect, but it does mean that you live a life of confession and repentance. Nothing chases a child away from the faith more, this I heartily believe, than to see a hypocritical father. He is not a hypocrite who fails to live out his faith each day. That's all of us. The hypocrite is the one who does not confess his failure. I hope that you have not heard this sermon as a how-to speech. I hate those And I hope you have heard a better than average sermon on St. Valentine's Day. As I mention Inherent in this instruction for husbands to better treat their wives is the final goal of winning an unbelieving spouse to follow Jesus Christ and to receive a heavenly reward. That is what we want for our children as well, and our grandchildren and our great-grandchildren, and on and on and on until Jesus returns. I have said this before. There is mixed rejoicing in heaven when a sinner walks into the church while a covenant child walks out. And that begins with cultivating our marriages. It is not a cliche to say that it all begins in the home. Let us pray. Our God, no doubt there is a standard here that all of us need to strive more toward. And for those of us who are failing, we seek your forgiveness. And we ask you to help us. Most importantly, we want to care for our wives. We want them to believe in you. And then we want our children, all of them, to believe in you so that eternity is theirs in your place in heaven For this we ask, for this we work, for this we have faith in Jesus' name. Amen.

sermons.title: Christians Needing One Another
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. Turn in your Bibles, if you would, to 1 Peter chapter 3, picking up at verse 8. 1 Peter 3, verses 8 through 12. Context. Saint Peter has addressed the family and given special instructions to husbands as leaders of their homes. And next, in our chosen section of this epistle, he turns to the congregation, the people of God as a whole. The word finally indicates that he has been addressing issues related to how we Christians treat one another. First, we examine and adjust our behavior in the home, and then we examine and adjust within the church as a whole. Our first instruction is to be of one mind. Referring to the mind recalls a part of the instruction of Jesus who told us To love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, soul, and mind. How we think upon God is very, very important. And what are we to be of one mind about? The simple answer is what we know about God. There are certain groups of Christians who are well-meaning, I have no doubt, who insist that what they know about God can be summarized by merely knowing Jesus. These Christian groups proudly proclaim that they have no creed but only Jesus. No creed but Christ, they say. It appears to them that such a slogan is a necessary protest against the organization of the Christian religion, as if the creeds are a result of aggressive administration policies. But when Jesus told us that he would send the Holy Spirit, and that he, the Holy Spirit, would come and guide us to all truth. When he said, you, guide you to all truth, it is necessary within our English translations to understand the word you to be plural. As would be stated in the South, He, the Holy Spirit, will guide you all unto all truth. We take the you all to be the church, the body of Christ, the entire people of God. And when we know our church history, we remember that the church was forced to make certain claims about Jesus because Of false teachers who tried to lure various Christian bodies to have not one mind of Christ, but several minds of God. We then conclude that the prophecy of Jesus, that the Holy Spirit would guide us, the Church, into truth, was fulfilled by what is now summarized in the creeds. And be assured, beloved, the creeds simply summarize the important, consistent teachings of the Bible regarding who is Jesus. While our brethren insist on no creed but Christ, someone at some time is going to ask, but who is Christ? And it is most appropriate to say he is one God, and yet he was born of the Virgin Mary. Suffered under Pontius Pilate. He was crucified, dead, and buried. He descended into hell. The third day he rose again and ascended into heaven. Only he shall return again to judge both the living and the dead. That is who Jesus is. And if you wonder whether he was always Jesus, as in being unique, From the Heavenly Father, and yet one with the Heavenly Father and the Holy Spirit, we have the Nicene Creed that says that he is very God, a very God, begotten, not made, being of one substance with the Father. Confessing such creeds are aids to help us be of one mind. Being of one mind then also has a look about it. It has evidence to it, which is to have compassion, he says, to one another. To have compassion on one another is to love one another as brothers To love his brothers is to be tender-hearted and courteous. This makes Peter's instruction very similar to St. Paul's words about love in 1 Corinthians chapter 13. You will recall such a standard of love seems almost unattainable because of how pure, how flawless it is And yet it is the standard for all of us to achieve, even though we fail to reach it in every relationship we have It would be the devil who would have us forget or lower such standards because of how difficult they are to achieve. And yet God says, no. The standard of love remains. To be tender-hearted is to be sympathizing and compassionate, having similar feelings or being mutually commiserative. Well, what does that look like? Well, if you are in a conversation where the person is telling a story, and that causes you to think about your own story, and To look forward to sharing that story even before the friend is finished, actually not even really listening to the person, you have not practiced being tender-hearted. Being tender-hearted is to enter into the story of your friend and work to feel what they felt and are presently feeling It is to practice dying to self by identifying with the pain or joy of a brother or sister in Christ. To be courteous is to be humble, which is to be lowly of mind, even modest about self. It is the opposite of self-seeking, meaning it is to seek the needs of others first. Thus, we are instructed not to ask a question similar to, well, what's in this for me? But instead to concern ourselves with what can I be to others? And what can I be to others that would most be helpful to their holiness? That's unusual thinking. The epitome of our tender-hearted and courteous ways is to be forgiving. Which is first described as not returning evil for evil. Returning evil for evil is too easy to do. It is not difficult to return to a wrongdoer what they wrongly have done to us and think that it's justice. God has refined, redefined justice for the Christian as we now see it as fulfilled in Jesus. Jesus was judge, jury, and executioner as he laid down his own life for the sins of all. Thus our justice is Jesus, and that means we return evil and reviling with blessing. As Christians, our end goal is not earthly justice, but eternal justice, where we can be confident God will reward the faithful while he separates the sheep from the goats. Verses ten through twelve are believed to be a poetic, perhaps even a hymn of sorts, that summarized what loving one another in the church is understood to be. When speaking to one another, we are to control our tongues while making it a priority to speak the truth. We are to be active in turning away from sin and purposefully seeking to do good where it is possible. Whether peace is possible or not, we are to pursue it. The overall purpose of living by the standard of God's love and pursuing righteousness is so that we are pleasing to God. Not pleasing in a finished condition, but pleasing in what we are pursuing, in what we are confessing, and what we are turning away from. I believe these verses are particularly important to us because of the times in which we live. Beloved, the devil is knocking at our doors, for he wants to enter our homes. And he wants to sell his goods to us, and his goods are not good. The devil knocks to sell us the power of positive thinking. Many megachurches are falling for this way of approaching the faith, treating sermons as TED Talks or a Tony Robbins seminar. The focus is on being your best self and thinking good thoughts for the sake of good outcomes. And good outcomes are always making more money. Buying more goods. And such is essentially setting our affection our affection on things of this earth, which Jesus explicitly told us not to do This positive thinking includes how you view yourself. It is the coach speak that encourages you to say, I'm good enough, I'm smart enough, and doggone at people like me. But the Bible says the opposite. You are not good enough. In fact, you are a dirty, rotten sinner. You are not smart enough, for if left to yourself, you would deny God and worship the earth. And people actually don't like you, but mostly pretend to in order to use you to their end goals. Am I being too negative? No. Only painfully honest. The only love you need is the love of God. The devil knocks again, and this time he is selling naturalism. Naturalism says that what is in this world is all that there is. Naturalism rejects any idea of a spiritual world, and that means not believing human beings have individual spirits or souls. Naturalists reject any revelation from God and instead replace revealed truth with scientism, which is the trust in what modern science discovers and concludes. Scientism is actually not dangerous to the Christian faith until it is politically motivated. During this pandemic, science has both hurt us in its experimentation and blessed us in its discoveries. And naturalism just isn't knocking at the door of Christian homes, but is entering the back door by way of natural products that supposedly heal. The danger as I see it is not the products we use, but the lack of theological awareness that because mankind sinned, God cursed the entire earth. Thus, what is natural isn't good simply because it's natural. If we were living in the Garden of Eden, we could be confident that all things are safe and healthy and healing. But we are barred from the garden, and a very great deal of what is natural is not healthy or helpful. Besides, logic insists that what we refer to as unnatural is nothing of the sort. Everything that exists is natural. Only some natural things have been combined with other natural things that are not unnatural, but only a combination of natural things. What Christianity provides that science cannot is identifying the reality of the human soul or spirit and identifying how important the soul is to the human condition. And Christianity provides purpose to our human existence. Christianity answers the why, while science can only answer the how. Oh, there he is again. The devil is at your door again, and this time he is trying to sell moral relativism. Moral relativism insists that morality and/or ethical standards are fluid, with the insistence that absolutes in any context do not exist. But that argument refutes itself because it makes an absolute statement. Therefore, all arguments regarding morality start with an absolute, even while denying absolutes exist. The real argument is between what absolutes are you going to start with? For the Christian, it is the holy scriptures and the scriptures are at odds with our present-day culture. It must be noted because it is so common that the interpretation of the Bible doesn't change when the culture changes. The prevailing sin of Sodom and Gomorrah doesn't change to be non-hospitality of its residents because homosexuality is no longer seen as perverted. Divorce isn't now pleasing to God because the courts say that there is such a thing as no fault divorce Fornication and cohabitation is not now acceptable because it is celebrated on television comedies. Laziness, cowardice, lascivious conduct, cursing, dishonoring parents, stealing from our neighbors, being prideful or boastful is simply or simply not caring about others All of it and much more remains immoral and sinful no matter what our culture celebrates, no matter what they march to. The primary goal of moral relativism is to make us comfortable in our sin. It came out of supposed logical progression that determined that the moral laws presented in something like the Bible could not be realized or lived up to, and therefore were either not true, or we Or we are at fault for failing to live up to them. The latter conclusion that we're at fault, our sinful hearts is not going to accept. It must be concluded that they are false as a standard, and the remaining option has to be for each person to do what is right in his or her own eyes. But just how well has moral relativism served us these past decades? Consider a sociological problem that has been solved or even helped because of moral relativism. Come up with one, anyone. Are our streets cleaner? Is drug use down? Are our inner cities prosperous? Are we less prejudiced? The answer is no to all the above. Instead of abandoning the moral standards of the Bible because we continue to fail to live up to them, let us look to the Savior, who came to forgive us of our failures and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness. Let us celebrate the standards as they are and find a true and everlasting freedom that can be found in living up to God's law rather than down. And again the devil knocks at a door at your door, and this time he is selling pluralism. Not a pluralism of race or culture, but of religion. He wants us to think that all religions are the same, or that they all lead to the same God, or that they are teaching with the same amount of evidence to their validity. Not true. None of that is true. Christianity makes specific claims and insists on specific articles of belief for people to confess, and very specific outcomes for those who believe and for those who do not believe. The claim that Jesus is the Messiah and that he is also the creator of the universe and thus one with God cannot be true for me. And not for you, or true for both of us, but not true for my next door neighbor. No, it is either true for all or false for all. The devil knows this, of course, so he invents religions that look like Christianity, but are false at their foundation. Then he creates competing religions that some insist, well, they must be valid simply because of how many people are following it. He, the devil, prefers anything and everything compared to mere Christianity. Well the devil knocks again, and this time he's selling emotionalism. Oh, next again Marxism, and then progressivism, and on and on it goes. I have used the image of the devil knocking to help you see that we have a choice to help keep him out or to let him in. To keep him out requires not just moral courage of one person, but the moral courage of all of us together. We cannot battle all of these isms on our own. We need each other to stay strong To not compromise because the devil is going to keep knocking. And he is going to have new things to sell us, or new, and each of them is an attempt to draw us away from the faith And most importantly, for the devil to draw our children away from the faith. Now, as much as ever, we need to be of one mind. We need to have compassion for one another. We need to love one another by being tender-hearted and courteous. We need not return evil for evil or reviling for reviling, but instead to bless one another. A house divided truly cannot stand. We need to be encouraging to one another purposefully in the faith. Purposefully means that we think through how we can be encouraging to one another so as to keep the devil and his isms out of our hearts and our minds. The two best weapons we have to win the battle over our minds and then our souls is the Word of God and one another. From our Ephesians study, we have recently read, quote, walk as children of light. Finding what is acceptable to the Lord, having no fellowship with darkness, but rather expose them. And then speaking to one another. Speaking to one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord. Giving thanks for all things to God the Father in the name of the Lord Jesus, submitting to one another, submitting to one another in the fear of God. What a wonderful description of being a part of the body of Christ. In order to expose lies, in order to be encouraged by one another, in order to submit to one another, you have to be an active part of your local church. I heard a Christian writer interviewed recently, and the interviewer was lamenting about the restrictions on Christians to gather during the pandemic, and the Christian author responded That she actually appreciates this time because for her, it gives opportunity to see who the true believers are and who are those who are simply pretending. The true believers, not being necessarily physically present, I am not trying to make anyone feel inadequate who is not physically present in the church. But I'm arguing that all of us need to be engaged in the work of the church, which is to be an active member of the body of Christ, which is to be an encouragement to one another in whatever way you can be. The more isms our culture embraces, the more secular our culture becomes, the greater separation we are going to have with the culture, and thus greater opposition. A greater separation creates more angst within individual Christians. It tempts people to compromise in order for them not to be left out. If we love one another as we ought, no one will be left out. Let us pray. God, we ask for your help. We confess the standard is a bit high for us. But we know because of your strength, because of the Holy Spirit, we are up to the task. Father, protect us from every ism that would come against the gospel. And may our unity be increased all the more that we might help protect one another until Jesus comes. It is in his name that we pray. Amen.

sermons.title: Brought to God
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, of the Son, of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. Please turn in your Bibles to 1 Peter chapter 3. We walk through these verses for clarification. First Peter chapter 3, picking up verse 13. Verse 13 is a rhetorical question. St. Peter has given instruction on how Christians are to do good, especially to one another. Doing good is to purposefully do the right thing to one another, and it also involves avoiding doing the wrong thing. The question then in verse 13 anticipates that doing good will result in you achieving the favor of other people As opposed to creating enemies. You do good, you get friends, right? But but Jesus did good and still made enemies, requiring Peter to acknowledge the possibility That even if you do good, you may encounter people who want you to suffer. The life of Jesus proves That some people don't want other people to live righteous lives. A righteous life of one man May cause another man to feel guilty about his own life, and that guilt cannot be addressed, it can't be removed. Resulting in the desire to destroy the life of the one who makes him feel guilty We see this today in the behavior of those who no longer say live and let live, but instead insist that not only Do I get to live in whatever manner I desire? But you must never speak against how I live. In fact, we will make it a crime for you to speak against how I live. Such a spirit is the same one that tried to silence Jesus by placing him on a cross. Verse 14 addresses the possibility of suffering under someone's judgment, even for doing good or for righteousness. If such happens to any person who follows Jesus, he or she is to know that he or she is blessed. How a person is blessed while suffering is not told to us, but we are to assume That we are blessed because we identify with Jesus. And anytime you can identify with Jesus, we are blessed by association The next instruction is to not be afraid in the face of threats by persons who wish to harm us for doing good. And again, we are not told how we are not to be afraid, but only we are told to sanctify the Lord in our hearts. To sanctify is to make holy and also to set aside. Thus God is to be given a special place in our hearts. That would enable us to persevere under suffering with the belief that what we are doing for him allows us to identify with Jesus in just a small way. And anytime you can identify with Jesus, that is a good thing. Also included in sanctifying the Lord in our hearts, we are to be ready to give a reason for the hope that lies within us. The early Christians needed such instruction because of how often they were mistreated and even to the point of being murdered. It wasn't sufficient that they would die for their faith, for Peter believed that they needed to be able to tell the persecutors why they were willing to die for their faith. A qualifier in this text surprised me this week as I have not paid close attention to it before. It's the phrase, to everyone who asks you. I had assumed that if a Christian is to suffer for his or her faith, said person should go to the gallows shouting the gospel. Here the qualifier is that someone should ask before you answer. That seems to match up with Jesus' instruction to not cast our pearls before swine. The swine are those who are not seeking truth but only care to silence it. Thus it is not for us Christians to take advantage of every silence and proclaim the gospel at every opportunity. But when persecuted, only to answer those who ask. People must ask, they must seek in order to hear and find the truth. And we Christians are to speak when we are asked. Now I ha I have been excited about a book I read recently uh called Mama Bear Apologetics. I mentioned it a few weeks ago. It is a book written for mothers So as to give them tools to fight against the many isms our children will encounter that would cause our children to doubt aspects of the Christian faith. Such doubts can lead to unbelief. And these isms are no longer limited to colleges taking advantage of young people being away from home, but now it's occurring within public and private school systems. Even elementary students are presented with moral relativism and and all alike. Books like Mama Bear Apologetics recognize that mothers are on the front lines when it comes to helping their children answer objections to the Christian faith. But I don't want to communicate that for you to give a reason for the hope that lies within you, you have to become a trained defender of Christianity. For many, the reason for the hope that lies within you is simply answering why you are a Christian. And that answer likely has a story to it. And each of us can tell our own story. Yours may be That when you read about God's love for the first time in 1 Corinthians chapter 13, you realized that you had never loved anyone in such a manner, nor had anyone loved you in such a manner. And if such a love was real, well, you wanted it. And so you confessed your sins and followed Jesus. Your story may be that you grew up in the church and you witnessed how people apply their faith in Jesus through their various trials. You compared that to how other people went through their life and suffered through their trials, and you were convinced that the Christian faith works Your story may be that you walked away from the Lord and went the way of the flesh. Like the prodigal son, the world ate you up and spit you out. And when you came to your right mind, you went back to the Father's house, confessed your sins, and received, and were received into God's house as an inheritor of his kingdom. Whatever your story is, you are to be ready to tell it. And to those who ask We are to be ready to tell our story in a manner, he says, that is meek and with fear. Meek because we are not to pretend it was our own wisdom, our own work that led us to the faith. In fear, because we owe God our lives, and we ought to fear that our lazy answers to the hope within us would not be dishonoring to him who owns our life. All such behavior on our part, from doing good to others, from refraining to do bad To not being afraid of threats, to sanctifying the Lord in our hearts, to giving a defense of the hope that lies within us allows a good conscience. And there is no greater gift in this life than an honest and good conscience. A good conscience makes for a healthy soul, and a healthy soul is never afraid to die. With a good conscience, we are best able to endure unjust attacks from those who have guilty consciences and yet do not know what to do with their guilt. Good behavior by others reminds them of their guilt, and so again they seek to be rid of the good by defaming those who are good. Even turning the rumors around to accuse a gooddoer of being an evildoer. In the end, when all has been revealed, God will shame such persons. Until then we are to be doing good whenever we get the opportunity If we suffer for doing good, according to verse 18, we are following the path of Christ Jesus, who also suffered for doing good. He did it that you and I can be brought to God and be his people and he to be our God. That is always the end goal. We next read in verse 19, where Peter mentions preaching to spirits in prison who were formerly disobedient, evidently all the way back to the days of Noah. And in those days, God was long-suffering regarding his judgment until the ark was finished, which we are told lasted at least two generations. The Ark carried Noah, his wife, his three sons, and their wives through the flood to save them from God's judgment. This leads Peter to mention baptism, for it was Peter, you remember, who answered the question in Acts chapter 2, what must we do to be saved? He said, repent and be baptized. Each of us is to come through our own flood waters in order to be saved. The baptism provides us confidence that we can have a good conscience before God because of what He does in our hearts at baptism. And all of it is accomplished by Jesus being resurrected, ascending to the right hand of the Father, and always interceding for us. That is what verses 19 through 22 says, because what it means is more elusive, particularly when it comes to identifying Who are these spirits in prison and not knowing what Jesus preached to them? Two things we can know. First, we know it was Jesus who does the preaching because he was described previously as being the one who was put to death in the flesh, but then was made alive. That's clearly Jesus. Second, the most natural interpretation of this passage, that is also the interpretation of early church fathers and most prominent reformers, is the following. Jesus, taking on the sin of humanity, had his spirit separated from his body at his death, which will happen to all of us at our death. This enabled his spirit to descend into hell and be seen by those who rejected God, going back as far as the days of Noah. If you remember, Genesis says, when the hearts of men were bent toward evil and that continually. And he there proclaimed to them the truth about God's plan of salvation. The purpose of this proclamation is not clear to us, but the revelation of God's plan had yet to be revealed until Jesus overcame death. For some ears, it sounds like Jesus went down and simply bragged. I say that such ears are too sensitive. Telling the truth is not bragging. And besides, the raising of the body and spirit was preaching enough about the victory of Christ without even using words. Well it gets lost in our desire to know exactly who Jesus preached to and what he said, what he preached. is the main goal of it all, which I said previously from verse 18, was to bring us to God, so that we might be his people and he might be our God. From last week, we can answer to what end are we to love one another as brothers? The answer is to be brought to God. To what end do we suffer unjustly? The answer is to be brought to God. To what end do we do good and have a good conscience? The answer is to be brought to God. To what end did Jesus suffer, die, descend, proclaim to those prisoners, rise from the dead and sit at the right hand of the Father? To what end all of it was for to be us to be brought to God. And this point forces us to examine ourselves, asking to what end do we do what we do? To what end do we do what we do when it comes to our employment? To what end do we do what we do when it comes to raising our children, to having children, and then raising them? To what end do we do what we do when we control our money, when we buy goods and services, when we plan for retirement? To what end do we do what we do when we get up in the morning and pursue what we pursue? No matter what it is, all of it should have the ultimate purpose, which is to be brought to God. If it is not to be brought to God, then it is not worth doing. Let us look more closely regarding why you do what you do when it comes to your employment. If you are in a ministry of some sort, like teaching or preaching or counseling or leading in some manner, you think that your end goal is obvious. But it is easy for people in ministry to work for a paycheck rather than to have the end goal of bringing people to God. No one is above the temptation to serve for manna instead of for the glory of God. But let us look at you who work for a company or in some government institution. You are one of the many cogs that keep the company or the department going. What is the main goal for you? You may first say it is to provide for your family, but why do you do that? You say this so your family can live, which means the kids can be cared for and they can go to school. But why should they go to school? You say to be educated so they can learn a trade and make money for themselves, but why should they make money for themselves? You say so that they can have their own family. But why should they have their own family? You say that so they can provide for them, so that their kids can go to school and and you begin to see it. Life can become a hamster wheel, spinning but going nowhere. So let us ask another way. To what end should you do your employment You say to provide for my children the basic necessities of life. And why do you do that? Because you answer, it is my duty as a God-fearing man, and I want to provide for them so that they can do good. So that they will be brought to God. Now that is a good end goal. That's a goal that has meat upon it. I recently heard of a man who had the end goal of having a lot of children, because he said he wanted to be obedient to God by being fruitful and multiplying, just as the Bible says. But he stopped there. He thought that all he needed to do was to have a lot of children without looking toward the chief end goal of bringing them to God. It is wise to understand that God never calls Christian couples to have children in order to populate hell. The end goal for all parents is to be that their children be brought to God. That is why we bring them to the baptismal water. That is why we pray with them on our knees. That is why we oversee their education. That is why we counsel them on who they should marry. It is all to help them be brought to God. Such takes a great deal of patience, time, resources, tears, a lot of tears, long suffering, and forgiveness But all of it is nothing compared to the reward of eternity with God. Before I close, I must address to what end goal To what end is our goal of how we use our money? As you may be aware, I was recently away attending a wedding of my nephew Christian, a son of my brother Chris. And while we were waiting for the reception to start, my brother and I, along with my sister Dana, began to talk about retirement. We talked about different types of retirement accounts and Social Security and an appropriate age for retirement. And while it was interesting, I came away with a very strange Feeling likely caused by realizing how old we all were talking about this, but also asking myself: what is the chief end of retirement? The more popular goals for retirement don't seem to match up with being brought to God. I have known persons that enter into their work the workforce in their twenties, already planning for retirement. Money is saved, pensions are paid into, Social Security is hoped for, all for the sake of those retirement years. And what are those years used for? For leisure, for leisure's sake, for freedom to do as you please? For having no responsibilities? That sounds good only to those who care not if they are brought to God. For the Christian What is always before us is that we are to do good and in the end to be brought to God. If my money If my saving of money, if my retirement does not have me doing good and being brought to God, it is in vain. All of it is in vain. I close by repeating what I have already asked. To what end are we to love one another as brothers? The answer is to be brought to God. To what end do we suffer unjustly? To be brought to God. To what end do we do good and have a good conscience? To be brought to God. To what end do we s did Jesus suffer, die, descend, proclaim, rise, and sit at the right hand of the Father? To what end? All of it was for us to be brought to God. So it was, so it always will be to be brought to God. Let us pray. Our gracious and merciful Father, we identify today the purpose of it all. And all of us sit with the weight of examining our lives and evaluating what we do and why we do it in light of being brought to you Father, where we are amiss, where we have not put that as our priority. Convict us, forgive us. And Father, help us to focus on the one thing that's most important to be brought to you. In Jesus' name we pray. Amen.

sermons.title: Needing One Another
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: Name of Father, of the Son, of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. Very much encourage you to turn to 1 Peter chapter 4, verses 1 through 11. 1 Peter 4 1 through 11. One fad on the internet that I like Is the collecting of what are called now dad jokes. Dad jokes are actually a collection of bad jokes. But sometimes they can be so bad that how bad they are makes them funny. For example, For example, did you hear what was missing at the funeral of the man who invented the throat lozenge? There was no coffin. Do you know why the bicycle couldn't stand on its own? It was two tires. What is the difference between a poorly dressed man and a on a tricycle and a well-dressed man on a bicycle? A tire. How does mo how does Moses make coffee? He brews it. Right over your head. He brews it. How does a penguin build a house? He glues it together. I'll stop. I start with levity or an attempt at levity because of how serious biblical texts can be. They can be so very serious that the message weighs heavy, making it difficult to listen and making it difficult to apply. Preachers can easily fall into sounding like little chicken, or chicken little, I should say, or Al Gore. Sounding as if the end is near when the end is actually a long ways away. Truth is, we don't know when the end is, but we are to be ready for it. And preachers are called to get God's people ready for it, even if the end is not in our lifetime. For St. Peter and the first century Christians, it felt very much like the end was near, considering the suffering they had to endure for Jesus. The following account is the suffering of Saint Peter. The language is archaic. Saint Peter was taken of the ministers of Nero and was delivered to the provost Agrippa. Then was his face as clear as the sun, as it is said. Then Agrippa said to him, You are he who glorified in the people and in women whom you inspire to depart from the bed of their husbands. The apostle denied this and said to him that he glorified in the cross of the Lord Jesus Christ. Then Peter was sentenced to be crucified as a stranger. And because that Paul was a citizen of Rome, it was commanded that his head be cut off. And when the horrible time came of their end that they were departed that one from that other, they bound the pillars of the world, but that was not without wailing and weeping of the brethren, said Saint Dionysius. And as Leo the Pope and Marcel witnessed, when Peter came to the cross, he said, When my Lord descended from heaven to the earth, he was put on the cross right up But me, whom it please him to call from the earth to heaven, my cross shall show my head to the earth and address my feet to heaven For I am not worthy to be put on the cross like as my Lord was. Therefore turn my cross and crucify me head downward. Then they turned the cross and fastened his feet upward and the head downward. Then the people were angry against Nero and the provost. and would have slain them because they made Saint Peter so to die, but he required them that they should not let his pass let his passion and as Leo witnessed our Lord open the eyes of them that were there And wept so that they saw the angel of the crown of roses and of the lilies standing by Peter, who was on the cross with the angels. Such is what loomed for Peter, and he was well aware of it. Thus, when we read his words of warning. And of soberness and seriousness, we can quite easily imagine how such soberness and seriousness was needed I say this not to intimate that the times in which we live are not serious. They are serious, but in a different manner. As of now, our physical lives are not in danger. But our spiritual lives are always in danger. And it could be argued that these days are more perilous because we are not aware of how we are being attacked. Football players are coached to keep what we say, keep your head on a swivel. Keeping the head on a swivel means The player players are to be looking to their right and looking to their left each play to see if an opponent is charging them to hit them, to hurt them. And this is an appropriate analogy for the Christian as we are looking to the right and looking to the left to see if the devil and his minions are trying to get a hit on us. I remind you that the devil wants one of two things for you. He wants you either to take your life or to lead you to deny the Christian faith. One of the easier ways to lure someone to deny the faith is to have them live for earthly pleasures. To combat the temptation to give in to earthly pleasures is to embrace the suffering that occurs when other people persecute you for your Christian faith. In the first three verses of chapter four, Peter makes the following plea. In order to thwart off temptations of earthly pleasure, He says we are to have the same mind of Jesus when Jesus suffered. And what was the mind of Jesus when he suffered? Well, we can know first that it was other focused. His suffering was done for others. We know from his prayer in St. John chapter 17 that he went to the cross desiring our holiness. Desiring that we would never be lost from the faith, desiring for us to be in the world but not of the world, and desiring that we would be united just as Jesus and the Father and the Holy Spirit are united. We can also know that his mindset was not to willfully give up give to willful excuse me. We also know that his mindset was to willfully give of himself In John chapter 10, he said of his life, he said, No one takes it from me, but I lay it down of myself. I have no power. I have power to lay it down, and I have power to take it up again. We can also know that his suffering was not easy for him. He prayed that if the cup would be taken from him, so it would be. He shows us in that garden scene that there is no shame in identifying fear. There is no shame of not wanting to experience pain. And he allows us to know his mind in that he desired for it to align with the will of the Father. For in that he said, Not my will, but thine be done. Our standard then in facing temptation, in facing persecution, is to have the mind of Jesus. A mind that is other focused And when we go through trials and temptations, we do so for others rather than for ourselves. We endure so that others can see our example and be encouraged. We are also to have the mindset of wanting others to be holy, wanting others to never be lost to the faith. Wanting to be in the world but not of the world, and to be united just as the Godhead is united And we can willfully, not avoiding facing temptation and persecution, we can do this willfully, but pleading with God and accepting His will and not our own. Such a mindset teaches, Peter teaches, helps us not to live by what our flesh desires. Such a mindset will have us wanting the will of God, whatever that is revealed to be. Another reason to not practice the desires of the flesh is that we have done so already. At least the audience of Peter did. The converts of Peter that he's speaking to did indeed live according to their flesh, and the culture in which they lived encouraged them to do so. Providing no obvious boundaries for moral living other than what the Roman state forbid, which wasn't much. Morality for the Romans focused on being a good citizen. And that meant, first and foremost, being loyal to the state. There were expected standards called Mos Maiworam, or the way of the elders. Which was not a written code of conduct, but was applied and expected, applied to fellow citizens, applied to how you behave toward your family. But was it was not applied to one's personal and private behavior. Thus lewdness, drunkenness, revelry were not looked down upon Unless you did it to someone else, but you're in your own behavior, it was not considered immoral. Jesus, we know, looked at personal behavior differently. He taught that the inner person was even more important to care for than the outer person, for it was from within that our sins begin. Thus, the inner personal holiness is to be the concern of every person who follows Jesus and calls themselves Christian. What Peter describes in verse 4 of the chapter is well known from experience by those who converted to Christianity later in life. When we convert later in life, we leave behind friends. And those friends expect us to continue on with our lewdness, with our lustfulness, with our drunkenness. When a person stops living in such a manner, he causes guilt on the consciences of those he leaves behind. And those persons don't care much for that guilt, and so they revile their former friend and even curse him and even the God that they now follow Peter assures the repentant sinner that such persons will be judged by God, for God will judge all. But God isn't just about judging sinners and condemning them, as Peter recognizes, as verse 6 states, the gospel is preached to the dead. Some believe that is the dead that is dead in their sin. And then some believe it referring to those who had heard the gospel but now are dead. But either way, it doesn't matter. It's to be understood that God gives people the opportunity to repent. He gives it to all men. Now I mentioned the seriousness of certain biblical passages, and if you look at verse 7, there is a clear example. It even has the word seriousness in it. The end of Peter's perspective was that Jesus promised in regards to his second coming. Jesus didn't return quickly, however. As St. Peter and even Paul thought he would, and most Christians of the first century thought he would. But what did come was great persecution. Resulting in Christians being removed from Jerusalem, followed by Jerusalem coming under attack by the Romans. You will recall that the siege was in 70 AD, the Siege of Jerusalem, and consisted of a military blockade around the city of Jerusalem during the first Jewish revolt. The fall of the city marked the effect effective conclusion of a four-year campaign against the Jewish insurgency. The Romans destroyed much of the city, including the Second Temple, just as Jesus prophesied. It is estimated that over one million people died. Consider how important our faith becomes when there is tragedy around us. Catastrophes, plagues, pandemics, sieges, wars, God uses them and more. To wake up faith in people and to reveal a lack of faith in others. Tragedies can also strengthen communities Consider how important we become to one another when our numbers get smaller, because there are less and less of us who are not willing to compromise. Consider how much more we are going to need to be sure we who loves us, who is around us that loves us. When people we used to call friends turn us into authorities for what is labeled now today hate speech. Consider how much more we are going to need to be in one another's homes, be hospitable. When we can't trust our neighbor who is spying on us. When we insist that certain behaviors are to be called sin and nothing else. You are aware, I trust, that our culture is squeezing the Christian church with a formulated plan to force the church to accept the immorality of the culture or be closed down, similar to the devil's desire to kill us or to have us compromise our faith. According to some, I am even referring to judges and legislatures. According to some, it should be required of me, a minister of the gospel, to preside over same-sex weddings. and to hire teachers who are openly homosexual. Why these controversies are always related to sex is inexplicable to me, but they are And for some, any prayer, any sermon that denounces abortion should be censored, and the speaker should be fined or jailed or both. Considering the time in which the first century Christians lived, we can better understand why they needed to be watchful in their prayers, as St. Peter instructs. And why they needed to love one another better, and why they needed to be hospitable to one another and to do it cheerfully. They were going to need one another as never before. And I say, we are going to need one another as never before. Most of you are not aware that a few years ago, we, St. Stephen's, were sued. And my name was the primary person on the charging document. I had terminated a teacher in our headmaster John's place only because she refused to talk to him. And so she sued me and us for a large sum of money, claiming we were prejudicial toward her age. First there was a hearing where some of us had to testify. Then there was a hiring of a lawyer and affidavits made and emails turned over. And a court date set, and then the hearing itself. It was time-consuming, a bit unnerving, and a true waste of resources. The judge ruled in our favor, thanks be to God, but the accuser decided to include in the documents for the case a statement of condemnation of my character. The lawyer said we could fight that state the statement be removed, but I chose to let it stand. I reason that if people want to believe what she says about me, that is to their detriment. Most of you didn't know about this because there was no need. We were confident there was no merit to the charges and we wanted to control the narrative rather than address rumors. My point in telling you this now is that I easily imagine going through something similar because of my preaching offending someone's lifestyle or because of a decision by our school board. We're going to be accused of breaking the Equality Act. I trust that you know that there is a bill before the Senate that, if passed, would make what we believe to be hate and thus criminal. It doesn't take much. And I'm not trying to give anyone ideas by mentioning this, but with the sensitivities of today, every accusation is given full attention by the courts.
