Romans chapter 9, verse 18 Because God hardening Pharaoh's heart precisely so that he could display his grace and power. He made Pharaoh unwilling to do the right thing, the sensible thing. in order to reveal to the world his grace and power. This way of God is repeated many times You remember the manner in which Joseph was captured and made a slave. It was by the evil of his brothers. When face to face with them many years later, he tells them what you meant for evil, God meant for good. In Deuteronomy chapter 2, verse 30, we read. But King Sihon, king of Heshbon, refused to let us pass through, for the Lord your God had made his spirit stubborn. And his heart obstinate, in order to place him into your hands as he has now done. And Joshua chapter eleven, verse twenty, we read. Except for the Hivites living in Gibeon, not one city made a treaty of peace with the Israelites, who took them all in battle. For it was the Lord Himself who hardened their hearts to wage war against Israel, so that he might destroy them totally. Describing why Rehoboam foolishly listened to the advice of his peers, the scriptures say, This turn of events was from the Lord, to fulfill the word the Lord had spoken to Jeroboam. And in case you might have the delusion that this was the way God acted only in the New Testament, the Old Testament, and not the New, we read this from 2 Thessalonians 2, verse 11. For this reason, God sends them, speaking of the rebellious, God sends them a powerful delusion so that they will believe the lie, and so that all will be condemned. God sends them. In Revelation chapter 17, verse 17, for God has put it into their hearts. God put it into their hearts. to accomplish his purpose by agreeing to give the beast their power to rule until God's word was fulfilled. Again, the modus operandi of God, the way God works then, is to use the sinfulness of men in a sinless manner for his will to be done. In doing so, as we might expect, God gets criticized by his creation. The pot does say to the potter, Why have you made me this way? What is illustrated by the manner God uses sinful men is how he has absolute divine sovereignty and unqualified control over his creation. Men in rebellion believe themselves to be escaping God's rule, yet in their breaking of his commands, they are only furthering his purpose. If they knew this, it would no doubt frustrate them, but they do not and will not know unless God allows them to see. Samson violated the sacred rules of his calling as a Nazarite, and still God used him to deal with the Philistines. There is no evidence that Samson was concerned about God's calling upon his life. He was not concerned about his own people. Yet even Samson's rebellion, our rebellion, accomplishes God's will. The pot needs to be careful. For it is tempting to argue that God uses the sin of a sinner for good, that the sin of the sinner is excused. Samson is an example of how God uses men in spite of themselves. There is no evidence of God forcing Samson to act in the selfish manner that he did. God simply uses what is already there. We revisit Pharaoh with this in mind. Pharaoh's heart was already hardened against God. That God did not let him out of his own noose does not impugn God. Because God uses the sin of men for the ultimate good, does not excuse men for their sin. Samson was no hero. He most certainly did not display characteristics for us to emulate. God is the hero here. He is sovereign over all, even the sinful acts of men. And may I put it in context for us today? He is sovereign even over the stupid decisions of politicians. He is. He very much is It is here in the truth of God's sovereignty that God's will will be revealed And we say Amen and Amen. Let us pray. Our gracious and merciful God, we thank you for the confidence you give us. For the message of your sovereignty, that your will is always going to be accomplished, regardless of our sin, of our foolishness. And we thank you for that confidence. May we have it each and every day, even as we hear the bad news of our media, that we have good news in Christ, and that good news always prevails. We pray these things in Jesus' name. Amen.

sermons.title: God will bring you back
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: And I'm going to win the other and then you can just go in the room. In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. Turn, if you would, to Judges 16. We read the latter part of the chapter, but we will be covering the whole story. Before there was Hollywood, there was the Bible. The Christian Rite, as some used to call it Speaks out against the sex violence that is glorified by Hollywood in movies and in television. Yet Hollywood does not write or portray stories more lustful violent, disloyal, and painfully sinful than the story of Samson and Delilah. The famous director Cecil D. DeMills recognized how the story of Samson and Delilah married well with Hollywood. So he put the story on the silver screen in 1949. For some reason, DeMills thought it necessary to tweak the story a bit and make Delilah a more complicated figure than she was. There is enough plainly stated in Scripture to satisfy the salacious minds of Hollywood producers and directors alike. As I said, we didn't read the first part of the story, so I will remind you what happens. The chapter begins with Samson lusting and then having sex with a prostitute. Samson's enemies set a trap for him, but he displays superhuman strength and frees himself. He then falls in love with Delilah, whom he does not marry, but lives with Delilah apparently does not love Samson, for she is offered eleven hundred shekels of silver by each of the five rulers of the Philistines. And Delilah was no dummy. She was able to calculate a potential earnings of 5,500 shekels. The money outweighed any feelings that she had for Samson, so she accepted the deal. What follows is a series of games played by Samson. He pretends to give away the secret of his strength only to lie to Delilah several times Instead of seeing her for who she was and what she was trying to do to him, Samson continued to play games. Delilah, however, wore on Samson, and he eventually told her of the covenant God made with Samson's parents at his birth The hair on his head was not to be cut. Uncut hair, you remember from last week, was symbolic of a rejection of Philistine oppression and of their idol worship. Uncut hair symbolize that Samson was owned by God and to be used for God's glory. Delilah took advantage of this knowledge and betrayed her lover. Samson's strength was gone with his hair. After this capture, he was taken into the lair of the Philistines. To the Philistines, Samson's capture was proof That their God was stronger than Samson's God, and thus stronger than the God of the Israelites. Samson was soon publicly humiliated. His eyes were gouged out, and he was put on public display. With their guard down, the Philistines allowed Samson to place himself in position to enact revenge. Samson's prayer for strength is answered, and he brings down the godless temple of the Philistines, killing many along with himself. Hollywood could not write a more dramatic script, and I'm embarrassed to say that if they did, some Christians would protest. Hollywood does not put out anything more sinful than the story of Samson and Delilah. The godlessness of Hollywood is not so much revealed in the stories they tell, but in the details. They enjoy depicting the intricacies of sin, while the Bible refers to them without glorified descriptions. For Hollywood, the purpose of telling such stories is to entice the mind toward lusts of the flesh. In Scripture, the purpose of telling the story is to show God's redemptive work. We remember from last week that Israel did not, did not cry out to God for deliverance from the oppression of the Philistines In fact, there is evidence that they were comfortable in their oppression. God took the initiative to deliver them. He drags them out of the mire in which they were bathing. That God initiates the deliverance is to be remembered as we continue the story of Samson. Instead of focusing on the salacious details of Samson and Delilah, I wish to turn our attention to the covenant that Samson disregarded. It is an inherited covenant. Samson was born for a particular task. He was chosen of God and dedicated according to the instructions of the Lord. Although Samson did not live with respect toward his calling, God used him in spite of himself. As we discussed last week, this manner or way in which God works is not new to God. God uses the sinful and the sinner sinlessly. It is the saddest of stories to hear of young men and young women who have been raised in the Christian faith or in a Christian home, as we say. To hear of them walking away from the faith, faith in the Lord Jesus Christ. There are many reasons for this walking away. Some reasons parents will not admit. And some children walking away, parents will not admit. They don't admit it, even though their child is not showing any fruit, to be living with Christ. What I wish to do this morning is to examine what went wrong in Samson's life with the hope that those who are young would not make the same choices And those of us who are parents might learn from the mistakes of others. One of the more important roles a parent plays is preparing their child for marriage. In our parenting videos, Bobby, Lynn, and I have discussed the biblical authority of a parent that he has in a young adult's life. The authority extends to dating practices of a young adult. The practice of recreational dating is not scriptural. Such a statement should not be a surprise to anyone who reads his or her Bible. Being alone with someone of the opposite sex for the purpose of, quote, having a good time Is willfully walking into temptation. A temptation, we pray in the Lord's Prayer, that we would not be led into. There are plenty of biblical warnings against having a good time so that all Christians are without excuse. There are also biblical models like that of Isaac and Rebekah that teach us to be careful when marrying. I am not preaching right now for arranged marriages, certainly not, nor am I touting the once popular courtship model. I am simply stating that what should be obvious, which is that young people do not have the self-discipline nor character development to make right choices And therefore should not be expected to exhibit self control even when they say that they love Jesus I realize this raises issues of trust between parent and child, but such trust is developed over time rather than being automatically given. Such thinking and adjusting flies in the face of modern culture. But that is what Christianity and that is what Christians are to do. Fly in the face of modern culture. One very simple but straightforward message children should hear beginning when they are very young is that they are not to marry a non-Christian. God's people do not marry outside of the faith. And such is not an issue of prejudice, but of obedience. God in his holy word is not concerned about interracial dating. He is not concerned about inter-class dating. He's not even concerned about inter-intellect dating. What he restricts is interfaith dating. Christians are not to be yoked with non-Christians And in case you have not heard the term yokt before, I remind you that it is not referring to the substance of an egg, but is rather a contraption that is placed upon two oxen helping them pull the plow together. Being unequally yoked makes for serpentine lines and circles. And the time to instruct a child to not marry a non-Christian is not when she is sixteen and begins to show interest in boys. Is when she is five and thinks that boys are icky. Samson's parents were aware of God's restrictions in marriage. They pleaded with Samson to look for a woman amongst his own people, but he did not listen to them. By the time Samson was of age, to lust after a woman and to marry her, his parents' warnings had no effect. A repeated mistake among parents from one generation to another is parenting by circumstance rather than principle. Warning a child about playing in the road after you scraped him off of the pavement is not enough. Biblical parenting is proactive parenting. Before a wanton woman confronts a young man, The wise father in the book of Proverbs has warned his son of the wanton woman and her temptuous ways. Biblical parenting sets godly principles in the lives of children early on, so that when they are older, they will not depart from them. Regarding Samson's culpability, he did not heed the instructions of his parents. This resulted in him being led by his lusts and going from the bed of one ungodly woman to another. Each of the women became a trap that he willfully walked into because of the confidence he had in his strength. Perhaps we could say he was more than confident. He was, as they say, cocky. His cockiness was caused by the fact that he had no regard for his calling as a Nazarite. As he defied God's laws openly and still retained his strength. We can imagine How a feeling of invincibility came over him, having, as he determined, gotten away with the behavior without any repercussions. And this is how it happens to all who rebel. There is initial fear before the first rebellious sinful act is committed. When the forbidden fruit is tasted, such as a joint being puffed, alcohol being drunk to excess, sensuality being explored, lying, cheating, and stealing practiced Nothing as far as immediate punishment is experienced, and we've thinking we've gotten away with it. No lightning flashes. No voice from heaven to bring us to our knees. Therefore, we believe a lie, any lie, that would tell us God didn't see it, or God doesn't care even if he did see it. God, of course, does care. He cares so much that he gave his only begotten Son, sending him to die the death of a cursed sinner on our behalf Yes, God cares. There is such a thing as eerie silence. It is the silence that is deafening, for it allows our conscience to be haunted by the spirit of our evil deeds. Though silent, the Spirit of God was around Samson, and he still defied God's law. Not only was he around, that is, the Spirit, he was intricately involved. The Holy Spirit used Samson's sinful ways to enact his will. In the end, the judgment of God was going to be experienced. It was a judgment passed on the Philistines and upon Samson. Samson did not anticipate As he lie in bed with the prostitute or enjoyed the flesh of Delilah, that he would be chained by the Philistines. Samson did not have the foresight that his eyes would be gouged out by his enemies when he played sport with them, time and time again. At those times, it appeared God was silent. It appeared that God didn't see or that God didn't care. Psalm 50 describes well how the eerie silence of God turns quickly into judgment. God describes Israel's sin as follows. He says in Psalm 50, you hate my instruction and cast my words behind you. When you see a thief, you join with him. You throw in your lot with adulterers. You use your mouth for evil and harness your tongue to deceit. Then God says, These things you have done and I kept silent. You thought I was altogether like you, but I will rebuke you and accuse you to your face. The lesson is that we should not be fooled by the silence of God. You may get away with your sin for a time. Because the lightning fails to strike initially, do not be foolishly concluding that it will not come at all. It can come to our bed, causing us to lie there in sickness. It can come to our workplace in the form of great stress or lost wages. It can come to us in the form of Strained and even broken relationships. It can come to us as confusion of thought and bitterness of heart. God's judgment can come in many forms, and in the midst of it, we are to be grateful that it comes in the manner that it does, instead of when it could. Which is when time is no more and there is no more opportunity for repentance. This is when the judgment of God is eternal. At the end of his days on this earth, Samson reaped what he had sown. He got, as we say, as he deserved. It is not that he should not be counted among God's elect. He is another that is listed in the book of Hebrews as a man of faith. His faith was not always obedient, and as we have seen, God still used him. What God did was choose him Because God chose him, Samson could not get away. It would have been to Samson's benefit If he would have surrendered to God's will and walked obediently all of his days. There was not the path, that was not the path that Samson chose, and so his life ended in the midst of a foreign people. Alone and disfigured. And I wonder to myself what Samson thought in those days that he sat imprisoned by the Philistines, having no eyes to see, waiting for his hair to grow back. Surely he must have regretted not listening to his parents He must have regretted listening to the lust of his flesh. He must have regretted playing games with the ungodly, and he must have regretted taking the calling of God on his life for granted. I am confident his conclusion was that the moments of earthly pleasure were not worth the suffering he endured by the hands of the Philistines. So, dear Christian, if God has chosen you and marked you as his own, you can do what you wish. There is freedom in Christ. You can go the way of the world and the way of the flesh, but God will not let your sinful deeds go unpunished. Whatever a man sows, we are told, that he will also reap. That is why the Apostle James says Two Christians, cleanse your hands, you sinners, purify your hearts, you double-minded. Such a call, again, is not directed to the outside world. He is saying that to Christians. A few years back. A young woman sat in my office. Her family used to attend this church. She was confirmed as a member here At the time of our conversation, she was not attending church and spending her nights in a bar. As I tried to talk sense to her, the one thing I kept repeating to her is that because she has been marked by God, God was not going to let her go. In fact, I spoke prophetically to her, explaining that God would make her life miserable until she repented and surrendered her will unto him. At this time, I do not know what has happened to that girl, but she could be any one of us I believe God is saying the same to all of us. We cannot get away from His presence. If we go down to the dwelling of the dead, as David said, God is there. It might seem odd to portray God as someone who would want to get a we someone that we would want to get away from. When God is after us, there is that presence of guilt if we do not repent. But that guilt is there, and that guilt will help save us from eternal fire. If you have been marked by Christ, God will assure by any means necessary to bring you to your knees Once you are finally there, you will regret that you did not do so much, much earlier. Beloved Samson's end of life is a call to us to live holy lives. If you have been baptized in Christ Jesus and if you have been blessed with the knowledge of the Lord Jesus Christ as your Savior, do not sell your birthright for a bowl of stew. Do not live for the moment, causing each of those moments of fleshly rule to corrupt the rest of your life here on earth. Samson would testify the same to us. Glory be to God that he had made something positive of Samson's life Glory be to God that he will do the same to each of us. Only let us be willing participants. Amen. Let us pray. Our gracious and merciful God, we think upon the life of Samson so much wasted and yet so much used by you. Heavenly Father, for those who have gone astray from the faith, those that are in our families, we pray for their repentance, we pray for their return. Heavenly Father, for those who are tempted by the world, help them to remember the life of Samson. Help them to learn from these lessons that they might hold on to the faith and never let it go. This we pray in Jesus' name. Amen. Let us help spare our hearts to receive the body of love, Collins.

sermons.title: We need a King
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: We will be referencing Judges chapter 17 and chapter 18. If you want to turn there in your Bibles, follow along. It may or may not come as a surprise for you to learn that we have finished studying the main body of the book of Judges. Although there are five chapters remaining, what we have read from chapter 17 is part of an epilogue. These chapters just describe and explain the end result the end result of Israel's assimilation into pagan culture. As well as setting the reader in the right frame of mind for the kings of Israel to come. This can be said with confidence because Samson is the last judge mentioned in the book of Judges. There is no political, religious, or military leader after Samson. What we are about to study is a series of stories that contain very little good. Once again, I find it difficult to be cheery within a sermon While preaching from a biblical text that has very little to be cheery about, I understand that many of you like to leave here in a cheerful mood. Both focusing on the negative can bring down the emotions. I appreciate that desire, and I know how popular it is for there are well-attended community type churches that only preach and teach what is positive But please bear with me this morning and next week. It is going to be a challenge to keep the mood bubbly. But you are not the type of Christian people who always want bubbly. I know that because you are here listening to me, and I am not a bubbly preacher As you have already heard from the first reading, a story told in the text is not only sinful, it is very odd. We will be speaking of the story contained in both chapters 17 and 18, and these chapters have oddities and strangeness about them. It is therefore necessary to keep in the back of our minds, while we look at these strange stories that the people were doing that which was right in their own eyes. Their moral standards were their own, thus their behavior. Also consider that there are moments in our lives When odd or strange things happen and they leave us literally dumbfounded. What was that? What just happened A number of years ago, I went to bed late around midnight. My mistake was not placing a cup of water by my bed. For as circumstances would have it, I woke up a mere one hour after laying my head down with a parched palate. Knowing that Bobby Lynn had brought her usual cup of water to her bedside, I asked her for her water. What ensued was quite strange. By asking for her for a drink of her water, I woke her from one of those dead sleeps. She responded to my request with a surprise. What I repeated my request, and her mumbling made me believe that she understood me. As I lay there, I hear her fumbling around at her night table next to her next to her side of the bed. She made another mumbling sound as if she had what I wanted. I reached out and there was nothing there. I spoke more poignantly and I told her I wanted a drink of water That request was followed by much banging and clanging, and still no glass of water was handed to me. I got up in a huff, went to the kitchen, found my own cup of water, and went to sleep. The next morning I awoke to understand what had happened the night before. Bobby Lynn, having been woken in her dead sleep, had little or no knowledge of what I had requested What she had first tried to hand me, at my request of a cup of water, was the lamp on her night table. Unable to reach the lamp to me, to my side, because of the cord plugged into the wall, she then proceeded to unscrew the light bulb from the lamp Hence all the banging and claiming, only to be frustrated by me that I would not take the light bulb from her once she was successful. In all my 35 years of marriage, I do not know what category to place those actions into. Simply odd, simply strange, simply weird. And so are these stories at the end of Judges. With a few comments carefully placed by the author to inform the reader why he is repeating these stories to us. So, chapter 17 begins evidently in the middle of a story. A woman, obviously wealthy by the amount of money stolen from her, is given money back by her son, and his name is Micah. Micah admits that he was the guilty party who had stolen her money. We are not told when or why he stole it, and the omission means that we do not need to know Why he gives it back, that's important. He heard his mother place a curse on whoever was guilty, and he feared the curse. This tells us that Micah was a superstitious man. The mother is happy with her son when he confesses and returns the money, and I think that that's odd. And in her happiness she plans a religious dedication, which is also odd. And she sets aside part of the money that was stolen to make idols, which is not only odd but sinful. Micah is not only superstitious superstitious, he is a as strange as his mother. He takes the idols made from his mother's money and makes a shrine to display the idols, to honor and worship them. Adding insult to injury, he then makes one of his sons priest over his man-made temple. The next development in this story is the arrival of a Levite priest. Both Micah and the priest are men of opportunity. The Levite needs a place to stay, and Micah needs a real priest. Here is evidence that the law of God has been completely disregarded, for the law has specific instructions for the care of Levites and the proper federal worship God. These laws are either ignored or unknown by the Levi and by Micah. The result is a very strange setup Where Micah pays a man to preside over a man-made shrine containing carved silver-cast idols At this point, we could consider how many strange ways Christians have tried to worship God. Chapter 18, which we did not read, introduces the tribe of Dan into the story as some men of the tribe come into contact with Micah and the Levites. What the Spirit is showing us by telling the story in this way is how a family in Israel was corrupted by the assimilation of pagan ritual into their faith, into their faith in Yahweh. By describing the behavior of the tribe of Dan That follows, we learn how a whole tribe is then conquered, captured, corrupted by the assimilation into pagan worship. Although the tribe of Dan was originally given its own territory next to Judah, the people evidently were not satisfied, which is a breaking of the tenth commandment. And they go looking for more land. Representatives from the Danites recognize the Levite in Micah's house, which is odd for we are not told how they would recognize him, and they inquire of him a word from God regarding the overtaking of the new land that they desire. The exchange between the Levite and the Danites could be identified as divination or false prophecy. Either way, it was another violation of God's law. The Danites liked what they heard from the Levites, so on their way back they took Micah's idols. Why, we don't know, and they took his priest, and oddly the priest is glad to leave with them. When Micah's household caught up with the Danites, Micah was told not to argue with the tribe, or his family would lose their lives. So the Danites settled nicely into their new territory, worshiping false images of God, being led by four higher priests. After this overview of the story, let us go back and pay attention to some of the details the narrator, the writer, carefully includes. He describes the Sidonians, and he does it in a way that we should be jealous, or at least the Israelites should be jealous. He describes them as being at peace in their land and lacking nothing. And we are to understand that these pagan people, pagan people are at the point in their tribal life where Israel should be. Israel should be at peace. Israel should lack nothing, but instead they are bloodthirsty. They want more. The roles then have been reversed, as the Israelites have become exactly like the pagan nations around them, and the pagan nations have become like Israel could have been The sinful world has infiltrated, has infiltrated the people of God. So much, so much so that the unrighteous are more blessed than the once righteous. There is also a play-by-play given of a squabble over these carp images. Micah made them The Danites liked them and wanted them. The Danites steepled them, and when Micah chases the Danites down, wanting his idols back, he says to them, quote, You took the gods I made. Now think upon that statement. In his own words, Micah admits that the idols, these so-called gods, were man-made. What kind of gods are these that could be made by a man? And what kind of gods can be stolen? The scene is odd, is weird, it is ridiculous. The description of this squabble is embarrassing, and yet each party is blind to their own ridiculous behavior. The final description of the tribe of Dan was how they set up house in their new land. Their setup worship was, again, obviously a violation of God's law, which states that God was to be worshipped in a place of his choosing. Of course, the use of idols was a clear violation of the second commandment, but none of this seemed to matter to the people of the tribe of Dan. It did matter to God, however, and although it would be centuries later, we are given God's ominous verdict of the Danites They would be wiped out by the Assyrians in the 8th century BC. And as it turns out, we will never hear about them as a single tribe again. What brought families like Micah and the tribe like Dan to worship false idols? is not complicated. And it's actually stated plainly in the text. The first thing was assimilation of pagan idols and rituals into Israel's faith and their worship of God You will remember that when we began our study of Judges, we labeled the sin syncretism, which is the assimilation of other religions into Israel's faith in God. Such sin is obviously repeated over and over again in Israel's history. Israel does not seem to be able to escape the trappings of each of the ages in which they lived. They do not reject Yahweh altogether, and they even at times do all that God requires while adding more in terms of the worship of false gods and sinful rituals. The Christian Church, both Roman Catholic and Protestant alike, have been guilty of doing the same down through history and in our contemporary expressions. Roman Catholics placed tradition and evolved dogma on an equal level with Holy Scripture. Examples are dogmas such as the teaching of the existence of purgatory. As Article 22 of our 39 articles states Purgatory is a fond thing vainly invented and grounded upon no warranty in the scripture. Protestants in like manner place emotion and personal preferences also on the same level of Holy Scripture. Which is actually closer to acting like the Israelites in the book of Judges, as everyone did what was right in their own eyes. The following quote is from a thesis paper done by Dr. Elizabeth Cook. It is titled The McDonald's of the Megachurch. This quote sums up the reality of what is going on today. Quote, the content of worship in these megachurches is aimed at a target consumer. Mega churches take many approaches with this. Some pick a particular population segment, and all services are aimed at that particular social group. A contemporary approach complete with guitar and drums is often the case if a church desires to attract Generation Xers or younger. To attract the baby boomer generation and their more conventional parents, traditional four-count hymns with traditional sermons are a possible or a possible, but a less probable drawing card. Mega larger, most mega larger churches, however, try to broaden their appeal to satisfy several social groups using one of two approaches. The first approach is to offer different types of services with different messages, music, and general worship styles. End quote. And I simply say to that, beloved, the gospel is not a product to sell. And people made in God's image are not to be consumers of worship styles. The second thing, which can actually be labeled the first thing, because it leads to assimilation or leads to syncretism, is that Israel had no king. And the result was that everyone did what was right in his or her own eyes. From the statement that Israel had no king It is not for us to conclude that once they have a king, they will behave differently. To say that Israel had no king is to say that they had no godly leadership. There was no one to point them in the right direction, to lead them into the right battles, or to live out a life by example for the rest to follow. As we learn in the book of 1 Samuel, Israel had a king. They had a king to lead them in all that was necessary, but he was rejected. That king was God himself. God wanted to be Israel's sole king, but he was rejected and replaced by got by the gods of other nations. Or for men who could be seen on earth in their thrones, but certainly not in heaven. That Jesus was given the title King of Kings and Lord of Lords is for us who know Israel's past to compare the men of Israel And recognize that Jesus, even he, was rejected, a man without sin, sacrificing for their lives. Jesus, who is now seated at the right hand of the Father. Today, we may describe unbelievers as those who have no king. If they do not acknowledge Jesus as King of Kings and Lord of Lords, they have no king, for all other kings are false imitators. The only person on the throne of the life of an unbeliever is the unbeliever himself. The byproduct of or fruit of men being kings unto themselves or men doing that which is right in their own eyes is all around us. Consider that the American Medical Association just last week began debating whether they should recommend states removing the category of sex from birth certificates Consider that secular classrooms are allowing teachers to teach very young students that their gender is a choice. Consider that public school boards are outwardly proclaiming that parents should not have the last say when it comes to raising their children. Consider how we continue to hear from secular media that babies in wombs are choices rather than human. How does the culture get to such a state of confusion? The answer is we have no king. We do not have the king of kings. A people who are not led by Jesus have a fool for their leader. Truth itself is defined by those who have no king as what an individual wants it to be. What is spoken to authorities, the courts, the government Spoken to a spouse, spoken to children, does not have to be factual, but simply in accord with the one who is speaking. For those who have no king, truth is subjective. Truth is elusive. Life is defined by those who have no king as personal. Each person who can carry an infant in her womb can decide whether the child lives or dies. Each person who is facing serious illness or injury can decide whether he or she will live or die. Each person in a depressed state is understood to be capable of deciding whether her life is now worth living. There is no creator to be accountable to for life because there is no king. These are just a few examples of how people live with no king. There are many minor things like manners, etiquette, courtesy, and decency. That are unknown because men without God only do that which is right in their own eyes While Israel lived in a state of odd, weird, and strange confusion, as if they have no king, there was a king. There was and still is the same king who is willing to reign over the hearts of men. And not, mind you, in order to control people or oppress people, but to help them to live the life he intended for them. That king of course is the king of kings. He is the Alpha and Omega. He was in the beginning. He is the only one who can bring calm to chaos and peace to contention. You need that king. I need that king. Our culture needs that king. Remember what God wants, what he is after. He wants to be our king and for us to be his people. That is his heart. And what his heart wants is for our greatest benefit. So it starts with each of us individually. Each of us must choose Jesus as our personal king. And you might say to someone, well I've already done that. Beloved, choosing Jesus as your King is something you must do each day, every day. And as a church, we need to agree to choose Jesus as our corporate king. And we need to invite as many as we know to join us in choosing Jesus as our king. And if God wills it, then maybe our community will choose him as king. Maybe our county, maybe our state, maybe our country, maybe our culture. Can we imagine turning our culture around? Having a culture that chooses Jesus as their King of Kings. Is that possible? Why not find out? Let us pray. We thank you for this challenging message to make Jesus our King every day, in each moment of every day. And we ask that you might increase our faith to believe that if we make Jesus our King individually in our families and in our church, that it might spread That it will spread to our community, to our county, to our state, to our entire culture. Increase our faith, Heavenly Father. May your will be done. In Jesus' name we pray. Amen.

sermons.title: We still need a King
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. I not only encourage you, but I implore you to turn in your Bibles to Judges chapter 19 As we are going to be reading from the text, starting at Judges 19, before we, as you do that, I Saw something on social media that struck me as I, Bobby Lind and I have been reflecting on what it was twenty years ago that happened. and all that's transpired since. But I saw on social media someone posted, I long for the spirit of nine twelve. I thought that's rather poignant to uh to say. Um on nine eleven I was actually in school here with the students and we were watching the events on television and I had to go to the hospital to visit one of the parishioners and uh on my way the second tower fell. It was all quite dramatic on the uh radio. And then as I got out of my car I was wearing my clerics. And every person I passed on that street, I I usually park on the street at Johns Hopkins and walk over a couple of blocks, and every person that passed me either bowed to me or said, please pray for us It was quite a spirit in response to the clergy in a moment of crisis. And it struck me how necessary it is to take a humble position before you're able to learn, before you're able to receive. And so it is that we were humbled on that day, and as a nation we were ready to receive, receive the mercies of God May we pray that we could return as a people back to that humility and be ready to receive what God has for us. Amen. As I said, turn with me to Judges 19. We have described these final chapters in Judges as odd and strange. What we have read and will cover today will verify that description. There is a progression we are to notice. of how ungodliness of pagan people has affected the ungodliness of God's people First, it has negatively affected a family, who we know through the person of Micah. Then it affected a whole tribe, the tribe of Dan. And now at the end of the book of Judges, we realize that the whole nation of Israel is in confusion about acceptable worship unto God, and they are in confusion about their morality. This is another piece of evidence showing a connection between our worship and our morality. We will see in these passages that Israel is so confused as a people that even when they try to get it right, they get it wrong. This sermon, as I said, will be different than I have done before. We will be covering three chapters today I will read large sections of the text and follow up each section read with summary comments. Once we get all passages read, we will highlight the primary lesson. Now, verses 1 through 10 of chapter 19 has already been read, so I'm not going to do that again. But two points are worthy to mention. First, what we learn from this passage as it immediately follows the narrative of Micah's household and the tribe of Dan. Is that public good cannot be divorced from private virtue? I'll say that again. The public good cannot be divorced from private virtue. Individual behavior has an effect upon the family and society. Second, all of the characters in this story remain anonymous. The purpose is for the reader, you and me, not to focus on individuals. But to understand that the concubine here could be any concubine, the Levite priest could be any Levite priest, that the concubine was not the wife of the Levite sets the moral climate of the time. And I would also say it should remind you of another story, the father-in-law not allowing his son-in-law and wife to leave. Goes back to Jacob and Laban. As I said, verses one through fifteen has already been read, so eleven through fifteen we have the Levite and his concubine. Not able to find hospitality. And that is a continuing description of the moral climate of the day Hospitality is a virtue in most parts of the world, but especially for the Israelites. You remember that God uses hospitality to explain to them how He treated them. He took them in. They were strangers, and he brought them into his household, and so he expects the Israelites to bring in strangers into their households. Then we have sixteen through thirty. Sixteen through thirty Just then an old man came in from his work in the field at evening, who also was from the mountains of Ephraim. He was staying in Gibeah, whereas the men of the place were Benjamites And when he raised his eyes, he saw the traveler in the open square of the city, and the old man said, Where are you going, and where do you come from? And he said to him, We are passing from Bethlehem to Judah, toward the remote mountains of Ephraim. I am from there. I went to Bethlehem in Judah. Now I am going to the house of the Lord. But there is no one who will take me into his house, although we have both straw and fodder for our donkey, and bread and wine for myself and your female servant And for the young man who is with your servant, there is no lack of anything. And the old man said, Peace be with you. However, let all your needs be my responsibility. Only do not spend the night in the open square. So he brought him into his house and gave fodder to the donkeys, and they washed their feet and ate and drank. As they were enjoying themselves, suddenly a certain men from the city, perverted men surrounded the house and beat on the door. They spoke to the master of the house, the old man, saying, Bring out the man who came to your house that we may know him carnally. But the man, the master of the house, went out to them and said to them, No, my brethren, I beg you, do not act so wickedly. Seeing this man has come into my house, do not commit this outrage. Look, here is my virgin daughter and the man's concubine. Let me bring them out now. Humble them and do with them what as you please But to this man do not do do not do such a vile thing. But the men would not heed him. So the man took his concubine and brought her out to them, and they knew her and abused her all night until the morning And when the day began to break, they let her go. Then the woman came as the day was dawning, and fell down at the door of the man's house, where her master was, till it was light. When her master arose in the morning and opened the doors of the house and went out to go his way, there was the concubine, fallen at the f at the door of the house, with her hands on the threshold. And he said to her, Get up, let us be going. But there was no answer. So the man lifted her on to the donkey, and the man got up and went to his place. When he entered his house he took a knife, and lay hold of his concubine, and divided her into twelve pieces, limb by limb. And sent her throughout the territory of Israel, and so it was that all who saw it said, No such deed has been done or seen from the day that the children of Israel came Up from the land of Egypt until this day, consider it, confer, and speak up. The reader should recall the scene of Sodom and Gomorrah as we read these verses. The NIV calls the men wicked. The literal translation from the Hebrew is men of the sons of Belial, which is the devil's men. These men are not from Sodom and Gomorrah, but are instead Israelites who are evil enough to be called the devil's men. The old man and the Levite do not see with any moral clarity whatsoever. The old man settles for what he considers a lesser sin, the corruption of his daughter. The Levite certainly appears heartless, for not only does he give his concubine over to the devil's men, but after she is used and abused, he expects her to get up and travel as if nothing has happened. Both these men exhibit a loss of chivalry and a disregard for covenantal male headship Which calls for a man to protect a woman, not throw her to abusers. The cutting up of the concubine is a gruesome act, indeed. Obviously, the Levite wanted a dramatic response from all of Israel, and that is what he received. There is a depth in truth not often discussed or acknowledged here, the sending out pieces of the concubine to each tribe in Israel communicates that all are responsible to see that justice is done. There is in Scripture an awareness of corporate sin as well as individual sin When the sin of some, corporate sin, is not addressed, it becomes the sin of all. Chapter 20, verses 1 through 11. So all the children of Israel came out from Dan to Beersheba, as well as the land of Gilead. And the congregation gathered together as one man before the Lord at Mizpah. And the leaders of all the people and all the tribes of Israel presented themselves in the assembly of the people of God Four hundred thousand foot soldiers who drew the sword. Now the children of Benjamin heard that the children of Israel had gone up to Mitzpah. And the children of Israel said, Tell us, how did this wicked deed happen? So the Levite, the husband of the woman who was murdered, answered and said, My concubine and I went into Gibeah, which belongs to Benjamin, to spend the night. And the men of Gibeah rose against me and surrounded the house at night because of me They intended to kill me, but instead they ravished my concubine so that she died. So I took hold of my concubine, cut her in pieces, and sent her throughout all the territory of the inheritance of Israel. Because they committed lewdness and outrage in Israel. Look, all of you are children of Israel. Give your advice and counsel here and now So all the people arose as one man saying, None of us will go to his tent, nor will any turn back to his house, but now this is the thing which we will do to give to Gibeah. We will go up against it by lot. We will take ten men out of every hundred throughout all the tribes of Israel, and a hundred out of every thousand, and a thousand out of every ten thousand, to make provisions for the people That when they come to Gibeah in Benjamin, they may repay all the vileness that they have done in Israel. So all the men of Israel were gathered against the city, united together as one man The call to the response of the entire nation is a good sign. They're responding, they want to have justice done. Although the account told to the tribes by the Levite, notice that it leaves out any culpability by the Levite himself, as if he did nothing to contribute to her demise. 12-23. Then the tribes of Israel sent men through the tribe of Benjamin, saying, What is this wickedness that has occurred among you? Now therefore deliver up the men, the perverted men who are in Gibeah, that they may put them to death and remove the evil from Israel But the children of Benjamin would not listen to the voice of their brethren, the children of Israel. Instead the children of Benjamin gathered together from the city to Gibeah to go to battle against the children of Israel. And from the cities at that time the children of Benjamin numbered twenty-six thousand men who drew the sword. Besides the inhabitants of Gibeah, who numbered seven hundred select men Among all those people were seven hundred and select men who were left-handed. Every one could sling a stone at a hair's breadth and not miss. Now besides Benjamin, the men of Israel numbered four hundred thousand men who drew the sword. All of these were men of war. Then the children of Israel arose and went up to the house of God to inquire of God. They said, Which of us shall go up first to battle against the children of Benjamin? The Lord said, Judah first So the children of Israel arose in the morning and encamped against Gibeah. And the men of Israel went out to battle against Benjamin, and the men of Israel put themselves in battle array to fight against them at Gibeah Then the children of Benjamin came out of Gibeah, and on the day cut down to the ground twenty-two thousand men of Israel, of the Israelites And the people, that is, the men of Israel, encouraged themselves again, formed the battle line at the place where they had put themselves in array on the first day. Then the children of Israel went up and wept before the Lord until evening, and asked counsel of the Lord, saying, Shall I again draw near for battle against the children of my brother, the Benjamin? And the Lord said, Go up against them. So here is described a very bad sign for the state of the people as the Benjamites cover up the sin of the men who are guilty. It is seen by the tribe as more virtuous to protect evil men from the consequences of their actions than to see that justice is done. Verse 24 through 36. So the children of Israel approached the children of Benjamin on the second day And the Benjamin went out against them from Gibeah on the second day, and cut down to the ground eighteen thousand more of the children of Israel. All these drew the sword. Then all the children of Israel, that is all the people, went up and came to the house of God and wept. They sat there before the Lord and fasted that day until evening, and they offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the Lord. So the children of Israel inquired of the Lord. The ark of the covenant of God was there in those days And Phineas, Phineas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron, stood before it in those days, saying, Shall I yet again go out to battle against the children of my brother Benjamin, or shall I cease And the Lord said, Go up, for tomorrow I will deliver them into your hand. Then Israel sent men in ambush all around Gibeah And the children of Israel went up against the children of Benjamin on the third day, and put themselves in battle array against Gibeah, as at the other times. So the children of Benjamin went out against the people and were drawn away from the city. They began to strike down and kill some of the people, as at the other times in the highways, one of which goes up to Bethel, and the other to Gibeah. And in the field about thirty men of Israel. And the children of Benjamin said, They are defeated before us as at first. But the children of Israel said, Let us flee and draw them away from the city to the to the highways. So all the men of Israel rose from their place and put themselves in battle array at Baal Tamar Then Israel Israel's men in ambush burst forth from the position in the plain of Gebah, and the ten thousand select men from all Israel came against Gibeah, and the battle was fierce. But the Benjamites did not know that disaster was upon them. The Lord defeated Benjamin before Israel, and the children of Israel destroyed that day twenty five thousand one hundred Benjamites. All these drew the sword So the children of Benjamin saw that they were defeated. The men of Israel had given ground to the Benjamites because they relied on the men in ambush whom they had set against Gibeah. That the tribe of Benjamin experienced the first two victories probably surprises us. It is a lesson testifying to the confusion that Israel was in. Who is in the right is not clear. As is usually the case in a civil war, when each part of a nation carries guilt. The eventual victory over the Benjamites was the Lord's victory. And that is made obvious because of the two prior defeats. That God is responsible for the judgment of the tribe of Benjamin is clear in these passages. Verses 37 through 48. And the men in ambush quickly rushed upon Gibeah. The men in ambush spread out and struck the whole city with the edge of the sword. Now the appointed signal between the men of Israel and the men of ambush was that they would make a great cloud of smoke rise up from the city, whereupon the men of Israel would turn in battle. Now the Benjamin had begun to strike and kill about thirty of the men of Israel, for they said, Surely they are defeated before us as in the first battle But when the cloud began to rise from the city in a column of smoke, the Benjamites looked behind them, and there was the whole city going up in smoke into heaven. And when the men of Israel turned back, the men of Benjamin panicked, for they saw that disaster had come upon them. Therefore they turned their backs before the men of Israel in the direction of the wilderness, but the battle overtook them, and whoever came out of the cities they destroyed in their midst. They surrounded the Benjamites and chased them and easily trampled them down as far as in front of Gibeah toward the east. And eighteen thousand men from Benjamin fell, all these were men of valor Then they turned and fled toward the wilderness to the rock of Ramon, and they cut down five thousand of them on the highways, and they pursued them Relentlessly up to Gidam and killed two thousand of them. So all who fell to Benjamin that day were twenty-five thousand men who drew the sword. And all these were men of valor. But six hundred men turned and fled toward the wilderness to the rock of Ramon, and they stayed at the rock of Ramon for four months And the men of Israel turned back against the children of Benjamin and struck them down with the edge of the sword. From every city, men of beasts, and all who were found, they also set fire to all the cities they came to So the remains of the tribe of Benjamin are minimal. The tribe is almost wiped out Ironically, this was the type of destruction to be made upon the Canaanites when Israel first entered the Promised Land. Now it is being made upon God's people. By God's people. The punishment inflicted upon the women and children of Benjamin was excessive. And is once again a sign of the moral confusion among the Israelites. The behavior that follows Can be called total moral confusion. Chapter 21, verses 1 through 14 Now the men of Israel had sworn an oath at Mitzpah, saying, None of us shall give his daughter to the Benjamin as a wife. Then the people came to the house of God and remained there before God till evening. They lifted up their voices and wept bitterly, and said, O Lord God of Israel, why has this come to pass in Israel, that today there should be one tribe missing in Israel? So it was on the next morning that the people rose early and built an altar there, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. The children of Israel said, Who is there among all the tribes of Israel who did not come up with the assembly to the Lord? For they had made a great oath concerning anyone who had not come up to the Lord at Mitzpah, saying, He shall surely be put to death. And the children of Israel grieved for the Benjamin, for Benjamin, their brother, and said, One tribe is cut off from Israel today. What shall we do for wives for those who remain? Seeing we have sworn by the Lord that we will not give them our daughters as wives. And they said, What one is there from the tribes of Israel who did not come up to Mispah to the Lord? And in fact, no one had come up to the camp from Jabash Gilead to the assembly. For when the people were counted, indeed, not one of the inhabitants of Jabash Gilead was there. So the congregation set out there twelve thousand of their most valiant men and commanded them, saying, Go and strike the inhabitants of Jabesh Gilead with the edge of the sword, including the women and children. And this is the thing that you shall do. You shall utterly destroy every male and every woman who has known a man intimately So they found among the inhabitants of Jabash Gilead four hundred young virgins who had not known a man intimately, and they brought them to the camp of Shiloh, which is in the land of Canaan. Then the whole congregation sent word to the children of Benjamin, who were at the rock of Ramon, and announced peace to them. So Benjamin came back at that time, and they gave them the women whom they saved alive of the women of Jabez Gilead and they had no y and then yet had not found enough for them So the oath made was to create unity among the different tribes. The irony of the oath is that the law forbids an intermarrying between Canaanite nations and Israel. There was not a law that forbid intermarrying between the tribes of Israel. Thus, here we have the beginning of good intentions, but again, a lack of a moral compass. The weeping is caused by the realization of what that has been done to a tribe in Israel. The solution is to pass judgment on others The behavior of the elders has been described as a comedy of correctness. Unfortunately, the virgins of Jabez Gilead are not enough, actually, 200 short. Verses fifteen through twenty-five. And the people grieved for Benjamin because the Lord had made a void in the tribes of Israel. Then the elders of the congregation said, What shall we do for wives for those who remain, since the women of Benjamin have been destroyed? And they said, There must be an inheritance for the survivors of Benjamin, that a tribe may not be destroyed from Israel. However, we cannot give them wives from our daughters, for the children of Israel have sworn an oath, saying, Cursed be the one who gives a wife to Benjamin Then they said, In fact, there is a yearly feast of the Lord in Shiloh, which is north of Bethel, on the east side of the highway that goes up from Bethel to Shechem, south of Labonah. Therefore they instructed the children of Benjamin, saying, Go, lie in wait in the vineyards, and watch, and just when the daughters of Shiloh come out to perform their dances Then come out from the vineyards, and every man catch a wife for himself from the daughters of Shiloh, then go to the land of Benjamin. Then it shall be, when their fathers or their brothers come to us and complain, that we will say to them, Be kind to them for our sakes, because we did not take a wife for any of them in the war. For it is not as though you have given the women to them at this time, making yourself guilty of your oath. And the children of Benjamin did so. They took enough wives for their number from those who danced, whom they caught Then they went and returned to their inheritance, and they rebuilt the cities and dwelt and dwelt in them. So the children of Israel departed from there at that time, every man to his tribe and family They went out from there, every man to his inheritance. In those days there was no king in Israel. Everyone did what was right in his own eyes. So the answer to the need for more women is to force the other other young women into marriage. We, the readers, are supposed to notice the hypocrisy. These men are giving the daughters of Israel away in the harshest and cruelest of fashions. The end result is that the punishment for one woman being raped is to allow the rape of 600 women. As usual, when men have lost their moral compass, women take the brunt of the repercussions. One of the great ironies of our modern struggles is that as women accept that there is no distinction between male and female, The quicker female influence fades into obscurity, and the abuse of women increases What happened in Israel at the end of Judges has served as a deep lesson for the people of God. The prophet Hosea refers to this story that we have read when he describes the judgment to come of the northern tribes. Hosea 9 9 says. They have sunk deep into corruption, the people of God, as in the days of Gibeah. God will remember their wickedness and punish them for their sins. Thus, the sin of Israel at Gibeah, recorded in these last three chapters of Judges, the chapters we just read, is a watermark for the sin of Israel. It becomes an example to God's people as to what happens to them when they forsake the one true God and then assimilate into their worship the ethic, the ritual, the morals of the pagan world. The primary sin of Israel in these stories is not the sexual perversions displayed by these devil's men. And enacted on the concubine of the Levite. It is not the Benjamites harboring the guilty. The primary sin is not the irrational vow made at Mitzvah. It is not the giving away of Israel's daughters to undeserving men. All of these are sins, of course. But what causes these sins, what is at the root, is having other gods before the one true God. From the breaking of the first commandment Folllows all the rest. Be reminded as you reflect on these stories of St. Paul's letter to the Romans In the first chapter of that epistle, he explains how God turns people over to their primal lusts, and men become attracted to men and women to women. God gives people over to such lust because they have first and foremost abandoned him as their king. Sexual perversion is not the greatest of sins. It seems to be the most interesting, but it is not the greatest. It is actually a byproduct of removing God from the throne of our hearts, from the throne of our families, from the throne of our churches, from the throne of our communities. Another byproduct of removing God from his rightful throne is the mistreatment of women. Remember Adam placing blame on Eve. Remember Abraham giving his wife over to a stranger. Women have been mistreated down through the ages simply because men have dethroned God from their personal lives. And society, resulting in women being treated as mere objects of lust or as property to buy and to sell. And woe to any man. Woe to any man who uses the Christian faith to force his wife into a submissive role. where he can be served and she can be mistreated. Such is not loving a wife as Christ loved his church. Such men should be outed and shamed until they repent. There are many well-meaning Christians in our country that believe that sexual sins can be overcome by legislation and court rulings There are well-meaning feminists who believe that women will be properly respected if there is legislation passed and court rulings made in favor of equal rights. Of course, both groups missed the mark. The answer is God reigning as king in the hearts of men. And the only way that that will happen is if men confess Jesus as their Lord and Savior. This sermon is sounding an awful lot like last week's sermon. It should. The point is still being made. The lesson from the last five chapters in Judges is how a people become corrupt. And confused when God is not their king and they do that which is right in their own eyes. The solution to this is what has always been. Repent and confess Jesus as King and Lord. Do so individually, do so corporately. Excuse me I remember after my conversion to Christianity, a saying that was used That was a challenge to people who were claiming to be Christian, but were not living as if Jesus was their king. It was a challenge something like You have to accept Jesus as your Savior and accept him as your Lord. It's clever. But it misses the point that if Jesus is your Savior, he is automatically your Lord, your King. If Jesus is not your King, he is not your Savior. Make him your Savior, which is making him your King. And do so every day of your life. And as we do, may we continue to pray that his kingdom will come and his will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Let us pray Our gracious and merciful Father. Once again, we are confronted with the reality of what happens to men who do not make you their king. And so we are once again challenged to do so individually, to do so corporately, and to pray that your kingdom will come. And so we pray this once again. And Father helped us to be people of honor, making you our King each and every day. We pray this in Jesus' name. Amen.
