Within all the symbolism and dramatic imagery of Revelation chapter 9, within all of that is the simple message That evil is practiced by men and spiritual powers of the first type, that which loves evil. Because such evil, because such evil men will suffer at the hand of God. When reading passages like Revelation 9, we can get caught up in all the strangeness and drama of what John is describing, and try to understand it using what we know about the contemporary world while failing to see the message given and the lessons learned. Today we will start with an image described and come back to what we must learn. As we read what happens when the fifth angel sounds his trumpet, We have to remember that all of this is taking place in the context of the seventh seal being broken. When the seventh seal is broken, the seven trumpets are blown. We are taking the position that the events revealed of the blowing of each trumpet run concurrently with the events revealed at the breaking of the previous seals. John describes a star falling from heaven when the fifth trumpet is blown, causing us to remember the stars he saw falling from heaven onto the earth with the breaking of the sixth seal. The obvious difference is that this is one star, and it is revealed that the star is a being. The star that fell from heaven was given the key to the bottomless pit. What does that mean? Stars are used to describe those who are in high positions in the Old Testament. Stars can be men. Stars can be angels. Satan, you remember, in Isaiah, is referred to as the son of the morning and having fallen from heaven. Which is consistent with the description of our Lord that he gave to his disciples when they came back. He sent them out, you recall, and they came back. Finding miracles done by their own hands and success in preaching the gospel. And Jesus says, I beheld Satan as lightning falling from heaven. Because Satan is given the keys to the abyss, we next recall that Jesus revealed himself in chapter 1 of Revelation as being the owner of the keys of heaven and hell. For Satan to be given the keys means it had to be given to him by Jesus. It appears that they were given to him for a specific time so that he could perpetuate evil. God does judge like that, allowing evil men to practice evil. Without hesitation, Satan does just that, for he is one of those who are evil continuously There is no hope within him, for he has fully rebelled against God. The opening of the abyss causes smoke to rise out. Allowing us to be reminded of the inferno that suffers all beings that have rebelled against God, both fallen angels and men. The smoke darkens the sun, causing an atmosphere of blindness and confusion. What comes next out of the pit are locusts. Only these are not insects. Locust, do you remember, was a plague on Egypt, and after Pharaoh suffered it, he initially allowed the people to go and then reneged on the promise. Pharaoh, like the devil, clung to evil. The instruction given to the locusts not to hurt any green things, but only men. Tells the faithful that these locusts are not like the locusts released upon the land in Egypt. These locusts are blood seekers. The description of the locusts tells us that they are creatures specially equipped for the task they are released to do. Suck blood. Their faces, like men, tell us that they can be like any of us. Their hair, being like women, tells us that they can be deceptive, as they appear to be something they are not. Their teeth, like a lion that sting like a scorpion, tells us that they are deadly. Some scholars believe that these locusts are symbols of heretics and infidels. Some have even identified them as Muslims. Such identity made sense to Christians who fought followers of Islam in Spain and Turkey and in Jerusalem in the Middle Ages. The followers of Muhammad wore long hair and carried a great sting with their swords. However We reject that interpretation because John's vision is not limited to one moment in history. An important instruction that should help us identify the locusts is that they should only hurt those men who do not have the seal of God on their foreheads. We spoke earlier about such a seal, and I explained how the seal is not something that one sees, but what only God knows. And we as a church represent that seal at baptism, just as we did this morning, giving each baptized child the sign of the cross cannot be seen But it is God marking his own people. Because the locust cannot hurt those with such a seal, and we know by experience That many Christians, too numerous to count, have been killed by the sword. It is wise to understand the sting of these locusts to be spiritual in nature. In other words, they are given the charge to hurt men spiritually. They cannot hurt those that God has redeemed, but they can torment those who are dead in their sin. They blind them by smoke and poison, poison by their sting of their tails, which means they delude their minds. To lose their minds to thinking there is no God, and if there is, he certainly is not Jesus Christ, and thus I do not need to repent, and I do not need to cry out for mercy. Deception and not physical strength is the greatest weapon wielded by the devil and his angels. The subversive tactics of the devil are covert. The devil and his demons convince men that religion is for the weak or the ignorant or both. Other men are convinced that all religions are the same. Still others are convinced that religion is the cause of the woes of mankind. And others masquerading in the church are deceiving into being puppets in the devil's play as they spread gossip, slander, and false teachings amongst God's people, convinced all the time. That God is actually using them. Of course, the devil does not openly reveal himself as the devil. He does not pass out his card before he deceives. Demons do not identify themselves as having come from the abyss. The only time the devil is overt is when he knows men will dress up in funny costumes or display him as a cartoon character. He then becomes something to laugh at rather than something to resist. He can make himself like us or an angel of light, but his teeth and his sting are deadly. Evil is practiced by the devil and his demons, beloved, and it is used to harm the souls of men. What is released from the abyss has true power, true power to deceive and destroy men Napollyon and his locust demons are not fictitious characters or symbols of private struggles within our psyche. They are real and they are hell-bent on destroying souls. Graciously, a reprieve to the badness is part of the instruction given to the demons as they wreak havoc upon men. The hordes from the abyss are given authority to torment God, to torment men, but not kill them. And the torment is for only five months. The five-month period refers to the locust season that lasts five months. Interestingly, usually from April to September. The result of the spiritual torment is great anguish among men who desire death. They would rather die than experience the torment. They become bitter of the soul. Souls that do not have God are souls that ultimately fill with bitterness. Life becomes a series of depressing moments, and soon meaning for today or hope for tomorrow is lost. Such men wish to die. Such men seek a right to die. They think there is no virtue in living, nor especially is there any virtue in suffering. So the only alternative is death. The hope we have for a reprieve is that the assigned work of the devil and his demons To deceive men has a particular time in God's plan and will not go beyond that time. The five-month reference simply means that there will be a season and that season will end. Verse 12 confirms the five months is a season of woe and gives warning of two woes to come. The blowing of the sixth trumpet reveals a voice from the altar in heaven, commanding four angels to be let loose to perform the specific tasks of judgment that have been planned for them. The altar described as the altar of incense that was before the curtain of the Holy of Holies, you remember, in the earthly temple. The horns of the corners of the altar that pointed up toward heaven were part of that. Because the four angels are let loose, they come from Euphrates. Why Euphrates? Well, that's in the north. And all of Israel's enemies came from the north. So Euphrates represents their enemies. Their breastplate reveals evil as well as the colors of fire, deep purple, and brimstone. These angels are the embodiment of fire and brimstone preaching. Their brushplate and configuration communicate judgment as they kill a third of the men that live on earth Once again, we must decide whether we are to understand the deaths of a third of mankind to be literal. This is especially difficult considering the specific time frame in which the prophecy was to occur. Because the judgment occurs by the powers of their mouths And their tail, which were like serpents, we may understand it to be both literal and spiritual. Literally, men are judged physically by the powerful tail of an evil being. Every generation gives birth to men who torture and kill even their own kind. But we can also take it spiritually, understanding that the power of the mouth leads men astray, leads the spirit of men astray. Oftentimes, as in the case of Historical figures like Hitler and Mussolini, men are killed by the power of false speech and the power of physical force. This is the second law, and thus the chapter ends with the described fate of those who were not killed, but in seeing what had happened to their fellow man, still this is the important point. Still, watching all of this, still chose not to repent of their sins. The judgment of a third of men Is their chance to confess their sin and to cry out for a Savior that their hearts are hardened? When men give themselves to evil, when they insist on following its immediate gratification, they find that evil practices soon control them. This is why there is a thin line between those who play at evil and those who are given over to it. Too often. Men think they can play with evil and always come back. Many do not come back. Because the men marked by God are not a part of the evil that take vengeance, or those that will be judged because of the evil they commit. It is curious to me why this vision is given to us. Why do we need to know what's going to happen to other people? Why do Christians need to be exposed to this vision in John chapter 9? I believe the answer lies once again in Jesus' words regarding the end of time. When Jesus warned of false Christs and false prophets that would appear, he said they would even deceive the elect if that were possible. But it's not possible. Christ has died for the elect. Christ has marked his own. They will not fall away. But the devil doesn't know that. And the devil doesn't stop trying. God protects those who are His, and although we may be harmed in body We are to be confident that our souls are protected by our Heavenly Father. But the devil still keeps trying What God does with such a vision as Revelation 9, such a vision of evil and its destruction, is to wake up the elect from complacency. That is to wake you up from complacency. Although we are told that those who have been marked will be spared from the scorpion's sting, the events revealed to us are here so that we might know the outcome. Might know the outcome of those who cling to evil. Might know the results Giving us the motivation to resist the devil again and to cling to what is good Also, we are to be scared into staying away from playing with the devil and believing we can walk in and out of evil practices with no harm to the soul. There is always endangerment of the soul when evil is practiced. When we read of men who refuse to repent We become troubled by the fact that they would cling to their sin when confronted by the judgment of God. But we should not be surprised. Drug addicts continually return to their supplier, even though they have lost their children, their home, and their livelihood. Men continue to debase themselves in sexual sin, even though their marriage is in shambles. Others continue to chase after material wealth, leaving behind children who are troubled. From such lives we can clearly see that giving over to evil has a price, and the price is truly greater than anyone can understand in this life. I was asked several years ago while looking at Psalm 51, the psalm that David praised after being confronted with his sin with Bathsheba. And the person asked me, they said, David prays that the Holy Spirit would not be taken from him, and yet God has already promised that he would not, that David would forever be in his line. Why would David praise such a prayer? And that question is essentially what I have described in reading why we need to hear the vision of Revelation chapter 9. The base answer is that God uses such a vision to wake us up. To wake us up to the evil that is hell-bent on stealing your soul. And being fully awake and paying attention to evil, that allows us to resist and to repent. Beloved, God's people are a people that repent. We look for opportunities to repent. And here today, he gives us another. Amen and Amen. Let us pray. Our gracious God for this vision of hell, this vision of Judgment, this vision of nasty, painful judgment. We pray that our souls would be awakened to realize The seriousness of evil, and how we must flee from it, and how we must be a people that repent, and how we must cling to the good. May it be so. In Jesus' name.

sermons.title: Eat the Scroll
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Ghost, Amen, please be seated Very much I want to encourage you to turn in your Bibles. Turn in your Bibles to Revelation 10. This is not going to go well if you're not able to follow along in the text. There is an immature paranoia that most of us experience when we perceive that we are being left out. For the personality that always wants to be in the know, being left out causes a high level of anxiety. I suspect that the reason for the anxiety is a bit of nosiness mixed with insecurity. Some people are tempted to be busybodies and therefore want to know all about the goings-on around them, even though they are not involved. Others are insecure about who they are and what others think of them, and knowing what others are saying and doing allows them to believe that they can control other people's perceptions And perhaps this is all unnecessary psychoanalysis, but I bring it up in response to what is revealed and not revealed in John's vision as recorded in Revelation 10. Thus far we have been privileged to see the inner sanctuary of the heavenly realm, and it would seem that nothing has been hidden from us. We have gone higher up and deeper in, as C. S. Lewis has said in the book, The Last Battle. And now we are told that there is a place where we have to stop By stopping, we are humbled with the realization that there are things we are not ready to know, and most certainly are not capable of understanding. It is my feeble observation that the popularity of a particular understanding of the end times that raptures the church to heaven before Armageddon is believed by many because it is so neatly ordered. That's my granddaughter. Because it's so neatly ordered. Such understanding of the end times was the first one that I embraced. And I did so because it mapped out quite a clear path for Christ to come again, except not offering an exact date Nothing is unknown in this perception of the end times. I have since abandoned such an interpretation because of passages such as this in Revelation 10 To cause a seeker to accept that there are things we simply will not know about the end times until they happen. It also came to my attention that this popular understanding of the end times, known as dispensational premillennialism. It takes a lot to say, that it was new to the Christian faith, meaning that it had not been taught in the church prior to the 19th century. So for 1900 years or more, nobody had ever heard of this understanding of the end times. Having said this, it is not my intention to malign one particular view of the end times and then promote another. Rather, it is our intention to study the scriptures and allow the Spirit of God to speak to us regarding what we ought to know about this John's revelation. Chapter 9 ended with the amazing stubbornness of men who were unwilling to repent of their sins, even in the midst of judgment. The judgment was made on a third of mankind and occurred at the blowing of the sixth trumpet. Remember, please, and this is where we get into the weeds. Remember, please, that there were seven seals to be broken. At the breaking of the seventh seal, there was the revealing of seven trumpets to be blown. As each trumpet is blown, the events revealed run concurrently with the events revealed at the breaking of the seven seals Stay with me. The vision of chapter 10 is a counting vision of the sixth trumpet and the seventh seal. If you have not kept up with what I have said, it is sufficient for you to know that chapter 10 and the beginning of chapter 11 are interlude visions between the blowing of the sixth and the seventh trumpet. Just like there was an interview, I mean, interlude between the revealing of the sixth seal and the seventh seal. From the unrepentant men in chapter 9, John's attention is turned toward a mighty angel coming down from heaven. Robed in a cloud with a rainbow above his head, having the face like the sun, and legs like fiery pillars. The description, you will note, is similar to the one of Jesus in chapter 1, and that this angel is immense. But this is not Jesus. It is an angel, a heavenly messenger, that is viewed in a grand stature symbolizing a grand purpose. The robe of clouds reveals his unearthly or heavenly origin. The rainbow symbolizes the completed covenant God has with his people. The brightness of his face and his fiery legs symbolize a two-fold mission. He brings a message of light and of judgment, and that's going to come back to us. The mighty angel holds a little scroll in his hand. The mention of the size of the scroll is to help the listener understand But the scroll he holds is not the same scroll that had to have seven seals broken by the Lamb. This little scroll contains something particular about the end of time. And it is open. Meaning that what is within is being revealed. Because of the immense angel that he plants one foot on the land and one foot on the sea is to be understood that what is within the scroll is going to affect the whole earth, because the whole earth is land and sea. The angel then shouts, and the shout is described as deep and powerful, such as that of a lion, only unlike any lion on this earth. There is no record of what was said in this shout. There may have been no words for a man to understand. What is important is the response to the angel's shouting. At the sound of the angel's voice, there were heard voices of seven thunders. To refer to thunder as voice is common in Scripture. In Psalm 29, the voice of God is described as thunder. It is powerful, it is majestic, it shakes the desert, it twists the oak trees. The voice of seven thunders is God's voice. And here again is the use of the number seven. We've seen this a lot in Revelation. There were seven lampstands, seven churches, seven seals, seven spirits, seven trumpets, and now seven thunders. It is expected by the reader that the seven voices or statements made by God would reveal even more about the end of time. And St. John is prepared to write it down and reveal it to the church, but he was stopped. He was stopped and told not to write down the things which the seven thunders spoke. The instruction to St. John is similar to the one given to Daniel. To Daniel, when he was given a vision regarding the end of time, the Lord said this to Daniel. But you, Daniel, close up and seal the words of the scroll, even to the time of the end. God has stopped us. He's keeping us out for a time. Similarly, our Lord Jesus said to his disciples, it is not for you to know the times or the seasons with which the Father has his own power. Not all of God's ways are to be known. God, in his tender mercy to his people, does not reveal all of his terrors. In truth, we are humbled by what we have been privileged to see and understand, and we are further privileged to trust that what is hidden from us is hidden for our benefit. And that all that will come to pass is controlled by our loving Heavenly Father. Regardless of what each of us accepts about the end times. It is necessary for each of us to be humbled by what we do not know and will not know until it comes to pass. In verses 5 and 6, it is natural for us to read exigency into the sworn oath of the angel. He swears that there will be no more delay, and from these words we expect that the end would occur at that announcement. But it did not, and still has not. An alternative translation, the King James, allows us to read the angel swearing that there should be time no longer. The New King James makes it sound as if all that has been promised will occur immediately. The King James Version simply guarantees that there will come a moment in which time as a measurement will no longer exist. Personally, I prefer the King James in this passage, for it fits with our experience. Meaning that there has been a delay. And it fits with the primary message of the church, which is that regardless of what is known or unknown about the end of time, the end of time will come. The end is what the angel is swearing will happen. This understanding brings verse 7 into a greater light. In the days when the seven seventh angel blows his trumpet, whenever that day is, we can be assured that the mystery of God will be accomplished, and that He has promised it As he did through the prophets. For the church suffering persecution, it is comforting to know that an end is assured. For the Christian dying by way of martyrdom, his soul is strengthened to know that there will be a time of vengeance. What happens next is again not unusual, at least to the biblical narrative and Jewish culture. And it is also a powerful symbol of what lies ahead for the prophet and anyone, that's laity and clergy alike, and anyone who would speak forth the word of God. John is instructed to take the little scroll from the hand of the mighty angel and eat it. He is told that the scroll will be sweet as honey to his mouth and bitter or turn sour as it is digested in his stomach. Culturally, it was the practice of some rabbis to begin instruction with little children. He would take them and sit them down, and he would take their slaves for which they would be writing their Hebrew And he would write the word Torah on their slate, and then he would place honey on the slate and instruct the little child to lick off the honey and thus and thus consume that which is sweet. But also Torah meaning the law, consume the law. It is quite possible that our Lord Jesus did something similar as a child. Biblically, the prophet Ezekiel was instructed in a similar manner as John. From Ezekiel chapter 2 and 3 we read: Then I looked and saw a hand stretched out to me In it was a scroll which he unrolled before me. On both sides of it were written words of lament and mourning and woe, and he said to me, Son of man, eat what is before you. Eat this scroll. Then go and speak to the house of Israel. So I opened my mouth, and he gave me the scroll to eat. Then he said to me, Son of man, eat this scroll I am giving you, and fill your stomach with it. So I ate it, and it tasted as sweet as honey in my mouth. Ezekiel later describes the bitterness that he felt when he had to speak to the people the words of the scroll, for again they were words of lament, of mourning, of woe. The harshness of the words made them bitter. From Ezekiel's experience We are to learn why the scroll eaten by John is sweet to the taste and bitter to the stomach. The reason the scroll, the word of God, that the prophet is to speak, tastes sweet at first, should be obvious to us. The gospel is sweet. It is good news to hear that the God of the universe is slow to anger, abounding in love, and gives promises of eternal glory. It is sweet to speak and to hear words of hope, joy, peace, forgiveness. We have the greatest message to speak for to humanity. And this positive message touches the deepest parts of the souls of men. For those who are weighed down by the guilt of their sin and the reality of their mortality, there can be nothing more peaceful. Than to know that God offers freedom from guilt and eternal life beyond the grave. Evangelism is simply sharing with others the sweetness of God's word. And yet it has been noted, it has been noted by preachers before me, the irony of the Christians The way we feel to share with our neighbors and friends the news about the gospel. We are so free to talk about the good restaurants that we enjoy or the good books we have consumed or good movies that we have enjoyed and headlines that we've read But shy away from sharing the good news of Jesus Christ. Contrasting such willingness to share about items of low priority compared to the message of eternal hope seems a little odd. We could reason that if those other items are worth making an effort to share, then surely the gospel is more worthy to be shared. But it is not that simple, is it? We don't like to share because as sweet as the gospel is to taste, there is a bitter side to it. We know there is a bitter side, and most of our neighbors and friends know there is a bitter side, and it is that bitter side that causes us to pull back, to keep silent. The bitter side is the lamenting, the mourning, and the woes that are part of the message that God has for us to share. We know well that for the sweetness of God's word to be its fullest, the bitter has to be known. We must speak the truth about hellfire and judgment for the forgiveness and the love of God to taste sweet, or taste as sweet as it should. But that part of the message, that hell, that judgment, that is not easy to speak. Like Ezekiel, Saint John is instructed to prophesy after he has consumed the scroll. His message is to be spoken to many people, nations, languages, and kings It is a message that will not be easy to speak, nor easy to hear, because of the judgment that is included with the sweet. The charge made to Ezekiel was to speak not to nations that did not know God, but to the people of Israel who should know God. Ezekiel was not pleased with this assignment, for he anticipated that it would not be well received by his fellow countrymen. For him to do as the Lord commanded, God said to Ezekiel that he would make him unyielding and hardened so that he would not shrink at saying what had to be said. Because of the similarities between Ezekiel and St. John, many scholars believe that the sweet and the bitter prophecies John was to speak From the scroll are to be directed primarily to the church, just as Ezekiel's were to Israel. And this should not surprise us when we consider what the church and individual Christians were going through in the days of Revelation up to today. The church has been persecuted, making the sweet bitter. The church has been disciplined by God, making the sweet bitter. The church has been oppressed, making the sweet bitter And individual Christians, Christians here today, have personally experienced the sweetness and bitterness of God's word, for we are being mocked by popular culture. No one eagerly wants to speak a message that is both sweet and bitter. It is inevitable that when the sweet and bitter word of God is spoken, the messenger will be blamed for the bitter. It is inevitable. It is inevitable that the messenger will be maligned for the bitter. The messenger will be identified with the bitter. The speaker becomes the negative one. He is the one accused of thinking that he's more righteous than the rest. The scoffers say he's the one that thinks he has a right to tell others what to do He's always telling others about their sin, but look at him. Who is he to point the finger? Ezekiel knew such rejection. For he testified that when he had to speak bitter words, that the people were overwhelmed. Because such criticism is unwanted, and feelings being overwhelmed are very real. Many shy away from what needs to be spoken. For the likes of Ezekiel and St. John, they did not have a choice. They were compelled to speak the message that is both sweet and bitter. Although none of us here is an Ezekiel or a St. John. Each of us is called to consume and speak the Word of God to your social circles, the social circles you occupy. A word of God spoken in those circles is going to be sweet and bitter. As followers of Christ, we too have no choice. Regardless of what we feel, regardless of how we fear. We are called to consume and speak, and it will be bitter, and it will also be sweet. Let it be so. Let us pray. A gracious and heavenly Father, we do take this vision of John And take it upon ourselves to realize that we have your word to consume, to enjoy, but also to speak, to speak it forth to a world that is lost and is getting more lost by the minute So we ask, give us the courage. Holy Spirit, you have not given us a spirit of timidity, but of power, of strength. May we use it as you call us to. In Jesus' name. Amen.

sermons.title: Choosing Sides
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. Turn in your Bibles to Revelation chapter 11. You are going to need to again walk. through these passages with me, Romans 11, Romans, Revelation 11, Revelation 11, chapters, or verse 1 through 14. Now I imagine that our study of Revelation during these past months has been difficult for some of you who miss a Sunday here and there. I imagined it to be similar to watching a movie and you keep having to get up several times to take care of the dog or whatnot, and upon returning you ask those who are there. What did I miss? Who's that person? Why did he do that? And so on. Unfortunately, I cannot get you entirely caught up on what you have missed, and I don't even think it would help when you heard the reading today. Who are these people and what is happening to them? What is going on? Well, first of all, this is an interlude period. between the blowing of the sixth trumpet and the seventh trumpet, and the trumpet blowing is all a part of the breaking of the seventh seal In the interlude vision of chapter ten, you remember that John the Revelator was instructed to eat a small scroll. And it was sweet as honey to his mouth and bitter to his stomach. We learned last week that the sweet taste is the good news of Jesus Christ. Who has offered himself as a sin offering for those who need God's forgiveness? The bitterness is the judgment And suffering that is part of living in the kingdom of God in this life. John was given a charge to speak to peoples, nations, and kings The message that he consumed that was both sweet and bitter. The position we will take this morning regarding the beginning of chapter 11 is that the content therein is the sweet It's the bitter message John was to eat, digest, and then speak. It begins with John being given an instrument of measurement, a ruler in our vernacular. and is told to measure the temple of God, to measure its altar, and to count the worshipers. For those who believe the temple of God had been destroyed at the writing of Revelation, this instruction is purely spiritual. For those like myself, who believe the temple was still standing at the time of John's vision, thus at the time of the writing of Revelation, before 70 A. D. The call to measure was literal. This instruction to measure the temple is similar to the one given to Ezekiel in chapter 40 through 43 of his prophecy. In Ezekiel, an angelic priest measures the ideal temple. Measuring is a symbolic action used in Scripture to divide between the holy And the profane. That which does not measure up is the profane. Measuring is like witness bearing. It is the precondition for judging. Measuring and witnessing correlates to guarding because it sets up boundaries and bears witness as to whether or not the boundaries have been observed. Along with being told what to measure, John is told what not to measure. The outer courtyard of the temple was built for Gentile worshippers. It was the outer courtyard where our Lord turned over those money changer tables while condemning them that they had turned a place of worship into a den of thieves. We are told that the outer court was not to be measured because the Lord had ordained for there to be A time in which the Gentiles would rule the holy city of Jerusalem and trample the outer court. Historic accounts inform us that the Roman Empire fits the description of such Gentiles when they sacked Jerusalem and burned the temple in 70 AD. The prophecy says that the outer court and the city of Jerusalem will be trampled on for 42 months. It was not by accident that the Roman siege of Jerusalem under Vespian and then Titus lasted three and a half years, from 67 A. D. to 70 A. D. Three and a half years is forty-two months. During the 42-month period, there were to be two witnesses. Clothed in sackcloth, who though they had the power of God and are slight excuse me, though they had the power of God, they are slighted by men. When their days are finished, there will be a great onslaught against them from hell itself. The witnesses will be put to death, and even the honor of a burial will not be granted them. But amazingly, after a period of three and a half days, they will be given new life. Terror will be felt by those who see the resurrection of these two witnesses In terror, they will hear the voice of heaven calling the witnesses home, and they will look on as the two witnesses ascend to heaven in a cloud. In the same hour as the ascension, an earthquake will strike down a tenth, a tenth of the city of Jerusalem, killing 7,000 people. The survivors will respond by giving praise to God. This is the summary of the vision, but what does it mean? To better understand, we must first recognize all of the symbolism that's involved. The city will be trampled by 40 for 42 months, and the witnesses will prophesy for 1,260 days. Each of these is a period of three and a half years. The number three and a half is half of seven. Seven is the number of completion. Three and a half is seven broken in half. Three and a half symbolizes brokenness. It is therefore a number that is not good in being the opposite of when God created all of his creation and said, it is good. Three and a half represents necessary brokenness. Next, there are two witnesses. There must be two witnesses according to Jewish law to verify a truth. There are also two lampstands that stand before the Lord. Light is the symbol of truth. The two olive trees supply the oil to the lamps of truth. The oil symbolizes the Spirit of God that guides men to truth. The lampstands are like the two witnesses, and the two witnesses are like the lampstands. The two witnesses wear sackcloth. Sackcloth is a garment for those who mourn and were worn by Elijah and the prophet John the Baptist. The identity of the two witnesses is unknown, but not mysterious. They have fire that comes from their mouths to devour their enemies As recorded in the book of Numbers, chapter 16, fire came down from heaven at Moses' word and consumed false worshipers that were rebelling against God. Similarly, fire fell from heaven at Mount Carmel and consumed Elijah's enemies when he spoke the word. From these accounts, fire became the standard symbol for the power of the prophetic word, as the Lord said to Jeremiah. Behold, I am making my words in your mouth fire, and this people are wood, and it shall consume them. So the witnesses also have the power to shut up the sky so that it will not rain. Elijah was given such a power, and it did not rain for three and a half years. There's that number again. They also had the power to turn water into blood and to strike the earth with every kind of play whenever they wanted. This is the same as Moses' power while leading the nation of Israel out of bondage from Egypt. From this evidence, it is natural for us to conclude that the two witnesses are Elijah and Moses. The same two witnesses that appeared on the Mount of Transfiguration with Jesus. Elijah is the representation of the prophets And Moses represents the law. Jesus said, the law and the prophets speak of me. Do you see the puzzle coming together? The person of Jesus and the gospel he came to proclaim are found in the law of Moses. In fact, Moses himself was a type or shadow of the coming Messiah. Elijah, in his words and actions, taught of Christ, and he too was a type or shadow of the coming Messiah. We must not, however, see it necessary to understand the two witnesses here in Revelation 11 to be actual or historical characters of Elijah and Moses. It is enough for us to understand that the witnesses represent what Elijah and Moses represented, the law and the prophets. Verse 7 says there will be a time in which the testimonies of the two witnesses will be finished. What that means, finished, is unclear. What is clear is that they will be killed by the beast that comes from the abyss. We know the abyss to be the burning depth of torment. It is the dark, raging deep where Satan and his evil spirits dwell. The abyss is hell The beast comes from the abyss and is a reference not describing, making it obvious that John expected his readers to be familiar with this meaning. You remember though that when Adam and Eve refused submission to God in the garden, they tried to attain their own godhood. They were choosing to submit to a beast, the serpent. By submitting to a beast, they became identified with beasts. Even in their redemption, you remember they were clothed with the skin of a beast to cover their nakedness. Beasts are consistently referred to in Scripture as being enemies of God. That's why we read from the Old Testament about Nebuchadnezzar. Who because of his pride was judged by God and became like a beast. Another example of beastliness That is in opposition to God and his people is contained in the dietary requirements for the Jews against unclean animals. Like the serpent or beast in the garden, all unclean animals eat dirt, that is refuse They crawl on the dirt with fleshly pads on their feet, making contact with the earth, and they revolt against human dominion by killing man and killing other beasts. To eat of such animal was to eat of beasts and to live as Satan lives. It was to eat of death, to eat of rebellion. Thus, the enemy of God and the church is represented by the title Beast. After the witnesses are killed, they are put on display for the whole world to see. If this is to be understood literally, we would have to imagine cable news organizations or cell phone footage for all to see. Not only will the bodies of the dead witnesses be viewed by all, but their death will cause a worldwide rejoicing They rejoice, even sending one another gifts, because the two witnesses tormented all the inhabitants of the earth. We know by historical precedent that a common enemy can make a strange for strange bedfellows The Soviet Union can be at volatile odds with the United States and still join forces to fight a Nazi regime. Shiites can hate Kurds or Hezbollah unless they are fighting against Jews. In this vision, given by St. John, the factions of the world send gifts to one another Because of their common enemy, and that enemy is dead. our Christian minds further confusion as we try to understand exactly who these witnesses are and what time of history or the future is the vision referring. Jesus is the only one that died at the hands of angry men and raised the third day, followed by ascending into heaven. This has caused scholars to wonder whether this vision is actually describing Jesus. After all, Jesus was a prophet, a witness like these two men. He was spoken of by the law and the prophets. He tormented rebellious men with his words of condemnation against self-adulation and cultural idolatry. All of these similarities could mean these witnesses represent Jesus. But no one confidently takes that position because obviously reasons such as Jesus being in a grave, not lying dead out in the open. Jesus ascended after 40 days, not immediately after his resurrection. And his ascension did not bring an earthquake that took the lives of 7,000 people. So far, as we have discovered, much of the symbolism in this vision, the meaning of the vision is still yet to be tapped. And I appreciate the honesty of learned men such as the late Bishop Frazier of Manchester, England, who said, I have no interpretation of this vision. I have no meaning at all. Personally, I have a desire to make a similar statement to you, but I anticipate that would not be received well. It is right for you to expect some application of my sermons to your life. Otherwise, why preach them and certainly why listen to them? I make it a point to present to you each Sunday something that you can be challenged to change in your life, or something that you can believe more deeply. I work to feed the Word of God to you that you might be nourished by it every Sunday. The same task is before me with this text, just as any other. It is quite likely that the vision John presents to us here is a mixture of events that have occurred or were occurring when John was writing or will occur It is quite likely that the symbolism of the passage is to take our minds beyond literal fulfillment, To a coming of the kingdom of God that is yet unknown to human experience. What we can take from the vision are at least three things Number one, the gospel we proclaim torments the rebellious. Number two, anger and violence will be expressed upon those who hold to the proclamation of the gospel. And number three, God will raise up those who are faithful unto death, and he will enact vengeance on those who rebel against him. Regarding the first, that the gospel torments the rebellious, the fire that comes from the mouth of the prophets condemns the guilty. Since all men are guilty of sin, all men feel the heat of the words. Regarding the second, anger and violence are expressed upon those who speak hard words The church, the messenger of the prophecies and law of God, will be hated and targeted to be silenced because of the truth it proclaims. Jesus clearly warned of this, and generations of Christians have known it to be so What I want burned in your mind, however, is the use of the numeral two in this section of Scripture. The use of the numeral two. First, this is the second law, the first use of the numeral two. Next, the measuring of John finds two sides, the worshippers of God and the Gentiles. Next, the time of destruction is forty-two months, a time which has a derivative of two Next, God has two witnesses, and their days of prophecy also have a derivative of two. Next are two olive trees, and then two lampstands. Finally, there are those who rejoice at the killing of the prophets, and those who gave glory to God, giving again only two sides. And because there are only two sides, two sides only, passages like this give all who hear them opportunity to choose which side you will be on. And just in case you don't see that a choice needs to be made today, you better notice You better notice that the same people who are promoting transgendering children are the same who insist that there are more than two genders. Are the same ones defending, mutilating children, are the same ones who perform drag queen dances before children. Are the same ones who think having abortion is a moral obligation to practice? Are the same ones who want to defend the pol defund the police and are the same ones who want to silence Christians. You may not choose a side, but they will choose a side for you And if you are against anything, anything they are for, you are an enemy, and it is personal. And so the third lesson is important, which is the resurrection and ascension of the witnesses, and the vengeance passed upon God's enemies. With it, we are assured that if we choose the side of righteousness, if we choose to be on the side of what the Bible teaches, We are assured that if we are faithful as the church in what we proclaim, God will be faithful in the end and reward to us heaven. We can also be assured that the enemies of God will be put down Notice notice that one tenth of the city will be destroyed. One tenth. A tenth is a tithe. God is owed a tithe. And if the city will not honor him, he will take what is his. 7,000 dead symbolize the number of completion multiplied by a thousand. God takes what is his, and the number that is judged will be complete. The use of symbolism and narrative in this vision gives warning to both the church and to the rebellious There are conflicts that have been, are being, and will be experienced between the church and the rebellious that will consist of proclamation, anger, retribution, fulfilled glory, and eternal judgment. For each ear that hears these words, it is for him or her to decide which side to be on. If you have not decided, now is the day of salvation. Let us pray. My gracious God, although there is much in this passage that is confusing, to our first hearing and much symbolism that needs to be brought out. There is no question that what you have done has painted us a picture of choosing a side. Choosing for eternity of life or eternity of death. Choosing for righteousness or sin. May those who are on the fence choose today, for today is their day of salvation. Amen and Amen.

sermons.title: Enjoy Your Life
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Be seated. I encourage you again to turn to Revelation chapter eleven following in verse fifteen through nineteen. That is our passage of scripture today, Revelation eleven beginning at verse fifteen. I do want to state also as you turn there, uh I did forget to mention, of course, that uh Bill Moores did pass away on uh Friday evening. Most of you I'm sure have heard that news. I don't have any updates in regards to when any services are being held. I believe it's going to be held here. But uh we do uh pray for Betty and the loved ones of Bill. He's going to be greatly missed. He was a mark in everybody's life who knew him, so we remember him well. As you listen to the reading from Revelation this morning, you have sensed an ending to the vision. If you did not know there were eleven chapters to be read, you could easily assume that The book was at an end. After all, we've learned of the seven seals, and at the breaking of the seventh seal, we learned of the seven trumpets. Before the last three trumpets were blown, we were warned by an eagle that there were three woes to come. In 1114, we are told that the two of the three woes have passed and that the third woe is coming soon. It is natural for us to assume from these words that we are about to hear the final woe. And since the seventh trumpet is blown according to verse fifteen, and there are only seven trumpets to be blown, it is understandable to expect that John's vision is over. The end, not just the end of his vision, but the end of the world as we know it has come. If you concluded this, you were correct. That's right, I said. Correct. What is revealed at the blowing of the seventh trumpet is the end. It is the end, in summary, placed in the middle of John's vision. The Princess Bride is a favorite movie of mine for various reasons. The movie is a depiction of a fairy tale as it is being read by a grandfather to his grandsons. The grandson is not thrilled about hearing a fairy tale, but soon finds himself engrossed in the story. In the first part of the story, the princess is captured by thieves who want to take her for bounty. The princess tries to escape from her captors by jumping out of the getaway boat that is sailing through eel-infested waters. As the princess bobs in the water, an eel starts toward her, and the sound of a shrieking eel is heard Just as the eel is about to strike, the scene is cut abruptly. The viewers are brought back into the bedroom of the little boy who is listening to the story, and the grandfather says to him She doesn't get eaten. The little boy is confused by this. The grandfather repeats himself. She doesn't get eaten by the eel. You looked worried, he said to the boy, so I wanted to relieve you The humorous part of the scene isn't the little boy denying that he was scared for the princess not wanting to admit that the fairy tale was actually exciting. Well, the vision we receive at the end of chapter 11 has a similar intent in mind for the concerned reader. Christians who are being persecuted for their faith are in need of encouragement, just like that little boy in his bedroom. The revelation provides encouragement in the midst of great upheaval, in the midst of violence, in the midst of mystery. We have just learned of the two witnesses that will be killed and then raised from the dead. We have just been warned that a third woe is coming. The intensity of the vision is frightening When it's taken all in at once, and so it is gracious for the reader or listener to be given a glimpse of the end, at least a summary, in order to be relieved. Just as the grandfather and the princess pride tells his grandson that the princess is not going to get eaten by the eel We too get a reprieve by being told that in the end, the kingdom of this world becomes the kingdom of Christ. Our Heavenly Father does this in other places. The prophet Isaiah is given visions of the demise of Israel, Egypt, and Assyria, to name a few. And usually within these visions of destruction. And judgment there is a reprieve. The reprieve takes the reader to a time of hope when men will be righteously judged and ruled by God Himself through His chosen Messiah. For example, after the described destruction of the promised land by means of judgment, the Lord promises a return of his people. To a land where burning sand will become pools of water and everlasting joy will crown the heads of all who return to the holy city. The message for the church in these verses of Revelation is a positive one. We are given a reprieve of hope. We are to be blessed by what we hear this morning. As I have already mentioned, the seven trumpets is sounded by the seventh angel in verse 15. It is a culmination sound and is responded to by voices that are not identified. There are loud voices in heaven which say, The kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of our Son, of his Jesus Christ, and he will reign forever and ever. At this pronouncement, we must stop and consider two things, at least. First, how the kingdom of the world ruled by Christ was different than before. After all, Christ reigns supreme over creation, even when Satan and his angels roamed the earth. Because the Godhead is sovereign over all creation, and Satan and his demons are part of that creation. The pronouncement of Christ's kingdom is at the blowing of the seventh trumpet undisputed You realize it is the devil's nature to mock, cajole, and lie about his power, about his authority. He claims authority on this earth, and he believes himself to be an equal in the battle with the Son of God And one of the devil's great lies upon humanity is dualism. It is the belief that good and evil are of equal power and they continue at odds. Eastern mysticism believes that good and evil have a love-hate relationship because although they are at odds, they need one another to balance the universe. Star Wars, anyone Such dualism is a lie that portrays Satan in a light that he can only wish for that is never known. At the time in history we now live, the sovereignty of God in Christ is disputed. It is disputed by men of other religions and men of no religion. At the blowing of the seventh trumpet, it will be undisputed. It will be clear to all regarding who truly reigns over all creation. The second consideration is how important these words are, knowing that such fulfillment has been the goal of the Lord from the foundation of the world. He has wanted to be the God of His chosen people. He has planned and moved in individual lives and through nations to bring about this very moment. The prophets have described it in various ways. Isaiah said it will be a day when jealousy will vanish. Ezekiel said it will be a day when plundering would cease and beasts would be cast out. Jeremiah said it would be a day when the law of God is written on the hearts of men. What prophets pointed to was the time of the Messiah. Jesus was the embodiment of the kingdom of God. When Jesus began his ministry, he announced that the kingdom of God, he himself, was upon men. Well he instructed us to pray. He told us to ask that the kingdom of God might come on earth as it already is in heaven. At the blowing of the seventh trumpet, this prayer is realized. When it is realized, it is a time of rejoicing. Because of the wanting planning and working toward this moment, the praise breaks out among the twenty-four elders around the throne. Verse 16 We now turn to the words of the worship of the elders that they speak before the throne of God. The first words are of thanksgiving. Men of God are thankful that the kingdom of the world is now the undisputed kingdom of Christ. The struggle over sin and death is over. The enemies of darkness that have tried to pull God-fearing men down have been vanquished The blowing of the seventh trumpet, the trumpet of completion, means that men who are pure of heart can now finally be at peace. Next is the description of the one to whom is given thanks. He is the one who is and who was. The passage, interestingly, is rare in that the King James Version and the New King James Version get it wrong, and the NIB gets it right. Surprise, surprise The New King James adds and is to come. But that's not in the text. That's not in the original text. That's not in the Greek. The translators put it there, believing it was mistakenly omitted. But he does not need to come, you see, for this is the end. And here is another reason why this passage should be understood as a summary statement of the end. Because it literally translates that God is and was. And there does not need to be a statement saying He is to come, for what was to be is in the future, is now realized. He's here. In verse 18, the words of the elders describe what happens in the end between God and the rebellious. The nations were angry, they say. We heard of such anger in the reaction of the people of the world to the testimony of the two witnesses described last week in the previous section of the chapter. I thought you might be interested to know that some theologians think that those two witnesses we talked about last week are a fitting image of the clergy and the laity. And I found that theory intriguing, for it recognizes different roles of laity and clergy in this life, both maintaining a singleness of mission. Often laity will expect the clergy to perform the role of evangelists when God has intended it to be done by the laity. Many are adept at inviting friends, neighbors, and co-workers, and even family to a church service, but fail to share about their own faith in Christ Jesus. The failure can work the other way as ministers are given opportunity to share the gospel but fail to grasp it because of the schedules they keep. I have learned of the importance of presence in my calling. I recall a time when I was in my study and having finished my sermon preparation, I decided just to sit and read. Unannounced, a woman came to the church looking for information about the school. I could have given her information and let her leave, but I decided to engage her in conversation. I soon found that she was unchurched and of Jewish heritage. In my half-hour conversation with her, I was able to share the gospel and connect it to her Jewish upbringing. It is one of the blessings of my calling to be able to have people literally drop in for help or for information about the school and to speak to them about their spiritual state I tell you this point to point out that testifying to the gospel is not done solely behind the pulpit. It is being present and available to others who wish to converse, to talk. Such testifying, such witnessing, done by both clergy and laity alike, is what is effectual for the kingdom of God. As we discovered last week, when the church testifies, when it witnesses, the nations become angry. Today we hear of Muslim nations outlawing proselytizing. With our visit to Greece a few years ago, we Found ourselves in a Turkish airport on Sunday, and I was determined to have prayer service, but it was difficult to find a quarter where we could pray. For although Christianity is not outlawed, it most certainly is against the law to proselytize in Turkey. Christians can be severely punished for witnessing Christ. Muslim nations outlaw Christian witnessing and are therefore of the nations that become angry because they know that Christ the Christian faith lived out In their land will tear down their false idols and strip them of their power. The words the elders describe of God's wrath upon the nations. In fact, the opening of the temple in heaven, followed by flashes of lightning and thunder, earthquake and great hailstorms, are descriptions of God's judgment upon the rebellious This reference to a heavenly temple uses Old Testament symbols to describe New Testament hope. You remember that the temple of old was a primary place of worship. It was a dwelling place of God on this earth. It represented God's presence. The Ark of the Covenant was an ornate golden box that contained the actual stones of the Ten Commandments and Aaron's staff. The ark symbolized God's power and was used as an instrument of punishment for those who rebelled against God and a blessing for those who obeyed him. The Ark of the Covenant was said to be lost when the Babylonians overthrew the city of Jerusalem. Legends said that Jeremiah was able to hide it in an unmarked cave. Its presence here in Revelation in the heavenly temple is not for the purpose of rejoicing about its return, but to show how the old covenant symbols have a new covenant place. Like the complete rainbow around the Savior's head, the temple and the Ark of the Covenant are heavenly symbols that the covenants are the same. They are now complete. Besides the destruction of God's enemies, the elders' words also praise God for rewarding the prophets and the saints. The prophets are witnesses who proclaim the gospel that angers the world. The saints are men and women, young and old, who have confessed their sins and trusted in the forgiveness of God offered through Jesus Christ. The prophets and the saints are those 144,000, or said better, thousands upon thousands. They're you and they are me. We are complete in this moment when we are around the throne praising our God for the forgiveness of sins. And it is remarkable that not only does he forgive us, but he rewards us. His reason for reward speaks to his empathetic character. He appreciates our struggles over sin. He embraces us for the humility we must know. He is moved by our willingness to endure trials and tribulations in this life. He loves us and so he rewards us. And I hope that doesn't sound as if we earn our rewards from God. I want it to sound as if God wants to reward us. He looks to reward us. He wants us to be at peace with him and our fellow men But the reward, the reward is not specifically described here. For again, this is a summary of the end We learn from the words of the prophets that the reward is like the Garden of Eden, where man was surrounded by beauty and took it in with all of his senses. We learn later in the revelation that the reward is like a city of peace, where there are streets of gold and mansions so large and numerous. For now, we don't marvel at the specifics, but simply we marvel at the knowledge that we will be rewarded. That is our reprieve. And we need to have reprieves. Recently, I listened to a panel discussion led by Dr. Jordan Peterson on the book of Exodus. And the panel, the panel spent time discussing each commandment. And the Jewish member of the panel, named Dennis Trigger, accused Christians Of only honoring nine commandments instead of ten, because much of Christendom ignores the fourth commandment, which is the commandment to honor the Sabbath day. I was convicted by that. The Sabbath is a reprieve given to us so that we might be at peace for a time each week. To live as if we don't need it is to claim a higher position, higher than God. For it was God who rested on the seventh day. It was God who hollowed the day which is set aside. It is God who made it holy. This isn't a sermon on the Sabbath, but the point must be made that we need reprieves, and God has commanded one. It is Sunday for the Christian. What this sermon is about is what the text is about, which is a retrieve from all the end times drama being described. God wants us to know the end so that we can endure the middle The media, our news sources, want us to believe that the time we are now living is the most tumultuous times ever in the history of America. The most dangerous of times, consisting of vast cultural differences, dangerous diseases. Deep political conspiracies, artificial intelligence taking over on the horizon, man-made climate change And apparently, that apparently endangers the very existence of humanity. And the belief that the intelligence of the commentators on the view will take over society. That is very scary. All that makes up this supposedly dangerous time But that is nothing compared to the victory Jesus has had and will be proved in the last day. And that known victory, that known victory is our reprieve that allows us to breathe. It is to calm us in the days in which we live. So have your babies. Enjoy your vacations. Work your job. Take your retirement. Enjoy your life. Never, ever let circumstances dictate your priorities. Because Jesus is on the throne and his ultimate victory is assured. We are allowed to rest and enjoy, if only for brief moments, for there is much to come Let us pray. Our gracious and heavenly Father, for this reprieve, for this moment in your scriptures, in the middle of This vision of revelation, you give us a reprieve to know that you indeed have the victory. You indeed have won to the end. And so we take that reprieve, and we take every moment that you give us that is a reprieve to allow our souls to rest with the idea that there is much to come. Bless our souls this way, we pray in Jesus' name. Amen.

sermons.title: Sacrifice
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Be seated. Turn in your Bibles to Revelation chapter 13. Want to be looking at our epistle reading. Revelation 13, verses 1 through 10. I ask, why is it that we become excited? To tell people news that we have just heard or seen. We are like reporters who want to be the first to get the scoop and then report the scoop. And it doesn't matter what it is. It could be a story about a past kidney stone that weighed ten pounds, a chocolate bar melting in the form of the Virgin Mary. Or breaking out of war in the Middle East. If we are the first to hear it, we work hard to be the first to tell somebody and be able to brag that we were the first to tell. The only problem is when you tell people earth-shaking news and they pass it on, and to whom they pass it on says, Who told you? They say, I don't remember. In the end, you have gone to all the trouble of being the first to break the story, and no one remembers that you broke it. Such is a scenario is related to what we are going to be exposed to this morning I'm going to be your hero today if you have always wondered who the beast is that is described in the book of Revelation. I am going to identify the beast and therefore solve the great mystery for some. You in turn, when you have the opportunity, will tell others Who the beast is, and when they ask you who told you that, you will say, I don't remember. Thus my legacy for solving the mystery will be short-lived, but I will enjoy it today Of course, I am not the first to solve the mystery, but many you will hear, many of you will hear it from me for the first time. So try to remember the source. From verse 1 of chapter 13, we learn that the beast is to be identified as different from Satan. We learned from the previous chapter that the dragon is Satan. The dragon has seven heads and ten horns with a crown on each of the seven heads. The beast also has ten horns and seven heads, but the crowns are on the beast on his horns, his ten horns, and not the seven heads. The beast also has a particular origin. The beast comes from the sea Hopefully you remember our discussion about the sea symbolizing pagan nations all the way from chapter 4. As the people of God are symbolized by land, the pagan nations are symbolized by the sea. Because the dragon comes from the sea, we understand that he comes from pagan nations, meaning also that he does not come from God's people. The description of the beast is a combination of feared and destructive carnivores, said to be a leopard, a bear, and a lion. In Daniel chapter 7, the prophet describes four beasts that have ten horns. Three of those beasts are the same that make up the beast in John's vision. Daniel the prophet emphasizes the dreadful look of those ferocious beasts, and that is to be the effect it's to have on the listener, to have some fear. The beast is to be understood as strong and terrifying. The beast is said to be given power by the devil or by the dragon. The power of the dragon includes his throne and great authority. His throne is this earth, and his authority is limited to this earth. Because of what happens to the beast, there is an increase of those who follow and worship it. The beast is given the ability to utter words that are boastful and blasphemous. It speaks these words and exercises the authority given to it for 42 months. That number is familiar to us. Forty-two months is the same as 1,260 days, or three and a half years, or times time and half a time. This is the same amount of time designated for the temple court to be trampled on by the Gentiles. It is also the same time that is given for the woman who is being protected from the dragon who is trying to kill her. Although the dragon could not kill the woman, or the church, as we identify her, the beast is able to conquer the saints of God. The difference would be that the church cannot be destroyed, but the saints can be physically armed. The conquering beast Is able to gain influence over all the known or inhabited world, bringing men to worship it John makes it clear that those who worship the beast are those who are John makes it clear that those who worship the beast are not those who follow the Lamb. They are not those who confess Jesus as their Savior. In general, we can say that the beast is a creature that is in a position of influence. He had something apparently miraculous happen that caused men to marvel at it. And he has focused his aggression on Christians. You may have noticed that I said has, implying that I believe the beast is past tense. I do not believe the beast is yet to come. Because I am confident that the revelation was written for the sake of the first century Christians as well as those that come after, the identity of the beast must be relevant to the first century Christians. The beast is called a beast because it is unclean. Unclean animals that are similar to the serpent are all called beasts in the Bible The label beast is also appropriate because of the beast-like cruelty in his actions. The historic figure. That best fits the description of John's beast is a man by the name of Lucius Domitius Henobarbas. Most people know Lucius as his adoptive name, Nero Kaiser, or Nero Caesar. Nero ruled over Rome from A. D. 54 to A. D. 68. Now before we get to examine why Nero fits the description of the beast, we must Examine a different identity of the beast as it is described in chapter 17. We learn in chapter 17 of Revelation that the seven heads of the beast are actually seven hills. The seven heads then are a geographical feature. The geographical feature of seven hills is particular to the city of Rome. There was even an ancient festival in Rome, a feast of seven hills city. Each of the hills had a name, and these were referred to in the writings of poets and historians. In general, then, we can say that the beast is Rome. It is the city and empire that tried to wipe out Christianity. But cities and empires do not have a mind of their own. They are ruled by men. The men who rule give a face, a personality to the identity of the beast. And so we look to Nero. We look back at Nero as the personality of a beast. The most fallacious evidence of Nero as the beast was his beastly behavior. It is said of Nero that he was neither discriminate nor moderate in putting to death whosoever he pleased. He is said to have compelled 400 senators to fight in the arena. He was a sodomist who reportedly castrated a boy named Sporas and then married him. He ruthlessly killed his mother, brother, wife, aunt, and many others close to him. One contemporary writer of Nero referred to him as the destroyer of the human race And the poison of the world. After his death, he was called a beast by the pagan writer Apollonius. The primary evidence of Nero fitting the identity of the beast was his treatment of Christians. In verse 5 and 7, we are told that the beast blasphemes God and makes war with the saints of God. The persecution of Christians by the Roman Empire began with Nero. Before that time, Christians were thought to be a sect of the Jews. The original persecutors of Christians were the Jews. Apparently, because of rumor and slander, Christians became thought of as superstitious and then dangerous In A. D. 64, Christianity no longer fell under the umbrella of Judaism and was given a non-legal religion status, meaning that to practice Christianity was against Roman law. The first focused persecution upon Christians by Nero followed the great fire within Rome. Rumors swirled that Nero had set those fires himself. He was trying to justify a building project to honor his reign. To rid himself of the rumors, he publicly placed blame on the Christians for the fire. Nero had numerous Christians rounded up and punished. He did not merely execute them, but tortured them, mutilated them until their death. Some were wrapped in hides of wild beasts, and Herod would have them torn to pieces by his dogs. Others were fastened to crosses set on fire to illuminate Nero's garden at night. The exact amount of Christians killed under Nero is unknown, but writers of the day use descriptive phrases such as an immense number and a vast multitude of the elect. In fact, the foremost leaders of the early church, Peter and Paul, were put to death under Nero. Every Christian alive in the first century would have recognized the beast described in Revelation to be Nero Caesar. It is not by coincidence either that Nero's persecution of Christians lasted three and a half years. It began in A. D. 64 and ended in the middle of A. D. 68 at the death of Nero. Other evidence pointing to Nero as the beast is the way he died. Nero lived by the sword. His sword decapitated the Apostle Paul. Church Father Tetolian credits Nero's sword as having provided the martyr's blood that was the seed of the church. Biblically and poetically, Nero's own death was by sword and his own hand. It is recorded that he drove a dagger into his own throat, being aided by his private secretary. Nero's death fulfills our Lord's promise that a man who lives by the sword will die by the sword. Nero is also a figurehead who was worshipped. Emperor worship began with Julius Caesar, who was given God status by the Senate, and was even referred to as a savior. Augustus, Tiberius, Gaius, and Claudius, all who preceded Nero, each embraced in his own way the idea of a godlike status. Citizens of Rome were to be more than loyal to the emperor. They were to worship him as their God. This is one reason why Christianity became such a threat to the Roman Empire. Christians not only worshiped God alone, but they gave him a name. His name was that of a man. It was Jesus of Nazareth. The worship of Jesus as Savior in God made Christianity a serious threat to the God status of the Roman emperors. The final evidence for identifying Nero as the beast personified is the description of his being given a fatal wound, and yet he was healed. The healing brought about greater worship of the beast and a belief that no one could stand against him The healing gives the beast a messianic quality, for of course it was Jesus who was dead and rose again The beast seemingly attempts to imitate the true Messiah, causing the world to follow him and to worship him. As we learned earlier, the beast is not just a man. It is also an empire. It is Rome. The Empire and the City of the Seven Hills, when Nero committed suicide, he ended that Julio-Claudian bloodline. After his death, Rome experienced a series of civil wars to determine who would rule. To the known world, there was a time when the Roman Empire appeared to be toppling to its death. It was under the leadership of Vespian that Rome was resurrected to re-establish itself as a dominating power in the world. This is very likely the near fatal wound and the rebirth John is describing in this revelation. Afterwards, it was the rebirth of Christian persecution. By Domitian a decade later. The beast then has two identities. It is in general Rome, the seat of the emperor. It is also Nero, the Emperor of Rome, at the writing of Revelation. No doubt it is much more difficult for us to make identification of the beast today than it was for the Christians of the first century who lived through what John is describing. Identifying the beast and understanding the symbolism John uses is not the primary importance of the passage. The purpose of the passage is stated in verses 9 and 10. Why should you know about the beast? Why should they know about the beast? It's in verses 9 and 10. These verses affirm that the need to acquire an understanding of what goes beyond the obvious He who has ears is the man who can understand the truth beyond what is being heard. He is a man who hears with ears of faith. He is given an understanding that is not obvious to most. And from the description of what the beast does, which is wage war on Christians, The faithful ear must understand that this is going to happen. It was and is unavoidable. As we learned last week, the church is at war with the devil. The devil gives his power and authority to governments like Rome and emperors like Nero. So that they can do his work in killing the children of the woman. The Christians, the church. Verse 10 tells Christians what it means to follow Christ. If anyone is to go into captivity, into captivity, he will go. If anyone is to be killed by the sword, by the sword, he will be killed. In plain speech, if Christians are destined to suffer under the hand of the beast, they will suffer. This is the will of God, and those who follow Christ must understand the sacrificial life they are called to live. To receive eternal reward, sacrificial living, the Christian must have being patient, endurance, and faithfulness during that sacrificial living. The warning contained in this vision is the same that Jesus gave when he said that those who follow him must pick up their cross. Which means they need to be willing to sacrifice themselves for a greater cause, the kingdom of God. These words do not mean near as much to us as they did to the first century Christians, for they knew what it meant to be hunted down by the beast. Today, the Christian church in the Western world has a soft underbelly. Many flock to preachers and ministries that tell us what we want to hear. They focus on wealth and affluence in this life. The only sacrifice taught is that of giving to a particular ministry. And believing that you are going to get ten times much in return. Very few want to hear messages about sacrifice. But sacrifice is what Revelation promises will happen. Sacrifice is what it takes to follow Christ. As followers of Christ, we are able to say, it is no longer I that live. I must take up my own cross. To die is gain. Others are more important than myself. He who gives up his life for Christ will find true life thereafter. No one knows what is going to be required of us to remain faithful in this life in the future. Two generations before the World War II generation, Was raised with the idea that sacrificing oneself for the greater good was a virtue. The Christian church needs to be training each generation with the same mindset. Sacrifice is a virtue. It is the call of every Christian And we parents need to be willing to say that if my son is going to be taken into captivity for the sake of the gospel, then captivity he must go. If my daughter has to be killed by the sword because of the gospel, then by the sword she must be killed. Acknowledging reality and hearing the warning, we must note that beastly behavior of empires and leaders do not end with Rome, and they did not end with Nero. There has been and will be more nations and leaders that the devil uses to kill the children of the church. I believe God wants us to prepare ourselves and our children for times of sacrifice. The description of captivity and death by the sword is not limited to any one generation. I do not know all the details of what is to come. I could speculate, but no one saw Gender confusion on the horizon, so who knows? Oh, God knows. Certainly There will be other empires and leaders to come that the devil will influence and give his power for the purpose of persecuting the church. I do know that the call to sacrifice must be heard, and the willingness must be a part of our identity. If we have chosen to follow Christ, we have already pledged our allegiance to him with heart, soul, mind, and strength. We have already said we will follow him to our death. It is for us to be prepared to live out that pledge. If it be us, if it be our children, our children's children, so be it. Amen. Let us pray. Gracious God, we do hear the great call of sacrifice in this passage, and we certainly know that the first century church knew it all too well. And there have been Christians after and still Christians today that are under the thumb of authority, under the thumb of the devil We pray, dear Lord, no matter what comes, no matter what lies ahead, that we too are willing to sacrifice because what we say is true, may your kingdom come and your will be done. In Jesus' name we pray. Amen.

sermons.title: Watch Out for This
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: The name of the Father, of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated.
