I really, really, really, really encourage you to turn to Revelation chapter 13 Picking up at verse eleven, it's going to be very important that you follow along with me in these verses to better understand them. Revelation 13 beginning verse eleven, and as you do that I do want to add to my comments about our uh general counsel. If you do have any questions, your your representatives were Diana Bowles and Bobby Lynn. Um they represented you at the cheapened our our trip there a little bit. Um but if you have any questions you can ask them or ask uh Father Bowles or myself of what's going on in the denomination. And if you're ever interested in a general council, three years from now, they've they've announced the the the diocese of the central states, which It's below us, Virginia and North Carolina and so on. They're hosting and they have chosen for three years from now, if you want to go, they've chosen Washington DC And I was the only dissenting vote of the whole when they approved it. I don't want to go to Washington DC, but other people do. So if you want to attend in three years from now Alright, Revelation 13, speaking up from verse eleven, before we examine the passage this passage from Revelation this morning, it is helpful for us to rehearse what we have concluded up until now. We have identified the woman who gives birth to a child as being and is being pursued by the dragon to be a metaphor of Mary giving birth to Jesus. And then a typology of the birth of the people of God, or we can call it the church. The dragon is the devil, as the scripture plainly states The beast who is given the power and authority from the dragon is both the Roman Emperor Empire and the Roman Emperor. I mentioned two weeks ago that we will later read in chapter 17 that the seven heads of the beasts are metaphors for the seven hills of the city of Rome, which was known as the city of the seven hills. The Emperor of Rome, who was a contemporary of John the Revelator, and the beast personified, was Nero Caesar. The number 666 will be more evidence for us to conclude that Nero is the first beast. We more easily identify the beast when we view these passages from the historical context in which John lived Because we believe the book of Revelation was written for the benefit of Christians living in the first century, I cannot emphasize that enough, under immediate persecution The identity of the beast had to be relevant to those Christians. Because we also believe that the Bible is a living book with truths that apply to Christians of every age We recognize Rome and Miro to be the first of many nations and leaders the devil uses to persecute even unto death children of the woman, or said differently, children of the church, or simply put, Christians. Every atrocity perpetrated upon Christians by governments and leaders of governments, whether it be a dictator, a king, or an emperor. Is a fulfillment of the symbolisms described by John, where the dragon uses a beast to do his bidding on earth In verse 11 of chapter 13, we are introduced to another beast. This now makes three creatures of evil, and the number is not by accident. Just as the beast of the sea attempts to take on messianic qualities, evil Evil in general tries to portray itself as having a Trinitarian nature just as the true Godhead has. The devil desperately desires to be considered a co-equal counterpart to God, so he attempts to be perceived as being three in one, just as the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost are three in one. The devil is a desperate wise fool. The description of the third beast provides the clues we need to identify him. He was seen by John coming out of the earth. The first beast, you remember, was seen to be coming out of the sea. And the second now is coming out of the earth. What's the difference? As we pointed out two weeks ago, the sea represents the pagan nations, and the land represents God's people. Thus, Israel, God's chosen nation, received her identity in the land she was to inherit. The pagan nations were represented by the sea, you remember, that was parted, and the river that was held back so that the people of God could go into the promised land If the second beast comes up from the earth, then it is a beast that comes up from among God's people. The two horns on its head make it appear to be like a lamb And tells us that the second beast appears on the outside as if he is like Christ. For it is Christ Jesus in John's vision who first appears as a lamb. You remember that it was the Lamb alone that was able to open the book of the seven seals. It was the Lamb that was pronounced once dead but now risen. It was the Lamb alone that was worthy to be worshipped. The second beast appears to be a lamb as well, appearing that way to take away the glory from the true lamb and place it on itself. Yet while the second beast appears to be like a lamb, the lamb of God, his voice is like the dragon. It is like the devil. What he speaks is definitely different than how he looks. The authority of the second beast comes from the first beast Who we should remember received the authority from the dragon. The purpose of the second beast is to make the inhabitants of the earth worship the first beast. He is able to do this by his speech and his ability to perform miracles or miraculous signs. The signs he performs, such as calling fire down from heaven, confuses the people of the earth into thinking that he has power from Almighty God. His signs are awe-inspiring, and his power is great enough that the people of the earth fear him, and thus they do as he instructs. The second beast becomes like all of the evil leaders we have read about in the Old Testament, who set up false idols to be worshipped. An image of the first beast is made. The image or false idol was given breath so that it could speak. Its speech was the cause for all who refused to worship the image to be killed. To separate more clearly those who were on the side of the beast and those who were against the beast, the second beast forces men and women of every race, of every status, of every creed, to receive a mark. Representing the first beast on the right hand and on the forehead. Those who were given the mark were given the right to buy and sell goods. Those who refused could not buy or sell, making them social and economic outcasts. The obvious reason for this marking is ownership. But why specifically on the right hand and forehead? Well, that is answered in Deuteronomy chapter 6, all the way back in the Old Testament, where the people of God are told to place the law of God on their hands and on their forehead. To force the mark of the feast in these same locations is simply another way to mock God. The mark is placed on the false worshippers according to verse 17, and that mark is the name of the beast or the number of his name. I have read enough explanations of this passage to conclude that modern interpreters want to avoid doing exactly what verse 17 suggests. Apparently because the name that comes up doesn't fit within their interpretation. Both Greek and Hebrew cultures had a game known as gematria Where standard letters from the alphabet were assigned numerical value. For example, the letter resh in Hebrew, which looks in our to our eyes as a backward R in English, That letter is assigned the number, the value 200. A letter, the letter noon is assigned 50. A Bob is six, and a gophus is one hundred, and a Sami is sixty. Each of these letters is found in the words Neron Kaiser. Iwon Kaiser is the Hebrew spelling of Nero Caesar. Hence 666 is the number representing Nero's name and his title. Now, one objection to this interpretation is the unusual spelling of Caesar Kaiser. But one of the Dead Sea Scrolls has revealed that John's spelling was not unusual at all, for in the Dead Sea Scrolls we find Neron Kaiser for Nero Caesar. Thus, as we have discovered two weeks ago, there are many reasons why we can interpret the first beast to be Nero. And 666 simply adds to those reasons. What we don't want to get caught up with, however, is limiting the beast's identity to only being that of Nero. We again point out that the revelation was for the first century church that suffered under Rome and under Nero, but it is for every Christian that has followed the early church as well. This makes the identity of the second beast all the more compelling. So let us now summarize what the second beast does. In the first place, the second beast does great things, signs and wonders. The purpose of these signs is to deceive men. Signs and wonders are used to establish prophetic authority throughout Scripture. Moses performed them before Pharaoh. Elijah performed them before on Mount Carmel. And Christ Jesus performed them when he began his public ministry as the Messiah. Taking on that identity. It is understandable why the second beast would perform signs, for he is trying to follow in line with the prophets of God. The prophet Daniel warned that the Antichrist would perform marvelous things as did Christ himself. Who said that the false messiahs and false prophets would arise showing various signs and wonders? The question we all ask is what shall these powers do? And this is where interpreters get lost because they take it all in a literal sense. and claim that the beast will be like a magician. Some have even suggested that popular magicians today use demonic powers. I do not doubt the probability of such speculation, but magicians today are not like the false prophet described here. A sign or wonder can be anything that convinces people that the prophet is of God or a type of God. It could be a scientist, a psychologist, a sociologist Or even a humanitarian that does something so surprising, so wonderful according to the perception of a people that he is given the status of a prophet It could have even then the ability of a man to draw a large crowd Modern Christians, since the 20th century, have been enamored by men who can draw a crowd, as if the number of people gathered is a sign that God is at work. The second beast then uses his gain influence to convince people to make an image of the first beast. Notice, please, that the second beast does not make the image of himself or by himself. But men who are under his influence make the image. The image, we are told, is a representation of the first beast. Emperors of Rome, of course, had such images made of themselves. But these are not only leaders of history, but also leaders of today. We remember the Iraq War and the images of Saddam Hussein or Even today, the image of the North Korean dictator, reminding us that idol worship is alive and well today. So far, nothing is surprising until verse 15. But it seems preposterous to conclude that this can be taken literally. Imagining an idol made of metal, stone, or wood coming to life and speaking is both odd and curious But to say it should be taken literally is the easy part. Should we not be taken literally is the easy part. Concluding how it should be taken is more difficult. And I believe it is safe and necessary to say, when one comes to passages like this, that its meaning or fulfillment is not obvious, well, it's meant to be not obvious. This is one of those passages that are not found in a historical example or a personal experience. It is likely that such interpretation is for the church at a later date. But I think this idea that the idol speaks, that that that's the important clue Considering all that the second beast does, including forcing the mark of the first beast upon all who would worship it, we conclude that the purpose of the second beast is to serve the first beast. The second beast causes the inhabitants of the world to wonder, admire, and worship the first beast. The second beast exercises the power of the first, and the first works and exercises through the second. The identity of the second beast is found in his work for the first beast and in comparison to the first beast. In comparison to the first, the second beast does not force the masses, but convinces them. He does not command or issue laws, but instead influences the hearts of men. He does this by his charm, i. e. , signs and wonders, and by his speech. Remember if the idol speaks. In general, we can identify the second beast to be a false prophet. Not just any false prophet, mind you, but one that leads many people astray. This general identification is found later in the book of Revelation, specifically in chapter 19, verse 20, where we read, quote, And the beast was taken, and with him the false prophet, the second beast. that wrought miracles before him, with which he deceived those who had received the mark of the beast, and them that worshipped his image. Those both were cast alive into the lake of fire that burneth with brimstone. And then in Revelation chapter 20, verse 10, he is mentioned once more. Quote, and the devil that deceived them was cast into the lake of fire. And brimstone, where the beast and the false prophet are. The beast that is mentioned in these passages is unmistakable. The beast is the first beast, and the false prophet is none other than the second beast. Biblical prophets are those who speak forth God's message, and the message could be what is going on today, and how to apply God's word to today. or what is going to happen in the future. A false prophet speaks lies while saying he is speaking for God. He does not speak the truth. He speaks lies. His lies are not easily discerned either, for the false prophet looks like the lamb. He is gentle and even sacrificial in his behavior, but his words are those of the dragon. The dragon's words, because he is the great deceiver, appear to be truth, but only on the surface. The best deceptions are those that mix truth with lies. And the vulnerable, the ignorant, and the blind cannot tell the difference. Because the description of the second beast is general and thoroughly wrapped up in the identity of the first beast. It can be argued that the second beast is not a specific person, either in history or in the future, to be revealed. This is more difficult to conclude, however, when we identify the first beast to be a specific person, Nero Caesar. If he is specific, then it is natural to think that the second beast would be specific as well. But we remember also that the beast refers to the Roman Empire as well as the Roman Emperor. And thus it could represent all governments, all leaders and such that would persecute Christians If this identity of the beast is being referred to, then the second beast can be anyone who would use the name of God in the cloak of a prophet to influence people away from the true God And thus worship government rulers and government entities. How this looks in our contemporary context is not so easily determined, but then again it's not supposed to be. It is interesting to note that there are certain ministers who speak in God's name that are more linked to liberal lobbies than they are the Word of God. False prophets linked to government leaders, government agencies, or lobbies fit the description of the second beast quite well. False prophets were a repeated warning of Jesus and the apostles. Meek minds and desperate hearts are vulnerable to those who would speak in God's name but tell lies. As we look to the identity of the second beast, we are to be warned as Jesus and the apostles warned. There will be false prophets who come in Jesus' name to lead the people of God astray, if that were possible. Confusion and deception are an effective way to lead people away from the truth. The warning, the warning, however, is not for us to be scared, but wise. To note its presence when we see and hear false prophecy. I took a class in seminary which studied the book of Revelation. And a buddy of mine, as we're sitting in a lecture, a buddy of mine next to me started to chuckle when we were studying this very passage. He had accidentally grabbed his wife's Bible rushing to class, and she had innocently written in her side notes the number 666 she wrote, watch out for this And we laugh because getting the mark of the beast isn't just standing in the wrong line, but it's much more deceptive. It is heeding the wrong teachings. It is listening and heeding false prophets who say they speak for God, but are actually deceiving you to follow the first beast. For example, I recently heard an advertisement for a podcast, heard this on the radio, a podcast of a prominent pastor of a very large congregation in the state of Texas. I won't say his name Who proclaims that a positive attitude in life is what will give you a happy life? Beloved, that is not the gospel of the Lord Jesus Christ. A multitude of preachers are teaching this very hour that God doesn't care about your moral living, but only cares that you live your own truth by expressing whatever sexuality you desire. Beloved, that is not the gospel of the Lord Jesus Christ. There are preachers this very hour who are telling people who call themselves Christians that Jesus wants them to be wealthy and earthly prosperous. While Jesus himself said, Blessed are the poor and needy. Beloved, there are preachers this very hour. For treating the pulpits from which they preach as counseling couches, where they simply want to make the congregation comfortable. Beloved, this is not the gospel of the Lord Jesus Christ. It is instead a message from the beast. Who comes from out of the land, which is to come from among God's people, to deceive them My closing point then is similar to the note from my buddy's wife. Watch out for this. But not for the stamp of 666 But for the false teachers who would lead you to that number. Watch out for false teachers who deceive and instead create instead of Listening to falsehood, instead crave the truth of the gospel of the Lord Jesus Christ. For in that truth are hard words, and in those hard words are eternal life. Desire such words. Insist on such words. And live. Amen. Let us pray. Gracious God, we thank you for the warnings found in in these words of John the Revelator. And we thank you for what it points us to, to insist on the truth, to insist on it being preached and heard and believed and lived. May that occur in our lives and may we encourage it to one another. We pray this in Jesus' name. Amen

sermons.title: Purchased by God
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Be seated. Turn in your Bibles, if you would, to Revelation chapter 14. Revelation 14, looking at verses 1 through 5. That is most helpful to you if you will follow along with me. Security In relationships is a foundation stone for mental health. I truly believe that I believe it because of personal experience and I believe it because of pastoral observation. We need security in our relationships to cope with the trials and tribulations of life. As a little boy who lost his parents at the age of three, I remember being driven away from our home. While looking back through the rear window of the car, I could not articulate my emotions, but I knew that I was scared, scared of the unknown. When my aunt and uncle became my parents, my insecurities were revealed whenever they would argue I would lie awake listening to them and contemplate what was going to happen to us children if they divorced. It scared me. I didn't know if I would have a place to live, food to eat clothes to wear, even though I have plenty of that around me. As a pastor, I have seen families struggle and even crumble, with the end result being insecurity residing in the hearts of the children and the parents No one knows who to trust after a family falls apart. And it does not matter how much therapy they receive or time that passes, the insecurity remains. In my experience, my issues with insecurity did not go away until I surrendered my life to Jesus Christ. It was not until I publicly confessed Christ as my Savior and owned my infant baptism that I began to know what security is. Mind you, it did not happen overnight, but in time, as I put my trust in God's promises, I found him to be trustworthy. My sense of security increased and I became more mentally healthy as an individual. I know it to be true that the whole world can be falling apart around me My dog could be in the pounds, my car in the shop, my mortgage overdue, parishioners angry with me, and whatever else bad could be happening to me, but I know that God loves me and I am therefore secure. That might make for a good country song. For Christians living in the first century, their world was truly falling apart around them. The persecution of Christians by Nero was horrifying, and it was common for Christian families to have at least one loved one die for having faith in Christ. We should be reminded that the custom of naming godparents for children at baptism began because of the insecurities brought upon by that first persecution. Parents wanted to ensure that their children would be cared for physically and spiritually if they became martyrs. The godparents thus took the same vows as the parents at the child's baptism to try to ensure the child's overall well-being. Christians wanted to know during those days of persecution: did God love them? They wanted security in his love. Chapter 14 of Revelation describes a scene in the midst of the persecution of Christians under Nero. The first beast, who we have said is Nero, but was also the Empire of Rome. Is given power by the devil, the dragon, to commence war against the Christian Church The second beast or false prophet influences the world to worship the first beast and punish those who do not. The Christians, as we have said, knew of this punishment firsthand. They knew what it meant to not be able to buy or sell because they were followers of Jesus Christ. They knew what it meant to be separated from those who had been marked with the number of the beast. The marking did not have to be physical, mind you. It was publicly proclaimed by those who followed the beast that they had no king but Caesar Those who did not worship the beast were obvious because of what they would not proclaim or what they would not worship. Christians were tempted to be insecure, for with no social or political allies, they were seemingly left to themselves. This is why chapter 14 is so important. But what is described is a contrast between what was happening to Christians in the flesh as they were being persecuted under Roman rule, and what was happening with their souls as they were in Christ. Dispensationalists failed to acknowledge the connection between chapters 13 and 14 because in its original form the book of Revelation didn't come with chapters and verses and their numbers. This was a succession of verses that we're reading here, backing up chapter 13. After John describes the second feast Forcing worshippers of the first beast to take his number as their identification, he looks in a different direction and he sees the true Lamb of God. He has seen the false lamb who speaks like the dragon, and now he sees in chapter 14 the true lamb. He knows this is the true Lamb because his identity was verified earlier, and the false lamb does not stand as a legitimate comparison when they stand side by side He also recognizes the 144,000 who were standing with the Lamb and had the Lamb's name and the Heavenly Father's name written on their foreheads. We discovered in chapter 7 that the 144,000 was a symbolic description of the thousands upon thousands that surrounded the throne of God. The number 144, you remember, is 12 times 12, which is the combining of the old covenant representatives, the 12 tribes, and the new covenant representatives, the 12 apostles. The multiple of a thousand in John's is John's symbolic way of saying that they were too numerous to count. These people have been marked by God, and by being marked by God, their salvation is assured. They are secure Since the devil has marked those who worship the false image and claim them as his own, and since God has marked those who worship him alone We are to notice that there is not a third alternative. There is no other group of people who are yet to make up their minds. You are either marked by the devil or you are marked by God. And if you are not marked by God, you are automatically marked by the devil. We note again that the Bible does not provide middle ground. There is no such thing as neutral territory or middle-of-the-road faith. Jesus said, we are either for him or against him. And in the vision given to John, we learn that if you are either marked by God or you are marked by the devil. Pluralism of religion is non-existent here. We cannot agree with those who say that they can have their religion and we can have ours, and they all end up in the same place. No, no, they do not. Because of the emphasis on exclusion By those who have the mark of the beast and keep themselves separate from Christians, it is helpful to know that Christians have a privilege that they are exclusive to them. This is why John tells us that the chosen of God, those marked by the Savior, sing a new song before God's throne. And no one could learn that song except the hundred and forty-four thousand. The vision Reminds us how peculiar, how special, how unique, how privileged Christians are to call upon the name of God To pronounce his name and understand his name is a privilege that those marked by the beast can never know Considering the Christian's privileged position, I wish to address the issue of worship for a moment. As your pastor, I pray perpetually for you to make worship a priority in your individual lives and in the life of your family. Because we live in a consumer-driven culture, people, including the faithful, are tempted to compare what the church has to offer them and what the world has to offer them and decide each Sunday which way they're going to go As we hear John's description of the chosen of God, who are privileged to stand before his throne and sing forth his name, we should be Awaken to the reality that the worship of God has nothing to do with what the church has to offer you or what appeals to you on a particular Sunday. We are privileged to worship. We are privileged to sing his name. Worship, regardless of how boring it is to the flesh, has nothing to do with what it offers us. But everything to do with how privileged we are to call upon the name of the Lord. It is remarkable what a change of perspective can do for the soul. Worship will become a priority in your life if you stop viewing it as a do I have to and make it a I get to. You get to worship God. Such is an honor afforded to a chosen few, and we should be ever grateful. Verse 4 provides a description of the 144,000 that is also unique. They are the people who did not defile themselves with women. An immediate and natural reading of this text seems to promote celibacy as a virtue and also label women as an unclean species. Taken literally, we could also conclude that only men are included in the hundred and forty-four thousand. Because we are careful not to interpret passages of scripture without context. We must recall that earlier John referred to a false teacher as Jezebel. That woman, Jezebel, he said. Who calls herself a prophetess to teach and seduce my servants to commit fornication and to eat things sacrificed to idols. His reference to a woman as a seducer and her seduction being false teachings allows us to conclude that those who have not been with a woman are those who have not believed the false teachings. Both the Old and New Testaments use sexual intimacy as a metaphor for believing false teachings and worshiping false gods. Such worship, as you know, is an affront to God, as he requires his people to be intimate only with him. To chase after other gods is to chase after whores who work to defile men. The description of the 144,000 includes following the Lamb wherever he goes and having no lie found in their mouths In summary, they are blameless. It is likely when you read or hear the description of these 144,000, you conclude that you are not included in that number. It would seem that if you have defiled yourself with a woman or even told an untruth or lie, you are automatically excluded. If you are not blameless, then you are not one of the number. If you have thought this, if you have thought this, let me counter your thinking by plainly stating that you are wrong. The reason why the hundred and forty-four thousand have not followed false teachings as a man would follow after a whore. And the reason why they follow the Lamb wherever he goes, and the reason why no lie is found in their mouths, and the reason why they are blameless, is not their own work or merits It is because they are purchased by God. As in all of the biblical descriptions of salvation, What underlines each is a reference or implication that men are not saved from hell and given the hope of heaven by their own works. The fact that men are saved by grace through faith in the shed blood and acceptable sacrifice of Jesus Christ, that is the foundation upon which the gospels The letters and the Book of Revelation are written. Men do not keep themselves from teachers who are like harlots or hold their tongues from lies by their own strength. They are not made a part of the number of God's chosen people by their ability to keep the number of the beast off of their forehead. They are made a part of the chosen number of God because God has marked them and God has purchased them. I ask you rhetorically, and I confront the devil defiantly by asking, if God has purchased you, who or what has the ability to take from God what is his? The answer to such a question bolsters our security, stating it plainly and simply: if God owns us, nothing or anyone can claim otherwise. And people know what he has paid with. God purchased us his people With the blood of his only son. The blood of Jesus. His life as a sacrificial offering was the purchase price, and we can state defiantly against the devil that nothing can match that price. There is nothing that is as valuable. Nothing can be staked against us, for we have been bought with a price that cannot be matched. So how secure are you? Where do you see yourself when you read the 144,000 described? Are you in or out? Are you in because of how good you are? Are you out because of how bad you are? Both ways of thinking fail to understand the truth. I recall hearing of a young man who came to the home of his pastor one afternoon looking for counsel. The young man shared with his pastor that he was tormented by feelings of inadequacy. He was adding up his character qualities next to God's holiness, and he realized how short he fell, woefully short. He knew the passages from Scripture that tell him he is saved by the grace of God, not by his own works. He had heard the sermons that proclaimed it was only by faith in Jesus Christ that a man can find forgiveness for sins past He reminded himself of these time and time again, but the feeling, the feelings of inadequacy would not go away. In his reasoning, his repeated sins indicated that he must not be sincere when he repents. He also reasoned that God must be getting tired. Tired of him confessing the same sins over and over again. After listening to the young man pour his heart out, the pastor pointed to the dog that was resting at the foot of the pastor's feet as they sat in his study Notice this loyal dog at my feet, the pastor said. He does everything I ask of him and more. He obeys my commands and is loyal to the point that he would give up his own life to save mine. I love this dog, and he loves me. The pastor then asked the young man to rise and follow him They went into the kitchen where the pastor's son, just two years old, was sitting in a high chair. Now look at my son, said the pastor. He has food on his face. on his tray and on the floor. He soils himself numerous times a day and struggles to obey me. I have to discipline him over and over again, and yet I love him I love him more than I love my dog. He is my inheritor. He will receive all that is mine. This is how our Heavenly Father perceives us. He does not love us because we are faithful, loyal, or obedient. He loves us because we are his chosen ones. We are his inheritors, the inheritors of his kingdom. He has marked us, and we are his own. I close by reminding you that a primary goal of Jesus Was that we know God the Father as our Father. Remember this exchange from the Gospel of John chapter 14. Lord said Thomas to Jesus, we do not know where you are going, so how can we know the way? You know the verse, Jesus answered, I am the way, the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father. Except through me. If you had known me, you would know my father as well. From now on, you do know him and have seen him Philip said to him, Lord, show us the Father, and that will be enough for us. Jesus replied, Philip, I have been with you all this time, and still you do not know me. Anyone who has seen me has seen the Father. How can you say, Show us the Father? Do you not believe that I am in the Father, and the Father is in me? The words I say to you I do not speak on my own. Instead, it is the Father dwelling in me, performing his works. Believe me that I am in the Father, and the Father is in me, or at least believe on account of the works themselves. Beloved, believing in Jesus is knowing God as our Father. No greater security Can be given. Amen? Amen. Let us pray. The gracious and mercy from God. How appropriate you chose this these verses for this Father's Day. We recognize you as first and foremost. our Father. And so those who are insecure this day may they find it in knowing you as their Father. In Jesus' name we pray. Amen.

sermons.title: Love Your Enemies
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, of the Son, of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Be seated. Once again, I ask that you turn in your Bibles to the book of Revelation. Most helpful that you follow along. It is easy to get lost in this text. Revelation chapter 14. We're looking at verses 6 through 20. Last week we were encouraged by the security we have in Christ Because we are marked by God and because he is our Father. Such encouragement is needed for Christians who are being persecuted for their faith, and as we will see today, such encouragement is needed when judgment day comes. In fact, it is even needed when Judgment Day is described As we study this section of Scripture, I remind you of my position, that the events of John's vision do not have to be taken in chronological order. We are free to understand that the events described in chapters 13 and 14 are the same events described in chapters 7, 8, and 9. We can also understand that what goes on in chapter 14, verses 6 through 20 occurs concurrently with what is described in chapter 14, verses 1 through 5. While John sees the chosen people of God around the throne of the Lamb, he also sees the three angels who announce and bring forth final judgment. Before we hear commentary on the passage as a whole, let us look at the particulars of the vision. This is where you can follow along with me. John sees another angel. Because he has described so many angels thus far, the reference to another simply adds this one to the rest. The angel symbolizes the preaching of the gospel around the world, which is the fulfillment of our Lord's promise. as articulated in Matthew chapter 24 verse 14, where Jesus said, and this gospel of the kingdom will be preached in all the world as a witness to all the nations, and then the end will come. That promise is a fulfillment of God's covenant with Abraham when he was told that by him that is by Abraham all nations will be blessed. Just hearing the gospel, whether you respond to it positively or not, but just hearing the gospel is a blessing. We are assured then before the final judgment begins that God has fulfilled all of his promises and the time to commence his judgment has arrived. The angel that claims the eternal gospel to all nations is the same that announces the judgment of God. We marvel at this vision, for it shows, again, the mercy of God as he mixes the preaching of the good news with the with the coming of the end and the condemnation of those who have rebelled against him and chosen to worship false gods. His love knows no bounds, as he proves that he takes no pleasure in punishing the wicked. He desires that all would be saved. But alas, not all are saved. We moderns stumble over such an understanding because we tend to think that if we want something And we can get it done, then we should do it. But God has insisted that a certain amount of autonomy is involved. In having faith. And does those who don't believe choose not to? The second angel is next seen in verse 8 and says, fallen. Fallen is Babylon the Great, which made all the nations drink the maddening wine of her adulteries. Babylon is a name given to a dominating world power such as Rome. The phrase was used in the vision given to Daniel. Babylon is a type name given to the world powers that persecute the people of God. Babylon represents Rome. It represents Islamic ruled countries, Hindu-ruled countries, Buddhist-ruled countries, communist-ruled countries. And any secular nation that has or will rise against the church all come under the identity of Babylon. The description, quote, made all the nations drink the maddening wine of her adulteries. confirms our interpretation of what it meant for the 144,000 not to defile themselves with women. The women are those who try to deceive men with false teachings and thus lead them away from worshiping the true God of the universe. The third angel follows with a loud voice. The announcement is not a gentle one, and so his tone matches his words. Those who worship the beast and receive its mark are considered of one class. Just as we discussed last week, there is no middle ground. People are either marked by the beast or they are marked by God. Those of the class that are marked by the beast will drink of God's fury. These people will be tormented, and their torment will rise up forever and ever. We will come back to this description later, but a brief comment is necessary. There are some who want to believe that hell or suffering of sinners will be for a moment, and then the sinners will be no more. This is called annihilation. Some do not like the idea that God would torture sinners continuously and forever. The simplest reading of this passage is that he will, indicating that he does not want us to think otherwise. We are to understand eternal damnation as eternal suffering. Verse 12 is another call for patience. The same patience called for in chapter 6, where you remember the saints were crying out for retribution. The vision assures that retribution is coming, but no timeline is given. What the Christian is to be concerned for is obedience to God's commands and his or her faithfulness to Jesus The pronouncement of blessing upon those who die in the Lord is an encouragement that although retribution may not happen in the lifetime of particular Christians who are persecuted. There is a great hope for reward and justice in the life after. The next part of the vision describes one who is like the Son of Man. Sitting on a white cloud. The phrase, like a son of man, comes from the book of Daniel. We read that this morning, which describes the coming Messiah as the Son of Man. Jesus took on the title because he was born a man. He was fully man. And yet fully God. Thus he is not ashamed to be called the Son of Man On ascension day, an angel described to the disciples that Jesus would return coming from the eastern sky on white clouds of heaven. His return would bring forth from the grave those who had died in him, and he would bring up to himself those who were still alive. This is the harvest of his people. The harvest is described in John's vision as being by way of a golden sickle, which is appropriate in the hands of the one who has a golden crown upon his head. He is the king of the universe. And gold is the only metal fitting for a king. Jesus was candidly speaking when he told the disciples that it was not for the Son of Man to know the time in which he would return. In John's vision, the voice of an angel announces the time, and it is obvious that the Savior was ready. For just after the angel speaks these words, the Savior swings his sickle to harvest the earth. When he walked this earth, Jesus said that Judgment Day would be like a harvest, where the harvester would separate the wheat from the chaff. The wheat consists of those who are ripe and useful. The chaff consists of those who hide among the wheat and are useless. What Jesus harvests as he swings his golden sickle is the wheat. The wheat is his people When it is time to harvest the evildoers, the worshippers of the second beast, the vision changes. It is not chaff that is described as being cut down, but grapes. An angel is specifically assigned to take a sharp sickle. Which is obviously distinct from the golden sickle held by the Savior. And with it, this angel is to cut off clusters of grapes. The grapes are ripe, meaning that the sin of the people has come to its forest. The grapes collected are then thrown into the winepress of the of the wrath of God. This is not the first time in the Bible that God's judgment is referred to as a winepress and the disobedient as grapes. In Isaiah chapter 63, God speaks through the prophet and describes his judgment as a wine press. There in Isaiah, the Lord explains that his garments are red because he has trampled upon the rebellious nations as a man would trample upon grapes. There's battered my garments and I stained all my clothing, he says from Isaiah The Lord describes his emotions in his judgment, saying that he was appalled that no one was there to help him. No one gives him support in his judgment. His own wrath sustains him, and he makes his enemies drunk and pours their blood on the ground. The amount of blood described reveals how violent the vengeance of God will be. A horse's bridle as a measurement could refer back to the four horsemen of the apocalypse as we studied from chapter six, or it could be a reference to the Savior as he rides in on a victorious horse and Chapter 19. Either way, the reference to a horse is to focus on war and victory. The measurement of 1600 stadia is another symbolic number. Stay with me here. 16 is the number four squared. We recall that number four refers to the earth, the four corners of the earth, or the compass. 100 is 10 squared, 10 being the number of completeness. Together we have 16 multiplied by 100, meaning that the blood covers all of the created world. Blood covering the created world means that no one can escape God's judgment. So now we turn to some commentary. I said at the beginning of this sermon That we should marvel that in the midst of God's pronounced judgment, the gospel is still going forth. We are to notice from this that God is benevolent to his creation. He loves his creation. As stated, he does not take pleasure in punishing the wicked. He wills that no man be condemned, but that all would come to repentance. But how does this match up with his wrath? His wrath being compared to a wine press. After all, he is the operator of the wine press. He personally smashes the nations and thus spills the blood of men so that it runs down and covers all the earth. We might consider that God would have to enjoy such vengeance in order to act in such a manner. Having an even greater sensitivity, we might question why God does not simply pardon all men. After all, if he does not enjoy seeing the wicked punished and wills that all men be saved, why doesn't he simply choose not to punish the wicked and instead save them? We will answer such questions from two directions. First, we must remember St. Paul's first letter to Timothy, where we read that God wills none should perish, but all would come to repentance. The use of the phrase God wills Is not to be understood as what God has ordained to come to pass, but rather a way to express God's disposition. He does not want to punish the wicked. His heart's desire is that all would come to repentance. Again, because we are tempted to perceive God as we perceive ourselves, we might wonder why He doesn't do what we would do, which is to do whatever we want to do. If we do not desire for something to be as it is, then we try to change it If we have the power to change it, we will change it. And since God is all powerful, we conclude that he would change whatever he wants to change. In the category of discipline, for example, if I didn't want to spank my son or punish him for his behavior because I was moved by sadness Then I wouldn't spank or punish him. It is that simple. But God is not that simple. We allow our emotions, be they justified or not, to dictate our behavior God expresses emotions, but such emotions do not dictate him as to what he will do. To be able to act out of what is righteous while feeling otherwise, that is divine. When men are able to do so, they do so by divine strength. The other direction from which we answer such questions about God's judgment compared to his disposition is from the text itself. Go back to verse 10 of the chapter, where those who took the mark of the beast are described as being tormented by burning sulfur. The text says that their torment is in the presence of holy angels and in the presence of the Lamb. Stated more obviously, those who suffer do so in front of the Savior's view. Jesus sees them suffer and does not stop or in any way interfere with their suffering. We wonder how he could do so if his disposition is for them not to suffer. We wonder because we are not divine. Only he who is divine can weep and do the right that causes the weeping. We also learned from Isaiah that the one inflicting the suffering is none other than God Himself. He is the one with the wine press. He states that his wrath sustains him as he suffers upon men. He keeps his judgment going by the sense of his wrath. To appreciate God's wrath, we must appreciate his disdain for sin. God has a righteous disdain for sin. God's character, being holy, cannot tolerate sin. He Who appeased his own wrath towards sin by killing his only son will practice wrath upon anyone who rejects his son and clings to sin And it is not as simple as saying that God's wrath towards sin is greater than his disposition toward the sinner. They are both powerful, and both he can practice at the same time. We cannot understand this. I know we cannot, because even as I wrote this sermon, I knew I was describing something I will never ever fully know. When I was a boy, about the age of twelve, I remember my father trying to find his belt so that he could spank my little brother, who was about the age of seven. As he searched for his belt, my brother wailed and carried on like he was being sent to the gallows. I hated to hear his cry, and so I myself cried out to my father for him, don't stop! Can't you see he's sorry? He won't do it again. I cried out for my younger brother because I empathized with him. I knew what it was like to be in his shoes, and his anticipated pain reminded me of my own. In an odd way, when we empathize or even pleading for someone, we are, in some way, pleading for ourselves. When we are tempted to perceive God as cold hearted and cruel for inflicting his wrath upon sinners, and for the Savior watching without interference, We are lightly thinking about it from a selfish perspective. We wouldn't want it to be us, and so we don't want it to be anyone else. But Jesus sees it differently. Jesus knows what it is to be bludgeoned by the wrath of God. Jesus doesn't stand by gazing while imagining what it would be like. He knows. And because he knows, he is a responsible witness to what is right. Understanding God's wrath and loving disposition helped me as a father I could spank my child with a rod and know that I am right in doing so, and I can spank him for yelling and carrying on as if he does not accept his own punishment, which is what my father should have done I can do this all with the disposition of love. For it really is love because it is what a rebellious child needs. The described wrath of God is to have a more profound effect upon us than practical fatherhood, however. We are to understand that just as God can administer his wrath upon the rebellious and still and still have the disposition of love. So too can we wait patiently for his wrath to come upon those who persecute the church, and so we still can love them We can pray that God's wrath would be known, but at the same time pray for our enemies to come to repentance. How we do this is found only in us coming under the authority, the influence of the Holy Spirit, and doing as Jesus instructed. Do you remember these words? Love your enemies, he said. Pray for those who persecute you. And then he said, for those who do it are acting as true sons of the Father. Let us pray. Our gracious God, we want to be true sons of yours. We want to be true inheritors and people who behave as your inheritors. And so with this challenge, help us to love our enemies. Pray for those who persecute us and ask for your divine judgment. This we pray in Jesus' name. Amen

sermons.title: Sing Boldly
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. May be seated. And as usual, I encourage you to turn In your Bibles to our text this morning, Revelation chapter fifteen Of the many games that young boys play, it should be required that every boy play games that test courage. Games of courage or games of chicken, the negative title, are games like Quick Draw or Floody Knuckles. The Bloody Knuckles game my buddies and I played in elementary school was with a comb C-O-M-B. Those were the days when everyone carried a comb in his back pocket to keep his feathered hair back. In bloody knuckles, the comb was placed on the back of the first boy's hand, making a fist with his palm facing down. The opponent then tried to grab the comb off of the first boy's hand quickly and then bring the teeth side down on his knuckles as quickly as possible. And most of the time the first boy would be able to move his hand away quickly. The key of the game, however Is that if the boy having the comb on his hand flinched at all and the comb fell off, it was a free shot. Now, you can imagine the damage that is done on a free shot to knuckles with a comb. That is why it is called Bloody Knuckles. The most difficult part of the game is trying not to flinch. When you were guilty of flinching, the anticipation of giving an opponent a free shot was almost unbearable. It was hard to stand still, and it made it easier not to look, closing your eyes. Knowing that something bad is going to happen can make the anxiety caused by the anticipation as difficult as the coming pain. Revelation 15 is a preparation chapter. It is a chapter that pre-warns about the final judgment that will come upon the earth. And the judgment is for the rebellious, and it is bad. The warning to us Should not bring about anxiety, however, for the anticipation of God's judgment for Christians, that is to bring us comfort. It is our comfort because the final judgment consists of what is left to be done to redeem our souls. Instead of anxiety, our anticipation of God's coming judgment should cause us to sing. And yes, I said, sing. John the Revelator begins this section of his vision with a familiar expression, quote, and I saw another sign in heaven. End quote. The last time we had this expression was in chapter twelve, where the history of the war between Satan and the church was described. This other sign is an introductory summary to what is more specifically described in chapter 16. The sign is said to be great and marvelous, which we should take not as a description of a miracle or as a fireworks display, but something that causes terrible fear and awe Once again, the number seven is used. In the case of plagues, the number seven denotes the universal, the all-extending of the plagues. We are told that they are the last plagues, but as we will see next, they resemble similar plagues that have already come with the blowing of the seven trumpets. John says that these final plagues complete God's wrath. That statement should be qualified. As completed in this world. For God's wrath upon the rebellious is eternal The setting of the vision is the same as in chapter 4, where the throne of God is described. The sea of glass, you remember, symbolizes the calming of the nations. Brought about by the preaching of the gospel and the victory of the Lamb. The temple also plays an important role again, as it did in chapter 11. Where it is opened and the Ark of the Covenant is mentioned as bringing forth lightning, thunder, and earthquakes. The temple symbolizes the innermost place where God's presence resides. It is used here to symbolize that it is from God's closest counsel That the angels come forth. They are nearest to him, and we are to understand that. They know his mind. These angels are specially dressed and specially assigned. Their dress is to reflect the high priestly garments that were worn by chosen men to enter the Holy of Holies, the earthly temple on the Day of Atonement. There is an emphasis here upon the whiteness or purity of their garments. These angels are dressed as the Savior, for they are holy before the Lord. Their holiness, however, is not to be understood as passivity or as gentleness. They are pure And they are vengeful. A concern for modern Christianity is our apparent inability to associate what is pure and holy with what is vengeful and bloody. Perhaps Christians are confused by what Jesus meant when he said that the meek will inherit the earth, or by the command that we are to turn the other cheek. Meekness is called for in times when persons are being mistreated for their faith. It is not called for when family and possessions are threatened by the violence of this earth who are filled with greed. A meek man can carry a sword, just as a holy angel dressed in pure white linen can carry a sword, and both can pour out the wrath of God. We must be careful as Christians not to allow the world or pagan minds to teach us what Christians ought to be or ought to do. There are men of this world that believe they are in the position to tell Christians how we should behave in society and even challenge us that a Christian ought not defend himself We should not bow down to such pressure or choose a defensive posture when someone of this world would tell us we are not acting as a Christian when we are being aggressive. The evil one would have Christians stay quiet and not speak out against injustices in society or immorality amongst social leaders. They would have Christians put away their weapons so that they themselves can pick them up and use them to cut us down. It is part of our Western Christian heritage to understand that there are times to be neat, to be meek, and times to be forceful. In general, meekness is applied when we proclaim and stand for the gospel If a government chooses to persecute me and my family because of the God I worship, then I shall be meek, but still stand for what I believe If men greedily want to take my land or harm my family, not because we are Christian, but because they are evil, then I shall fight until a victor is determined. Castivity is a godly virtue when practiced for the sake of the gospel. It is foolish to practice before the threat of thieves. As we note the pure white that covers the angels as they collect bowls of God's wrath, we also notice that they have golden sashes. Gold is the medal or color of royalty. The angels come against nations of the world, against principalities and powers of this age, in the name of the only true King. He is, of course, the King of Kings. That God is acting in a kingly manner toward the dwellers upon the earth is also communicated in the gold of which the bowls full of his wrath are made. From them, he is going to prove that he is the king of all ages. Kings pull down other kings and establish their dominion. A kingdom is a king's dominion. God's rightful dominion is all of the earth. The importance of these plagues is stated in verse 8, for it is Only after the plagues are fulfilled that men are able to enter the temple. The smoke that fills the temple reminds us of the Shekinah or glory cloud that symbolized God's awe-inspiring presence amidst the Israelites during the day as they walked in the desert. His presence, his abiding self among his people, is the ultimate goal of all that the Savior and the Father's plan of salvation worked for. That is where we want to be in his presence. That is where he wants us to be, with him, in his bosom. Yet we must wait until the final plagues are fulfilled. So what is to be done in the meantime? What do we do as we wait for these final plagues to be fulfilled? What are we supposed to be doing? The answer is so very simple. The answer is, we are to sing. The most overlooked and underappreciated theme in Holy Scripture is the importance of song. Preachers like myself, who focus on the grammatical and historical specifics of Holy Scripture, not only fail to appreciate how much song plays a part in Scripture, But fail to appreciate the vital role that song plays in Scripture. Song is not just for the gifted. It is true that the scripture instructs those who are gifted in song, whether it is playing an instrument or singing, they are to lead God's people when God's people gather. But it is also true that all the people of God are to be singing. You ever been to a service amongst Christians, and hardly anyone is singing? It's rather depressing. By my count, verses 3 and 4 of chapter 15 are part of as many as twelve songs sung in the book of Revelation. Each song, starting with the first in chapter 4, described God's attributes as well as his mighty works of salvation. The singers of this particular song in chapter 15 are those that have been victorious over the beast Meaning that they were faithful to the mark of God that God had placed upon them as they did not worship or comply with the beast. Thus the ones who were persecuted, who offered up themselves, who watched their own blood be spilled, as well as the blood of their friends and family. These are the ones that offer up a song unto the Lord. The song, you will note, is accompanied by a harp. It is unfortunate that the harp has gone out of style, and it is today depicted as a feminine instrument. Rarely do you see a man play the harp, and men also on average tend not to sing out or sing loud in church, at least as loud as they should And part of the reason is likely that music itself and instruments like the harp are perceived as more feminine in nature. However, a closer look at Scripture reveals something quite different. The harp is primarily introduced in Scripture through David. Who plays it to soothe the tormented soul of King Saul? The harp is played here in John's vision by those who stood their ground. Who stood victorious during their time on earth. Both men and women withstood the beast, and all of them hold harps, and all of them sing Music accompaniment transcends gender. Musical accompaniment should have a high priority within the church. The people of God should invest in those who can play and sing well, so that they can lead the rest of us to sing boldly. The more boldly people sing around you, the more boldly you will sing. These musicians should consist of both men and women. And I will go out on a limb and say that there needs to be more men raised in Christian homes to play instruments to aid the people of God in singing. It should be duly noted that Jubal is referred to in Genesis as the father of all who play the harp and flute. It was David, a manly king as Israel ever had, that wrote most of the Psalter, which is the church's eternal hymn book. And it was a male director of music to whom David wrote his Psalms and instructed them to be sung in the temple. I point this out to say that music is to be masculine, not to be masculine alone, whereas as I have said and noted, we are to understand both men and women played the harps and sang in John's vision My application is for us to more fully embrace the masculine side of music that is lacking in the church today. Besides the importance of musical accompaniment, there is the importance of the words we sing. The song sung in Revelation 15 by those victorious is called the Song of Moses and the Song of the Lamb. The title brings the two covenants together, just as we have seen with the 24 elders, and just as we have seen with the 144,000. We remember that by way of Moses was God's deliverance of his people out of the bondage of Egypt, and by the Lamb, our Lord and Savior, was God's deliverance of his people out of the bondage of sin. And notice the contents of the song as it first celebrates God's attributes Thou art holy. Second, it magnifies the goodness of the divine government. Righteous and true are thy ways. Third, God's divine greatness is extolled. He is the king of the ages. Fourth, the only reference to men is in relation to God. Think of how many hymns we might sing or choruses we might sing that focus on man as opposed to God. The question that is put forth is a challenge. It humbles us. Who will not fear you, O Lord, and bring glory to your name? Fifth and finally, the certainty of God's coming triumph is proclaimed. Quote, all nations will come and worship before you. Such are bold words. They are not sentimental. They do not express feelings. Instead, they conjure up conviction, determination, and the desire to fight for righteousness. They are words for masculine voices. And there I go again, focusing on the masculine, and I cannot help it. It is time we men perceive singing as a masculine thing to do. It is not by accident, but by consequence, that choirs are short on men. Culturally, we have generalized that women sing and men grunt. But biblical singing or singing songs of Scripture is part of what it is to be amended Be manly in God's kingdom. To bring down the mighty nation of Assyria, the Lord Himself gave the following instruction to Isaiah Quote, and you will sing as on the night you celebrate a holy festival, your hearts will rejoice as when men go up with flutes to the mountain of the Lord to the rock of Israel Every stroke the Lord lays on them will be his punishing rod. It will be to the music of tambourines and harps, as he fights them in battle with the blows of his arm. It is a manly duty to fight in the name of God Almighty to defend the land and families He has given us. And the primary weapon, according to Isaiah, is song. Isaiah also describes the Lord singing with his people, the Lord himself singing with us. Quote, the Lord will cause men to hear his majestic voice and will make them see his arm coming down with raging anger and consuming fire. Do you understand that? It will be the Lord Himself. He will join the chorus of men. His song accompanies the salvation he brings for his people. The rhetorical question that challenges us from this passage is: if the Lord sings of our salvation What should stop us from singing his praises? Are we more masculine than God that we should let him sing while we are silent? Was it not he who said to his people, And you will see? For the four living creatures around the throne of God, for the thousands upon thousands who stand before the Lamb. For those who overcame the beast, singing is what they do. It does not have to be commanded. It comes out of a soul that has been redeemed. In fact, a redeemed soul must sing. As we have said, chapter 15 is a prelude or an introduction of the coming wrath of God. What the people of God do is what we are to do in anticipation of that wrath. We are to not fear or flinch in anticipation. We are to sing. Sing boldly, church. Sing boldly. Amen. Let us pray. A gracious God, we thank you for the standard set. at the celebration of the coming of your wrath. It is odd to our ears to think that that is a time to celebrate, but that is what your people do. And we want to join in. Give us the courage to do so. Pray this in Jesus' name.

sermons.title: Half-assing It
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, of the Son, of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. I encourage you to turn to Revelation chapter 16 We read through a short portion of the chapter, but we will be covering the entire chapter, so being in the Word following along will be helpful for you. We get lost a bit in Revelation. There are some weeds to to walk through, to be sure. But follow along with me if you would. I have interpreted the book of Revelation in a particular way. And that way is different than what has been popular in books and even movies that uh present a particular understanding of the end I have argued that the events described are primarily symbolic, and that the symbolisms enable us to apply John's vision to every historic context the New Testament church uh since the New Testament church began have also taught that the events described are not necessarily chronological. John's vision includes things that have happened, were happening and are happening today and will happen in the near future and in the distant future. We were told in chapter 15 that the final plagues of the judgment upon the wicked were about to be described. In chapter 16, we have the description of the plagues, but it is important, if not necessary, to notice that the seven bowls of wrath have an uncanny resemblance to the judgment that occurred at the blowing of the seven trumpets in chapters eight and nine. The resemblance has led many scholars to conclude that the bowls of wrath are a recapitulation of what has already been foretold in the trumpets and in the seals that were broken by the lamb. In other words, the judgments at the breaking of the seven seals are the same judgments at the blowing of the seven trumpets, which are the same judgments in the seven bowls of wrath. And I have a theory as to why the interpretation I put forward is not popular. First of all, there is no identifiable timeline. If most of what we read in John's vision is symbolic and not chronological then we cannot get a handle on what the exact indicators of Jesus' return will be, and people love those indicators Second, most of us like to have things neat and tidy. Those who put forth an interpretation that identifies particular signs being fulfilled followed by a rapture, followed by a period of tribulation, followed by a thousand-year reign, and then final judgment, have everything neatly categorized. We can follow such a chart and imagine how it will all unfold. Thirdly, Modern man likes the idea that a particular book of the Bible was written primarily for their day and for their age. We are generational-centric, which is to think that a book written 2,000 years ago was written just for the people in my generation. But the truth is, most of the New Testament is addressed to churches and people that have long since passed. If we read the revelation as being future-oriented, then it means that it was written specifically for us. My interpretation has it written for Christians of every age, and that does not make us modern Christians feel special. Setting that point aside, my main point is that any interpretation of John's vision cannot avoid acknowledging the similarities between the judgments that follow the seven trumpets and the judgments from the bowls of wrath here in Revelation 16. The first bowl of wrath is specifically directed upon those who worship the beast. The punishment is for them. It is a punishment that does not have a finality. It consists of sores, and those sores are for the purpose of hurting and making miserable those who are guilty of false worship. The second bowl is poured out upon the sea, and the sea is made of as blood We remember that when the second trumpet was blown, one third of the sea was made blood, and one-third of the creatures of the sea died. The bowl of wrath here increases the death toll for the life of every living being in the sea is taken. The third bowl is poured upon the rivers and fresh water reserves. When the third trumpet was blown, one-third of the rivers were made bitter. Here again, we have the bowl of wrath increasing the extent of God's judgment. No river or fresh water is spared One third of the trumpets, all of it with the bowls. The angels' verse or song following this judgment reveals a principle of God's judgment That Dante captures well in his Divine Comedy. That principle is judgment fitting the sin. God turns fresh water into blood because of the blood of the innocent, or the blood of the prophets that was shed by the guilty on earth In other words, God is saying: if it is blood that they want, blood they shall have. They shall have it to the point of their own suffering and their own demise. There is no response, of course, to this pronounced judgment. Who can say that it is not fair? Who can claim it is undeserved? The fourth bull of wrath affects the sun. The sun becomes an enemy or punisher of men. The response of those who suffer by the sun reveals their rebellious hearts. Instead of crying out to God for mercy, they curse his name. They have given themselves over to evil, and it is evil that controls them. You remember when the fourth trumpet was blown, one-third of the sun was smitten, and a third of the day was darkened. At that time, men longed for more light. And here, with the bowl of wrath, now the light punishes them. The fifth bowl brings about judgment upon the beast specifically. His kingdom is placed in darkness. The darkness represents its powerlessness before the light of the world. The people can no longer look to the beast or to any leader or any false god for comfort. They can only wallow in their suffering as they continue to curse God. Again, remember when the fourth trumpet was blown, stars from the heaven fell into the abyss. Men could no longer find direction from signs in the heavens. They attempt to seek death to avoid suffering on earth, but death eludes them. This is how we know The suffering is great when men seek death to be relieved of the suffering in this life. The sixth bowl dries up the rivers the river of Euphrates. Euphrates was the river that all of God's enemies crossed. to reach the promised land. It is also the name of the river that ran through the Garden of Eden. When the Sixth Trumpets blew, armies from the east crossed over the Euphrates and destroyed one-third of the population of man. Now, at the pouring out of the bowl of wrath, the way is made easy, made easy for the armies of wrath to cross over and destroy all persons that are left. What happens next is also similar to what is described before the blowing of the seven trumpets. You should recall an interlude we studied between the sixth and seventh trumpet that described two witnesses coming forth. Here Between the sixth and seventh bowl of wrath, we have three witnesses coming forth in the form of frogs. They come with miraculous signs to deceive as many as possible in order to form an army to engage the God of all creation one last time. This is the devil's last gasp for survival. This is the Armageddon. The Armageddon we hear so much about, that the announcement of this last battle, the battle at Armageddon, Jesus says, Behold, I come like a thief. Blessed is he who stays awake and keeps his clothes with him, so that he may not go naked and be shamefully exposed. Clothes or garments he speaks of are those that are given to every Christian. It is a garment of righteousness. It is a sign of the fervent love of God for each of his people. Because of the description of Jesus coming as a thief, It's the same warning he gave to his disciples. And because of the blessing of being clothed in righteousness, we can conclude that Christians are included in this great battle in Armageddon. They have not experienced a rapture which would put them at a distance while watching the end of the world unfold like we were all spectators. No, in this depiction they are involved. And I would say this involvement is not something to be frightened about. If we are part of such a great scene, it should be in our mindset to do our part, just as our brothers and sisters in Christ have done their part down through the ages. The seventh bowl is finality. The content of the bowl is poured out on the air. The air encompasses all of creation, and therefore, all of creation is affected by the last bowl. The announcement that it is done is similar to Jesus who said it is finished The content of the bowl stirs up the foundation of the earth. It shakes apart the core of the earth The great city that becomes the focus of the last furious wrath of God is Babylon We discussed a few weeks ago that Babylon is a name given to all cities that persecute the people of God. It is a city that symbolizes enity between God and the principalities and powers of this world. Babylon is any city. It is every city that comes against the King of Kings and the Lord of Lords. The Savior of the world. God has special judgment for such cities, for such nations that have set their hearts against him. He has for them a cup filled with the wine of fury. It is a fury that will consume and it will reach every portion of their being. The wine represents a covenant drink of their condemnation. The devastation from God's wrath will be palpable. It will be experienced by all of man's senses And what men will see will have never been seen before and it will never be seen again. Islands will be overwhelmed by the sea. Mountains will be flattened like prairies. The sky will give up hail storms, a hundred pounds each, and this hail will fall upon men, crushing them where they rest and where they run. In comparison, we remember that when the seventh trumpet is blown, there is an earthquake And a great hailstorm, but the details of the effect of both the earthquake and the hailstorm hailstorm are not given And this leads us to ponder whether the events orchestrated by the seventh trumpet are the same as those started at the pouring of each bowl of wrath. The numbering there is the same. The primary judgment is the same. What is not the same is the extent of each judgment and the detail provided by John. Some authors conclude that the visions after the blowing of each trumpet were shadows, shadows of clearer vision revealed of the same scenes at the pouring out of each bowl. And I can accept that interpretation to a point. What I believe is provided to us involves a little more in regards to the purpose. Of the vision, the trumpets versus the bowls. To understand the bowls of wrath in relation to the trumpets blown, We can go to passages such as our gospel reading from this morning from Luke chapter 13. In that passage, Jesus prior It's being told about the Galileans who suffered under Pilate, who were killed While they were giving an offering to the Lord. And then Jesus mentions the falling of the tower at Siloam. We don't know all the details of that, but obviously a tower in Siloam fell. people died. And Jesus taught his disciples at that moment that they were to read those events as a sign, a sign of God's judgment. Jesus then explains that those who were killed by Pilate and those who were killed by that accident are all examples of judgment to come. Jesus used the example of murder and catastrophe to remind his disciples that there is a much harsher and more extensive judgment to come. Unless a man repent, so the warning tells us, much worse than Pilate murdering or a collapsing of a tower will be visited upon the guilty. This warning is implied in the seven trumpets and the seven bowls of wrath as well. The destruction that occurs at the blowing of each trumpet has numerical limitations. One-third, and so forth. It is one-third of the sea that turns to blood. One-third of the creatures of the sea that are killed. Torture lasts five months. The limitations or boundaries placed upon those judgments is to be compared to the full force of God's fury that comes with the pouring out of each bowl of wrath. God's judgment there is not limited. Not limited when the wrath is poured out. No longer will there be boundaries. It is quite likely that what we are to conclude from the difference, the difference between the judgment of God at the blowing of the trumpets and the judgment of the bulls at the pouring out of God's wrath. It's that those judgments that are limited or have boundaries are warnings. Warnings of the great and final judgment to come. When the seas are contaminated so that creatures die, do we understand and speak about them only in terms of nature running its course? Or accidents by men and fail to see the hand of God as a warning When disease strikes hundreds of thousands, do we believe the reports that more money needs to be spent on research or development of drugs or vaccines? That would cure or prevent disease, and not see the right hand of God's judgment upon the immoral again as a warning. When earthquakes destroy buildings, when hurricanes wipe out cities, when famine strikes a land, do we see these as merely natural disasters? Meaning that these catastrophes are expected because man is subject to the whims of nature? Or do we acknowledge that the God who created and sustains all that is Controls the wind, controls the waves, and thus warns his creatures of his wrath to come that has no boundaries. Let us confess that usually our stomachs are not up for such acknowledgement. We notice, do we not, those who seemingly have done nothing wrong, who contract a deadly disease? We witness families and homes like our own, torn up and displaced, and we wonder, what have they done to deserve such suffering? The answer to those questions is the same Jesus gave to his disciples in Luke chapter 13. Those people are like us. And unless we repent, we will suffer even worse fate. The pain and suffering we see happening around us, whether it is caused by neglect of man or the powers of nature, Are all the result of trumpets being blown. These trumpets warn us of the bowls of wrath to come And after the bowls are poured, there is no more opportunity to repent. We know all too well the reaction of our fellow citizens now twenty-two years ago when the towers in New York collapsed People went to church to pray. They were more kind and thoughtful of their neighbors on the street. They took 9-11 as a warning, at least for a time. But soon they went back to their self-absorbed lives, and it was like it never happened. When the threat or crisis was over, so was their need for God and their need for their neighbor in their lives. Have you ever done that? Have you ever increased your presence at church? Increased your time in prayer? Increased your time in Bible study? Increased your giving? When you were in crisis, and then when the emotions caused by the crisis dissipated, did you go back to doing what you would rather be doing? For shame, for shame. The bowls of God's wrath are an increase From the wrath of his judgment at the blowing of each trumpet. Meaning that the blowing of each trumpet was a warning of the final wrath to come.
