The increase of God's wrath poured out of the bowls is a warning to us all that it will get worse If you do not know Christ this day as your Savior and Lord, be firmly warned If you claim to be Christian, but you are half-assing it with living out your faith, be firmly warned. And you who are more concerned that the preacher used the phrase half-assing from the pulpit, more than you are concerned about people repenting, be warned. If you do know Jesus, but you are playing with sin like a child plays with his favorite toy, be warned. Be warned and turn to the only one who can save your soul. Be warned by the trumpets that blow in light. So that you will be surely prepared for the bowls of the wrath to come. Let us pray. A gracious and heavenly father, we now take this revelation seriously, for each and every generation has Trumpets blown, warnings of your bowls of wrath to come. May each of us in this hearing repent And turn and know that there is a greater life to be had. In Jesus' name we pray. Amen

sermons.title: The Harlot
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, of the Son, of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. Turn in your Bibles to Revelation chapter 17. That is where we are resting ourselves this morning. Revelation chapter 17. Before I begin my exhortation, I want to read this creed to you. I believe in the non-binary God whose pronouns are plural. I believe in Jesus Christ, their child, who wore a fabulous tunic and had two dads, and saw everyone as a sibling child of God. I believe in the rainbow spirit, who shatters our image of one white light and retracts its into rainbow of gorgeous diversity. I believe in the church of everyday saints, as numerous, creative, and resilient as patches on the AIDS quilt, whose feet are grounded in mud and whose eyes gaze at the stars in wonder. I believe in the call to each of us that love is love is love, so beloved let us love. I believe, glorious God, help my unbelief. Amen. What I just read to you is called the Sparkle Creed. And was confessed in a Lutheran church in Minnesota this past June. And I ask. How does a historically confessing Christian church confess such blasphemy? A blasphemy that could not be farther from the Apostles or Nicene Creeds One answer to that question is how they are so far removed from Christianity is that they did not, do not take the warnings. of Revelation chapter 15, 16, and 17, seriously. Before we begin our study It is important to state that the interpretations of passages such as Revelation chapter 17 vary greatly. With so many diverse opinions regarding who the harlot is and who the beast is and what it all means, we should conclude that the Spirit of God has not revealed to the church all there is to know about this passage. What we should take from it is what we can know for sure. And what we can know for sure is derived from what Scripture already says. We must use the scriptures prior to the book of Revelation and the words in Revelation prior to chapter 17 to understand and to interpret what John's vision of a harlot and a beast means. We first notice that the vision of the harlot and the beast is to be understood in relation to the bowls of wrath. The angel that poured out the seventh bowl of wrath is the one that speaks with John and shows him the vision of the harlot riding the beast. We learned last week that the bowls of wrath are the final judgments of God. Thus the vision of the harlot and the beast are in the context of the final judgment, or specifically the battle of Armageddon. We are to understand this vision to be a closer look into the last battle. The initial vision described in the pouring of the seventh pole of wrath is as a widescreen version. It encompasses the whole earth. This next vision focuses in on one aspect of the whole vision. It focuses on the judgment of the harlot and the beast. The simple sequence of these visions teaches us that while the judgments are large in scope, they are also specific. Nations will be judged. Cities will be judged. Rulers will be judged. Citizens will be judged The vision John sees in Revelation 17 is a specific judgment of the harlot and the beast. We shall see in our study of chapter 21 that God wants us to contrast the relationship the harlot has with the beast and the relationship the church has with Christ Jesus. Both the church and the harlot are female, but each is identified by per morality. In Scripture, a faithful female is referred to as a virgin and then a bride. An unfaithful female is a prostitute, a whore, and a harlot. Referring to unfaithful people as a woman of ill repute is not new to scripture, as we should well know. In Isaiah 1, verse 21, the city of Jerusalem is referred to as a harlot. In Jeremiah 2, verse 20, the idol-worshipping nations that Israel has treaties with are called prostitutes. In Ezekiel chapter 16, Israel is graphically described as an unfaithful bride. In Hosea, the Israel of the prophet's day is unfaithful, and her mother is described as an adulterer. In Micah, the judgment upon the city of God is pronounced because the prostitutes of the people allowed to live amidst them, the people receive wages from their prostitution As we can see, describing the unfaithful people of God as a whore, a prostitute, an adulterer, is frequent in Scripture In fact, the whole book of Hosea is based on the analogy of an unfaithful harlot. To the prophet she marries. She continues her adulterous ways in their marital union, and Hosea continues to take her back, only to lose her again to the call of the flesh. And God uses the broken heart and broken family of the prophet to depict what Israel has done to him, continually falling back to false idols. Because so many passages use the metaphor of an unfaithful woman to describe God's unfaithful people, it is justifiable for us to conclude that the harlot described in John's vision is the same. The harlot on the beast and on the waters is a personification of the unfaithful people of God. She is the tares among the wheat. She is the goats among the sheep. She consists of the false prophets. She consists of the Pharisees who invent new laws that weigh men down. She is the Sadducees who refused to acknowledge that Jesus was the Messiah. She is the Judaizers who taught that men must be circumcised to be saved. She is the false teachers that proclaimed that Jesus was not a man. She is the Mormons. Jehovah's Witnesses, those who deny the divinity of Christ. She is the Pope, the Protestant And the fundamentalist who adds to the gospel by adding tradition to grace and insisting on both for men to be saved. She is the men and women who kill the unborn, practice prejudice, changed the plain reading of Scripture, and referred to Christianity as just one of many religions. She is made up of those who confess the Sparkle Creed. As you can see from this identification, the harlot represents a lot of people. But not everyone agrees with this identification. There are some very convincing scholars who believe that the harlot is a representation of the unfaithful Israel, the Jews. This interpretation goes back to the covenant God made with the nation of Israel as recorded in Deuteronomy chapter 28. We read in that chapter the blessings that God will bestow upon Israel if they are obedient, and the cursings if they are disobedient. The cursings, interestingly, sound very much like the events that occur at the breaking of the seventh seal, the blowing of the seven trumpets, and the pouring of the bulls of wrath. When drawing connecting lines, one can easily identify how God could be punishing disobedient Israel with the bulls of wrath as a fulfillment of the cursings in Deuteronomy 28. The woman, the harlot, is sitting on a scarlet beast. Scarlet is the color of blood or the color of sacrifice. Such a color would be fitting for Israel, for she is the nation that was to sacrifice only in honor and obedience to the living God, as they were pronounced guilty because of their sins. The color is also fitting because it was Israel that killed the prophets. Jesus told a parable of an owner of a vineyard. Who sent servants to check on the vineyard? They had grown, and then he rented it out to a chosen people. The people beat and killed the servants that the owner sent. When the owner sent his son, the people killed him, thinking that they would be the inheritors of the vineyard by the son's death. In the parable, Jesus warns that the master of the vineyard will destroy the people chosen who were guilty of punishing his servants and murdering his son. The implied message is that God will do the same to Israel, who was guilty of rejecting the prophets and turning his son over to Rome to be put to death. The blood of the prophets and of the Son of God is the responsibility of the chosen people of God. The guilt is upon them. The same guilt did not end with the death of God's Son either. It continued toward those who followed the Son. The Jews were the first to persecute the Christians Stephen, you remember in Acts, was stoned to death by those who claimed to throw rocks in defense of God. Like the harlot in John's vision, these murderers become drunk with the blood of the saints, the blood of those who bore the testimony of Jesus. All that might sound anti-Semitic, so hold on. Still there are other scholars, almost just as convincing, who believe that the woman is symbolic of the Roman Empire. Because the woman is arrayed in purple and scarlet and decked out with gold, precious stones and pearls, she appears to be an arrogant royalty. Like the Caesars of John's day, she flaunts her royal position while riding on the authority of the power of the beast. Also, the identity of the woman is clearly linked to the great city that reigns over the kings of the earth. At the time of John's writing, that city, of course, was Rome. All kings paid tribute to Rome. All kings knew they were ultimately subject to Rome. Well, we don't end there. Still other scholars who are convincing, at least to those during the Reformation. believe that the woman is the Roman Catholic Church and an image of the papal office. This interpretation does not carry as much weight biblically as do the previous two. However, it does provide a unique perspective regarding the tie in between the governing state and the church. You see, wherever the Roman Church established herself during the Middle Ages, she became directly tied into the state's governing body. The church eventually used the governing bodies it influenced as tools for persecuting and prosecuting the people of God. The popes during the time of the Reformation became synonymous with the devil according to leading Protestants When they read of the harlot riding on the beast and being drunk with the blood of the saints, that was correlated to the description of the Pope that they held responsible for the death of so many Protestant Christians That she was tied into the city of Rome confirmed that she came forth from her papal seat. Well it is understandable why Protestants in the Middle Ages would take such a position. It is also a dangerous position. It is dangerous to understand that such evil could only be applied to the Roman Church. Protestants, at least they who claim to be Protestant, are capable of the same atrocious behavior and have committed similar crimes against people who are supposed to be brothers and sisters in Christ. As you can see, the harlots description could apply to the Jews. It could also apply to the Roman Empire. It could also be applied to the Roman Catholic Church during the Reformation, and it could be applied to anyone who teaches falsely and is responsible for the death of those who believe and follow the truth. If the identity of the harlot is not clearly understood, she is definitely clearly marked Verse 5 says, and upon her forehead was written with a name written, Mystery Babylon the Great, the mother of harlots, and of the abominations of the earth. We have already identified Babylon as a reference to any city or people that persecutes the people of God. Here we can add deception as well. Babylon represents punishers and deceivers. The harlot on the beast is the mother of harlots. She is the personification of all that is deceitful. She gives birth to false teachers and cruel leaders of every age of man. We have no problem when we hear of the description of the harlot to match her with what we readily identify as evil. Of course, she represents evil empires, idol worshippers, and those who persecute Christians. But there are others she represents that might not be so easy for us to see Deception, by definition, is subtle. The subtlety of false teachers is a favorite strategy of the beast against the church. There are many, too many to count, that have mixed false teachings with biblical truth. There are others, more obvious groups, I've mentioned the Mormons and Jehovah's Witnesses and people of the way and so on. These groups plainly state in their doctrines that their teachings are not solely biblical, but because they take on names that are biblical. and use parts of Scripture, they have been successful deceiving millions. Other groups, mostly independent groups, practice acts of kindness toward the weak, the ill, and poor of society in the name of Christ, and at the same time believe that the Jesus of Scripture is no more a prophet than Muhammad of the Quran Or the Dalyama or Mahatma Gandhi. These people proclaim a universality of religions, making Jesus nothing more than a good man who did good deeds and told his followers to do the same. Jesus, of course, was a good man and did good deeds, but was also much, much more. But we need to get even more close to home in identifying false teachers. There are Christian teachers that we might respect because of their bold witness and their preaching. That are actually legalists. These false teachers believe a person is not really truly saved unless he does not smoke tobacco, drink alcohol, dance to modern music. watch Hollywood movies or or play games associated with gambling. If a man abstains from these things, then then and only then can he be saved. As apparently well meaning as such teachers might be, they are simply mere modern Pharisees For they believe their righteousness is based on what they do not do, as opposed to being based on the blood of Christ, which is the only thing that can cover our sins. Even more subtle and close to home are those that would change what we might call secondary doctrines of the church. Within the Protestant Episcopal Church were those in the 1960s and 70s who began to question the Scriptures' teachings on women in leadership within the church. They believed the fact that Jesus chose twelve men as his disciples and Paul restricted women from leadership, that all that was culturally bound. meaning that such need not be applied to contemporary times. And this new understanding of Scripture persuaded many, and soon women were being ordained as priests within the Episcopal Church in the United States. And once this view of Scripture was accepted, the door was swung wide open, and others who had more sinful plans entered in. Other passages of Scripture were labeled as being culturally bound, and the result today is not only the acceptance of sexual immoral behavior, but a consecration of sexually immoral bishops. And those who would dare stand against such sins are now the new enemy of the so-called church or faith. And I need to add one more modern-day harlot to the list. Those who teach a gospel that focuses on material wealth are scoundrels Of the lowest form, and as evil as Simon in the book of Acts, whom the apostles rebuked for trying to buy the power of the Holy Spirit. Thus, the identity of the harlot is not only those who hate God's people and persecute them outside the church. She is also those who claim themselves Christians, but in the end will be discovered to be the tares we have been warned about, the wolves in sheep clothing. The description of the harlot and her judgment is a warning to persecutors of Christians and to false teachers who would add or take away anything from the gospel. For true followers of Christ, she is a reminder to test the spirits For as Jesus said, not everyone who says, Lord, Lord, will enter the kingdom of God. Test the spirits, for you will know them by their fruit. Let us pray. Our gracious God. This message is certainly hitting home and the fact that we get deceived or attempted to be deceived time And time again by those who would claim to follow you, claim to speak truth, but are nothing more than mouthpiece for the devil. Father, help us to be a disciplined people, to be a people who seek truth and grab it when we find it and hold on to it and never let it go. And Father, bring down those who deceive your people. Bring them down and judge them as you will. In Jesus' name we pray.

sermons.title: Let Evil Destroy Itself
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Maybe seated. I ask that you would turn to Revelation chapter 17, picking up at verse 7. We will treat the verses from Revelation 17 a little different than usual. We are going to walk through this section verse by verse. It's a little bit like a Bible study, and then we'll get into what needs to be proclaimed. So Revelation 17, picking up at verse 7, but the angel said to me Why do you marvel? I will tell you the mystery of the woman and the beast that carries her, which has the seven heads and the ten horns. So the angel notices John marveling at the woman drunk with the blood of the saints. And we said last week that she represents false teachers who persecute those who teach and believe truth, and she deceives all who would listen to her. The angel gets John to snap out of it, marveling, in order to tell him what the vision of the woman and the beast mean. The beast has seven heads and ten horns. The numbers seven and ten are symbolic of completion. As God completed his creation of the heavens and earth in six days while resting on the seventh, and the ten represents his perfect law, that is summarized in the Ten Commandments. Verse 8. The beast that you saw was and is not, and will ascend out of the bottomless pit and go to perdition. And those who dwell on the earth will marvel, whose names are not written in the book of life from the foundation of the world, when they see the beast that was and is not and yet is The most plain meaning here is that there was a time when the devil was made manifest and was prior to this vision John is having. and could easily refer to the time when Christ was on the cross. The present time for John was when the devil is not Meaning that Jesus overcame sin and death, and the powerlessness of the devil is revealed. In the future, there will be a moment when the devil ascends from the bottomless pit and goes to perdition. And that will be a marvel to those who do not believe in Jesus, allowing them to see their affection on the beast. The difficulty when interpreting this section is the mentioning of perition, for perdition is final judgment in the abyss. For it seems that the unbelievers marble at the beast going to perdition, which I don't think it means If put in a different order, it means that they marvel at the beast ascending, and that same beast will ultimately go to perdition. Verse 9. Here is the mind which has wisdom. The seven heads are seven mountains on which the woman sits. The opening of this verse tells us to prepare to think more deeply and wisely. The classic description of the city is of the city of Rome. Which was a city known as a city of Seven Hills. So the identity of where the woman sits is now very clear. Verse 10. There are also seven kings. Five have fallen, one is, and the other has not yet come. And when he comes, he must continue a short time. The seven kings are not specific people, but represent kingdoms that rise and fall. The number seven is not specific either, but symbolic of the number of completion. The number of kingdoms that rise and fall will be according to God's will, as his will is assured to be complete. Verse 11. The beast that was and is not is himself also the eight, and is of the seven, and is going to perdition. Here is confirmed the order I described from verse eight. The numbering is because the rising of the eighth is really a continuation of the previous seven. Making sense? Yes. Verses 12 through 14, we'll read this together. The ten horns which you saw are ten kings who have received no kingdom as yet. but they receive authority for one hour as kings with the beast. These are of one mind, and they will give their power and authority to the beast. They will make war with the Lamb, and the Lamb will overcome them, for he is Lord of Lords and King of Kings. And those who are with him are called chosen and faithful. These verses describe and explain one longer theme. The ten horns are ten kings to come who will combine their authority and devote themselves to the devil, and the result will be making war with the Lamb, who we know is Christ Jesus. The war will be short, and the victory of the Lamb is assured because again he is King of Kings and Lord of Lords. Those who are with him at his victory are called chosen and faithful, for they believe in the Lamb, no matter the miracles or displays the devil placed before them. Verse 15. Then he said to me, The waters which you saw were the harlot where the harlot sits are peoples, multitudes, nations, and tongues The many waters upon which the woman sits is a reference back to verse 1 of chapter 17. We recall that water has symbolized nations of the earth, both in the Exodus and in the Psalms. Verses 16 and 17. And the ten horns which you saw on the beast, these will hate the harlot. Make her desolate and naked, eat her flesh, and burn her with fire. For God has put into their hearts to fulfill his purpose, to be one of one mind, and to give their kingdom to the beast until the words of God are fulfilled. Such verses have to be read together in order for them to make sense. What is being described is evil turning on itself to destroy itself. Falsehood and lies eventually have to turn on themselves. And the kingdoms of earth are going to turn to destroy the falsehoods and lies they have been deceived by, which in turn is turning on themselves, and God has planned this all along. Devil, I mean evil will destroy itself. Verse 18. And the woman whom he saw is that great city which reigns over the kings of the earth. Here is confirmed our interpretation, for Rome is symbolic of the lies and deception that take over the unbelieving world. So as I said, in summary, what we have just read is evil coming to a crescendo as it turns on itself, for that is what evil has to do. It hates so much that it hates itself, but doesn't realize it yet. Eventually it will turn and thus on itself destroy itself What Christians are to learn from this is really quite simple. We are to know the end that evil has ahead of it. And we are to be convinced that evil is not something to be redeemed, but something to be destroyed. Now notice that I did not say that people who attach themselves to evil aren't to be redeemed. I didn't say that. Again, we remind ourselves that God takes no pleasure in the suffering of sinners. God's heart is that all men will repent and be saved, but not all men will. And the why of that we will have to get to in another sermon. What I want to address today is the seriousness of evil, and to point out where it is manifesting itself today. And I don't think I am being over-dramatic when I say that where it is manifesting itself is the most sinister that evil has ever been. I say that not because the atrocities that are going on today are worse than atrocities in the past, but I think it is safer to say that such atrocities have never been so blatant and obvious, and no one in power No one in power, political or otherwise, seems to care. To get you to agree with my assessment, I point you to the passage in the book of James. Where James is talking about what a true religious person does, and by religious he's not talking in general, he's talking in the context of Christianity. People who truly believe the gospel of the Lord Jesus Christ will first, according to James, bridle their tongue. And in doing so, we'll prevent a great deal of damage within the Christian community because what we say can be offensive and unfaithful when we do not take control of what we say To ensure that it is helpful to our fellow Christians and pleasing to God. James next says that a religious person, a Christian person, a true faithful Christian person, will next care for widows and orphans Now you may ask why are widows and orphans the standard for Christians? Well, the answer is likely obvious to you. They are the most vulnerable in society. And were the most vulnerable in the first century. For you will recall that there was no financial security net such as we have today in Social Security If a woman was widowed with no adult children to care for her, she was on her own, and then subject to the wills of men who could treat her as they wished. An orphan was the same and usually homeless while also being treated at the wills of men To care for such persons who were cultural outcasts and according to Roman thinking were likely cursed by the gods and therefore were to be mistreated To care for such persons was truly to care for the least of these, as Jesus called them. And Christianity, at its heart, is to care for the least among us in society. Disgustingly, and quite the opposite, our culture has chosen to be at war with women and children, for it is women and children who make up the widows and the orphans. And while our culture is at war with women and children, it is also convincing women and children to be complicit in their own demise. What do I mean? What is my proof? One proof is the documentary hosted by political commentator Matt Walsh titled What is a Woman? What is discovered in the documentary is that no political leader, no social leader, and no doctor who considers himself or herself or itself to be progressive Will define what a woman is. They have this trance-like mantra of saying that the word woman is essentially meaningless Because the word can mean whatever a particular person wants it to mean. And as such, they are essentially wiping out the category of a particular gender altogether. And there are women who are perfectly fine with not being able to define their own gender. And it has become laughably ridiculous Again, it has been as if the minds of certain women have been shut off. A clear example of this is men entering women's sports and few women seeming to have a problem with it. Competitive swimming and track and field are the most prominent examples of men who say they identify as a woman and are given the opportunity to compete against other women Well there's not really other women, and they're a man, and then trouncing the average competitor, and then going into the woman's dressing room and proving that there is a great deal of difference between men and women I was in middle school when Title IX took effect and was applied to public schools. Part of Title IX allowed women, including young girls, to have access to the same funding for sports as men and young boys did. When in physical education class in the gym of Ilihe Junior High, where I attended, I had excuse me, there was a very large curtain, some of you will remember, that divided the gyms And the girls would play on one side and the boys would work out on the other side. Well, that curtain symbolically and actually lifted Then girls and boys' physical education classes were combined and it was supposed to be a liberating event There was not then, however, a belief that boys and girls or men and women should actually compete against each other, but it was a gesture, the lifting of the curtain was a gesture that the girls and women would be given access to compete more fully into sports. Such was to be the beginning of the end of patriarchy where boys and men received all the funding for their sports, and girls and women had second-class citizen rate. And here we are, so many years later, with the concept of a category of women being wiped out so that m men can compete against women because They are psychologically broken and they want to identify as a gender they are not, and crush the competition so that patriarchy wins again. And some women are applauding it all Such is baffling at best. But it doesn't end with sports. On July 8th of this year, a trans woman, which is not a woman at all, but a man who wants to be a woman Was crowned Miss Netherlands at a beauty pageant by the same name. Patriarchy again for the win. Before that, the ad agency that chose a trans woman, who again is no woman, to be a spokesman for a particular beer And now has lost millions of dollars in boycotts because of that choice. That same ad agency was given an award in June for being the ad agency of the year. Patriarchy again for the win. What both men and women and the it's of the world are saying is that men are better at being women than women are being at women. Patriarchy for the match. And then there is this war on children. The war on children is both in the womb and outside the womb. Regarding abortion, I talk about it enough. Let me simply argue, by way of question, what is the difference, DNA-wise, what is the difference? Between a fertilized egg in its mother's womb and a child who is two years old. What is the difference? DNA, DNA-wise, what is the difference? And the answer is nothing. When a woman's egg is fertilized, that embryo is everything DNA-wise that it is going to be. Its hair color is determined, its height is determined, its eye color is determined. The only thing that needs to take place is for it to grow. Which is the same as a two-year-old, where all of his DNA, her DNA, is determined, and the only thing that needs to happen is for it to continue to grow. As Horton says, a person is a person, no matter how small. The war on children outside the womb is just as sinister as the one inside the womb. The sexually immoral have never been satisfied with their queer and homosexual agenda being ratified by law and by the culture. They have always been about sexualizing children. What was on the fringe of society and only stated in anonymous chat rooms is now mainstream as children are being taught how to have sexual pleasure even before their teen years. I trust many of you have seen the videos or audio clips of people reading pornographic books that have been placed in their public school libraries that describe children being sexual When parents take these books and read them in public in front of school boards, the parents are quieted, their microphones are silenced because the content is too graphic for the school board to hear And does the school board do anything about it? They do nothing. I recall teaching an ethics class in college. I tried to make the point that there is morality that is universal, meaning that it is common to all. And I I gave the example of child rape. I said, that that we can all agree, can we not? That child rape is wrong And only half the class agreed by the nodding of their heads, and the rest remained silent. Today, progressives Newsfeeds are trying to convince us that a movie that is a true story about child sex trafficking titled Sound of Freedom is right-wing propaganda And beloved, I had heard the testimony of the man the movie is based upon. The movie doesn't come close to getting into the graphic horrors witnessed by those who fight such trafficking of children. It is a true story, and yet media outlets and announcers speak their talking points as if they are under a spell, so that evil prevails. Beloved, as Christians, we are to identify evil as evil. We are to identify it and point to it and call it out when it rears its head. The war on women is evil. We have to appreciate the differences between the sexes and defend women Defend women against men who try to overcome them and control them and steal away their dignity as women. The war on children is evil. Any sexualizing of children, any exposing them to the perverted is from the pit of hell. And any chance we get to prevent such exposure and speak up for those who do not have a voice. any chance we get should be taken. And we are to pray against these evils. We are to use those imprecatory psalms that seem so out of place because they call for the demise of God's enemies rather than praying for their repentance. But men who cling to evil are men who need to be taken to the deepest pit with evil and be seen no more. This is from Psalm 5. Psalm 5, verse 10. Make them bear their guilt, O God. Let them fall by their own counsels. Because of the abundance of their transgressions, cast them out, for they have rebelled against you. From Psalm 79, verse 6. Pour out your anger on the nations that do not know you, and on the kingdoms that do not call upon your name. From Psalm 9. Arise, O Lord, let not man prevail. Let the nations be judged before you. Put them in fear, O Lord. Let the nations know that they are but men. From Psalm 140. Grant not, O Lord, the desires of the wicked. Do not further their evil plot, or they will be exalted As for the head of those who surround me, let the mist the mischief of the lips overwhelm them. Let burning coals fall upon them. Let them be cast into fire, into my pits, no more to rise. I close by simply saying, Amen. Amen to such prayers, for Amen means let it be. Let evil destroy itself. Let us pray. Our God, we take passages such as Revelation 17, the description of the beast turning on the harlot, evil turning on itself. And we recognize the end. We see it from your eyes. We see how you will bring evil to naught by having it destroy itself. And so we ask, dear Lord, that you would give us the courage we need to take stands where stands need to be taken, to defend the powerless, to defend the fatherless, to defend the woman who cannot defend herself. That we might be a people that do not fear men, but fear only you. Pray this in Jesus' name. Amen.

sermons.title: Come Out
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated and turn to Revelation chapter 18 and follow along there with me, if you would. Revelation 18. As the reading indicated, I have decided to deal with all of chapter 18 this morning because there is no natural break The entire chapter describes one event, and in the middle of the description is an instruction given to Christians. We will look first at the description of the one event before we get to the instruction After we have received the identification of the beast and the harlot from chapter 17, we are now to receive a description of their demise. The vision of their demise is a new one. It is introduced by a new angel, who is an angel we are told, that has great authority. enough authority to proclaim in a poetic manner, mind you, the judgments of God's enemies. It should not surprise us that the city being judged is called Babylon. This is consistent with our interpretation of Babylon referenced earlier when we concluded that it represents or symbolizes all that is against God. Babylon as an identity represents all people, all powers, and nations that have come against God since time began. Babylon represents ancient Babylon that took the Israelites captive and destroyed the temple. Babylon represents Rome, both the city and the empire. Babylon represents Mecca, Berlin, Baghdad, Beijing, Islamabad, and any other city that has housed or houses governments. and leaders that have persecuted the church and denied that Jesus is Lord and Savior. In summary, Babylon is the lair of the devil on earth It is the place or places on earth where evil, its devils, and foul spirits congregate to plan deception upon the earth. The description of Babylon's sin reminds us that unless men are redeemed, sin piles upon sin. Verse 5 states, her sins are piled up to heaven, and God has remembered her crimes. When sin is not repented of, when it has not been paid for by the blood of Christ, it piles up and is a testimony against a man or a people before God. And if our sin is piled up, we are without excuse. We are without excuse because God has provided the means necessary that our sins might be removed. In regards to people and nations, sins not repented of, corrupt generations that follow. The sins of the fathers are visited upon the next generations, and too soon more sins are added, generation after generation, until a people collapse under the weight of their sin. Individually, the sins of a man unforgiven become befetting sins Descetting sins are sins that attack us from all sides, and from which a man cannot find relief His sin affects his work, his family, his friends, and even his time alone. Such sins make a man bitter, for he cannot find peace of mind. In order to get relief, he pursues other sins that give him escape, if only for a moment. This is sin piling upon sin. And eventually something must give way Either a man humbles himself to his knees before God, or God brings judgment. The judgment God brings upon Babylon is not merciful. The time for mercy is over. The judgment is a double portion. The sins of Babylon will receive double in judgment. Babylon has drunk from the cup of the devil and shall be punished appropriately. After the announcement of Babylon's judgment, there is mourning for her from men who used her, admired her, and obtained earthly wealth because of her. It has been noted that there are six classes of goods that men mourn for. There are goods of personal adornment, goods of lavish furnishings, goods of sensual gratification Goods for food, goods for decorative display, and finally the good of the souls of men. The souls of men are mourned for because they have aligned themselves with Babylon's wealth. Men mourn for Babylon because their source for all earthly wealth and pleasure is no more. Men also mourn for Babylon because they have so closely aligned themselves with her, and consequently, Babylon's demise is their own. Thus they mourn for themselves. The people of God, on the other hand, are instructed to rejoice over the fall of Babylon. Rejoice over her, O heaven Rejoice, saints and apostles and prophets. God has judged her for the way she treated you. The described judgment of Babylon is what the people of God have longed for, cried out for. Do you remember in Revelation chapter 6, the cry of the martyrs, how long, O Lord? Referring to the time that God would enact vengeance on those who cling to evil. And that question is answered here. How long? Well, this is the judgment. This is the judgment for Babylon. As a side note, it is interesting that the judgment of Babylon, although future, is described here as if it's in the past And that is because it is predetermined by God. This mentioning of it in the past allows Christians in the day of John's writing and every day since In particular, those who are being persecuted because of their Christian faith, to rejoice over the judgment of Babylon, even though it might not come to fruition many years in the future. Verse 21 moves us into a different part of the same vision while remaining on the same subject. John next sees a mighty angel. Whether this angel is the same as the one with authority or the one who owned the other voice. We do not know. The mighty angel uses a large boulder to exemplify what will happen to Babylon. This part of the vision brings us back into the present time, making the events described occurring in the future. After the mighty angel throws the giant boulder into the sea, he explains that his actions are an example of what will happen to Babylon. The emphasis of the angel's descriptive words is upon the absence of daily or cultural living among men within Babylon. No music will be played. No tradesman will be needed. No grinding of a millstone will help feed the hungry. Lamps will be darkened. Women will not be given away in marriage. Merchants will have nothing to sell and no one to sell to. No life will be recognizable, and any life left will not be worth living. But all of this will happen. To Babylon, to cities and people, great and small, who defy God by rejecting his son. That Babylon represents what is evil and what is at odds with the gospel is confirmed in verse 24. Where it states that in her is found all the blood of the prophets and the saints and all who have been killed on the earth. In Babylon, all that is violent and malicious toward God and his people is represented and judged. The description of Babylon's demise in this chapter is similar to the prophecies of Jeremiah and Isaiah. Who described the destruction of Tyre, Sidon, Egypt, Syria, and even Israel The descriptive destruction in John's vision has the same purpose as those of the prophets. God's people are to trust in the plan of God. Also, and this will be the remainder of our focus this morning, also the people of God are to heed God's instruction. He has only one instruction in this chapter. Before the destruction of Babylon takes place, a voice from heaven says, Come out of her, my people. So that you will not share in her sins, so that you will not receive any of her plagues. You recall when Jesus prayed what is called his high priestly prayer in John 17, he made a distinction when referring to his disciples. Saying that they were in the world, but not of the world. That distinction, although subtle, needs to be grasped For the sake of the soul of anyone who would follow Christ. When Jesus was conversing with doubting Jews, he referred to them as being of this world. And proclaimed that he himself was not. Today is Transfiguration Day. That's why we read from the Gospels about the transfiguration of Jesus. Jesus displayed that he was not of this world at his transfiguration when he revealed his heavenly nature in physical form. The light that came from him was like that revealed to Moses. Moses shone so bright, you remember, after standing before God that the people of Israel could not look upon his face. Jesus also explained that this world was passing away, and the inference was clear that those who were of the world and remain of the world will pass away with the world, and those who were of him would escape from the world's certain destruction. Later, when Jesus was warning his disciples of his own suffering and the suffering they would endure because they followed him. He explained that those who were of the world automatically hate those who are not of the world. To save his people, Jesus says that he chooses them out of this world Being chosen out of the world does not mean, of course, that the disciples are physically removed. They remain in the world just as we are in the world. Which is just as Jesus came into the world, it is not wrong for Christians to be in the world. And in fact, when Babylon is destroyed, Christians are called out of it. So that they are not destroyed. And being called out of it means that they were in it. We have to be in the world, but not of the world. For Christians to be able to physically remove themselves easily from Babylon when the time is right requires that they are not of the world or of Babylon. To be of the world is to be a product of the world There is a spirit of the world, a deceptive spirit that confuses the minds of men. Causing them to concern themselves first and foremost with the things of the world These deceived men become enamored by material and physical, material wealth and physical pleasure. They embrace what is popular. They think, vote, and converse like the irreligious men around them. They follow trends and reject tradition, all because that's what modern man is doing. They wear clothes that don't fit, either too small or too big, because that is what is acceptable in these days. They laugh at the blasphemous and the profane, because that is what is considered entertainment of the world. The deceived hear political arguments that are espoused by celebrities, and they agree because the person, well, the person is a celebrity. They don't spank their children when warranted because the popular psychologist on the popular talk show said they shouldn't. They don't eat red meat because the talk show host on the popular talk show doesn't like the way cows are treated. They read the latest book on the best seller list because it must be good, because it's on the best seller list. They watched the highest graded television program faithfully because it's, well, the highest graded television program. These are the people of the world. They do not think for themselves. They definitely don't think as God does. They don't believe in or want a higher standard for truth. They are simply willing followers of the world. Many of us know these people of the world because perhaps we used to be one of them. You know what it is to be of the world if you were brought to Christ in your teen years or sometime later. Even those who have been brought up in the church know what it is to be of the world because you have grown up with those who are of the world. And you have friends who are of the world What the voice of heaven is calling for, and what Jesus prayed for, is that Christians, although in the world, would not be of the world when the end of the world comes. The call is there. The prayer is there because they need to be there because there is a problem amongst Christians. There is a problem with Christians that while they are in the world, they actually become of the world. The church at Corinth was confronted by the Apostle Paul on different fronts because some of them were of the world. Paul said, Do not deceive yourselves. If any one of you thinks he is wise by the standards of this age, he should become a fool so that he may become wise. Paul described Christ Jesus as our deliverer from the present evil world. And reminded them that they were once enslaved by the basic principles of the world. He also addressed the heresies of the Christians at Colossae, who were going back, going back to the principles of the world. The Apostle Peter was also concerned about Christians returning to the world when he said, if they have escaped the corruption of the world by knowing our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ and are again going back entangled in it and overcome by it, they are worse off at the end than they were at the beginning. James addressed the issue directly in his epistle when he said, Don't you know that friendship with the world is hatred toward God? Anyone who chooses to be a friend of the world becomes an enemy of God. Such cannot be more plainly stated. And yet with these warnings and many others, people call themselves Christians, followers of Jesus Christ, bearers of the cross of his glory, who are also friends with the world. If you wonder whether you are a friend of the world, ask yourself hard questions. Do I have more social friends who are Christian than non-Christian? Am I able to talk freely about my faith amongst those with whom I socialize? What determines my fashion sense? What are my standards of propriety? And from where did I receive them? Where did I receive my moral values and how do they compare with Scripture? Where did I receive my political views? And how do they compare with Scripture? Does my social life and those and those whom I am social with encourage me about my devotion to God? Such questions are hard to ask and to be honest in answering if we have allowed ourselves to be drawn back into the world. If we are going to come out of Babylon before its destruction, for some it may require a wholesale change of friends and daily activities. It may require a new wardrobe. It may require a new way of thinking and behaving. It may require dying to old habits and creating new ones. The call to come out from among the world needs to be heard by the college student who has accepted his professor's skepticism and denial of truth. It needs to be heard by the wife and mother who is wearied by the effort to keep her and her children up to speed with the latest fads and fashions. It is to be heard by every father who, in order to fit in with the guise, compromises his conversations at work. It is to be heard by all who are in the world, because they follow Christ, are not to be of the world. Bishop J. C. Ryle said this: quote, in every age of the church Separation from the world has always been one of the grand evidences of a work of grace in the heart. He that has been really born of the Spirit and made a new creature in Christ Jesus has always endeavored to come out of the world and live a separate life. They who have only had the name of Christian without the reality, the reality of separation, have always refused to come out and be separate from the world. So which one are you today? Are you one who has always endeavored to come out of the world and live a separate life Or have ye refused but kept the name of Christian without the reality of living a separate life? Today is another chance to heed the call of Christ and come out. Come out from among the world and be free. Be free from the shackles that cuff those of the world. Be free to live as God has bidden. And in that freedom, you will know eternal life. Let us pray. Gracious God, we thank you for this call to come out. This call to come out before the destruction of Babylon, before the destruction of the world, and you making a new world, new for you to dwell with your people Help us to have the courage to come out and be free. This we pray in Jesus' name. Amen.

sermons.title: Submit
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: The name of the Father, of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated and turn to Revelation chapter nineteen. Revelation chapter nineteen. Many of you know that when I was installed as rector here at St. Stephen's, now over 24 years ago A burden of mine was the absence of men within the Christian church, especially their absence for weekly worship services. I am a confident believer and a strong proponent of covenantal headship of men. While all of us will stand before God to be held accountable for our actions on earth. Men and specifically husbands will be held accountable for both themselves and for their family. Wives will not be held accountable for their husbands, but husbands will be held accountable for their wives and for their children. Men are called by God to physically protect their home with the recognition that the woman is the weaker vessel. Men are also called by God to provide for their families. If a man does not provide for his own family, the scripture says he is worse than an unbeliever. Men are also responsible for their children's sexual purity and for their faith, especially if a man holds an ecclesiastical office. If a minister of the gospel does not have believing children, he essentially forfeits his position within the church. These are the responsibilities of men and only men. With such eternal responsibilities, men need to be held up in prayer. encouraged and fed in the faith and emboldened to fulfill what God has called them to do Unfortunately, in my estimation and the estimation of others, the body of Christ today has not fulfilled its obligation toward men. Example after example could be cited that show a greater feminization of the church, causing men to pursue NASCAR. Football, hunting, video games, and other alternatives where their masculinity can be expressed Because of the feminization of the church, alternatives have been offered by groups who recognize the problem. This past Friday night we had a meeting that is called a meeting for men that we call Holy Smokes It was given such a name because men are to feel free to bring cigars and pipes and to enjoy a smoke with good conversation. The conversations are based on how we apply our Christian faith to contemporary issues. And as enjoyable as such a time can be, that does not get men back to church. The modern church seems to think the answer is to split everyone up into groups Churches have groups for women, and then groups for couples over fifty Singles over 50, singles under 50, teens, young married, mothers with young children, and groups for men who want to be able to act like men What the church actually needs is not another group, but an environment conducive for men to be leaders. I thank God that He has given us such an environment as St. Stephen's. Our men do lead, and they lead well. As a side note, it has been asked of me in the past, and I have heard it asked of others, why do we not have women on the vestry? It is a legitimate question, considering that our canons do not restrict women from being on the best street. I admit that the reason we do not have women on the vestry is my doing. The vestry is a body of leadership that I choose to use to encourage men to lead in the church. While it is true that a woman holding the position on the vestry does not violate a biblical mandate Meaning that those on the vestry are not ordained clergy and thus could include women It is nonetheless a governing body that gives opportunity for men to step forward and to lead. It is the opportunity for men to lead, and that is what I take advantage of. It might not seem like it now, but all of my thoughts thus far about men and leadership and the church are a preface to Revelation chapter 19. I believe it is a necessary preface, for we are going to see that although leadership is masculine In the body of Christ, there is also a feminine aspect to such leadership that is necessary And yet it in no way compromises masculinity. Simply and plainly stated, although leadership in the body of Christ is male, the body of Christ is also the bride of Christ. To understand the content of chapter 19, we must quickly rehearse what was learned from chapters 17 and 18. The whore that rides the beast represents false prophets. False prophets who corrupt the gospel and persecute true believers. The beast that she rides represents every leader or city or nation that uses the whore and attempts to destroy the body of Christ. Babylon is a representation of both the whore and the beast, and as such, its demise is described and guaranteed in chapter 18. Chapter 19 comes on the heels of Babylon's judgment. Because of the judgment of all that is in an enemy of God and his people. The population of heaven shouts in worship. One of the weaknesses Of this congregation of St. Stephen's is that we do not sing out as we should And don't be offended. But consider that John says that he heard a loud voice saying, Hallelujah! Bold singing is heavenly singing. Singing a hymn such as a mighty fortress in a whisper. is unfortunate at best and disobedient at worst. To be sure, it can be noted that the loud voice heard by John is because of the great multitude that are singing. And yet we all know by experience that the louder each of us sings, such emboldens those around us to sing louder And when we all sing loudly, we become a loud voice. And thus we join heaven with our loudness. Because the words are shouted, we can conjecture that the verses are not meant to be put to a soft piano Or acoustic guitar strums, or anything that would be considered melodious. The words shouted are bold and require bold accompaniment. We should also notice regarding the words of the shout that they proclaim judgment. God is praised. Hallelujah. Because he has saved his people and has condemned the great harlot at the same time. The words shouted by the multitude are similar in content to the tone to many psalms written by King David. It has struck me, and I'm sure many of you, that much of David's Psalms, although they are songs of praise to God, contain verses that request God's judgment upon David's enemies. For example, David wrote, Contend, O Lord, with those who contend with me. Fight against those who fight against me. He then said, The righteous will be glad when they are avenged, when they bathe their feet in the blood of the wicked And then he said, May the praise of God be in their mouths and a double-edged sword in their hands to inflict vengeance on the nations and punishment on the peoples. To bind their kings with fetters, their nobles with shackles of iron, to carry out, to carry out the sentence written against them. This is the glory of all his faints, praise the Lord David, like the shouting in Revelation 19, rejoices in God because his enemies are destroyed. And recall, and recall that rejoicing because of the defeat of God's enemies did not begin with David. For we remember the song of Miriam when the Israelites rejoiced over Pharaoh's army being drowned in the Red Sea. I will sing unto the Lord, for he has triumphed gloriously. The horse and rider has fallen into the sea. While those songs are understandable to our sense of justice, they can also appear to clash, at least at first glance, with other biblical statements. Such as God takes no pleasure in the punishment of the wicked. God so loved the world that he gave his only son. God wills that all men be saved. Such passages reveal the heart of God toward his most intimate creation, man. Scripture teaches us that there is great sympathy between heaven and earth, and that there are emotions of tender pity felt in heaven towards man below. How is this class to be accounted for? We answer by first observing that the rejoicing is not caused by wailing or suffering itself. There is a separation between actual suffering and judgment. Secondly, we note that the rejoicing is not from vindictive feelings. There is no childish bragging with tongue out and face contorted to mock the enemies of God. All such feelings will be, we must, we trust, completely sanctified. What brings on the rejoicing is the knowledge that there are matters of immensely greater importance than the happiness or misery of individuals. It is a grievous thing to see a human being with a tear in his eye. That is true. But it is much more grievous thing to see him in rebellion against God. This we need to be taught. It is better to see men weeping over the bitter fruits of rebellion than to see them at ease in their revolt. One of the more insufferable things politicians do today is use the suffering of individuals. To shut down their opponents or a legislation they are against. If one person is suffering as a result of a particular piece of legislation, And such legislation may be a good thing for the majority of citizens and for the future. Because there is a story of one person suffering today, that is the story that makes the difference It moves the politician or the voters emotionally, and that emotional reaction sways the press, and such eventually sways the voter. I recall years ago a celebrity who does not need to be named but suffers from a debilitating disease while the symptoms are clearly evident and painful to watch when he speaks, you feel sorry for the man. And if you could do something to change his condition, you you would. This celebrity was speaking out favorably for stem cell research to be done from aborted babies. He is in favor of such for his own sake. But he is asking too much He is asking us to ignore the fact that God is the creator and that every child in its mother's womb carries the image of God. He is asking us to treat discarded children as lab experiments rather than embodiments of eternal souls. This we cannot do for the sake of those children, for the sake of children to come, and for the honor of God Himself. There are matters of immensely greater importance than the happiness or misery of individuals I know. I know what those who oppose this view would say in response. What if it was your loved one? What if someone you loved was suffering from a debilitating disease and you had to watch their suffering every day, not just on when they were on television? Wouldn't you want every possibility for a cure to be explored? Such questions are fair questions. They're fair because I do not know how I would react or certainly how I would feel. I do not know what I would want. I do know, however, what I should want. I do know what I should do. There is right and there is wrong in such situations. And that does not change simply because myself or a loved one is now the victim. I should want and do what is of greater importance than my own happiness or the happiness of someone that I love. To put it another way and to tie it together with the reference to the Bride of Christ, we rejoice because we submit To what is of greater importance, which is the divine sovereign will of God Continuing in chapter 19, after rejoicing over the judgment of the enemies of God, there is another shout, another great roar that sounds like thunder across the sky. That rejoicing is based on the wedding of the Lamb of God to his bride, the people of God. We are not going to get to the actual wedding until chapter 21. But here it is mentioned that the people of God are like a bride to the Savior, Jesus Christ. It is this reference that brings us back around to my initial comment regarding masculinity and the church. Isaiah, Ezekiel, Hosea, Matthew, John, and the Apostle Paul all refer to the people of God being as a bride to the Savior. Each of these references does not strip men from their masculinity, but explains a very important aspect of our relationship to Christ. We are to submit to him. The metaphor of a bride and groom relationship is used to explain our relationship to Christ Because it best communicates how we are to submit to him and how he will care for us. Submission is a godly characteristic that is best understood in terms of a wife's relationship to her husband. Submission in general is very masculine, very masculine, for it was the Son, Jesus Christ, who submitted to the Heavenly Father so that men might be saved from sin and death. Men, as in males, are to replicate that submission as they submit to Christ. And women, as they submit to their husbands, each is to accept the leadership above them, again, in doing so for the greater importance, the greater good of the kingdom of God. As the bride in this vision, we must notice that we prepare ourselves for Christ. The bride makes herself ready. In the context of this passage, the bride makes herself ready by rejoicing in the victory of God over his enemies. In rejoicing that the time of the Lord having full reign and authority over our lives is at hand, and that we are given fine linen, bright and clean to wear. Which represents righteous acts. Submission as a bride means that we accept the judgment of the groom We submit to his choice as to who is part of the bride and who is not. We submit to his judgment upon those who would come against his bride. We submit to the time of the wedding. We wait for him. He does not wait for us. We wait for him. And finally, we submit by receiving the fine linen that is bright and clean, for it is righteousness, his righteousness, that we are given. As most of you know, my parents died in a plane accident when I was very young. I have often imagined a scenario where they are on the other side of God's judgment on the day Christ returns. Would I be able to still rejoice? Would I be able to shout, Hallelujah? I will not, if I submit to my own heart or my own judgment, my individualism. I will be able to shout, Alleluia, if I submit to the groom. Submission to him is not just accepting his judgments when we agree with them. But must be when we don't. And submission is love We are to love the Bride of Christ. And in loving her, we are to treat her as a man treats a woman he loves. God said such love is laying down one's life. To lay down one's life is to do the opposite of sleeping around on her. Is the opposite of leaving her for another bride. Modern Christians, in their bouncing around from church to church, treat the bride. of Christ like she is a fluzy. But she is the opposite of a fluzy. And is to be treated as adorned and loved by her groom. We are to worship God as that ride, and when doing so, doing it loudly and boisterously So that the gates of hell shake and the world knows we have won. Shout for the bride, beloved. Shout as the bride. Jesus is coming. Amen. Let us pray. A gracious Father, it is It is not easy to communicate how we are the bride and yet we are to treat her well. The metaphor does break down a bit. But it is clear what you want us to do as the bride, to submit to your will, but also to worship you, to honor you for saving us, your bride. May we treat her as she should be treated. We pray this in Jesus' name. Amen.

sermons.title: Riding the White Horse
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. We are looking at the latter half of Revelation chapter nineteen, again picking up a verse Eleven. As a young boy I attended Roman Catholic Mass on a semi-regular basis with my father or my grandparents I did not have an appreciation for the service, nor did I fear God as I should, and consequently I was bored. Bored as they say out of my mind. Bobby Lynn is convinced that if I were born In the next generation, I would have been labeled ADHD. Probably so. I spent my time during the service primarily doing two things. I was either straining my neck to look at the clock that was mounted on the back of the wall just below the choir loft, counting the minutes left in the Mass, which always lasted exactly an hour. I don't know how they did that. Exactly an hour. And why would you put a church uh a a clock in a church sanctuary is beyond My wisdom, but there it was. I did that or I studied the statues adorning the walls of the sanctuary. The carvings were detailed images of what are called stations of the cross, the same stations we have depicted in our sanctuary. The images of those carvings remain with me to this day, and I thank upon those times with a feeling, as I felt then, of sadness. My sadness was due, I assume, to the manner that our Savior Jesus is portrayed in those stations. He was, after all, a suffering Savior. The primary focus of the stations of the cross is the suffering of Christ. This is not wrong. I make no judgments regarding such a focus. Because we are sinners before Almighty God There needs to be a continuous reminder that Jesus had to suffer so that we would be able to approach the heavenly throne. Without his suffering, there is no salvation. The blood of Christ enables our access to God. This we must never forget, never underappreciate. It is what goes along with this suffering that we can and should include in our worship. What goes along with his suffering is Jesus riding in on the white horse. Verse 11 of Revelation chapter 19 is a part of a new vision In another scene described to us, John sees heaven standing open. Heaven is open. And why is heaven open It is open because Jesus rides in on the white horse. Heaven standing open means at least two things for God's people. Blessings can come out of heaven, and God's people can go in. Blessings can go out and God's people can go in because Jesus rides in on the white horse. I have briefly mentioned the meaning of riding a white horse earlier in our study of the book of Revelation, and it would be Do as well to rehearse the meaning here in greater detail. Courses themselves symbolize power, speed, and agility. They also symbolize service, for they are a beast that is most useful in the service to men. Horses, although powerful and agile, are beasts that can be tamed. And thus the white horse is a contrast to the beasts. With the seven heads that is in rebellion to God. The one that Jesus rides is in submission to its creator The horse being white symbolizes the purity of its rider Whenever Jesus appears in John's vision, there is something about his appearance that communicates purity. He is the sinless one. And not only does the white horse symbolize purity, it also symbolizes victory. We often refer to Jesus riding in the city of Jerusalem on a donkey as a gesture of peace. It was culturally understood that a leader of men who was coming into a city would ride on a donkey if he was coming in peace. On a dark horse, either black or brown, when he is coming in war, or on a white horse, if he was coming to proclaim victory. Thus, Christians are assured of victory because Jesus rides in on the white horse. I have already identified the rider of the white horse as Jesus the Christ, but you will notice that his name is not mentioned in this passage. Other names provide his identity. The called name of the writer is Faithful and True This was the name given to Christ Jesus as he wrote to the church at Laodicea. The adjectives, faithful and true, are in reference to the writer's position as judge who executes justice. Faithful and true The writer is also said to have eyes of blazing fire. These are the same eyes of the Son of Man as described in chapter 1. They are blazing fire because they purify all that he sees. The crowns on his head are plural and are fitting for his title revealed in verse 16, which is King of Kings. His name that no one knows is another way to identify him. We may conjecture that the name is the same One prompt that was promised to be written on those who are faithful to the end. You remember in Revelation chapter 3, we we have Jesus saying, I will write on him the name of my God. And the name of the city of my God, the new Jerusalem, which is coming down out of heaven from my God, and I will also write on him my new name. The faithful will have that name, that new name written on them because Jesus rides in on the white horse Further identification of the rider confirms his sacrifice. His robe, it says, has been dipped in blood. Is it his blood or the blood of his enemies? Perhaps it is both. Because John refers to him as the Word of God, our minds automatically go back to John's gospel. Where it reads, in the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God The title confirms John's identification of Christ and his authorship of the revelation. The Word of God leads an army of heaven who are purified by the blood of their leader. making them righteous and able to wear white. The armies of heaven ride white horses and wear white linen because Jesus rides in on the white horse. As he rides, Jesus is armed. He is always armed, and his choice weapon is the sword. The sword he carries is his word, and that is why it is described as coming from his mouth. Remember when the God had created heaven and earth, he spoke it into being. God spoke and it was. Whatever he speaks comes to pass. Thus Jesus, being of the divine nature, speaks victory He speaks righteousness. He speaks rebuke of evil. And what he speaks comes to pass. The mission of the writer, thus the mission of Jesus, is to strike down the nations. The nations being targeted, his targeted foe, tell us that he is judging the harlot. The beast and Babylon, which is the same as judging the nations. He will destroy boundary markers He will tear down flags that distinguish one man from another. He will unseat local and national government heads His intent, and have no doubt he will accomplish it, is for there to be one kingdom, the kingdom of God. And he will strike down the nations, not by going from one battle to another, like an army of men would have to do. The reference to a wine press tells us he judges all at one time. That image of a wine press causes us to go back to Isaiah 63, which was our Old Testament reading. The Lord said, I have trodden the winepress alone. From the nations no one was with me. I trampled them in my anger and Trod them down in my wrath. Their blood spattered my garments, and I stained all my clothing. For the day of vengeance was in my heart, and the year of my redemption has come. The dominant and uninhibited way the writer will strike down the nations is emphatically stated in the title that is written on his robe and on his thigh. And while scholars get caught up with questions such as, was the name written on both the robe and the thigh? Is part of it written on the robe and part on the thigh? We will remember that a royal robe was placed on Jesus in a mocking manner after he was flogged, and that it was stripped from him before he was crucified. Now, now a royal robe is upon him, stating that the mocking words of men were prophetic words. He is a king, and more than a king. He is the king, the king of kings. The meaning, the meaning of the name being written upon The thigh tells us that where the sword normally hangs, this writer has a word that proclaims his identity. His sword, we remember, is in his mouth. He brings his enemies down with his word. The authority of his word proves he is Lord of Lords. It is at this point that the world will know Jesus as King and as Lord and will bow down to him Because he rides in on the white horse. Next, John sees an angel. An angel standing in the sun. The sun is also referred to elsewhere as being in mid-heaven, and the position is fitting for the glory of the angel. The call of the angel is to the birds of the air and is similar to the call uttered by the prophet Ezekiel. The birds are a chosen means. To remove the cursed flesh of man from the earth. A man, according to Scripture, is considered cursed who has his flesh torn and eaten by birds. We see from the list of men consumed that none of the enemies of God will be able to escape. The supper of the foul. Of the air is in contrast to the great supper God prepares and serves his people. Whereas the people of God dine on the choices of food and drink The enemies of God become choice food because their flesh is cursed. The enemies of God will be a feast for the fowl because Jesus rides in on the white horse. The vision moves again to another scene that at first reading we would anticipate it being lengthy and drawn out. When men gather to war against one another, we expect the battle to be lengthy, with casualties on both sides. But what John sees is not a lengthy battle, and certainly there are no casualties from God's army. The armies gather, but the beast is captured. With no beast, the enemies of God have no leader, and thus no strength Along with the capture of the beast is the capture of the false prophet. That's important. The identity, our identity of the harlot as representative of the false prophet is confirmed. The false prophet captured is the harlot that rides the beast. These two are thrown into the fiery lake, which is their final destination. The end of the nation's armies is a foregone conclusion, and the revelator describes their demise as a passing reference. The battle between the armies of nations and the heavenly host is short because Jesus rides in on the white horse. The casting of the beast and false prophet is assured because Jesus rides in on the white horse. The death and consumption of the flesh of men who are enemies of God will be realized because Jesus rides in on the white horse. I have ended each segment of the vision of John in chapter 19 with that phrase because Jesus writes in on the white horse. With the desire and pastoral hope that the victory declared might be seen in your mind Realized in your heart and appropriately applied to your everyday life While the suffering savior is to be prominent in our minds for reasons I have already stated, Some Christians shy away from such images, even concluding that crucifixes should not be worn or displayed. Such a conclusion is an overreaction For images of Jesus on a cross are historically accurate. But so are empty crosses Which is the part of the story we are focusing on today. For Jesus was a suffering servant and is the Savior victorious. Because the Savior rides in on the white horse, everything is different. Everything is different for those who follow him. Everything There is no such thing as a bad day if the Savior rides in on the white horse. Sadness is turned to joy, mourning is turned to laughter, and bleakness is turned to hope because Jesus rides in on the white horse. I also know, by personal experience and the experience of others, that the spirit of the false prophets have their day. Minds become confused. Lies are believed. Disillusionment reigns. False gods are followed, worshipped, bowed down to. False teachings become bestsellers. Scary politicians are elected. False teachers have their day. But in the background, we know that these are short-lived. There will come an end, and the false prophets will be cast into the lake of fire because Jesus rides in on the white horse. I also know by personal experience and the experience of others that the beast will have his day. He will persecute the godly. He will murder the faithful. He will kill the unborn. He will ravage bodies and minds with disease. He will brainwash children and their parents. He will raise nation to fight against nation He will be followed and he will be worshipped because the people of this world will be and have been and are deceived. But in the background, we have to know that this that his day will also be short-lived It seems a long time from our perspective that these evils prosper. But in God's terms and within his plan of salvation, it is actually short-lived. There will come an end to the power of the beast, as he too will be cast into the lake of fire, because Jesus rides in on the white horse. Our Christian heritage provides us magnificent artistic impressions of Jesus, his ministry on earth Paintings of an infant Christ with his mother tell us of his humanity. Paintings of his times of teaching and healing or breaking bread tell us of his brotherhood Carvings of his suffering body upon the cross tell us of his passion for the souls of men. Depictions of the empty tomb tell us of his glorious resurrection All of these are important images of important aspects of our salvation and how it was won. But where, I ask, is the depiction of Jesus riding in on the white horse? We need one. We certainly need one in our minds, for the image means victory, a victory that is not determined by life circumstances. Failing bodies or faulty thinking skills do not change the victory of Jesus. News reports across the sea or in our local community do not have an effect on who rains. Elected leaders have no more power than what is allotted to them by God. We are victorious because Jesus rides in on the white horse. I do not know all that you are going through this morning, what you went through yesterday, or what you faced tomorrow. Whatever it is that tempts you to be downtrodden, depressed, or fearful of the future, I am privileged to proclaim that Jesus rides in on the white horse. That knowledge will be enough for now. It will be enough for now. Let us pray. A gracious God, for the image provided in this chapter, for the for the coming resolution of this revelation, we thank you. May that image of Jesus, our Savior, your Son, riding in on the white horse remain with us, regardless of what we are tempted to. Believe or tempted to become discouraged. Whatever it might be, Heavenly Father, may that image always be before us, that we might know a victory has been won. And a victory will be known, as we pray in Jesus' name, Amen

sermons.title: Trinitarian Ten
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
