So we're dealing with Paul, we're dealing with Jesus, and we can even go back to the Old Testament from Proverbs chapter 16 verse 4. The Lord has made everything, everything. For its purpose, even the wicked for the day of trouble. There are other such passages in the Bible, but I want you to hear one more that gets to the heart of the subject. This is from John chapter 1, verses 11 through 13. Speaking of Jesus, he came to his own, his Jewish family, and his own did not receive him. But as many as have received him, to them he gave the right to become children of God, to those who believe in his name, who were born, who were born not of blood. Nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God Allow me to underline the end there. No one becomes a child of God by his own human will, but only the will of God. There are two things I hope to instill in you by pointing out this apparent dilemma of us making choices and God choosing. Some skeptics and critics would call it a contradiction, but I am sticking with the word dilemma, and here's why. Holy Scripture does not have to meet the standards of the reader. Such a statement causes concern because it may sound as if I am promoting a reading of Scripture as a belief in what the Bible says with blind faith. I do not As I teach every year in confirmation class, we start with Jesus. If Jesus taught what he taught and did what he did, That everything else in the Bible, what it teaches and proclaims, can be trusted. It is also a recognition that in order for us to know God And to have an understanding of God's ways, there is going to have to be paradoxes. I say necessary paradoxes because the Bible is describing the infinite who is God. Describing it to the finite, who is us, and we don't have the intellectual capability or the divine capability to know and understand all that God is. And so what does he do? He dumbs it down. He dumbs it down for us so that we can have a relationship with him. And so God can say that those who are born again are not born by way of their own will. but by his will, and then he can turn around and tell us to choose to serve him, because that is the type of language we understand. The manner I am explaining such paradoxes in the Bible is why I personally became frustrated in a systematic theology class in seminary. All of the Bible was being forced to be systematic by way of interpreting certain passages of scripture away from the plain reading so that they can fit into somebody's system. And so an Arminian, those who followed the teachings of James Arminius, would interpret a particular passage in a completely different manner than someone who followed the teachings of John Calvin. And the Calvinists would do the same without each group simply allowing the scriptures to say what they say Also, we can and must not interpret a particular passage from our vantage point. Referring back to verse 4 again and reading it from God's perspective, at least trying to read it from God's perspective, we can interpret it to mean that God is telling us His will, in terms of how he has compassion and desire for all men to be saved, that is in his heart. But that is not going to be what he does. And this is troubling to us For if we have a passion and desire for something, and we have the ability to see that same desire come to fruition, there is no doubt we are going to make it happen. If I will it, and I can fulfill that will, you and I are going to fulfill it, no question. That is because our passions can control us. Such is not true for God. His wills and desires are balanced. For God, there are other things He wills and desires, such as justice and righteousness. And he also wills that we have a say in all of this. And that reality brings me to my last point. There are places in Holy Scripture that call us to make choices. We see that in the wording of Jeremiah, who pronounced that he and his family were choosing to serve the Lord. It is implied in passages such as John 3. 16, again, where we are told that all that believe God sent his son will have eternal life, which implies that we must choose to believe. So there is a tension between God choosing us and us choosing God, and there is no way to reconcile the two. I have spent my entire ministry trying to better understand where our will ends and where God's will begins in an individual life. And where God's will ends and where the individual wills begin. And I am no closer to understanding the will of man and the will of God than when I started. I have given up the quest, and I've learned to accept it. The Bible says, choose this day whom you will serve. And it says we are not born of the will of man, but of God. So we are to choose, yes. And God chooses, yes. Both are true. Looking at this dilemma another way has helped me. I do not have a clean scorecard when it comes to keeping my word. Such as promises to remember something, or to be at a certain place at a certain time, or even to be a part of a group that I once committed to. After all, after seminary, I was ordained and thus made promises before God and men to serve as a clergyman in the Nazarene denomination. As my convictions changed, I gave back my orders. The point is, I have gone back on my word. So, if I can do that in other parts of my life, why am I safe from not leaving my faith in Christ Jesus? Thus, I am ever so grateful that my salvation, your salvation, is not dependent upon my will or your will. Because my salvation is based on the grace of God, by the will of God, I then can know my salvation is assured. But I still need to choose to follow him. Yes, every day. Every minute of every day. And the two realities can coexist. And I say thanks be to God. Amen.

sermons.title: Men Only
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. Turn in your Bibles to 1 Timothy chapter 2, picking up at verse 8. 1 Timothy chapter 2, picking up at verse 8, and I will give a bit of a warning. Some may need to buckle up on this one. Gonna be a bumpy ride for some. There are two generational sins. That my generation and the generation before should be ashamed of, because we have passed it down to the generations coming behind us. The first in is our national debt. That we can't control spending to the point of putting ourselves in debt to over $33 trillion is a disgrace. To give you an idea of what the number trillion is, understand that a trillion seconds Just one trillion seconds is equal to about thirty two thousand years. That means that if we were to pay one dollar One dollar every second to pay back what our nation owes in debt, it would take 1,056,000 years to pay it Such facts are so mind-blowing, words such as shameful and disgraceful are not strong enough. The other sin of my generation and the generation before me are responsible for is gender dysphoria The confusion about the differences between the sexes is the fault of our two generations because we failed to make it clear, a clear distinction of male and female roles in society. And when men did make those distinctions clear in the home, too many men abused their role, resulting in fear and chaos within the wives and children. And the church in general is a large part of the problem. The Christian church failed to continue to preach the whole counsel of God, which includes instructing husbands to love their wives as Christ Jesus loves his church and to preach such sacrificial love over and over again until the husbands start doing it What woman would not willingly submit to a man who is loving her sacrificially, just as Jesus has loved his church, giving his very life for her? And the church from the 1960s slowly allowed the secular culture to come into its doors. And not just take a seat in the pews, but a seat in the chancel, where ministers were ordained with no faith in the Bible and what it teaches about the different roles of men and women. The result was a clear example of the proverbial camel's nose in the tent. Once you let in the nose, the rest of the camel is going to come in. And so a doubting of authority of Scripture led to a rejection of certain passages of the Bible that were not popular with secular modern faithing. Which led to rejecting passages such as the one read today from 1 Timothy 2, where Paul instructs that women should not have leadership in the church over men And that rejection was a camel's nose being allowed in the tent, bringing with it a complete rejection Of any of Paul's writings that had to do with any moral teaching and any ecclesiastical instruction Such has proven true down to history, which is that if the Christian church stops leading a culture, it then starts to follow the culture. While all of this is serious stuff, and the truth of who is at fault for our national and now worldwide sins. There is a misfortune, a misfortune of not being able to enjoy the differences between the sexes. I came across a website that reveals the differences in habits between men and women. For instance, 95% of women will wash the dishes immediately after they have used the dishes. And 95% of men will wash dishes when they run out of clean dishes. One hundred percent of women use a hairdryer to dry and style their hair. Well, fifty percent of men use a hairdryer to dry their hair, and fifty percent use it to dry their socks. Women are equally split when choosing a shampoo, with concerns being the shampoo adds volume to their hair, or shine to their hair, or vitamins and minerals to their hair Men in comparison choose shampoo based on whether the bottle says shampoo Here are some other unique characteristics of men versus women. A married man is likely to live longer than a single man. But a married man is more willing to die than a single man. A man needs seven items in the bathroom. Toothbrush, toothpaste, razor, shampoo, deodorant, a towel, and cologne. There, on average, a woman uses 150 objects in the bathroom, with the maximum known by the man to be twenty. So a list of differences between men and women could go on and on, and many comedians have made a living pointing them out. And again, I state that such differences should be celebrated and never ever denied. So let us look at the passage of Scripture read from 1 Timothy 2, starting at verse 8. When Paul began the chapter, he was giving instructions on how the church should pray when they gathered for corporate worship. There was an order to worship in the early Christian church, and their traditions and liturgies were handed down and compiled in what is called the Apostolic Constitutions. We follow some of those traditions in our liturgy. In verse 8, Paul goes back to how he began the chapter, which is to instruct Christians on prayer. Men are to pray everywhere. And Jesus said that his followers are to pray always. And so we are to be in prayer always and everywhere. This means that, at the very least, we are to be in constant communion with God. We are to let Him know our concerns, our joys, our hopes, and our petitions. The Holy Spirit is our constant companion and we should honor Him for His constant presence And then Paul adds the lifting up of holy hands. Such was the Jewish practice, not only in taking a solemn oath or in giving a blessing, but also in prayer to lift up the hands. It is a sign of surrender for us, as well as a reaching to the heavens so that God would lift us up. As when a child lifts up his hands in order to be held by his parents So we are to lift up our hands to God. As we pray and as we lift up our hands to the heavens, we are to do so without wrath and without doubting. The word doubting can be translated disputing, which means that Paul is concerned about fighting between Christians. Our prayers are to be offered in peace, which is to be at peace with our fellow Christians. Such a need to be at peace with other Christians was known then by the very first Christians and is known now and all the times in between. There is a continuous need for Christians to work at loving one another. In verse 9, Paul turns to the women of the church and begins by addressing his concern for how some of the women are dressing. One of the two scenarios had likely occurred that caused Paul to address the issue of how women dress. Either he had forgotten to mention it. and thus brings it up here in this letter, knowing it was a problem in a largely populated city such as Ephesus, where wit modern women then would dress to be attractive to men The second scenario might have been that there was a problem within the church, and he has been made aware of. And so he brings his apostolic authority to weigh in on the issue. Some commentators and even preachers like to get in on the specifics, such as talking about braiding hair, but I believe we are to stick with the principles. We need to focus on the principles and underlying Paul's concern. First, Paul does not say anywhere that women shouldn't adorn themselves. Instead, he is giving principles of moderation. When women adorn themselves, said another way, a woman's purpose for adorning herself should be to accentuate her femininity as opposed to her sexuality. And the idea of moderation is to not make herself the center of attention. After all, she is attending church to worship, not to be ogled. And it can work the other way. I remember a young woman attending my brother-in-law's church wearing dirty torn jeans and a t-shirt. to church worship without having bathed for several days. She was trying to show that she didn't care what the world thought regarding how she looked, and all the while getting as much attention as she would have if she did care what others thought. This brings us to the principle of verse 10, which describes a woman who is to be most concerned about good works that she does that reflect the godliness within her. Elsewhere, Paul praises Christian women for doing works of charity, for caring for widows and young women, which can be a part of those good works he is naming here. Next, as we follow Paul's line of thinking while addressing issues of women in the church, as compared to men, he makes it clear that women are not to take positions in the church teaching or otherwise, that would place them in a leadership role over men. The silence he requires in verse twelve is in regards to the leadership roles. Much has been made. Much has been made about these verses, especially in the 20th and 21st century. Western minds have accepted a feminist mindset. That insists that women are equal to men. Unfortunately, but necessarily, I must state some qualifications. Women are most certainly equal to men in their value and in their image of God they bear And as I mentioned earlier, men are to treat their wives as being above equality, as they are to love them as Jesus loves his church, and there is no higher standard. By equality, the feminists have insisted that women can do anything a man can do. Certainly, men on average are stronger than women But of course there are always exceptions on both the part of a woman and a man. But overall women are not equal in terms of physical strength. There's nothing wrong with that That should be accepted as obvious, though I am aware it is not. But those who deny it are simply lying to others and lying to themselves. Other differences are found in what women and are drawn to do in life. While the majority of steel workers and mechanics and carpenters and truckers are men, and the majority of teachers and caretakers are women, There is absolutely nothing wrong with those choices in life. And while there are women who are very good public speakers and thus would likely preach good sermons, and while there are women who fear God We pray without ceasing and can even lead vestry meetings. Such gifts are wonderful to have, but a woman is not called to use those gifts as a leader in the church. The main point being the person must be called to lead the church, whether it be a deacon, a presbyter, priest, or a bishop. Such offices can only be filled by men. There are so many ways the Bible teaches this, but I don't have time to address each one, so I will only list a few God chose patriarchs such as Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and Joseph, and Moses, and Aaron, and Joshua, etc. To lead his people. God chose men as prophets to speak his word to his people, such as Elijah, Elisha, Isaiah, Jeremiah, etc. Jesus chose twelve men to be his closest disciples. And when one fell away, God chose another man And then God chose Paul to be an apostle to the Gentiles. And the church chose men to replace the apostles, calling them bishops. And the Church for centuries, both to the East and in the West, only ordained men to lead the Church The ordaining of women was only introduced to the Christian church starting within the main denominations in the 1960s. And since that time, the Christian Church has become less and less significant in each culture that it has been a part of. Because again, they don't lead the culture, they follow it. There have been many objections, of course, to what I have said, and the primary one, or the one that seems to have stuck, is that Paul, when he wrote these restrictions on women in the church, That he was, in his character, misogynistic. And for the people who concluded such, it was reason enough to dismiss what Paul instructs But the objectors also add that women were not formally educated in the days of the apostles, and since that has been rectified, women can now teach in the church But there is a very, very obvious problem with that way of thinking. For Paul makes it clear in verse 13. Why he gave the instruction for women not to teach or lead in the church? It is because Eve was deceived, not Adam. Adam's sin was to follow the leadership of his wife. And Eve's sin was listening to the serpent instead of to her husband. Thus, Paul is referring to Holy Scripture as the reason for his instruction. And he is referring to the created order that God chose. And he was referring to the curse placed, a curse placed upon the woman, which is that she will yearn for her husband, which means to want his place, but he will still rule over her. Such explains the tension seen in every generation and in every culture between men and women, husband and wives. That the Christian Church have camels standing in their tents is now blatantly obvious, and the ordaining of women and giving them a place of authority over men is one of the reasons why. And you can you can easily see how this progresses. A church leadership justifies ordaining women, going against what Paul specifically teaches. And going against precedence in Scripture and against the traditions of the church historic, and how it has always interpreted Scripture, all because Paul is now thought of to be misogynistic And now everything that Paul writes about is a fair game to be doubted and even rejected. The result is churches ordaining openly, sexually immoral men and women. And even elevating such sinners to the office of bishop. The result is an abandoning of the words of Jesus Himself, making him to be no more than a wise sage. The slippery slope has been slipped upon, and many are sliding down it as a toboggan, a toboggan slide to hell. Of course, what Paul says regarding the reason why women should not have authority over men in the church is good enough for those who trust the scriptures as our authority. I want to add another biblical argument, one that I discovered some years ago, and now it needs repeating. When I started to walk with Jesus, I was always told that the Christian life can be summed up by understanding it to be a relationship with Jesus. The Christian life is about knowing Jesus. That is what I understood, and that is what I taught. Until I asked the question. What focus does Jesus have in regards to our relationship with Him? And the answer is that Jesus taught us to go to the Father. Jesus wanted us to see the Father in him. When he taught us to pray, we were not taught to pray to him, but to the Father. And this is fitting. For from the Old Testament, we are told that the main goal of God, the Father, is for us to be his people and for him to be our God. It then makes sense. It follows that the best and only representative of the Father to lead God's people in the church is the male. For the male comes closest to fitting the person of the father. And so let us take back what has been so foolishly given away. We are to let men lead. Lead in the home, lead in the culture, and of course, lead in the church. And if they do a poor job, we simply need to raise better men. I realize that I cannot end this sermon here because Of verse 15, where we are told that women are saved via childbearing. Such a principle is similar to the curse of Eve. Who was to give birth in pain, and the seed from her would crush the serpent's head. The seed we know we now know was Jesus. And the serpent was and is Satan. And Jesus has crushed his head by overcoming death But all women are to be able to identify with the curse of Eve, either by enduring the pain of childbirth or enduring greater pain, the sanctifying pain of raising children. And all Christian women are to continue in faith, love, holiness, and self-control. And that makes them equal to men, because men need to do the same. Amen. Let us pray. A gracious and merciful God, these words come in such contrast, in conflict with our culture. And yet it is your word, it is your will. Give us the courage to live it out. This we pray in Jesus' name. Amen.

sermons.title: Recruits Needed
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. We are looking at 1 Timothy 3 verses 1 through 7 and as always it would be helpful for you to follow along in your pew Bible First Timothy chapter 3, 1 through 7. I had a friend in the state of Washington who went to a different high school than myself. But he told me a story of recruiters from armed forces coming to his assembly in his school's gymnasium And each representative of the armed forces gave a pitch for why young men and young women should sign up for their particular branch of our armed forces. The representative from the Army was first, and then the Navy, then the Air Force, and so on. All gave inspirational speeches, except one. The representative from the Marines was last to speak. And when he got to the podium, The only thing he did was stare at the crowd, glare at the crowd, giving them all a look over, and then he said the following. There isn't one person here good enough to be a Marie. And then he sat back down. When the assembly ended, each representative had a booth where students could get more information about each branch of the armed forces. And the longest line by far was the line for the Marines. Now I picture a similar scenario. Where I am invited to an assembly where different professions are being introduced to the students Where they can hear what it takes to be a part of different professions, such as what it was like to be a doctor, a policeman, a firefighter, a chef, and so on. And then it's it's my turn, and I too go last, and I scowl at the students. And I also give them a lookover, and then I say in a gravelly voice, there isn't one person here good enough to be a pastor. And then I sit down. And we too are given booths where students can find more information. And I guarantee you. I guarantee you my line would be the shortest, and it's quite possible that no one would come to my booth. My point is that being called to serve in the ministry of the church is not attractive no matter how it is presented. Beloved, I am on the board of our seminary. I am on the examining chaplains committee that gives oral exams to potential presbyters, priests, and deacons. Thus, I can report to you from firsthand knowledge that the seminary is poorly attended, and not all who attend are going to serve in the Reformed Episcopal Church. And we are in no sense busy giving oral exams to potential priests or deacons. For example, in Maryland, for several years, over a decade, St. Stephen's was the only parish that has two priests And Father Bill has been the only replacement our churches have had if a minister is necessarily absent. Stating it plainly. We need more men. The church in general needs more good men. And I am sincere when I add the word good. The church does not need more warm bodies. The church does not need salary collectors. The church does not need more men to preside over dead and dying churches. We have plenty of those The church needs good men. It is easy to see The train of thought that St. Paul had when he starts to address the qualifications for men to serve as ordained officers in the church. He had just explained, as we went over last week, that he did not want women to teach or have authority over men in the church. And so it is natural to ask, what does God want in leaders? And so Paul sets out to answer the question. As he does, we should consider why these subjects need to be addressed. And part of it is likely because of the false teachers in the midst of the church at Ephesus. And you will remember that Timothy was indeed ministering to that church. Those false teachers caused Paul to send Timothy on his behalf and straighten out the church. And so when Paul says that a minister must not be a lover of money, There was likely false teachers who loved money. Such can be assumed about all of the qualities mentioned And so we come to verse one of chapter three. The word translated here To be the English word bishop is episcopoi in the Greek, and it is where we get the word episcopal. It is fair to say that the Presbyterians have gotten a few things correct, and one of those things is recognizing that the word bishop and the word elder in the New Testament are interchangeable and thus are referring to the same office, and both words mean overseer. It was not until the apostles died out that the church used three offices, for they needed to have an office to do what the apostles were doing, which is defend the faith and ordain priests and deacons. That happened in the second century by the second generation Christians. Paul expects men to desire such positions and to encourage them, he says, those persons who desire such desire a good work. But many people see it, but not many people see it that way. They don't see it as a good work. And I can speculate why. In your average church, the pay for a minister will likely not be what they can get in a secular job. Properly feeding the sheep, which is properly teaching and preaching, can be time-consuming and burdensome. Carrying the burdens of numerous people can be emotionally draining. A minister soon realizes That with every trip to the hospital, there is only one good reason, and all the others are bad. But those are the negative side. The joys are plentiful. As a minister, you get to be a part of some of the most joyous times in people's lives. The baptisms, the confirmations, the weddings, the graduations are just a few of those joys you get to be a part of. Although you do realize at times you get invited just to say the prayer at the beginning. You might as well leave after that. And the privilege of preaching, the privilege of preaching God's word, never gets old, at least not for me. So it is desiring a good work. Verse 2. Here we have a full verse on what is needed of every man who desires this good work. To be blameless is not to be sinless, but is more of being a man of a good reputation. Notorious. Notorious sinners should not apply. Now, if you are notorious in the past, like Paul, But have shown fruits of repentance and a new life in Jesus, then you can still desire this good work To be a husband of one wife does not mean you have to be a husband, for neither Paul nor Timothy were married. And there was polygamy being practiced by a few in the Jewish community, but it was very difficult to afford two or more wives. For a man who had been divorced, as you remember, how easily it was according to the Mosaic Law to get a divorce, which was simply to hand your spouse a piece of paper That is not what Paul is specifically addressing, and most churches have decided to handle such on a case-by-case basis. To be temperate, sober-minded, and of good behavior can be summarized by living a life of self-control. An overseer's temper must be under control, his drinking habits must be under control, and his overall behavior must be under control. One of the greatest gifts a parent can give their children is discipline, which leads to having self-control. Having self-control in all areas of your life is a great gift. Being hospitable is next, and that means that if a man does have a wife, she better be on board with him serving the church. When we examine possible candidates for ordination, we want assurances from the candidate that his wife is on board. We have even talked of including the wife in a portion of our examinations because having people in your house being hospitable is part of what it means to be a pastor of people. Being able to teach is next, and that is a given. The last thing Jesus told Peter was, feed my sheep. And it is to be a priority in ministry. Next is not being given to wine and not violent. And the two might go hand in hand, for people are more likely to be violent when they are drunk. And this again may be a direct reference to the behavior of those false teachers. The importance of not being greedy for money, and soon after mentioning not being covetous, is speaking to similar realities. An overseer can think that the money people give is because of him, or primarily for him, and some churches allow the minister to handle the money. Thanks be to God. That is not how things are done in this parish. I don't see the money. I don't know who gives or how much you give. I don't touch the money. And what I spend on behalf of the church, I am accountable for. All ministers should have in place a protection system that prevents accusations of being greedy. The not being covetous part means to be satisfied with what you are paid and how you are cared for. And to accept the reality that there will be people in your parish that have more and nicer things than you have. When you are desiring to be an overseer, you are in it to serve the Lord. And so what you get in return needs to be enough in your heart. Finally, in between those two words are the standards of being gentle and not quarrelsome. Being gentle can relate to not being quarrelsome because words can be powerful and they can hurt. As a younger man, I took pride in my ability to win arguments. But the best challenge I received during those days. was to be asked if I wanted to win arguments or if I wanted to win people, because you cannot do both. That has a has certainly calmed me down over the years. If we were to stop at verse three, We would recognize that the standard of an overseer is quite high, especially when the character of a leader is to be displayed day in and day out. But then there is verse four. And perhaps this verse scares most of the people away. An overseer is to rule his own house well. And by well, he means having his children in submission to his authority and In reverence to God. The principle for this standard is stated in verse 5, and it is impossible to refute If you can't do something in a small context, you're not going to be able to do the same in a larger context. You must be able to pastor your own family before you can pastor a congregation. I read one commentator say that this standard is the most violated one in the evangelical church of all the standards listed. It is a shame that people make jokes about the preacher's kid being the most rebellious in the church. The joke works because of how many examples we have seen down through the years. What I have never understood. It's how pastors know their son or daughter is in rebellion and they refuse to step down. Each overseer should know that the most important parishioners they have are their family members. The gesture of stepping down would hopefully show to the rebellious child that how important their soul is to the father. For such is important enough for the father to change his calling and to face an uncertain future. Such would give the greatest chance for the child to repent. Admittedly, there is a problem in saying what I have said. Just how long should a family wait in terms of when a child of a minister rebels? If a child of mine turns away from the Lord in his 30s, does that mean I am now disqualified? Paul doesn't address such a scenario, and once again, we might need to look at each case differently, but it is interesting to note. That at the Council of Carthage, the Council of Carthage in 397 A. D. , the Council where they settled such things as what books should be included in the canon in the Bible They also decided that no man could be ordained a bishop, a presbyter, or a deacon unless he could show that all of his children had converted to Christianity. I don't know how well such a practice would go over today. Next, the overseer cannot be a novice or someone new to the calling. We can imagine that it was tempting for first-century Christians, first or second generation Christians, to choose as their overseers men who were charismatic in personality. Or better looking than most. What they needed, what the congregation needed, was someone who was humble and who took his calling seriously. All others would be susceptible to pride for being chosen. And like Paul warns, they are susceptible to go the way of the devil. And finally, the overseer must have a good reputation in the outside world. He should be known to the unbelieving world as a man of integrity. He is to be a man people can trust. If he does not have a good reputation in the world, it is the church that can ruin its own reputation Now there are two points I wish to make, having said all that I have said regarding these verses. There is nothing peculiar in this list for all Christians. For there is nothing unique regarding Christian ethics to church officers. It is tempting to think that the type of life an ordained man is to live is of a different and higher standard than a common Christian. But Paul is actually describing the Christian life for all Christians. Every Christian should strive to live by these standards. But it is the man seeking to be a priest that needs to be examined regarding these standards. Examine in his personal life. Consider how these standards apply to all Christians. Number one, every Christian should strive to live a life that is above reproach. Consider that when the idea of blamelessness appears in the New Testament, it is in reference to all Christians, not simply to the leaders. Number two, similarly all Christians are to be faithful to their spouses. All forms of sexual or marital infidelity are condemned, condemned outright in the Word of God. Number three, all Christians are to be sober-minded, self-controlled, respectful. decent, dignified, and we are all commanded in other places in Scripture, such as in the book of Romans, Book of Hebrews, Book of 1 Peter, to show hospitality. which is to have an open and welcome home. Number four, no Christian is permitted to be drunk or violent or quarrelsome or a lover of money. We are taught repeatedly and explicitly that such vices are to be banished from our lives and also repeatedly warned of the consequences if they are not. Number five, every Christian parent is to raise his children in the instruction and discipline of the Lord. Paul refers to it as raising children in the fear and admonition of the Lord. 6. We are all to be humble. And we are all to be the salt of the earth, light of the world, a city set on a hill. Jesus instructed that the world should be able to see our good works and glorify God in heaven. So let us conclude that this sermon is for the purpose of a few excuse me. Let us not conclude that this sermon is for the purpose of a few. Or these verses apply only to those who are seeking the church office. They are in fact to apply to each and every one of us. My second point Goes back to my story about recruiters coming to a high school or an auditorium where someone will care to listen to their pitch. So here's my pitch. The church today needs men. And as I said earlier, the church needs good men. Fathers and mothers, you should be upholding the offices in the church with honor before your children And you should make them aware that serving the church as an ordained minister is an option to pursue as they search to see what they want to be when they grow up. And young men, there are great challenges ahead of you if you pursue the ministry There is spiritual warfare to engage in. There are words that need to be spoken in truth and with conviction that no one else is speaking. There are people who need to be fathered, pastored, led, and inspired. There is a world that doesn't believe the Christian life can be lived faithfully, and you will have the challenge to show them different. And there are plenty of souls who have not heard the gospel of Jesus Christ because it has been lost in cultures both in the East and the West Hemispheres. And the gospel won't be heard, and souls will not be turned from darkness to light without a preacher. We need men who have the courage as Isaiah did when the Lord queried who he should send to speak forth his word. And Isaiah said, Here I am. Send me. Send me no matter the cost. Send me no matter the pay. Send me no matter the ridicule or scorn I receive. Send me no matter the spiritual or physical danger I face. Send me And to the old men, there are still years you can fill by serving the Bride of Christ. You will find that serving the bride of Christ is one of the most privileged works. you will have ever done. It is indeed a good work to aspire to, but only for good men. Let us pray.

sermons.title: Deacons
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: The name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. You would join me turning in your Bibles to 1 Timothy chapter 3. Picking up at verse eight. First Timothy three, picking up at verse eight. There are plenty of stories in the Bible that teach the dangers of pride and the positive effect of humility. It was pride that rose up within Eve when she believed she could be like God, and therefore she ate of the forbidden fruit. It was pride that was within Adam that moved him to blame God for his own disobedience because God gave Eve to Adam. It was pride that led Cain to be jealous of his brother Abel, jealous to the point of killing him. And it was pride that prevented him from telling God the truth when he was confronted with his evil deed. It was pride that moved the people to resist the presence of God in the world. Which led to the people's hearts being bent toward evil and that continually. It was pride after the flood that convinced the people they could build a tower that would keep them safe from another flood. And therefore they didn't need God. And all of that pride is just in the first eleven chapters of the book of Genesis. There is a great irony today in the fact that there are certain political groups who want to force moral change on Western society who use the word pride as a positive. But the reality is that pride is one's vice, a vice that ends in a bath in the likes of sulfuric acid. Because pride leads to destruction, the opposite is true about humility. There is a natural power in humility that even men with evil hearts cannot deny. I came I came upon the following story that highlights such a power. One day A sage came to a king for an interview. The sage had to wait for a long time because the king was very busy. Finally, the king said he could come in. When the sage entered the hall, the first thing he did was take off his hat and bow to the king. Immediately the king took off his crown and bowed to the sage The ministers and others who were around the king asked, What are you doing? He took off his hat because he is an ordinary man, but you are the king. Why should you have to take off your crown? The king said to his ministers, You fools, do you think I wish to remain inferior to an ordinary man? He is humble and modest. His humility is a pillow's virtue. He showed his respect to me. If I did not take off my crown, then I would be showing less humility than an ordinary man, and I would be defeated by him. If I am the king, I should be better than everybody in everything. That is why I took off my crown and bowed to him. Such is a recognition of the power, again, of humility. Now I have started with the dangers of pride and the power of humility. because of what is instructed in 1 Timothy chapter 3, starting at verse 8, regarding the office of a deacon. The word deacon simply means servant And as you are aware, being a servant requires a great deal of humility. As we look at these verses, let us again Be again mindful that the false teachers Timothy was having to confront were likely practicing the opposite of what is being required of priests and deacons. Verse 8. The word likewise harkens back to the previous verses on what is required of a priest. In fact, there are at least six similar requirements for deacons as there are for priests. To be reverent is to fear God in a reasonable manner Meaning that his fear is not so much that it scares him or freezes him, and it is enough to not want to offend God. A double-tongued man is one who speaks one thing and does another, or teaches one thing and believes the opposite. We could simply call him a liar. Being not given to wine is one of those duplicates from the previous list, and once again reminds us of the virtue of self-control. To not be greedy for money means that every single one of those prosperity preachers on your television screen are in violation and are plainly of the devil No matter what their words say, no matter their denials, they are Simonizers. Simonizers are named after a man in the book of Acts called Simon. Who wanted to buy the power of the Holy Spirit, but not be controlled by the Holy Spirit. Thus, a Simonizer is a person who only relates to God and the gospel in reference to money. Such men do not know God and will be eternally condemned. Verse 9 The mystery of the faith mentioned here is a reference to the gospel itself. In St. Peter's first letter, he refers to it as that which angels longed to look into. To describe it as such is identifying how it all looked before Jesus and his sufferings were revealed. First, you had the covenant promises to Abraham. Then you had the wandering of his family, the famine, the jailing of Joseph, then the elevating of Joseph. Then the enslavement of the whole people of Israel, then the deliverance of Israel, then the giving of the law and all of its sacrificial requirements, and then the dispersion, and then the prophets Where was God going with all that had happened? Such was a legitimate question. No one knew except the Trinitarian God how it would all come together. And now we know, for from the family of Abraham came Jesus, who was the promised seed spoken about to Eve. Now we know that the enslavement of Israel and the freedom given to them was a foreshadow, a foreshadow of how men would be free from sin. And the sacrifices. The sacrifices were a foreshadow of what Jesus would do for mankind. And the crowning of kings and the use of prophets Fill out the offices that Jesus would fulfill as he is revealed to be prophet, priest, and king. The mystery revealed. And the mystery is solved, but it must be protected The call to protect it must not be taken lightly. Consider how many mainline churches have not protected it and are now bankrupt of faith. Verse 10. I mentioned last week that the requirements of a priest should be the standard of living for all Christians. It is only that the priest must be examined to be assured that they are living such a life. That is said plainly here regarding deacons. They should be examined, they should be tested, they should be Tested and required to show they're living up to the standard. And I can offer a behind-the-scenes look at what such examinations can be like The questionnaire we require for the office of deacon is shorter than what is required for a presbyter, but certainly thorough enough. And in case you are not aware, our form of government requires a man to be first examined and ordained a deacon before he can even pursue being a priest. But the answers to the required questions to the required questions can reveal the heart of a man toward the ministry and the standard of education he has achieved. The results vary and sometimes very dramatically. I can assure you that no one gets a pass just because we need men. Again, we desire and require that they be good men. It is not possible to know if a man is blameless. Which means he is not given to patterns of sin. But such is why men are required to serve in the church. So that their lives can be seen and the process to even be examined includes a recommendation of two priests. And a recommendation from the vestry where the man serves, all to give evidence that a blameless life is being pursued. Verse eleven. Here, Paul is more specific regarding what is required of a minister's wife. Before, in the charge of a priest, the wife simply needed to be one in number. Here, there are specific behaviors practiced and avoided. Of the ones to practice, she is to be reverent, temperate, and faithful. Of the ones to avoid, she is not to slander. Which is to speak falsely of someone to damage their reputation. Now, regarding the wife of a minister, let me say that she is not a pastor in any way. Too many parishioners expect the wives of pastors to do counseling and to lead the ladies in prayer and to know biblical insights. It is important for pastors' wives that you know That it was their husband that was ordained and not her. And my wife didn't insist I tell you that. But there are plenty of moments where things were expected of her as if she was me and she is not. And secondly, it is true beyond doubt that a wife can make or break a man's ministry. If she is not reverent, others in the church will believe they too don't need to be reverent. If she is not temperate or faithful, others will believe they too don't need to be either of those things as well. And if she slanders, oh my, she can be the cause of division in the church And I might as well start working on my CDL again to go back to driving a school bus if my wife is a slanderer. Verse 12. We come back again to be a deacon, being a man with one wife and a man who rules his home well, which is to love his wife as Jesus loves the church. And it is to train up his children in the fear and admonition of the Lord. And it is to live his personal life as if they, his family, are the most important church he could ever pastor. I confess that when I started to pursue the ministry, I knew that because of my personal pride and my more direct personality That I would need a good woman who stood by me and that my children didn't resent me and were faithful to the church. I know how people reason. They may not like me or my style, but they are impressed that my wife stands by me. And because of it, they conclude that he can't be all that bad. And if my children respect me and are faithful in the church, parishioners can conclude that at the very least I can pastor my family. But training up children to believe and walk with Jesus is not only for the clergy to heed Every man can see his family as his own parish, in the sense that they need to see their father's faith in Jesus And the manner he loves their mother and how he loves them will affect their faith really for the rest of their days. The manner a man pastors his own family is his greatest testimony regarding his Christian faith. Men, you must take on those responsibilities for the church needs it and the world needs it. Verse 13 Here is described the effectiveness of a faithful life lived. A man who has a calling on his life to serve the church formally. and does it well, not only helps the Christians, but also the unbelieving world. Simply and honestly put, there are too few men in the church who live up to the standards required. And the church and the world need such men and such testimonies. We are not Our attention to to go next is back to the meaning of the word deacon, which again means servant. I remind you of how the office of a deacon came about. Recall in the book of Acts that shortly after 3,000 people were added to the Christian faith, and the Christians started gathering and sharing their wealth and goods with one another It naturally and understandably occurred that disagreements arose among them. Of course there were contentious moments. For these people were in no sense perfect, and all were immature in understanding how their new faith in Jesus as the Savior was to be expressed in their personal lives And in their gatherings with other believers. And when you are sharing everything with everyone, discrepancies cannot help but arise. And that is what happened. The Jews who had become Christian and the Greeks who had become Christian, they came from different cultures, and they had not yet been united with one another What happened was, when it was time to distribute the food being shared, the Greek Christians noticed that the Hebrew Christian widows were getting a greater share than the Greek Christian widows. Meanwhile, the apostles were busy sharing the gospel and teaching the people, and more people were being added to their body of believers every day. But the controversy was so great that the congregation bothered the apostles with it, but the apostles did not want to be interrupted. So they instructed the people to choose from among them men, men of good reputation, to help settle daily struggles. This pleased the people, and so they chose seven men, and hands were laid upon the men, and prayers were made by the apostles to consecrate them, what we call today ordaining. And the men, the seven men, were the first to be placed in the office of deacon. Thus, at the very heart of the office of deacon is service. A deacon, then, is a man who does not run away when there is service to perform, but instead runs to the need. And I remember Father Ricky when he was here telling me that he was taught in seminary that an ordained man, no matter his office, is still and always will be a deacon. That, of course, means that all ministers, whether he be ordained a priest or consecrated a bishop, is to have the heart of a servant. Deacons, priests, and bishops should line up right beside the men of his church and mulch the grounds, pick weeds, vacuum floors, paint walls. Well no, I ha I hate painting, so that's not gonna happen. Put away chairs and tables after fellowship, etc. , etc. All ministers should be men of service and more service. And to serve, I remind you, it takes humility. For a true servant, there should not be a task too meaningless. The servant, the humble one, never puts himself First, because his master said that the first shall be last, and the last shall be first. In the foreword of Simon Sinek's book titled Leaders Eat Last Lieutenant General George J. Flynn of the United States Marine Corps says the following, and I apologize to those of you who serve in other branches, for this is the second Sunday I've mentioned the Marine Corps. My fault. But this is what he says. When you are with Marines gathering to eat You will notice that the most junior are served first, and the most senior are served last. When you witness this act, you will also note that no order is given. Marines just do it. At the heart of this very simple action is the Marine Corps' approach to leadership. Marine leaders are expected to eat last because the true price of leadership is the willingness to place the needs of others above your own. Great leaders truly care about those they are privileged to lead and understand that the true cost of leadership privilege comes at the expense of self-interest. Such a description are biblical principles lived out. Of course, for the Christian The example set by the United States Marine Corps cannot be compared to the example in leadership that we know, for it is in Jesus himself. Who St. Paul said made himself of no reputation, but humbled himself to be formed in the image of man that he might serve man. There is no greater example of service and humility than Jesus the Christ. So the standard for ministry Even at the lower office of a deacon, is still very high. And still, the standard is for all men, especially for fathers. And the only way any man can be reverent, self-controlled, hold the faith, be found blameless, and rule his family well is to be humble and to serve. And as this section of Scripture ends, the end of verse 13, such living will lead to great boldness in Jesus Christ. Amen. Let us pray. Gracious and merciful Father, we thank you for these standards. Help us not to shy away from them, even if we are not called to be a priest or a deacon, but simply called to be good men for your kingdom's sake. Especially for our fathers here. Help them to take up this mantle, to live it out by service, that their children might bless your name. It is in Jesus' name we pray. Amen.

sermons.title: What we Believe
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. Turn if you would to first Timothy chapter three. Picking up at verse 14. First Timothy three, picking up at verse fourteen We are all aware, having learned from our social studies class, or civics class, that in the United States there are three branches of government You have your executive branch, which is the president and his cabinet. Next is the legislative, which consists of the Senate and the House of Representatives, also known as the Congress. And finally there is the judicial, which at the top is the Supreme Court, with lower federal and state courts below. But I should not have said finally regarding the judicial, for there is one more branch of our government. That is not official, meaning that it has no constitutional power, but it is just as powerful as the other three branches. And that fourth branch is the media. I watched a documentary this week. That showed a climate change activist, I think her first name was Greta, staging an arrest for her activism. That was reported by the mainstream media with no mention that the whole matter was staged for the purpose of publicity. The documentary showed the police and the person being arrested waiting patiently for the media to get in place so the propaganda could ensue. The same happened with congresswomen who call themselves the Squad, who were protesting in favor of abortion. And when they were moved from blocking an intersection in Washington, DC, they placed their own hands behind their backs as if they were being handcuffed, with no handcuffs were on them. And again, that part of the story was ignored by the media. This documentary showed how news sources use pictures and videos that depict a story they want to tell when the pictures and videos themselves are not actually supposed to be the same news story that they said it was. But such deception by the media and outright propaganda has been going on for a long time. In the 1980s, there was a supposed serious effort to eliminate the federal deficit centered on the Graham-Rudmond Hullings Amendment. For several years, newspapers, magazines, and television newscasts ran stories, hundreds of stories, on the debates over Graham Rudman The views of all sorts of experts on the urgent need for deficit reduction and eventual enactment of the legislation, politicians postured and were described as working diligently to get a grip on the deficit Anyone who read a newspaper or watched television news received the message that Congress and the Reagan administration were heroically and painfully struggling to contain the government spending and reduce the deficit. Behind the smoke and screen, however, congressional committees and federal officials were increasing spending and adding new programs in the routine annual budget appropriations process. Of course they were. Journalists conspired with politicians to create an image of a government fighting to the end of the deficit crisis, but they ignored the routine procedures that increased the deficit. And listen to this quote. Quote, the U. S. press, like the United States government, is a corrupt and troubled institution. Corrupt not so much in the sense that it accepts bribes, but in a systematic sense. It fails to do what it claims to do, what it should do, and what society expects it to do So said Paul H. Weaver, a political science professor at Harvard back in 1995, almost 30 years ago. And things have gotten worse. It is all real trouble because we don't know who to trust. We don't know who is telling us the whole truth. We don't know what the agendas are of those who are feeding us the information. But here is a quote I hope you will not forget. Stanford journalism professor Ted Glasser stated this in 2020 that journalism needed to, quote, free itself from this notion of objectivity. To develop a sense of social justice. He then added, journalists need to be overt and candid advocates of social justice, and it's hard to do so under the constraints of objectivity. Beloved, objectivity is the enemy of liars and false teachers, but it is a friend to those who want to handle the truth. Timothy. The primary audience for this pastoral letter from the Apostle Paul was dealing with false teachers within the church at Ephesus And false teachers were being used then, and were being are being used today by the devil with the same strategy. The devil never changes his strategy. And that strategy is to take a truth that has been produced by God. And to twist it, and twist it enough, so that it not only is a lie, but a lie that leads away from God and toward evil. Understand that the devil has no original ideas. He is limited. He is incapable of creating anything new. That is why he takes what God has created and he distorts it. Examples are everywhere. The examples I choose are some of the most controversial in the history of our country. Slavery in the Bible is caused by circumstances that could not be avoided. If a man himself or his entire family was in debt, a debt that could not be paid in any reasonable time He could sell himself, a family member, or his entire family into slavery, or what was more comfortably titled servanthood, until the debt was paid off In some instances, the debt was paid off, but the family in slavery found themselves so much better off financially than they were before that they chose to remain servants. Another form of slavery occurred when a nation would go to be at war, and when an army was defeated on the battlefield, the men who were still alive on the side of the enemy were either to be killed or made slaves. There was no other alternative, for if they simply let him go, or them go, to go back to their homes, they would surely rise up again and go to war again in the near future. Under such circumstances, slavery was understandable and even humane. But the devil twisted it and made it corrupt and evil by convincing men who even claimed to fear God And be Christian to enslave another race by man stealing and then keeping them by force because they thought the race to be inferior. And those same men would use Bible verses, verses I explained they have a completely different context, and claim what they were doing by hating and enslaving a different race was being defended by the Bible. Some ignorant teachers today condemn the Bible for what it says about slavery without knowing the context in which such passages are used and how men have distorted it over the years. Another example is the subject of abortion. We know that the womb in every culture, in every age, has been considered the safest place on earth. Until the devil takes. Takes what God created, the ability for a man and a woman to conceive and for a child to grow inside its mother. The devil has taken that and relabeled it so that the child, the infant, the baby, is none of those, but is instead a fetus which is supposedly a non-person. And the act of abortion is no longer the killing of a baby, but is said to be a part of reproductive rights. Making the act of abortion a right places it in the political category rather than the moral category. Where there was once a clear objectivity that the evil of taking the life of an unborn child is now twisted to be seen only as a right and a choice. Of course, the child has no rights and has no choice. And so, as we know the ways and means of the devil, We can more easily, readily, and wisely fight the lies of the devil, as Timothy was being instructed to do. In verse 14 of chapter 3, Paul makes a personal remark to Timothy about his hope and attempt to be where Timothy is, and the hope is to do a short-time ministry. Ministry, Paul knows, is most effective when done in person. In verse 15, we have what some consider the most succinct reason for Paul writing this letter He is writing it because he is delayed in coming to Ephesus and because he wants Timothy and those Christians under Timothy to know how to conduct themselves within the house of God, which he says is the church. I remind you that the word church in the Greek is ekklesia, which means gathering, and it is used in a formal manner, which is to say it is not a kumbaya around the campfire gathering. But is a formal gathering where persons have specific duties to perform and roles to fulfill. This is why so much time was taken up describing what is expected of the leaders of the church. And it should be underlined that for Paul to refer to what ought to be conducted in the house of God means there is an objective manner That was and is to be followed within the church. Man has certain and specific roles in the church, and women do as well. And specific men have specific duties to practice in the church and specific standards to be seen in their lives. There are no alternatives to these roles or these standards And this is where the Protestants and more precisely the American Christian Church has been deceived We Americans already have a spirit of independence built in us. It comes from our history, and we call it freedom. But such freedom and independence does not include remodeling the Christian faith to fit our own definitions of what it means to conduct ourselves in the house of God. We cannot ignore the office of a priest, bishop, and deacon as some have done, even getting rid of the practice of ordination altogether. We cannot be locked in what is required of men in their personal lives to hold these offices we have studied these past few weeks And we most certainly cannot throw away moral standards, allowing clergy to sleep with other men, or unlawfully be divorced, or to covet money. Beloved, here is the truth as I plainly can say it. Either all the Bible is God's word, or none of it is. We can't pick and choose which parts we will believe and follow and which parts we will not. For frankly, to do so, we'll be making ourselves our own God. For we would be the interpreter and gatekeeper of truth and falsehood, making us only accountable to ourselves. And that fits perfectly within the will and strategy of the devil. At the end of verse 15, Paul says that the church of the living God is a pillar and ground of truth. Once again, the devil has used such a statement to divide Christians by having some interpret Paul to mean that the church comes first, and it comes first over God's Word. But the church is only the instrument God has chosen to defend and proclaim objective truth, the objective truth of the gospel of Jesus Christ. And that is seen in verse 16, where he lists what the church is to believe and proclaim. And so he starts. God was manifested in the flesh. Jesus became man and dwelt among us. Believing God became man is absolutely essential to understanding the Christian faith And especially since the devil has tried to convince false teachers to teach that it isn't true. Some said he only appeared to be a man. Some said it was impossible for God to be a man Some said if he was a man, he was in no sense God. But the fact that he was fully man and fully God confounds not only the understanding of men, but the wisdom of the devil also Such is the mystery of godliness, as verse 16 states. God manifested in the flesh is why Christmas is so important to celebrate. Not in terms of lights, colors, and trees, although those can be fun to enjoy. That a true celebration of Christmas is to worship Jesus as Savior in the house of God. Next, we are to believe and proclaim that Jesus was justified by the Spirit. This statement speaks to the obedience of Jesus. And the obedience of Jesus is how he was tempted in the desert and did not sin. And how he lived amidst brethren and did not sin. And how he faced the whipping, crown of thorns, the being nailed to a cross, the shame of being naked The death on the cross and facing it without sin. Next, we are to believe and proclaim that he was seen by the angels. Which speaks to them caring for him after he was in the desert being tempted. And it also speaks to them knowing his origin and being a witness to both his divinity and his humanity. Next, we are to believe and proclaim that the salvation offered by and through Jesus as the Messiah is also offered to the Gentiles Who were always, always a part of God's plan of salvation. And why Epiphany is so important to celebrate to celebrate it in being in the house of God, worshiping Jesus Next, we are to believe and proclaim the effectiveness of the gospel of Jesus, for not only has it spread throughout the world, it has literally changed nations and reformed cultures. And finally, we are to believe and proclaim that Jesus was received into glory, which is when he sat down at the right hand of the Heavenly Father to take his place as Judge of the world and as our intercessor. He sits so that we can stand. Stand and be confident that we are his people and he is our God. It is also why it is important to celebrate the ascension and celebrate it in the house of God. All of what we are to believe and proclaim, having been listed, leads Paul to remind Timothy and those in his charge. But there will be times when some will say they are Christian, but they will depart from the faith, and they will also do so because they listen which is to heed, they heed the deceiving spirits. and doctrines of demons. Now we started off talking about how difficult it is to know who to trust with the news And then he talks the strategy of the devil as he twists truth. Next week we will get into what those twisted truths specifically were and what they are today. But I want you and I to go away today with the confidence that there are objective truths and that those truths do not change. I have pointed out before from this pulpit that there are laws of logic that must be identified and followed if truth is going to be known. One of those laws you might remember is the law of identity. The law of identity states that the truth value of a statement never changes. A simple example is that if 2 plus 2 is 4, is a true statement, that it was always true, it is always true, and will forever be true. And it doesn't matter the culture it is stated, it doesn't matter the year it is stated, it doesn't matter with any other changing factors. Its value of being true remains the same. Adding to that example, if it is said that 2 plus 2 equals 5, Such a statement is false, and the identity of that false statement always was false, is false, and will be false. The identity of an emphatic statement does not change. Thus, we can say that God becoming flesh and dwelling among us, and his name being Jesus. And his obedience being complete, and the angels being witnesses to his identity, and the gospel is believed throughout the world, And that he is seated at the right hand of the Heavenly Father, saying all of that to be true, that it is always true, never to be changed or altered or twisted. And whoever does try to change it, alter it, or twist it is to be an anthem, which is to be cursed. May God give each of us to never deny these truths. Amen. Let us pray. Our merciful God, we thank you for the revelation of these truths. We thank you for the strength that you give us to hold on to these truths. As was stated in the sermon, may we each have the courage all the days of our life to hold on to them. In Jesus' name we pray. Amen.

sermons.title: Enjoy
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Be seated I do warn you that I was told from social media that moving the clocks backwards one hour means that each preach preacher gets to preach an extra hour. So get comfortable. I don't know why anybody would want to do that. I wouldn't want to hear myself that long, that's for sure. We are in 1 Timothy chapter 4. Working through verses one through five. First Timothy four verses one through five One of the great mysteries of the human condition is our ability and our choosing to step out of relationships. The most difficult of broken relationships, of course, occurs within the nuclear family. All of us well know how damaging a broken marriage can be, especially when it is not amicable For those who are outside looking in, it appears that the husband woke up one day and said to his wife, I don't love you anymore. I want a divorce. From that point on, their friends have to choose sides. Their extended families are no longer a part of one another's lives because invitation to gatherings cease. And of course, the spiritual and emotional damage divorces can have on children of the once happy couple can stay within their psyche for the rest of their lives. And then there are friendship breakups that can be baffling. A person who was at one time a very important part of your life. Say you attended church together, you shared meals together, you talked politics over a drink, your families played together, and then one day they are gone They don't return emails, they don't return texts, they won't answer your phone calls, they start going to a different church, they don't talk to you, not even greeting you as your paths cross And you are never told why. You're given no chance to apologize if an apology is needed. The friendship is just over. But the worst breakup that can happen, even though the marital breakup causes a great deal of lasting pain, the worst breakup is when a person chooses to no longer believe in Jesus Christ as Lord and Savior. And it is the worst because it has eternal consequences. We ended last week with the emphasis on being confident about objective truths, and we were challenged to hold on to the essential truths of what the Bible teaches about Jesus. At the end of the chapter 3, we have what is close, close to being a creed. And the creeds we confess serve the purpose of helping us remain faithful to essential truths. In verse 1 of chapter 4, we are told that the Holy Spirit has warned that in latter times people will depart from the faith. Jesus warned of the same as did many prophets in the Old Testament. And I want us to note that just after Paul speaks about a future time, he then pivots and goes into the present tense. For what was going on in Ephesus was happening at the present tense when Paul was writing this letter. It was one of the main reasons for him writing this letter. People were then leaving the faith by way of heeding, which is listening to and believing, doctrines of demons. The word heed, the word heed also implies that these people were listening and believing lies and speaking lies and knowing what they were doing The phrase having their conscience seared with a hot iron is a metaphorical way to say that they were doing what they were doing, they were doing on purpose. They knew what they were doing. They knew it was going against the once stated faith that they had in Jesus. And now they were choosing to repeat falsehoods from the devil And that's quite a choice to make, and one that appears to offer no way back. If you have ever wondered Why people make such choices. I wonder if it is similar to why people drop out of other people's lives so suddenly. One theory is that there are certain personalities that make friendships with certain people because of what those certain people can do for them. Todd meets Hank. Todd finds out that Hank works for McCormick. Todd has always wanted to work for McCormick, and so he befriends Hank. Their families even spend time together and like each other. And then Hank helps Todd get a job at the Cormic. And soon after, texts are ignored, the phone calls are not returned, and Todd is on to the next friendship that will help him get his kids into the school that they want. And we ask, what happened to sincerity and loyalty? So with that scenario in mind You can imagine people who come to Christ Jesus and choose to confess him as Savior because of what they think they can get from him. What we know we can get is unfettered love, forgiveness and hope, but we may be thinking we can get a wife, a better job, a position of influence, etc. And when those reasons and other reasons why they became a Christian do not come to reality, that's a reason now to drop the faith. No longer speak the language, become angry at God because they thank God reniged on promises, promises he never gave to begin with. And so, what were these doctrines and lies these apostates were believing and speaking within the church? You remember Timothy was pastoring the church at Ephesus. Well, according to verse 3. They were forbidding marriage and teaching the Christians to stay away from certain foods. Now it is natural for us to think that such doctrines are odd and maybe a little weird We don't know the reason behind such doctrines because Paul doesn't give such reasons. And I appreciate that he does it because that would make it seem like these apostates and their doctrines were worth engaging and debating. When they were not. And so Paul ignores the reason for such doctrines, but we can do a little digging, being quite removed from those days. So the falsehood that was being propagated by the false teachers in Ephesus was one that was common and even reoccurring in the Greco-Roman world of that day. The Greco-Roman world was susceptible to finding asceticism as an attractive lifestyle. And it was asceticism in regards to marriage and food that was particularly attractive Now, asceticism is the severe self-discipline of denying yourself of something pleasurable. The Greco-Roman world was particularly susceptible to that thought that the spiritual part of man was what counted. Where his true goodness and greatness was to be found. And the physical part of man, and what is more the physical, then what is more physical than food and sex. Was what was hurting the spiritual part of man. And this way of thinking would soon after plague the Christian church. With some false teachers even denying that Jesus could have ever taken on human flesh. It is also interesting that there were also Jews who thought in a similar manner. The Essenes of Quran, for example, thought abstinence from marriage and a strict regulation of the diet was the way to greater holiness. as well as did Christian monks some years later. But why would ascetics choose marriage and food? Why would they choose marriage and food? Plainly put, both include the most basic desires of our flesh. In marriage, couples are free to engage in physical intimacy, and sex is a strong desire for many people since mankind was created. It is such a strong desire that men break up their own marriage over wanting to have sex with another woman. It is such a strong desire that pornography is a billion-dollar industry. Sex is such a strong desire that some expose themselves to all sorts of diseases for a brief moment of pleasure. And then there is food. For many people, food is the most difficult of vices. People are either thinking about it while craving it or thinking about it while abstaining from it. We all have to face the reality that those numbers on our scale aren't getting any higher because of a grandeur problem. And so sex and food are where we can be our weakest when it comes to our flesh. Paul goes on to give an argument regarding why marriage and some foods should not be avoided. It is because God created them, and He created them to be used for the good by us. We remember, of course, that the Jewish faith consisted of certain foods being forbidden We have all heard about certain shellfish being forbidden and pork being forbidden and others. The reason for some foods being forbidden could be the dangers of those foods But the main purpose was certainly, certainly, for the Jewish people to see themselves as separated unto God, and thus they could not do what the other tribes around them were freely doing. They were to be a people set aside. This is clearly seen when God uses their dietary laws to reveal his plan to include the Gentile world into his covenant under Jesus. That was the whole purpose of Peter being given a dream in the book of Acts, if you remember, where God places a clean, unclean animals before Peter in a dream on a sheet. And tells Peter to get up and eat. When Peter refuses, because he will not eat what is unclean, God tells Peter to not call unclean what God has now called clean. That dream told Peter that not only was there no longer unclean food, but there was also no longer unclean people. And that Peter was to go to the house of the Gentile Cornelius and tell him about Jesus and the gospel. And when he did, Cornelius' whole household was baptized, both by the Holy Spirit and in water. And such is a wonderful story, indeed. And so all that God created to be food is good for us. And we are to eat of it freely, with thanksgiving, he says. And you should always give thanks for every meal. For we are believers who know the truth, Paul says at the end of verse 3. But what is the truth? What is the truth that we know? We know that Jesus became flesh and dwelt with men. We know that Jesus had that flesh torn and nailed and speared We know the very same flesh was placed in a grave, and we know that very same flesh rose from the dead and was seen by over 500 witnesses. And we know that flesh ascended into heaven. And we know that flesh will one day return to this world, splitting the eastern sky. Such flesh is good flesh, because God made it, just as He did all flesh of all men and beasts. And so verses four and five repeat the point of how we are to receive all that God has made for us as good. And to do so being Christians by sanctifying it with God's word and with prayer. That is, of course, exactly what we do at Holy Communion. But there is more being said in this verse, in these verses. Those who are teaching doctrines to avoid marriage and certain foods are choosing to go specifically and directly against God. They are making up their own system of righteousness While denying what God has said and done as creator and sustainer of the world.
