Such deceptive teaching is truly of the devil, for it is in direct rebellion against God. So there are two points I want to leave you with from this sermon. My first point is to expound on the point I just made. That these false teachers, shunning marriage and refusing certain foods, were making up their own system of righteousness While denying what God has said and done as creator and sustainer of the world. Again, such deceptive teaching is truly of the devil. For it is in direct rebellion against God. It is a form of self-righteousness And self-righteousness was and is a real and serious problem. See, I believe that within every human being is a desire to be righteous. Of course, the desire is stronger in some than it is in others, but it is within us all because we are made in God's image, and God is righteous. So we all want to be righteous to some degree, but we are not truly righteous. We are fallen. We're not righteous as God is righteous. And so we settle for being self-righteous in order to fulfill that righteous desire. And self-righteousness can be very deceptive Because you think you are honoring God by what you do and do not do. You think your life is more pleasing to God if you don't smoke, drink, or chew or go with those who do And I'm not telling you to smoke or drink. I am telling you that you are not only not pleasing God by abstaining. You are practicing works of supererrogation, which are rightfully condemned in the 39 Articles of Religion, right as stated in your Book of Common Prayer. And the word supererogation is a fancy way of describing works that go beyond what is necessary. For what is necessary for Christians is to believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, to confess your sins, to have faith in his blood, and have hope for eternity. It is not abstaining from anything, and it is most certainly not looking down on anyone. Illnesses in this decade have reminded us how quickly we can be self righteous. When a person concludes she is more righteous than her fellow shoppers because she wears a mask to the store, she is being self-righteous. When a man yells at another man because he is not keeping a six feet distance like he is, he is being self-righteous. When you believe the manner you vote reveals your higher moral standards, you are being self-righteous. Beloved, the only righteousness we have is the righteousness of Jesus. The second point I want you to leave with Is the same point made several times in the book of Ecclesiastes? And you heard it repeated over and over this past spring and summer when I preached through that book. That point is that God wants us to enjoy what He has given for us to enjoy. First, God wants us to enjoy marriage. Celibacy is meant for very, very few people. The command to Adam and Eve to be fruitful and multiply still applies to all of God's people and will apply until Jesus returns. And within marriage and having children, God wants us to enjoy sexual intimacy with our spouse. A celibate marriage is more difficult than a celibate single life. God would not have made sexual intimacy so enjoyable if he did not want his people to enjoy it. And if you don't enjoy sexual intimacy within your marriage, then you're not doing it right. You need more practice. When we read the Ten Commandments, we more readily focus on what we cannot do. However, although most are written in the negative, they also include the positive. The negatives are the fence that shows us the borders we're not to cross. But we are more than free to run around and enjoy the fence inside. Sexual intimacy within a marriage is to have fun within the fence. To commit adultery is to go outside the fence. So stay within the fence and enjoy. Secondly, still under point two, is to enjoy food. Of course, the Bible is not encouraging us to over-indulge in food and drink. That is the sin of gluttony, and it is condemned along with other sins of the flesh. But enjoying good food is not a sin. And God wants us to enjoy good food You don't need to settle for that sirloin stake, because a humble Christian would choose such. Choose the filet. And sear it nicely, medium rare is the best, with lots of butter. And when you drink your wine at that state dinner, you don't need to settle for Sutter Home Merlot year 2023 Instead, choose La Flore des Baudour, La Lande de Pomerol, year 2018 It is well balanced and juicy. The 2018 vintage offers flavors of fleshly blackberry, raspberry, and blueberry, enhanced with a touch of licorice, dark chocolate, and ripe almond. Only fifty-five dollars a bottle. And enjoy it all with prayers and thanksgivings. G. K. Chesterton said the following. You say grace before meetles. All right. But I say grace before the concert and the opera, and grace before the play and pantomime, and grace before I open a book. And grace before painting, swimming, fencing, boxing, walking, playing, dancing, and grace before I dip the pen in ink. Sounds like a lifestyle of prayer and gratefulness. Sounds like a lifestyle to emulate. Beloved, what God has given us is good. So reject the false teachers and cling to what is good. And it is good because God has given it to you to enjoy. Amen.

sermons.title: The Fundamentals
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, of the Son, of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. The reading for the epistle is what we're working on this morning as we work through First Timothy chapter And we're in 1 Timothy chapter 4. Actually the reading went through 16, but we're going to go only through verse 11. So if you turn in your Bibles to 1 Timothy chapter 4, we're working from verse 6 through verse 11. No matter how much natural talent a person has, it is absolutely necessary that said person works on the fundamentals of whatever he or she wants to be great at doing. With the fundamentals in place, a person can then work on what is more complicated and precise. I found the following instruction on how people learning to play the piano should begin. Relax the fingers and place your hand on a flat surface with all of the fingertips resting on the surface. And with the wrist at the same height as the knuckles, the hand and fingers should form a dome. All the fingers should be curved. The thumb should point slightly down and bend slightly towards the fingers so that the last nail phalange of thumb is parallel to the other fingers. The fingers are slightly curve curled, curving down and meeting the surface at angles near si 45 degrees. The tip of the thumb and the other fingertips should form an approximate semicircle on the flat surface. Such are the beginning instructions of great detail on how to play the piano. Well I don't know how to play this yet. But I remember wanting to become a great football player and become great at catching the football. I knew I needed to work on the fundamentals each day that I practiced. The fundamentals. Hands out. Don't use your body, unless necessary, to protect the ball. Catch with the top pads of your fingers. With the fingers facing up when the ball is chest high or higher Catch with your fingers facing down when the ball is stomach high or lower. Catch the nose of the ball whenever possible. Once the ball is caught, tuck it in and protect it, covering the nose. And always, always tuck in with your eyes. The eyes should follow the ball all the way until it is secure. And you do this these drills, remembering these fundamentals, every day, every day until you no longer think about it, because it has become deep-seated habits Working on the fundamentals of whatever you want to become great at is necessary. And Paul wanted Timothy to be great at ministering God's word to the Christian church. especially to the Ephesians to whom Timothy was assigned to serve. And so we get the instructions that begin on 1 Timothy 4, verse 6. The first responsibility is for Timothy to instruct. This matches the words Jesus repeated to Peter. When after his resurrection and in order to restore Peter to his place amongst the apostles, after Peter had denied knowing Jesus three times. Jesus asked Peter if Peter loved him and he asked him three times. Peter confirmed each time that he loved Jesus and after each confirmation Jesus told Peter, feed. My sheep. Such is a minister's primary responsibility. The people of God are in need and deserve solid food A good minister provides milk when needed and solid food when needed. To do so, a minister needs to be well educated and constantly improving on his education. So that the sheep, the sheep he is assigned to feed, do not grow hungry, and thus are not carried away by wolves who seek to deceive. The phrase these things next mentioned in the verse refers to what Paul has written about in the previous verses. Two weeks ago, we studied Paul's words about the nature and works of Jesus that sound similar to a creed at the end of chapter 3. And last week we spoke against the false teachers claiming that marriage should be avoided as well as certain foods The primary lesson is that what God has made for us is good for us and we should enjoy it. Such, Paul says, are nourishing words of faith and good doctrine, and Timothy has been faithful to teach them. Unfortunately, not every minister is faithful to do the same. Even in our own denomination, Some men get carried away from the fundamentals of the faith by following along the lines of the culture around them, focusing on social justice issues from behind the pulpit. So to do so leads down a Y road that leads only to heresy This encouragement to Timothy was all the more necessary because of the opposition he was facing at that Ephesian church. His teaching, even his presence probably, was being actively criticized by one party in the church Verse 7. Instead of following the godless teachings of the culture around a minister, He is instead to reject them as profane and as old wise tales. I only discovered this week that the phrase old wise tales goes back to ancient Greece. With the speculation that it comes from older mothers passing on superstitious sayings of supposed wisdom to younger mothers. In the context, Paul uses it It is likely referring to teachings of rabbis who would expound on the law in such a way that would take it to mean far beyond what its natural reading was And such is one reason why Jesus was considered a great teacher, for he was concise in his interpretation of the law and concise in his new teachings. Paul then tells Timothy that instead of paying attention to such unnecessary and misleading teachings, he should pursue godliness. in a manner an athlete would pursue exercise. Similar to the opening examples, such a pursuit has to begin with the fundamentals, and they must be rehearsed over and over again. But this line of thinking leads Paul to mention the profit gained from bodily exercise, and that leads him right back into the prioritizing of the pursuit of godliness. We recall that Paul was addressing just a few verses earlier the dangers of being obsessed with an ascetic life. And focusing on physical exercise can contribute to that excess of an ascetic life. Instead, Paul wants Timothy to focus on a godly life, which is a well-rounded life, which is a life that does everything within its right season. At the end of verse 8, Paul acknowledges the tension of Christian life, which is to have the promise of the life that now is. Which can be profitable, a profitable life, if we enjoy our spouses, if we enjoy good food, if we enjoy godly fellowship, and with passing on our faith on to our children No life is better lived than those who are faithful in marriage, who have children, who love them and love one another. And have spouses of their own who love one another and who are raising their children in the fear of the Lord. Such makes family gatherings comfortable, joyful, and filled with hope. But the promises in this life, we all know, are limited. Limited. Tragedy does strike. Illnesses do come Death eventually separates. And such leads Paul to also mention the promises to come, which is the heavenly promise. Where bodies are made new, where streets are gold, and death is permanently defeated. That is the tension of every Christian. that we must live within. We have the promises where some are fulfilled already and some not yet. In verse 9, the phrase, this faithful saying, is referring back to the phrase, godliness is profitable for all things. Godliness is profitable for all things. And by pointing to it and saying such is worthy of all acceptance. is to say that all Christians should agree that such is true. And I haven't any doubt That if I was to pull all of you hearing me and ask you if you believe that godliness is profitable for all things, you would answer yes. And you would likely do so without hesitation But if I asked you if your life reflected that godliness is profitable for all things, such would be much more difficult to answer. Because we would have to examine ourselves in all things in our lives. Do I see godliness in all aspects of my life? And likely we would see that godliness is not a priority in certain parts of our lives. When confronted with a challenge like this, we must follow the example of King David, who asked the Lord He said, Search me, O God, and know my heart. Try me and know my ways, and see if there is any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting. David asked the Lord to try him, knowing that he could not do a thorough job enough of examining himself. The human psyche in its fallen state can compartmentalize certain behaviors and thoughts. So that one behavior doesn't connect with other behaviors, and one way of thinking doesn't relate or even communicate with other ways of thinking. It can be seen in how I behave at work, my vocabulary, my tone, my subject matter, those are all different and not even recognizable in how I behave at home. And most certainly how I behave at church. But all of those different behaviors are different than how I behave when I am alone. And none of those different behaviors need to know about each other. But Paul wants Timothy, a minister of the gospel, thus wanting all ministers of the gospel. To teach Christians that godliness is profitable in all things. And so it is for me to implore you to pursue godliness in all things. With the expectation that your life will profit from it. And the only way you're going to know that your life will be benefited by your godly pursuit is if you try it out. And find out. And I realize, in saying such, that some of you don't have an idea of how you can pursue godliness in all aspects of your life What it looks like may not be clear. So let us start with something applicable to all of us, which is the manner in which we speak. After all, the Epistle of James tells us, quote, the tongue is a fire, a world of iniquity. The tongue is so set among our members that it defiles the whole body and sets on fire the course of nature, and it is set on fire by hell. Sounds pretty bad. Sounds like a tall order to control our tongues. In order for your tongue to be tamed, you must work at it. You must do the fundamentals. And so we start with holding our tongue, holding your tongue, which is to not say anything. Before you speak, ask yourself if what you're about to say is true, wholesome, kind. And if it's necessary. Try not to take what I say next personally. But your opinion is not necessary. Your opinion is not necessary. The culture today has the motto, speak your truth. But as Christians, we don't follow the culture. The Bible says nothing similar. Your opinion is not true Now, of course, if someone asks for your opinion, then it can fit under the category of necessary, but only then I also mentioned wholesome. Many men speak crassly around other men for whatever psychological reasons they have, and it is the Christian man. But here's these words from Paul in his letter to the Ephesians. He said, Let no unwholesome talk come out of your mouths But only what is helpful for building up the one in need and bringing grace to those who listen. And the Christian man, hearing that, concludes that a godly way to speak Is not to be crashed like every other unbeliever, but is instead in a manner that is helpful and useful Upon hearing these challenges, you might want to say, Pastor, such a change in my speaking is to change many years of past talk. It is going to change how my friends and co-workers see me. Yeah? I know. But look at verse 10. Look at verse 10 where Paul says For to this end, he is referring to the end of being profitable in this life and in the world to come, we both labor, so we as Timothy and Paul and suffer reproach. Reproach is disapproval of the world around us. Because we trust in the living God, to trust is to have faith that such godliness will be profitable Beloved, to pursue godliness in all things cannot be done without people reproaching you, and it cannot be done without labor. It takes work. It requires awareness of what you are doing, whether it is godly or not. It takes honesty within yourself, whether you want to be godly, and whether you truly have faith that such is profitable. And you have to make decisions going forward regarding what you want to be, who you want to be, where you want to be. Beloved, the Christian life is laborious, and that means it requires energy, attention to detail, repetition with the fundamentals. Until we get to where what we do, the godly life we live, is a natural part of who we are. During One particular football game in college. I was called to the sideline to run in a play. That was titled left, slot right, 83Z, Y out. The word left told the Z receiver, which was me, and it told the tight end to line up on the left. The slot right told the X receiver and the slot back to line up on the right. The number eight in 83 told the linemen what type of protection they were to give And it told the quarterback how many steps he should take once he received the snap. The number three in 83 told the quarterback and the receiver what route was being run. And the letter Z told the receiver and the quarterback who the quarterback was to look to first. The Y, who was the tight end, and the word out told the quarterback end tight end that he was to be the second choice running out and underneath excuse me running and out underneath the three route which was the go route. You with me? So with that information, the coach added, while grabbing me, pulling me to him, looking at me in the eye, he said, don't drop it. Now I was offended. I didn't drop passes Well maybe one or two, but not not. Well now the pressure was really on me. I needed to also tell you that we were playing in Flagstaff, Arizona, against the Northern Arizona Lumberjacks. They played in a dome where the lighting was terrible. It was a number of bulbs that glared brightly. Up high, making it light up the ceiling while it was darker and shadowy in the field below. So I line up on the left side of the formation. The ball is snapped. I run by the defender, and the ball is thrown. I see it, and then I don't It's in the lights. My mind is racing. I was told not to drop it. But I remember my training. I had learned that if you lose a ball because of the sun, then catch the sun, meaning the ball will be where the sun is. And so I apply that to the lights that are affecting my ability to see the ball. I put my hands out, waiting to catch the light that I trust is the ball, and it falls into my arms Training fundamentals working on the same roots every day, catching balls over and over again until it is second nature, resulting in touchdown dances It used to be back in the 1980s, a starting point for Christian evangelists to tell non-Christians that the Christian life is exciting. The Christian life is fun. Well it may be for some, but more often it's work. It's hard work. The challenge to pursue godliness in all things is before us, and it is daunting. After all, we only talked of the example of controlling our speech. It is a whole other workload to talk about controlling our thoughts. And yet that should be first, for from our minds and from our hearts our mouths speak. Fact is, the Christian life can be quite daunting. And because it is daunting, it is compared to be like a narrow road that few are willing to travel upon. While the wide road is easy, and many travel on it, not knowing that they are traveling to destruction. Beloved, choose your road. Looking at verse 11, it ends with Paul telling Timothy to command and teach these things. This I have done for you. Let us pray. A gracious and heavenly Father, we pray together that we might have the courage. To work hard, to do the fundamentals, to understand that this road is narrowed, to understand that it is difficult to travel on it. But we trust that you have given us the strength, your Holy Spirit has empowered us, that you have shown us the way. Give us the courage to walk it. We pray this in Jesus' name. Amen. That's not take this time to worship the Lord and give you a high strawberry to remember the God

sermons.title: Priority of Preaching
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: I can just find some questions. In the name of the Father and of the Son, the Holy Ghost. Amen. He'd be seated It would be best for you to turn in your Bibles to 1 Timothy chapter 4. We will be working through verse 12 through 16. First Timothy chapter four, working through verse twelve through sixteen. Small talk. Some people like to share small talk. Small talk actually has an official definition. It is polite conversation about unimportant or uncontroversial matters, especially as engaged in a social situation. Small talk usually includes the weather, which includes what the weather is now, what it has been, and what it will be. Small talk includes the local sports teams. We discuss what happened last week, what we hope will happen next week, and how the referees robbed our team of a victory. Small talk includes a recent doctor's appointment, television shows we recently watched, restaurants we recently enjoyed, or Didn't enjoy. In general, small talk includes words that will soon be forgotten Small talk uses throwaway words. But as the official definition states, small talk is an attempt to be polite, which is the primary purpose of small talk. We may not know each other well, or we don't have time, or it is not the right place to talk on a personal business or something meaningful. And so small talk fills the space. The positive about small talk is that it is polite. The negative is that it is quickly forgotten. And frankly, quite boring. And I'm getting boring talking to you about small jumping. In contrast, when it comes to the Christian faith, when it involves the words of God, small talk doesn't exist. In fact, the most obvious display of God's power and authority is displayed by the words He speaks. And it is the call of a Christian minister to speak the words of God. For any other word a minister speaks is only the words of a man. But when he speaks the words of God, such words have an inherent authority. And so the minister must speak God's words for the salvation of God's people. Now I know that sounds dramatic. But we will get there. Paul's instruction to Timothy regarding how he was to personally minister in the church comes after his instruction to Timothy to focus on the fundamentals of the faith and not be carried away by what he calls old wives fables and the profane. What we read in verse 12 of 1 Timothy 4 is very personal regarding who Timothy was and how he was to fulfill the calling God had placed upon his life. Paul tells Timothy not to allow people to despise his youth. To despise in this context is to disregard. To ignore, to conclude that because Timothy was a younger man, perhaps in his thirties, he was not experienced enough to be wise or even knowledgeable But what do we know about Timothy? We know he was from the city of Lystra in Asia Minor. Which was one of the cities the Apostle Paul journeyed to with Barnabas and with Mark during his first missionary journey, or trip, which was in A. D. 46 through 48. Timothy was raised by his parents and grandmother, though Paul only describes his mother and grandmother, for we read from 2 Timothy 1, verse 5, quote, When I call to remembrance The genuine faith that is in you, which dwelt first in your grandmother Lois, and your mother Eunice, and I am persuaded is in you also. His father was said to be a Greek, while his mother was Jewish. It is believed that when Paul was evangelizing in their city of Lystra, Eunus converted to Christianity and was even mentioned by Paul in the Book of Acts. In Second Timothy chapter three, verse fifteen, Paul shares what impressed him about Timothy It was his knowledge of the Holy Scriptures. He said of Timothy, wise for salvation through faith, which is in Jesus Christ. Some time later, Paul made the decision to bring Timothy with him in spreading the gospel and had him ordained and circumcised to avoid any questioning or ridicule by the Jewish Christians. Not much else is known about Timothy other than what is inferred in what Paul writes to him. To make up for his youth, Paul advised Timothy to be an example to his fellow Christians in terms of the words he spoke. His conduct in love, which is his everyday living, his spirit, his faith, and his morality Such counsel matches what is required as an ordained minister, as we learned in chapter 2. Such is a high calling. People are watching you as a minister. People want to know if a minister's life matches up with what he says he believes and what he teaches and preaches. People might even deny the faith or give up on pursuing a godly life if a minister is found to be a hypocrite. It is fair to ask if anyone actually believes what the Bible teaches, if no one is living by the standards of morality the Bible upholds. Some of you have heard this story, but I repeat it for emphasis. When I was teaching at the university, I assign students to consider a scenario of a person who was a Christian and thus did not believe in cannibalism. But was stranded on a mountain after a plane crash, and weeks had gone by with no rescue in sight and no food to eat. Should such a person consume the flesh of those who had died in the crash? One student was adamant that the Christian should practice cannibalism. Because the priority should be survival. When I challenged the student's answer by reminding him of the Christian conviction not to consume flesh, he looked at me and said I have never met anyone who is that serious about their religion. Let that sink in. I was greatly, greatly saddened by that answer. It got me wondering how many people are dissuaded from the Christian faith because they have never witnessed anyone who was actually living by the standards of the Holy Scriptures. To be sure, to be sure, all of us fall short of the glory of God. And as it says in 1 John, if we say we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us. So all of us have sinned and do sin. However, however, we should still pursue righteousness and still pursue not giving in to sin. And we should also project humility while confessing our sins readily. Next, Paul instructs Timothy to give attention to reading, to exhortation, and to doctrine. And what reading was he to do? And from where was he to exhort? And from where was he to get doctrine? He was to read, exhort, and get doctrine from the writings of the apostles and from the Old Testament No. The canon as we know it today, the 66 books of the Bible we call the Old Testament and the New Testament, was not officially established and would not be for years to come But the gospels had been written and were dispersed throughout the Christian community, and Jesus said that the Psalms and the prophets spoke of him, and that Abraham saw his day and was glad And so to study the Old Testament, to read it, to exhort from it, and to receive doctrine from it, it was available to Timothy. Now I must say a word here about the word doctrine. Doctrine refers to a set of established beliefs. Too many soft-minded and soft-principled people say they avoid doctrine because it only divides people. Don't listen to such talk. Jesus divided people and said he came to divide because there is truth and there is falsehood There is what is morally right and there is what is morally wrong. There is good and there is evil. You can't simply say that you believe in Jesus, and that is enough doctrine for you. No. Who was Jesus? And who did he say he was? And who is he today? Was he and is he fully man? Was he and is he fully God? Did his life reflect what he taught? Did his death mean anything for us? Did he actually rise from the dead? Where is he now? And does it matter? All such questions need to be answered for the name of Jesus to have any meaning. And to have any purpose of a person putting his faith in that name. So embrace doctrine. We need it. The prophecy specifically spoken regarding a gift that Timothy has is not explicitly stated, and thus not specifically known. In the context of this section of Scripture, we can speculate that it might have been in regards to Timothy being a gifted communicator. Some people write better than others, such as the Apostle Paul, and some people preach better than others, such as the Apostle Peter. Whatever Timothy's gift was, it was in the context of God's Word. Verse 15 is a call for Timothy to put in the work necessary to be a good minister of Jesus Christ. Which was our topic last week. To meditate on such things is to be focused and attentive to the details of what is required to be a good minister of God's Word. And the work that Timothy puts in is to be noticed by those who receive Timothy's ministry. So let us be honest with one another. Most of us can tell when a minister is going through the motions when it comes to his preaching and his teaching. We can tell whether he put the time in during the week to prepare his sermon or if he mailed it in, as some like to describe. I have heard sermons that I knew were taken from a devotional the minister had read that week What else he did with his time during the week I could not tell, but because I read the same devotional, I knew there wasn't any original thoughts involved. Good sermons are words that stay with God's people throughout the week. They are words that come back to God's people when circumstances in life are difficult and God's word needs to be applied. Good sermons are reflected upon, edited, reworked, and meditated upon before they are ever publicly heard. Good sermons fit in the category of knowing them when you hear them. The last thought In verse 16 is what struck me hard this week. A minister who takes heed regarding what he reads, exhorts, and teaches regarding doctrine. Is saving both himself and those who hear him. Is there anything more important? Or is there any higher calling than that? When we worked through the requirements of a minister regarding his personal life and family life in Chapter 2, I tried to portray such a calling as difficult but also privileged. But I did not think about it in the manner Paul writes in verse 16. The salvation of a minister and of those he pastors is affected by what he reads, teaches, and believes. Such then is a call for me to impress upon you who hear me the importance of the Word of God in your life. Recall that at creation in Genesis it describes the earth without form, a place that was void, only having darkness going down into its deepest level. And then God spoke. By way of words, God's words, he made something out of nothing. By words, God made the stars. God made the moon. God made the sun. By words, God made all living things according to their deep complexities. By words, God made man and separated him from all other living creatures, giving man the privilege of being made in God's likeness. And giving him dominion over all the beasts of the fields. And when mankind, via Adam and Eve, were disobedient to God's words, God spoke words of judgment. And so his judgment is assured. And yet, within those words, God spoke a promise. And we were to be confident that his word would come to pass. And the pattern is repeated over and over, as God spoke words of judgment when the earth was flooded, and then words of promise never to judge mankind in the same manner again. And then more words did God speak as he called Abraham to a new land, and then gave more words of promise regarding that land. And the offspring that would come from Abraham that would be too many to count. And then Abraham's offspring were enslaved in Egypt, and God spoke words to Moses. To lead his people out of bondage and back to the land of promise. And as Moses led the people, God spoke ten words. For that is what the commandments were originally called. God's ten words were spoken, and the people received the standards God had set regarding their everyday lives. And when the people disobeyed God's words, he spoke more words, promising a Messiah who would Be there forever sacrifice for sins. And so it was not happenstance that when the Messiah came, he was called the Word, the Lagos of God. Jesus was what God spoke so that his people could be saved for eternity The Gospel of John begins, you remember, in the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. And so Jesus taught his followers that because they were children of God, that their words were to matter. Their words were to be that of truth. That when they said yes, it was to be as if the promise had already been fulfilled. And when they said no, the subject was finished. All because We are a people of the Word. For a preacher To help save himself and those who listen to him, he is to teach and preach the word, which is contained in Holy Scripture. Timothy was to devote himself to knowing that word and knowing it so well that when he spoke, it was God who spoke. What he exhorted as truth was reflecting Jesus Himself. What he established as doctrine was to be the very character of God, and was a hedge of protection against falsehood. Of false teachers and the demons who motivate them. One of the clearest examples of the power of preaching God's word and hearing sound doctrine. is when our namesake, Stephen, as recorded in the book of Acts, preached God's word before the high priest after being arrested and taken to the high priest. He was taken there because he was so effective at declaring Jesus as the Messiah. When Stephen spoke, he started with the covenant promises God made to Abraham And from there told of Joseph being sold into slavery by his brothers, and yet God raised him up. From there he spoke of Israel in bondage and how God raised up Moses And then the rising up of David and then Solomon, and still the Jewish people repeatedly rebelled against God. And then finally God raised his only son to redeem his people from sin and death, and the people were too stiff-necked to receive him. And so they turned him over to be crucified, thinking they were done with him. When Stephen's sermon was done, the writer of Acts says When they heard these things, they were cut to the heart, and they gnashed at him with their teeth. Then they cried out with a loud voice, Stopped their ears and ran at Stephen, casting him outside the temple and stoned him to death. And what for? What was the cause of such a visceral reaction? It was the demons who knew the power of the Word of God read, exhorted, and believed. Beloved demons don't care about your small talk. And please don't hear me saying that you shouldn't participate in small talk. My point is to make Paul's point, for Paul is speaking God's word, and such words are to be read, exhorted, and believed. Demons hate it. Hate it every time that happens. And so let us make angry as many demons as possible. Every time we open our Bible and read it, every time we participate in Bible study, and most certainly every time we participate in Sunday morning worship until Jesus returns. Amen. Let us pray. Gracious and merciful Father, we thank you for this teaching of Paul giving us a heavy burden. to realize how important your holy word is for the salvation of those who speak it, preach it, teach it, and those who hear it. And so Holy Spirit guide us in all truth, we pray, and may we forever be praying your preaching and believing your word until you come. Amen.

sermons.title: How to Treat your Elders
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. I encourage you to turn to 1 Timothy 5, picking up at verse 17. Best to follow along as I reference each of these verses. First Timothy five, verse starting at verse seventeen. If you want to hurt a minister, If you want to make him feel low and a failure, if you want to hurt my feelings, tell the minister that under his preaching and teaching you are not getting fed. The phrase being fed accepts the metaphor of the Word of God, of the Word of God as food. So to say that you are not being fed under the teaching and preaching of a man would be an accusation that the pastor is not doing as Jesus instructed Peter, which was to feed his sheep. The responsibility of an ordained minister to preach and teach the Word of God well is addressed in verse 17 of 1 Timothy 5. It is clear from verse 17 that an elder or presbyter or priest, whatever title you want to give him, Who rules well is one who labors hard in preaching and teaching the Word of God. Of course, there are several different ways a minister can preach and teach When it comes to preaching, the minister can choose to do what is called expository preaching, which is to take a particular section of the Bible we can call text. And break them down to understandable interpretations and practical application. Another manner of preaching is topical A preacher can choose a topic such as marriage and use a number of different texts from the Bible to make points he thinks need to be made. Another manner of preaching is what is called jumping off. This is where a minister reads a text. And then uses it to jump to what he wants to get off his chest or how he wants to influence the congregation, with the original text either being wrongly interpreted or simply forgotten. A great deal of megachurch preachers use this method and use it repeatedly. And another matter of preaching I'll mention is therapeutic preaching. Which is where a minister chooses a text from the Bible that is non-challenging and soothing. His goal is to make the congregation feel better about themselves and the world around them. This has become very popular since the pandemic. The ideal manner of preaching and teaching for me is to preach and teach the whole council of God, which means that every book of the Bible should be read and taught and preached. so that the Holy Spirit is given opportunity to speak to every soul that would care to listen and be made whole. I continue to try to do that even with 25 years behind us. The phrase double honor, as verse 18 makes clear, and the use of honor in verse 3 also indicates, is financial payment. However, it is not a text that any preacher can justify as to why he should be paid well It is a passage that simply follows the pattern of the practice of the apostles in the book of Acts, who wanted to focus their efforts on preaching and teaching and not on everyday problems. I have joked with some of you in the past that when I am asked a question about where something is to be placed in the church such as toys for Operation Christmas Child or food for a reception, I put my hands up, I say I know nothing about it at all I do around here, all I do around here is preach and teach. I say I joke, but a joke has If it has any humor in it, is to include a type of truth. I purposefully stay ignorant about certain things because I need to focus on preaching and teaching. Also, while some ministers focus their attention on being paid to preach, the real responsibility is to labor in the Word of God and in doctrine well. in order to be worthy of such pay. Some say that verse 18 is dear to every pastor's heart. But it is important in what lies not only in the being made at the moment the churches should support our pastor financially, but that Paul cites the Old Testament Believing that the principle taught was still in force under the covenant of Jesus Christ. In truth. Such happens a good many times in the New Testament and is proof, if proof is needed, that the law of God, even in its details, are not counseled when the church moved into the revelation of Jesus Christ. There were many changes of form, to be sure, but the principles enshrined in the law of God are eternal, rooted as they are in the nature of God. And this is not the only place where Paul cites the same verse to make the same point. The second citation The laborer is worthy of his wages, is in the color red in your pew Bible. It is in red because it actually is a statement from the Lord Jesus from Luke chapter 10, verse 7. And such is evidence that the Lord's teachings as we have it in the Gospels was well known among the Gentiles by the time Paul wrote this letter to Timothy. An elder, an elder is not to be a lover of money, as Paul said in chapter three, verse three. But the work of the ministry of the word is important and demands a man who does it conscientiously. So he is to be paid his due. Christians have often fretted about thinking that a man who is getting paid for such holy work would have divided motives. Some groups, like the Brethren, have, in part for this reason, declined to have full time ministers and have left the preaching and pastoring up to the layman, usually with predictable results Bobby Lee and I attended such a church many years ago now, and it was about 20 people sitting around in a very casual setting with casual clothing And when the top of the hour came, someone asked, So whose turn is it today? A young man in jeans and flannel shirt got out of his seat and took his Bible to the portable podium and began to teach. And not very well, I need to add. Somebody with training and time to prepare is truly needed. Also, you might want to know that our diocese has attempted to recommend salaries to be paid to ministers according to their experience and education But the truth is, in each matter, in the Reformed Episcopal Church, most churches can't afford to pay a cost of living full-time salary Which requires the minister to be effective in growing a parish in order to receive any form of income. Now I used to think that addressing the subject of money was a very uncomfortable topic for ministers, but I don't think that anymore There is a social media outlet that exposes ministers and churches practicing what is called money grabs. An example, recently a mega church pastor in Ohio started a series of sermons on increasing the offerings to their church to 10x. Whatever that means. The stage, and we call this area a chancel, but they call it a stage, which tells you something It was decorated with what looked like a space control center, and the pastor was dressed in a NASA jumpsuit. He took passages of scripture completely out of context, such as from Joshua, where the people were to enter a new land that they had never been before. And he compared that to giving money to the church where you have never been before. He then showed a video. of a couple who testified that they had pledged to give eighty-five thousand dollars to the new church project, and the pastor told them that that was not enough Then they pledged to give a million dollars because they wanted to reach the 10x plateau. The video was supposed to motivate the congregation to give 10x while expecting God to bless them in return. Historically, the church has called such offerings as simony Named after the person of Simon in the Bible who tried to buy the power of the Holy Spirit from the apostles It is very, very troubling to not only hear such teaching, but that people would actually believe it. The love of money is indeed the root of all kinds of evil. But what of an elder, priest, a pastor? Perhaps especially a preacher who does not perform his duties acceptably. What of them? And alas the situation has occurred far too often in Christian history. In verse 19, Paul first explains what is to be done when an elder is accused, and then what is to be done if he is found guilty. No charge about an elder is even to be received unless it is substantiated by two or three witnesses. The two or three indicating that the testimony must be plausible and serious enough to be addressed. This is also an Old Testament reference, and is to protect people, and in particular protect ministers from people who are vindictive or untruthful. The fact is, ministers are particularly susceptible to slander because of the influence they have, and especially today, within a culture that loves to litigate. And let us also remember that any minister that is effective in his preaching and teaching God's Word, so that God's people continue faithful, any minister that does that is going to be a target of the devil. The counter to that is that God is a defender of the righteous. So let us also say that these instructions about accusing a minister of the gospel also applies to social media. Slander is posted much more easily and freely than accusing someone to their face. On the other hand, if the sin is actually proved, Paul instructs in verse 20 that the man is to be rebuked publicly. No doubt, if the rebuke doesn't work, more severe punishment would follow. The phrase, in the presence of all, is a reference to the whole church. The rest is likely a reference to the remaining elders. Public rebuke can be helpful. To bring a man to see his sin for what it is, in its destructiveness, and it can be put a healthy fear. Into anyone who is tempted by the same sins. And there is to be no favoritism, as verse 21 states. Such favoritism practices continue to be revealed as ministers have too often looked out for fellow ministers at the expense of the church and at the expense of God's righteousness. It was just a few weeks ago that the Archbishop of Canterbury resigned. Resigned because it was revealed that he had a long standing relationship with a minister who was found guilty of sexual abuse with minors, and the archbishop turned away from the truth for many years and thus chose partiality. Such is a great shame and a personal affront to the Lord Himself Nothing, nothing is more destructive in and outside the church than sinful ministers who get away with their sins. Many respects. This is the story of the Protestant mainline churches. They have been destroyed by ministers who have sinned overtly and unrepentantly. And have been kept in their offices, teaching their people to do the same. But we know, we know it goes beyond Protestant mainline churches. As such behavior of covering up the sins of ministers has been exposed in the Roman Catholic Church and recently in conservative Baptist churches and in mega churches. So both concerns must be kept in view. This is a quote from Augustine from the fourth century. He said Here is a dilemma which often occurs. If you punish a man, you may ruin him. If you leave him unpunished, you may ruin another. The seriousness of what Paul is teaching is underlined by the directness of verse 22. Paul invokes his own apostolic authority, the present God and his angels, to command Timothy to treat elders in the way he has described. Neither going beyond the evidence nor falling short of it. The reference to the laying on of hands is clearly a reference to ordination For that is what is described as the practice in the Book of Acts. One important and sensible way to avoid future problems, of course, is not to rush to ordination. But to make sure that the man in question is both qualified and spiritually and emotionally ready to assume the responsibilities of the office. If ordination is given too hastily, Timothy will find that he has a share. A share in the sins the minister later commits. Because, as we all know, the only solution to a great many problems in life is not to have gotten into them in the first place. It also speaks to the spiritual nature and danger of sin For just as Achan's sin in the book of Joshua had an effect upon the whole people of Israel, so does sin in the church, in the local church. Sin that goes unchallenged or sin that is simply ignored. Verse 23 next seems a little bit out of place. Paul tells Timothy to drink a little wine. The best explanation I have read is that Paul means to ensure that Timothy doesn't misunderstand what it means to keep yourself pure. It doesn't mean the asceticism being taught by the false teachers in Ephesus. And Paul has already warned that a minister should not be a drunkard. So he is in no way advocating the abuse of wine. But I looked up this week the medicinal use of wine, and here's what I found. Red wine contains antioxidants called polyphenols. That may help protect the lining of blood vessels in the heart. Researchers say people who drink a moderate amount of red wine have better gut health. And reservatrol, an antioxidant found in grapeskin, has been linked with fighting inflammation. This is no excuse to go home and drink a glass of wine In general, the use of wine as medicine does not have enough studies behind it to be conclusive. Verse 24 is a necessary proverb to remember if we are going to be just and loving to one another. Some people's sins go before them Like a woman who is nine months pregnant and unmarried, while the man who impregnated her shows no evidence of his adultery To say some people's sins follow later refers to the day of judgment in which those sins hidden will be exposed. This is similar to what is said in Psalm 50, where God says regarding the sins of his people These things you have done, and I kept silent. You thought that I was altogether like you, but I will rebuke you and set them in order before your eyes. And the next, the principle in verse 24 is stated in verse 25. The same is true for good works. Some are obvious and some are hidden, but all will be revealed. Whether it be hidden sins or hidden good works, God knows all. And that is to be good news for us. It tends to scare us, but it's good news for us For it should stop us from sinning in secret. For there truly is no such thing as secret when God is ever-present and all-knowing And it should give us hope that all will be judged in a just manner in the end. But this section of scripture is primarily about addressing the conduct of ministers. It addresses how to reward them when they do the hard work of ministering the Word of God in their preaching and teaching. And it instructs the church on how to discipline a man who fails to do the work he is ordained to do. And what to do if a minister has committed an egregious sin. Overall, it can be said that the purity of the church is the responsibility of all its members. We are responsible for the sins we commit, which can be things we ought to have done and things we ought not to have done. And we are responsible for the sins of others when we see them in sin or know of their sin. We have a blueprint in Matthew chapter 18, where Jesus instructs us as individuals to go to a brother whom we have seen sinning. And help him towards repentance. If he refuses, we are to bring another witness. If he refuses again, then we are to bring him before the church. If he refuses, then he is refusing to be a part of God's body and is no longer welcome in the church until he repents. Beloved God wants his church, his bride, to be pure. What we are never instructed to do when we know of sin, when we witness sin, is to do nothing. He has given every power needed to overcome sin and every instruction needed when sin is in her midst. It is up to us to do the work. The purity of the church is the responsibility of all its members. Let each of us take up that responsibility. Amen. Let us pray. Gracious God, for these instructions given to Timothy, the desire to make the office of a minister holy and righteous, we thank you for it. We pray, dear Lord, that as you raise up men, they would take hold of that standard and live it till the end. And if there be any sin amidst us, may we pursue Purity. May we pursue that your body, that your bride be not sulfied. In Jesus' name we pray. Amen.

sermons.title: What to Say Last
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. I very much encourage you to turn in your Bibles to 1 Timothy chapter 6. The reading was verses 1 through 10, but I'm actually going to be covering the whole chapter. We're going to be walking through the whole chapter of 1 Timothy 6. What should I say to you if this was my last sermon to preach to you? Because partings between loved ones is most difficult, you want to say something that is memorable Recall the dramatic scene described in the book of Acts, chapter 20, where Paul is leaving the Christians at Ephesus. Paul reminds them in his closing remarks, he reminds them of the dangers he encountered while ministering to them, and how often he prayed in tears for their salvation. He recanted how he went door to door to minister to them the gospel, both the Jews and the Greeks. Regardless of the tribulations he faced, he counted his calling as joy to his soul because of the privilege of testifying about the gospel of grace in Christ Jesus. Paul next assured them that although they will not see his face again, that he had labored to present to them the whole counsel of God. He then warns them to protect the church as a good shepherd would protect his sheep. This is necessary. For he told them false teachers, whom are called wolves, would come among them to draw them away. To draw the believers from the gospel. And in fact, Paul warned them of this attack for three years. For all three years, he was with them. He closes with commending them to the grace of God, and that he has been an example to them of self-sacrifice. And then he quotes Jesus, who said, it is more blessed to give than to receive. Luke then describes the scene after Paul's address, again from Acts chapter 20. And when po when he, Paul, had said these things, he knelt down and prayed with them all. Then they all wept freely and fell on Paul's neck and kissed him. sorrowing most of all for the words which he spoke, that they would see his face no more. And they accompanied him to the ship. Such a narrative reminds me of the great quote from the Muppets Christmas Carol, where Kermit the Frog, who is playing the part of Bob Cratchit, And the scene is Scrooge being shown a possible future Christmas where Tiny Tim has died. And Kermit's character says to the other children It's all right, children. Life is made up of meetings and partings. That is the way of it. I am sure that we shall never forget Tiny Tim or this first parting That there was among us. It's that line. Life is made up of meetings and partings that has stayed with me from the first time I heard it. So profound and yet stated so simply. So if I were parting from this pulpit, what would I say to you? Well perhaps I would start off by addressing a particular problem I was aware of. Perhaps like Paul, I became aware of there being strife amidst certain groups in the church. In Paul's case, he was aware that slaves in the church were rebelling against their masters. Of course, I must qualify my remarks because slavery in the ancient Near East, as I addressed a few weeks back, wasn't anything like the enslavement of Africans in the West. Slavery in the ancient Near East was likely a business transaction where a person or a family were was in debt. And they sold themselves or part of their family into servanthood to pay off the debt. Hence why we use the word bond servant. And it was certainly understandable for a person who is a slave in such a situation to think that their freedom in becoming a Christian should apply to all aspects of their life After all, their debt of sin had been paid. Why not their debt financially to be paid as well? But Paul recognizes how important it is to maintain a good witness for Christ. And that means by staying in a business agreement and pay what is owed. And he qualifies his statement with recognizing there could be a situation Where a slave owner is also a Christian, which would make the slave and the slave owner brothers in Christ, thus equal in Christ. But still, Paul wants that which is the greater witness to the world. That is what Paul cares most about. He cares about how we look to the world, how Christians look to the world, because he remembers the words of Jesus, who said that the world will know we are Christians by our love for one another. Such love the world cannot have unless they come to Jesus. The second subject I might address, if this was my last sermon to preach to you, Is the presence of the stubborn within the church who don't want to accept or hear sound doctrine, sound doctrine that leads to godliness. Unfortunately, there have been and always are people in the local church who would rather argue than learn. Such persons would find it easier to dispute a teaching as opposed to submitting to a teaching. Such persons are all about, but what if? Or, but what about? For such persons, exceptions discount the rule, any rule. No truth can be in place because there are too many variables to consider. So landing on truth for them is impossible and frankly quite annoying. For such persons, disputes are the motivation for being in church in the first place. But disputes are a means of avoiding self-examination. To address doctrines of godliness requires a look, a look into the inner man and to face what is being seen. It is to accept moral absolutes that require a level of self-discipline that most persons want to avoid. I chuckle at Paul's instruction for Timothy to withdraw from such people because he doesn't mention what to do if such persons won't withdraw themselves. Thankfully, if a minister is faithful to preach the Word of God, such persons will withdraw themselves because the truth is being heard and their chance for disputes is decreased to the point of falling on. deaf ears. The third subject I might address in my last sermon might be about being content. and the importance of contentment as opposed to the love of money. In this I would likely address more to younger men I see discontentment as a serious issue in our culture today, and that includes with Christians. Young men today seem irritable and anxious. They want more in life and thus are discontent with what they have been blessed to receive. And here again we point to the tenth commandment regarding coveting. And coveting is difficult to resist, even though the middle class in America are one percenters when compared to the rest of the world. It is the devil who says you need more, you deserve more. It is the Holy Spirit who says the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil. And yes, we notice that the saying is that the love of money is a root, not the root. And it says that the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil, not the root of all evil. But Paul's point is important. For he knows of people, he knows of people personally who have left the faith because of their love for money. And when that happens, such persons have not understood that they truly brought nothing into the world and certainly And will certainly carry nothing out when their days on earth have ended. Jesus called such persons fools, for they thought their lives would go on and on. And when the truth is there, they will be there will come a day where their days will end, and a reckoning will occur as it will for all of us. The fourth subject I would want to address, if this was my last sermon, would be speaking on a positive side. Being corrected, we all know, can be difficult upon the psyche as we want to think in a positive direction, even though the negatives addressed are accurate. But we all need encouragement. And so I would say that as you flee the negative of being discontent, pursue the positive, which is righteousness. godliness, faith, love, patience, and gentleness. Such, you will note, are very similar to the listing Paul gives to the Galatians regarding the fruits of the Spirit. Such things come out of a believer who is filled with the Holy Spirit and is listening to the direction the Holy Spirit is pointing. I'll give you an example. Let us imagine that a friend of yours wants to meet with you. You have no specific idea what the meeting is going to be about, so you're not worried. The meeting starts out cordial, and then the friend pulls out a list of grievances this person has with you. You think to yourself that the Bible says that love keeps no record of wrongs, so this person is in violation of the scriptures, and I don't need to listen to his grievances. Another thought in your head is saying, don't get angry, listen to what is being said, and be humble. Can you next decipher which thought is of the Holy Spirit and which is of the devil or your own flesh? I can guarantee you that the devil is never going to tell you or encourage you to be humble. Such a thought only comes from God. Listening to such thoughts is pursuing righteousness, godliness, faith, love, patience, and gentleness. Well in being positive, I would also want to be a coach for you, and that I would want you to get fired up for the battle you are going to face. I would say fight the good fight, as Paul does in verse 12. And the encouragement to fight requires the adjective good. For fighting to fight is the same as the description of persons who want to dispute. No doubt. That after this past cycle of elections, you became weary of reading and listening to pundits who care more about disputing than settling disputes Whether it be the personality of the pundit that likes to dispute, or the fact that the disputes get more clicks, the end goal is the dispute. Those are bad fights. But there are good fights. There are good fights. And those are to be engaged with fists ready to fly. Paul calls the good fight the fight of faith that will eventually lay hold of eternal life. Such include right doctrine and moral standards that do not break or bend. The right doctrine includes the full divinity and full humanity of Jesus. The moral standards include being sexually moral and protecting the least among us. Included in my positive remarks, if this was the last sermon I was to preach to you, would also be a charge. Charges are what preachers give at ordinations or consecrations or installations and weddings. They sound more like a challenge, such as to live up to your calling, take the challenge of your position, never compromise, and so on. Paul called Timothy to live up to his confession, which apparently was a confession Timothy made in public. And perhaps he's referring to the day of his ordination, where each minister pledges a faith in Christ and a commitment to the church. But all faith, all of us who have faith, it's a confession. We are saved by saying Jesus is Lord. The more difficult part is to live up to the level of your confession. Now remember Hearing the testimony of Dr. Jordan Peterson, who was asked if he was a Christian, and he shared with tears That he was scared to be one because he didn't think he could live up to the standards of what a Christian should be. I suspect we all can relate to such apprehension, but that is where faith comes in. We are saved by grace through faith and not by our works. And we work, we work to get our lives to match up to what we say we believe. And we keep on working We keep on working until we are no more in this life. For that is what servants do. They keep working. And you will want God to say to you, Well done, thou good and faithful servant. Enter into your rest. The fifth subject I would preach on if this was my last sermon to you is to be sure that Jesus received all the glory in my words. I would say, as Paul does here in 1 Timothy 6, I would say that Jesus is the blessed and only potentate Which is ruler over all, which is why we call him King of Kings and Lord of Lords. Jesus alone has immortality dwelling in unapproachable light. Whom no man has seen or can see, and to him only is honor and everlasting power given. Amen. And my closing remarks, if this was my last sermon to you, would be to return to the warning against the pursuit of money. It is, of course, no sin to be wealthy. Some come by it naturally, and others by inheritance. But it is the love of money that is dangerous to the soul Money may be likened to the idol such as Molech, who has the spirit of the devil and the substance of being empty inside. Paul tells Timothy to warn the rich and then to help protect them from making wealth an idol. Instruct them instead to be ready to give For it is again more blessed to for it is a again more blessed to give than to receive My final words to you, if this were my last sermon to you, would be for you to guard what has been entrusted to you. There is a need to guard, because the devil is indeed prowling around as a lion, as a lion seeking whom he may devour. And he devours more easily inside the church than he does outside. For when he is inside, people think that what they hear can be trusted, and so they are not on guard. And so when the preacher tells them that the sin of Sodom and Gomorrah was not being hospitable instead of sexual immorality. There is a temptation to trust the preacher because we know him. We have known him for years, and so we trust him. He wouldn't lead us astray, right? And then you hear the preacher say that the letters of Paul are tainted because Paul was a misogynist, a racist, a homophobic. You think that the preacher must know more than you because after all he went to seminary We all know that if a person has a degree, they're likely right about most things, right? And once again I remind you of the saying that we shouldn't fear the uneducated, but the poorly educated. And when the preacher says that Jesus didn't really rise from the dead bodily, but that Easter is a celebration of his spirit rising. And thus our hope is also our spirits rising. And you think that because you didn't actually see Jesus' body, and it does sound like an unbelievable miracle, and the preacher is not the only one denying such a resurrection He may be right. Such is what some people call knowledge, and thus some have strayed concerning the faith. And this is why Christians need to be on guard The enemy without can also be the enemy within, and we must fight him off wherever he is found. Beloved, Lord willing, this is not my last sermon I will preach to you. But it is the end of the first letter Paul wrote to Timothy. I told Bobby Lynn how I was going to approach this sermon, and she said, Well, if it was your last sermon, I know what you would say. And I said, What is that? And she said, fight the good fight. She knows me well. And so I close with these statements. Hold on, stand firm, keep the faith, fight the good fight until he comes. Amen. Let us pray. Gracious and heavenly Father, we thank you for these final words of Paul to Timothy. We thank you for the correction that's needed, and we thank you for the encouragement that is also needed. May we take heed and fight that good fight and hold on and be on guard. In Jesus' name we pray. Amen.

sermons.title: Christmas Eve 2024
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. One one of the repeated themes that runs throughout Charles Dickens' A Christmas Carol. is a contrast between communal celebration and private grumpiness. The contrast begins with the familiar greetings from Scrooge's nephew, a hearty Merry Christmas. And the famous Ba Humbug response. The next passing description is of a young man who tries to visit Scrooge at his place of business and sing him a Christmas song with the hope of a returned gift for the gesture. Before the bo young voice was able to express itself fully, Scrooge scares him away with great energy and action. The contrast between a happy heart in celebration and a cold one that thinks only of one's thoughts is intensified with the coming of the three ghosts. You remember that the ghost of Christmas Past is first, and the ghost takes Scrooge to his old school house. The first people they see are young boys passing. They are wishing one another Merry Christmas All the boys were in great spirits and shouted at each other until the broad field was so full of merry music that the crisp air laughed to hear it. Going from that place into the schoolhouse, Scrooge comes upon his this scene. Dickens writes They went across the hall to the door at the back of the house. It opened before them and disclosed a long, bare, melancholy room, made barer still by lines of plain deal forms and desks. At one of these, a lonely boy was reading near a feeble fire, and Scrooge sat down upon a form and wept. Wept to see his poor forgotten self as he used to be. The boys on the street are merry in heart and merry with one another. Anyone who would look upon them would smirk and be amused at their gaiety. But the boy in the schoolroom reading alone brings a different reaction upon the observer. Something is wrong with him, or something is wrong with them who would leave him out. Whatever the problem, it is simply not a happy boy or a happy scene. A few scenes later, Scrooge finds himself standing at the shop of his first apprenticeship. It was almost time for the proprietor, Mr. Fezziwig's beloved Christmas party. The party started with a closing of the shutters and a clearing of the floor for dancing, for what was a party without dancing All were invited to the party, the housemaids, the cook, the cook's family, the boarders, even those who were behind on their rent. All who were part of Fezziwig's life and business were invited. Then the dancing began. Dickens writes. There were dances and more dances, and there were forfeits and more dances And there was cake, and there was negas, and there was a great piece of cold roast, and there was a great piece of cold boiled, and there was mince pies and plenty of beer. The evening did not reach a crescendo until Fezywick stood up and danced with Mrs. Fezywick. Dickens writes. And when old Fuzzywig and Mrs. Fezziwig had gone all through the dance, advance and retire, hold hands with your partner, bow and curtsy, corkscrew, dribble the needle, and back again to your place. Fuzziwig's cut Cut was so deftly that he appeared to wink with his legs, and came up on his feet again without a stagger. Scrooge was agitated while he watching all of this. Not because he hated it, but because he remembered loving it so much. Scrooge then describes the effect that merriment of Mr. Fezziwig had upon him. Again, Dickens writes He has the power to render us happy or unhappy, to make our service light or burdensome, a pleasure or a toil. say that his power lies in words or likes in things so slight and incid incident is nicknamed. That it is impossible to add or count them up. What then? The happiness he gives is quite as great as if it cost a fortune. At these words, the mind of the reader and the thoughts of Scrooge are taken back to the manner that he treated his clerk earlier that day. It was hardly in the same spirit of old Fezziwig. It was the opposite. And Scrooge began to ponder, at least a little, how his countenance affected others He too had the power to make service light or burdensome, pleasure or toil, and he chose the latter every time. When the ghost of Christmas present reveals himself, it is in Scrooge's own room, in his own house. Dickens writes, there is no doubt about that. That phrase lets us know that although it was Scrooge's room, it looked nothing like the room he once owned. The lights, colors, roaring fire, meats, puddings, chestnuts, fresh fruits and bowls of punch filled every part of the once dark, dingy, and cold space. Scrooge had never seen anything like the ghost of the colours and the excess of Christmas, because he had never truly celebrated it. himself the four. When the ghost of Christmas present takes Scrooge throughout the streets of London The attitudes of the people are notably lighter than any other day, as their tempers were fairer and their manners politer, because it was Christmas Day. The first house visited was owned by Scrooge's clerk, Bob Cratchit. The Cratchits had six children, varying in ages. Each of their countenances was bright and cheery, for they all anticipated a great day of celebration. Their feast was meager by our modern standards, and by the standards of their day, but they would never complain or want more. Each course and portion was cherished and enjoyed thoroughly. When the feast was finished, it was time for good cheer. Blessings and singing. Singing is what tells others that the heart is merry. All the time the chestnuts and the jug went around and round and by And by they had a song about a lost child traveling in the snow from Tiny Tim, who had a plaintiff little voice, and sang it very well indeed. Dickens writes, There was nothing of high mark in this. They were not a handsome family. They were not well dressed. Their shoes were far from being waterproof. Their clothes were scanty, but they were happy, grateful, pleased with one another, and contented with time. The lessons regarding the joy and singing and contentment continued as Scrooge is taken to a home poorer and in greater need than the Cratches. And the main focus of the family's Christian celebration is gathering around the fire to sing. Christmas celebration is gathering around the fire to sing. It is the same with men they visit on an ocean vessel who, at least for one day, can think happy thoughts about families who remember them fondly, and thoughts bring their voice to a pitch. The next house visited is that of Scrooge's nephew, who is identified by his smile and hearty laughter. His house is filled with family and guests who desire to make merry every moment of the day When they are not laughing, they are playing. And when they are not playing, they are singing. When they are not singing, they are laughing again. The last game played was called Yes and No. Dickens writes, where Scrooge's nephew had to think of something, and the rest must find out what, he only answering to the questions yes or no, as the case was. The brisk fire of questionings to which he was exposed elicited from him that he was thinking of an animal a live animal, rather a disagreeable animal, a savage animal. An animal that growled and grunted sometimes, and talked sometimes, and lived in London. As you know, he was thinking of Scrooge. And this brought great laughter to the gathering. The effect upon Scrooge, as he witnessed himself being the butt of their joke, was surprising. When they all had wished an absent Scrooge Merry Christmas, Uncle Scrooge had imperceivably become so gay and light of heart That he would have pledged the unconscious company in return and thanked them in inaudible speech if the ghost had given him time. He was grateful for their merry wishes even if they did so in spite of their disliking of him But we know the rest of the story, as Scrooge was changed, a changed man after that night, and it is said to have kept Christmas better than anyone. And Dickens wants that to be said of us. And if we are to do so, we must understand what it is to be merry and what it means when we say Merry Christmas. For we are to be merry in contrast of a secular world that says the days are too stressful, or that the season is supposedly based on a pagan holiday. And Kowanza and Hanukkah should be highlighted and eventually replaced the public celebration of Christmas. With that reality as our backdrop, we are to be merry. To be married suggests cheerfulness, joyous, uninhibited enjoyment of frolic and festivity. It is expressing what is within our hearts in a holy manner. Expressing merriment is what Mary, mother of our Lord, did when she visited Elizabeth and had it confirmed that what the angel said was true and that she would give birth to the Messiah. To be married is what Zechariah did when he heard that his son would lead the way and make the way for the Messiah to come. To be merry is what the angels did when they announced the birth of the Son of God to the shepherds watching their flocks by night. They made merry on Christmas. It is very sad that we, we as a post-Christian culture, have lost the ability to make merriment. We don't sing in our homes as we used to. Music, games, and laughter are not central to our celebrations as they should be. If true merriment is to be regained, it needs to start within Christian homes. My charge this night to every home this Christmas is to sing around a fire or around a lighted tree or around a piano And if you are too uncomfortable with your own voices, put on Bean Crosby, Nat King Cole, or any other Christmas album and sing along with them. Play a game, tell stories, and laugh. Laugh at yourself. Laugh at one another. Make merry And when we do, when Christians truly make merry, the contrast between us and the world will be as stark as old Scrooge and the merry people around him. And the result might be that the unbelievers around us may desire to know how they too, how they too can have a merry and thus have a merry Christmas. Amen.

sermons.title: Christmas Day 2024
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. Here is the Christmas sentence. The word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we beheld his glory It is two sentences, really, one with a compound predicate. God has spoken to us by his son, the brightness of his glory, and the expressed image of his person. Each of us has likely imagined what it would be like to witness creation in those six days God wielded his power to bring into being that which did not exist before he spoke. The green leaves, the brightness of the flowers, the sparkling waters, the movement of the hills and mountains, all that have astounded us, likely placed us in a state of befuddled awe. But as our imaginations take us beyond what we have experienced, we ought not underestimate the beauty of the second creation. And which was, in an important sense, far brighter than the first creation. The second, the incarnation, God becoming man, built upon the first, and then turned it upside down. Thus we can say that Christmas turned creation inside out. It broke the stranglehold of death. It thickened water. How could we even begin to express this second creation? Wineskins could not hold it. Even Saint John, even Saint John, who gave us the Christmas sentence, gave up. He gave us word upon word, sentence upon sentence in his gospel and in the book of Revelation. And then he had to finish by saying Even the world itself could not contain the books that could be written. If this is true If John struggled to describe it, it is quite ironic that we are expected to teach the story to our children and our grandchildren. If John didn't have the words, where are we going to get them? And yet it is impossible to hold it in. Like a pregnant woman, it pushes our skin out to its breaking point. It gives us stretch marks.
