And yes, what you just heard makes sense Only you might have to listen to it or read it again a few times to follow the track of logic. But my point to go on In such a manner is to show how difficult it is for finite minds like ours to understand the full nature of God. The great mind of Saint Anselm of Canterbury, a twelfth century theologian Put forth his famous ontological argument for the existence of God by defining God as that by which nothing greater can be conceived. Such a definition works well within the ontological argument, but it has a flaw, in that it seems that God's existence is based on what man cannot fully comprehend. Of course, God's existence isn't dependent upon anything that humanity can or cannot understand, but the definition of God being that by which nothing greater can be conceived At least gets to the point that to compare God to humanity or any one man ever besides Jesus Is to fall embarrassingly, shamefully short of coming close to knowing God. It is only after we try to comprehend just how much we cannot comprehend God That we can reasonably see why it is necessary for us, who are created beings, to worship the one who created us. So God is beyond our comprehension, and yet there are truths that God has revealed to us that He wants us to focus upon. But we find it difficult to focus upon what God has revealed to us about Himself because as we are worshippers by nature, we are also sinful due to our fallen nature. Having established the argument that God, because of his nature, is worthy of praise, worthy of our praise, it is next necessary for us to examine the nature of humanity in particular. In particular, examine our nature as compared to God. God reveals to us that we are worshipers by nature by telling us of our first parents, Adam and Eve. Who were placed in a perfect environment where food was plenty, the temperature was such that no clothing was necessary And because there was no sin, there was no need for shame, requiring nothing to be hidden All that was given by God, and therefore God was to be thanked, honored for his giving of such gifts that required no toil of humanity But only to enjoy the fruits of the garden, except one fruit, the fruit of the knowledge of the tree of good and evil. The fruit of the tree of knowledge of good and evil was the only fruit God instructed Adam and Eve not to eat, and with that instruction they were placed in a position of possible failure. To not eat said fruit would require them to fully love God, as He would reign supreme in the hearts of Adam and Eve, and to disobey by eating said fruit would of course bring about what God promised, which was the curse of death. From the choice of our two parents that they made, it was revealed that they loved something other than God. And we know from the previous sermon that disobedience excuse me, back up From the previous sermon, that obedience is an act of worship, and disobedience is refusing to practice proper worship. When God curses Adam and Eve because of their disobedience, he reveals what is meant for Adam and Eve to know good and evil. Now, no one to my knowledge has better explained what it meant for Adam and Eve to know good and evil after their sin better than C. S. Lewis. In his second installment of his space trilogy titled Paralandra, Lewis describes a planet that has been recently occupied by two human-like creatures, a male and a female, who are given the duty by God to procreate and fill the new planet with their own kind. But they were not alone. For a demon-possessed man who on earth, on earth was a scientist named Weston, had created a ship that enabled him to land on Peralandra. With the goal of corrupting the undefiled creatures and eventually the whole planet. This plan for corruption is interrupted by another scientist named Ransom who is the hero of the story, working diligently to expose Dr. Weston to the innocent creatures for what he truly was While helping the new creatures resist the temptation to disobey God. Just like the biblical story, The possessed Dr. Weston tempts the female creature while she is unwillingly separated from her mate. The story is more complex than I am able to describe in this sermon, but what Lewis brilliantly shows from the conversations the female creature has with both the possessed Dr. Weston and the hero Dr. Ransom. Is the difference, the difference between knowing good and evil from the devil's perspective versus God's perspective. From the biblical narrative of the fall of Adam and Eve, some have interpreted that God did not want humanity to know good and evil at all, or ever. What Lewis explains is that God did and does want us to know good and evil only from the side of obedience. And holiness rather than from the side of disobedience and sin. Because of the choice of our first parents All of us know good and evil from the side of disobedience and sinfulness. And that perspective makes our knowledge distorted, limited, and corrupt. When the Hebrew preacher teaches us that Jesus knew our weaknesses because he was tempted in all ways like us, yet without sin. We learn from that that Jesus as a human being is the first to know good and evil as God intended, which is again from the side of obedience and holiness. From such aside, it can be said that Jesus is the only person to ever truly know good and evil. For the devil himself only knows it from the say from the side that we are on, from the side of disobedience and sin. Because we know good and evil from the wrong side, the distorted, limited, and corrupted side, everything we do. Every act we perform, thought that we have, project we complete, relationships we have, motives we use, all of it is tainted by sin. This is the same as where it says in the Bible that all have sinned and fallen short of the glory of God. Romans 3:23. This, as I have described, is confirmed by the prophet Isaiah, who said that all we, like sheep, have gone astray. Isaiah 53, 6 The Apostle Paul said of humanity that there is none righteous, no, not one. Romans 3:10 If reminding you of the fallen state of humanity is depressing, I must interrupt your thoughts to say that it is not my goal, not the goal of my words, but the goal of scripture to depress. But rather to awaken our conscience to our need for God's forgiveness. Every time we are reminded of our fallen condition, our sinful condition, it is to awaken our souls. So that we might utter the same words spoken by the crowd after St. Peter's sermon in the book of Acts, when they shouted, What then shall we do? If you are not a Christian, then you need to know that the answer is to repent and be baptized. And if you are a Christian Then you have been baptized, so then it is your next duty to repent. The Christian life is indeed a life of repentance. Thus, repentance should play a central role in Christian worship. If you go to a Christian worship service and there is no confession of sin, that is no Christian worship. And after we repent of our sin, we are to believe that God is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness. It is when we have believed that God has forgiven us that we must next give thanks, give Him thanks, give Him praise, give Him our worship. And we must give him our worship because if we do not, then we will give it to something other than God. Guaranteed. To be convinced that we humans are, by our natures, beings that must worship. Allow history to teach us For there is no civilization civilization known to history that does not have some form of worship of some form of God or gods. If history is not enough, then examine people you know and observe their obsessions. If a person is not a follower of Jesus, he or she is a follower of something else. People give themselves over to anything to serve as their God. Substances we refer to in the context of addictions are worshipped. Money is worshipped Fads are worshipped. Material goods are worshipped. Social causes are worshipped. Family is worshipped. Politicians are worshipped. Sports, athletes, celebrities are worshipped. Even recreation is worshipped, and even laziness is worshipped, as there are people who work hard for the purpose of avoiding work. We can also see how emotions are worshipped as people on one end of the emotion expression pursue the high of joyfulness while others pursue the high of anger and bitterness. And if history and observation and observation is not enough, then be convinced by Bob Dylan. Who famously sang, you've got to serve somebody. It may be the devil, it may be the Lord, but you have to serve somebody I've been told I'd do a good imitation of him, so putting the puzzle pieces of the sermon together you need to see that The peace that shows that the nature of God is naturally to be worshipped and the need for humans to worship go together. The troubled piece that doesn't seem to fit is that we are sinful because we have fallen natures. The missing piece that helps our fallen natures to fit with the creator of the universe. Is that Jesus fits perfectly between us so that we are no longer estranged from God, even while we have not yet received heavenly holiness? Before we do, we are to be acting out the task of worshiping God. The question that remains is: how? How are we to worship God That question is going to be answered more fully in the next sermon. What I want all of us to realize is how modern worship has failed to answer the question, how is God to be worshipped? There is a British satire television series called Yes Minister that performs dialogue, skits, giving humorous insights into British culture, including politics. In one particular scene, the Prime Minister is to appoint a new bishop, but is having trouble choosing from the candidates. He discovers that all of the political all of the politically acceptable candidates are not true churchmen, but rather politicians. He learns that the primary candidates For bishop no longer dress for their position as Christian ministers, but rather for social steps. The Prime Minister is told that their modern dress is for the purpose of relevance. The Prime Minister responds to this by asking, relevant to God? The answer comes back, no, of course not, Prime Minister. I meant relevant as a sociological term. It is that term, relevant, that has dogged the modern church as many bodies of believers have worked hard to be socially relevant. There is the attempt to be relevant in terms of society, resulting in what are called liberal Christian churches. These churches have abandoned the Judeo-Christian morals set forth in Holy Scripture and instead have adopted moral standards that set no standards at all except the virtue of tolerance And even that virtue is rejected if it is tolerance for those who still uphold Christian morals The other Christian group that wants to be relevant is made up of the independent Christian gatherings who confess to abide by Judeo-Christian morals. but who worship in the manner that they think is appealing to the greater masses of people, especially younger people. And so these groups replicate popular music styles while placing Jesus in the lyrics. Some even use light shows and fog because, well, such staging is thought to make worship more relevant. The vagin question is, relevant to who? Relevant to God? No. And there lies a very serious problem. I submit that the more relevant Christian worship becomes to humanity, particularly Western humanity, the more God begins to look like Western humanity, and such a picture is not worthy of any worship. I also submit that if you examine the worship as commanded by God for both the tabernacle and temple and the worship described in the book of Revelation. You will realize that corporate worship of the one true God is to be heavenly relevant, not earthly relevant. Christian worship is only relevant when it ascends into heaven, where the Father and the Son reign. I also submit that we are only relevant to the kingdom of God when our worship is relevant to heaven. That should be our goal, that should be our standard, and nothing less. When it comes to worshiping the only, true, and everlasting God, there should be no compromise. Let us pray. A gracious and merciful God As we recognize the standards of your word regarding our worship to you and our need to worship you and you to be rightfully worshipped May we continue, continue to raise our standards that it might be heavenly relevant. In Jesus' name we pray. Amen.

sermons.title: Conscience
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Peace be seated. Starting a new series of sermons. This Sunday and I have seen a popular thing to do in megachurches is to have a series of sermons and they have fancy titles I've ran across one, a brand new you. Does that sound enticing? How about miracles, signs, and wonders? And receive the anointing. Well, my the title of of my series of sermons is The Ramblings of a Rector. Right? Catchy? Draws a lot of people in. Yeah, I'm gonna be rambling this summer about a lot of things. And today it's about our conscience. A repeated misguided perspective, and we can call it a sin, amongst God's people, is to believe That if they received no immediate rebuke or punishment for a sin committed, then God must not be concerned about it. What many people fail to recognize is how sin begets sin, especially when it is not immediately rebuked or there are no clear negative consequences. Hear this rebuke from a psalm of Asaph, Psalm 50, starting at verse 16. But to the wicked God says, What right have you to declare my statutes or take my covenant in your mouth, seeing you hate instruction and cast my words behind you? When you saw a thief, you consented with him, and have been a partaker of adulterers. You give your mouth to evil, and your tongue frames deceit You sit and speak against your brother. You slander your own mother's son. These things you have done and I kept silent. You thought that I was altogether like you But I will rebuke you and set them in order before your eyes. A lesson from such words is: be not fooled by God's silence. Be not fooled by God's silence. Because simple men have their heads down, they only believe that rewards in life and punishments in life will come from what is down. What is of the earth and not from above where God rewards and where God prepares his judgments I'm aware that some of you will get riled up about what I'm about to say, but I need to say it to make a following point. I Don't conclude that it is a sin to go over the speed limit while driving, because it is not a moral sin, but it is instead a wrongdoing against man-made laws And not God's laws. Now there's a fair response to that statement that says that St. Paul teaches us in Romans 13 to obey our governing authorities. And yes, it does say that. But governing authorities have laws for various reasons, and Paul was actually breaking Roman law by preaching the gospel and was put into prison for it. Allowing us to conclude that the laws of men can be broken, only we are to accept the consequences of the laws we break. If I go over the speed limit and I get pulled over by a policeman and he gives me a ticket for speeding, that would be a just thing to happen. And I would be obligated to pay the fine because that would be obeying my governing authorities. But let me give you a more simple example. Let's say I am playing in a football game. And I'm trying to block for my teammate. And the guy I am blocking is getting by me, and so I hold his jersey. In doing so, I broke a rule of the game placed there by the governing authorities of the game, and therefore I disobeyed my governing authorities. A referee sees it and throws a flag, and the punishment is a 10-yard penalty against me and my team. I did a wrong thing. I suffered the consequences for it. Almost sounds the same as going over the speed limit. But going back to my example of going over the speed limit, I must acknowledge that if my steaming endangers other people's lives, then that adds a moral component to it that would make it a sin against God because I was not loving my fellow man. So I need to be honest with myself when I go over the speed limit and ask. Is the place I am speeding safe Is the traffic in which I am speeding congested? And are conditions on the road in which I am speeding dangerous? If the answer is yes to any of those concerned, then I am obligated by God's moral law and man-made law, to not speed. Of course, the risk of hurting someone is always a reality when driving, regardless of your speed limit. For life itself is a risk as we function in this world. But we are to weigh our risks to see if they are reasonable or unreasonable. But here is the thing with speeding. If I speed and I don't get pulled over and thus I don't have to pay a fine, the likelihood of me speeding again is greater. It is the same with my football analogy. A player who doesn't get a penalty for a rule violation is going to do it again. He will do it again and again until he gets caught, and the penalty hurts his team. The reality is the driver who speeds and the football player who holds will only be detoured if the punishment for the infraction has too high of a cost. The driver who speeds stops speeding when his license could be revoked. The football player stops holding when a penalty he receives causes his team to lose. It is the same way with people that Asaph rebuked in his psalm. They won't stop sinning until God punishes And the point of all these analogies is that it should not be the same for Christians. We should not have to wait until we are punished. From chapter 9 of Hosea, for those who have been participating in our weekly Bible study, will recall that we learned that Israel Thought they could rejoice because their harvest of wheat and wine had come in, and such made them conclude that God was happy with them. But Hosea called out their sin, telling them they have played the harlot by worshiping foreign gods. But ASAP teaches us And what Hosea points out is that God's people are not to base their behavior or way of thinking based on what they see outwardly, but they are to examine themselves inwardly. And to be honest as to whether they are living by faith, which is to live by the conscience God has given them. The context of the passage read from 1 Corinthians chapter 10, you may recall from other studies done from 1 Corinthians, but for those who have forgotten, I will explain. From what we gather from history and from the text itself, there were Christians in Corinth who in their past lives, lives before they were called to follow Jesus, That found them worshiping in Greek temples and participating in temple rituals, which included eating meat and drinking wine that was offered to idols Paul reminds such people that with them being now Christians, they could not participate in such rituals anymore because they would be mixing the food they consumed To idols with holy communion, making them no different than their former selves and no better than the Israelites during the time of Hosea. To do so, to mix the two, would be a burden to the heart of God. Next, Paul moves into an area of examination that the people of Corinth may have Been brought up in the form of a question asked of him or regarding something he had heard about them. It seems that the practice of the Greeks was to take the meat left over from the idol worshipping and to sell it in the marketplace for anyone's consumption. Such became confusing to Christians who did not participate in the worship of idols, but didn't know if buying meat that was used for idol worship would make them idol worshipers. It is a guilt by association question that many Christians work to understand even today. For example, we live in a country that allows abortions and euthanasia. We can legally kill the youngest among us and the oldest among us and the depressed among us With no apparent, and I emphasize apparent consequences. Being a citizen of such a state and country Are we as guilty of such sins just as those who want such killings to be legal? And the answer is to such a question: no. And it has to be a no because of Jesus himself, who paid taxes, taxes to an empire that enslaved people, killed innocent people, raped and pillaged other nations, and oppressed the poor. If Jesus were guilty by association, there would have been no sinless sacrifice for sin, and we are then still hopeless. But Jesus was sinless and a fulfillment of the prophecy from Jeremiah, who promised a new revelation in God's covenant. In Jeremiah chapter 31, we read, In those days it will no longer be said, the fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the teeth of the children are set on edge. Instead, each will die for his own iniquity. If anyone eats the sour grapes, his own teeth. Will be set on edge. Behold, the days are coming, declares the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah. It will not be like the covenant I made with their fathers when I took them by the hand and led them out of the land of Egypt. A covenant they broke, though I was a husband to them, declares the Lord But this is the covenant I will make with the house of Israel. After those days, declares the Lord, I will put my law in their mind and inscribe it on their hearts And I will be their God, and they will be my people The point of the great synology is that each person under the covenant of Jesus will be responsible for his own sin and his sin only. Thus, Jesus is not responsible for the sins of Rome, nor was he made unclean by them, and we are not responsible for the sins of our fellow man, nor are we made unclean by them. But notice, but notice what we will be responsible for. The prophecy says that God will write his law on the minds and hearts of his people. God will speak to each of his followers directly so that they can know how God's law is to be applied in their lives. Now looking back at 1 Corinthians 10, notice how Paul applies the freedom to not be responsible for the sins of others. He says in verse 23, all things are lawful for him, meaning that the law does not restrict him regarding what he can eat. And where it is from. However, he says, not all things are helpful. All things he is free in Christ Jesus to do, but those same things he is free to do Do not always edify. And where he is going is to convince Christians who also feel feel free in Christ to not automatically and in every situation practice that freedom Which in this case is eating meat once offered to idols. And the reason, notice the reason. The reason is because of the conscience of others. Such teaching and such living is truly the application of the teachings of Jesus who told his followers to take up their own cross, which is what they are to die to in order to follow him. It is to think of others before yourselves. It is to assume that you are to sit in the back of the banqueting table and not the front Paul describes the same when he says, let no one seek his own, but each one the other's well-being. Although such a point is a powerful one and a high standard to live up to, that is actually not where I want this sermon to go. The final point I want to make from this passage and from the Old Testament passages we have read is how important it is for the Christian to live by his or her own conscience. The main reason we are to live according to our conscience is so that we would be obedient to God by obeying the law He has placed in our hearts. Living by faith alone and being obedient to God seem to be in tension with one another, but we know St. James in his epistle teaches our obedience to God as a fruit and a sign that we are living by faith. Paul proclaims to Christians that all of us who follow Jesus are created for good works. Such good works bring glory to God and actually bless us in this life. As I preached last week, we are free to be motivated to do good work because we love God and because He promises us reward. He wants reward to motivate us. And so it should. Receive this example. Good marriages are not good because the husband and wife are self-righteous. They are good because the husband works at resisting the temptation to lust towards other women who are not his wife. Good marriages are good because the wife chooses to submit to her husband in all circumstances. Good marriages are good because the husband examines how he is treating his wife as compared to how Jesus loves the church. And where he is failing, he owns up to it, confesses it as sin, seeks forgiveness from his wife, and they forgive one another whenever there is a breakdown. Living obediently in such a manner results in having God-fearing children who also seek to be obedient to God and eventually love their spouses as God instructs. And the result is that a lot of laughter when the families get together, and a lot of smiles watching grandchildren playing together, with every hope that they will be obedient to what God says as well Such is a reward from God. The other main reason why we need to live according to our conscience is how we will eventually ignore the voice of our conscience entirely if we think we can compromise our conscience on a case-by-case basis Using the example I gave earlier, compromising our conscience while not receiving any immediate negative consequences makes it easier and easier to compromise the next time. Remember, the one who speeds and receives no ticket will speed again. The one who breaks the rules of a game and receives no negative consequences will break the rules again. But as Christians, we are to obey the voice of the Lord, the law written on our hearts, not because of negative consequences, but because we love God and want his rewards. Now, an objection to what I have been proclaiming could be to give doubt as to how we can know for certain that what our conscience is telling us is what the Holy Spirit is telling us. How can a Christian know that our conscience is reminding us of God's law and not man-made laws? Let's examine such a concern with some examples in the negative first. In the negative first. If a person is tempted to dishonor his father and mother because he perceives they are unjust, we can conclude from the fifth commandment that such temptation is not of the Holy Spirit. If a person hears a voice saying, lie to your boss, don't get caught, lie. Because of the ninth commandment, we can say again, that's not of the Holy Spirit. If we are contemplating covering evidence for your sin because you want to maintain a certain reputation, there was no example in Holy Scripture ever of guiding his people to do such a cover-up If we are true to our conscience, we know that to be true. And let us now look at it from a positive perspective. If I have the opportunity to go to a rodeo on the Lord's Day, Sunday morning. Versus attending worship at church, and my conscience prods me to choose to worship the Lord. Such prodding will never be of the devil or your own flesh. If you have the opportunity to gossip to your dear friend about a person you and your friend do not like, and your conscience tells you to pray for the person you don't like instead of gossiping about her That will not be a demon speaking to you. If a person is upset at you and you perceive he is unjust when upset at you, and you have the opportunity to defend yourself and prove this person wrong. But your conscience is reminded that the Bible says, be quick to listen and slow to speak. Such a reminder is not from the devil. It's not from your own flesh. It's from the Holy Spirit. It's the law of God written on your heart. In truth, listening and walking according to our conscience is not complicated, or at least not complicated, if we don't ground our conscience with compromising. I close with a qualifier that I am not simply saying, as Jiminy Cricket sang to Pinocchio, that all persons should always let their conscience be their guide. Although Disney back then did have a conscience, a Christian ethic as opposed to today. Our conscience can only be our guide When it is the Holy Spirit who is writing the law of God on our hearts, so that we willingly are walking according to said law. It is being obedient with ourselves, knowing that we are going against our conscience. A conscience that is speaking to us God's truth And when we are honest with ourselves that such is indeed what we are being tempted to do, to go against our conscience, we are then to strive to be true to our conscience, to be true to God, to be true to ourselves. As Paul says, for our conscience' sake, let us pray My gracious God, we accept this standard. The standard to be careful about other people's consciences, but also our own For we know your law has been written on our hearts. You have chosen us. You have made us your people. And now we ask you to help us in our weakness that we might obey that conscience and thus obey your law. We pray this in Jesus' name. Amen.

sermons.title: Know Your Bible
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated Remind you that this series for the summertime is titled The Ramblings of the Rector, which basically means that I gotta get a few things off my chest. Let's begin with a quiz. And don't answer out loud. Because I'm not trying to embarrass anyone today. Rule number one for public speaking If you want people to like what you are saying, you need to make them feel good. And you won't feel good if you are embarrassed. Truthfully, however, my goal is not just for you to feel good, but for you to feel good because you feel challenged. So let's start the quiz. True or false? Jesus taught using parables because he wanted what he was teaching to be more relatable to his listeners. Answer false. In Mark chapter 4, after Jesus tells the parable of the sower, his disciples didn't understand the parable, and so they asked him what it meant. Before Jesus tells them, he says the following, quote, the mysteries of the kingdom of God has been given to you. But to those on the outside, everything is expressed in parables, so that they may be ever seeing, but never perceiving. And ever hearing, but never understanding. Otherwise, they might turn and be forgiven. The latter part of the verse is a quote from Isaiah chapter 6. Jesus uses the words of Isaiah in the context that he was in. in which consisted of people who were truly seeking the kingdom of God while others were seeking to destroy his ministry and have him put to death Thus, those who are willfully blind will not see the truth, and those who do not seek the truth of the teachings of Jesus will never understand him and never believe him to be the Son of God, so they receive his teachings in parables they won't understand. So if you answered that Jesus told parables in order for his teachings to be more relatable, it is actually the opposite of what you thought. Quiz question number two. We all know that the fifth commandment of the Ten Commandments says for God's people to honor their father and their mother. And God promises that if they do, that their days will be long in the land the Lord God gives them. But Jesus said the following. If anyone comes to me and does not hate his father and mother, wife and children, brothers and sisters, yes, and his own life also, he cannot be my disciple. Is this a contradiction and thus a proof that the Bible contradicts itself? The answer is a cold no. And the reason should be obvious to every Christian, but sadly it is not. The answer is that the fifth commandment comes after the first commandment, which commands that God's people have no other gods before him. And that word before means anywhere in the vicinity of him. The first commandment, beloved, is read into all the other commandments that follow it. If you break any of the last nine, you have also broken the first. Therefore, to love a family member more than God. Or even in the same manner you love God is to have another God before him. And to do so means you cannot be a disciple of Jesus Quiz question number three. The first letter of John chapter three, verse six, reads. Whoever abides in him, and him is God, does not sin. Whoever sins has neither seen God nor knows God. But then we have passages like Ecclesiastes 7, verse 20, that says the following: For there is not a just man on earth who does good and does not sin. Are these another example of the Bible contradicting itself? It could be answered that the Ecclesiastes was written before the time of Jesus, and therefore men could not be made righteous or obedient until their hearts were set free by the gospel and the very presence of the Holy Spirit But that's not an answer that holds up because John seemingly contradicts himself when he wrote previously in chapter one of the same letter. What we hear every Holy Communion service saying, if we say we have no sin, we deceive ourselves and the truth is not in us. If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness. If we say we have not sinned, we make him out to be a liar, and his word is not in us. Thus we must ask. Did not John know that he wrote in chapter 1 in the same letter what he wrote in chapter 3? Did he just push send without proofreading his letter? The answer is actually more simple than some would think. The Greek language which John uses has tenses like our English language, past, present, future, although the Greek has more nuances in its tenses. Without getting into more detail, the point of John in chapter 3, verse 6 is that a person who knows God is not to continue in their sin. He or she is not to be living in sin and still claiming to know God. Thus, a person who does know God and sins Responds by confessing his sins and does not stay in his sins Now hopefully you're asking what is the point of my quiz and why I am asking the questions the way I have asked them The point is that many of us don't know our Bibles well enough. The point is That when the devil places an apparent contradiction in the Bible before our eyes and ears, wanting us to conclude that the Bible isn't trustworthy, We are more likely to listen to such demonic prompts because we don't know our Bibles as well as we should. And beloved, beloved, a sermon once a week is not enough. It's not enough. You must understand that if you do not know your Bible, the devil will use the oldest trick of temptation on you. He will say, just as he did to Eve in the garden, did God really say? Really say not to eat of every tree of the garden? And that phrase, Did God really say, has led millions astray Because they find a reason to live according to their flesh, because they are now convinced that God didn't say what the Bible says, and therefore there is no God. And I get to be my own God of my own life. So, so in order not to be led astray, I want to challenge you to better know your Bibles. We are blessed to live in the time that we do, because we can have more and more confidence that the Bible is the very Word of God, and therefore worthy of our study of it. And one of the reasons why we can have confidence that the Bible is the Word of God is archaeological discoveries. They keep being uncovered. Two years ago for Adult Sunday school, we watched a documentary series about archaeological proofs of the Bible's validity. We saw evidence of the location of King David's tomb. We saw evidence for the place where God came down and spoke to Abraham We saw evidence for the sulphur that rained down upon Sodom and Gomorrah. We saw evidence for the destruction of the walls of Jericho. We saw proof of the tomb from which Lazarus was raised. We saw proof of the hill of Golgotha, where the cross of Jesus was planted. And just this past year, the great stone of witness placed by Joshua has been identified Along with the place where Jacob saw the vision of angels descending and ascending. And the city of Ai has been identified, which is the city overrun by the Israelites after they won the battle of Jericho. It is. It is all very exciting. And not because we need such discoveries in order to believe, but because they are fascinating verifications of what the Bible tells us What the Bible tells us regarding how God has interacted with His people in history. And they do help us trust that what the Bible describes did indeed occur with real people in real time. Another reason we can be confident that the Bible is the very Word of God is its historical veracity. Historical events in the Bible can be verified by other historical documents outside of the Bible There are ancient Egyptian texts that claim that Egypt had conquered a people called the Israelites. And there is a letter written to the Egyptian pharaoh, written? Written at the time of Joshua, coming from the land of Canaan, that asked for help because a people known as the Haburi Or Hebrew people were conquering tribes in the land just as Joshua had done Tacitus, a Roman historian, wrote in 116 A. D. of a man named Christus, who was put to death by the Romans under Pontius Pilate. Jewish historian Josephus mentioned Jesus and his followers, describing Jesus as a wise teacher and a doer of wonderful works. A second-century Greek philosopher named Celsus identified Jesus as a doer of good works by sorcery. Pliny the Younger, a Roman official sent to the province of Bithynia in what is now northern Turkey, about 110 A. D. , was bothered by the Christians Although Pliny had extensive governmental experience, he had never been involved in a trial involving Christians. So when it came time to question some of them, he wrote to Emperor Trajan for advice. He wrote this. I do not know what crime is usually punished or investigated, or to what extent. He was uncertain whether those admitting to be Christians should be punished, or if they had to be charged with a crime as well. Meanwhile, he asked the accused if they were Christians. To those who confessed, he asked a second time, then a third, when even after threatening punishment, they still confessed to be Christians. Pliny ordered that they be punished. He said, quote, For I did not doubt that whatever it was they admitted, obstinacy and unbending perversity certainly deserved to be punished The seeming lack of respect toward Roman authority seems to have angered Pliny more than anything He likened this Christian attitude to a kind of contagious insanity or mental disorder that would inevitably result in crimes against the Roman state. He closed his letter warning, quote, this contagious superstition is not confined to the cities alone, but has spread its infection among the country villages. Trajan, the Emperor Trajan, incidentally commended Pliny for his actions. The Christians were even called atheists, sorcerers, and cannibals. They were called atheists because of their worship of one God rather than the many gods worshipped by the Romans. They were called sorcerers because of the way they prayed over the bread and wine they consumed at Holy Communion. They were called cannibals because they proclaimed to eat and drink the body and blood of Jesus. All of these writings verify That what became of Christians within the Roman world was exactly what Jesus told them would come about. But along Along with the confidence we can have that when we study the Bible, we are studying the very words of God, we are also to realize that Jesus and only Jesus has the words of eternal life. And that phrase, that phrase, words of eternal life, comes from John's gospel. Now we called it, we call the setting. Jesus has fed over 5,000 people. Jesus explains that in him doing so, he is reminding them of the bread God gave his people while they wandered in the wilderness. And the people say to him, Lord, give us bread always proving that many people were following Jesus, not because he was the Messiah or that he was teaching them godly words, eternal truths. No, they were following him because they wanted a free meal. And a free meal continually And Jesus then reveals to them that the bread in the desert that fed the nation of Israel, and the bread that fed two over five thousand people, was bread that pointed to himself. For he revealed to them that he was the bread of life. For just as he is the living water, so he is the bread of life, so that whatever the souls of men need, he is the provider. And after saying all this, the people started doubting him and exchanging doubts, for that is what doubters do. They influence others to doubt. And so they murmured about him, saying that Jesus is just an ordinary man. And they can prove it. They can prove it because they personally knew who his father and mother were. Jesus responds by talking crazy, at least that is the perspective of the doubters. He talks about himself being able to give them eternal life But to receive eternal life, they must believe his words. And to show they believe his words, he tells them. He tells them Unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you have no life in you. And then he added, Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life. And I will raise him up at the last day, for my flesh is food indeed, and my blood is drink indeed. It was then, it was then that the doubters had heard enough. They said to one another that the words of Jesus were too hard to understand. And John says that many of those who followed him went back home and walked with him no more. And Jesus sees them walking away and does not go after them. He lets them go And then he gives his closest disciples a chance to leave as well by asking them, do you too also want to leave? And Peter answers in the most humble and articulate manner possible. Lord To whom shall we go? You have the words of eternal life. And such is why we should follow Jesus No one before him taught in the manner he taught. No one blessed the poor before Jesus. No one taught people to care for the least persons in a society before Jesus. No one propped up humility as a virtue before Jesus. No one before Jesus gave warnings to the rich that their wealth will make them spiritually poor. No one before Jesus taught that salvation was realized. By having faith in a man, a man who is God. No one helped disciples understand that in the most simple things you can find the kingdom of God. No one before Jesus. The kingdom of God is like a mustard seed. The kingdom of God is like a lamp. The kingdom of God is like a fig tree. The kingdom of God is like a lost coin, a lost sheep, a lost son. It is like virgins burning oil. It is like a hidden pearl. It is like a banquet feast. The kingdom of God is all of these and so much more. The Bible, beloved, has the words of eternal life, which means words for in this life and words for heaven. It has words of hope, such as confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord, and believe on him in your heart that God raised him from the dead, and you will be saved. It has words of warning, such as some will say, Lord, Lord, and I will say, Depart from me, I never knew you. It has words of joy, such as the Lord is gracious and full of compassion. It has words of desperation such as, My God, my God, why have you forsaken me? It has words of peace, such as Jesus saying to his disciples after the resurrection, peace to you. It has words of chaos such as, in those days men will cry out for the rocks to fall on them It has words of direction for all of our lives, such as, be anxious for nothing, but let your request be made known to God. And be angry and do not sin. Do not let the sun go down on your anger. And return to your first love. And seek first the kingdom of God. And pray without ceasing. And love one another. And set your affection on things above. Today, we acknowledge the important doctrine of the Trinity, and yet many Christians are poorly prepared to defend said doctrine when ignorant Jehovah's Witnesses or Mormons Come to your door and tell you the word Trinity isn't in the Bible. It truly is a moronic point to make. Because the doctrine of the Trinity is found not in the Word itself, but all over the Bible. It is in the word Elohim. Which is a word God uses for Himself, and yet it is a plural word. It is in the account of creation of man when God says, we We will make man in our image. It is in the visitation of the angels to Abraham, the wrestling with Jacob. The persons of Joseph, Moses, David, Elijah, Elisha, and in the words of the prophets. But this would be more readily known by Christians if we better knew our Bibles. Beloved, study the Word of God. Study the Bible. Be in Bible studies with learned men. Don't be in a Bible study that just reads a passage and says, what do you think? Be in a Bible study with learned men. Attend Sunday school and learn from those ordained to teach. Read your Bible. Read your Bible for stories, for devotion, for information. Whatever the motivation, read and study your Bible. Amen. Let's pray

sermons.title: Don’t Follow the Crowd
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. Continue our series on the ramblings of a rector The title of this sermon, so that you know where I'm going, is Stop Following the Crowd. Three weeks ago, a woman appeared at the front door of this church knocking and looking to speak with someone. I was the only person in the building, so I went and opened the door. She appeared around my age. Although I really don't know what that looks like anymore, but she looks like my age. She wanted to speak to the pastor, and since I am the pastor, I spoke to her. We sat down in the vestibule and she began her complaint. She had been attending a local parish, but was upset at the priest Because he was speaking disparagingly about homosexuals. She said that although she knew the Bible speaks against sexual immorality, She wants everyone to be treated with respect and kindness. She continued on about all of her life experiences, dealing with all sorts of sexually confused people and she sees the good in them. After what felt like a good while of her doing all of the talking, she asked me what I thought I shared what the Bible teaches about sexual immorality and that we firmly stand on what the Bible teaches as we acknowledge all persons being made in the image of God. She responded with the same arguments and frustrations she began with, and then added comments about Israel and Hamas, about Russia and Ukraine. And her emotions were building and building. And I was able to stop her and ask if she watches a lot of news. She said, oh yes, I watch the news all of the time and from many different sources I then suggested that she stop watching the news for a time and get a different perspective on life. She she said that she could not do that because she cares too much about our country. And she reminded me of people I have watched. online who are picketing against the president or against some policy. And when a person asks them what specific policy They are protesting, they can't articulate it, and then they get mad at the people filming them and asking them questions. My point is that people get caught up in protests, movements, politics, for the simple reason that it is a popular thing to do. People become swayed regarding their outlook on life and how they view the future of their country based on what is said by the media. And most of you will know I consider the mainstream media the most dangerous influence upon our culture as it has been an effective tool in the hands of the devil for decades. The most vulnerable to the mainstream media in our culture are those who are elderly and those who live alone, which the woman who I spoke to fit both categories. And if you think I am mistaken, I encourage you to watch a mainstream media broadcast on television. And pay attention to the type of ads that pay for the programming and come to your own conclusion. Ads for fiber. Ads for adult diapers, ads for heartburn, arthritis medicine, all of them are common But of course, it isn't only the elderly and the alone who are susceptible to the media and its propaganda. Our young people love to be a fan of what everyone else seems to be a fan of. Now I am about to state What may be the most controversial thing I have ever stated behind this pulpit. But here it goes. I think Taylor Swift is not very talented. I even add Beyoncé to that statement. They don't sing well and they don't dance well, but the media height keeps them in the spotlight, and so they are multi-millionaires, and everyone knows their names The reason why I am pointing these things out is because the following of the mass media and the acceptance of things that are not true is how the devil wants us to think and then live What I'm calling us to do as Christians is to come out of such deception, such propaganda, such nonsense, and be free. Christians are to be free from the false, to be free from what is deceptive, and to be free from what is foolish. There are dramatic teachings in Holy Scripture that call Christians to be separate from the world, and thus to be different from the unbelieving world in which we live. One of those passages with part of our gospel reading today. It is found in the title Sermon of the Sermon on the Mount. During our Bible study on Wednesday, we have been looking at the parables of Jesus. And the last parable Jesus tells from his Sermon on the Mount is about a wise man building a house on a rock, not upon sand. Jesus says that in the parable that a person who hears his teachings and does not live by them is like a man who builds his house upon sand. In our study, we considered all that Jesus had taught up to that point, and it is quite a bit The following is not at all exhaustive, but I want you to recall some of what Jesus has taught just in a few chapters in Matthew's gospel. Followers of Jesus are to see people as blessed and blessed even though they're downtrodden and poor. We are to be glad we're persecuted. We are to be salt and light. Our righteousness is to exceed the righteousness of the scribes and Pharisees. Don't hate. Don't lust. Keep marriage sacred. Keep your word. Let people take advantage of you for your witness of Christ. Love your enemies. Pray in this manner. Fast in private. Store treasures in heaven. Be a lamb. Don't serve riches. Don't worry. Don't condemn. Ask and keep on asking. And then he says, then he says, enter the narrow gate. All of what I have listed is to be a part of our lives. All of it is to guide our lives. And if such teachings do not guard our lives, we have built our lives on sand. We are the fool. And what I want us to focus upon today is that we are to enter the kingdom of God by way of the narrow gate. While others, while the unfaithful, the unbelieving, the deceived, walk through a wide gate that will eventually lead to their destruction, we are to walk through a narrow gate. And as a narrow gate, Jesus says it is a difficult way. And because it is difficult, there are few who find it, which is to say, few who choose to go through it. Comedian Nate Bargetsey once joked that the best time to be Christian was to live in the 1980s and the 1990s The joke is funny to us who were Christians in those decades because we thought being a Christian back then was cool. We thought Christianity was popular. That was when Christian bookstores were a popular trend. You could go to such stores and get a Bible on all sorts of translations and study Bibles, particularly geared towards teenagers or women or athletes or empty nesters You could buy cool Christian music that tried to sound like the secular music on the radio, but with Christian lyrics. Even rap with Christian lyrics. Truth be told, it never sounded as good as what was on the radio, but we lied to ourselves that it did. You could buy keychains that said, I love Jesus. Or John 3. 16, you could get bracelets that had WWJD on them. And that told everyone who inquired that you were willing to do what Jesus would do. It was such a great time to be a Christian until it wasn't. Jesus became a commodity to be sold. His teachings were being watered down. Christians were adjusting their faith to the culture. Christian leaders on television became an embarrassment. Beloved Christianity, following Jesus, living the Christian life, was never meant to be a fad. But that is what the devil wants to tell us. He works to make Jesus a fad. A fad to the point where it means nothing to say you are Christian. Because being a Christian means to enter the narrow gate and to go the difficult way, by its very nature, it can never be a fat. But why is it? By its nature, difficult. Why is it a difficult way to travel? Why is it a difficult way to live? Well, as I listed, the teachings of Jesus Consider how such a way of living goes against the manner other people are living their lives, and even goes against what each of us is naturally inclined to do. Personally, I am not meek by nature. I don't feel blessed when downtrodden, nor when I am persecuted. I more easily hate than I love. I more easily lust than I don't lust. I naturally worry. I naturally condemn. I want to store up treasures in this life. I more naturally hold a grudge than I do forgive. To do the opposite of all that I am naturally inclined to do is to go the difficult way. It is to enter through a narrow gate. And of course, it is not just the teachings from the Sermon on the Mount that we are expected to build our lives upon. Jesus says some provocative and seemingly impossible things elsewhere. He taught for his followers not to fear men with weapons, but fear only God, who can kill the body and condemn the soul. He said that his followers would be enemies within their own family members because of his teachings. And then he says that all who follow him must pick up their own cross. Then he added that whoever desired to save his life or her life will lose it, and must lose it for his sake to receive a heavenly reward. Such is not a broad road, beloved. To follow Jesus is the most difficult road a person can follow. Any preacher that does not tell you the same as a liar and a charlatan. And I don't care how good the preacher on your television makes you feel. He is a charlatan, and Jesus will say to him on judgment day, depart from me, for I never knew you. Another way the Bible teaches us to not be followers of men or of a culture is from Paul's letter to the Romans, where he says this. I beseech you, therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, you present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable to God, which is your reasonable service. And do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, that you may prove what is good and acceptable and the perfect will of God. These words begin Paul's final instruction to the Christians in Rome and thus reflect in a general manner of how Christians are to live their lives. For Christians to present their bodies as living sacrifices follows that same language Jesus used. Picking up your own cross is the same as offering yourself as a living sacrifice. That Paul calls it a reasonable service tells us that nothing less is expected. Nothing less. Again, the false teacher, the charlatan, will never use such language because it doesn't sell. It doesn't put people in the seats. It doesn't encourage people to tune in, and it most certainly doesn't fill the offering plate. But it is the truth. Christians are to be living sacrifices and nothing less. And then Paul follows his instruction with the call for Christians not to be conformed to this world. To be conformed to the world is to think like the world. And how does the world think, or how does our world, our 20th century world, think? Well, first it believes that every boy who cries wolf and every chicken little that says the sky is falling is telling the truth. Our world is motivated by fear, and the mass media knows it and exploits it. We who are Christian must not fear fear. Instead, we are to trust in the sovereign reign of our God, who made heaven and earth, and therefore nothing can occur without his divine will, which fits into his plan of salvation. His perfect love casts out the fear that tempts the hearts of Christians. The second way our present world thinks is that morality is evolving. Just as many believe the human species has evolved, so we think the same about morality. And much of our morality changes because our emotions change. Many of you, I know, have been tempted to change your stance on sexual immorality. Because a friend announced she was a homosexual. Or a relative announced that he would be living with his girlfriend And because you love such people, you don't want to emotionally detach yourself from them, you are tempted to change your opinion about sexual morality and what is acceptable. And it's not just sexual morality. I know of a minister who condemned acts of suicide, believing it such to be the ultimate statement against God's commandments. And then his son attempted to commit suicide, and his teachings changed. And suicide for him is now a forgivable sin. But the Bible knows of no such compromising. The Bible teaches standards of morality that do not change. They do not change with circumstances, or because of family members, or because of emotions Another way our modern world thinks is that if it is popular, it must be right and good. Many Christian churches have operated on such a premise for years. In the 1990s, many church growth models were based on what would more likely draw a large crowd. Every compromise, every decision regarding programs, worship styles was based on what would draw the biggest crowd. Anything and everything was justified in terms of outreach. If you could attach the word outreach to a program, that program was justified. Churches had weightlifting presentations, wrestling matches, light shows, rock bands, circus acts, all in the name of outreach. And yet, and yet Jesus said, where two or three are gathered, there I will be in the midst of them. Two or three is all it takes. As I shared in Sunday school a week ago, I am aware, very much aware, that what we do here and the way we do it will not draw a large crowd. But the crowd I hope to draw are people who want to honor the Lord Jesus Christ because they have been saved by him. They don't want to do what everyone else is doing. They don't want to sit at the cool kids' table at lunch. They only want to honor God, who is the only one deserving of our praise, our adulation, and our imitation. Our epistle reading describes a double-minded man being unstable in all his ways. Such is a warning to every Christian that an unstable life is a life that comes in and out of joy, it comes in and out of security and in and out of faith. It is the stable life that decides not to follow the crowd, but to confess one God, one faith, and one Savior, and to do so, no matter the cost. Let us pray. Gracious God, we thank you for the standard that you set. No compromise. To choose to go through the narrow gate, to choose to have a new mind. Holy Spirit, help us to do just that, that we might hear those precious words, well done. In Jesus' name we pray. Amen.

sermons.title: Grateful for the Material World
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, of the Son, of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. We continue the rector's rambling. There are several reasons why modern churches are leaving carnage behind them and sliding into proverbial gutters of falsehood And today I want to address one of those reasons. To show just how far deep these churches have slid into the gutter We have in one mainline church in America, its leader, publicly stated a few years ago that Jesus was not only Not the only way, excuse me, that Jesus was not the only way to God, and that for anyone to say so would be to put God in a box In another mainline church in America, a woman pastor described herself as, quote, Christian by birth, a Baha'i by reason, a Taoist in spirit And a pastor in faith and vocation. What is remarkable beyond the audacity to make such statements is the cowardice of all who are unwilling to hold these so-called ministers to their ordinal vows. Where we should be concerned beyond the poor witness these statements make for the Christian faith is how it came to be that such statements could be made within the Christian bodies, bodies that once proclaimed the same confessions and creeds that we proclaim. We can be assured that it did not happen overnight. I have preached previously that in order to protect ourselves from going down the wrong path, the Bible has to be embraced as our first And primary source of authority for salvation and godly living. I have preached that we are to hold on to understanding of absolute truth in order to avoid compromising in life and in doctrine. I have preached that men need to be a primary concern when worshiping in the church So that they take their needed place in leadership within parishes and within their homes. Today I address an issue that might seem too subtle to be important, and yet, as I see it It is subtle because it is important. The devil has made it subtle so as to cause us to overlook it. The subject is the true importance of the material world, and thus the importance of the physical church. The problem is modern Gnosticism within the church, and its effect can be seen in the manner we build and upkeep our sanctuaries. In the manner we dress, in the manner we treat ordained officers of the church, in the manner we treat our personal bodies while alive and even after death. And finally, in the manner we view sin. Gnosticism, like so many other words in the English language, has several meanings. The prefix is the Greek word gnosis, which can mean knowledge or secret knowledge. When someone says he is an agnostic He is saying that he does not know if there is a God, even though God is not in the word agnostic. Some time ago, I was sent an email that poked fun at our English language. The following sentences use words that are spelled the same but have entirely different meanings. For example, the bandage was wound around the wound The farm was used to produce produce. The dump was so full it had to refuse more refuse. We must polish the Polish furniture. He could lead if he would just get the lead out. The soldier decided to desert his dessert in the desert. Since there is no time like the present, he thought it was time to present the present. When shot at, the dove dove into the bushes. How can I how can I intimate this to my most intimate friend? There are more, but you get the point. These exemplify that the English language is a melting pot of misfit words and Gnosticism is no different. The word Gnosticism was originally used to describe how to know God. During early Christianity, the word took a new direction and it became a type of religion. Today it describes a rejection of the material world in favor of the spiritual world. It is a belief that the created world, the world of matter, is corrupted and therefore unimportant. In place of the material world, the Gnostic believes that the spiritual world is the only place where God can be found. God, according to the Gnostic, can only be known in the spiritual world. Gnostic belief has been practiced in two seemingly opposed expressions One expression says that because the material world is not a concern, and that it is only the spiritual world where truth can be found. Anything we want to do in the material world is acceptable because it is already corrupt and thus cannot be corrupted more than it is. This is a dualistic philosophy that says the material world and the spiritual world are entirely separate from one another. Therefore, whatever we want to do with our bodies is acceptable. Whatever we want to do with property is acceptable. Whatever we want to do with creation is acceptable because it has already been corrupted. Some would even say the material world was always evil. Another, as I said, seemingly opposite expression of Gnosticism. Is the understanding that because the material world is corrupt or evil, it is to be avoided. These people believe in denying the flesh of anything pleasurable. They believe in simplistic living while searching for spiritual peace. So while one group may not care what happens with the material world, And another tries to avoid the material world, they do so because they both believe that matter is corrupted and that salvation is only found in the spiritual realm. But why do why do we care about such groups, you may ask? Well, as I stated, There has been a subtle influence upon the Christian church that has slowly eroded a previously strong-held belief that the physical church mattered. If you have ever thought that going to a worship service isn't important and that a person can worship God anywhere, then you have been influenced by Gnosticism If you've ever thought that what you wear in the presence of God isn't important, then you have been influenced by Gnosticism. If you have never been concerned that the house in which you worship would also be used to host a basketball game, you have been influenced by Gnosticism. If you have believed that baptism is not necessary for the Christian, or that the laying out of hands is for the Pentecostals only. Or that Holy Communion can be celebrated once a week or once a year, it really doesn't matter. And you have been influenced by Gnosticism. To show why Gnosticism is to be identified when it appears and rejected for the heresy it is, we must turn, of course, to Holy Scripture. From the scripture we learn that matter matters. The physical world is important. What God did say regarding creation after he finished it was that it was good. And if God says that something is good, should any man say the opposite? Now, in objection to these rhetorical poin would be that because sin has entered the world through Adam, and along with that sin was a curse that caused thorns to grow, the earth to shake, the skies to storm, disease to spread, and death For all that is living. That which was once good is good no longer. In theory, in theory, this might be true. That God did not say it. And he most certainly did not respond to sin entering the world as a Gnostic would. No. Instead of avoiding the material world, God invaded it. Instead of avoiding or destroying the created order, Jesus became a part of the created order And that included being subject to creation. Jesus, we know, became flesh. Jesus became subject to gravity, to hunger, to thirst, and of course to death. Jesus became a man, fully a man, and yet was without sin. If Jesus could be without sin and also be a man, how could all of creation be evil? What Jesus did was take that which is fallen and thus corruptible and first consecrated it. After he consecrated it, he sanctified it, and after he sanctified it, he glorified it. Meaning that which was corruptible took on the incorruptible, which Paul says in 1 Corinthians 15 Remember, beloved, that Jesus did not take only the form of a man. He was a man. And remember that he did not stop being a man. Once he was raised, he continues to be a man and will be for eternity a man. This is part of the amazing grace we proclaim. Jesus will forever be flesh. Thus, how can we ever say that flesh is not our concern or that the spiritual world is superior? And also, is not part of God's redemptive plan to bring forth a new earth I realize I'm asking a lot of rhetorical questions, but they seem necessary as what I'm saying most you already know. I'm simply reminding you of how these truths apply. If God is going to create a new earth, then can we be assured that He cares about the physical material world Again, from Genesis 1, God saw all that he made and said it was very good. And there was evening, and there was morning the sixth day. As a man, Jesus embraced the world in a very tactile, touching manner He laid hands upon the sick. He stood on the ground, made clay, and placed it on the man's eyes. He picked up the little children. He turned over the tables of the money changers He took the five loaves and the two fish and made more. And he took bread, and he broke it, and he gave it to his disciples and told them to take and to eat. And afterward he took the cup and gave it also to them. I said previously that Jesus first consecrated matter, and by that I meant his own body. Consecrate, you recall, means to set something aside, something physical for a sacred purpose. Jesus himself was something set aside. He made himself of no reputation. St. Paul explained to the Philippians, by becoming a man. Jesus' life was set aside to serve the Heavenly Father As he said of himself, that he did nothing but what he saw the Father have him do. The second thing he did was to sanctify himself. To sanctify is to make holy or be made holy. Jesus did this in many ways. The public way was to be baptized. Another was to fast for 40 days. It was there that he proved his mettle by resisting temptation. And what would be the weakest moments of a human condition, which is hunger? Of course, the most public way Jesus sanctified his body was to be obedient unto death, even death on the cross. With that one act, with that one act he sanctified all flesh that would cry after him to be saved. And next, of course, Jesus' body was glorified as he walked among men after his resurrection and was then received into heaven by God the Father. Beloved, the faith of a Christian, faith in all that Jesus did, is testified in the manner we treat the material world. So first, let us start with our own bodies. The body is to be made subject to the spirit, and therefore it is to be buffeted and disciplined. The body is to be cared for as it is the house of the Spirit of God. A Christian testifies to the goodness of the body when he or she cares about what goes into the body and how much goes into the body. A Christian testifies to the goodness of the body when it is adorned with appropriate dress that honors the God who created him or her. The body is to be honored at death as well, for the manner we treat is a testimony to the world that it will one day be raised. I do not say that cremation is forbidden, and I understand the pragmatic reasons for it, but there is a far greater testimony to be made to the world. When we embrace Christian burial by saying ashes to ashes and dust to dust, while also proclaiming that the dead in Christ will be raised first. We testify to the goodness of the material world also in the manner we treat the created order. While Adam was given the call to have dominion over creation, he was never given the right to abuse creation. Christians should be stewards, good stewards of the created order. Christians should not be wasteful. Christians also care for natural resources. Christians should not be need a crying Native American, if you remember that commercial and I heard he wasn't even Native American. But we shouldn't need that to tell us that we should not be throwing trash into rivers, lakes, and oceans. Christians should also work to preserve natural beauty, because it is that beauty, in that beauty, is a testimony of God as creator. We testify to the goodness of the material world also in the manner we treat structures and furnishings in our homes and in our church buildings. There used to be a day when a minister was invited to a home when it was first built or purchased to first give thanks to God for his provision and second to pray prayers of consecration over each room. So that each room was intended, how it was intended to be used, would be realized. There used to be a day when a sanctuary was finished being built, that all its furnishings, including the vessels used for Holy Communion were blessed by the minister to be consecrated for their particular use. And the manner the furnishings and vessels were treated after the consecration was reverent. Because it was recognized by all that each had a particular use in worshiping God. And each room, and each of the rooms, the vessels were placed, were also blessed because God said his creation. is good. There used to be a time when God's people by great conviction would gather on Sunday mornings, not sun Saturday evenings, not every other Sunday in a month. But Sunday mornings, every week, because Jesus said that where two or more are gathered in his name, he will be in their midst. He is with God's people that worship like he is at no other time when they physically gather. In the Old Testament, such was called a holy convocation. In the New Testament, it is called the gathering together of the saints. In both descriptions, there is a physical gathering. The bodies God physically created physically gather for worship And the people also gathered because the church has called Sunday morning the time when Jesus should be worshipped. And that was good enough for Christians because the church was and still is a physical manifestation of God's presence in the world. There's a scene in the movie, It's a Wonderful Life. Where George Bailey, you know, played by Jimmy Stewart, gives Mr. Potter an earful, and afterward he gets control of his emotions and says, Well, I've said enough. As if he could say more, but he must stop. That is where I am on this subject. The ramifications of this subtle Gnosticism are to not see the world as God sees it. And God wants us to see it as he sees it, so that we would treat the physical world around us as good stewards. As I said, there used to be a day when things were important because Christians understood that the material world was important. Included in those days was a belief that ministers of the gospel carried with them, because of their office, special anointing and authority that made their prayers over new houses and new sanctuaries effectual. It was a time when Christians used to believe in the laying out of hands, which is what was and is done when a man is consecrated to perform special duties in the church. Duties that no one else is called to perform. There used to be a time when Christians believed that whatever the clergy bound on earth would be bound. Whatever the clergy loosed would be loosed That was what Jesus said to the 12, and that is what the 12 passed on to those who were called to the anointed officers of the church. There used to be a time when clergy would consecrate the bread and wine used to represent the body and blood of Jesus And that when such bread and wine were eaten in an unworthy manner, there was judgment. And when such bread and wine were eaten in faith, there was blessing. You don't have to be a believer in transubstantiation to know the power that is in the bread and wine set apart to be used to commemorate the offered body and blood of the Lord. Now I have been using the phrase used to be a time to create in us a desire that those days would return. As the prophet longs for the old paths, so we should long for and work for to bring back days in which the material world is cared for. With faith that it too will be redeemed. Let us pray. Gracious and heavenly Father, we're always amazed by your incarnation, by the incarnation of your Son Jesus. And as we think upon that, as we ponder all that it means, help us to be better stewards of what you placed before us. Heavenly Father, we thank you for this material world. Help us to be grateful for it. In Jesus' name. Amen.

sermons.title: First the flesh
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, of the Son, of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. I very much appreciate effective life hacks. In case you don't know what a life hack is, it is a way of doing something in life that everyone does, only doing it in a way that makes life easier. It lessens hassles. One life hack I love and practice is taking a picture of your parking spot when parking in a multi-level parking garage. Another hack I love and necessary I practice is speaking out loud what I am doing with my keys or passport or plane ticket, which I tend to lose a lot. I say to myself, I am putting my keys in the front pouch of my briefcase. And it works. It makes it easier to remember where I put my keys. So life hacks are great, but sermons should not be about life hacks. And I very much dislike what are called how-to sermons such as how to have a better marriage or how to have a better make a better living or whatever a preacher wants to put at the end of the phrase how to That is not what preaching is to be about. Preachers are to put forth the Word of God and help God's people apply His Word to their lives. Faith does not come by hearing the latest life coach guru. Faith comes by hearing, hearing the word of God. What I am concerned about is that what I am preaching to you today may sound like a life hack. It may sound like a how-to. But it is from the Word of God. And it is a principle of life that God has placed in the world He created, and it is for us to know it and to use it as God intended. So let's get into it. A couple, a couple sat before their pastor desperate to improve their marriage. Because they had begun to live separate lives as they slept in different rooms. They ate their meals alone. They didn't vacation together. They didn't even watch television together And when they did come together, they could only bicker with one another. The pastor asked them, when was the last time they were intimate together? It had been so long, neither one of them could remember. And principle of life missing in their marriage was first the flesh and then the spirit. A young woman sat before her pastor desperate to get out of a rut. She had a part-time job that didn't make enough money for her to move out of her parents' home She spent most waking hours while at home on social media. Her phone had almost become a part of her body. She was obsessed with what her friends were doing and what she was not doing. Her rut was caused by not understanding the principle, first the flesh and then the spirit I have counseled people using the message of first the flesh and then the spirit, but I have never preached on it. I was watching a British television show that had a character who was a policeman Who was required to see a counselor after being shot while on duty? When he sat down, he noticed a bowl of tennis balls and asked about them. The counselor told him they are to lessen stress, for the patient squeezes the ball to lessen their anxiety He picked up a ball, squeezed it, and found it to work. It was then that I realized that even the secular world can identify a principle God has placed in his creation. First the flesh and then the spirit. In Genesis chapter 2, we find the principle of first the flesh and then the spirit when God created Adam. Genesis 2, verse 7 describes God creating Adam out of the dust, meaning that his body, his flesh, was first created And after God was finished with the flesh, he then breathed life into Adam. And the Bible consistently uses breath of God to describe God's spirit. Thus we have the first example, the first principle of first the flesh, and then the spirit.
