We also find the principle of first the flesh and then the spirit in Paul's first letter to the Corinthians chapter 15. where Paul is arguing for the essential doctrine of bodily resurrection. And I want you to recall the content of 1 Corinthians chapter 15, for it is a glorious chapter. And it summarizes the essentials of the gospel that we cherish and necessarily believe to have a hope of salvation. Paul begins that chapter by saying that he came to the people of Corinth with just one mission, which was to preach the gospel. He did not come for money, he did not come for fame. He came because God commissioned him to preach the gospel to the Gentiles. And then Paul rehearses what he preached to them. He preached that Jesus died for their sins according to the scriptures. He preached that Jesus was then buried and then rose again the third day, according to the scriptures, for proof of that resurrection. He preached of Jesus being seen first by Peter, and then by the twelve apostles, and then by some five hundred other witnesses, with a great part of those witnesses still being alive. When Paul preached to the Corinthians. The challenge there is that if anyone doubted the resurrection, they could talk to those witnesses and hear their testimonies. Paul then gives his own testimony of seeing Jesus as Jesus revealed himself to Paul on that road to Damascus. Although being called to preach to the Gentiles, Paul considered himself the least of the apostles. Next in the letter, in that chapter, Paul challenges the Corinthians that if Jesus is indeed raised from the dead, why are some in their midst saying there is no resurrection? What most scholars believe from the evidence is that there were teachers who were saying that Jesus may have been raised from the dead, but his followers will not be raised. Paul argues back that it is either all or none. If none will be raised, then Jesus was not raised. If that it then follows that if Jesus is not raised, then what Paul has preached to them is empty and done in vain. Paul further concludes that if Jesus is not raised, then all of us are still in our sins and thus condemned by those sins, making us have no hope. Without hope and still preaching the gospel would then mean that all who call themselves Christians are to be pitied over all other people. Paul's logic through this argument is sound, making it all the more embarrassing that there are Christian churches today, and thus pastors today, who call themselves Christians Who claim in their pulpits that the resurrection of Jesus did not happen in bodily form because, in their logic, miracles can't occur But these churches and these pastors worship God because of the metaphor, they say, of the resurrection of Jesus. And that metaphor means we can find hope in a metaphor. I advise that if you ever visit a church that teaches in like manner, get up and walk out. If you hear a teacher on a media platform say something similar, turn the station. If you pick up an article and read such teaching, put it down. It is heresy, and thus it is of the devil. It is a lie. Because Paul knows the denial of the resurrection is of the devil, He next describes how Jesus is the first fruits of all who have fallen asleep who have faith in God. Jesus became a man so that he could die and rise again to life to overcome the curse of the first man, Adam, the one who brought sin into the world. The life, death, and resurrection of Jesus put the world back in the order God intended, so that mankind can have authority over the devil and eventually authority even over death. This is what it means for all things, which includes death, to be placed under the feet of Jesus, meaning that he has authority over all. Paul then goes back to his argument regarding what a waste of time, what a waste of suffering he and other Christians endure if there is no resurrection. In fact, the motto of eating and drinking today, for tomorrow we die, would make sense if there is no resurrection. Live it up. Indulge the flesh. Why not? If there is no hope after this life, and with this life being so fleeting, why not find some pleasure before you become dust again? Such thinking makes sense. But Paul says next: do not be deceived. Evil company corrupts good habits. The type of thinking that leads you to pursue pleasure over righteousness is of the devil. Paul says next, awake, awake to righteousness and do not sin. And next comes the questions regarding exactly how this resurrection of our bodies will take place. How does it work? Paul answers by describing the new bodies that will replace the old bodies. Paul calls such bodies celestial bodies, which are bodies fit for heaven. He then comes to the principle I have referred to earlier. The principle follows the rule of first one thing and then another. Our bodies, our bodies were made from dust and thus limited And yet they will be raised in incorruption, meaning they cannot return to dust. He says, what was sown in weakness will be raised in power. And the example is Adam. Adam was made from dust, which is flesh. But the last Adam, who is Jesus, became a life-giving spirit. And then the passage I have been leading up to, I will read it in full. 1 Corinthians 15, beginning at verse 46. Paul says, however, the spiritual is not first, but the natural, and then afterward the spiritual. The first man was of the earth, made of dust. The second man is the Lord from heaven. As was the man of dust, so also are those who are made of dust. And as is the heavenly man, so also are those who are heavenly. And as we have been born in the image of man of dust, we shall also bear the image of the heavenly man. The stated hope that Paul teaches is that believers will receive bodies that bear the image of Jesus, who is the heavenly man. And this is based on the principle in verse 46. The spiritual is not first, but the natural, the natural being our flesh. It is then the principle of first the flesh and then the spirit. This is foundational of our heavenly hope and our earthly living. So let us apply this principle of first the flesh and then the spirit to our given dilemmas. We had a young girl in a rut Who was primarily concerned about her friends posting on social media instead of being a faithful Christian and a productive citizen? The first way to apply the principle is for her to orderly structure her life so that when she regularly accomplishes a physical task, her spirit will be revived and she will want to accomplish more. In Dr. Jordan Peterson's book, Twelve Rules for Life, he recognizes this same principle by counseling people to make their bed every morning. The next step turns into keeping your bedroom in order, and then your house, and then your workplace, and soon you are living an orderly and productive, and for the Christian, a faithful life. First the flesh and then the spirit. The principle also applies to parenting The parent must train their child to be disciplined in the flesh. That is why purposeful parenting is so important. Because when the child is trained and thus gifted with self-control of the flesh He or she then has a spirit that follows, wanting to please the parent and eventually eventually wanting to please God. The principle of first the flesh and then the spirit is ingrained in us, and we don't know it. But I would wager that each of us can recall an incident. where we can identify that principle working within us. For example, one of my sheds goes from orderly to messy to orderly to messy in a predictable cycle. And I know, I know that if I start to pick up just one item and store it properly, my psyche, my spirit is going to see the results and I'm going to want to store something else properly. And do it again and again until the whole shed is orderly again. Such is how God made us But let's go back to our first example of a couple who are acting as roommates and not husband and wife. They don't want to be around each other. They don't even like each other, let alone love each other. And likely, one of the reasons their relationship has become what it is is the lack of intimacy. And by intimacy, I am not thinking only in terms of sexuality, but in terms of hugs, pecs, hand-holding And there may have been something that happened in their marriage that caused the physical separation, but a necessary way back To being husband and wife is to return to physical touch with the hope that the hurt that was the cause can then be addressed. First the flesh and then the spirit. There is a comic strip. It's been around for a while. It's not really comic, it's very serious, but it tells the story of this principle. It tells the story of a husband who is at the dinner table, and he tells his wife that he has fallen in love with another woman and he wants a divorce. She tells him that she has been waiting for their current conversation for a while as she has noticed him distancing himself from her and from their only son. She asked for two things from him before they officially divorced. She asked for him to wait until their son finished his school year, which was in a month. And in that month, that he would carry his wife to their bedroom each night until the month was done. The husband agreed. At first, it was awkward for both the husband and the wife, for he had not carried her since their honeymoon. And as you can imagine, the young son was overjoyed to see his parents doing what he thought was playing with one another. As the days went on, the carrying got less awkward, and the wife even found herself burying her head into her husband's chest. Well she did. He looked down and admired her beauty, admired her character, and this led to him appreciating her love. A few days before the month was over, the husband called his mistress and told her that they must end their relationship because he had fallen back in love with his wife. Now, in some renditions of the story, the husband returns home with flowers only to find his wife was dead, having died of a cancer never disclosed to him. But I don't like that ending. So we will say that the husband came home with flowers and asked his wife's forgiveness. while restating his vow to be her husband until death do they part. That makes us feel better. And regardless of the ending, the principle is effectual. First the flesh And then the Spirit. As I began this sermon, I state again that sermons should not be about life hacks or how-to's. But this principle is too good not to point out and proclaim it to you in order to help the Christian overcome besetting sins and broken relationships. A child doesn't want to pray. Have him kneel. Friends don't want to forgive. Have them hug. A person doesn't believe in the resurrection, look upon his pierced hands. First the flesh, and then the spirit. Amen. Let us pray. Well God, we're grateful for this principle. It's not hiding from us. It's a part of our everyday life. It's also a part of the kingdom that you created and the hope of the resurrection. May we use it to glorify you and to love one another. This we pray in Jesus' name. Amen.

sermons.title: Honor the Sabbath
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, of the Son, of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated Remember that this is a series in which your rector is rambling. I got a lot of problems with you people We had an interesting moment in the adult Sunday School class several weeks ago now. We were talking about honoring the Sabbath day and how it is addressed in the sermons from Article 35 of the 39 articles found in the Book of Common Prayer. The conversation recognized a flaw in our Christian living. It was pointed out That if a fellow Christian had committed a felony and we knew this person, we would feel obligated to confront the person to call them away from such sin. And we could go down the list of the Ten Commandments and recognize that if a fellow Christian were worshiping false gods, making idols, Taking the Lord's name in vain, dishonoring their parents, murdering, stealing, and the rest We would confront them and call them to repentance because we would feel it was our duty to do so. But what about the breaking of the Sabbath? Would we confront a fellow Christian about breaking the Sabbath And there were crickets being heard in the Sunday school class just as there are right now. But some say the Sabbath law isn't the same as the other laws. Or is it? Breaking the Sabbath isn't like bowing down to an idol or sleeping around on your wife or lying under oath, right? Let's see what God has to say about it. Written in Exodus chapter 31, we read. You shall keep the Sabbath because it is holy for you. Everyone who profanes it shall be put to death. Whoever does any work on it, that soul shall be cut off from among his people Six days shall work be done, but the seventh day is a Sabbath of solemn rest, holy to the Lord. Whoever does any work on the Sabbath day shall be put to death. Therefore, the people of Israel shall keep the Sabbath. Observing the Sabbath throughout their generations as a covenant forever. It is a sign forever between me and the people of Israel. That in six days the Lord made heaven and earth, and on the seventh day he rested and was refreshed. Sounds pretty serious to God. But God doesn't want his people to see the Sabbath as something like a burden they have to carry. Hear what he says through the prophet Isaiah, Isaiah chapter 58. If you turn back your foot from the Sabbath, From doing your pleasure on my holy day, and call the Sabbath a delight and a holy day of the Lord honorable If you honor it, not going your own ways, or seeking your own pleasure, or talking idly, Then you shall take delight in the Lord, and I will make you ride on the heights of the earth. I will feed you with the heritage of Jacob, your father. For the mouth of the Lord has spoken. From this, from this, keeping the Sabbath sounds quite wonderful. What we find in the covenant God made with Israel is how important Sabbath-keeping was to him as he repeated the commandment many times. This is from Leviticus chapter 23. Six days shall work be done, but on the seventh day is a Sabbath of solemn rest. Holy convocation. Convocation means gathering. You shall do no work. It is a Sabbath to the Lord in all your dwelling places. The following is from Exodus 35. Long after the giving of the Ten Commandments, God wanted the law repeated to the people. Six days work shall be done, but on the seventh day you shall have a Sabbath of solemn rest, holy to the Lord Whoever does any work on it shall be put to death. The following is from the prophet Nehemiah. And if the peoples of the land bring in goods or any grain on the Sabbath day to sell We will not buy from them on the Sabbath or on a holy day. We will forgo the crops of the seventh year and the exaction of every debt. From the prophet Ezekiel, in a dispute they shall act as judges, and they shall judge it according to my judgments. They shall keep my laws and my statutes and all my appointed feasts, and they shall keep my Sabbath holy. Having repeated God's will regarding the Sabbath in so many different ways and through so many different messengers, we can conclude that it is important. So why isn't it treated the same in the same manner the other commandments of the Ten Commandments are treated? The following are current arguments against Christians honoring the Sabbath day. One argument against Christians keeping the Sabbath is how Jesus spoke of the Sabbath. The following is from the Gospel of St. Luke, chapter 6, very familiar to the Gospel reading from Matthew this morning. Now it happened on the second Sabbath after the first that he went through the grain fields, and his disciples plucked the heads of the grain and ate them, rubbing them in their hands. And some of the Pharisees said to them, Why are you doing what is not lawful to do on the Sabbath But Jesus answering them said, Have you not read this, what David did when he was hungry, he and those who were with him? How he went into the house of God, took and ate the showbread, and also gave some of those with him, which is not lawful for any but the priest to eat And he said to them, The Son of Man is also Lord of the Sabbath. Several points of truth are to be extracted from this section of Scripture. First, the Pharisees were referring to the book of Deuteronomy, which explicitly states, as we have already heard, that work is not to be performed on the Sabbath. Interestingly, when we were in Israel, we observed several unique ways the Israelis avoid physical work on the Sabbath. One of them is to shut down public transportation altogether. Another interesting way is to not allow the use of elevators, or at least not allow people to push the buttons on elevators. This is because starting a fire or igniting a spark is considered work. And therefore using electrical devices are interpreted to be lighting a spark. To still use elevators, they have what are called Shabbat elevators. Shabbat is another word for Sabbath. These elevators stop at every level of a particular building on a continuous basis so that the pushing of buttons is not required. In the first century, no such interpretation of the law was needed, of course, but the Pharisees were very technical in their interpretation of the law. They interpreted the fourth commandment strictly so that any physical exertion could be identified as labor, including walking certain distances. And with their self-righteous hearts, they looked for ways in which the disciples of Jesus were not obeying God's law. Their interpretation of the Sabbath work included harvesting, and the act of a person taking their hands and picking pieces of grain from the head of wheat was an act of the world. Of harvesting, at least their interpretation. Jesus' answer to their accusation reveals several very important points He first shows how necessity requires a proper response. The showbread in the temple was sacred. And yet when it came to God's anointed needing sustenance, it was allowed to be consumed by others besides the priest. Jesus was of the line of David. Jesus was the promised anointed one from the line of David. And thus the same line of reasoning applied to him as it did to David. Also, by referring to himself as the Son of Man, he is taking on the title of the promised Messiah promised from the prophet Daniel and thus declaring himself the Messiah. although in a more subtle manner than he would later. In Mark's Gospel, as in Matthew's Gospel, he records the same incident, but adds that Jesus said that the Sabbath was made for man. And not man for the Sabbath. And such means that God did not intend his people to serve the Sabbath But the Sabbath would serve his people, and this we will get to. The overall point is that Jesus honored the Sabbath as did his disciples, only Jesus did not interpret the disciples. Such honoring in a legalistic manner as the Pharisees did. Another argument against Christians honoring the Sabbath is interpreting the following words from Saint Paul, who wrote to the Colossians, and said the following as you heard this morning So let no one judge you in food or in drink or regarding a festival or a new moon or Sabbaths. The New King James rightly puts the word Sabbath in a lower case because the word Sabbath did not just refer to the weekly Sabbath, but instead referred to any day in the Jewish calendar that was set aside as a day of rest. Thus there were several Sabbath days that the Jews observed outside the weekly Sabbath. The point Paul was making is that the Gentile Christians at Colossae were not required to observe any Sabbath in the same manner the Jews insisted, making the point the same as Jesus made of the Pharisees. Again, Paul is not saying, don't observe the Sabbath. He's arguing not to do so as the Jewish people insisted. And the final argument for Christians not honoring the Sabbath, at least the final argument for this sermon. Is that Christians don't keep the Sabbath because we don't worship on Saturday. And Saturday's the Sabbath Such an argument is the primary argument of the justification of the existence of the Seventh-day Adventist Church. To respond to this, we first must recall the historical reality of the Christians and the Sabbath. When the Christian faith primarily consisted of Jewish converts, The believers would honor the Sabbath on Saturday as they interpreted the fourth commandment, and then gather together with fellow Christians for the breaking of bread and the consuming of wine. on Sundays to commemorate the resurrection of Jesus. When the gospel came to the Gentiles and the majority of Christians became converted Gentiles The Jewish traditions on the Saturday Sabbath were no longer followed, but instead the Sabbath for the Gentiles became every Sunday, where they would rehearse the gospel stories, read the letters of the apostles, and share the bread and wine. In communion. Now, the logical argument of making the Christian Sabbath Sunday instead of Saturday was because there was no evidence That the exact seventh day, identified as Saturday on our present-day calendar, was the exact day that God identified as the original seventh day or Sabbath day. Well, the Jews identified as the seventh day could have been the seventh day of creation, or the third day of creation, or any one of the seven days. Thus, the exact day identified as the Sabbath is impossible to identify, allowing for Christians to identify Sunday as the Sabbath day. In Scripture, the day is also referred to as the Lord's Day, for that is what Saint Jaw called Saint John called it when he described his vision in the book of Revelation, where he was taken up in the Spirit on the Lord's day. Thus, Christians have gathered for Christian worship on Sundays since the days of the apostles, and Christians have referred to the Lord's Day as their observance of the Sabbath since that time as well. What I am wanting you to conclude is that Sundays for Christians are to be our Sabbath day, the day we obey the fourth commandment. But I am not going door to door, visiting your homes, if you don't worship Jesus every Sunday I'm not going to be deriding you for mowing your lawn on Sundays or going to a baseball game. What I will tell you Is how fundamental honoring the Sabbath should be for every Christian. The most obvious point to make is that God, if God Needed to rest on the seventh day. If God needed to rest on the seventh day, what arrogance it is for us to think that we don't need to rest on the seventh day We are created in God's image. And if you don't follow his example, we will not continue in his image, for we become our own God. Who chooses our own schedule, and such is not sustainable because that is not how God has designed us. We need the Sabbath. It was created for us, which means for our benefit. And we need all the benefits we can get. The second point to make is how the honoring of the Sabbath day establishes a necessary priority in our lives. When we use the Sabbath day to worship our God, our Savior, we are obeying the first and second commandments as well. We are placing God as first priority in our lives. And we are not choosing an idol to worship in place of him. And beloved, there are so many activities the devil wants us to participate. In besides the worship of God. And you may not see it as an idol, but instead it is a mere sports season or a scout excursion or necessary recital But it shines like an idol, just as those in the days of Pharaoh. What I want to motivate each one of us is not what we shouldn't do on the Sabbath. But the beauty on what we are able to do on the Sabbath. We are able to stand, kneel, and sit in the presence of God. And that presence is like no other. For Jesus taught us that when two or more are gathered together in his name, he is uniquely there. That unique presence is different than when each of us is alone. And even though he is with us individually at all times, he is with us in a special manner when we gather in his name. And that unique presence is amplified at the reading of God's Word, at the preaching of that same word, and next, even more uniquely. When we break bread, which is his body, and share the wine, which is his blood. You may ask me To be more specific in the matter, Jesus is uniquely present, and how exactly is the bread, his body, and the wine, his blood? And I can answer that with no reservation by saying, I don't know. When we try to know, when we try to explain it, we will likely fall into superstition, which is believing more than what the Bible teaches. Or we could fall into heresy, which is to believe what the the opposite of what the Bible teaches. Or we could simply sound like a fool who is trying to say something while really saying nothing. Instead, we can embrace the idea of mystery. Mystery is accepting a truth we cannot fully understand, at least in this life. Remember that the Bible tells us that we see through the glass dimly. And glass in the first century was not what it is like today. Things looked oddly shaped and the colors were fuzzy. The Bible also tells us that we are under the sun, meaning that our vantage point to see reality is very much limited. So we are to accept our limitations and accept what Jesus tells us. When we gather, when his word is read and preached, when we break bread and share wine, we are uniquely blessed by his presence. Making them a means of grace given freely to us. But gathering for Christian worship on a Sabbath day isn't the only beautiful part of honoring the Sabbath. It is also gathering with friends and family after worship and sharing a meal and sharing about your weak past. And sharing about plans for the future, and telling humorous stories, and updating one another about family achievements and family prayer needs It is watching children play together and including them on telling old family stories. The Sabbath is also quietly sitting alone or sitting with your spouse and reading a book Playing a game, enjoying some form of entertainment, while your body and mind rest, being prepared for another week Another week of to-do lists, car trips, work meetings, school meetings Church meetings, phone calls, emails, tragic news on the television, money gained, money lost, groceries to buy, bills to pay, relationships to maintain, and I became depressed writing this all down. Honoring the Sabbath takes us away from all that needs to be done and all that we think needs to be done during the week. It gives us time to be like God, which is to rest the seventh day. I told Bobby Lynn last Sunday night That I felt like I had had preached what I preached last week was an infomercial on the studying the Bible. Well, this also sounds like an infomercial on honoring the Sabbath, and I accept that I preach this out of conviction that the Sabbath was made for you. Amen. Let us pray. My gracious and heavenly Father, we are convicted because we at times so lazurely approach your fourth commandment, not treating them as not treating it as the same as the rest. And yet what we have said here from your holy word is that we need to honor it. It is a gift from you to us, and we receive it. In Jesus' name. Amen.

sermons.title: Flood in Texas
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: Pero la bebida en la mente no la voy a llegar a tu ir, como no me agradezco nada, tu querido ir, señor. Name of the Father, of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Please be seated. The title of this sermon is Calamity in Texas. So you know where we're going this morning. We're going to be looking at Luke chapter 13, our gospel reading as well. The body count From the flood in Texas was not near complete, and the primary victims known on July 4th were young girls from a Christian camp. When the following was posted on social media, quote, may all visitors, children, non-MAGA voters, and pets be safe and dry. Kerr County MAGA voted to gut FEMA. They deny climate change. May they get what they voted for. Bless their hearts. Kerr County in Texas was the primary area hit by the flooding that took now well over 100 lives, including many girls attending Camp Mystic. The person who posted the condemnation of her political enemies was not just a physician, but a female pediatrician. And I read the quote again. May all visitors, children, non-MAGA voters, and pets be safe and dry. Kerr County, MAGA voted to gut FEMA. They deny climate change. May they get what they voted for. Bless their hearts. The following are other social media posts from the general public. From someone who goes by Samurai Barbie, quote, cry harder, Texas deserves it. From someone who goes by just some guy, quote, it's not awful. It's what Texas deserves And from someone who goes by Judea, quote, Texas deserves every flood, God has spoken, and it, it is God, hates Texas. There's more, much more, but these are enough examples to make the some to make some points. We can first notice That too many tragedies include natur including natural disasters have become politicized. Whatever the tragedy, it is a politician's fault, and the fault of all those who voted that politician into office. The second thing to notice is how these comments have a type of justice standard they have adopted. They believe in a form of justice and they believe in their righteousness, and so whoever disagrees with their politics and suffers is suffering because they are on the wrong side of a political issue. The third thing we notice is how falsely brave and self-righteous such anonymous comments are. This understanding of poetic justice and universal karma is not only noted by those on the liberal side of the politics or of the faith, but on the conservative side as well. Public comments were made about divine justice when fires burned in Malibu, a place where many Hollywood elites lived, and that was less than a year ago. Back in the 1980s, many Christians believed that the spread of AIDS was God's judgment on homosexuals. Individually Each of us has been tempted to question God when events in our lives don't go well, or when we get ill, or when we get injured. We are tempted to ask God what we did to deserve our present suffering. It seems ingrained in us that when something bad happens, it is because we have done something wrong Again, the desire to identify a cause and effect within any tragedy appears innate in each of us. We hear of a man committing heinous murders, and we want to identify what his past was like so that we can conclude what brought him to behave in such an evil manner. We hear of a woman engaging in immoral behavior, and we begin with the assumption that something drove her to behave in the way she did. What is likely the purpose of our desire to identify a cause in every tragedy is that we want to be able to control our future. And so we think that if we can avoid the causes of others, we can also avoid tragedies of others When it comes to natural disasters, we have another variable to understand, one much more mysterious than the human psyche. We appear to have the mind of God, for we make the automatic assumption that He is directly responsible for controlling all weather patterns and all seismic activity. If a devastating earthquake occurs, as it has in places like Haiti, where there was much devastation devastation, Christians can conclude that Such was the result of the people rejecting the gospel and embracing superstitions associated with witchcraft, which are also associated, of course, with the devil. If an earthquake, fire, and flood occur in places like Japan, we can conjecture that it was brought on by the nation's aggression during World War II. Or we can conclude that it is a punishment for its continued embrace of Buddhist tradition rather than responding to the missionaries who brought them the gospel. It could also be for the nation's trade imbalance with the United States, but I have not heard anyone project that theory yet To think that God in his sovereign plan is enacting vengeance on individuals and groups of people who do wrong against him in order to balance some type of cosmic scale. Is wrong-headed and shows no true understanding of the gospel. If there is a cosmic scale, it was violently tipped when Adam brought sin into the world. The gospel tells us that God isn't looking for mankind to balance it, for mankind can do nothing to appease him. And anyways, God does not want the scale balanced. He wants it fully tipped to the side of righteousness. And the only way that was going to happen is if his son Jesus became the perfect sacrifice to pay for the sins of the world, which we know he did. And that is why we are here this morning. If you anticipate that my attempt this morning is to answer the ultimate question Of why bad things happen to good people, I'm sorry to say I will disappoint you. The easiest answer to such a dilemma is to point out that when Adam brought sin into the world, he brought in a curse not just upon himself. and his offspring, but upon all of creation. When God says to Adam that the ground will bring forth thorns and thistles as a result of his sin, he is saying That all of creation, including vegetation, would be cursed. Because the ground is cursed Weather patterns are not safe and are unpredictable, no matter how many satellite systems a television news station owns. Because the ground is cursed, all forms of beds of water can overflow or dry up. Undesired rays fall in some areas and do not fall in other areas. Because the ground is cursed, winds can blow as a gentle breeze or Category 5 hurricane. Because the ground is cursed, the earth underneath is unsettled and moves without warning, causing devastation to anything that rests upon it. Because the earth is cursed. Because the earth is cursed if a if the people didn't cry out with Hosanna's Jesus said the rocks would do so, because even the rocks want to be redeemed. So why do bad things happen even to good people? They could simply answer, it is because of the sin of Adam and the curse that followed. But that would not be answering what we are truly asking. What we are truly asking is why bad things don't happen to all of us if Adam is to blame. We want to know why earthquakes, fires and floods seem to have selected places and selected times. We want to know if there is a specific purpose to everything that happens. And if there is, what is it? We especially want to know the specific purposes for the things that happen to us. And such questions, beloved, are not questions any minister can answer. What we can provide, however, is the wisdom that is given in somewhat obscure conversation. Jesus has A obscure, somewhat obscure conversation with strangers at the beginning of Luke chapter 13 I say it is obscure because it is between Jesus and those Luke says were present at the season. Those present are not given a name. The phrase season does not refer to a particular religious celebration, but a general reference to a nondescript time of year And the story referred to by the nondescript people during this nondescript time is one that is specifically recorded, not specifically recorded, excuse me, not specifically recorded elsewhere. The Jewish historian Josephus does record stories of Jews being murdered by Roman soldiers during Jewish festivals, so the events alluded to were not uncommon. We can imagine that there were men from Galilee who were merely accused of a crime against the Roman state, and as they were worshiping and offering sacrifices, were killed by the sword of the Roman soldiers. And the result was their blood mixing with the blood offered in worship. Those questioning Jesus were assuming at least two things First, Jewish Galileans are not as righteous as Jews from Jerusalem. Second People who suffer such horrible deaths must be guilty of something heinous to make them deserve their own fate. From Jesus' response in verse 2, we are able to note that the questioners did assume that the Galileans were worse sinners because of the manner they were killed. It is natural to wonder if these questioners knew that Jesus grew up in Galilee. If they did not, their question is comical, and if they did, their question is quite bold, for they are Taking a swipe at the righteousness of Jesus. And Jesus' response was a rhetorical question They did suppose the murdered Galileans were greater sinners because they understood the world to work in such a manner that worse sinners receive worse punishment in this life. Jesus doesn't directly refute their thinking, but only redirects. Redirects what they need to be most concerned about. Unless they repent. Unless they repent, they too will perish in the same manner. In what manner is that? Does Jesus mean that unless people repent, they will die by the sword or in some violent manner? Before we answer that, we need to listen to Jesus more. Jesus next mentions another historical catastrophe that is also not recorded elsewhere, but was obviously known by his listeners, likely making it a recent event. Apparently a tower was being built near the city's water supply, and when it was at a good height, it collapsed, killing 18 people. Jesus' rhetorical question about the victims being worse sinners implies that they were average citizens, simply average workers. The tragedy allowed for everyone to conclude that they could have easily been victim to the same event, for there was nothing about the dead that separated them from those who survived. These types of seemingly random tragedies wake all of us up from our daily doldrums. And the news media knows this. That is why they lead with stories that scare as much of the populace as they can. They want us all to think that we need to watch their news so that what happened to others won't happen to us. What Jesus wants us to understand and accept is that there is nothing you can do to prevent such tragedies from happening. Regardless of how safe you think you are, there are certain things in life that you and I simply have no control over. We try to build buildings so that they can withstand category five hurricanes or 10. 0 earthquakes. And we see what forces of nature can do in response. But beloved, we cannot build the Tower of Babel. You remember That the inhabitants of the earth responded after the great flood by building a tower that they thought would protect them from another flood. And God thwarted their plans. God did not allow it. He didn't allow it then, and he would not allow it ever. If we think that we we can do it for ourselves to prevent tragedy. We may have to learn the hard way that we are not our own defender. Jesus' teaching gives us at least one vital piece of wisdom. It is a wisdom that unites every catastrophe, every violent ending to another person. It is the wisdom that each tragedy tells us that we need to repent Or we too will find our life ending in a similar manner. But notice, please, that Jesus is not saying that every person who does not repent will find his or her life end tragically. When he says, you will all likewise perish, he is describing two things. First, that the unrepentant will perish in a manner that catches them unprepared to meet God. And second, that they will perish a second time, which will be their eternal punishment. The message in each example that Jesus gives remains the same. Repent now. The parable that follows must be dissected in detail at another time, but its main message, its main message, is the same as Jesus' previous lesson. Only this lesson is directed specifically at the Jews. They were given time to produce fruit. Jesus had been publicly in their midst for three years. After three years of having the Messiah with them, they did not bear fruit. Although the owner of the fig tree ordered the tree to be cut down, the keeper of the vineyard, Jesus. Pled on behalf of the fig tree that it be given one more year. Beloved God is slow to anger. Jesus desires the salvation of his people. God takes no enjoyment out of punishing the wicked. But fruitlessness cannot go on forever. The only means by which a man or woman can bear fruit is if he or she repents. Repentance. It sounds so very negative. It is a word that does not provide comfortable emotions. It does not sound like a happy word. The need to re for repentance means that we have done something wrong, terribly wrong, so wrong that we need to change direction, complete change. We have to do the opposite of what we are guilty of doing. Repentance assumes guilt, and guilt is in no way a happy word. And yet, and yet a result of repentance is a new beginning. Repentance provides a clean slate. Repentance is a means to remove guilt. Repentance places us on the road to eternal life. Perhaps repentance is a happy word, after all. From the examples Jesus uses To emphasize our need for every man, woman, and child to repent, we can see that part of our repentance should include our judgment of God. We judge God when we say that disasters caused by nature are unjust. We judge God when we think that tragedy should befall certain persons and should not befall other certain persons. The irony of such judgment is that our sense of justice actually comes from God. Without Him teaching us what it is to be just, our sense of justice would be distorted. And yet we easily judge God when we do not think a catastrophe played out the way it should have. We think we could have done better We are confident our way would have been more just. And from that type of thinking evermore, we must repent. When all is thought through, when all is considered, we must come to some basic conclusions about human suffering. We cannot possibly know God's sovereign plan. We cannot see the past working with the present toward the future, which contains God's plan of salvation. We cannot know how God is working in all dimensions of existence, so that all suffering is good in the end, for all that love him are called according to his purpose. The only true justice is enacted and defined by God Himself. In summary, I don't know what the people in Kerr County, Texas have done to deserve the suffering they have gone through and are going through. I can't unequivocally know what the people of Haiti or Japan were guilty of. I don't know what the people of New Orleans did. I don't know specifically what the people who worked in the World Trade Center towers did, or what the firemen did who worked to save them only to be buried under rubble. Can we say that God is trying to speak in a dramatic way to a city or a nation that suffers through a disaster? Absolutely. What he specifically is saying, only those who suffer can truly say. What he is saying to every person, everywhere, out of every disaster, is the need to repent. And he is ready and willing to forgive. And all of God's people said. Amen. Let us pray. Father, we are grateful that we can find comfort in your holy word. Jesus, we thank you for teaching us, for helping us see things through your eyes. And see what is necessary, what is most important. Not this life, not this life, but the life to come. Father, we all pray for those who are still suffering so mightily from this great loss in Texas. We ask, dear Lord, that you would be their comfort, that you would be their strength, and Father, bring them to repentance. This we pray in Jesus' name. Amen.

sermons.title: A Call to Arms
sermons.speaker: Rev. Eric W. Jorgensen
sermons.text: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, of the Holy Ghost. Amen. Leave me seated. This continues our series. That I have titled The Ramblings of a Rector. And the title of this sermon is A Call to Arms. And as you can tell, by the songs that were chosen that the uh the piano player, the organist lives with the preacher. On the 7th of July 2005, four suicide bombers struck London's transport network, killing 52 people and injuring over 770 others. Three of the blasts happened on London Underground around 8. 50 a. m. in the vicinity of Aldergate, Edgeware, and Russell Square stations. The four device expl the fourth device exploded at 9. 47 a. m. on a bus that had been diverted via Travis Scott Square, close to where the British Transport Police headquarters was at the time. The building became a base for the walking wounded. One of the bombers was named Muhammad Sadiq Khan. age 30. He lived in Easton Leeds, which is north of London. He lived with his wife and young child, where he worked as a learning mentor at a primary school. Khan detonated his bomb on the number 216 train, killing seven people, including himself. Mr. Kahn left a video to give reasons for his evil actions. In the video he said the following. Quote, I and thousands like me are forsaking everything for what we believe. Our drive and motivation doesn't come from tangible commodities that this world has to offer. Our religion is this Islam Obedience to the one true God, and following the footsteps of the final prophet messenger. Your democratically elected governments continually perpetuate atrocities against my people all over the world. And your support of them makes you directly responsible, just as I am directly responsible for protecting and avenging my Muslim brothers and sisters. Until we feel security, you will be our targets, and until you stop the bombing, gassing, imprisonment, and torture of my people, we will not stop this fight We are at war and I am a soldier. Now you too will taste the reality of this situation And he continued, I myself, I myself make dua, which is prayer, to Allah, to raise me against those whom I love, like the prophets, the messengers, the martyrs, and today's heroes. like our beloved Sheikh Osama bin Laden and all other brothers and sisters that are fighting in this cause I chose to share Mr. Khan's personal information because of what evil must have controlled him. I remind you that Mr. Kahn had a wife, a small child, while also working as a mentor at a primary school. We should have no doubt that Mr. Khan sincerely believed that what he did honored his God. But let us make no mistake, his actions were evil. His actions were of the devil. And we Christians need to be reminded from time to time that evil is real, and the devil is real. And we as believers in Jesus Christ are to be wary of him and to be about the business of warring against him. That the devil can influence a man to abandon his wife and son, to murder people he did not know, for a cause that would not change after his actions. shows us how cunning and deceptive the devil can be. And I hesitate to describe the devil in such a manner because I don't want to give him any credit or descriptive that would make him proud. But the facts are the facts. We often hear that the devil is a fallen angel who used to be the angel of light But few know where that understanding comes from. Theologians and Bible scholars believe it started with interpreting a passage from the prophet Isaiah, which reads the following. How you are fallen, O heaven, O daystar, Son of Dawn! How you are cut down to the ground, you who laid the nations low. You said in your heart, I will ascend to heaven above the stars of God. I will set my throne on high. I will sit on the mount of assembly in the far reaches of the north. I will ascend above the heights of the clouds. I will make myself like the Most High. The description is found in Isaiah 14, 12 through 14. In its historical context, it is describing the king of Babylon. But the description is so very dramatic and grand enough. To be describing someone or something greater than an earthly king. The passage from Isaiah that I just read was then interpreted with a passage from the prophet Ezekiel. Who was given the following words from God? You were the seal of perfection, full of wisdom and perfect beauty. You were in Eden, the garden of God. Every kind of precious stone adorned you, a ruby, topaz, and diamond, barrel, onyx and jasper, sapphire, turquoise, and emeralds. Your mountings and settings were crafted in gold, prepared on the day of your creation. You were anointed as a guardian cherub For I had ordained you. You were on the holy mountain of God. You walked among the fiery stones. From the day you were created, you were blameless in your ways until wickedness was found in you. By the vastness of your trade, you were filled with violence, and you sinned. So I drove you in disgrace from the mountain of God, and I banished you O guardian cherub, from among the fiery stones. Your heart grew proud of your beauty. You corrupted your wisdom because of your splendor. So I cast you to the earth. I made you a spectacle before kings. Now, again, the historic context was that Ezekiel was to rebuke the king of Tyre But because the words are so grand in scale and of importance, even going back to the Garden of Eden, they seem to be speaking of an earth-moving and heaven-moving event. And an earth and heaven moving creature. And then we have the following from the book of Revelation, chapter 12. Then war broke out in heaven. Michael and his angels fought against the dragon, and the dragon and his angels fought back. But the dragon was not strong enough, and no longer was any place found in heaven for him and his angels. And the great dragon was hurled down, that ancient serpent called the devil and Satan. The deceiver of the whole world. He was hurled to the earth and his angels with him. And I heard a loud voice saying, Now have come the salvation and the power of the kingdom of our God. and the authority of his Christ. For the accuser of his brothers has been thrown down. He who accuses them day and night before our God. They have conquered him by the blood of the Lamb. And by the word of their testimony, and they did not love their lives so as to shy away from death. Therefore, rejoice, O heavens, and you who dwell in them. But woe Woe to the earth and sea, with great fury the devil has come down to you, knowing he has only a short time. If this passage from Revelation is describing the same events as Ezekiel and as Isaiah described, we can indeed conclude. That the devil did have a place in glory, but chose to rebel against God, wanting to be the highest above God, and was judged for it. And it is in Jude's letter that describes the angels that followed Satan. Jude verse six reads. And the angels who did not keep their proper domain, but left their own abode, he has reserved in everlasting chains under darkness for the judgment of the great day. After understanding the devil's past, we are next to heed the warnings about him given to us. First, notice what is said in the passage that was read from the book of Revelation. But woe to the earth and the sea, with great fury the devil has come down to you, knowing he has only a short time. A woe to the earth is a woe to us who live in the earth. The devil being on the earth isn't playing around. He has purpose, and that purpose is to destroy the souls of every human being that has and will exist. Saint Peter gave this warning. Your adversary, the devil, walks about like a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour. The idea of the devil being a roaring lion is a way to say that he is on the prowl. He is purposefully hunting each and every one of us, and that includes our children and the most vulnerable He desires to sink his teeth into your soul and let the juices run down his throat. And while the devil is loud and proud as a lion, he is also cunning and deceptive. In Paul's second letter to the Christians at Corinth, he wrote, Satan himself masquerades as an angel of light. It is quite possible that Paul describes the devil in such a manner because of Isaiah calling him the day star, which is light. But we more importantly note that the devil masquerades as an angel of light, for he is no longer the day star, but has been kicked out of heaven. And his days are numbered. But those numbered days are still continuing. And so we must be diligently resisting him. And one way to do so is to identify in practical ways where and how the devil masquerades. And I'll start with a more obvious way, Satan masquerades as an angel of light. He does so in the occult, with seemingly innocuous things such as tarot cards, psychics, horoscopes, and games such as dungeons and dragons Beloved God's law speaks against such conjurings and playing in the spiritual world Because an evil spiritual world does exist. It really does exist. And the demonic will come into you if you let them If you have followed the murders that occurred in Idaho, the University of Idaho, my alma mater, and witnessed the suspect. Being sentenced this week, you should have no doubt that what you viewed in that man was a man possessed by evil. His lack of honesty and remorse are signs of someone who has left the demonic in his soul Reminding us that we are all susceptible to allow evil to live within us because we are fallen in a similar way that the demonic is fallen. We are only protected by the filling of the Holy Spirit Another way Satan masquerades himself is in false teachings and false teachers In fact, that is the very context that Paul is speaking when he warns of such masquerading, and here's the whole passage. But I will keep on doing what I am doing in order to undercut those who want an opportunity to be regarded as our equals in the things of which they boast. For such men are false apostles, deceitful workers, masquerading as apostles of Christ. And no wonder, for Satan himself masquerades as an angel of light It is not surprising, then, that if his servants masquerade as servants of righteousness, their end will correspond to their actions. These false teachers were teaching such things as Jesus wasn't really a man, and he certainly wasn't God. While also undermining the teachings of Paul by arguing that Paul was not a true apostle, and therefore did not have the authority he said he had. The end goal of every false teacher is earthly fame and earthly wealth. It was that way in the first century, and it is the same today. And sadly, there are other ways false teachers masquerade. They pretend to care for young people and become involved in the personal lives of young people when in truth they are predators. Sexually deviant predators. The damage that such sexually deviant predators do to young people is deplorable as too many young people have been spiritually damaged So that the church becomes a frightening place and God is only understood as a being who would not protect them. People who use young people to satisfy their sexual deviancy are sick and disgusting. That they are also real, and the devil uses them for evil. Another way the devil is currently masquerading himself as an angel of light is self-righteousness. We witness a great deal of this on social media and from politicians. The devil has convinced so many people that they can be labeled righteous if they fight hate with being hateful. They think they can be righteous by fighting for the rights of the sexually immoral. They think they can be righteous by standing against tyranny where there is no tyranny. Like Don Quixote fighting windmills and thinking they are dragons, so the earthly righteous protect us from kings where there are no kings. What I've attempted to do so far in this sermon is to convince you that the devil is real and evil is real. But of course, we cannot leave you there without an answer. We then must go back to St. Peter and hear more about the devil as a roaring lion. The whole section reads this: Be sober-minded and alert. Your adversary, the devil, prowls around like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour. Resist him, standing firm in your faith And in the knowledge that your brothers throughout the world are undergoing the same times of sufferance. This entire sermon to source has been about making us sober and alert. An inebriated man does not have full awareness of his surroundings, nor full control of his motor skills. Therefore, he is not a man, the man he could be. A sober man is the opposite and therefore able to be used of God in battle. An alert man anticipates the enemy and anticipates a fight. This is why after Peter describes the devil as a roaring lion, he next instructs every Christian to resist him. Every Christian is to actively resist the devil. We are not to expect others to resist him for us, but each of us is to be active in the resistance. And what are ways to resist the devil? Peter has already said one way, which is to stand firm in your faith. It has been stated. From this pulpit before, and I don't mind saying it again, and I and I hope and pray you will repeat it to the next generation until Jesus returns. The devil only has two plans for your life. He either wants you to deny your faith in Jesus Christ or he wants you dead. If you deny your faith in Jesus, he has your soul with him for eternity. If he doesn't have that, he would rather you be out of the way, which is for you to be dead, so that God cannot use you to share his gospel and worship his holy name. Therefore, the best way to resist the devil is to rub the truth in his face and to stand firm in your faith. Remember what Paul wrote to the Ephesians. Put on the full armor of God, that you can make your stand against the devil's schemes. For our struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the powers of this world's darkness, and against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly realms. Therefore take up the full armor of God, so that when the day of evil comes you will be able to stand your ground, having done everything to stand, stand firm then, with the belt of truth buckled around your waist. with the breastplate of righteousness arrayed, and with your feet fitted with the readiness of the gospel of peace. In addition to all this, take up the shield of faith, with which you can extinguish all the flames and arrows of the evil one. And take the helmet of salvation and the sword of the Spirit, which is the Word of God. I want to allow you to enter the Jorgensen world for a moment. When my boys turned 30, I gave each of them a statue. Of St. George. And St. George is stabbing a dragon. Of course, Jorgen's son is Danish It means son of George. It refers to Saint George. And if you know the tradition of Saint George, it is said in Lore that There was a damsel in distress who was captured by a dragon, and Saint George braved himself up to go and fetch the girl and kill the dragon. And so I remind my boys, as the devil is represented by dragons, that it's our responsibility as inheritors of St. George to kill dragons. To kill the devil, to be at war with him and to defeat him. Beloved, the spiritual world is real. The devil exists. And his purpose is to destroy the souls of as many humans as possible. The fight for your soul and the souls of those you love is real. But do not shrink. Stay in the fight, slay the dragon, and save the girl. Amen.
